<!-- foundations/usage.md -->

# Using WebKit in an app

> Start from a block, find a component, import it tree-shakeably, app-level setup and the quality checklist.

## Overview

`@aziontech/webkit` is the Azion design system: a set of themed, accessible Vue 3 components. This project depends on it. When you build or review UI here, reach for a webkit component first, import it with the flat path, and style with `@aziontech/theme` tokens. This skill is the paste-safe reference for doing that right.

## Start here: one app layout, then each screen is a page body

The chrome is composed **once**, in `App.vue`, around `RouterView`, from the layout of the surface:

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsoleLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/console-layout-root'
  import { navigation } from './navigation'
</script>

<template>
  <ConsoleLayout
    :navigation="navigation"
    :breadcrumbs="$route.meta.breadcrumbs ?? []"
    :account="{ name: 'Jane Doe', email: 'jane.doe@example.com' }"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </ConsoleLayout>
</template>
```

- **Console:** `ConsoleLayout` — navigation rows `{ id, label, icon, href }` (an in-app `href` is
  followed with the app's router, no `@navigate` wiring needed) and the active row follows the
  route; `actions`, `account-menu`, `search`, `header-start`, `breadcrumbs`, `notifications` and `tools` slots. A page
  opens the shared palette with `useConsoleLayout().openSearch()`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/use-console-layout`); a body that also renders on its own calls
  `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })`, which returns `null` outside a layout. Bind `v-model:navigation-expanded` to persist the rail or
  to offer `Collapse sidebar` in the palette (`search` slot + `@search-select`). A page sets its own
  trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`, and a full-height workspace puts
  `data-layout-fill` on its root (never `calc(100dvh - …)`).
- **Site:** `SiteLayout` — `navigation` and `footer` are the `SiteNav` and `SiteFooter` data. The
  site is dark: `<html data-theme="dark">`. `SiteFooter` binds its language select with
  `v-model:language`; switch the locale from that value.
- **Docs:** `DocLayout` — the docs tree, section links, `outline` (the article's headings), and
  `actions`, `navigation-footer`, `aside`, `footer` slots. The document scrolls. A drill row
  (`kind: 'drill'`) opens in place and the rail's Back reads `Back to Docs` (`rootLabel` renames it);
  never add a hand-made Back row.

The shell blocks (`shells/console`, `shells/website`, `shells/documentation`) are these layouts with
the real navigation: copy one as your `App.vue` and replace its stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
A page never renders its own `<main>`, `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `GlobalHeader`, `SiteNav`,
`SiteFooter` or `Command`. Every platform block is a page body; the one exception is a screen with no rail — a
create flow (`platform/create/*`, headed by the `headers/creation-header` bar) or a
signed-out screen (`platform/auth`): route it outside the layout (a route meta `App.vue` reads), and
it keeps its own bar and `<main>` (`webkit-navigation`).

## A screen begins from a pattern

Before composing anything, check whether the screen already exists as a block:
`npx @aziontech/webkit search <the screen in plain words>` ("login", "account settings", "delete
confirmation"), or the `webkit` MCP `search_patterns`. Read the best one with
`npx @aziontech/webkit view <block-id>` (or `get_pattern`), then start the screen with
`npx @aziontech/webkit add <block-id>` (`--variant <state>` for another state): it copies the SFC
into the views directory, checks its imports, records it in `webkit.blocks.json` and prints the
route entry. `npx @aziontech/webkit diff <block-id>` later shows what you changed against the
canonical block. Before adapting it, read the guidelines (`view`, or the `guidelines` field
`get_pattern` returns): when to use the screen and when another block fits better, what each building block (A,
B, C…) is for, do and don't, the copy rules and the accessibility rules. If "When not to use"
matches your case, switch to the block it names. Then change only the content of the copy,
keeping to the guidelines. Only when no pattern fits, compose from components (below). A marketing band is a page section, not a pattern (rule
`webkit-sections`).

## Headers and the docs home — never hand-build these

- **Every app header has search.** A console, demo, docs or site header puts `SearchTrigger`
  (`@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger`) first in `GlobalHeader.Right`, opening a `Command` palette;
  it draws `Search … ⌘K` (`Ctrl K` off macOS) on a wide bar and the magnifier on a narrow one, and
  binds the shortcut. `ConsoleLayout`, `SiteLayout` and `DocLayout` already carry it, wired to
  their palette (rule `webkit-header-search`, lint `webkit/header-search-trigger`).
- **A docs home is `shells/documentation --variant Landing`.** It opens on `DocHero` (display
  title with air above it, deck, `Get started` then `CopyPromptButton` — the dark "Copy prompt"
  chip carrying the Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Cursor marks — and a note), then the first section
  opens on `DocAgentCard` ("Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" with the inline Copy prompt; "Prefer the
  guided route?" with the orange Agent setup over a halftone) above the Console, CLI and API
  `DocCard`s (`ai ai-azion`, `ai ai-azion-cli`, `ai ai-azion-api`). Framework templates use the
  brand-colour icons (`ai-cor ai-react`). Do not substitute `DocPageHeader`, a `DocPrompt` or a
  `DocCard` with an overline for these.

## Which skill for which task

Structure and states first, polish last:

- **Structure:** `/webkit-ux-heuristics` (right component per moment) · `/webkit-ui-states` (loading,
  empty, error, async) · `/webkit-form` · `/webkit-create-surface` (page vs drawer) · `/webkit-errors`
  (where a failure goes) · `/webkit-tables` · `/webkit-lists` · `/webkit-navigation`
- **Layout:** `/webkit-layout` · **Words:** `/webkit-microcopy`
- **Foundation:** `/webkit-baseline-ui` (tokens, typography, spacing rhythm)
- **Cross-cutting:** `/webkit-theming-dark-mode` · `/webkit-data-viz` · `/webkit-genai` (AI chat
  and agent actions)
- **Polish:** `/webkit-motion-polish` → `/webkit-impeccable-polish`
- **Verify:** `/webkit-ui-verify` (real browser, both themes, several widths, axe)
- **Adopting WebKit in an existing app:** `/webkit-ds-adoption`

## How to find a component

Do not guess a component name or import path. Look it up.

1. Ask the webkit MCP. The server exposes tools grounded in the exact webkit version this project installed:
   - `suggest_component` — describe what you need in plain words; it returns the matching component(s).
   - Import/validation tools — confirm a subpath is real and get the canonical path.
2. No MCP? Read `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/llms.txt`. It links one Markdown page per block (`llms/blocks/<id>.md`: guidelines, variants, the primary SFC), per component (`llms/components/<name>.md`: props, events, slots, examples, accessibility, do and don't, with the same data as JSON in `<name>.json`) and per foundation (`llms/foundations/`: tokens, color, typography, spacing, motion, i18n, RTL, devices). `llms-full.txt` is every page in one file.
3. Read the catalog directly. `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/catalog.json` has an `imports` object; every key is a real published subpath (`button`, `empty-state`, `table`, ...). If a subpath is not a key there, it does not exist.

## App-level setup (`setup` in the catalog)

A few components need **one-time wiring in the app entry before first use** — the catalog entry (and `get_component` on the MCP) carries it in a `setup` field. When `setup` is non-null, apply it BEFORE emitting code that uses the component, and check whether the project already has it (do not duplicate).

- **Toast**: fire-from-anywhere (`toast.success('Saved')`) only renders if a region is mounted. Wire the service once in the entry — `import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'` and chain `.use(ToastPlugin)` onto `createApp()`; the plugin mounts the region automatically (options: `app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'top-right' })`). A manually mounted Toaster also counts — never add both blindly (the store keeps only the first region active, but one wiring is enough). `npx webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

- **Theme (light or dark)**: the theme is light by default. An app that is always dark sets `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` in `index.html` (`<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">`), so the first paint is dark; a toggle writes `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` (`'dark'` / `'light'`), and a `.dark` class on an ancestor works too. Every token switches with it — never add per-theme classes (`/webkit-theming-dark-mode`).

- **WebkitProvider (languages)**: mount it once at the app root with the user's locale. Every built-in string a component ships (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) then reads from the locale's catalog, and dates, numbers, file sizes and plurals format with `Intl` for that locale; `dir` follows the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). English is built in; Portuguese and Spanish are opt-in: import them from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR` and `@aziontech/webkit/locales/es` and pass them through `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), or the provider falls back to English and warns in development. With no provider every component falls back to English. A label prop you pass still wins over the catalog; `messages` renames a built-in string for the whole app. Import it as `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`.

```vue
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup>
  import { es } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/es'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'

  const catalogs = { 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    :locale="user.locale"
    :catalogs="catalogs"
  >
    <RouterView />
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

In your own components, `useLocale()` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-locale` returns the active `locale`, `dir`, `t(key, params)` and the `Intl` helpers (`formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList`, `formatFileSize`, `plural`), so your numbers and dates match WebKit's. `t` reads the provider's catalog; pass the English messages it should fall back to when no provider is mounted (`useLocale(en)`, with `en` from the same import).

## Must Have

- ✅ Flat import: `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`.
- ✅ PascalCase binding matching the last path segment: `@aziontech/webkit/mini-button` -> `MiniButton`.
- ✅ One `WebkitProvider` at the app root with the user's locale and the catalogs of every language the app offers.
- ✅ Color, spacing, radius, and typography from `@aziontech/theme` tokens (`var(--primary)`, `var(--spacing-md)`, `text-button-lg`).
- ✅ `import '@aziontech/theme'` and `import '@aziontech/icons'` once near the app entry (e.g. `src/main.ts`).
- ✅ The tree-shakeable `<name>-root` path (or specific sub-components) when you only need the root.
- ✅ Icons via the `@aziontech/icons` font: side-effect import once (`import '@aziontech/icons'`) + the icon CSS classes.
- ✅ Artwork and icon names from the published lists: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/foundations/` (`illustrations.md`, `diagrams.md`, `line-figures.md`, `brand-marks.md`, `icons.md`) or the MCP `list_assets` (`kind`, plus a `query` such as "ddos" or "delete"). Icon classes are `ai ai-<name>`, `pi pi-<name>`, and `ai-cor ai-<name>` for a colour brand icon.
- ✅ A webkit component reused instead of a hand-rolled or third-party equivalent.

## Must Not Have

- ❌ Category-prefixed import: `@aziontech/webkit/feedback/skeleton`.
- ❌ `/src/` or deep-internal imports: `@aziontech/webkit/src/components/...`.
- ❌ Barrel import: `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'` (no barrel exists).
- ❌ Binding that disagrees with the path: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chips'`.
- ❌ Hardcoded color: `#fff`, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)`, `text-[#1e40af]`, or raw Tailwind palette (`bg-blue-600`).
- ❌ Restyling a webkit component: `<Button class="bg-(--primary)">`, `:class`, `style` on its tag. Use its props; put your classes on your own wrapper or in its slots. Only layout utilities may sit on the tag: `w-full`, `h-full`, `max-w-*`, `min-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `min-h-*`, `flex-1`, `flex-auto`, `flex-initial`, `flex-none`, `grow`, `grow-*`, `basis-*`, `self-*`, `shrink-0`.
- ❌ An illustration, diagram, figure or mark name guessed from a file in `src/` or from the page title: an unknown illustration renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder, an unknown diagram or figure draws nothing.
- ❌ `ai-<name>-cor` or `ai ai-<name>-cor` for a colour icon: neither is a class. Use `ai-cor ai-<name>`.
- ❌ A default/namespace binding of `@aziontech/icons` (`import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`) — it is a font; import it for side effects only.
- ❌ A custom Button, Modal, Table, Tooltip, etc. when webkit ships one.
- ❌ Passing a translated label to every instance (`aria-label="Fechar"` on each close button) instead of setting the locale on `WebkitProvider`.

## Common Patterns

### Import + tokens

Tokens style **your own** markup around a component. The component keeps its own look and changes
it only through its props (`kind`, `size`); a class or style on its tag is restyling it (rule
`webkit-style-override`):

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <section
    class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md) rounded-(--shape-card) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-lg)"
  >
    <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">Changes apply to every domain.</p>
    <Button
      kind="primary"
      label="Save"
    />
  </section>
</template>
```

### Compound vs tree-shakeable root

`Table` (and other composition components) has two import shapes. Use the narrow one when you can:

```js
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root' // root only — smallest
import TableRow from '@aziontech/webkit/table-row' // one sub-component
import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table' // full compound: Table.Row, Table.Cell, ...
```

### Lazy-load a heavy overlay

```js
import { defineAsyncComponent } from 'vue'

const Dialog = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('@aziontech/webkit/dialog'))
```

### Docs pages: code samples and diagrams

- A code sample is `DocCodeGroup`. Set `language` on every sample; the block shows a label header
  with its readable name (Shell, JavaScript, JSON) by default.
- A **command** block holds only what the reader runs; its copy control copies exactly that (a
  leading `$ ` prompt is drawn but not copied). What the command prints goes in the sample's
  `output` field, drawn as a separate muted "Output" block with no copy control, or in prose. Never
  write output into the command as `# HTTP/2 200` (lint `webkit/no-output-in-command`, rule
  `webkit-code-samples`).
- A standalone printout (a deploy log) is `<DocCodeGroup kind="output" …>`, not a "Text" sample.
- A flow diagram in a docs column is `Diagram` with one `row`: in the docs column it stacks, the
  nodes are centred, connectors run through the centre of each node and an edge label sits on its
  line. Do not offset nodes or labels to fake that.

### Logos, badges and photos

Logos, compliance badges and illustrations ship in the package: import the file and pass the URL
(`import magalu from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/magalu-extended-color.svg'`, then
`logo: magalu`). Names follow `<brand>-<extended|symbol>-<color|mono|reversed>` (`extended` is the
wordmark, `symbol` the mark; `color` for light surfaces, `reversed` for dark ones, `mono` in one
ink); `catalog.json` lists every file under `imports` with `"kind": "asset"`. A client wall
(`ClientQuotes`, `LogoWall`) on the dark site shows each brand in colour: `-extended-color` where it
reads on black (GPA, Zoop, HeroSpark, Magalu), `-extended-reversed` where the colour logo has dark
lettering (Axur, Contabilizei, Dafiti, `gfg`); a one-ink registry `mark` only for a client with no
logo file. Photos, covers,
banners and clips are your content: pass URLs your app serves, or
`@aziontech/webkit/assets/placeholder-image.svg` / `placeholder-clip.webm` until you have them.
Never copy a root-relative `/marketing-components/…` or `/media/…` URL from azion.com or the docs
site: your app does not serve it (lint `webkit/no-root-relative-asset`).

### Large data and server rendering

- Pass the whole list: `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `LogView` and `CodeBlock` mount long lists (over 300 rows) in chunks as they scroll into view, and `Tree` renders collapsed children only when expanded. Do not page or slice the data yourself to make them fast.
- `Chart` takes 10k points per series; its hidden data table keeps an even sample of 1,000 rows, so turn on `tableView` when people need every value on screen.
- `PhoneInput` loads its flag sprite the first time the country list opens; the closed field costs no image download.
- Every block and example renders on the server (`renderToString`). Keep `window` and `document` out of `setup` in your own screens: read them in `onMounted`.

### App entry (styles + icons)

```ts
// src/main.ts
import '@aziontech/theme'
import '@aziontech/icons'
```

## Quality Checklist

Before you finish UI work in this project:

- [ ] Every webkit import is flat (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`), no category, no `/src/`, no barrel.
- [ ] Every binding is PascalCase of its subpath's last segment.
- [ ] No hardcoded colors — all color/spacing/typography via `@aziontech/theme` tokens.
- [ ] Icons imported individually; the whole set is never bulk-imported.
- [ ] Root-only usage takes the `-root` path; heavy overlays are lazy-loaded.
- [ ] No custom component reinvents something webkit already provides (checked via MCP or `catalog.json`).
- [ ] `@aziontech/theme` and `@aziontech/icons` are imported once at the app entry.
- [ ] `WebkitProvider` wraps the app once with the user's locale, and `catalogs` registers every non-English language the app offers.

## Part B — using a webkit component in your project

Install the ESLint plugin and enable the `recommended` preset — **every rule is `error`**, so
off-pattern usage fails your lint.

```js
// eslint.config.js
import webkit from '@aziontech/webkit/eslint-plugin'
export default [...webkit.configs.recommended]
```

| Do this                   | ❌ Avoid                                                | ✅ Do                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Import**                | `import { Button } from '@aziontech/webkit'`            | `import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'`          |
| **No internal / typo**    | `@aziontech/webkit/src/…` · `…/buton`                   | `@aziontech/webkit/button`                               |
| **Tree-shaking**          | `import Table` (compound) when you only render the root | `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`   |
| **Don't override styles** | `<Button class="p-8" />`                                | compose inside its slots, or use a `styleSeam` component |
| **No deprecated**         | importing a deprecated component                        | the suggested replacement                                |
| **Tokens, not colors**    | `class="text-[#fff]"`                                   | `class="text-(--text-default)"`                          |
| **Icons**                 | `import Icons from '@aziontech/icons'`                  | `import '@aziontech/icons'` (side-effect)                |

**Discover the API before you write it:** the webkit MCP server (`npx webkit-mcp`, wired
into `.mcp.json` by `init`) answers
`list_components`, `get_component`, `list_tokens`, `suggest_component`, `get_best_practices`,
and `validate_usage` — so an AI (or you) gets the right import / token / prop _before_ the lint
has to reject the wrong one.

<!-- blocks/headers/auth-header.md -->

# AuthHeader (`headers/auth-header`)

> The console bar for the signed-out and onboarding screens: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the first-run steps.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/headers/auth-header/auth-header.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("headers/auth-header")`
- Components: Brand, Button, GlobalHeader
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

auth header; signed-out header; login page header; onboarding header; public console header; header without navigation; logged-out top bar; cabeçalho de login; cabeçalho deslogado; barra do topo sem navegação

The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

## When to use

- Above the auth card on sign in, sign up, reset password and MFA screens (`platform/auth`).
- Above the onboarding steps that run before the organization exists (`platform/account/onboarding-form`).

## When not to use

- Any page with a session: use `headers/resource-header` inside the console shell (`shells/console`), or `headers/creation-header` for a create, edit or deploy flow.
- Documentation pages: use `headers/docs-header`. Marketing pages: use `headers/site-header`.

## Building blocks

- A. Bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)
- B. Brand — `Brand` (required)
- C. Documentation — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/headers/auth-header.md](blocks/headers/auth-header.md).

## Do

- Keep the bar identical across every signed-out step so the user knows they are still in the same flow.
- Let the page under it own the heading and the primary action (the auth card).

## Don't

- Don't add an avatar, a menu or a search: a control that implies a session reads as broken when there is none.
- Don't put the Sign in or Sign up switch in the bar; it lives in the card as a link.

## Copy

- **Documentation button:** one noun, sentence case, no icon-only variant: `Documentation`.
- **Brand link label:** names the destination: `Azion home`.

## Accessibility

- The `GlobalHeader` is a landmark with its own label (`Console`); keep one per page.
- The brand is a link with an accessible name, not a decorative image.
- Tab order is brand, then Documentation; nothing else in the bar takes focus.

## States

- Default: the only state; the bar never changes between signed-out steps.

# ActivityHistory (`platform/account/activity-history`)

> The account's audit log: a `PageHeader` with Documentation over one controls row (`PropertyFilter` on event, category, user and IP address; a `DateRangePicker` for the period, last 30 days by default; Refresh, Downloa…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/account/activity-history/activity-history.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/activity-history")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, CopyButton, DateRangePicker, EmptyState, IconButton, PageHeader, PropertyFilter, Table, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

activity history; audit log; audit trail; account activity; security log; who did what; user activity; event history; histórico de atividades; log de auditoria; trilha de auditoria; atividade da conta

The account's audit log. An admin or a security reviewer answers "who did this, from where, and when": a token that was revoked, a role that changed, a sign-in that failed, a plan that was upgraded. They narrow the log by period, category, person and address, read the newest events first, copy an IP address into another tool, and export what they found. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The account or organisation audit log: sign-ins, security changes, member and role changes, billing changes, deploys.
- Any append-only list of events people search by who, what, where and when.

## When not to use

- Request logs or metrics explored over time with a chart: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- The deploy history of one resource: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs` or the details page's history tab.
- A short "recent activity" card on a dashboard: use `Item` rows in a `Card` and link here with View all.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Period — `DateRangePicker` (required)
- D. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- E. Event table — `Card`, `Table`, `CopyButton`, `useCollection` (required)
- F. No match and empty period — `EmptyState` (required)
- G. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/activity-history.md](blocks/platform/account/activity-history.md).

## Do

- Write each event as a past-tense sentence with the object's name: `Revoked personal token “Nightly export”`.
- Show the newest first and keep the exact time on the tooltip.
- Keep IP addresses left to right and copyable.
- Keep the period and the filters in the controls row, the export last but one, preferences last.

## Don't

- Don't let anyone edit or delete an event from this page.
- Don't put the period in the property filter, or show a period with no events as an error.
- Don't truncate the event sentence without the full text on the row.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Activity history`. **Filter:** `Filter activity`. **Period:** `Activity period`.
- **Categories:** `Sign-in`, `Security`, `Users`, `Billing`, `Deploy`.
- **Empty period:** `No activity in this period`, then `Nothing happened in the account in the selected period. Pick a longer period to see older events.` and `Show the last 30 days`.
- **No match:** `No matching events`, `No event in this period matches these filters.`, `Clear filters`.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`; the table is named `Activity history`.
- The filter and the period picker carry `aria-label`s; icon buttons have names that match their tooltips.
- Category is text in a tag, never colour alone; the relative date has the exact time on its tooltip.
- User and IP cells keep their own direction (`dir="auto"`, `dir="ltr"`) inside a right-to-left page.

## States

- Default: ten events over three weeks, the last 30 days selected, with filter, period, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and paging wired.
- Empty: the last 15 minutes hold no event; a flush empty state offers the last 30 days.
- Loading: the first load; the controls and the table's loading rows.
- Failed: the log did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list page this one follows.
- `platform/account/tokens` and `platform/account/team-permissions` — the screens whose changes are logged here.
- `platform/view/split-view` — events over time with a chart and a document pane.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/account/activity-history.md](blocks/platform/account/activity-history.md), `get_pattern("platform/account/activity-history", { variant })`.

- Toasts — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer.md](blocks/platform/account/change-plan-drawer.md).

## Do

- Disable every field and secondary action while the upgrade submits, and release the lock when it ends, on success and on failure.
- Show the total and the period it is billed for before the Upgrade button.
- Close both drawers once the upgrade succeeds.

## Don't

- Don't let the current plan's action do anything; it is disabled and labelled `Current plan`.
- Don't ask for the card number again when one is on file; offer Change.
- Don't toast a declined card; it is scoped to the Payment method section.

- **Plan actions:** a verb and the destination: `Continue with Pro`, `Contact sales`, `Current plan`.

- **Field labels:** 1 to 3 words, sentence case, no parentheses; put formats in the description: `Expiration date` with `Month and year, as MM/YY.`, `Security code` with `3 or 4 digits on the back.`, `Address line 2` with `Optional. Apartment, suite or floor.`
- **Charge rows:** `Next charge`, `Subtotal`, `Yearly discount`, `Total`.
- **Card on file:** `Ending in 8888`.
- **Declined card:** `The card was declined, so the account is still on Free. Check the number or use another card, then select Upgrade again.`
- **Unscoped failure:** a toast with Retry: `The upgrade failed. The account is still on Free.`, described by `The payment service did not answer. Your entries are kept.`
- **Success:** `The account was upgraded to Pro.`

- Each drawer is a dialog labelled by its title; focus moves into it on open and returns to the trigger on close, including when the stacked drawer closes.
- Each fieldset has a visually hidden legend (`Payment method`, `Address information`).
- After a failed Update or Upgrade, focus moves to the first field in error; after a decline, to the card number.
- The billing period toggle is labelled; a price change is visible text, not color only.

## States

- Default: the plan drawer open on an account that is on Free, Yearly selected. In the upgrade drawer, a new card ending in 0002 is declined and one ending in 0119 makes the payment service fail, so both failure paths can be walked.
- Checkout: the Upgrade to Pro drawer open on its own, as the checkout step: the charge card adds Due today and a note that taxes come from the billing address and the plan renews on the upgrade day; under the address a required `Checkbox` accepts the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy (each a `Link` in a new tab). Upgrade without it shows `Accept the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy to upgrade.` on the field and focuses the checkbox; the card and service failures work as in the primary.

- `platform/account/payment-method-card` — the Payment method card on its own, with its editing state.

- `platform/account/profile` — the account settings layout Billing shares.

- D. Details panel — `Card`, `Tabs`, `Alert`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Move — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Select` (required)

- Keep selection per row: selecting a group does not select its workspaces; Delete then says how many are inside.
- Open the destination after a move so the moved rows are visible.
- Say what moves with a resource, and what happens to its inherited bindings, before the move.
- Keep deleted resources recoverable and link to where they wait.

## Don't

- Don't offer a resource, or anything inside it, as its own new parent.
- Don't hide the chevron behind hover; leaves keep a blank space of the same width so names align.
- Don't put a separate expand button in the tab order; the row is the tab stop and Arrow Right and Arrow Left open and close it.
- Don't delete a branch without counting what is inside it.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Manage resources`. **Create:** `Create workspace`, `Create group`.
- **Bulk:** `Move`, `Labels`, `Delete`; row menu `View details`, `Move`, `Edit labels`, `Delete`.
- **Panel:** `No resource selected`, `1 resource selected`; `Select a resource to see its role bindings and labels.`; `Select a single resource to see its role bindings.`; `This resource has no labels.`
- **Toasts:** `2 resources moved to Digital services.`; `3 resources scheduled for deletion.` with `They stay in Resources pending deletion for 30 days.`; `Labels updated on 1 resource.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The table is a `treegrid` labelled by the Resources heading. Rows carry `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded` when they have children, and `aria-selected` when selected.
- One row is in the tab order. Arrow Up and Arrow Down move between rows, Home and End go to the first and last, Arrow Right opens a row or moves into it, Arrow Left closes it or goes to its parent (mirrored right to left), Enter toggles it and Space selects it. Tab reaches the checkbox, ID copy and row menu of the focused row.
- The chevron is pointer-only and hidden from assistive technology; the row's `aria-expanded` is the state.
- The action row is a `role="group"` named `Resource actions` (plain Tab order, no arrow-key toolbar); disabled bulk buttons stay visible so the actions are discoverable.
- The details heading is a polite live region, so a change of selection is announced.
- Dialogs trap focus and return it to the button that opened them.

## States

- Default: two organizations, three groups and six workspaces; the first organization and its first group open, nothing selected, and every action wired.
- Selected: one workspace selected; bulk actions enabled and the details panel filled.
- Empty: no resource; an empty state with Create workspace.
- Loading: the first load; the table's loading rows.
- Failed: the hierarchy did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `platform/account/team-permissions` — what a role binding grants.
- `platform/account/users` — who the members of a binding are.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the flat list page this one extends with tree rows.
- `platform/view/file-browser` — moving objects between folders with the same Move dialog pattern.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Selected` · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/account/manage-resources.md](blocks/platform/account/manage-resources.md), `get_pattern("platform/account/manage-resources", { variant })`.

# MfaManagement (`platform/account/mfa-management`)

- Surface: product

- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/mfa-management")`

## Asked as

mfa management; multi-factor authentication; two-factor authentication; 2fa; require mfa; reset mfa; security settings; gerenciar mfa; autenticação multifator; exigir mfa; redefinir mfa

Multi-factor authentication for a whole account. An admin sees who signs in with a second factor and who uses a password only, requires MFA for everyone, reminds the people who have not set it up, and resets the factor of someone who lost their device. Setting up a factor and the sign-in challenge are `platform/auth` (`MfaSetup`, `MfaChallenge`); this page manages them for other people. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- An account or organisation page where admins enforce or audit multi-factor authentication.
- Helping a person who lost the device that holds their factor.

## When not to use

- A person setting up their own factor: use `platform/auth#MfaSetup`.
- The code prompt at sign-in: use `platform/auth#MfaChallenge`.
- Inviting or removing people: use `platform/account/users`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Require MFA — `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Switch`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- C. Password-only warning — `Alert` (conditional)
- D. People table — `Input`, `Table`, `Avatar`, `useCollection` (required)
- E. Row actions — `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- F. Load failure and outcomes — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/mfa-management.md](blocks/platform/account/mfa-management.md).

## Do

- Name who is affected before requiring MFA.
- Keep people without a factor visible and marked, with a way to remind them.
- Say what a reset does (password only until they set it up again) before confirming it.

## Don't

- Don't show or copy anyone's secret or recovery codes here; only the owner of the factor sees them.
- Don't reset without a confirmation; it weakens one person's sign-in.
- Don't make the warning color the only signal; the Alert and the status say it in words.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Multi-factor authentication`. **Setting:** `Require MFA`.
- **Statuses:** `Enabled`, `Not set up`. **Actions:** `Reset MFA`, `Send setup reminder`.
- **Toasts:** `MFA is now required.`, `MFA is optional again.`, `MFA reset for Jordan Reyes.`, `Reminder sent to priya.nair@example.com.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The Switch is named Require MFA and the setting description explains the effect.
- The row menu is named `Actions for <person>`; status is text, not color.
- Both confirmations are dialogs that return focus to their trigger.

## States

- Default: five people, three with a factor, MFA optional, the warning shown.
- Required: MFA required for the account.
- Loading: the first load.
- Failed: the list did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `platform/auth` — `MfaSetup` and `MfaChallenge`, the person's own side.

Who can do what in the account. An admin keeps one team per role (Administrators, Developers, Security, Finance), sees what each grants and how many people it covers, and creates or edits a team by ticking View and Edit per resource in one matrix. People get permissions only through teams; nothing is granted per person, so the list of teams is the whole access model. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Any grant of view and edit rights over a fixed list of resources.

## When not to use

- Inviting people or assigning them to teams: a users list with a team `MultiSelect` per person.
- Credentials that act as one person: use `platform/account/tokens`.
- Feature flags or plan entitlements: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search and refresh — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Team table — `Card`, `Table`, `Avatar`, `useCollection` (required)
- D. Row actions — `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- E. No match and empty — `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- G. Members — `Button`, `Avatar`, `IconButton` (EditTeam)
- H. Delete team and save — `ConfirmDialog`, `Button` (EditTeam)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/team-permissions.md](blocks/platform/account/team-permissions.md).

## Do

- Grant through teams only, and say so in the page description.
- In the matrix, make Edit imply View: checking Edit checks View, clearing View clears Edit.
- Give each area a group checkbox that is indeterminate when partly checked.
- Show how many permissions are selected out of the total while editing.
- Say how many people lose access before a team is deleted.

## Don't

- Don't list permissions as a long paragraph in the table; use `Table.CellTags` with `+N`.
- Don't offer an Edit checkbox for a resource that has no edit action; show a dash with a hidden "Not available".
- Don't save a team with no permission; say so above the matrix.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Teams and permissions`. **Create:** `Create Team`; the page title is `Create Team`, the save button `Create`.
- **Permissions:** `View <Resource>`, `Edit <Resource>`; the whole set reads `All permissions`.
- **Matrix hint:** `What this team can see and change. 3 of 15 selected.`
- **Errors:** `This field is required.` under Name; `Select at least one permission.` above the matrix.
- **Edit:** the page title is `Edit Team`, the save button `Save changes`; `Team "Developers" updated.` after saving.
- **Members:** `Add member`, `Search users of this account`, `Remove <name>`; `Choose a user to add.` when Add is pressed with nothing chosen.
- **Delete:** `Delete team`; `The 12 members of “Developers” lose the permissions it grants, unless another team grants them.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The matrix is a real `table` with a caption, column headers View and Edit, one `tbody` per area whose first row is a `rowgroup` header holding the area's checkbox, and a row header per resource.
- Each matrix checkbox is named `View <Resource>` or `Edit <Resource>`; the area checkbox is named by its label and reports mixed when partly checked.
- After a failed save, focus moves to the name field or to the permissions filter.
- Members are a list named `Members`; after Remove, focus moves to the next member's Remove button, or to Add member when the list is empty.
- Table name links say where they go on their tooltip; the row menu is named `Actions for <team>`.

## States

- Default: five teams (one with every permission, one inactive with no members) with search, refresh, sorting, row menus, duplicate and delete wired.
- CreateTeam: the create page with three permissions preselected; the matrix filter, Select all, Clear, Edit-implies-View, required name and at-least-one-permission errors, and a success toast on Create. Cancel and Create sit in a `SaveBar kind="centered"`, a raised card centred over the bottom of the scroll region; the Edit Team page keeps the full-width `plain` bar.
- EditTeam: a saved team with three members and six permissions; add and remove members, Discard, Save changes with a success toast, Delete team behind a `ConfirmDialog`.
- Empty: no team yet; the heading and an empty state with Create Team.
- Loading: the first load; the search row and the table's loading rows.
- Failed: the teams did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

personal tokens; personal access tokens; api tokens; api keys; access tokens; create token; revoke token; copy token once; token expiration; tokens pessoais; token de acesso; chaves de api; criar token; revogar token

The Personal tokens page of the account settings. A person creates a token for a script, a CI job or the CLI, copies its secret the one time it is shown, sees which tokens are still alive and when each expires or was last used, and revokes one that leaked or is no longer needed. The secret never comes back: the list shows only the name, status and dates, and a lost secret means a new token. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Credentials a person creates for themselves to call the API: personal tokens, API keys, deploy keys.
- Any secret the server returns once: the same reveal dialog (warning, masked value, copy) applies.

## When not to use

- Team or service credentials with roles and scopes managed by an admin: start from `platform/account/team-permissions` and add a scope field to the create drawer.
- Secrets the product stores and shows again (environment variables): use `platform/edit/attribute-editor` with masked values.
- A single key shown on a resource's details page: use `CopyButton` beside the value in `platform/detail/details-page`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search and refresh — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Token table — `Card`, `Table`, `useCollection` (required)
- D. Row actions — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. No match and empty — `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Load failure — `Alert` (conditional)
- G. Create drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- H. Fields — `Field`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `HelperText` (required)
- I. One-time reveal — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `PasswordInput`, `CopyButton` (required)
- J. Confirmations and outcomes — `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/tokens.md](blocks/platform/account/tokens.md).

## Do

- Show the secret once, masked by default, with a copy button and a warning that says it will not be shown again.
- Say the exact expiry date while the person picks the duration.
- Warn in the Status column a week before a token expires.
- Revoke behind a confirmation that names the token and what breaks.

## Don't

- Don't show a secret, or part of one, in the list.
- Don't let a token be edited or extended; create a new one.
- Don't offer Delete on a live token; revoke it first.
- Don't toast the reveal; the secret belongs in the dialog, where it can be copied.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Personal tokens`. **Create:** `Create Personal Token` on the page, `Create personal token` as the drawer title, `Create` in the footer.
- **Status:** `Active`, `Expires in 3 days`, `Expired`, `Revoked`. **Last used:** relative time, or `Never used`.
- **Reveal:** title `Copy your new token`; warning `Copy the token and store it somewhere safe, such as a secret manager. After you close this dialog, it cannot be shown again; create a new one if it is lost.`
- **Revoke:** title `Revoke token`; description `Scripts and tools that use “<name>” stop working right away. You cannot undo this.`; button `Revoke token`; toast `Token “<name>” revoked. Requests that use it are now refused.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- No `main` of its own (the layout's is the only one); the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`.
- The search `Input` and every icon-only button carry an `aria-label`; the row menu is named `Actions for <token>`.
- The drawer and the dialogs trap focus, are named by their titles and return focus to their trigger; the first invalid field takes focus after Create.
- The reveal labels the secret field `Token`; the copy result is announced in a polite status region.

## States

- Default: four tokens (active, expiring in 5 days, expired, revoked) with search, refresh, sorting, row menus, the create drawer, the reveal, revoke and delete wired.
- Empty: no token; the heading and a flush empty state with Create Personal Token.
- Loading: the first load; search row and the table's loading rows.
- Failed: the list did not load; a danger Alert with Retry replaces the table.
- Created: the one-time reveal dialog open after Create.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list page this one follows.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the drawer pattern behind Create.
- `platform/account/team-permissions` — who can do what; tokens act with the creator's permissions.
- `platform/account/activity-history` — where token creation and revocation are audited.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty` · `Loading` · `Failed` · `Created`. Code: [blocks/platform/account/tokens.md](blocks/platform/account/tokens.md), `get_pattern("platform/account/tokens", { variant })`.

# Users (`platform/account/users`)

> The people who can sign in to an account.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/account/users/users.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/account/users")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, Input, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Table, Tag, Toast, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

users; users management; invite user; invite teammates; members; account members; assign teams; resend invitation; remove user; usuários; gerenciar usuários; convidar usuário; membros da conta; atribuir times

Who can sign in to the account, and through which teams. An admin invites a teammate by email, chooses their teams, sees who has not accepted yet, resends or cancels an invitation, moves a person between teams and removes people who left. Permissions come only from teams (`platform/account/team-permissions`), so this page assigns teams; it never grants a permission to a person. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Inviting people to an account or organisation and assigning them to teams or roles.
- Following pending invitations: resend or cancel.
- Removing a person's access.

## When not to use

- Defining what a team can do: use `platform/account/team-permissions`.
- Credentials that act as a person: use `platform/account/tokens`.
- Who turned on multi-factor authentication: use `platform/account/mfa-management`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search — `Input` (required)
- C. Users table — `Card`, `Table`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `useCollection` (required)
- D. Teams per person — `MultiSelect`, `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Row actions — `Table`, `DropdownMenu`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)
- F. Invite drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field`, `Input`, `MultiSelect`, `Button` (required)
- G. Only the owner, no match and load failure — `EmptyState`, `Alert` (conditional)
- Outcomes — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/account/users.md](blocks/platform/account/users.md).

## Do

- Show pending invitations in the same list, marked Invited, with Resend and Cancel.
- Name the teams in the invitation toast and in every team change, and offer Undo for a team change.
- Say what stays when a person is removed (their teams and the resources they created).
- Keep the owner's row visible, with its controls locked and the reason on the tooltip.

## Don't

- Don't grant a permission to one person here; teams are the only way.
- Don't apply an invitation without a team silently; a person with no team gets no access, so the form asks for one.
- Don't hide the email of an invited person; it is the only name they have until they accept.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Users`. **Action:** `Invite User`; the drawer title `Invite User`, the submit `Send invitation`.
- **Statuses:** `Active`, `Invited`, `Inactive`; **Last active** for an invitation: `Not signed in yet`.
- **Errors:** `Enter the email address to invite.`, `Enter an email address like name@example.com.`, `This person is already in the account.`, `Choose at least one team, or they get no access.`
- **Toasts:** `Invitation sent to sam.okafor@example.com.`, `Teams updated for Priya Nair.`, `Invitation sent again to sam.okafor@example.com.`, `Jordan Reyes removed from the account.`
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each Teams control is named `Teams of <person>`; the row menu is named `Actions for <person>`.
- The invite form is a `form` named Invite User; each `Field` ties its label, description and error to the control, and `Field.Error` is announced when it appears.
- After a failed Send, focus moves to the first invalid control.
- The owner's locked controls are disabled and the reason is on the tooltip, not only in color.

## States

- Default: six people (the owner, four active or inactive, one invited) with search, inline team changes, resend, cancel and remove wired.
- Invite: the invite drawer open.
- OnlyOwner: the owner alone and the invite empty state.
- Loading: the first load.
- Failed: the list did not load; a danger Alert with Retry.

## Related

- `platform/account/team-permissions` — what each team can do.
- `platform/account/mfa-management` — who has multi-factor authentication on.
- `platform/account/activity-history` — where invitations and removals are audited.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the error pattern the invite form follows.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Invite` · `OnlyOwner` · `Loading` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/account/users.md](blocks/platform/account/users.md), `get_pattern("platform/account/users", { variant })`.

# AiActionApproval (`platform/ai/ai-action-approval`)

> A user-authorized action inside a generative AI conversation: the reader asks the assistant to deploy, the assistant records the read-only call it made (`ToolCall`), explains in `StreamingResponse` and proposes the de…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval/ai-action-approval.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-action-approval")`
- Components: ActionConfirmation, ChatMessage, CodeBlock, Conversation, CopyButton, PromptInput, StreamingResponse, ToolCall
- Skills: `webkit-genai`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

ai action approval; approve ai action; user authorized action; agent asks permission; human in the loop; tool call approval; confirm agent command; allow tool; aprovar ação da ia; autorizar ação do agente; confirmar comando; aprobar acción de la ia

The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The assistant is about to call a tool or run a command with side effects: deploy, purge, change a rule, delete.
- A one-time decision about a consequential action, made inside the conversation.
- An irreversible action: add a typed confirmation to the card.

## When not to use

- Read-only calls (listing, reading metrics): record them with `ToolCall` and continue without asking.
- Tools the reader already allowed for this conversation: record the call, do not ask again.
- A destructive action the reader started from the UI, not the assistant: use `ConfirmDialog` (see `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`).
- Several fields to fill before acting: link to the create or edit page; the card only approves or denies.

## Building blocks

- A. Conversation frame — `Conversation`, `PromptInput`
- B. Request — `ChatMessage`
- C. What the assistant checked — `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`
- D. Authorization card — `ActionConfirmation`, `CodeBlock`
- E. The action running — `ToolCall`
- F. Outcome — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md).

## Do

- Show exactly what will run, with the real identifiers.
- Label the approve button with the verb of the title.
- Dismiss the buttons as soon as the reader decides and show the outcome in text.
- Acknowledge a denial and say nothing ran.
- Expire a request the reader leaves undecided and say nothing ran.
- Require typing the resource name before an irreversible action.

## Don't

- Don't run anything before Approve.
- Don't focus or pre-select Approve, and don't trap focus in the card; it is part of the conversation, not a dialog.
- Don't ask again for a tool the reader allowed for this conversation.
- Don't hide the command behind a summary; show it.
- Don't show secrets or tokens in the command or the tool details.

## Copy

- **Title:** a question naming the action, with the command or tool in code: ``Allow `azion deploy --env production`?``, "Delete the domain `old.example.com`?".
- **Description:** what changes and what stays, e.g. "Deploys build `b-4821` of storefront to production. The current version stays available for rollback."
- **Buttons:** Deny and the verb of the title (Deploy, Delete); "Approve" only for a generic tool call.
- **Typed confirmation:** "Type old.example.com to confirm" (built in).
- **Outcomes:** Approved, Denied, Request expired (built in).
- **Assistant after a denial:** "Got it, nothing was deployed."; **after expiry:** "This request expired. Nothing was deployed."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", present tense.

## Accessibility

- The card is a group named by its title and described by its description; it does not trap or take focus.
- Outcomes are text announced through a polite live region; status color is never the only signal.
- Tool calls announce their status changes (Running, Completed, Failed) through `StatusIndicator`.
- The typed confirmation has a visible label; Approve is disabled until it matches.
- Keyboard order: request, tool calls, response text, command, phrase field, Deny, approve.

## States

- Pending: the deployment waiting for Deny or Deploy; approving runs the deployment to completion.
- Irreversible: a domain deletion that needs the domain name typed before Delete enables.
- Approved: the card approved, the deployment completed and the assistant's report.
- Denied: the card denied, the call recorded as denied and the assistant's acknowledgement.
- Expired: the request expired and the assistant says nothing ran.

## Related

- `platform/ai/ai-chat` — the conversation this card lives in.
- `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same flow in a drawer over a resource page.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — confirming a destructive action the reader started.
- `skills/webkit-genai` — when to ask, what to show and how to record the outcome.

## Variants

`Pending` (primary) · `Irreversible` · `Approved` · `Denied` · `Expired`. Code: [blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-action-approval.md), `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-action-approval", { variant })`.

# AiChat (`platform/ai/ai-chat`)

> The full-page generative AI assistant: a header with the assistant's name, a Preview `Tag` and New chat; before the first message an `EmptyState` that says what the assistant knows, over vertical support prompts from…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat/ai-chat.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat")`
- Components: ArtifactCanvas, ArtifactPreview, Button, ChatMessage, CodeBlock, Conversation, CopyButton, Drawer, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, IconButton, PromptInput, Reasoning, Resizable, Sources, StreamingResponse, SuggestionGroup, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-genai`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

ai chat; ai assistant; chatbot; copilot; chat with ai; generative ai chat; assistant page; ask ai; llm chat; conversational ui; prompt and response; streaming response; chat de ia; assistente de ia; assistente virtual; conversa com ia; chat con ia; asistente de ia; artifact; artifact canvas; generated file; code canvas; canvas de artefato; artefato gerado

A full page where a person talks with the generative AI assistant about their account: they ask in their own words, watch the response arrive, check where it came from, and keep going with a follow-up or a new question. The page is the conversation; everything else (header, composer) stays still while only the log scrolls. Use it as the assistant's home; on a resource page, open the same conversation in a drawer with `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: it fills the layout's content region (`grow basis-0 min-h-0`, never `h-dvh`), so only the log scrolls, and the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A dedicated assistant page (Console → AI assistant) where the conversation is the main task.
- Open-ended questions across the whole account: how-to, troubleshooting, explaining settings or metrics.
- A conversation the reader expects to scroll back through and continue.

## When not to use

- Help about the page the reader is on, next to their work: use `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`.
- The assistant proposes an action that changes the account: add `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` to the conversation, never run it from a response.
- One generated paragraph in a page (a summary of a chart): render `StreamingResponse` in place, no chat.
- Searching documentation by keyword: a search field and results list are faster than a conversation.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `Tag`, `Button`
- B. Empty state — `EmptyState`, `SuggestionGroup`
- C. Message log — `Conversation`
- D. Prompt — `ChatMessage`
- E. Response — `ChatMessage`, `Reasoning`, `StreamingResponse`
- F. Sources — `Sources`
- G. Response actions — `ChatMessage`, `CopyButton`, `IconButton`
- H. Follow-up questions — `SuggestionGroup`
- I. Composer — `PromptInput`
- J. Artifact canvas — `ChatMessage`, `PromptInput` (Artifact)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md).

## Do

- Show the loading text only after a second; a response that arrives faster streams directly.
- Keep actions visible on every complete response, not on hover.
- Cite sources inline with numbers and list them under the response.
- Let the reader stop a response and keep what streamed, marked as stopped.
- Keep the composer usable while a response streams so the reader can draft the next prompt.
- Return focus to the composer when a response finishes.

## Don't

- Don't auto-scroll while the reader is reading an older message.
- Don't render model output as HTML; `StreamingResponse` renders Markdown as elements only.
- Don't show actions or feedback on a response that is still loading or streaming.
- Don't use the feedback thumbs for anything but the AI response.
- Don't put more than five support prompts or three follow-ups on screen.
- Don't call the assistant by a person's name or make it apologize; state what happened.

## Copy

- **Title of the page:** `AI assistant`; the Preview tag while in preview.
- **Empty state:** a question the reader would ask themselves, e.g. "How can I help with your Azion account?", and one sentence on what the assistant can read.
- **Support prompts and follow-ups:** written as the reader would ask, under 72 characters, e.g. "How do I purge the cache of one URL?".
- **Placeholder:** `Ask a question`, no end punctuation.
- **Disclaimer (hint):** "The AI assistant can make mistakes. Check important information before you act on it."
- **Loading:** `Generating a response` (built in); `Loading <what>` when fetching data.
- **Error:** what happened, in one sentence, e.g. "The connection was interrupted before the response finished.", with Try again.
- **Stopped:** "You stopped this response."
- **Feedback:** Helpful, Not helpful, Feedback submitted (built in).
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, "select" not "click", "response" not "answer", no "please".

## Accessibility

- The log is a named `role="log"` whose own live behavior is off; a polite live region reads each finished response once, with its author.
- Each message is an `article` named by author and time; avatars are hidden from assistive tech because the author line names the author.
- Responses are `aria-busy` while loading or streaming; the caret is hidden.
- The composer is named Prompt, described by its counter and disclaimer; Enter submits and an IME composition never does.
- Feedback thumbs are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`, and the submitted state is a status message.
- Keyboard order: header, log (focusable to scroll), each message's links and actions, follow-ups, composer.
- Alignment never carries meaning alone: every message has its author line.

## States

- Empty: the assistant before the first message, with the empty state and four support prompts; selecting one runs a full response.
- Streaming: a response arriving with its caret and Stop in the composer, then sources, actions and follow-ups.
- Error: a failed response with its partial text, the error line and Try again.
- Artifact: two turns that wrote top-orders.sql in two versions, the canvas open beside them on version 2; a follow-up streams version 3 into it.
- LongThread: six earlier turns that overflow the log, opened on the newest response.

## Related

- `artifact-canvas` — the side panel of the Artifact variant; `artifact-preview` — its card in the message.
- `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer` — the same conversation in a drawer over a resource page.
- `platform/ai/ai-action-approval` — when a response proposes a change the reader must authorize.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — long-running work outside a conversation.
- `skills/webkit-genai` — the rules this block follows: loading stages, streaming, citations, feedback, authorization.

## Variants

`Empty` (primary) · `Streaming` · `Error` · `LongThread` · `Artifact`. Code: [blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md](blocks/platform/ai/ai-chat.md), `get_pattern("platform/ai/ai-chat", { variant })`.

# Auth (`platform/auth`)

> The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `GlobalHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/auth/auth.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/auth")`
- Components: Alert, Brand, Button, Card, CopyButton, Field, GlobalHeader, HelperText, IconButton, Input, OtpInput, PageHeader, PasswordInput, PasswordRequirements, QrCode, Separator, Tag, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

login; log in; sign in; signin; login page; authentication; auth; forgot password; reset password; new password; entrar; tela de login; acessar conta; esqueci a senha; redefinir senha; signup; sign up; register; registration; create account; new account; free account; cadastro; cadastrar; criar conta; tela de cadastro; registrar; check inbox; check your email; verify email; email verification; confirm email; verification sent; resend email; verificar e-mail; confirmar e-mail; confira seu e-mail; session expired; auth errors; sessão expirada; erro de login; mfa; multi-factor authentication; two-factor authentication; 2fa; authenticator app; one-time code; verification code; totp; recovery code; autenticação em dois fatores; autenticação multifator; código de verificação; código de autenticação

The signed-out screens of a platform app: sign in, sign up, reset password and check your inbox, frame included. The user has one job here, to get into their account, and one object on the page to do it with: a single card under the signed-out bar. Every step of the flow (`email`, `password`, `reset`, `sent`, `new-password`) swaps the contents of that card in place, and every answer the server gives, success included, lands in one `Alert` inside it. Auth never toasts. It is a full page with its own focused header: the app routes it outside `ConsoleLayout`, never into the layout's default slot.

## When to use

- `/login`, `/signup` and `/signup/verify`, and the reset-password link the user follows from their inbox.
- Re-entering after a session expired: the same card opens on the password step with the address already filled.
- Any signed-out step that asks for credentials (sign in, MFA, set a new password).

## When not to use

- First-run steps after the account exists (profile, plan, organization): use `platform/account/onboarding-form`.
- Changing the password or email of a signed-in user: use `platform/account/profile`.
- Signing out an expired session over a console page: the shell wire is `platform/states/page-wires` (SessionWire); this block is where it lands.
- Any signed-in form: use `platform/states/form-validation` for the submit states and `platform/settings/settings-form` for settings.

## Building blocks

- A. Signed-out bar — `GlobalHeader` (required)
- B. Product mark — `Brand` (required)
- C. Actions — `Button` (required)
- D. The card — `Card` (required)
- E. Card notice — `Alert` (conditional)
- F. Social divider — `Separator` (email step only)
- G. Field label — `Field`, `Field.Label` (required)
- H. Email — `Input` (required)
- I. Field message — `HelperText` (conditional)
- J. Step hint — `Tooltip` (password and reset steps)
- K. Back control — `IconButton` (password and reset steps)
- L. Password field — `Field` (password and new-password steps)
- M. Password — `PasswordInput` (password and new-password steps)
- N. Password rules — `PasswordRequirements` (new-password step, sign up)
- O. Last used — `Tag` (email step only)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/auth.md](blocks/platform/auth.md).

## Do

- Keep one card and one notice slot for the whole flow; swap the step body, not the page.
- Validate on submit only, then clear a field's error as the user types in it.
- After a 401, put the message above both fields, clear the password and move focus back to it.
- Keep the credentials after a 503, a 500 or a timeout; Retry re-sends the same request.
- Carry the email between steps (sign in to reset, reset back to sign in) so the user never types it twice.
- Release the in-flight lock on every outcome so Retry can run again.

- On a code screen, put the code in one `OtpInput` (autofill reads `autocomplete="one-time-code"`), submit on `complete`, and keep a Verify button.
- Give every QR code a typed alternative: the setup key with a copy button.

## Don't

- Don't toast. Not for errors, not for success, not for the session-expired notice.
- Don't say which half of the pair was wrong after a 401; it confirms the address exists.
- Don't put a Retry button on a 401: the form under the notice is the retry.
- Don't put client-side validation in the `Alert`; it belongs on the field.
- Don't call a timeout a failure (`danger`) or say the account was not created; the request may have landed.
- Don't stack notices: a new outcome replaces the one in the slot.

- Don't split a one-time code into separate inputs or move focus between them by hand; `OtpInput` is one field.
- Don't toast a rejected code; it is the field's reason, and the field is cleared and focused.

## Copy

- **Card heading:** names the step, sentence case, no punctuation: `Welcome back`, `Reset your password`, `Check your inbox`, `Sign up for a free account`. The lead under it is one full sentence: `Sign in to your account.`
- **Primary action:** a verb for what happens: `Continue with email`, `Sign in`, `Send reset link`, `Reset password`, `Return to sign in`.
- **Field labels:** one to two words, no colon, no parentheses: `Email`, `Work email`, `Password`, `New password`, `Confirm password`.
- **Links:** sentence case: `Forgot your password?`, `Resend email`.
- **Field errors:** what is wrong, with a period: `This field is required.`, `Enter a valid email address.`, `Passwords don't match.`
- **401 notice:** `Incorrect email or password. Check both and try again.`
- **503 notice:** says what is down and what is not lost: `Sign-in is unavailable right now. Your credentials are fine.`
- **500 notice:** says what failed and what state the user is in, code last: `Sign-in failed on our side. You are still signed out. Error 500.`
- **Timeout notice:** names the unknown, never a failure: `The server did not answer in time. Your session may already be open.`
- **409 notice:** the fact plus the two exits as links: `This email is already registered. Sign in or reset your password.`
- **Session expired:** `Your session expired. Sign in again to pick up where you left off.`
- **Action in a notice:** `Retry`, never "Try again".

## Accessibility

- The form has an accessible name (`aria-label="Sign in to your account"`) and `novalidate`, so the browser does not show its own bubbles over the field messages.
- Each input has a visible `Field.Label` tied to it by its `Field`; each error is linked with `aria-describedby` (or through `Field.Description` inside `Field`).
- Use the right `autocomplete` on every field (`username`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `email`) so password managers and autofill work.
- Icon-only back buttons have an `aria-label` equal to their tooltip.
- After a submit with errors, focus the first field that needs attention; after a 401, the password.
- The notice uses the `Alert` role from the component; don't add a second live region for the same message.
- Every transition sets `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:transform-none`.
- Social buttons are `type="button"` so Enter in the email field submits the email, not a provider.

- MFA: the code field is named by its label (`Authentication code`, `Recovery code`) and described by the reason when rejected; the QR code is an image named after the account, and the setup key is real text.

## States

- Login: the sign-in flow on the email step, with Google and GitHub over the `or` divider; the same file walks through password, reset, sent and new-password.
- SignUp: create an account with a work email (and a password checked by `PasswordRequirements`), Google or GitHub.
- SessionExpired: opens on the password step for the same email, with an info notice that clears on the next action.
- CheckInbox: the `/signup/verify` card: where the link went, the resend prompt and a secondary Return to sign in.
- IncorrectCredentials: 401 on Sign in; a danger notice above both fields, no action, the password cleared and focused.
- ServiceUnavailable: 503 on Sign in; a warning notice with Retry, credentials kept.
- ServerError: 500 on the request; a danger notice with Retry in the card instead of a toast.
- Timeout: no response; the same notice as the 500 in warning, with Retry, because the request may have gone through.
- EmailAlreadyRegistered: 409 on Sign up; a danger notice with Sign in and reset your password as links, the address left in the field.
- MfaSetup: turning on multi-factor authentication: three numbered steps, a `QrCode` of the `otpauth://` URI the API returns (issuer, account and secret) with the setup key and its `CopyButton` for people who cannot scan, then an `OtpInput` in a `Field`. The code submits on `complete` or Verify code; a wrong code (`000000` in the demo) clears it, marks the field invalid with the reason and keeps focus; no answer (`999999`) is a warning notice with Retry; success is a success notice and Continue to Console.
- MfaCode: the sign-in challenge after the password: a 6-digit `OtpInput`, focused when the challenge opens (not with `autofocus`), that submits on `complete`, Use a recovery code (an 8-character alphanumeric `OtpInput` grouped by 4) and Sign in with another account. Same outcomes as MfaSetup: field reason for a rejected code, warning notice with Retry when the check does not answer.

## Related

- `headers/auth-header` — the signed-out bar this block renders at the top.
- `platform/account/onboarding-form` — where a new account goes after it verifies its email.
- `platform/states/page-wires` — the session wire painted while an expired session signs out, before this screen.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — the same field mechanics (required versus invalid, validate on submit) in a signed-in form, where unscoped failures do toast.
- `PasswordRequirements` — the live password checklist used on sign up and reset.

## Steps

- email
- password
- reset
- sent
- new-password

## Variants

`Login` (primary) · `SignUp` · `SessionExpired` · `CheckInbox` · `IncorrectCredentials` · `ServiceUnavailable` · `ServerError` · `Timeout` · `EmailAlreadyRegistered` · `MfaSetup` · `MfaCode`. Code: [blocks/platform/auth.md](blocks/platform/auth.md), `get_pattern("platform/auth", { variant })`.
