# CreateHub (`platform/create/create-hub`)

> The Creation Center, where a project starts: the creation header with a single current crumb and a back control to Home, a large page heading whose lead also offers to pick a file or a folder, then two columns side by…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/create-hub/create-hub.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/create-hub")`
- Components: Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, EmptyState, GlobalHeader, IconButton, Input, Item, Link, PageHeader, ScrollArea, Select, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

create hub; creation center; new project; start a project; import from github; import repository; start from template; template gallery; create from git; central de criação; novo projeto; importar repositório; começar de um template

The Creation Center, where a new project starts. The user arrives from Home or a Create action with something to deploy and needs to pick its source in one look: a repository from their Git account, a template, or a file or folder from their machine. The page puts the two main sources side by side, Import from GitHub and Start from template, under one heading, and accepts a dropped folder anywhere.

## When to use

- The entry point of every new project, before the user has decided where the code comes from.
- The user may import an existing repository, start from a framework or starter template, or upload local files.
- The choice leads to a focused flow outside the console shell, such as `platform/create/deploy-template`.

## When not to use

- Creating a first-level resource that has no source code: use `platform/create/single-page-create`.
- A guided multi-step creation once the source is known: use `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Adding something inside an existing resource: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- The drop target and upload progress after a folder is dropped: those are `platform/states/project-intake`.
- Teaching a module to a new account: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Git connect — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required until connected)
- D. Repository search — `Select`, `Input` (required once connected)
- E. Repository list — `Card`, `Item`, `Button`, `Skeleton` (required once connected)
- F. Template gallery — `Button`, `ScrollArea`, `Card` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md](blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md).

## Do

- Keep both sources visible at once from the large breakpoint, the Git column first.
- Show the connect state only until an account exists, then go straight to the list.
- Let the search accept a pasted repository URL, so the user does not have to find it in the list.
- Keep template sections in the same order on every visit; Recommended first.
- Offer file and folder buttons in the heading so uploading works without a mouse.

## Don't

- Don't put the hub inside the console shell or open it in a drawer; it is a focused page.
- Don't replace the list with a spinner while a scope loads; use skeleton rows in its shape.
- Don't add a Continue or Next button; each Import and each template card starts its flow.
- Don't let the template gallery push the page into a long scroll on large screens; it scrolls inside its own area.
- Don't show templates as a dense table; the glyph and sentence are what the user scans.
- Don't hand-write the file and folder links or underline them at rest; use `Button kind="link"`.

## Copy

- **Heading:** a verb phrase for the task, e.g. "Start a new project"; description one sentence with a period, e.g. "Start from a repository or use a framework template."
- **Column titles:** short fragments, e.g. "Import from GitHub".
- **Connect state:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect your repository"; description one sentence, e.g. "Select a Git provider to connect your repository and start the deployment process."
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Continue with GitHub", "Import", "Filter".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what it takes, e.g. "Search projects or enter a Git repository URL".
- **Template cards:** title is the template name; description one sentence, e.g. "Compile Rust to WebAssembly and run it."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, select rather than choose or pick, no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`; column titles are `h2`, template titles `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link, the account button, the scope `Select` and the search each have an `aria-label`.
- Template cards are focusable with `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"`, and respond to Enter and Space.
- The loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; skeleton rows are hidden from assistive technology.
- Drag and drop always has a keyboard alternative: the file and folder buttons in the description.
- The `ScrollArea` is named so screen reader users know which region scrolls.

## States

- Default: no Git account connected; the connect state beside the template gallery.
- Connected: jane-doe is the selected scope and its seven repositories are listed, most recently pushed first.
- LoadingRepositories: a scope was just picked; six skeleton rows stand in for the repositories.

## Related

- `platform/create/deploy-template` — where a template card or Import leads.
- `platform/states/project-intake` — the drop target and upload overlay for a dropped folder.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — the guided flow once a source is chosen.
- `headers/creation-header` — the header this page uses.
- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — Home, where the back control returns.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Connected` · `LoadingRepositories`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md](blocks/platform/create/create-hub.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/create-hub", { variant })`.

# CreateInDrawer (`platform/create/create-in-drawer`)

> The right-side form drawer every item created or edited inside a resource opens, such as a domain, a record, an environment, a variable or a rule: a panel header with the title, a muted one-line description and the cl…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/create-in-drawer/create-in-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/create-in-drawer")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, Field, HelperText, Hint, IconButton, Input, InputGroup, Item, KeyValuePairs, Link, NumberInput, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioButton, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, Switch, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

create domain; add domain; create domain form; add domain drawer; edit domain; new domain; create drawer; custom domain; criar domínio; adicionar domínio; novo domínio; create in drawer; add record; add environment; criar em gaveta; form drawer; side drawer form; add item drawer; edit drawer; dns record form; nested resource form; gaveta de formulário; adicionar registro; formulário lateral; add origin drawer; form in drawer; formulário em gaveta; nested drawer; stacked drawers; drawer on drawer; create related item; create option in select; child form; gaveta aninhada; gavetas empilhadas; criar item relacionado; add rule; create origin in drawer; build and deployment; build deployment settings; deployment settings; deployment defaults; deploy configuration; workload deployment defaults; build settings; configurações de build; configurações de deploy; implantação; create deployment settings; deployment settings drawer; criar configuração de deploy; certificate; upload certificate; tls certificate; pem; certificate expiry; certificado; importar certificado; certificado tls

The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. The user is working on the resource behind it and must keep it in view, so the form slides over the page instead of replacing it. They fill a few sections, press the one commit button and land back where they were, with the new item in the list. The drawer opens over a console page: ItemRows and NestedDrawer draw that page as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

## When to use

- The item belongs to a resource that is already open (a domain on a workload, a record in a zone, a rule or an origin on a resource), per the surface rule in `skills/webkit-create-surface`.
- Editing that same item from its row menu; the drawer opens on its values and saves them.
- A first-level tuple normally created in bulk, such as variables, the one exception the surface rule allows.
- A select needs another item of the same resource that may not exist yet, such as the origin a new rule sends requests to: the NestedDrawer shape creates it in a second drawer and selects it back.

## When not to use

- A resource the sidebar routes to: create it on a page with `platform/create/single-page-create`, or `platform/create/multipage-create` when it needs several pages.
- A blocking yes or no question, or a destructive guard: use `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- Deploying what exists: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`, which commits a deployment rather than a record.
- Binding a whole resource that may be reused or created in a create flow: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.
- A select that needs a missing first-level resource, such as a service or a function: the stacked drawer would create on the wrong surface. Link to that resource's create page, or bind it with `platform/create/resource-picker`.
- Editing the settings of the resource itself: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger — `Button` (required)
- B. Drawer frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- C. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose` (required)
- D. Sections — `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection` (required)
- E. Environment select — `Field`, `Select`, `HelperText` (required)
- F. Domain source — `Field`, `RadioButton` (required)
- G. Domain name — `Field`, `InputGroup` (required)
- H. Certificate — `Field`, `Select`, `HelperText` (optional)
- I. Context alert — `Alert` (optional)
- J. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- K. Certificate import — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Button`, `PanelFooter` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/create-in-drawer.md](blocks/platform/create/create-in-drawer.md).

## Do

- Open on a blank form every time, or on the edited item's values, and clear every error on open.
- Lock the `fieldset` and pass `:disabled` to every control from the same flag while saving; release it on success and on failure.
- Validate on submit only: an empty required field gets the amber required prompt after Save is pressed.
- Close the drawer on success and show the new item in the list behind it, with a toast that names it.
- Stack a second, medium drawer for a missing item of the same resource, such as an origin for a rule, and select the new one back into the parent.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't create in a dialog, or open a page for an item that lives inside a resource.
- Don't add Cancel next to the commit button.
- Don't flag fields while the user is still typing, or show required and invalid on one field at once.
- Don't hide a required field inside a collapsed section.
- Don't reset the form on close; the content would jump while the drawer slides out.
- Don't deploy or publish as a side effect of Save.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** one string, `Add <Product Module>` inside a resource, e.g. "Add Domain"; editing keeps the verb the row menu used.
- **Description:** one or two muted sentences with a period under the title, e.g. "A domain is what puts an environment on this resource. Say where it answers, and name the address."
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "Where the domain answers."
- **Options:** labels name the choice, descriptions one sentence, e.g. "Use your own DNS and point it to this resource."
- **Helper text:** states the consequence of the current value, e.g. "Production publishes with the Deployment Settings set to Single."
- **Required:** "This field is required."
- **Create option:** `Create <Object>` at the foot of the select, e.g. "Create Environment".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", select rather than pick.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open, moves it to the first field on open and returns it to the trigger on close.
- The `form` has an `aria-label` that matches the title; `DrawerTitle` names the dialog.
- Every select trigger points at its `HelperText` with `aria-describedby`, so the consequence is read with the value.
- The choice cards are a radio group named by the Domain source label; each card's title and description are the radio's name and description.
- The loading button keeps its label and announces the busy state; the disabled `fieldset` keeps keyboard users out of the form while saving.
- Escape, the close button and the overlay all dismiss; none of them submit.

## States

- Default: Add Domain opened from the resource's Settings tab, blank, on the free domain option.
- AddEnvironment: the same form opened from the environment menu, titled and saved as Add Environment.
- EditDomain: opened from a domain row menu on www.example.com, with the Certificate select showing the covering wildcard.
- AddRecord: the DNS zone record form; Name and Value are flagged as required only after an empty Add Record.
- ItemRows: Add Origin on the Origins page of the storefront resource, a large drawer whose sections are `Item` rows in flush cards, saved together by one Add Origin.
- NestedDrawer: Add Rule on the storefront resource's Rules Engine, with an Origin select whose Create Origin option opens a second, medium drawer and selects the new origin back.
- DeploymentSettings: the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting, with General and Routing and policy sections.
- Certificate: Create Certificate opened with shop.example.com pasted as a server certificate: the details panel reads Issued to shop.example.com, Issued by Example Test CA and the expiry with the days left; the private key is empty, so Save flags it.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list a create drawer usually opens over.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where Add actions on a resource's tabs open this drawer.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the page a first-level resource creates on instead.

# DeployDrawer (`platform/create/deploy-drawer`)

> The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer/deploy-drawer.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-drawer")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, Field, Input, Item, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Popover, RadioButton, Separator, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

deploy drawer; deploy panel; deploy service; choose versions to deploy; dependencies before deploy; release drawer; gaveta de deploy; implantar serviço; escolher versão

The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by Deploy on a service or a project. The user is about to put a version into traffic and needs to confirm exactly what goes out (each resource and dependency at a version), where it goes (a project and one of its environments) and what else it reaches (every project that shares the environment's Deployment Settings). One Deploy at the foot commits all of it.

## When to use

- A service or a project has a ready version and the user deploys it from its page or list.
- The deploy reaches more than the resource itself: dependencies at their own versions, or other projects through shared Deployment Settings.
- A service deploys to a project that may not exist yet; the Project section creates it in place.

## When not to use

- Creating or editing an item inside a resource: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- The first deploy at the end of a create flow: use `platform/create/deploy-template` or `platform/create/provision-wizard`, which stream `platform/create/deployment-flow` in the page.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs` or `platform/detail/version-detail`.
- Binding one resource to another without deploying: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Trigger and frame — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent` (required)
- B. Panel header — `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose` (required)
- C. Sections — `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection` (required)
- D. Resources card — `Card`, `Separator`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Button` (required)
- E. Dependencies — `Accordion`, `Item`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- F. Project — `ToggleGroup`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu` (required on a service)
- G. Environment — `Field`, `RadioButton`, `Tag` (required)
- H. Projects impacted and commit — `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Popover`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on a service)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that will go out, even when the user changes nothing.
- Preselect the last used project and environment, and say so with a tag.
- List every project a shared Deployment Setting reaches before the user deploys, not after.
- When no version is pinned, open as Build and deployment with a Building row, keep the other sections faded and `inert`, and disable Deploy until the build lands.
- On a project, warn with an `Alert` above the environments when its Deployment Settings also publish elsewhere.
- Keep an environment that Strict Deployment Settings lock visible but disabled, with a Strict tag and one sentence naming the settings and the service they keep bound.
- Tag an environment Also deploys (warning) when the chosen environment's shared settings reach it, and say once, in a warning `Alert`, how many environments go live at once.
- Say in an info `Alert` when the deploy replaces another service on the chosen project, naming both.
- When a choice changes what the deploy reaches, reload that section in place: `Skeleton` rows, `aria-busy` on the region and one `role="status"` line; never clear the whole drawer.
- Tag a dependency other services reference as Shared, name them in a `Tooltip`, and say once that a shared dependency deploys at one version.
- When a dependency has no ready version, disable Deploy and say why in the footer, next to the button it disables.
- After Deploy, follow `platform/states/async-submit`: the drawer closes and one toast per run turns from Deploying… into the outcome, with Edit (reopens the drawer with the same choices) and Redeploy.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't deploy from a dialog, or ask for confirmation after Deploy; the drawer is the review.
- Don't hide dependencies or impacted projects behind a second step.
- Don't let Change version list hundreds of versions at once; search plus Load more.
- Don't add a second commit such as Save as draft; one Deploy.
- Don't print the shared-settings warning on each impacted row; it belongs once, above them.
- Don't hide a locked environment, or let it be picked and fail at deploy time.
- Don't offer View deployments in the outcome toast; it carries Edit and Redeploy.

## Copy

- **Trigger, title, commit:** "Deploy" on all three; "Build and deployment" as the title only while a build runs first.
- **Section hints:** one sentence on what the section decides, e.g. "The project whose domains serve the service."
- **Version control:** "Change version"; search placeholder and `aria-label` "Search versions"; footer "Load 10 more".
- **Project modes:** "Use existing" and "Create new".
- **Environment descriptions:** one sentence on how it serves, e.g. "Live traffic. One version serves the domain, and deploying replaces it."
- **Tags:** one or two words, e.g. "Ready", "Active", "Last used", "Selected", "New".
- **In progress:** the progressive verb with `…`, e.g. "Building…".
- **Run toast:** "Deploying web-app…" with "<version> to <environments>. It keeps running if you leave."; the outcome "web-app is live in Production." or "web-app wasn't deployed." with what failed and that nothing changed; actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Locks and reach:** "<settings> is Strict, so <service> stays bound to <environment>."; "Also deploys"; "<settings> is shared, so it deploys at one version."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish or activate; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the Deploy trigger on close.
- The `form` and the `ToggleGroup` carry `aria-label`s; the environment group is named by its `aria-label`.
- The version menu is a `role="menu"` moved with the arrow keys, each version a `menuitem` named by its version, author and age; the current one carries `aria-current`; search inputs have an `aria-label` that matches the placeholder.
- Each impacted environment group has an `aria-label` with its count, e.g. "Projects impacted in Production (3)".
- Faded sections during a build are `inert`, so keyboard users cannot reach controls that do nothing yet.
- A section that reloads carries `aria-busy="true"` with its `Skeleton` rows `aria-hidden`, and a `role="status"` line reads Loading the projects this deployment reaches, or Loading dependencies.
- A locked environment's radio is `disabled`; its reason is the card's description, so it is read with the choice.
- The Shared tag sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard, and its name already says who else references it.
- A disabled Deploy is described by the footer line that explains why (`aria-describedby`).
- Run progress and outcome reach screen readers through the toast region, so the user hears them from any page.
- Glyphs in rows are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; tags give the state in words.

## States

- Service: a service deploying environment first; Resources, Project with the last used project, Environment and Projects impacted.
- Building: no pinned version; titled Build and deployment with a Building row in place of Resources, the other sections faded and inert, Deploy disabled.
- ServiceProjectFirst: the project-first flow; Resources, the Project card with the last used project and a Change popover, then every environment.
- Project: deploying a project; its service and storage in Resources, Production and Preview, and a warning about other projects that share its storefront settings.
- Environment: a locked Strict environment, an Also deploys tag, the replace and multi-environment `Alert`s, Projects impacted grouped per environment and reloaded on switch; the run ends in a success toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Dependencies: the open Dependencies disclosure with a Shared dependency, a not-versioned integration and a dependency with no ready version that blocks Deploy; changing the service version reloads the list. The first run fails and its toast offers Edit and Redeploy; Redeploy succeeds.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the drawer that creates items rather than deploying.
- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the run a deploy streams once it starts.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the toast and outcome rule every deploy started here follows.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the logs of a deploy after it ran.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — what a version contains before it is deployed.
- `platform/create/resource-picker` — the Existing or New pattern the Project section follows.
- `SettingsSection` — the band each section uses; see `skills/webkit-create-surface` for the drawer commit model.

## Variants

`Service` (primary) · `Building` · `ServiceProjectFirst` · `Project` · `Environment` · `Dependencies`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-drawer.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-drawer", { variant })`.

# DeployProgressDialog (`platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog`)

> The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog/deploy-progress-dialog.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog")`
- Components: Button, Dialog, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, OutcomeMark, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Progress, Spinner, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy progress; deploy progress dialog; drop to deploy; deploy a folder; multi deploy progress; progresso do deploy; arrastar e implantar; progreso del despliegue

The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The user dropped a folder (or started a deploy whose environment publishes through several Deployment Settings) and wants to see each one activate, know which failed and why, and retry only those. The page behind the dialog is a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`); the dialog teleports over it.

**The toast stays the standard.** Every deploy reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy (`platform/states/async-submit`). This dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy path and for a deploy that fans out to several Deployment Settings; even there the outcome still reaches the user through the toast, so they can close the dialog and leave.

## When to use

- A folder dropped on a service deploys straight to an environment.
- One deploy activates several Deployment Settings that can succeed or fail independently.

## When not to use

- A deploy of one service or project: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`, which closes and reports through the toast.
- A deploy with build steps and logs: use `platform/create/deployment-flow` and `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Reviewing what a multi-resource release reaches before it runs: use `platform/create/release-impact`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drop confirm — `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `Tag`, `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required on the drop path)
- B. Progress frame — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `OutcomeMark` (required)
- C. Progress — `PanelContent`, `Progress` (required)
- D. Filter — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- E. Rows — `OutcomeMark`, `Spinner`, `Tag` (required)
- F. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- Outcome toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md).

## Do

- Let each Deployment Setting settle on its own and keep the ones that succeeded live.
- Say why a row failed on the row itself.
- Offer Retry failed for the failed rows only.
- Report the outcome through the toast as well, so the user can close the dialog.

## Don't

- Don't use this dialog for a single deploy; the toast is enough.
- Don't let the dialog be dismissed while the run goes on, or the user loses the only view of it.
- Don't roll back the settings that succeeded because another failed.

## Copy

- **Drop:** "New production deployment", "Dropped files", "Deploy to Production".
- **Title:** "Deploying 2 of 5…", "Deployed 5 Deployment Settings", "Deployed 4 of 5 Deployment Settings".
- **Tally:** "4 succeeded, 1 failed. Each Deployment Setting activates on its own, and the ones that succeeded stay live."
- **Tags:** Queued, Deploying, Done, Failed. **Actions:** Retry failed, Close.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, the progressive verb with `…`.

## Accessibility

- The dialog traps focus and is named by its title and described by the tally.
- The `Progress` bar is named; a `role="status"` line announces the outcome once settled.
- `OutcomeMark` names its outcome; tags give the state in words, glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- The dropped files list is a focusable scroll region with an `aria-label`; paths are `dir="ltr"`.
- Motion: the marks honour reduced motion and the `Spinner` stops under it.

## States

- Running: two settled, one deploying, two queued; advances to its outcome.
- Drop: the confirm that starts a drop-to-deploy run.
- PartialFailure: settled with one failure, Retry failed, error toast.
- Succeeded: every setting deployed, success toast.

## Related

- `platform/states/async-submit` — the toast rule this block follows.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — the standard way to deploy.
- `platform/create/release-impact` — what a release reaches, before it runs.
- `OutcomeMark` — the settled mark.

## Variants

`Running` (primary) · `Drop` · `PartialFailure` · `Succeeded`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog", { variant })`.

# DeploySuccess (`platform/create/deploy-success`)

> The outcome screen a create flow ends on, in the terminal column of the wizard page: a heading with its lead and, for a Git source, the scope as a Tag; the deployment card with a preview tile, the service name with a…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-success/deploy-success.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-success")`
- Components: Button, Card, CodeBlock, Item, SectionHeader, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

deploy success; deployment successful; deployed; success page; deployment complete; next steps after deploy; wizard finish; deploy concluído; sucesso do deploy; aplicação publicada

The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a source or provision wizard) has finished and the resource is serving, or was created for the first time.
- The flow created or bound more than one resource and the user should see each one.
- A resource was made from the CLI and nothing serves it yet: the CliCreated state shows how to deploy it.

## When not to use

- The run is still going or has failed: keep `platform/create/deployment-flow` on screen.
- A resource created from a form that does not deploy: end on the resource's page with a success toast that names it, as `skills/webkit-create-surface` describes; there is no outcome screen.
- An item added inside a resource from a drawer: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer` and close it on save.
- The onboarding steps for a CLI resource on its Overview tab: use `platform/detail/get-started`.

## Building blocks

- A. Outcome heading — `Tag` (required)
- B. Deployment card — `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Resources list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Next steps — `Card`, `Tag` (required)
- E. Manage — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md).

## Do

- Lead with the outcome and the live address; the user came to see it work.
- Tag every resource Created or Bound so the list doubles as a receipt of what the flow touched.
- Open external links in a new tab, with a `Tooltip` and a visually hidden note saying so.
- Drop the scope tag and the repository row when the flow had no Git source.
- In CliCreated, replace the deployment card with next steps that deploy the resource, and add the Get started paths for the CLI and GitHub Actions.

## Don't

- Don't celebrate: no confetti, no exclamation, no emoji. State the fact.
- Don't put more than one Recommended tag among the next steps.
- Don't add a Deploy again or Create another action; the user starts a new flow from the Creation Center.
- Don't leave the screen without a way into the resource; Manage is required.
- Don't repeat the resource list inside the deployment card.

## Copy

- **Heading:** the object and the past-tense result in sentence case, e.g. "Resource deployed", or "Resource created" when nothing serves it.
- **Lead:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "You deployed a new resource." followed by "Source:" and the source tag. Never a dangling fragment after the period.
- **Status tag:** one word, e.g. "Live"; resource tags "Created" or "Bound".
- **Links:** verb first, e.g. "Visit site", "Add custom domain"; tooltips name the target, e.g. "Open acme/web-app in a new tab".
- **Next steps:** title verb first in two or three words, e.g. "Customize domain", "View analytics"; description one sentence with a period.
- **Exit:** "Manage", a single verb.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no ampersand, no "please".

## Accessibility

- The heading is the page's only `h1`; the service name and the section titles are `h2`.
- The preview tile and Visit site have an `aria-label` that names the address and says it opens in a new tab.
- Links that open a new tab say so in visually hidden text, not only with the external-link glyph.
- Glyphs in rows and cards are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the Created or Bound tag gives the state in words.
- A next-step card is one focusable link or button with a visible focus ring; its title and description are its name.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading, deployment card, resources, next steps, Manage.

## States

- Default: a deployed service from a Git source, with the scope, the deployment card, four resources and three next steps.
- CliCreated: a resource made from the CLI that nothing serves yet; no deployment card, one resource row, next steps to deploy it here or on a new service, and the Get started paths.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the run this screen follows.
- `platform/create/deploy-template` — a flow that ends here.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — a wizard that ends here.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — a wizard that ends here with its own title.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — the CLI and GitHub Actions steps the CliCreated state embeds.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where Manage leads.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `CliCreated`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-success.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-success", { variant })`.

# DeployTemplate (`platform/create/deploy-template`)

> The deploy template page, a focused flow outside the console shell: the creation header with Back to Creation Center and the Start from a template crumb, the template preview card naming the repository it clones from,…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deploy-template/deploy-template.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-template")`
- Components: Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, EmptyState, Field, GlobalHeader, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupInput`, `InputGroupRoot`, Link, Select, Switch, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deploy template; clone template; template deploy page; connect git provider; deploy from template; one click deploy; start from a template; implantar template; clonar template; conectar git

A focused page, outside the console shell, where the user turns a template into a running project. They chose a template in the Creation Center and now need to see what it clones, connect a Git provider if they have none, name the repository it creates, fill the settings the template requires and deploy. The same column then shows the build and the outcome, so the user never leaves the page.

## When to use

- The user picked a template, a Git import or an upload from `platform/create/create-hub`, and the next step is to deploy it.
- The flow creates a repository from a source in the user's Git account and deploys from it on every push.
- The template needs a few settings (tokens, a domain) before its first build can run.

## When not to use

- Choosing what to start from: use `platform/create/create-hub`.
- A first-level resource created from a form with no source code: use `platform/create/single-page-create`.
- A source that needs several steps (where it runs, how it builds): use `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Provisioning a resource and binding it to another: use `platform/create/provision-wizard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Template and Git step — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (required)
- C. Browse templates — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-template.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-template.md).

## Do

- Keep the template preview card at the top of the column through every phase, so the user always sees what is being deployed.
- Ask for Git first; show the form only once a provider is connected.
- Disable Deploy until the repository name and every required template setting have a value.
- Hand the same column to `platform/create/deployment-flow` on Deploy, then to `platform/create/deploy-success`.
- Trim the form to the repository fields for Import from Git, and to the uploaded files for Upload a Project.

## Don't

- Don't open this flow inside the console shell or a drawer; it is a page with its own header.
- Don't ask for settings the template does not use, or move a required setting out of view.
- Don't create the repository before Deploy is pressed.
- Don't replace the page with a new route for the build; the column changes, the page stays.
- Don't put a Cancel next to Deploy; the back control and Browse templates already leave.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** the entry point, then the template name, e.g. "Start from a template" then "Nuxt E-commerce".
- **Back control:** `aria-label` names the destination, e.g. "Back to Creation Center".
- **Git step:** title states the task, e.g. "Connect a Git provider"; description one sentence saying what happens, e.g. "Nuxt E-commerce is cloned into a repository in your account, then deployed from it on every push."
- **Provider buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Continue with GitHub"; the link names the place, e.g. "Manage connected providers".
- **Form heading:** e.g. "Deploy your project"; settings labels 1 to 3 words with the constraint in the description, e.g. "You can find this token in the API credentials of your store."
- **Commit:** "Deploy", the same verb on the button and in the run that follows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash in labels or `aria-label`s, no parentheses in labels.

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark under the header; the step title is an `h2` and the settings group an `h3`.
- The back `IconButton`, the brand link and the account button each have an `aria-label`.
- The repository name has a visible `Field.Label` tied to its input by its `Field`; the privacy switch is labelled Public repository and announces its on or off state.
- Settings use `Field` labels and descriptions, so each input announces its name and constraint.
- A disabled Deploy is explained by the required markers on the fields, not by the button alone.
- The page enter animation stops under reduced motion.

## States

- ConnectGit: no Git provider yet; the template preview over the Connect a Git provider card and Browse templates.
- Form: GitHub connected; scope and repository name side by side, public by default, over the template settings, with Deploy disabled until the access token is filled.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-hub` — where the user picks the template.
- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the build card the column shows after Deploy.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the outcome the column ends on.
- `headers/creation-header` — the header this page uses.
- `platform/states/project-intake` — the upload path that reaches this page with files instead of a template.

## Steps

- connect-git
- form

## Variants

`ConnectGit` (primary) · `Form`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/deploy-template.md](blocks/platform/create/deploy-template.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/deploy-template", { variant })`.

# DeploymentFlow (`platform/create/deployment-flow`)

> The deploy flow card a create flow streams while it deploys: a Card titled Deployment whose header carries the run status, a StatusIndicator while it runs and the Phased or Complete ToggleGroup once it has failed, ope…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/deployment-flow/deployment-flow.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/deployment-flow")`
- Components: Accordion, Card, LogView, `LogViewContent`, Progress, Spinner, StatusIndicator, Tag, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deployment progress; build logs; deploy logs; creation progress; deployment status; build pipeline; deploy failed; progresso do deploy; logs de build; status da implantação; deploy flow; streaming deploy logs; fluxo de deploy

The card a create flow hands its column to once the user has pressed Deploy. The user waits here for the first deploy of what they just made: they need to know that it started, what it is doing now, how far it has gone and, if it stops, which step failed and why. The card opens on a cloning splash, then streams the pipeline steps with their logs, and either hands over to the success screen or stays open on the failure.

## When to use

- A create flow (a template deploy, an import from Git, a provision wizard) starts a build or a provisioning run the user should watch before the resource is usable.
- The run is long enough to need progress, and short enough that the user stays on the page for it.
- A failed run must keep the user in the flow, with the failing step open on its output.

## When not to use

- The logs of a deployment that already exists, read from its detail page: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- A run of half a minute or more the user is expected to leave and come back to: use `platform/states/async-submit`, which reports the status where the user returns.
- A dropped folder being uploaded before anything is built: use the Initializing overlay in `platform/states/project-intake`.
- The outcome once the run has finished: hand the column to `platform/create/deploy-success`; do not keep the finished card as the last screen.

## Building blocks

- A. Deployment card — `Card` (required)
- B. Run status — `StatusIndicator` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/deployment-flow.md](blocks/platform/create/deployment-flow.md).

## Do

- Open on the cloning splash the moment Deploy is pressed, so the column never goes blank between the form and the first log line.
- Keep one step open at a time: the one running, or the one that failed.
- Show each step's time once it ends, and the step count in the Logs row while it runs.
- On failure, open the failing step on its error output and mark the steps behind it Skipped.
- Retire the progress bar when the run settles, then hand over to `platform/create/deploy-success` a beat after the last line prints.

## Don't

- Don't show a bare spinner with no words; the status label says what is happening.
- Don't put the run status in a toast; it belongs in the card header.
- Don't auto-advance to the success screen after a failure, or hide the logs that explain it.
- Don't expand every finished step; a long log pushes the step in flight out of view.
- Don't add a Cancel or a second action to the card; the flow around it owns navigation.

## Copy

- **Card title:** one noun naming the run, e.g. "Deployment" or "Provisioning".
- **Run status:** the progressive form of the verb with `…` only while in progress, e.g. "Building…" in prose, "Building" as an indicator label.
- **Splash line:** fragments naming source and destination, e.g. "Cloning acme/web-app to acme".
- **Outcome tag:** one or two words stating the result, e.g. "Completed", "Failed".
- **Pending steps:** say they have not started, e.g. "Waiting to start…".
- **Errors:** the log output says what failed; the step title names the step in sentence case, e.g. "Routing rules".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The status label is text, not only a colour or a spinner; screen readers hear Building, then the outcome.
- The progress bar has an accessible name, e.g. "Deployment progress", and the logs region an `aria-label`.
- Decorative glyphs in the splash and in step rows carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the status of each step is also given in words.
- Step headers are keyboard-operable accordion triggers; opening a step does not move focus.
- New log lines do not steal focus or announce one by one; the step change and the outcome are what is announced.

## States

- Initial: Deploy was just pressed; the cloning splash with a Building indicator, before the first step starts.
- Running: two steps done with their times, the current step spinning and open on its lines, the step count shown and the progress bar on the bottom edge.
- Finished: every step checked and collapsed, a Completed tag, the progress bar retired, just before the success screen.
- Failed: the failing step open on its error output with a Failed tag, the later steps Skipped, and the Phased or Complete switch in the header.

## Related

- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the same logs as a standalone block on a deployment's detail page.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the screen the column hands over to once the run finishes.
- `platform/create/deploy-template` — the template flow that streams this card after Deploy.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — a create flow that titles the card Provisioning.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — a long run the user leaves and comes back to.
- `Card` — the container; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for loading, progress and failure rendering.

## Variants

`Initial` (primary) · `Running` · `Finished` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/deployment-flow.md](blocks/platform/create/deployment-flow.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/deployment-flow", { variant })`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/multipage-create/multipage-create.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/multipage-create")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Field, GlobalHeader, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, RadioButton, SaveBar, SectionHeader, SettingRow, Stepper, Switch, Tag, Textarea, Toast
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

multipage create; multi-step create page; stepper create; create wizard; step by step form; criação em etapas; formulário em etapas; review step; review and create; confirm before create; wizard review; summary before submit; revisar; etapa de revisão; revisão antes de criar; review before create; summary step; revisar antes de criar

The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time. The user first says where the resource runs, then answers each step's fields in order, and only reaches the create action on the last step. A rail on the left shows how far they are and lets them return to any step already reached; if the host they chose lacks a module the resource needs, a step is inserted that offers to turn it on, so nothing is created that would silently never be read.

## When to use

- A first-level resource whose fields fall into groups that make sense one at a time (general, then type, then entries) and where a later group depends on an earlier answer.
- The resource must first bind to a host (a policy, an application) and that choice can change what is asked next.
- A code resource whose editor needs a whole step to itself.

## When not to use

- Everything fits on one screen without order: use `platform/create/single-page-create`.
- The resource is created inside another one: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- The flow provisions a service, binds a project and deploys: use `platform/create/provision-wizard`.
- The flow starts from a code source (Git, CLI, template): use `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Binding an existing or new resource inside a form step: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Step rail — `Stepper` (required)
- C. Step heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- D. Where it runs — `Input`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Button` (required)
- E. Module step — `Card`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Switch` (conditional)
- F. Field steps — `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (required)
- G. Choice cards — `Field`, `RadioButton` (optional)
- H. Long entry — `Textarea`, `HelperText` (optional)
- I. Footer — `SaveBar` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/multipage-create.md](blocks/platform/create/multipage-create.md).

## Do

- Ask where the resource runs first, and insert the module step only when the chosen host needs it.
- Validate one step at a time on Next, and mark a failed step `error` on the rail.
- Unlock a step on the rail only once it has been reached, and let the user jump back to any unlocked step.
- Keep Cancel apart from Back and Next, on the opposite side.
- Keep the create action on the last step only; every step before it says Next.
- Keep the chosen host visible in the chooser even when it falls outside the first six.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't let the rail skip ahead to steps not reached yet.
- Don't put a Next button on a step answered by a click; picking the host is the answer.
- Don't block the create when a module is off; warn, offer the switch and let the user go on.
- Don't repeat the step title as a second heading inside the card.
- Don't validate fields of later steps, or judge a field while it is being typed.
- Don't use more than one step for fields that only make sense together.

## Copy

- **Title, breadcrumb and last submit:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Access List".
- **Step titles:** short nouns, e.g. "Where it runs", "General", "List settings".
- **Step descriptions:** one sentence with a period, e.g. "Select the policy whose rules match it. It needs IP filtering on."
- **Chooser:** instruction with "Select", e.g. "Select a policy to continue"; the search placeholder and `aria-label` name what is searched, e.g. "Search policies".
- **Module tag:** the missing module and its state, e.g. "IP filtering off".
- **Module alert:** the consequence in one sentence, e.g. "acme-staging has IP filtering off, so no rule reads this list until the module is on."
- **Escape routes:** verb first, e.g. "Create a policy", "Continue without a policy".
- **Required message:** "This field is required."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Choose"; no em dash; no "simply".

## Accessibility

- The `Stepper` has an `aria-label` naming the flow; disabled steps cannot be focused or activated.
- The `form` takes the current step's title as its `aria-label`; a `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` repeats it.
- Host rows are native `button`s with `aria-pressed`; the chooser's search has an `aria-label` and Enter selects the first match.
- Choice cards sit in a `fieldset` with a `legend`; each `RadioButton` is labelled by its card.
- Required messages are tied to their control with `aria-describedby`; focus stays on the step after a failed Next.
- Step transitions honour reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the first step; the centred chooser of policies with search, module tags and the two escape routes.
- ModuleOff: acme-staging was chosen with IP filtering off, so the IP filtering step shows the warning, the switch card and the note.
- ListSettings: the settings step; Type as radio choice cards and the List textarea. An empty list marks the step red on the rail.
- Review: the last step, read-only, with the create action in the footer. Where it runs is one `Alert` whose severity says whether anything will read the resource; What gets created pairs each value with the property it is sent as and shows long lists as their first five `Tag`s and a count; What can reference it names the consumers. Each band that maps to a step has an outlined Edit (`aria-label` names the band) that jumps back to that step. Create re-validates every step and, on a failure, opens the first step with an error.

## Review step

- Add a Review step when the create has three or more steps or binds the resource to something; skip it for a one-step create.
- Show values as they will be sent, with the property name under each, and never show secrets in clear.
- Put Edit on each band, not on each value; after the edit, Next walks forward through the later steps, already filled, back to Review.
- Say plainly when nothing will read the resource yet (unbound, or a module off) with a warning `Alert`, not a disabled create.

## Related

- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the same job when the fields fit one screen.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — a step wizard that starts from a code source and deploys.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — a two-step wizard that binds a project and deploys.
- `platform/edit/code-editor` — the editor a code resource can use as one step.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — required and invalid states on Next.
- `Stepper` — the step rail; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Steps

- where-it-runs
- module
- settings

## Variants

`WhereItRuns` (primary) · `ModuleOff` · `ListSettings` · `Review`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/multipage-create.md](blocks/platform/create/multipage-create.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/multipage-create", { variant })`.

# ProvisionWizard (`platform/create/provision-wizard`)

> A two-step creation wizard that provisions a resource and binds it to another: the creation header, a Stepper rail that only lets you go back, a page heading over the form column, and a borderless SaveBar footer that…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/provision-wizard/provision-wizard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/provision-wizard")`
- Components: Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Field, GlobalHeader, HelperText, Hint, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, RadioCards, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Stepper, Switch, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

provision wizard; create service wizard; two-step wizard; stepper form; bind domain and deployment; create and deploy; multi-step create; assistente de criação; assistente em etapas; criar serviço

The two-step wizard that provisions a resource bound to another and puts it into traffic. The user first binds the project the service serves, reusing one from a paged list or creating it right there with its cache and origin, then sets the domain traffic arrives on, the environment and certificate, and the deployment the first release is cut against. The address is previewed as they type, the defaults sit under Advanced, and the last button says it both creates and deploys, so the cost of pressing it is never a surprise.

## When to use

- A first-level resource that is useless until it is bound to another resource and deployed, such as a service that serves a project on a domain.
- The bound resource may already exist or be created in the same flow, and its essentials fit on the first step.
- The user expects one act to end with traffic arriving, and the button can say so.

## When not to use

- A resource that is only created, not deployed: use `platform/create/single-page-create` or `platform/create/multipage-create`; Save must not deploy.
- The project comes from a code source picked in the flow (Git, CLI, template): use `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Deploying an existing package from inside a resource: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`.
- Only the existing or new picker is needed inside another form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Step rail — `Stepper` (required)
- C. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- D. Project band — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Field`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Item`, `Skeleton`, `Button` (required)
- E. New project configuration — `Card`, `Item`, `Switch`, `Field`, `Input`, `SettingRow`, `RadioCards`, `HelperText`, `Select` (conditional)
- F. Project read-back — `Card`, `Item`, `Button` (required on step two)
- G. Domain — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- H. Environment and certificate — `Card`, `Field`, `RadioCards`, `Hint`, `HelperText`, `Select` (required)
- I. Deployment — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Item`, `Input`, `Skeleton`, `Button` (required)
- J. Advanced — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Select`, `Field`, `SettingRow`, `Switch` (optional)
- K. Footer — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/provision-wizard.md](blocks/platform/create/provision-wizard.md).

## Do

- Bind the project first, with Existing as the default whenever one exists.
- Validate the current step on Next, and only open fields that their switch turned on.
- Preview the address and the resource name as the user types, so the result is known before the commit.
- Keep the answer from step one when the user presses Change and comes back.
- Label the final action with both acts, since it creates and deploys.
- Submit into `platform/create/deployment-flow` and end on `platform/create/deploy-success`.

## Don't

- Don't call the final button Save or Create when it also deploys; the label must name the deploy.
- Don't put a required field inside Advanced, or open Advanced to show an error.
- Don't let the rail jump forward past a step that has not validated.
- Don't make the user leave the wizard to create the project or the deployment.
- Don't show both the existing list and the new fields at once; the toggle decides.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Service".
- **Description:** what the resource is and what the last step does, e.g. "A service is the public entry point: what it serves, and the domain traffic arrives on. The last step provisions both."
- **Step titles:** nouns, e.g. "Project", "Domain and deployment".
- **Toggle options:** short and parallel, e.g. "Existing project" and "New project"; "Free platform domain" and "Your own domain"; "Create one" and "Use existing".
- **Preview:** a label and a value, e.g. "Traffic arrives on" over "https://my-first-app.example.com"; empty, it tells what to type, e.g. "Type a prefix to see the domain."
- **Required messages:** what to do, as a sentence, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one.", "Enter the prefix for the platform domain.", "This field is required."
- **Read-back action:** "Change".
- **Final action:** "Create and deploy". Back is "Back".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: no parentheses in labels (move asides to the description), "Select", never "Pick"; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `Stepper` has an `aria-label`; the disabled next step cannot be focused.
- Every `ToggleGroup` has an `aria-label` that states its question, e.g. "Where the domain comes from".
- Picker rows are native `button`s with `aria-pressed`, and each picker has a `role="status"` count line and `aria-hidden` skeleton rows.
- Switches carry an `aria-label` matching their row or policy title; the `Select` triggers carry the field name.
- The platform suffix inside the prefix `Input` is `aria-hidden`; the preview line repeats the full address as text.
- The collapsed Advanced region is `inert` while closed.

## States

- Project: step one with Existing project chosen and the paged project list; Next validates the binding.
- NewProject: New project chosen; the Name field replaces the list, with the Cache Settings switches and the Add an origin switch each opening its fields.
- DomainAndDeployment: step two with web-app bound; the read-back row with Change, the Domain card on a free platform domain, Environment and certificate, Deployment, collapsed Advanced, and Back plus Create and deploy.

## Related

- `platform/create/resource-picker` — the Existing or New band this wizard binds its project with.
- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the provisioning log Create and deploy runs.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the screen the flow ends on.
- `platform/create/source-wizard` — the wizard that starts from a code source instead.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the lock and loading state while the submit is in flight.
- `SettingsSection` — the collapsible Advanced band; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Steps

- project
- domain-and-deployment

# ReleaseImpact (`platform/create/release-impact`)

> The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/release-impact/release-impact.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/release-impact")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Badge, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, Field, Select, Skeleton, Spinner, Switch, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

release impact; review and deploy; release composer; what a deploy changes; dependency versions; deployment impact; impacto do release; revisar e implantar; impacto del despliegue

The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once: a service, the policy in front of it, its storage, its error page and every dependency they reference. The user is about to put all of it into traffic and needs to see, before deploying, which version of each resource goes out, which dependencies go with it, and every Deployment Setting, environment and project the release reaches. One Deploy release at the foot commits it, after one confirmation.

## When to use

- A release spans several resources that deploy together, each at its own version.
- The release reaches projects through shared Deployment Settings, and the user must see how far it goes before it goes.
- Dependencies are detected from the resources and may be shared between them.

## When not to use

- Deploying one service or project from its page: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`, which is the default way to deploy.
- Watching several Deployment Settings activate after a deploy started: use `platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog`.
- Reading what a past deploy did: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Switching one resource back to an earlier version: use `platform/detail/version-detail` (Revert).

## Building blocks

- A. Outcome — `Alert`, `Button` (required after a run)
- B. Resource cards — `Switch`, `Tag`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Resource and version — `Field`, `Select`, `Tag` (required)
- D. Dependencies — `Badge`, `Accordion`, `Alert`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `Select` (required when a resource references others)
- E. Impact — `Card`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Skeleton`, `Alert`, `Button` (required)
- F. Footer and commit — `Button`, `ConfirmDialog` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/release-impact.md](blocks/platform/create/release-impact.md).

## Do

- Show every resource and dependency with the version that goes out, including the ones the user did not touch.
- Say what tracking the latest Ready version resolves to now.
- Block Deploy release only for something the user can fix here, and say what it is in the footer.
- Keep Deploy possible when the impact cannot be computed; say the impact is unknown.
- Report the outcome through the toast and the page `Alert`, both with Edit and Redeploy.

## Don't

- Don't hide shared dependencies; changing one changes it everywhere in the release.
- Don't confirm twice: the page is the review, the `ConfirmDialog` is the only step before the run.
- Don't keep the user on the page while it runs; the run reports wherever they are.
- Don't draw the Flow view with `Flow` until its list semantics pass axe.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Review and deploy". **Commit:** "Deploy release"; in progress "Deploying…".
- **Confirmation:** "Deploy this release?" and one sentence with the resources, versions and reach.
- **Versions:** "Track latest Ready", "resolves at deploy", "Pin a ready version", tag "Current".
- **Blockers:** "<name> has no Ready version, so the release cannot be deployed."
- **Outcome:** "Release deployed." / "The release wasn't deployed." with the cause and that nothing changed in traffic.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: Deploy, never publish; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- Each resource card is a `section` named by its type and resource; the Resources heading takes focus on Edit.
- Every `Select` is labelled through its `Field` (visible for the resource, `sr-only` for dependencies).
- The include `Switch` has an `aria-label`; its `Tooltip` repeats it for pointer users.
- The Shared `Tag` sits in a focusable wrapper so its `Tooltip` opens from the keyboard.
- The Impact region is `aria-busy` while loading and announces it in a `role="status"` line.
- The `ConfirmDialog` traps focus and returns it to Deploy release.

## States

- Ready: every resource with a version, the impact computed, Tree view.
- Loading: the impact being computed.
- Unavailable: the impact could not be read; Retry lands on a truncated list.
- MissingVersion: a resource without a Ready version blocks the deploy.
- Failed: the last run was refused; Edit and Redeploy on the toast and the page `Alert`.

## Related

- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — deploying one service or project.
- `platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog` — several Deployment Settings activating after the deploy.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the toast rule every deploy follows.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — one version, its history and revert.

## Variants

`Ready` (primary) · `Loading` · `Unavailable` · `MissingVersion` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/release-impact.md](blocks/platform/create/release-impact.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/release-impact", { variant })`.

# ResourcePicker (`platform/create/resource-picker`)

> The card a create flow uses to bind one resource to another: a lead, a ToggleGroup choosing between an existing resource and a new one, then either a hint over a searchable list of the existing resources with a select…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/resource-picker/resource-picker.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/resource-picker")`
- Components: Button, Card, Field, HelperText, Input, Item, Skeleton, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

resource picker; select existing or new; choose resource; bind resource; searchable picker; pick application; seletor de recurso; escolher recurso; existente ou novo

The band a create flow uses when the resource being created needs another resource that may already exist. The user either reuses one of theirs or makes a new one on the spot, and answers it in one place: an Existing / New choice, then a searchable, paged list of what exists or the few fields that create a new one. The chosen row is marked, every search and load is announced, and a missing answer is flagged above the list where it is seen first.

## When to use

- A create flow binds a whole resource that the user may reuse or create: the project a service serves, the deployment a release is cut against, the firewall that protects a workload.
- The candidates can run past seven, so the list needs search, paging and a no-match line.
- Creating the bound resource takes one or a few fields that fit in the same card.

## When not to use

- A single field that references an existing resource (a certificate, an environment, a function): use a select row inside the form, as `platform/create/provision-wizard` does for Environment.
- Choosing where a resource runs as a step of its own, with module tags and an inline create row: use the chooser in `platform/create/multipage-create` or `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- Browsing or managing the resources themselves: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Creating the bound resource needs its own full form: link to its create page (`platform/create/single-page-create`) instead of nesting it here.

## Building blocks

- A. Band card — `Card` (required)
- B. Existing / New choice — `ToggleGroup` (required when something exists)
- C. New resource fields — `Field`, `Input` (required in New)
- D. Search and required message — `Input`, `HelperText` (optional)
- E. Resource list — `Item`, `Skeleton` (required in Existing)
- F. Load more — `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/resource-picker.md](blocks/platform/create/resource-picker.md).

## Do

- Default to Existing when anything exists, and drop the toggle entirely when nothing does.
- Mark the chosen row three ways: background, trailing check and `aria-pressed`.
- Keep the required message above the rows, under the search, so it is read before the list is scanned.
- Offer the other mode in the no-match line, so an empty search leads to creating one.
- Keep the chosen value when the user switches to New and back.
- Build the band once and pass the noun, icon and options; every flow that binds a resource reads the same (see `skills/webkit-create-surface`).

## Don't

- Don't use radio buttons or a select for a whole resource the user may also create; that is this band.
- Don't show the search for a list that fits in one batch.
- Don't validate the Name while it is being typed, or show required and invalid together.
- Don't render a loading spinner in place of the rows; show skeleton rows in the row shape and keep the visible ones.
- Don't put the create fields in a dialog or a second page; they belong in the same card.

## Copy

- **Card title:** the bound noun, singular, e.g. "Project".
- **Lead:** one sentence on what the binding does, e.g. "What this service serves on each environment, so one service can serve different projects on Production and Preview."
- **Toggle options:** `Existing <noun>` and `New <noun>`, e.g. "Existing project", "New project".
- **Search:** placeholder and `aria-label` name the collection, e.g. "Search projects".
- **Load more:** the verb and the batch size, e.g. "Load 5 more".
- **No match:** the fact, then both ways out, e.g. "No project matches “api”. Create one instead, or clear the search."
- **Required:** what to do, as a sentence, e.g. "Select the project this service serves, or create a new one."
- **Name guidance:** the allowed characters, e.g. "Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Pick" or "Choose"; sentence case; no em dash.

## Accessibility

- The `ToggleGroup` has an `aria-label` that states the question, e.g. "Where the project comes from".
- Each row is a native `button` with `aria-pressed` reflecting the selection; the check icon is `aria-hidden`.
- Search has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder.
- A `role="status"` region announces the count after every search, load and no-match, e.g. "5 of 19 projects".
- Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`; the Load more `Button` carries `:loading` so its busy state is announced.
- The required message is tied to the search group by `data-field-invalid`, and focus stays where it was when it appears.

## States

- Existing: resources exist; the toggle sits on Existing with a row already chosen in the first batch.
- New: the user switched to New; the list gives way to the Name field with the allowed characters as helper text.
- Loading: Load more was pressed; five skeleton rows follow the visible ones and the button spins.
- Required: Next was pressed with nothing chosen; the required message sits under the search, above the list.

## Related

- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — binds its project with this band on the first step and reuses the list for the deployment.
- `platform/create/multipage-create` — the step wizard whose Where it runs chooser follows the same list rules.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — how required and invalid messages appear on submit.
- `Item` — the selectable row the list is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `ToggleGroup` — the Existing / New segment; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Existing` (primary) · `New` · `Loading` · `Required`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/resource-picker.md](blocks/platform/create/resource-picker.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/resource-picker", { variant })`.
