# SinglePageCreate (`platform/create/single-page-create`)

> The page a first-level resource is created on in one screen: its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column opening with a small page heading, then stacked sections, each a heading with a Hint over a f…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/single-page-create/single-page-create.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/single-page-create")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Checkbox, Field, GlobalHeader, HelperText, IconButton, Input, InputGroup, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, PasswordInput, PhoneInput, RadioButton, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Textarea
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

create page; create resource page; create zone; full page create form; top-level create page; new resource form; creation page; página de criação; criar recurso; formulário de criação; single page create; create purge; create service page; criação em uma página; sectioned form; single column form; import from git form; form with sections; deploy form; acknowledgement checkbox; formulário em seções; formulário de uma coluna; importar do git

The page a first-level resource is created on when everything it needs fits on one screen. The user arrives from the module's `Create <Object>` button, answers the required fields at the top, leaves the defaulted ones folded under Advanced, and commits from a bar that never scrolls away. The page has its own URL, its own creation header and no sidebar, so it survives a reload and the back button, and leaving it returns to the list.

## When to use

- The resource is one the sidebar routes to (a domain, a service, a purge) and the user came only to create it (`skills/webkit-create-surface`).
- Its fields fit in a few sections without depending on each other's answers step by step.
- An action that takes a form and runs once, whose submit names what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- The settings page of the same resource: it reuses these sections in the same order.

## When not to use

- The fields split into steps that unlock in order, or one answer adds a step: use `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- The resource binds another one and then deploys: use `platform/create/provision-wizard` or `platform/create/source-wizard`.
- The thing is created inside another resource (a record in a zone, a rule in an application): use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- Editing an existing resource where the commit bar should mount only after a change: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- Never put a create form in a dialog.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item` (required)
- D. Field rows — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (required)
- E. Switch rows — `Switch` (optional)
- F. Commit bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md](blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md).

## Do

- Put every required field in the first band; never inside Advanced, so a failed submit always points at something on screen.
- Validate on submit only, then clear each message as soon as its field is edited.
- Give every control an `aria-label` that repeats its row title.
- Keep Cancel and the submit in the same bar, submit last, and name the submit after what it does (Save, Purge, Deploy).
- Lock the whole `fieldset` and every control with one `submitting` flag while the request is in flight, and put `:loading` on the submit.
- On success, show a toast that names the resource and opens it (`skills/webkit-errors`).

## Don't

- Don't show the sidebar on this page, or open it as a modal over the list.
- Don't stretch the commit bar across the page or build the centred card by hand; it is `SaveBar kind="centered"`.
- Don't print the band's guidance as a paragraph under its title; use the `hint`.
- Don't mark fields required or invalid before the first submit, or show both states on one field.
- Don't make Save deploy, publish or charge as a side effect; creating is not deploying.
- Don't add a validation summary at the top; each message sits at its field.
- Don't squeeze a textarea or radio group into the right-hand cell; stack the row.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label, verb first with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Domain". Identical to the button that opened the page.
- **Description:** one sentence on what the resource is, e.g. "A domain holds the DNS records that answer authoritatively for a hostname."
- **Section titles:** the domain, not the widget, e.g. "General", "Target", "Delivery settings", "Advanced".
- **Row descriptions:** a full sentence with a period, saying what the value does, e.g. "Identifies the domain in this list. It is not the hostname."
- **Submit:** one verb, e.g. "Save", "Purge", "Deploy". Cancel is always exactly "Cancel".
- **Required message:** "This field is required."
- **Invalid message:** what to enter, with an example, e.g. "Enter a valid domain name. Example: example.com."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no parentheses in labels, no "please".

## Accessibility

- One `main` landmark holding one `form`, labelled by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby`, with `novalidate` so the page's own messages replace the browser's.
- A `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` groups the sections.
- Each message is tied to its control with `aria-describedby` and appears only on submit; required and invalid are announced through the control's own state.
- The collapsed Advanced region is `inert` while closed, so keyboard focus never lands in hidden fields.
- The back `IconButton` and the account trigger have `aria-label`s; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: header, heading, General, Advanced toggle, then the bar's Import, Cancel and Save.

## States

- Default: the Create Domain page at rest; General holds Name and Domain name, Advanced is collapsed, the bar shows Import, Cancel and Save.
- CreatePurge: a Target band of radio choice cards for Layer and Purge type, an Arguments textarea that follows the type, a warning alert and a bar with Cancel and Purge.
- CreateService: a long create in five groups of rows under the same centred `SaveBar` with Cancel and Save.
- RequiredFields: Create Service after Save on the empty form; Name and Address show "This field is required." until edited.
- ImportFromGit: the same job as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`) with standalone field stacks under plain headings, an acknowledgement checkbox and one Deploy button at the end of the column.
- ImportFromGitSubmitted: Import from Git after Deploy on the untouched form; every required field shows its required state and message.

## Related

- `platform/create/multipage-create` — the same job split into steps.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — create inside a resource without leaving it.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — the edit page that reuses these sections.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — required and invalid states on submit.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list whose `Create <Object>` button opens this page.
- `SettingRow` — the field row every section is built from; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `CreatePurge` · `CreateService` · `RequiredFields` · `ImportFromGit` · `ImportFromGitSubmitted`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md](blocks/platform/create/single-page-create.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/single-page-create", { variant })`.

# SourceWizard (`platform/create/source-wizard`)

> A creation wizard that starts a resource from a code source and deploys it: the creation header, a Stepper rail that only lets you go back, the form column, and a borderless fading SaveBar footer with Back and the pri…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/create/source-wizard/source-wizard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/create/source-wizard")`
- Components: Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Field, GlobalHeader, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, SaveBar, Stepper
- Skills: `webkit-create-surface`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

source wizard; deploy from git; import from git wizard; create project wizard; select a method; select a source; sync with cli; git import flow; assistente de importação; importar do git; criar projeto

The wizard that starts a resource from code and deploys it. The user first says which service the project deploys to (an existing one, a new one created inline, or none yet), then picks how the code arrives: import from Git, sync from the CLI or start from a template. The method they pick declares the steps that follow on the rail, and the flow ends on the provisioning log and the success screen. Steps answered by a click carry no Next, so the user moves as fast as they decide.

## When to use

- A first-level resource whose content is code from somewhere else: a project from a repository, a local folder or a starter template.
- The resource is created and deployed in the same flow, and the user must first say where it runs.
- The remaining steps depend on the source the user picks.

## When not to use

- A resource with no code source, created step by step: use `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- Provisioning a service that binds a project, a domain and a deployment: use `platform/create/provision-wizard`.
- Deploying a ready template from a gallery: use `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- Every field fits on one screen: use `platform/create/single-page-create`, or its Import from Git form for a single-page Git import.
- Choosing among all the things the user can create: use `platform/create/create-hub`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar` (required)
- B. Step rail — `Stepper` (required)
- C. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required after the first step)
- D. Where it runs — `Input`, `Item`, `Button` (required)
- E. Inline create — `Field`, `Input`, `Button` (optional)
- F. Method card — `Card`, `Item` (required)
- G. Footer — `SaveBar`, `Button` (conditional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/create/source-wizard.md](blocks/platform/create/source-wizard.md).

## Do

- Open on Where it runs, and let the user create a service inline or continue without one.
- Advance on the click for steps that are a single choice; show Next only where fields are typed.
- Let the rail go back to completed steps, never forward.
- Seed the inline create name from the search text and focus it.
- Describe each method by what the user does and what they get, in one or two sentences.
- Hand off to `platform/create/deployment-flow` on submit and end on `platform/create/deploy-success`.

## Don't

- Don't show a Next button beside a list where clicking a row already answers the step.
- Don't open a dialog or a new page to create the service; create it inline in the chooser.
- Don't list the method's own steps on the rail before a method is chosen.
- Don't hide the chosen service behind the six-row limit.
- Don't make the user scroll past the method card to reach the footer.

## Copy

- **Title and breadcrumb:** the create label with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Project".
- **Step titles:** short, with "Select" for a choice, e.g. "Where it runs", "Select a method", "Select a source", "Create and deploy".
- **Chooser instruction:** e.g. "Select a service to continue". Search placeholder and `aria-label`: e.g. "Search services".
- **No match:** the fact, e.g. "No service matches “api”." A count line states the rest, e.g. "4 more. Type to narrow the list."
- **Inline create row:** the create label, e.g. "Create Service". The field label: "New service".
- **Skip:** verb first, e.g. "Continue without a service".
- **Method card title:** the question, e.g. "How do you want to start?".
- **Method titles:** verb first, at most four words, e.g. "Import from Git", "Sync with the CLI", "Start from a template".
- **Final action:** names both acts, e.g. "Create and deploy".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: "Select", never "Choose"; no em dash in the count line; "Back" only for the previous step, never for Cancel.

## Accessibility

- The `Stepper` has an `aria-label`; disabled future steps cannot be focused.
- The `form` is labelled by the `PageHeader` title; a `fieldset` with a visually hidden `legend` names the flow.
- Service and method rows are native `button`s; service rows expose `aria-pressed`; icons, checks and chevrons are `aria-hidden`.
- The search has an `aria-label`; Enter picks the first match or opens the inline create.
- The inline create moves focus to its Name field and returns it to the list on Back.
- Step transitions and the footer's entrance honour reduced motion.

## States

- WhereItRuns: the first step; the centred service chooser with search, the Create Service row and Continue without a service; no footer until answered.
- Method: service-01 was chosen; the page heading over the three-method card, with only Back in the footer.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the provisioning log the last step submits into.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the screen the flow ends on.
- `platform/create/multipage-create` — the step wizard for resources without a code source; same Where it runs chooser.
- `platform/create/provision-wizard` — the wizard that provisions a service and binds a project.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — its Import from Git form is the one-page version of this flow.
- `Stepper` — the step rail; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Steps

- where-it-runs
- method
- source
- configure

## Variants

`WhereItRuns` (primary) · `Method`. Code: [blocks/platform/create/source-wizard.md](blocks/platform/create/source-wizard.md), `get_pattern("platform/create/source-wizard", { variant })`.

# ActivityOutcomesDashboard (`platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`)

> An activity outcomes dashboard: what a set of actors requested through the rules and what the rules decided.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Field, Hint, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, Select, SeverityTag, StatTile, Table, `TableRoot`, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

activity outcomes dashboard; requests and decisions; allowed vs blocked; policy decisions dashboard; request log dashboard; outcomes by actor; painel de atividades; decisões das regras; permitidos e bloqueados

The page an operator opens to answer "what did these actors ask for, and what did the rules decide?".
It counts every request by its outcome (allowed, blocked, held, approved, denied, over budget), shows
how those outcomes moved over time, breaks them down by actor, category and destination, and ends in
the request log, where each row names the rule that decided it. Every region reads the same filters,
so narrowing the time range or the actor moves the whole page at once.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A policy or rule engine decides on requests made by a known set of actors (agents, users, service
  accounts) and the reader needs the outcome mix and the evidence behind it.
- The outcomes are exclusive (one request has exactly one outcome), so they can stack.
- The reader needs to go from a total to the individual request and the rule that decided it on one page.

## When not to use

- The page monitors latency or error rates of services, not decisions: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- The subject is open alerts and their severity rather than every request: use
  `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.
- The reader only needs the log with filters and no summary: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Traffic volume per host or country with no decision behind it: use
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Refresh — `IconButton` (optional)
- C. Filter row — `Field` (required)
- D. Time range, actor, outcome and category — `Select` (required)
- E. Destination — `Input` (optional)
- F. Outcome tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- G. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- H. Chart and breakdown cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- I. Outcomes over time — `Chart` (required)
- J. Breakdowns — `BarList` (required)
- K. Outcome in the log — `Table`, `Tag` (required)
- L. Request log — `TableRoot` (required)
- M. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)
- N. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep every region on the same filters; a change of range or actor updates the whole page together.
- Stack only outcomes that are exclusive, and keep the series order the same in the chart, the legend,
  the tiles and the tags.
- Mark rising-is-bad tiles as `inverse`.
- Name the deciding rule in every log row.

## Don't

- Don't color a categorical series (actor, category) with a status token.
- Don't put a second filter row inside a card; the page has one set of filters.
- Don't hide an outcome with zero requests from the tiles; show `0` so the set stays complete.
- Don't explain a metric in its label; use the `Hint`.

## Copy

- **Title:** a noun phrase for what is reported. `Request activity`.
- **Description:** one sentence, what the page shows. `What each actor requested through the rules and what the rules decided.`
- **Filter labels:** one or two words, no colon. `Time range`, `Actor`, `Outcome`, `Category`, `Destination`.
- **Tile labels:** the outcome name in sentence case. `Over budget`, not `Over Budget (requests)`.
- **Hint:** one sentence defining the metric. `Requests the rules held for a person to approve.`
- **Empty state:** what is missing, then what fills it and what to do. `No requests in this time range` / `Requests the rules evaluate appear here. Widen the time range to see older ones.`
- **Outcome tags:** past participle, one word. `Allowed`, `Blocked`, `Held`.

## Accessibility

- The refresh control is an `IconButton` with `aria-label="Refresh"`.
- The filter container is labelled `Filters`, the tile grid `Outcomes`, each `BarList` names what it ranks.
- Every filter has a visible label through `Field.Label`; the destination placeholder is an example, not the label.
- Outcome is never color alone: the chart legend, the tooltip and the log `Tag` all carry the word.
- Times, counts and deltas use `tabular-nums` so columns do not jitter on refresh.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected time range.
- Loading: while the range loads, tiles, chart and breakdowns render their own `Skeleton` and the log holds Skeleton rows; nothing reflows.
- Empty: no request in the range; tiles show a dash with no delta, every card keeps its box with an empty state, and the log says to widen the time range.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — when the reader starts from open alerts instead of every request.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the same tiles, chart and table grammar for traffic volume.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the log on its own, as a filterable list page.
- `SeverityTag` / `Tag` — severity and outcome are separate columns with separate scales.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard", { variant })`.

# AlertsDashboard (`platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`)

> An alerts dashboard: what is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard/alerts-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Card, Chart, ChartCard, EmptyState, Hint, PageHeader, Select, SeverityTag, Skeleton, StatTile, Table, `TableRoot`, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

alerts dashboard; open alerts; alerts by severity; incident dashboard; false positive rate; alert triage; painel de alertas; alertas abertos; alertas por severidade

The page a security or operations lead opens to triage: what is open, how severe it is, what kind of
alert it is and which entities are involved. It leads with the open counts, shows how many alerts were
raised each day by severity, and ends in the open alerts table, ordered from critical to info, where
the reader picks what to work on next. Severity reads on one scale everywhere: tiles, chart, tags
and tables.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Alerts carry a severity level and the reader has to decide which to handle first.
- The reader needs both the trend (are we raising more?) and the queue (what is open now?) on one page.
- Alerts name entities (hosts, users, accounts) whose accumulated risk is worth ranking.

## When not to use

- Every request and the rule that decided it, not only alerts: use
  `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard`.
- Service health with latency and error thresholds and a short alert rail: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Items waiting for a verdict from an analysis engine: use `platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Only the list of alerts with filters: use `platform/view/table-view`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Summary tiles — `StatTile` (required)
- D. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Alerts per day — `ChartCard` (required)
- F. Daily stack — `Chart` (required)
- G. Open by severity — `Card` (required)
- H. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. Severity — `SeverityTag` (required)
- J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- K. Alerts by type — `BarList` (required)
- L. Highest risk and Open alerts — `TableRoot` (required)
- M. Alert status — `Table`, `Tag` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Use one severity ramp for every severity on the page, in the same order.
- Sort the open queue by severity first, then by age.
- Mark every count where growth is bad as `inverse`.
- Give each region its own empty state that says why it is empty.

## Don't

- Don't color severity with categorical series tokens, and don't use the severity ramp for anything else.
- Don't show a donut for open by severity; the reader needs exact counts.
- Don't add a per-card period selector.
- Don't collapse the page into one empty state when only some regions are empty; each region speaks for itself.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Alerts`.
- **Description:** one sentence on the page's job. `What is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved.`
- **Tile labels:** sentence case, no parentheses. `Critical or high open`, `False positives`.
- **Hint:** one sentence definition ending with a period. `Alerts nobody has closed yet, at any severity.`
- **Empty states:** state the fact, then the next step. `No alerts in this period` / `Nothing was raised in the last 30 days. Select a longer period.`
- **Severity labels:** the level only. `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`.

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; the tile row is a region labelled `Summary`.
- Severity is always a word in the `SeverityTag`, never a color alone; the chart tooltip lists every level by name.
- Counts and shares use `tabular-nums`.
- The `BarList` carries an `aria-label` naming what it ranks.

## States

- Default: the populated page for the selected period.
- Loading: tiles, chart, bar list and both tables render their own `Skeleton`; Open by severity holds Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no alerts; tiles show a dash with no delta, and every region keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that says why and what to do next.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard` — every request and its outcome, not only alerts.
- `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard` — blocked traffic and the rules that block it.
- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — threshold alerts beside service health.
- `SeverityTag` — the one severity scale the page shares.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard", { variant })`.

# AnalyticsDashboard (`platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`)

> The analytics dashboard pattern: KPI tiles, charts and a table that all read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard/analytics-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, PageTabs, Select, StatTile, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

metrics; metric panel; kpi tiles; sparkline; real-time metrics; analytics dashboard; painel de métricas; indicadores; analytics; traffic analytics; requests over time; period comparison; painel analítico; análise de tráfego; real-time metrics per product; product metrics; metrics by product; period filter; métricas por produto; métricas en tiempo real

The page a developer or operator opens to see how much traffic their services handled and how well
they handled it: requests, data transferred, success rate and server errors for the period, then the
charts and the table that explain those totals. Every tile, chart and the table read the same period,
so one change of range moves every region together. It is the reference grammar for the other
dashboards: KPI row first, a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s below, one shared card header.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The reader monitors volume and quality of traffic (requests, bytes, status codes) over a period.
- Several metrics share one time window and one set of dimensions (host, country, status code).
- The reader needs to move from a total to the breakdown and then to the rows behind it.

## When not to use

- Usage per project or product, with the previous period overlaid: use
  `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- Latency percentiles and live service health with an alert rail: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- Blocked and allowed requests and the rules behind them: use `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- The reader arranges the cards themselves: use `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. KPI row — `StatTile` (required)
- C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Aggregation and variation — `Tag` (required)
- F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- H. Expand — `IconButton` (optional)
- I. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)
- J. Charts — `Chart` (required)
- K. Table search — `Input` (optional)
- L. Top hosts — `TableRoot` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- N. Product and period — `PageHeader` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the KPI row to the four numbers the reader checks first; put the rest in cards.
- Use one card header layout for every card, so the controls are in the same place.
- Let one period drive every region.
- Keep the period when the product tab changes, so the reader compares products over the same window.
- Give each product the same grammar: four tiles, then cards of two per row.
- Distinguish "nothing recorded" from "nothing matches the search" in the empty copy.

## Don't

- Don't give a card its own period selector.
- Don't offer Line or Bar on a ranked breakdown; bars are the only form there.
- Don't put more than one search on the page header; table search belongs to its table.
- Don't use status colors for categorical series such as countries or hosts.
- Don't sum a rate or a percentile in a legend total; Metrics turns totals off for those cards.
- Don't nest product tabs inside a card; the product is a page-level choice.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Analytics`. **Description:** `Requests, data transferred and errors your services handled in the period.`
- **Card titles:** noun phrase, sentence case. `Requests over time`, `Status codes`, `Top hosts`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric name only. `Data transferred`, never `Data transferred (GB)`; the unit belongs to the value.
- **Hint:** one sentence ending with a period. `Requests that ended in a server error. A rise is a regression.`
- **Menu items:** verb first. `Copy query`, `Export CSV`.
- **Metrics:** title `Real-time metrics`; tab labels are product names; aggregation tags name the math (`Sum`, `Median`, `Percentile`).
- **Empty state:** `No traffic yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that names its card, plus a `Tooltip`.
- The `ToggleGroup` is labelled with the card it controls.
- The search `Input` has an `aria-label` equal to its placeholder, since there is no visible label.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign and a word, not color alone.
- The product strip is a tab list (`PageTabs`); the region under it is named after the product and the period (`Functions metrics, Last 24 hours`).
- Charts expose their table twin and keyboard model through `Chart`; do not replace them with a bare SVG.

## States

- Default: the populated dashboard for the period.
- Loading: every tile, chart and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`; the grid does not reflow.
- Empty: no traffic in the period; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState`.
- Metrics: real-time metrics per product, a `PageTabs` strip of products and a `Period` `Select` in the header; each product shows four tiles and four area, line or stacked bar cards.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — the same grammar for usage per project, with the previous period overlaid.
- `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard` — when the reader arranges the cards.
- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — latency percentiles and an alert rail.
- `ChartCard` / `StatTile` — the card and tile every dashboard shares.
- `platform/view/split-view` — the events behind these numbers, row by row.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` (DataStream) — where the streams counted under Data stream are set up.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed` · `Metrics`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard", { variant })`.

# CompositionDashboard (`platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`)

> A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard/composition-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DonutChart, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, PageHeader, Progress, Select, StatTile, `TableRoot`, Tag, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

composition dashboard; spend breakdown; cost by category; donut chart dashboard; stacked area chart; top contributors; mix over time; painel de composição; gastos por categoria; custos por categoria

The page that answers "what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?". The block's example is
the organization's monthly spend: the total and its three largest categories first, then the mix over
12 months, the current month's split, and the resources that drive it, ranked. The same shape fits any
total that breaks down into exclusive parts (storage by type, requests by product, seats by team).

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- One total splits into a small number of exclusive categories (up to six, plus Other).
- The reader needs both the current split and how it changed over time.
- The reader has to find the individual items that drive the largest share.

## When not to use

- The parts are not exclusive or do not sum to the total: use a multi-series line in
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` instead of a stack or a donut.
- The reader tracks progress against targets: use `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- Steps that people drop out of: use `platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard`.
- Changing the plan that drives the spend: use `platform/account/change-plan-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Export — `Button` (optional)
- D. Total and top categories — `StatTile` (required)
- E. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- G. Area or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- H. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)
- I. More options trigger — `IconButton` (optional)
- J. Spend by category — `Chart` (required)
- K. Current split — `DonutChart` (required)
- L. Top contributors — `TableRoot` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- N. Category and change — `Tag` (required)
- O. Share of total — `Progress` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the category order and colors identical across tiles, stacked chart, donut and table.
- Put the total first in the tile row, then the parts.
- Show a percentage next to every share bar.
- Mark spend tiles as `inverse`.

## Don't

- Don't use a donut for more than six slices; fold the tail into Other.
- Don't stack series that overlap or do not sum to the total.
- Don't color categories with status tokens; a category is not a state.
- Don't drop the absolute amount and show only the share.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Cost breakdown`.
- **Description:** `How the organization’s spend splits across categories and the resources that drive it.`
- **Tile labels:** the category name only. `Total spend`, `Compute`, `Database`, `Storage`.
- **Card titles:** `Spend by category`, `Current split`, `Top contributors`.
- **Donut center label:** the period it shows. `This month`.
- **Empty state:** `No spend in this range` / `Nothing was billed to the organization in the selected period.`

## Accessibility

- The period `Select` has `aria-label="Period"`; icon-only controls name their card.
- The donut has an `aria-label` (`Current split`) and its legend lists every category with its value.
- Each `Progress` names its resource; the percentage is visible text, not only the bar.
- Amounts and shares use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the populated breakdown for the period.
- Loading: every tile, both charts and the table hold their place with a `Skeleton`.
- Empty: nothing billed in the period; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and the stacked chart, donut and table each keep their box with an `EmptyState` that names the reason.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard` — targets and trends instead of parts.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — non-exclusive series as lines.
- `platform/account/change-plan-drawer` — where a reader acts on the spend.
- `DonutChart` / `Chart` — share now, mix over time.

# ConfigurableDashboard (`platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`)

> A configurable dashboard: the reader arranges the cards.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard/configurable-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, BarList, Board, Button, Chart, ChartCard, DonutChart, Hint, PageHeader, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

configurable dashboard; custom dashboard; drag and drop dashboard; resizable cards; edit layout; board; dashboard grid; dashboard builder; painel configurável; painel personalizado; reorganizar cards

A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it
is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about
different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and
height, in order) and binds it to `Board`, which moves, resizes, clamps and announces; the
`ChartCard` inside each `Board.Item` provides the drag handle and the resize corner.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The same dashboard serves readers with different priorities, and each comes back often.
- The cards are independent: none depends on its position to make sense.
- The product has somewhere to store per-user preferences.

## When not to use

- A dashboard read once to answer one question, or one whose order tells a story: use a static
  dashboard such as `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `platform/dashboard/executive-summary-dashboard`.
- The reader needs to add or remove widgets from a palette; this block only rearranges and resizes the
  cards it has.
- A single chart with editable settings: use `ChartCard` alone.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Edit layout, Done and Reset layout — `Button` (required)
- C. Grid — `Board` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Card definitions — `Hint` (required)
- F. Span while editing — `Tag` (required in edit mode)
- G. Split cards — `DonutChart` (optional)
- H. Ranked cards — `BarList` (optional)
- I. Time series cards — `Chart` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Keep the layout as data (id, span, height, order) owned by the page, bind it to `Board`, and persist
  it wherever the product stores preferences.
- Give every `Board.Item` the card title as its `label`; it is what moves and resizes announce.
- Announce a reset yourself in a polite live region (`Layout reset to the default.`); the board
  announces only what it did.
- Keep every card at its place and size in loading and empty states, so the reader can arrange it
  before data arrives.

## Don't

- Don't show handles outside edit mode; a dashboard that can be dragged by accident is worse than a static one.
- Don't let a card shrink below a span where its content stops reading (3 columns here).
- Don't put card menus, toggles or exports in the header; they conflict with the drag handle.
- Don't hide Reset layout behind a menu once the layout is customized.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Traffic overview`. **Description:** `Requests, regions, errors and response time for the period, in the layout you set.`
- **Mode button:** `Edit layout`, then `Done`. Never `Save`; changes apply as they happen.
- **Reset:** `Reset layout`.
- **Help line:** two short sentences on how, no layout positions. `Drag a card by its handle to move it, or by its corner to resize it. Focus a handle to use the arrow keys.`
- **Handle labels:** verb plus card title. `Move Requests over time`, `Resize Requests over time`.
- **Announcements:** full sentences with a period. `Layout reset to the default.`
- **Empty state:** `No requests yet` / `Metrics appear here once a service serves requests.`

## Accessibility

- The drag handle moves a card with the arrow keys; the resize corner changes span with Left and Right and height with Up and Down (`Board` handles both and mirrors them under right-to-left).
- Focus returns to the moved card's handle after a reorder.
- `Board` announces every move and resize in its own polite live region; the page announces the reset in an `aria-live="polite"` `sr-only` region.
- The board is a list named `Traffic overview cards`, one item per card.
- `Edit layout` exposes its mode with `aria-pressed`.
- Charts carry an `aria-label` equal to the card title.

## States

- Default: the arranged dashboard, read-only.
- Editing: handles and resize corners on every card, span tags in the headers, help line visible.
- Loading: every chart renders its own `Skeleton` inside its card; the layout holds its shape.
- Empty: nothing recorded yet; each card keeps its place and size and shows its empty state.
- Failed: the request failed; every card keeps its place, size and header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the static version of the same cards.
- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — a fixed dashboard when the order tells the story.
- `Board` — the grid component: layout model, bounds, reorder, resize and announcements.
- `ChartCard` — the card inside each item, with the drag handle and resize corner.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Editing` · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard", { variant })`.

# DataDashboard (`platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`)

> The data dashboard pattern: KPI tiles with sparklines and period-over-period deltas, followed by the breakdowns that explain them.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard/data-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/data-dashboard")`
- Components: Alert, Chart, ChartCard, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Hint, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, StatTile, `TableRoot`, Tag, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

data dashboard; metrics dashboard; kpi dashboard; stat tiles; data transferred; usage dashboard; breakdown charts; métricas; painel de dados; painel de uso

The usage page: how much the account's projects consumed in the period, how that compares with the
previous period, and which projects drove it. It leads with six KPI tiles (each with a sparkline and
the change against the previous 24 hours), then explains the headline number with this period against
the previous one, a ranking of projects and a table of usage per project.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The reader checks consumption across several products or meters (requests, data, jobs, images).
- The comparison that matters is this period against the previous one.
- Usage is attributed to projects or other owners the reader can act on.

## When not to use

- Traffic quality (status codes, success rate) rather than consumption: use
  `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`.
- Money, split by category: use `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard`.
- The reader arranges the cards: use `platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. KPI row — `StatTile` (required)
- C. Metric definitions — `Hint` (required)
- D. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- E. Aggregation and change — `Tag` (required)
- F. Line or Bar — `ToggleGroup` (optional)
- G. Control labels — `Tooltip` (required)
- H. Expand — `IconButton` (optional)
- I. More options — `DropdownMenu` (optional)
- J. Charts — `Chart` (required)
- K. Table search — `Input` (optional)
- L. Usage by project — `TableRoot` (required)
- M. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Compare against the previous period of the same length, and say so in the delta label.
- Keep the same card header on every card.
- Rank breakdowns largest first.

## Don't

- Don't color a rise in usage red unless it is a cost or a limit the reader wants to stay under.
- Don't mix units in one chart; one metric per chart.
- Don't add a per-card period.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Data usage`. **Description:** `What your projects consumed in the period, against the previous period.`
- **Tile labels:** the meter name. `Jobs run`, `Logs exported`.
- **Delta label:** what the change is against. `vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Card titles:** say what is compared. `Data transferred, this period vs previous`.
- **Series names:** `This period`, `Previous period`.
- **Empty state:** `No usage yet` / `Usage appears here once a project serves requests.`
- **No-match state:** `No matching rows` / `Change the search.`

## Accessibility

- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` naming its card and a `Tooltip`.
- The search `Input` has `aria-label="Search projects"`.
- Figures use `tabular-nums`; deltas carry a sign.
- The two comparison series differ in more than color (legend names, tooltip rows).

## States

- Default: the populated usage page.
- Loading: `Skeleton`s hold every tile, chart and table row in place.
- Empty: no usage recorded yet; each tile shows a dash, and every chart and the table explain that nothing was recorded.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — the same grammar for traffic quality.
- `platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard` — when the total is money split by category.
- `platform/account/change-plan-drawer` — where usage limits are changed.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/data-dashboard", { variant })`.

## Do

- Use status words for goals (`On track`, `At risk`, `Off track`), with color as reinforcement.

## Don't

- Don't add more than about six scorecard tiles; the page is read, not explored.
- Don't give trend cards different periods or sizes.
- Don't mark growth metrics `inverse`; only cost and error style metrics read a rise as bad.

# FunnelCohortDashboard (`platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboard`)

> A funnel and cohort dashboard: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort is retained.

funnel dashboard; conversion funnel; cohort retention; retention heatmap; signup to paid; growth dashboard; funil de conversão; retenção por coorte; painel de funil

- Use a dash, not zero, for a week that has not ended yet.

## Don't

- Don't color a retention matrix as a heatmap; a plain table with tabular figures is easier to compare.
- Don't sort the funnel by size.
- Don't add filters inside cards.
- Don't plot more than six cohorts as lines; fold the rest or narrow the period.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Funnel and retention`.
- **Description:** `How visitors move from a first visit to a paid plan, and how many of each weekly sign-up cohort keep coming back.`
- **Step names:** the state the user reached, one or two words. `Sign-ups`, `Activated`, `Paid`.
- **Cohort names:** the start date. `Oct 5 cohort`.
- **Column headers:** `Week 1` … `Week 6`.
- **Empty state:** `No visitors match these filters` / `Select another segment or widen the period.`, action `Clear filters`.

- Funnel bars are labeled with their values, and the step table states the same numbers as text.

- Empty: the filters match nothing; tiles show a dash with no delta or trend, and each card keeps its box with an `EmptyState` that names the filters and offers `Clear filters`.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- Many raw signals (latency, packet loss, DNS time, Wi-Fi signal) are combined into one score the
  reader can act on.
- The score has fixed bands that mean the same thing everywhere on the page.
- The reader's job is to find the worst application or place and the cause behind it.

## When not to use

- The raw metrics themselves (p50, p95, error rate) matter more than a score: use
  `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard`.
- A pass or fail verdict per item: use `platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboard`.
- Alerts triaged by severity: use `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Period — `Select` (required)
- C. Cards — `ChartCard` (required)
- D. Definitions — `Hint` (required)
- E. Band — `Tag` (required)
- F. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- G. Score per hour — `Chart` (required)
- H. Rankings — `BarList` (required)
- I. Hourly strips — `Tracker` (required)
- J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)
- K. Open incidents — `Card` (required)
- L. Incident rows — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Use the same three bands, with the same thresholds and words, in every region.
- Sort rankings lowest first.
- Name the top cause next to every poor score, so the reader knows what to fix.
- State the band thresholds in the overall `Hint`.

## Don't

- Don't show a score without its band word.
- Don't use the status colors for anything other than the bands on this page.
- Don't average away the worst hour; the hourly strip exists to show it.
- Don't sort rankings best first.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Experience score`.
- **Band words:** one word each. `Good`, `Fair`, `Poor`.
- **Cause:** subject, a middle dot, the cause in lowercase. `CRM · slow DNS lookups`.
- **Empty state:** name the period. `No open incidents in the last 24 hours` / `An incident opens when an application or a location stays poor for several samples in a row.`

## Accessibility

- Each `Tracker` has an `aria-label` naming its application, and each block a label with time, score and band.
- Bands are always words; the strip is never color alone.
- Rankings carry an `aria-label` (`Score per application`, `Score per location`).
- Loading regions set `aria-busy="true"`.
- Scores use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: the scored period.
- Loading: the chart, rankings and trackers render their own `Skeleton`; incidents hold Skeleton rows.
- Empty: a period with no samples; the score shows a dash with no band, and every region keeps its box with an empty state that names the period and says what fills it.
- Failed: the request failed; the score shows a dash, and every region keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard` — the raw latency and error metrics.
- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — when incidents are triaged as alerts by severity.
- `Tracker` — hour-by-hour status strips.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard", { variant })`.

# HomeDashboard (`platform/dashboard/home-dashboard`)

> The whole Home page body, in both of its states.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard/home-dashboard.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/home-dashboard")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, Button, Card, DropdownMenu, IconButton, Illustration, Input, Item, Popover, SearchTrigger, Spinner, StatTile, StatTileGroup, Tooltip, `use-console-layout`
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

home; home page; home dashboard; console home; usage overview; página inicial; início do console; first access; home empty state; new account home; welcome screen; first run; brand-new account; getting started home; primeiro acesso; tela de boas-vindas; home vazia

The Console's Home page: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job
is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and
the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a
brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors
to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on
each resource's own dashboard.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header, the search palette and the `main`. The populated Home fits the screen at `xl` (each resource panel scrolls its own rows), so its root carries `data-layout-fill` and scrolls itself (`overflow-y-auto`): below `xl` the root scrolls as one page, its content centred while it fits (`justify-center-safe`). The first-access screen (Empty) is a centred page with nothing pinned; it does not fill, and the layout's `main` scrolls it (`h-dvh` on the populated root only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- The landing page after sign-in in the Console.
- The reader needs to resume work (open a recent resource) more than to analyse data.
- The same page must serve both a populated and a brand-new account.

## When not to use

- Analysing traffic or usage: use `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` or
  `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- The empty first page of one resource list: use `platform/states/first-use`.
- Only the shell, with another page inside: use `shells/console`.
- A placeholder while Home loads: use the Overview and Onboarding wires of `platform/states/page-wires`.

## Building blocks

- A. Row actions — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- B. Control labels and metric definitions — `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Icon-only controls — `IconButton` (required)
- D. Usage band — `StatTileGroup`, `StatTile` (required)
- E. Agent onboarding — `Card` (optional)
- F. Resource rows — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Greet by first name in a muted heading; it is the only personal line on the page.
- Make every resource row a single link with the actions menu as a separate control.
- Let the user dismiss the agent card for good.
- Show the first-access screen, not a grid of empty panels, when the account owns nothing.
- Open the layout's palette from the first-access prompt with `useConsoleLayout({ optional: true })` and `layout?.openSearch()` (the body also renders alone, in its preview and test, where the call returns `null`); never wrap `useConsoleLayout()` in `try` / `catch`, and never mount a second `Command`.
- Mark the populated page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll, so the panels scroll their rows at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't add charts to Home; link to the dashboard that has them.
- Don't put more than four usage tiles in the band.
- Don't hand-build the band's card, grid or dividers around the tiles; `StatTileGroup` draws them.
- Don't pass figures as strings or flags as `'true'` / `'false'`: a tile's `value` and `delta` are
  numbers, and the string `'false'` is truthy.
- Don't nest the dismiss button inside the card's button.
- Don't show a second highlighted button next to `Agent`.

## Copy

- **Greeting:** time of day and first name. `Good morning, Alex`.
- **Tile labels:** the metric in sentence case. `Data transferred`, `Requests per second`.
- **Tile tooltips:** one sentence with a period. `Total bytes delivered across all your resources.`
- **Agent card:** imperative title plus one sentence. `Set up your coding agent` / `Give your editor a prompt that teaches it to build and deploy here.`
- **Empty panel:** `Nothing here yet.`
- **Prompt label:** `Search resources, pages and commands`.

## Accessibility

- The usage band is labelled `Usage` and the panels `Resources`; the layout owns the header, the rail and the one `main`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
- Row actions are reachable by keyboard: the menu trigger appears on focus as well as hover.
- On a new account the prompt opens the layout's command palette, which also opens with ⌘K / Ctrl K.
- Entrance animations and the card's dismiss transition honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: populated Home for an account that owns resources (usage band, agent card, resource panels).
- Empty: a brand-new account; the first-access screen with the greeting, the command prompt that opens the palette, and the three doors (create a project, add a domain with an availability check, set up an agent).

## Related

- `shells/console` — the shell Home renders inside.
- `platform/states/page-wires` — the Overview and Onboarding wires that hold Home while it loads.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the first-use state of one resource list.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — where usage detail lives.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/home-dashboard", { variant })`.

## Asked as

project status; sprint dashboard; project dashboard; tasks done; burndown; overdue tasks; status do projeto; painel do projeto; andamento da sprint

Where one project stands against its plan, one project and sprint at a time. A lead or a team member
opens it before a stand-up or a review to see completion, the sprint burndown, the next milestones,

## Asked as

scan results; scan dashboard; analysis verdicts; malware scan; flagged items; submissions in analysis; resultados da análise; painel de varredura; itens sinalizados

The page for a pipeline that sends items (files, attachments, packages) for analysis and gives each a
verdict. The reader checks what was submitted, what is still waiting, what was flagged, and above all
two exceptions: deliveries held until a verdict arrives, and items that were delivered before they

## When not to use

- F. Verdicts — `DonutChart` (required)
- G. Sources — `BarList` (required)
- H. Held and flagged — `Card` (required)
- I. Loading lines — `Skeleton` (required)
- J. Exception links — `Link` (required)
- K. Search — `Input` (required)
- L. Filters — `Select` (required)
- M. Submissions — `TableRoot` (required)

## Do

- Keep verdict colors identical in the donut and the table.
- Put the exceptions (held, delivered then flagged) in sentences with links, so each leads to an action.
- Offer an "Any" option on every filter so the default is the whole set.
- When nothing was ever submitted, replace the filters and the table with one empty state.

## Don't

- Don't show Pending as a failure; it is an unknown, not a verdict.
- Don't use the verdict hues for sources or categories.
- Don't keep filters visible over a table that can never have rows.

## Copy

- **Title:** `Scan results`.
- **Tile labels:** short noun phrases. `Held for a verdict`, `In analysis`.
- **Verdicts:** one word. `Clean`, `Suspicious`, `Flagged`, `Pending`.

- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

- `platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-dashboard` — decisions made in real time.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the submissions table on its own page.

> The security dashboard pattern: blocked and allowed requests over time, breakdowns by attack category and origin, the top sources and an attention list.

- Surface: product

## Asked as

security dashboard; waf dashboard; blocked requests; attack categories; threat origins; top attackers; painel de segurança; requisições bloqueadas; ataques

The page a reader opens to see what their security rules are doing: how many requests were blocked
and inspected, how blocking moved over time, which attack categories and countries it came from, which

## Do

- End every Needs attention entry with exactly one action.
- Mark blocking metrics as `inverse`.
- Replace the grid with one setup empty state when no rule exists; empty charts would only repeat it.
- Keep the attention list short; it is a queue, not a log.

## Don't

- Don't use the danger color for a categorical breakdown such as countries.
- Don't put more than one action on an attention entry.
- Don't show the full grid of empty charts when the cause is a missing rule set.

## Copy

- **Attention title:** the problem as a statement. `Service without a rule set`.

- Empty: no rule set yet; tiles read as dashes and one bordered `EmptyState` offers `Add rule set` instead of a grid of empty charts.
- Failed: the request for the period failed; tiles show a dash, and every card keeps its header with a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

> The service monitoring dashboard pattern: status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail.

service monitoring; monitoring dashboard; latency p95; error rate; uptime; service health; observability; monitoramento; painel de monitoramento; latência

The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many
requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and

## When not to use

- E. Window — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- F. Latency and error rate — `Chart` (required)
- G. Alert level — `Tag` (required)
- H. Loading placeholders — `Skeleton` (required)
- I. Alert rail — `Item` (required)
- J. Empty regions — `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md).

## Do

- Write the service state in words in every tile.
- Keep alerts in a rail that stays in view; fold it below the charts on narrow screens.
- Title an alert with the threshold that tripped, not with a generic name.
- Give each chart its own window.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill` and let it scroll (`overflow-y-auto`), so the panes scroll on their own at `xl` and the page scrolls as one below it.

## Don't

- Don't average latency into one line; show the percentiles.
- Don't use the status colors for percentile series.
- Don't make the rail scroll the page with it at wide screens.
- Don't hide the rail when there are no alerts; say `No open alerts`.

## Copy

- **Service state:** one word. `Operational`, `Degraded`, `Down`.
- **Delta label:** what is compared. `p95 latency vs previous 24 hours`.
- **Alert title:** metric, comparison, threshold with unit. `p95 latency above 800 ms`.
- **Alert time:** relative. `12 minutes ago`.
- **Empty rail:** `No open alerts` / `Alerts appear here when a service crosses a threshold.`

## Accessibility

- Each `ToggleGroup` names its chart.
- The rail's `Item.Group` has `aria-label="Open alerts"`. An independently scrolling region must be reachable by keyboard.
- The rail's scroll container is a `region` labelled by the `Open alerts` heading with `tabindex="0"`, so a keyboard user can scroll it in every browser.
- State and level are words (`StatusIndicator`, `Tag`), never color alone.
- Latency figures use `tabular-nums`.

## States

- Default: services reporting, both charts populated, open alerts in the rail.
- Loading: every tile, both charts and the rail hold Skeletons; the window switches stay usable.
- Empty: no traffic yet; tiles show a dash, both charts say metrics appear once a service serves requests, and the rail reads `No open alerts`.
- Failed: the request failed; tiles show a dash, and both charts and the alert rail show a danger `Alert` that names what did not load and offers Retry.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard` — the full alert queue with severity trends.
- `platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboard` — the same services as one experience score.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` — volume and status codes over a longer period.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Loading` · `Empty` · `Failed`. Code: [blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md](blocks/platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard.md), `get_pattern("platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-dashboard", { variant })`.

<!-- blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md -->

# DeleteWithConfirmation (`platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`)

> The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name as a click-to-copy chip…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation/delete-with-confirmation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation")`
- Components: Alert, Button, ConfirmDialog, Dialog, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogTrigger`, Field, Input, Item, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-ux-heuristics`, `webkit-microcopy`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

delete; delete dialog; delete confirmation; delete resource; type to confirm; destructive confirmation; remove resource; excluir; confirmar exclusão; excluir recurso; apagar; delete with confirmation; excluir com confirmação; form in modal; dialog form; modal form; blocking decision; type name to delete; confirm in dialog; formulário em modal; formulário no diálogo; modal com formulário

The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches. LabelledField draws the page it is opened from as a page body for `ConsoleLayout` (the layout owns the rail, the header and the `main`).

## When to use

- Any permanent delete of a resource, a folder of files or a record, opened from the row Delete action of `platform/view/table-view`, `platform/view/file-browser` or `platform/detail/record-table`.
- The resource takes other things with it (settings, instances, files) and the user must read that before confirming.
- A delete that lives in a settings page as its own row: use the LabelledField variant, a labelled field inside a medium `Dialog` opened from an outlined `Item`.

## When not to use

- Detaching a reference while the object survives: that is Remove, a plain action with an undo toast, not this dialog.
- A reversible change such as disabling or archiving: save it through `platform/settings/settings-form` or `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- A plain yes-or-no decision with nothing to type: use `ConfirmDialog` with its actions only, without the typed name.
- A failed or slow delete request: the submit lifecycle is `platform/states/async-submit`.

## Building blocks

- A. Dialog and trigger — `ConfirmDialog`, `Button` (required)
- B. Consequence — `Alert` (required)
- C. Name chip — `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Typed confirmation — `Input` (required)
- E. Actions — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md](blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md).

## Do

- Name the resource kind in the title and the resource itself in the chip, so the user knows exactly what goes.
- Keep the confirm button disabled until the trimmed value equals the name; that is the prevention, not a toast after the fact.
- Reset the typed value each time the dialog opens.
- Let the user copy the name from the chip; never block paste in the input.
- Put the consequence in the `Alert` and the sentence below it, before the input that asks for the decision.
- Use the LabelledField variant on a settings page, so the confirmation is a real labelled `Field`.

## Don't

- Don't delete on the first click, from a row menu or anywhere else.
- Don't enable Delete on a partial or case-insensitive match.
- Don't put the warning in the input's label or placeholder.
- Don't make Delete the only button, or use primary for it; it is `kind="danger"` beside an outlined Cancel.
- Don't clear the input as the dialog closes; the field would flash empty during the exit.

## Copy

- **Title:** Delete plus the resource kind, in sentence case, e.g. "Delete workload"; the visible trigger and the confirm button repeat it.
- **Trigger:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource" on a visible button; "Delete" in a row menu.
- **Alert:** one fact, e.g. "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed."
- **Consequence:** one sentence naming what goes with it, e.g. "The selected bucket will be deleted, along with all its files."
- **Prompt:** "Type" before the name chip and "to confirm." after it; never a position such as "in the box below".
- **Confirm:** the title's verb and object, e.g. "Delete resource"; never "OK", "Confirm" or "Yes".
- **Cancel:** exactly "Cancel".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- `ConfirmDialog` traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger.
- The input is named by the prompt paragraph through `aria-labelledby`, so a screen reader hears the name to type.
- The name chip is a real `button` whose `aria-label` switches from "Copy resource-01 to the clipboard" to "Copied resource-01"; its icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Enter in the input confirms only when the name matches; otherwise focus moves on to Cancel and Delete in reading order.
- In the LabelledField variant the `Field` label carries the prompt, so the name to type is part of the input's accessible name.
- Motion on the Copied reveal is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Default: the danger trigger is visible; opening it shows the warning, the name chip and the empty input with Delete resource disabled.
- LabelledField: an outlined `Item` row on a settings page opens a medium `Dialog` asking for the name through a labelled `Field`, with Delete resource disabled until it matches.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the row menu Delete that opens this dialog.
- `platform/view/file-browser` — Delete on a file or folder row.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — Delete on a record of a resource.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — where the LabelledField variant sits.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the delete request in flight and its failure.
- `ConfirmDialog` — the dialog this block fills; see `skills/webkit-form` for the Dialog form type.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `LabelledField`. Code: [blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md](blocks/platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.md), `get_pattern("platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation", { variant })`.

# AttachedResources (`platform/detail/attached-resources`)

> An attached-resources card in a resource settings tab, here its domains: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its depl…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources/attached-resources.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/attached-resources")`
- Components: Button, Card, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, Table, `TableRoot`, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-tables`

## Asked as

domains section; domains card; domains table; resource domains; domain list in settings; hostnames; seção de domínios; domínios do recurso; lista de domínios; attached resources; related resources table; recursos vinculados

A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

## When to use

- A section of a resource's Settings tab lists related records owned by that resource (domains, attached origins, bound certificates) and the list is short enough to read without search or paging.
- Each related record has two to four attributes worth scanning side by side, and one or two row actions.
- The user adds a related record from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The related records are many and need search, filters or columns: use the records table in `platform/detail/record-table`.
- A first-level list of one resource type reached from the sidebar: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Pairs of keys and values the user types in place: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Container — `Card` (required)
- B. Attached table — `TableRoot` (required)
- C. Environment chip — `Tag` (optional)
- D. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption` (required)
- E. Footer — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md](blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md).

## Do

- Keep the card unpadded and the table borderless, so there is one border around the whole list.
- Keep one chip per row: the Environment `Tag` (secondary, medium, rounded); every other attribute is plain text, with a glyph where it helps.
- Leave a cell empty when the attribute does not apply to that record.
- Hide the row menu on records the user cannot change, rather than showing disabled options.
- Count the records in the footer with the right singular or plural noun.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for column kinds and the action column.

## Don't

- Don't add search, filters or pagination; switch to `platform/detail/record-table` when the list needs them.
- Don't use a primary or large button for Add; the page's Save belongs to the settings form.
- Don't put Delete in the same group as Edit, or use a destructive color in the menu trigger.
- Don't write a dash or "None" in cells that do not apply.
- Don't wrap the table in a second card or give it its own border.

## Copy

- **Column headers:** short nouns without punctuation, e.g. "Domain", "Environment", "Policy", "Certificate".
- **Add action:** `Add <Module>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Add Domain"; never "Create" inside a resource.
- **Count:** a number and the noun, singular or plural, e.g. "1 domain", "3 domains".
- **Row menu:** single verbs, e.g. "Edit", "Delete"; the trigger tooltip reads "Row actions".
- **Attribute values:** the value as the product names it, e.g. "Production", "Managed".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The row menu trigger's `aria-label` names the record, e.g. "Actions for shop.example.com", so a screen reader user knows which row it acts on.
- Menu option icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the option label is the accessible name.
- The action column has no visible header; its cells hold only the labeled trigger.
- The menu is reachable by keyboard, opens on Enter or Space and returns focus to its trigger on close.
- The count is plain text, read after the table, before the Add button.

## States

- Default: three domains, one generated by the platform with no row menu, two the user added with Edit and Delete, and the footer counting them beside Add Domain.

## Related

- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the Settings tab whose Domains section renders this card.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — the full records table for longer related lists.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `TableRoot` — the table this card wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary). Code: [blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md](blocks/platform/detail/attached-resources.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/attached-resources", { variant })`.
