# DeploymentLogs (`platform/detail/deployment-logs`)

> The deploy logs block on its own: a Logs row that reports the step count and the step in flight while the run goes, or the outcome Tag, the time and the Phased or Complete switch once it has settled; then the pipeline…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs/deployment-logs.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/deployment-logs")`
- Components: Accordion, LogView, `LogViewContent`, Progress, Spinner, Tag, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

deployment logs; deploy logs; build logs; pipeline steps; log viewer; phased logs; logs do deploy; logs de build; etapas do pipeline

The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles.

## When to use

- Inside the deploy flow card of a create flow, while the deployment runs and once it finishes.
- In the Deployment logs card of a deployment detail page, for a run that has already settled.
- Any build or deploy pipeline with a fixed, known list of steps whose output the user needs to read.

## When not to use

- The whole deploy screen of a create flow, with its card, header and next steps: use `platform/create/deployment-flow`.
- The deployment page itself, with its status banner and facts: use the DeploymentDetail state of `platform/detail/details-page`.
- Events or logs explored over time with filters and a chart: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- A short async action that finishes in seconds: use the button's loading state from `platform/states/async-submit`.

## Building blocks

- A. Step list — `Accordion` (required)
- B. Running indicator — `Spinner` (required)
- C. Step output — `LogView`, `LogViewContent` (required)
- D. Run progress — `Progress` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md).

## Do

- Show the Logs row with the step count and the step in flight, e.g. "3/8 steps" and "Build", while the run goes.
- Once settled, replace the count with the outcome `Tag`, the total time, and a medium `ToggleGroup` between Phased and Complete labelled "Log view".
- Open the failed step automatically and mark every step after it Skipped.
- Inside a deploy flow card, move the Logs row controls up to the card header; on a deployment page, drop the Logs row and progress and put the controls in the Deployment logs card header.
- Keep step times in a code label at the end of each trigger.

## Don't

- Don't open several steps at once or auto-expand every step after a success.
- Don't show copy buttons while lines still stream.
- Don't print lines for steps that never ran in the Complete view.
- Don't summarize the error in a vague sentence; the failed step shows the reason in full.
- Don't animate the shimmer or the spinner when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Copy

- **Header:** "Deployment logs".
- **Running status:** count and step, e.g. "3/8 steps", "Build".
- **Outcome tags:** a past-tense word, or the failure and its step, e.g. "Completed", "Failed on Routing Rules".
- **Run time:** past tense with the duration, e.g. "Deployed in 42s", "Failed after 42s".
- **Step titles:** a short noun phrase in sentence case, keeping a product name as written, e.g. "Access token", "Install dependencies", "Routing Rules"; descriptions state the outcome without a period, e.g. "478 packages installed".
- **Waiting:** "Waiting to start…", the only place an ellipsis appears, because the step is in progress.
- **Skipped step:** two sentences, never a dash, e.g. "Never ran. The deployment stopped at Routing Rules."
- **View switch:** "Phased" and "Complete".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy` and `skills/webkit-errors`: say what failed and why, no "please", no exclamation in console copy.

## Accessibility

- Each step is an accordion trigger, a button that announces expanded or collapsed and is reachable by keyboard in run order.
- Status glyphs are `aria-hidden`; each step trigger carries its status as screen-reader text (Done, Running, Failed, Skipped, Not started) before its title, and the outcome tag carries the run's, so it never depends on color.
- While the run goes, the Logs row's step count and step in flight sit in a `role="status"` region, so a screen reader hears each step as it starts.
- The progress bar has `aria-label="Deployment progress"`; the view switch has `aria-label="Log view"`.
- Copy buttons on the logs announce what they copy.
- Shimmer and spinner animations stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- Running: the run is in flight; the Logs row shows 3/8 steps and Build, Build is open with the spinner and the progress bar runs along the bottom.
- Succeeded: every step checked, the last one open, a Completed tag with Deployed in 42s and the view switch, copy on every step log.
- Failed: the Routing Rules step is open on its error output with a Failed tag, the steps after it read Skipped and the Logs row names the failed step.
- CompleteView: a finished run in the Complete view, every line as one `LogView` with its copy button.
- FailedCompleteView: the failed run in the Complete view, the lines up to the error and nothing from the skipped steps.

## Related

- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the deploy flow card that hosts this block in a create flow.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the deployment page whose Deployment logs card hosts it.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — where a create flow lands once the run goes live.
- `LogView` — the log reader each step and the Complete view use; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the running and failed states.

## Variants

`Running` (primary) · `Succeeded` · `Failed` · `CompleteView` · `FailedCompleteView`. Code: [blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md](blocks/platform/detail/deployment-logs.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/deployment-logs", { variant })`.

# DetailsPage (`platform/detail/details-page`)

> The Overview tab of a resource detail page: the full-bleed tab bar, sticky while the layout scrolls, then the column that opens on the resource summary card.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/details-page/details-page.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/details-page")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Avatar, Button, Card, CodeBlock, ConsoleLayout, CopyButton, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, LogView, `LogViewContent`, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Popover, SaveBar, SectionHeader, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, TopologyDiagram
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

overview page; resource overview; detail page; summary page; deployment detail; application overview; deployment failed; página de visão geral; detalhe do recurso; página de resumo; details page with tabs; versions tab; build tab; detalhe com abas; resource summary; summary card; overview card; resource facts; status card; resumo do recurso; cartão de resumo; visão geral; details page; resource details; página de detalhes; application detail; application tabs; topology tab; deployment topology; detalhe da aplicação; topologia

The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A user opens one resource, service, policy or deployment from its list or from a deploy flow.
- The resource has more than one concern (overview, versions, build, deployments) that each deserve a tab.
- The user needs the live address, the status and the latest deployment of a resource at a glance, with Visit and the resource actions one click away.

## When not to use

- Many resources of one type to compare and filter: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Editing one version's settings, source or rules: use `platform/detail/version-detail`.
- Changing a resource's settings in a form: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- Following a deployment as it streams inside a create flow: use `platform/create/deployment-flow` with `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- A key and value list that belongs to the resource: use `platform/detail/record-table`.

## Building blocks

- A. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Summary subject band — `Card`, `Tooltip`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Summary facts band — `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Summary state band — `Button` (optional)
- E. Get started — `SectionHeader`, `ToggleGroup`, `Card`, `CodeBlock` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/details-page.md](blocks/platform/detail/details-page.md).

## Breadcrumb and environment

- The trail is in the layout's header: `breadcrumbs` from the route meta (`module › resource name`, e.g. Resources › analytics-app), or the page's own `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`. A page body never renders `Breadcrumb`, `GlobalHeader` or a `<main>`.
- A service ends the trail on its environment. That crumb is a control, so the page sets the trail itself: `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs` with the module and the service as `items` and, in its default slot, a `Select` with `kind="transparent"` and `size="small"` (no `w-full`: it sizes to its value like a crumb), labelled `Switch environment`, with a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy and Add Environment at its foot. The environment is part of the route, so picking one navigates and the page reads it. ServiceOverview and `shells/console` (DetailPage) show it.
- The layout hides its breadcrumbs while compact, so below md the service summary's Deployment Settings band carries its own environment menu.

## Topology tab

- Use `TopologyDiagram` for the path a request takes to the resource (Application and ServiceOverview both do). Binds, changes and removals are staged on the node, counted beside Deploy and listed in the deploy `Drawer`; the run ends in the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy. A production-checklist step that binds a slot (Bind Policy, Bind Error Page) scrolls to the topology and expands that node instead of opening a separate form.
- Bind, create and remove act on staged state only. Nothing reaches Production until Deploy, and the deploy drawer lists every staged change before it runs.
- Show the staged count on the tab row next to Deploy, so it stays visible from every tab.
- Report the deploy through the async-submit toast (Edit and Redeploy) and clear the staged marks once it succeeds.
- A node that collects many resources adds to itself through the diagram's `actions` slot: the Domains node of ServiceOverview carries an outlined small `IconButton` (`pi pi-plus`) named Add domain inside a `Tooltip`, picked by `node.key === 'domains'`. Never hand-draw a node card to get the `+`.

## Do

- Keep the content in `layout-column` with its boundary inset, and let the tab bar run full-bleed above it.
- Open the Overview tab on the summary card; every other section of the tab comes after it.
- Name the resource in the breadcrumb, not in a `PageHeader` title above the card.
- Put the one primary page action (Deploy) on the tab row, medium and outlined; keep Visit in the summary.
- Give Versions and Deployments the same controls row and table shape as `platform/view/table-view`, scoped to this resource, with a small section heading.
- On a deployment page, lead with a status banner (success, or danger with Redeploy) and disable Visit until the deployment is live.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't put the tab name in the breadcrumb, or repeat the resource name as a large heading.
- Don't add a second primary button to the tab row or the summary card.
- Don't spread the facts across several cards; one summary card holds them in bands.
- Don't hide the live address behind the actions menu; it is the card's primary link.
- Don't render empty facts as blank space; show the action that fills them, e.g. Connect Git repository under Source.

## Copy

- **Breadcrumb:** module, then the resource name as created, e.g. "Resources" › "analytics-app".
- **Tabs:** one or two nouns, e.g. "Overview", "Versions", "Build", "Deployments".
- **Fact labels:** a short noun, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Deployment", "Domains", "Status", "Created", "Source", "Framework".
- **Created:** relative time and author, e.g. "2 weeks ago by John Smith".
- **Actions:** a verb, e.g. "Visit", "Deploy", "Redeploy"; menu options "Copy URL", "Settings".
- **Link tooltips:** say where the link goes, e.g. "Open analytics-app-z1x2c3.example.com in a new tab".
- **State band:** one sentence on the next step, e.g. "To deploy to Production, drop your project anywhere on this page, connect Git, or run platform deploy via the CLI."
- **Failure banner:** what failed and what still serves, without an em dash, e.g. "A rule with the same behavior is already bound to this service, so the manifest was refused."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The body renders no landmark of its own: the layout's single `main` holds the tab bar and the tab content, and the rail and header are the layout's.
- The tab bar is a tablist; arrow keys move between tabs and the active tab is announced.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words, e.g. "Resource actions", "Add domain".
- Status uses a `StatusIndicator` with a text label, never color alone.

## States

- ResourceOverview: the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI, the summary card followed by Get started.
- Resource: the summary card alone, in its resource shape.
- Service: the service summary with its domains, environment menu, ID and the Deployment Settings band.
- Policy: the policy summary with the resource it protects, a Rules shortcut, its status, environment, rule count and modules.
- ResourceVersions: the Versions tab, a small Versions heading with Add Version over the controls row and the versions table.
- ResourceBuild: the Build tab, the Git repository, Build configuration and Deployment bands, with a save bar once a command changes.
- ServiceOverview: a service (its environment crumb is the page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`), Deploy on the tab row, the production checklist and the deployment topology on `TopologyDiagram` (policy, error page and origin slots staged until Deploy).
- DeploymentDetail: a deployment that went live, the success banner, the Deployment details card and the Deployment logs card.
- DeploymentFailed: a deployment the rules rejected, the danger banner with Redeploy, Visit disabled and the logs open on the failed step.
- Application: a whole application page body, with working tabs. Overview is the summary card; Versions and Deployments are a small `SectionHeader` over a flush `TableRoot`; Topology draws the request path with `TopologyDiagram` (domain, workload, firewall, application, function instance). Binding or removing the firewall or the function only stages the change: the node turns dashed with a Staged status, a polite status line names it, and the tab row shows the count as a warning `Tag` beside Deploy. Deploy opens a `Drawer` that lists each staged change as from and to, then runs on its own: a loading toast, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the Topology tab) and **Redeploy**, never View deployments.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list a row of which leads here.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — the section that follows the summary for a resource made from the CLI.
- `platform/detail/production-checklist` — the card on a service overview.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the steps inside the Deployment logs card.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — where a row of the Versions tab leads.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — the drawer the Deploy action opens.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the service Settings tab.
- `shells/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in; see `skills/webkit-navigation` and `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

`ResourceOverview` (primary) · `Resource` · `Service` · `Policy` · `ResourceVersions` · `ResourceBuild` · `ServiceOverview` · `DeploymentDetail` · `DeploymentFailed` · `Application`. Code: [blocks/platform/detail/details-page.md](blocks/platform/detail/details-page.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/details-page", { variant })`.

# GetStarted (`platform/detail/get-started`)

> The onboarding block for a resource made from the CLI: a section heading with a toggle between the CLI and GitHub Actions paths, then three numbered step cards, each with a code block for its commands.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/get-started/get-started.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/get-started")`
- Components: Card, CodeBlock, SectionHeader, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

get started; cli setup steps; github actions setup; onboarding steps; deploy with cli; numbered steps with code; primeiros passos; como começar; passos de configuração

The first thing a user reads about a resource they created from the CLI and have not deployed yet. They need the exact commands to build and ship it, in order, for the path they work with: the CLI on their own machine or a GitHub Actions workflow. The block names the two paths, lets them pick one and walks them through three numbered steps, each with commands they can copy.

## When to use

- Under the summary card on the Overview tab of a resource made from the CLI that has no deployment yet.
- At the end of a create wizard, on the deploy success screen, when the next move happens in a terminal.
- Any onboarding that comes down to three ordered steps with commands per step.

## When not to use

- A resource that already serves traffic: show the summary and its deployments in `platform/detail/details-page` instead.
- A list of gates to pass before going to production (domain, policy, error pages): use `platform/detail/production-checklist`.
- A module the account has never used: use `platform/states/first-use`, which explains the module before any resource exists.
- Connecting a repository or editing build commands: that is the Build tab of `platform/detail/details-page`.

## Building blocks

- A. Section heading — `SectionHeader` (required)
- B. Path switch — `ToggleGroup` (required)
- C. Step cards — `Card` (required)
- D. Commands — `CodeBlock` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md](blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md).

## Do

- Keep exactly three steps per path, in the order the user runs them: install or authenticate, connect, deploy.
- Make every command copyable and runnable as shown, with the resource name already filled in.
- Keep the two paths parallel: same number of steps, same card shape, same last step that ends in a live deployment.
- Point to the docs from the description, not from a separate button.

## Don't

- Don't add a primary button to the block; the action happens in the terminal or the repository.
- Don't put secrets or real tokens in a command; refer to the repository secret by name.
- Don't nest cards or put more than one `CodeBlock` in a step.
- Don't let a long command push the page sideways; the code block scrolls inside its card.

## Copy

- **Section title:** "Get started".
- **Description:** one sentence that names the choice, then the docs link, e.g. "Two ways to build and deploy this resource. Select one and follow the steps, or read the CLI docs."
- **Path options:** the tool names as their makers write them, e.g. "CLI", "GitHub Actions".
- **Step titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Install the CLI", "Link your project", "Push to deploy".
- **Step descriptions:** one or two sentences that say what the step does and why, e.g. "Authenticate, then link the local project to this resource so every deploy lands on it."
- **Copy button label:** names the step, e.g. "Copy the commands for Install the CLI".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The section title is a heading below the page `h1`; each step title is an `h3`.
- The toggle group carries `aria-label="Deploy with"`, so the switch reads as a choice of path.
- The step number is visible text, so the order is announced; the dashed connector is `aria-hidden`.
- Each copy button names its step, so several copy buttons on the page stay distinguishable.
- The docs link opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and keeps a visible focus ring.

## States

- Cli: the CLI path, install the CLI, link the project, then deploy and sync.
- Ci: the GitHub Actions path, store a personal token as a repository secret, add the deploy workflow, then push to the production branch.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — the resource Overview tab this block sits on, under the summary card.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the end of a create flow that can show these steps.
- `platform/detail/production-checklist` — the next set of tasks once the resource is live.
- `CodeBlock` — tabs, file name and copy for each step's commands.

## Variants

`Cli` (primary) · `Ci`. Code: [blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md](blocks/platform/detail/get-started.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/get-started", { variant })`.

# ProductionChecklist (`platform/detail/production-checklist`)

> A production checklist on a resource overview: a card that names the gates between the generated hostname and production, counts how many are done and lists each as a row, with an expand button that opens the same lis…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist/production-checklist.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/production-checklist")`
- Components: Button, Card, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, IconButton, Item, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

production checklist; go-live checklist; checklist; setup progress; launch steps; onboarding checklist; checklist de produção; lista de verificação; passos para produção

A service that is live on its generated hostname is not yet ready for real traffic. This card tells the user what stands between the service and production (a custom domain, a security policy, custom error pages), how many of those gates are done and which one to take next. It expands into a drawer where each gate explains itself and offers its action, and it shrinks to a single line once every gate is done.

## When to use

- On the Overview tab of a service or resource that is deployed but still has setup gates before it should take production traffic.
- When the gates are few (three to five), independent and each completed by one action elsewhere in the console.

## When not to use

- Commands to build and deploy a resource for the first time: use `platform/detail/get-started`.
- Ordered steps the user must complete before the resource exists: use `platform/create/provision-wizard` or `platform/create/multipage-create`.
- A list of resources already bound to this one: use `platform/detail/attached-resources`.
- A module the account has never used: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Checklist card — `Card` (required)
- B. Progress tag — `Tag` (required)
- C. Expand button — `IconButton` (required)
- D. Gate rows — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md](blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md).

## Do

- Order the gates by how much they matter for production; domain first.
- Count done gates in the tag and keep the count in step with the rows.
- In the drawer, give each open gate one outlined action named for what it adds, and replace it once done with a Done `Tag` and a muted sentence naming what it now serves.
- Collapse the card when every gate is done; keep the title, the success tag and the expand button.

## Don't

- Don't block the rest of the page or nag with an alert banner; the checklist is guidance, not an error.
- Don't put the gate actions on the card rows; the card only lists, the drawer explains and acts.
- Don't show a percentage or a progress bar next to the count.
- Don't remove the card once complete; the success tag confirms the service is ready.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Ship to production".
- **Progress:** "<done> of <total>", e.g. "1 of 3"; when complete, "Ready for production".
- **Gate titles:** verb first, sentence case, no period, e.g. "Add a custom domain", "Enable a security policy".
- **Gate descriptions (drawer):** one or two sentences on what the gate gives the service, e.g. "Answer 4xx and 5xx with your own page instead of the default response."
- **Gate actions (drawer):** `Add <Module>` or a verb and noun, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add Domain", "Attach Policy", "Add Error Page".
- **Done note:** a muted sentence beside the Done tag naming what the gate now serves, ending with a period, e.g. "Serving shop.example.com."; the tag itself reads "Done".
- **Drawer description:** one plain sentence on where the service stands, e.g. "This service is live on a generated hostname. These steps take it to production."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card title is an `h2` under the page `h1`; the drawer has its own title.
- The expand button has an `aria-label` that names what it expands.
- Gate icons and the done check are `aria-hidden`; each row announces "Done" or "Not started" in visually hidden text, so status never relies on color.
- Rows are real buttons, reachable by keyboard in reading order.
- The drawer returns focus to the expand button when it closes.

## States

- Card: some gates done; the card lists every gate with the count in its tag.
- Complete: every gate done; the tag reads Ready for production and the rows are gone.
- DrawerDetail: the expand button opened the right-side drawer with every step, its description and its action or its Done tag and note, over a Done footer; a card row opens the same drawer.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — the service Overview tab that renders this card under the summary.
- `platform/detail/get-started` — onboarding before the first deployment, for a resource made from the CLI.
- `platform/detail/attached-resources` — where an attached policy or error page shows up once added.
- `Item` — the row primitive for each gate; see `skills/webkit-ui-states` for the done and empty states.

## Variants

`Card` (primary) · `Complete` · `DrawerDetail`. Code: [blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md](blocks/platform/detail/production-checklist.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/production-checklist", { variant })`.

# RecordTable (`platform/detail/record-table`)

> A DNS zone detail page, opened from its index: a full-bleed tab bar with Main settings and Records over a scrolling tab panel.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/record-table/record-table.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/record-table")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Badge, Button, `CalendarRoot`, Card, Chip, CopyButton, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, Field, FileDropzone, HelperText, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, `ItemList`, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, SaveBar, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Table, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-navigation`

## Asked as

dns zone; dns records; record table; zone detail; nameservers; dnssec; records list; zona dns; registros dns; tabela de registros; import zone file; zone file; bind import; import dns records; importar arquivo de zona; importar registros dns

The detail page of a resource that owns a long list of records, here a DNS zone. The user arrives from the zones index to do one of two jobs: adjust the zone itself (name, nameservers, DNSSEC, status) and save, or find, add, edit and delete the records the zone answers with. A tab bar splits the two jobs so the settings form and the records table never share a scroll. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A resource has its own settings and also owns many child records that need search, filters, sorting and paging (DNS records, firewall entries, list items).
- Users copy values out of the resource into another system (nameservers, DNSSEC digests) and need a copy control next to each value.
- Child records are added from inside the resource, so the action reads `Add <Module>`.

## When not to use

- The child list is short and needs no search or filters: use `platform/detail/attached-resources` inside a settings section.
- A first-level list reached from the sidebar: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- A resource whose detail page is an overview with several tabs and no dominant record list: use `platform/detail/details-page`.
- Settings only, with no child records: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.

## Building blocks

- A. Tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `ItemList`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (required)
- C. Copyable values — `InputGroupRoot`, `Input`, `CopyButton` (required)
- D. Toggles — `Switch` (required)
- E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- F. Records heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- G. Filter popover — `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Button`, `Badge`, `IconButton`, `CalendarRoot`, `Input`, `Avatar` (optional)
- H. Toolbar and columns — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Field`, `Switch`, `Button` (optional)
- I. Applied filters — `Chip`, `Avatar` (optional)
- J. Records table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellLink`, `Table.CellActions`, `Tag` (required)
- K. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md](blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md).

## Do

- Keep settings and records on separate tabs, each with its own scroll.
- Show required errors only after a failed save, and clear each one when its field changes.
- Make every copyable value read-only and pair it with a `CopyButton` whose label names the value.
- Raise the save bar only when something changed, and keep it until Save lands or Discard restores the record.
- Reuse the table view controls row and table recipe in the Records tab so filters, search and columns behave the same as on index pages.
- Rewind pagination to the first page when filters or search change.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't put a primary or large Create button in the Records heading; it is `Add Record`, outlined.
- Don't validate on first render or on blur; the form is quiet until Save.
- Don't make nameservers or digests editable text the user could change by accident.
- Don't save Main settings from a button inside each section; one save bar covers the whole form.
- Don't let the records table scroll the page sideways.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** short nouns, e.g. "Main settings", "Records".
- **Section titles:** a noun or a short instruction, e.g. "General", "Configure your nameserver".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that ends with a period, e.g. "Give a unique and descriptive name to identify your zone."
- **Required error:** "This field is required."
- **Save bar:** the label states the fact, e.g. "You have unsaved changes."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Records heading:** title "Records", description one sentence, e.g. "The authoritative records this zone answers with."; actions "Documentation" and "Add Record".
- **Copy buttons:** name the value, e.g. "Copy nameserver 1", "Copy record value".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form is labeled "Zone settings" and its fieldset has a visually hidden legend with the same words.
- Each `Input` has an `aria-label` matching its row title; an `Input` with an error points to its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` and a `Tooltip` with the same words; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`, and so does the filter `Badge`.
- Search has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, "Search records".
- Focus order follows reading order: tabs, form fields, save bar; or heading actions, Filter, search, toolbar, chips, table, pagination.
- Tab panel entrances respect reduced motion.

## States

- MainSettings: the Main settings tab with General, nameservers, DNSSEC and Status; the save bar appears on the first edit.
- Records: the Records tab with the zone's one A record, the ID column hidden by default.
- ImportZoneFile: Import zone file, beside Add Record, opens a large `Drawer`. The file comes from a `FileDropzone` (one `.zone`, `.txt` or `.db` file; a rejected or empty file shows an invalid `HelperText` under it) or is pasted into a `Textarea`. Every line is previewed in a `TableRoot`: line number, name relative to the origin, type, value and a Ready, Skipped or Error `Tag`, with the reason under the value. The counts sit in a polite status line, errors add a danger `Alert` above the preview, and Import N records (disabled at zero) adds only the ready lines, then a toast says how many were imported and how many lines were left out.

## Importing a zone file

- Parse on the client as the text changes and preview every line before anything is written; never import on drop.
- Name the line number on every row, so the user can fix the file.
- Skip with a reason what the zone manages itself (SOA, apex NS) and types it does not support; mark as errors only values that are wrong.
- Import what is ready even when some lines fail, and say in the toast how many were left out.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the index this page is opened from, and the source of the controls row recipe.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern used by Main settings.
- `platform/detail/attached-resources` — a short related list inside a settings section.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.

## Variants

`MainSettings` (primary) · `Records` · `ImportZoneFile`. Code: [blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md](blocks/platform/detail/record-table.md), `get_pattern("platform/detail/record-table", { variant })`.

# VersionDetail (`platform/detail/version-detail`)

> One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab, as a page body for ConsoleLayout: the layout's last crumb is a transparent select that switches between the resource versions, each with its state Tag, or creat…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/detail/version-detail/version-detail.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/detail/version-detail")`
- Components: Avatar, Button, Card, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, DropdownMenu, Field, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, PageTabs, Resizable, ScrollArea, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, SplitButton, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

version detail; resource version; draft version; version history; version switcher; versioned settings; detalhe da versão; histórico de versões; versão rascunho; revert version; rollback version; reverter versão; revertir versión; environment switcher; environment crumb; switch environment; seletor de ambiente

One version of a resource, opened from its Versions tab. The user is here to change a draft and ship it, or to read what a built version holds and redeploy it or branch a new version from it. The page keeps the version they are on in the breadcrumb, where they can switch to another, puts the version's settings in tabs, pins the state and the save or deploy action to the bottom, and opens the version history beside the work when they need to see what changed. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The workspace pins its own bars, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview) and its panes scroll.

## When to use

- A resource whose configuration is versioned: drafts are edited, built and deployed, and built versions are read-only.
- The user opens a row of the Versions tab of `platform/detail/details-page`, or creates a new version.
- The version has several areas of settings (Settings, Source, Variables, Cache Settings, Custom Code, Rules) that share one save and deploy action.

## When not to use

- The overview of the resource itself, its domains and deployments: use `platform/detail/details-page`.
- A resource without versions whose settings save in place: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- The Rules tab content: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- Deploying from a list without opening a version: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Version switcher — `ConsoleLayout`, `Select`, `Input`, `Tag`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- B. Workspace — `Resizable` (required)
- C. Version tab bar — `PageTabs`, `Tabs`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` (required)
- D. Settings panel — `ScrollArea`, `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Switch`, `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Version bar — `Tag`, `SplitButton`, `Button` (required)
- F. Version history — `IconButton`, `Tag`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button`, `Avatar` (optional)
- G. Revert — `Button`, `Tag` (optional, on an earlier Ready version)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/detail/version-detail.md](blocks/platform/detail/version-detail.md).

## Do

- Keep one primary action on the page, in the version bar; the tabs share it.
- Lock the settings fieldset, not each control one by one, when the version is built.
- Let the user switch versions from the breadcrumb without going back to the list.
- Set the trail from the page with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`, and mark the root with `data-layout-fill`.
- Show the state in three places that agree: the breadcrumb option, the tab row tag and the version bar.
- Keep the history pane collapsible and resizable so the settings keep their width when it is closed.
- Show what a revert changes before it runs: the settings with old and new values, and the rules added and removed.
- Report a revert like any deploy: one toast that turns into the outcome, with Edit and Redeploy.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't let a built version look editable; disable the fieldset and say Read-only.
- Don't size the body with `calc(100dvh - …)`.
- Don't put Save or Deploy in the tab row or the page header.
- Don't name a tab in the breadcrumb.
- Don't list every earlier version at once; show five and Show older.
- Don't save a description edit without Cancel and Save buttons.
- Don't revert without a confirmation, and don't make the diff depend on an arrow glyph or color alone.
- Don't delete or hide the version a revert replaces; it stays in history.
- Don't offer View deployments on the revert toast.

## Copy

- **Version state tags:** one word, e.g. "Draft", "Deployed", "Ready", "Editable", "Read-only".
- **Version bar:** one sentence on what the user can do, e.g. "This version is open for editing. Deploy it when ready." or "Viewing a deployed version".
- **Save actions:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Save and deploy", "Save and build", "Save".
- **Built version actions:** "Add Version", "Redeploy"; on an earlier version "Revert to <id>".
- **Revert:** bar "Viewing an earlier version"; dialog title "Revert to <id>?", description "Reverting deploys <id> to Production in place of <deployed>. <deployed> stays in the version history, so you can redeploy it later."; diff heading "What changes against <deployed>"; toasts "Reverting to <id>…" then "<id> is deployed.", actions "Edit" and "Redeploy".
- **Version picker:** search placeholder "Search versions", no-match line `No versions match "<query>".`, footer "Add Version".
- **Setting rows:** a noun title and one sentence with a period, e.g. "Active" with "When disabled, the resource stops serving traffic."
- **History:** "Current version", an empty changes line, e.g. "No changes yet. Each change you save shows up here.", description placeholder "What changed in this version?".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The body renders no `main`: the layout's single `main` holds the workspace; the Settings `PageHeader` title is its heading, and the history pane is a region labelled by its "Version history" `h2`.
- The resize handle has an `aria-label` and works with arrow keys.
- The version `Select` trigger is named "Switch version"; its search input is named "Search versions".
- Every `Switch` and `Input` in a setting row has an `aria-label` that matches the row title.
- A disabled control with a reason gets a `Tooltip` that the keyboard can reach.
- The revert dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to Revert on close. Each changed setting carries a visually hidden sentence ("changes from On to Off"); the struck-through values and the arrow are `aria-hidden`. The toasts live in the app's one `Toaster` region (the app mounts it; the page body only calls `toast`), and the bar's status line announces "Reverting to <id>…".
- Icon-only buttons (Version actions, Close version history, Edit version info) have an `aria-label`; decorative icons are `aria-hidden`.

## States

- Draft: the editable draft on its Settings tab, with the Editable tag and the Save and deploy split button in the version bar.
- Deployed: the deployed version, read-only, the fieldset disabled and the version bar offering Add Version and Redeploy.
- Revert: an earlier Ready version, read-only, with history open, Revert to <id> in the bar, a confirmation with the diff, and the revert reported by a toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- VersionHistory: the draft with Version history open beside it, the current version, the empty changes entry and the five newest earlier versions.
- EnvironmentCrumb: a resource that is deployed to several environments. The page's `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs` ends on two control crumbs, environment then version, each a small transparent `Select` with a search field (`Switch environment`, `Switch version`). Environments carry their deployment policy as a `Tag` and Add Environment in the footer; picking an environment moves the version crumb to the version live there, and each version option says where it is live (Live in Production). The environment always comes before the version, because a version is chosen within an environment.

## Related

- `platform/detail/details-page` — its Versions tab lists the versions that open here.
- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — the content of the Rules tab.
- `platform/create/deploy-drawer` — deploying a version outside this page.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — how the version bar locks while Save and deploy runs.
- `SettingRow` — the row primitive of every settings section; see `skills/webkit-form` and `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

# AttributeEditor (`platform/edit/attribute-editor`)

> A key/value editor, drawn as a variables list page and the Create Variable drawer its heading action opens.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/attribute-editor/attribute-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/attribute-editor")`
- Components: Alert, AttributeEditor, Avatar, Button, Card, Checkbox, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, HelperText, IconButton, Input, `InputGroupAddon`, `InputGroupRoot`, MultiSelect, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SettingsSection, Switch, Table, `TableRoot`, Textarea, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

variables; environment variables; env vars; secrets; create variable; edit variable; variables list; version history; variáveis; variáveis de ambiente; segredos; criar variável; key value editor; attribute editor; .env upload; editor de chave e valor; delete variable; clone variable; paste .env; paste env file; import .env; colar .env; importar variáveis; dotenv; network list; ip list; asn list; country list; bulk paste; lista de rede; lista de ips; lista de red

A list of key and value pairs and the drawer that edits them, here environment variables. The user scans the variables already defined, then opens Create Variable to type or paste several pairs at once, mark the sensitive ones as secret, and select where they apply (the whole account, or specific environments, projects, services or policies) before saving them in one step. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- Users define many free-form pairs of a name and a value (environment variables, headers, metadata, tags) and often bring them from a file.
- Some values are sensitive and must be masked and write-only once saved.
- Each pair applies to a scope the user picks from existing resources.

## When not to use

- Conditions and actions evaluated in order: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` or `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- A short read-only list of related records inside a settings tab: use `platform/detail/attached-resources`.
- A long document or code the user edits as text: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Controls row — `PropertyFilter`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- C. Variables table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellLink`, `Avatar`, `Tooltip` (required)
- D. Row actions — `Table`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- E. Create and edit drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent` (required)
- F. Variables section — `SettingsSection`, `Button`, `ToggleGroup` (required)
- G. Key and value rows — `AttributeEditor`, `Field`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Checkbox`, `HelperText` (required)
- H. Paste .env panel — `Button`, `Textarea`, `HelperText` (optional)
- I. JSON view — `Textarea`, `HelperText` (optional)
- J. Scope — `SettingsSection`, `InputGroupRoot`, `InputGroupAddon`, `MultiSelect`, `Input`, `Switch`, `HelperText` (required)
- K. Drawer footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)
- L. List states — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- M. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input`, `Button` (required)
- N. Network list drawer — `Drawer`, `SettingsSection`, `ToggleGroup`, `Button`, `Textarea`, `HelperText`, `AttributeEditor`, `MultiSelect` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/edit/attribute-editor.md](blocks/platform/edit/attribute-editor.md).

## Do

- Validate only after Save is pressed; then flag each empty, malformed or duplicated key under its own pair and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep secret values masked in the list and in the drawer, and say in the hint that secrets are write-only once saved.
- Let users bring pairs in bulk: Upload, Paste .env, paste into a key, or edit as JSON.
- Before pasted pairs land, say how many were found, which lines are skipped and which keys will be replaced.
- Build the rows on `AttributeEditor` so add, remove, focus and announcements behave the same on every key and value editor.
- Keep the label of each field inside its `InputGroupAddon`, tied to the field by `for`.
- Reset the drawer on open so a closed and reopened drawer never shows stale rows.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for required states and `skills/webkit-lists` for the list page.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't show required errors on first render or while the user is still typing the first pair.
- Don't offer Remove on the last remaining pair.
- Don't drop invalid pasted lines silently, and don't add duplicate keys from a paste: replace the existing value and say so.
- Don't reveal a saved secret value in the table, a tooltip or the copy control.
- Don't add a Cancel button beside Save; `DrawerClose` and the overlay close the drawer.
- Don't keep Global on together with a specific scope.

## Copy

- **Title and create action:** "Variables" and "Create Variable"; the drawer title repeats "Create Variable", or reads "Edit Variable" from a row.
- **Empty states:** "No variables yet" / "Create a variable to store a value your services read at runtime."; "No matching variables" / "No variable matches these filters."
- **Delete dialog:** title and danger button "Delete variable"; the prompt reads "Type API_BASE_URL to confirm."
- **Field placeholders:** show the format, e.g. "MY_VARIABLE" for the key, "my-variable-value" for the value.
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "Key is required.", "Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.", "Select at least one resource for this scope."
- **Secret control:** "Mark as secret" and "Unmark as secret"; the hint states the rule, e.g. "Secret values are hidden and write-only after saving."
- **Network list:** title "Create Network List"; types "IP/CIDR", "ASN", "Countries"; panel label "Paste one address per line"; report "7 entries found. Text after # is kept as the comment.", "Lines 4 and 8 are not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range; they are added with an error to fix.", "Line 7 is already in the list and will be skipped."; row error "198.51.100.300 is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range."; toast "Office and partners created."
- **Paste panel:** label "Paste .env contents"; report "3 variables found. Lines starting with # are ignored.", "Line 5 is not KEY=value with an uppercase key and will be skipped.", "CACHE_TTL is already in the list; its value will be replaced."; buttons "Paste .env", "Add 3 variables", "Cancel".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Upload", "Add variable", "Save".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every key and value field has a visible `label` in its addon; an invalid field sets `aria-invalid` and points to its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`.
- Icon-only controls (Remove variable, Show value, Hide value, row actions, toolbar) carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`.
- The Secret `Checkbox` and each scope `Switch` have an `aria-label` naming what they toggle, e.g. "Enable Project scope".
- The `ToggleGroup` is labeled "Variables view"; the hidden file input is removed from the tab order and the Upload button triggers it.
- Adding a pair moves focus to its new Key field; removing one moves focus to the pair now in its place (or Add variable); both are announced in a polite live region by `AttributeEditor`.
- The paste panel's `Textarea` is described by its report, so skipped lines and replaced keys are read with the field; Paste .env exposes `aria-expanded`, and applying announces how many variables were added.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to Create Variable on close.

## States

- List: the variables list page with the controls row and table; the drawer is closed.
- First use: no variables yet; the card holds the first-use `EmptyState` with Create Variable.
- No match: the filter matches nothing; the table shows the no-match `EmptyState` with Clear filters.
- Edit: a row's Edit opens the drawer on that variable; Save replaces it in the list.
- Delete: a row's Delete opens the typed confirmation; confirming removes the row.
- Create: the drawer open with one empty pair, the Form view and Global on; errors appear only after Save.
- PasteEnv: Create Variable opens the drawer with one pair and the Paste .env panel holding a pasted file with a comment, an `export`, a skipped lowercase line and a repeated key that is already in the list; Add 3 variables merges them.
- NetworkList: Create Network List opens the drawer named Office and partners, type IP/CIDR, with the Paste list panel holding nine lines: a comment line, two lines that are not valid addresses and one already pasted above; Add 7 entries appends them as rows, the two invalid ones showing their errors.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the general drawer create pattern this drawer follows.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the controls row and table recipe the list page reuses.
- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — a drawer for ordered conditions and behaviors instead of free pairs.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — when and how errors appear after Save.
- `InputGroupRoot` — joins label, field and actions into one row; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `AttributeEditor` and `TagEditor` — the components behind the rows; `TagEditor` for resource tags.

# CodeEditor (`platform/edit/code-editor`)

> The code editor page, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the service): the Code and Settings tabs, an editor toolbar whose ToggleGroup switches between the Code document and the Arguments doc…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/code-editor/code-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/code-editor")`
- Components: Button, Card, CodeEditor, CopyButton, EmptyState, Field, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, KeyValuePairs, Link, LogView, `LogViewContent`, PageTabs, RadioButton, `ResizableHandle`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableRoot`, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, StatusIndicator, Switch, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, Trace
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

code editor; code editor page; function code editor; editor page; code and arguments editor; split editor; monaco editor; editor de código; página do editor; editar código; function editor; edge function; function detail; function arguments; json schema arguments; function settings; editor de função; argumentos da função; detalhe da função; test run; function test; run trace; span waterfall; invocation trace; testar função; execução de teste; rastreamento da execução

The editing page of a service whose behavior lives in source code. The user writes and saves the code, defines the argument form each instance of the service asks for (its fields, types and defaults), and adjusts the service's settings. The editor fills the page so the code has room, and one save bar commits code, arguments and settings together. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the Services breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`. The editor pins its own panes, so its root carries `data-layout-fill`: the layout's `main` stops scrolling and the root fills it (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- A resource is mainly a document the user edits as text: function code, a schema, a configuration file.
- The document comes with a structured companion (an argument form) that is easier to edit as fields than as JSON, and the user wants both views side by side.
- The same resource also has a few settings, shown on a second tab of the same page.
- The user tests the code before saving it and needs to read where the run spent its time and what it printed (variant TestRun).

## When not to use

- A resource made only of settings: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- Ordered conditions and actions the user composes without code: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`.
- Free key and value pairs such as environment variables: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- Running queries and reading results: use `platform/view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Editor toolbar — `ToggleGroup`, `Button` (required)
- C. Code document — `CodeEditor`, `HelperText` (required)
- D. Test run — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle` (optional)
- E. Arguments split — `ResizableRoot`, `ResizablePane`, `ResizableHandle`, `CodeEditor`, `Button` (required)
- F. No fields — `EmptyState`, `Button`, `Link` (optional)
- G. Field list — `Card`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- H. Field settings — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Textarea`, `HelperText` (required)
- I. Settings tab — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `Field`, `RadioButton`, `Switch`, `HelperText` (required)
- J. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md](blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md).

## Do

- Let the editor fill the pane; the page scrolls inside the editor, not around it.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`.
- Show the schema JSON and the fields form side by side, so the user can check one against the other.
- Keep collapsed fields as one-line summaries with their tags, and open settings only for the field being edited.
- Lock fields that cannot change after creation, with a lock glyph and a description that says so.
- Use one save bar for both tabs, and take the user to the tab that holds the error.
- Show a test run under the code it ran, on the same page: the trace and the logs on one clock, the summary first.
- Select the span the user most likely wants (the slowest or the failed one) when the run finishes.

## Don't

- Don't put the code editor inside a card, a drawer or a modal.
- Don't add a page heading above the tabs; the layout's breadcrumb names the service.
- Don't size the page with `calc(100dvh - …)`; it overflows under a notification.
- Don't save from inside the Arguments pane or a field; Save lives in the bar.
- Don't flag a new field's name before the user has touched it.
- Don't let the schema pane squeeze the fields pane below a usable width; collapse it instead.
- Don't open a test run in a dialog or a new page; it covers the code the user is about to fix.
- Don't save as a side effect of Run test; a test runs the code in the editor, saved or not.
- Don't report a test run with a toast; the result lives in the pane, where the user is looking.

## Copy

- **Tabs and documents:** single nouns, e.g. "Code", "Settings", "Arguments".
- **Field count:** a number and the noun, e.g. "1 field", "2 fields".
- **Buttons:** verb first, three words or fewer, e.g. "Add field", "Remove form", "Discard", "Save".
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, e.g. "This form has no fields"; description says what to do, e.g. "Add the first argument the service reads."
- **Errors:** short and specific, e.g. "This field is required.", "Another field already uses this name."
- **Save bar:** "You have unsaved changes."
- **Test run:** status as one word ("Completed", "Running", "Failed"); the outcome as the status code and what happened, e.g. "200, served from the transform and written to cache."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Both editors have an `aria-label` that names the document, e.g. "Source code", "Argument form schema, as JSON".
- The split is labeled "Argument form", its panes "Schema" and "Fields", and the handle "Resize the schema".
- Field grips are focusable buttons named "Reorder" plus the field name, and move the field with the arrow keys.
- The expand button sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and names the field it opens.
- Every icon-only control has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar's motion respects reduced motion.
- In TestRun the vertical split is labeled "Code and test run", its panes "Source code" and "Test run", and the handle "Resize the test run". The pane is a `section` named by its Test run heading, with Trace and Logs as `h3`s.
- The trace is a `treegrid` with one tab stop (see `Trace`); the running state is announced by a `status` line.

## States

- Code: the Code tab with the Code document filling the editor pane.
- Arguments: the Arguments document of image-optimizer, the schema on the left and two fields on the right, one expanded.
- NoArguments: the Arguments document of a service with no form, the empty schema and the no fields empty state.
- TestRun: the Code document with a finished test run of image-optimizer under it, the origin fetch selected in the trace; Run test shows the running state.
- Settings: the Settings tab with General, Runtime, Execution environment and Status; editing raises the save bar.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the settings form and save bar pattern the Settings tab follows.
- `platform/view/query-editor` — an editor page that runs queries and shows results.
- `platform/view/split-view` — the events explorer, where the logs of every run land.
- `Trace` — the span waterfall of the test run.
- `platform/detail/version-detail` — reading a deployed version of the code.
- `ResizableRoot` — the split between schema and fields; see `skills/webkit-layout`.

## Variants

`Code` (primary) · `Arguments` · `NoArguments` · `Settings` · `TestRun`. Code: [blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md](blocks/platform/edit/code-editor.md), `get_pattern("platform/edit/code-editor", { variant })`.

# EditResource (`platform/edit/edit-resource`)

> The settings page of a resource, a page body for ConsoleLayout (the layout's breadcrumb names the resource): a small Settings page heading over stacked `SettingsSection` bands in the form column, each a heading with a…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource/edit-resource.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/edit-resource")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CodeBlock, CodeEditor, ConfirmDialog, ConsoleLayout, CopyButton, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, Field, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PasswordInput, RadioButton, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Switch, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip, `use-unsaved-changes`
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-layout`, `webkit-ux-heuristics`

## Asked as

settings page; resource settings; settings tab; application settings; workload settings; firewall settings; edit settings; página de configurações; configurações do recurso; aba de configurações; save bar; unsaved changes bar; sticky save bar; discard and save; commit bar; barra de salvar; alterações não salvas; salvar alterações; edit resource; editar recurso; data stream; data stream settings; log streaming; stream destination; sampling; log template; configurações do data stream; envio de logs; streaming de logs; stale record; changed elsewhere; overwrite changes; conflict on save; danger zone; delete resource; type the name to confirm; zona de perigo; excluir recurso; alterado em outro lugar; leave page guard; unsaved changes dialog; cache settings; cache policy; browser cache; edge cache; tiered cache; configurações de cache; protocol settings; https ports; http/3; tls version; mutual authentication; mtls; autenticação mútua

The settings page of one existing resource. The user comes here to change how the resource is named, what it runs with and whether it is active, review the change, and commit it or throw it away. Every field sits in a labeled section of the form column, and one save band appears only once something has changed, so the page reads as the resource's current state until the user edits it. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header with the resource breadcrumb, the ⌘K palette and the `main`; the save band sticks to the bottom of the layout's scrolling region.

## When to use

- A resource has a Settings tab (or, with no tabs, its own `/<resource>/:id/settings` page) with fields grouped into a few sections.
- Changes are reviewed together and committed in one save, with a way to discard them all.
- Some settings are fixed or paid and must be shown locked, with the reason beside them.

## When not to use

- Creating the resource for the first time: use `platform/create/single-page-create`, which shares this field list.
- Account or organization settings outside one resource: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- A resource whose content is code or a document: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.
- Deleting the resource: the Danger zone action opens `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- A short list of attached records inside a section: use `platform/detail/attached-resources` as that section's body.

## Building blocks

- A. Resource tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (optional)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Settings sections — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Locked settings — `Tooltip`, `Switch` (optional)
- E. Save bar — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)
- F. Conditional fields — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText` (optional)
- G. Template editor — `SettingRow`, `HelperText` (optional)
- H. Section warnings and server errors — `SettingsSection`, `Button` (optional)
- I. Leave guard — `Tabs`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- J. Changed elsewhere — `Button`, `SaveBar` (optional)
- K. Danger zone — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `SettingRow`, `Button`, `Input` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md).

## Do

- Show the save bar only while the form differs from the saved record.
- Disable the whole fieldset while saving, not each field separately.
- Give every section a short hint that says what it controls, and an anchor so a link can land on it.
- Keep locked settings visible, disabled, with the reason and the way to unlock them.
- Put destructive actions in a Danger zone section at the end, never in the save bar.
- Check every field when Save is pressed and show errors only then; see `skills/webkit-errors`.
- Put the choice that decides other fields first, and show only the fields that choice needs.
- Show a preset document read-only, with Copy, beside the way to make it editable.
- Mark the tab that holds unsaved changes with `dirty`, and ask before leaving it while dirty.
- Offer Save changes in the leave dialog when the form can be saved from there; the user keeps their work without going back.
- Say when the record changed elsewhere as soon as it is known, and ask before Save overwrites it.
- Keep the edits on screen after a reload with an Undo, so a stale form never loses work silently.
- Ask for the resource name before a delete, with a copy button beside the name.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't place a permanent Save button at the top or bottom of the page; the save bar appears on demand.
- Don't save on each toggle; changes wait for Save.
- Don't hide fields the user cannot change; lock them and say why.
- Don't use `size="medium"` or larger for the Settings heading; the tab bar or breadcrumb already names the resource.
- Don't add a Cancel button that leaves the page; Discard restores the record in place.
- Don't report a rejected destination or credential in a toast; it belongs above the section it concerns.
- Don't echo a saved secret back into its field.
- Don't rely on the dot alone: the dirty tab also says "Unsaved changes" to screen readers.
- Don't overwrite a record that changed elsewhere without the overwrite confirmation.
- Don't put Delete in the save bar, the page heading or a menu of the form; it lives in the Danger zone.
- Don't enable the delete confirm button before the typed name matches.

## Copy

- **Heading:** "Settings", with one sentence ending in a period, e.g. "Core configuration for this project."
- **Section titles:** short nouns, e.g. "General", "Modules", "Subscription modules", "Status".
- **Row descriptions:** one sentence that says what the setting does, e.g. "When disabled, the project stops serving traffic."
- **Save bar:** state what changed and when it applies, e.g. "Project settings changed." with the hint "Saving publishes them on the next deployment."; buttons "Discard" and "Save".
- **Locked reason:** one sentence with the way out, e.g. "Contact sales to activate this module."
- **Server error on a section:** what happened, then what was kept, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer the test record, so the stream was not saved. Your other changes are still here."; the field reason is one line, e.g. "The endpoint did not answer within 10 seconds."
- **Leave dialog:** "Unsaved changes", "This page has changes you haven't saved. If you leave now, they're discarded." (with Save: "Save them before you leave, or discard them and continue."); buttons "Keep editing", "Discard changes", "Save changes". These are the built-in `unsavedChanges` messages in en, pt-BR and es.
- **Changed elsewhere:** "Changed elsewhere." + "This project was saved by someone else after you opened it. …"; button "Reload"; dialog "Overwrite changes made elsewhere?" with "Go back" and "Overwrite and save"; after a reload "Edits discarded." with "Undo".
- **Danger zone:** section "Danger zone" with "Actions that cannot be undone."; row "Delete this project"; dialog "Delete project", "Once confirmed, this action can't be reversed.", "To confirm, type <name>"; buttons "Cancel" and "Delete project".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The form has an `aria-label` and its `fieldset` a visually hidden `legend` with the same words, e.g. "Main settings".
- Every `Input` and `Switch` has an `aria-label` matching its row title.
- A disabled `Switch` keeps its `Tooltip`, so keyboard and pointer users can still read why it is locked.
- External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and an icon marked `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The save bar enters after the form in reading order and its motion respects reduced motion.
- An invalid field points at its `HelperText` through `aria-describedby`; on Save the first invalid field takes the focus.
- A section `Alert` is announced by `Alert` itself; its recovery `Button` is a real button inside it.
- The `CodeEditor` and the read-only `CodeBlock` are named after their row (`Data set`, `Copy the data set as JSON`).
- The dirty tab mark is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "Unsaved changes" joins the tab's accessible name, and under forced colors the dot paints in `CanvasText`.
- The leave dialog is a `ConfirmDialog`: focus moves into it, Escape and the close button count as Keep editing, and focus returns to the control that asked to leave.
- The changed-elsewhere notice sits in a polite live region and takes focus after Reload so the change of values is announced; both its actions are real buttons.
- The delete confirmation `Input` is labelled by the "To confirm, type …" sentence (`aria-labelledby`); the `CopyButton` has its own name ("Copy the project name") and announces Copied.

## States

- ProjectSettings: a project's Settings tab with General, Modules and Subscription modules; the save bar is hidden until an edit.
- DeployableSettings: a deployable resource's Settings tab with General, Domains, collapsed Advanced settings and the Danger zone, whose Delete resource opens the type-to-confirm `ConfirmDialog` of `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- PolicySettings: a security policy's Settings tab with General, Modules with one locked on, Debug rules and Status.
- ResourceSettings: a first-level resource with no tabs at its own settings route; Save checks every field before it commits.
- UnsavedChanges: after one edit; the save bar is up with Discard and Save.
- Saving: while the request is in flight; Save is loading and Discard is disabled.
- DataStream: a data stream at its own settings route with General, Source, Sampling, Template and Destination; the destination fields follow the connector, Save sends one test record, and an endpoint that does not answer raises the section `Alert` of the form-error rule.
- StaleRecord: the form holds edits and the record changed elsewhere; the warning notice with Reload is up, Save asks before overwriting, Reload turns the notice into Edits discarded with Undo.
- DangerZone: the settings end with the Danger zone; Delete project opens the typed-name confirmation, enabled only on a match, loading while the delete runs.
- CacheSettings: one cache setting of an application; General, Browser cache, Edge cache and the collapsed Advanced cache key. Rows that only apply under a switch or an override sit one level in (`SettingRow` `level`). An edge TTL under 60 seconds and an empty allowlist or denylist are field errors with their reason, focused on Save. Save deploys and reports through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- Protocols: the protocol settings of a workload; ports per protocol, TLS version and cipher suite, then Mutual authentication. Mutual authentication stays off, with a helper line saying why, until HTTPS is on; once on it shows the mode as `Field` choice cards, the trusted CA picker (search, expiry beside each certificate, Upload certificate in its footer opening a `Drawer`) and the revocation lists. Save checks a port per protocol and a CA, then deploys through the async-submit toast with Edit and Redeploy.
- UnsavedChanges (leave guard): the Settings tab carries the dirty dot, and switching tabs while dirty opens the Unsaved changes dialog.

## Settings that deploy

Some settings only take effect once the resource is deployed (cache settings of an application, protocols of a workload). For those:

- Say so in the save bar hint, e.g. "Saving deploys storefront to Production."
- On Save, validate first (field errors per the form-error rule), then run the deploy on its own: a loading toast while it runs, then the async-submit toast with **Edit** (back to the form, focus on its first field) and **Redeploy**. Never offer View deployments.
- Keep the form usable while it runs; the baseline moves to the saved values only when the deploy succeeds.
- Keep switches that depend on each other consistent in both directions, e.g. HTTP/3 turns HTTPS on and HTTPS off turns HTTP/3 and mutual authentication off.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the `ConsoleLayout` this page body renders in; a crumb that is a control (DeployableSettings' environment) is set by the page with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs` (the module and the resource as `items`, a `Select` with `kind="transparent"` and `size="small"` in its slot).
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the create page that shares this field list.
- `platform/detail/attached-resources` — the Domains section body in DeployableSettings.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the Danger zone action.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — account settings that end with the same save band.
- `SaveBar` — the unsaved-changes band; see `skills/webkit-form`.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the section-scoped server error DataStream follows.
- `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard` (Metrics) — where the records a stream sends are counted.
- `useUnsavedChanges` — the dirty baseline and leave guard behind the save bar, the tab mark and the leave dialog.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the rule the changed-elsewhere notice follows.

## Variants

`ProjectSettings` (primary) · `DeployableSettings` · `PolicySettings` · `ResourceSettings` · `UnsavedChanges` · `Saving` · `DataStream` · `StaleRecord` · `DangerZone` · `CacheSettings` · `Protocols`. Code: [blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md](blocks/platform/edit/edit-resource.md), `get_pattern("platform/edit/edit-resource", { variant })`.
