# RuleBuilder (`platform/edit/rule-builder`)

> A rule builder drawer, the richest form pattern: a large right-side drawer with General, Phase, Criteria, Behaviors and Status sections over a single Save in the footer.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder/rule-builder.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/edit/rule-builder")`
- Components: AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Combobox, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerTrigger`, Field, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioButton, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Switch, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-create-surface`

## Asked as

rules engine; rule form; add rule; criteria and behaviors; if then rules; conditional rules; rule builder; motor de regras; criar regra; regras condicionais

A drawer where the user writes one rule of a rules engine: when it runs (the phase), the conditions that decide whether it applies, and the ordered behaviors it performs when they match. The user composes groups of variable, operator and argument rows (every row in a group must match, any group is enough), picks behaviors that fit the phase, puts everything in order and saves, without leaving the resource's Rules tab.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered list of rules, each made of conditions and actions (request and response rules, firewall rules, routing).
- Conditions combine with And inside a group and Or across groups, and the order of behaviors matters.
- The rule is edited from a list inside the resource, so the drawer opens as `Add Rule` or `Edit Rule` and keeps the list in view behind it.

## When not to use

- Free-form pairs of a name and a value: use `platform/edit/attribute-editor`.
- A short create form of three fields or fewer: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- A resource's own settings: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- Logic the user would rather write as code: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drawer and trigger — `Drawer`, `DrawerTrigger`, `Button`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent` (required)
- B. General — `SettingsSection`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Phase — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Field`, `RadioButton`, `HelperText` (optional)
- D. Criteria — `SettingsSection`, `AttributeEditor` (grouped), `Combobox`, `Select`, `Input` (required)
- E. Behaviors — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Select`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Button` (required)
- F. Status — `SettingsSection`, `Card`, `Item`, `SettingRow`, `Switch` (required)
- G. Footer — `PanelFooter`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md](blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md).

## Do

- Show the Name error only after a failed Save, never on first render, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Read the logic aloud in the layout: and inside a group, or between groups, then the behaviors in order.
- Make every argument field follow what was picked before it, so the user never types a value the operator or behavior cannot take.
- Offer both drag and buttons to reorder behaviors; the buttons are the keyboard path.
- Filter variables and behaviors by phase, and lock the phase on an existing rule.
- Follow `skills/webkit-form` for fields and `skills/webkit-errors` for error timing.

## Don't

- Don't put a Cancel button beside Save; `DrawerClose` and the overlay close the drawer.
- Don't nest groups inside groups; one level of Or over And is the whole model.
- Don't draw criteria rows by hand; `AttributeEditor` grouped mode owns their labels, errors, limits and announcements.
- Don't let the user switch an existing rule's phase; tell them to create a rule in the other phase.
- Don't open the drawer in a medium size; condition rows need three columns side by side.
- Don't clear the form while the drawer is closing.

## Copy

- **Drawer title and trigger:** `Add Rule` for a new rule, `Edit Rule` for an existing one.
- **Section hints:** one sentence saying what the section decides, e.g. "The conditions that decide whether the rule runs."
- **Logic labels:** single words, e.g. "and", "or", "Then".
- **Add buttons:** verb first, e.g. "Add condition", "Add OR group", "Add behavior".
- **Errors:** "Name is required.", "Enter the variable to compare."
- **Reorder controls:** name the item, e.g. "Move condition up", "Remove behavior".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Every `Input` and `Select` trigger has a label: a `Field.Label` tied by `for`, or an `aria-label` such as "Behavior"; the criteria cells are `Field`s of the `AttributeEditor`, labelled Variable, Operator and Argument, and groups are `group`s named "Group n".
- The variable `Combobox` is a `combobox` with a `listbox` of `option`s; picking one keeps focus in the field.
- Behavior drag grips are labeled, e.g. "Drag to reorder behavior, or use arrow keys", and the Move up and Move down buttons give the same result without a pointer.
- Icon-only controls carry an `aria-label` that matches their `Tooltip`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- The drawer traps focus while open and returns it to the trigger on close; motion respects reduced motion.

## States

- Default: Add Rule with an empty Name, the Request phase, one empty condition and one empty behavior, Active on.
- Composed: Edit Rule for the seeded Docs rewrite rule, the phase locked with its note, one URI condition and two behaviors.
- In a list: `platform/view/rules-list#EditRule` drives this drawer without its trigger (`v-model:open` from a rule's name and from Add Rule) and writes the saved rule back to its row.

## Related

- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the simpler drawer create this one extends.
- `platform/edit/attribute-editor` — a drawer for free key and value pairs; `AttributeEditor` is the component the criteria are built on.
- `platform/view/rules-list` — the list of rules by phase this drawer opens from.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — when errors appear after Save.
- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — the resource settings that sit beside the Rules tab.
- `Drawer` — the side panel; see `skills/webkit-create-surface`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Composed`. Code: [blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md](blocks/platform/edit/rule-builder.md), `get_pattern("platform/edit/rule-builder", { variant })`.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/edit/schema-editor/schema-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`

## Asked as

schema editor; create table; add column; insert row; alter column; change column type; truncate table; table schema; database schema; column types; criar tabela; adicionar coluna; inserir linha; alterar coluna; esvaziar tabela; esquema do banco

The table schema of a SQL database: the definition of one table and the drawers and dialogs that change it. A developer creates a table with its columns, adds a column, inserts a row by hand, changes a column's type or empties a table, and stays on the same surface while each change runs. It sits behind the Create Table, Add column, Insert and table menu buttons of `platform/view/query-editor`. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the ⌘K palette and the `main`.

## When to use

- A SQL database's tables are created and changed from the console rather than only with SQL.
- A table's columns, types and constraints are shown and edited one change at a time.
- A row is added by hand to check a table, without writing an INSERT.

## When not to use

- Running SQL or reading query results: use `platform/view/query-editor`.
- Rows of a resource that is not a database (variables, records): use `platform/edit/attribute-editor` or `platform/detail/record-table`.
- A form that creates a resource in its own page: use `platform/create/single-page-create`.

## Building blocks

- A. Definition surface — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Table`, `Tag`, `Button`, `DropdownMenu`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- B. Create Table drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent`, `SettingsSection`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` (required)
- C. Column rows — `Select`, `Checkbox`, `HelperText` (required)
- D. CSV import and foreign keys — `FileDropzone`, `FileTokenGroup` (optional)
- E. Add column drawer — `Switch` (required)
- F. Insert row drawer — `PanelFooter` (required)
- G. Change type dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor` (required)
- H. Truncate table dialog — `ConfirmDialog`, `CodeEditor`, `Input` (required)
- Outcome toasts — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/edit/schema-editor.md](blocks/platform/edit/schema-editor.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, then keep each error next to what caused it: the field, the column row or the list.
- Keep the drawer open and its values intact when the server refuses; say so in the section `Alert`.
- Show the SQL a destructive or rebuilding change will run before it runs.
- Ask for the table name before truncating it.
- Let the grip reorder columns by drag and from the keyboard, announce each move, and keep focus on the moved row.
- End every change with a toast whose action continues the work on the same table.

## Don't

- Don't validate column names on every keystroke; wait for the first submit.
- Don't put a deploy action (Edit, Redeploy, View deployments) on a schema change.
- Don't let a primary key be nullable; lock Not null while Primary key is on.
- Don't drop rows on a type change silently; warn that values that don't fit make it fail.
- Don't close the Create Table drawer on a server error.

## Copy

- **Titles:** `Create Table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change the type of <column>`, `Truncate <table>`.
- **Buttons:** the title's verb and object: `Create Table`, `Add column`, `Insert row`, `Change type`, `Truncate table`; Cancel beside each.
- **Errors:** `This field is required.`, `Start with a letter or an underscore; use letters, numbers and underscores.`, `Another column is also named email.`, `Add at least one named column.`, `customers already has a column named email.`, `email cannot be NULL. Enter a value.`
- **Server rejection:** `The table wasn't created. A table named customers already exists in acme-store. Your columns are kept; pick another name and create it again.`
- **Toasts:** as in building block H.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case except the product's object names (`Create Table`), no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each drawer's content is a `form` named by its title; the `fieldset` carries a visually hidden `legend` and is disabled while the request runs.
- `Field` wires every label, description and error to its control; column row controls without a visible label are named `Name of column 2`, `Type of column 2`, `Default value of column 2`.
- The grip is a real `button` named `Reorder <column>, position <n> of <total>. Drag, or use the up and down arrow keys.` with `aria-keyshortcuts`; dragging is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.7), moves are announced in a polite status line, and reordering keeps focus on the moved grip.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the per-column menu trigger names its column.
- The read-only `CodeEditor`s are named (`Statements that will run`) and can be selected and copied.
- Drawers and dialogs trap focus, close on Escape and return focus to the button that opened them.

## States

- CreateTable: the Create Table drawer open on a new table, with the default id and created_at columns.
- AddColumn: the Add column drawer with phone as varchar.
- InsertRow: the Insert row drawer after a submit with email empty, showing the NOT NULL error.
- ChangeType: the Change type dialog for email with the statements that will run.
- TruncateTable: the Truncate customers dialog waiting for the typed name.
- ImportCsv: Create Table with subscribers.csv read (six columns, six rows, a quoted comma) and one foreign key, customer_id to customers.id on delete cascade.
- Failed: Create Table refused by the server because customers already exists; Alert in General and the Name field invalid.

- `platform/view/query-editor` — the database page whose buttons open these drawers and dialogs.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — the drawer recipe these drawers follow.

# SettingsForm (`platform/settings/settings-form`)

> A settings form and its save strategy, one variant per strategy.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/settings/settings-form/settings-form.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/settings/settings-form")`

## Asked as

save all; single save for the page; sticky footer save; account settings form; save as one unit; cancel and save footer; salvar tudo; rodapé fixo com salvar; formulário de conta; save per group; save per section; preferences page; grouped settings save; section save button; independent groups; salvar por grupo; preferências; salvar por seção; save per card; card with its own save; project settings; configuration cards; independent saves; long settings page; salvar por card; configurações do projeto; salvar cada seção

The place the user goes to change how an account or a project behaves. They scan a few topics, change one or two values, and commit them knowing exactly what the save covers. The block is one layout with three save strategies: one save for a form that is one logical unit, one save per group, or one save per card on a long configuration page. The save model follows how the page is partitioned, not the container. It is a page body for `ConsoleLayout`: the app renders it in the layout's default slot, and the layout owns the rail, the header, the breadcrumbs, the ⌘K palette and the `<main>`.

## When to use

- Account-level settings read as rows of a label, a description and a control (Profile, Preferences, Notifications): SaveAll.
- Topics on one page that the user commits independently, such as General and Notifications: SavePerGroup.
- A long configuration page where each topic needs an explanation and its own commit, such as Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection: SavePerCard.

## When not to use

- The settings tab of one resource, with anchored sections and an unsaved-changes bar: use `platform/edit/edit-resource`.
- The signed-in user's full profile page with all its sections: use `platform/account/profile`.
- Creating a resource: use `platform/create/single-page-create` or `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.
- Walking every submit outcome (invalid fields, server rejection): use `platform/states/form-validation`.
- Deleting the account or a resource from a settings page: open `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` (its LabelledField variant) from an outlined row.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Topic sections — `Card`, `Item` (required)
- C. Setting rows — `SettingRow`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Select`, `Switch` (required)
- D. Save — `SaveBar`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/settings/settings-form.md](blocks/platform/settings/settings-form.md).

## Do

- Pick the save strategy from how the page is partitioned: one logical unit gets one save.
- Disable only the fieldset being saved; the other groups or cards stay editable.
- Drive Save's `:loading` and the fieldset's `disabled` from one `submitting` flag.
- Validate on submit only, show the error at the field it belongs to, and move focus to the first field in error.
- Keep every control in a row at the same size, and every row title in sentence case.
- Explain a card's effect in an info `Alert` at the top of the card, before its fields.

## Don't

- Don't render a `Sidebar`, `GlobalHeader`, `Command` palette or `<main>` in the page; `ConsoleLayout` owns them.
- Don't mix a page-level `SaveBar` with per-card Save buttons on the same page.
- Don't put Save in the page heading or float it beside a single field.
- Don't flag empty required fields before the user presses Save.
- Don't add an error summary block or an `Alert` for field validation; the field's own state is the feedback.
- Don't put a consequence or a constraint in the row title; it goes in the description or the `Alert`.

## Copy

- **Page title:** the page's name, e.g. "Profile"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Define and manage personal account preferences."
- **Breadcrumb** (the route meta `ConsoleLayout` reads): the parent, then the page title exactly, e.g. "Account settings" › "Profile".
- **Choices:** sentence case and no parentheses, e.g. "Team default", "Standard protection".
- **Section heading:** a short topic noun, e.g. "General", "Notifications".
- **Row title:** names the setting in one to three words, e.g. "Timezone"; description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "Times across the app are shown in this zone."
- **Save:** exactly "Save" for the footer and every group or card; Discard is exactly "Discard", never "Cancel": it restores the saved values and the reader stays on the page.
- **Errors:** what is wrong plus what to do, e.g. "Enter a valid email address."
- **Docs link:** names the topic, e.g. "Learn more about the Preview Toolbar".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The `form` is named by the `PageHeader` title through `aria-labelledby` and uses `novalidate`; the title is the page's only `h1`.
- Each group is a real `fieldset`; SaveAll gives it a visually hidden `legend` ("Profile settings").
- Every control has an `aria-label` that repeats its row title; errors are linked with `aria-describedby` only while they show.
- Disabling the `fieldset` while saving takes every control out of interaction at once; Save announces its loading state.
- Focus order follows reading order: the rows from top to bottom, then Discard and Save.

## States

- SaveAll: Profile with General, Preferences and Notifications in one fieldset and one sticky Discard and Save footer.
- Saving: the whole fieldset and Discard are disabled and Save shows its loading state.
- SavePerGroup: Preferences split into General and Notifications cards, each with its own secondary Save.
- SavingOneGroup: General is saving with its rows disabled while Notifications stays editable.
- SavePerCard: Project settings with Preview Toolbar and Deployment Protection cards, each with an info `Alert`, its fields and its own Save.
- SavingOneCard: Preview Toolbar is saving with its selects disabled while Deployment Protection stays editable.

## Related

- `platform/edit/edit-resource` — settings of one resource, with anchored sections.
- `platform/account/profile` — the full account profile built on the same layout.
- `platform/states/form-validation` — every outcome of a submit.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — a save that runs long or fails on the server.

# AsyncSubmit (`platform/states/async-submit`)

> The async counterpart of the server rejection in the FormError template: a deploy that runs for about half a minute, so the user walks away before it ends.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/async-submit/async-submit.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/async-submit")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Button, Card, EmptyState, LogView, `LogViewContent`, PageHeader, Progress, Spinner, StatusIndicator, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup
- Skills: `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-form`

## Asked as

async submit; long running action; background job status; deploy in progress; async deploy result; operation status; envio assíncrono; ação demorada; status da operação

The async-action pattern, taken from the design sample (`/forms/async-deployment`), and the standard for every build and deploy screen. A long-running action the user is free to walk away from: a deploy that runs for about half a minute and asks nothing while it does. The user's job is to start it, go on working anywhere in the console, and learn how it ended without coming back to check. The page that started the run shows its status in the heading, the logs while it runs and an inline outcome when it ends; in a full app the run lives outside the page, so its progress and its outcome also travel with the user as a toast, on success and on failure.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

The run toast rides the app's one toast region, never the page's: the app installs `ToastPlugin` (`app.use(ToastPlugin, { position: 'bottom-right' })`) or mounts one `Toaster` near its root, beside `ConsoleLayout`, and this page body only imports `toast` from `@aziontech/webkit/toast`. A `Toaster` inside a page body is a second region for the whole app: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active, and it gives that up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, stops every toast once the user leaves the page, the opposite of a run toast that follows the user. The docs preview mounts one region around the block the way an app root does, so its frames show the toasts; a copy of the page shows them wherever the app has mounted the region.

The toasts are raised through `toast` with one id per run so each state replaces the last. Every outcome toast passes `actions: [{ label: 'Edit', onClick }, { label: 'Redeploy', onClick }]` and `closable: true`, so the app's `Toaster` renders both as `Toast.Action`s beside `Toast.Close`; the progress toast carries no action. The Running frame raises the progress toast, Failed the permanent failure toast and Succeeded the success toast; leaving the page dismisses the story's toast so the next story starts clean.

## When to use

- Any action that takes long enough to leave: build, deploy, redeploy, import, provision, a bulk change.
- When the outcome must reach the user on whatever page they are on when it lands.
- As the reference for the idle, running, failed and succeeded states of a run started from a page.

## When not to use

- A save that answers in about a second: use `platform/states/form-validation`.
- The full deployment flow with its own steps and logs page: use `platform/create/deployment-flow` and `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Confirming a finished deploy with next steps: use `platform/create/deploy-success`.
- A deploy configured in a side panel: use `platform/create/deploy-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Actions — `Button` (required)
- B. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- C. Run status — `Tag` (required)
- D. Simulated ending — `ToggleGroup` (simulation only)
- E. Nothing running — `EmptyState` (idle only)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/async-submit.md](blocks/platform/states/async-submit.md).

## Do

- Keep the run, its timer and its outcome outside the page component (a small module-scope store), so leaving the page never cancels it or loses the result.
- Show progress as a `loading` toast (no duration, not closable) that follows the user through the app while the run lasts.
- Report the end wherever the user is, on success and on failure. A failure toast is permanent (`duration: 0`) and `closable`; a success toast is `closable` with the default 6 second duration.
- Raise the toasts through `toast` only; the app mounts the region once (`ToastPlugin` or one `Toaster` at its root), so the page body never renders a `Toaster`.
- Give both toasts the same two actions through `toast()`'s `actions` option: **Edit** for the item that was deployed, and **Redeploy**. Don't rebuild the toast body in the `Toaster` slot to get two actions.
- On the page that started the run, show the outcome inline as well, with the same two actions as the toast: a danger `Alert` with the reason, **Edit** and **Redeploy** over the stopped logs, or a success `Alert` naming the new address with **Edit**, **Redeploy** and **Open service**.
- Disable Deploy and the controls that would change the run while it is in progress, with Deploy in `loading`.
- Use one toast id per run, so the progress toast turns into the outcome toast in place, and a Redeploy turns it back into progress.
- Apply this to every build and deploy screen (deploy drawers, deployment flows, redeploys from a list, imports): the run lives outside the page, the page shows the status `Tag` and the outcome `Alert`, and the toast reports wherever the user is.

## Don't

- Don't tie the run to the component that started it; unmounting a page is not an event the run hears.
- Don't let a failure toast expire; the user was not there when it arrived.
- Don't point the toast at a list of runs ("View deployments"); it carries **Edit** and **Redeploy**.
- Don't block the page with a modal or overlay while the run is in progress; the whole point is that the user can leave.
- Don't claim an outcome before the server confirms it; the heading reads `Deploying` until it does.

## Copy

- **Page heading:** names the action, sentence case: `Async deployment`. Lead: what the run does and that the user may leave: `A deploy runs for half a minute and asks nothing of you while it does.`
- **Status tag:** one or two words: `Idle`, `Deploying`, `Failed`, `Deployed`.
- **Empty state:** title states the fact, description says what to do: `No deployment running` / `Start one above. It takes about 25 seconds.`
- **Progress toast:** present progressive with the single-character ellipsis, names the item: `Deploying web-app…`; description names the source and that the user may leave: `acme/web-app. It keeps running if you leave.`
- **Failure toast:** what failed and why, then the ways out: `web-app wasn't deployed.` / `The routing rules were refused.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the item and where it is live: `web-app is live.` / `It is available at web-app.example.com.` Actions: `Edit`, `Redeploy`.
- **Failure Alert:** the reason the server gave, as full sentences, with `Edit` and `Redeploy`.
- **Success Alert:** names the address and the attempts: `web-app is live at web-app.example.com. It took 1 attempt.`, with `Edit`, `Redeploy` and `Open service`.
- **Simulation panel:** a colon, never a dash: `Simulation: how this deploy ends`.
- **Actions:** `Deploy`, `Redeploy` (never "Retry deploy" or "Try again"), `Edit`, `Open service`.

## Accessibility

- The run status is text in the heading's `Tag`, not color alone.
- Toasts are announced politely by the app's `Toaster` region; the progress toast must not steal focus.
- The failure toast's actions and close button are reachable by keyboard, and it stays until closed.
- The simulation panel is an `aside` with its own label so screen reader users can skip it.
- The logs card (Running and Failed) streams into a `LogView`; do not announce every log line.
- Page entrance and the outcome `Alert` animate with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## States

- Idle: nothing running; the heading reads Idle and the `EmptyState` offers Deploy.
- Running: mid-run; the heading reads Deploying, the simulation controls are disabled, Deploy shows `loading`, the logs card streams under the Building status and the progress toast reads `Deploying web-app…`.
- Failed: the routing rules were refused; the heading reads Failed, the danger `Alert` carries the reason with Edit and Redeploy, the permanent failure toast carries the same two actions, and the logs stay open on the failed step.
- Succeeded: the run is live; the heading reads Deployed, the success `Alert` names the new address with Edit, Redeploy and Open service, the success toast carries Edit and Redeploy, and the logs card is gone.

## Related

- `platform/states/form-validation` — the synchronous counterpart: field, section and toast placement for a save that answers right away.
- `platform/create/deployment-flow` — the deployment logs card the Running and Failed states reuse.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the full logs of a run, the page Edit or a failure leads into.
- `platform/create/deploy-success` — the confirmation page after a deploy completes.
- `shells/console` — the layout this body renders in, which the user moves through while the run reports back.

## Variants

`Idle` (primary) · `Running` · `Failed` · `Succeeded`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/async-submit.md](blocks/platform/states/async-submit.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/async-submit", { variant })`.

# FirstUse (`platform/states/first-use`)

> The block a first-level list renders before the account owns any resource of that kind: a flush Card holding an EmptyState (the resource glyph, headline, lead and a Documentation link) over an Item.List of the ways to…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/first-use/first-use.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/first-use")`
- Components: `claudeMark`, `codexMark`, `cursorMark`, `geminiMark`, Button, Card, CopyButton, EmptyState, Input, `InputGroupRoot`, Item, Link, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

empty state; empty list; first use; no resources yet; create first resource; product empty state; zero state; estado vazio; lista vazia; primeiro uso

What a first-level list shows before the account owns any resource of that kind. The user's job is to create the first one, so the block replaces the empty table with a short explanation and every way to get started on the same screen: the methods to create one (import, CLI, from scratch), then the promotions that shortcut it (a Catalog template, a coding agent). Every list that is still empty renders this block with its own nouns, methods and promos.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The first visit to a list page (Resources, Services, Domains…) when the account has none of that resource.
- When there is more than one way to create the first item and each deserves its own action.

## When not to use

- A list that has items but a filter or search matched none: use the no-match state of `platform/view/table-view`.
- An empty panel inside a dashboard or detail page: use `EmptyState` alone, without the method list.
- Choosing what to create across every resource kind: use `platform/create/create-hub`.
- The Home page before the first project: use `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` (its Empty state).
- A list that failed to load: that is an error, not first use; see `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Building blocks

- A. Frame — `Card` (required)
- B. Explanation — `EmptyState` (required)
- C. Documentation — `Link` (required)
- D. Methods — `Item` (required)
- E. Method action — `Button` (required)
- F. Command row — `InputGroupRoot` (CLI method)
- G. Command — `Input` (CLI method)
- H. Copy — `CopyButton` (CLI method)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/first-use.md](blocks/platform/states/first-use.md).

## Do

- Rewrite the headline, lead, methods and promos for each resource kind; the structure stays, the nouns change.
- Show the Catalog template promo only for resource kinds that have a template catalog.
- Keep one primary action across the whole block, on the method most users take.
- Keep the documentation link as the only action in the `EmptyState`.
- Hold the block's footprint with `Skeleton` bands while the account reloads, so it does not jump in.

## Don't

- Don't write an agent mark's mask as an unquoted `url(...)`: the build inlines the SVG as a `data:` URI and the unquoted value renders the mark as a solid square. Quote it (`url('…')`).
- Don't show list controls (search, filters, pagination, column settings) over a list that has never had an item.
- Don't render this block for a filtered list with no matches; that state says how to clear the filter.
- Don't show it while the list is still loading; the user would see "create your first" for an account that has items.
- Don't add a second primary button to a promo card; the whole card is the action.

## Copy

- **Headline:** names the first action and the noun: `Create your first resource`.
- **Lead:** one sentence on the ways in: `Start from scratch, from a template or by importing your code.`
- **Method title:** two or three words for how: `From GitHub`, `Via CLI`, `From scratch`.
- **Method description:** one sentence on what happens: `Import a repository and deploy it on every push.`
- **Method action:** one verb: `Import`, `Create`.
- **Promo title:** sentence case, product names capitalized: `Start from a Catalog template`, `Set up your coding agent`.
- **Promo description:** one sentence on the result: `Deploy a framework starter and the resource that serves it, in one step.`
- **Documentation link:** `Documentation`.

## Accessibility

- The method icons and promo marks are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`, `alt=""`); the titles carry the meaning.
- Each promo is a real `<button type="button">` covering the card, so it is reachable and announced by its title.
- The command `Input` has an `aria-label`; the copy button has its own label and announces the copied state.
- The documentation link opens in a new tab; say so in the destination or let `Link` mark it.
- The headline is the page's first heading under the list title, not a second `h1`.

## States

- Default: the explanation, three create methods and the two promos.
- Loading: while the account reloads, two `Skeleton` bands hold the block's footprint.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the list this block stands in for once the first item exists, and the home of the no-match state.

# FormError (`platform/states/form-error`)

> The form-error pattern from the design sample (`/forms/error-validation`): a server rejection scoped to one section of a long create form.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/form-error/form-error.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/form-error")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Field, GlobalHeader, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, MultiSelect, NumberInput, RadioButton, SaveBar, SectionHeader, Select, SettingRow, Skeleton, Switch, Tag
- Skills: `webkit-errors`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

form error; server validation; server-side error; rejected save; field scoped error; section error; stale reference; linked resource deleted; api error on save; reload options; erro de formulário; validação no servidor; erro da api; salvamento rejeitado; error de formulario; validación en el servidor

The form-error pattern, taken from the design sample (`/forms/error-validation`): what a long create form does when the server rejects the save because of one section. The user's job is to create a service; another user deletes the origin it links to while the form is open, so the save comes back with an error the Origin section owns. The page takes the user to that section, says what happened and that nothing else was lost, offers the one action that recovers (Reload origins), and marks the field with its own reason. This is the standard for every server rejection that a section or a field owns.

This block is a focused create page with its own creation header and no rail: render it outside `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`).

## When to use

- A long, sectioned create or edit form whose save can be rejected because of one section: a linked resource deleted or changed by someone else, a value the server refuses for that section only.
- As the reference for where a field-scoped or section-scoped server error renders, and how the user recovers without retyping anything.

## When not to use

- The submit states of a short form (required, invalid, in flight, a conflict on a one-section form, an unscoped failure, success): use `platform/states/form-validation`.
- A long-running action that reports back later (build, deploy): use `platform/states/async-submit`.
- A failure no field or section owns (network, timeout, 500): an error toast with Retry, as in `platform/states/form-validation` ServerError.
- Signed-out screens: use `platform/auth`, where every outcome lands in one card `Alert`.

## Building blocks

- A. Creation header — `GlobalHeader` (required)
- B. Back — `IconButton` (required)
- C. Product mark — `Brand` (required)
- D. Location — `Breadcrumb` (required)
- E. Account — `Avatar` (required)
- F. Simulation — `Tag` (simulation only)
- G. Actions — `Button` (required)
- H. Section heading — `SectionHeader` (required)
- I. Group surface — `Card` (required)
- J. Rows — `Item` (required)
- K. Setting row — `SettingRow` (required)
- L. Text values — `Input` (required)
- M. Ports — `MultiSelect` (required)
- N. Linked resource — `Select` (required)
- O. Choice cards — `Field` (required)
- P. Choice — `RadioButton` (required)
- Q. Toggles — `Switch` (required)
- R. Numbers — `NumberInput` (required)
- S. Field reason — `HelperText` (required)
- T. Section notice — `Alert` (rejection only)
- U. Loading — `Skeleton` (reloading only)
- V. Footer — `SaveBar` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/form-error.md](blocks/platform/states/form-error.md).

## Do

- Put a section-scoped server rejection in a danger `Alert` under that section's heading, and set the field it names to `invalid` with its own one-line reason. Both surfaces, never one.
- Say in the `Alert`, as separate sentences, what happened, why, that nothing else was lost, and what to do: `Origin "web-origin-prod" no longer exists. Another user deleted it while you were filling in this form, so the service wasn't created. Nothing else was lost: reload the origin list and select another one.`
- Put the recovery on the `Alert` itself (`Reload origins`), not in the footer and not in a toast.
- Scroll the section into view and move focus to the field, after the lock is released; an instant scroll when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.
- Keep every entry. Only the field the server refused changes, and only after the user recovers.
- While the recovery runs, show its `loading`, replace the field by a `Skeleton` and disable Save.
- After the recovery, close the `Alert`, clear the stale value and flag the field `required` with what to do next.

## Don't

- Don't toast a rejection a section or field owns: the toast leaves, and it points nowhere.
- Don't show a validation summary at the top of the page.
- Don't clear the form or send the user back to the start.
- Don't use the amber `required` state for a value the server refused; the value is there, so it is `invalid`.
- Don't auto-dismiss the `Alert`; it stays until the user recovers.
- Don't open more than one `Alert` for one rejection.

## Copy

- **Section Alert:** the fact, the cause, what was not lost, what to do: `Origin "web-origin-prod" no longer exists. Another user deleted it while you were filling in this form, so the service wasn't created. Nothing else was lost: reload the origin list and select another one.`
- **Recovery action:** verb plus the thing reloaded: `Reload origins`.
- **Field reason (refused):** `This origin no longer exists.`
- **Field reason (after reload):** `Select an origin to continue.`
- **Required messages:** `Name is required.`, `Host header is required.`, `Select an origin.`, `Select at least one HTTP port.`
- **Simulation panel:** a colon, never a dash: `Simulation: the other user`.
- **Actions:** `Cancel`, `Save`, `Reload origins`.

## Accessibility

- The `<form>` has an accessible name and `novalidate`; while the request is in flight the fields sit in a disabled `fieldset`.
- The `Alert` sits in reading order before the fields it governs; its action is a real button reachable by keyboard.
- Focus moves to the refused field after the save, with `preventScroll` so the scroll to the section heading is the only movement.
- The field's reason is wired to the control with `aria-describedby`.
- The `Skeleton` has an accessible name while the list reloads.
- The `Alert`'s expand and the page entrance honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- InSync: the form filled in and linked to an origin that still exists; the simulation panel reads Server in sync.
- Rejected: User 2 deleted the origin and Save was pressed; the page scrolls to Origin, the danger `Alert` opens under its heading with Reload origins, and focus lands on the Origin select, which reads This origin no longer exists.
- Reloading: Reload origins in flight; its button loads, the select gives way to a `Skeleton`, Save is disabled.
- Reloaded: the list is back without the deleted origin; the `Alert` closes, the select is cleared and flagged required with Select an origin to continue.

## Related

- `platform/states/form-validation` — the submit states of a short form, including a conflict on a one-section form and an unscoped failure.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the long-running counterpart, where the outcome reports back wherever the user is.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the sectioned create page this one is built on.
- `skills/webkit-errors` — where every error renders, row by row.

## Variants

`InSync` (primary) · `Rejected` · `Reloading` · `Reloaded`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/form-error.md](blocks/platform/states/form-error.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/form-error", { variant })`.

# FormValidation (`platform/states/form-validation`)

> A standalone form that walks through every state a submit can land in, one story per state, on a single Create Variable page with no card around it: a heading, then `Field`s wrapping `Input`, `Select` and `Textarea` s…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/form-validation/form-validation.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/form-validation")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Field, Input, PageHeader, Select, Skeleton, Textarea, Toast
- Skills: `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

form validation; validation errors; submit states; required fields; server error on submit; conflict error; saved state; validação de formulário; erros de validação; campos obrigatórios

Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading. A server rejection scoped to one section of a long form is its own block, `platform/states/form-error`.

This block is a page body for a create page: render it under the focused creation header (`headers/creation-header`), not in `ConsoleLayout`.

## When to use

- As the reference for the submit states of any create or edit form: what happens on Create with gaps, while the request is in flight, and on each kind of answer.
- A short create form with a handful of fields and no sections (a variable, a key, a token).

## When not to use

- A sectioned create page with many settings and a sticky save bar: build it from `platform/create/single-page-create` and apply these states to it.
- A create that runs for tens of seconds and can be left (build, deploy, import): use `platform/states/async-submit`.
- Settings of an existing object saved section by section: use `platform/settings/settings-form`.
- A long sectioned form whose save is rejected because of one section (a linked resource deleted under the user): use `platform/states/form-error`.
- Signed-out screens: use `platform/auth`, where nothing toasts.
- A create launched from a list without leaving it: use `platform/create/create-in-drawer`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader` (required)
- B. Loading rows — `Skeleton` (loading only)
- C. Field — `Field` (required)
- D. Text value — `Input` (required)
- E. Choice — `Select` (required)
- F. Long text — `Textarea` (optional)
- G. Actions — `Button` (required)
- H. Section notice — `Alert` (conflict and rejection only)
- Result notices — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/form-validation.md](blocks/platform/states/form-validation.md).

## Do

- Validate on submit, not on every keystroke; after the first submit, a field's message updates as the user fixes it.
- Move focus to the first field in error after a submit, after the lock is released.
- Lock the whole scope while the request is in flight: Create shows `loading`, every field and Cancel are disabled, `aria-busy` is on the form. Release it on success and failure alike.
- Keep every entry after a failed or rejected save, and say so in the copy.
- Clear the form after a success, so the next entry starts clean, and name the new object in the toast.
- On the one-section form, a key already in use raises the danger `Alert` above the fields as well as the `invalid` Key, and focus moves to Key.

## Don't

- Don't show a validation summary at the top; each field carries its own message.
- Don't toast a rejection a field owns (a key already in use, a deleted origin). The toast dismisses itself and points nowhere.
- Don't use the amber `required` prompt for a value the server rejected; the value is present, so it is `invalid`.
- Don't disable Create to signal missing values; let submit run and show the messages.
- Don't auto-dismiss an `Alert` that names a required action; it stays until the user recovers (see the Reloaded state of `platform/states/form-error`).

## Copy

- **Page heading:** `Create` plus the entity, matching the page it lists: `Create Variable`. Lead: one sentence on what it is for: `Add a key-value pair your services read at runtime.`
- **Field labels:** one to three words, no colon, no parentheses: `Key`, `Value`, `Environment`, `Description`.
- **Field descriptions:** a constraint or purpose, one sentence with a period: `Uppercase letters, digits and underscores, for example API_TOKEN.`, `Optional. Up to 200 characters.`
- **Required message:** names the field: `Key is required.`; for a select, the action: `Select an environment.`
- **Invalid message:** what is wrong and the rule: `Use uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.`
- **Conflict message:** the fact, on the field: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists.` The section `Alert` adds what happened and what to do: `A variable named API_TOKEN already exists in this account, so it wasn't created. Your entries are kept: change the key and press Create again.`
- **Error toast:** what did not happen, then what was kept: title `The variable wasn't created.`, description `The request didn't reach the server. Your entries are kept.`, action `Retry`.
- **Success toast:** past tense, names the object and where it applies: `API_TOKEN was created.` / `It is available in Production.`
- **Actions:** `Cancel`, `Create`, `Retry`.

## Accessibility

- The `<form>` is labelled by the heading (`aria-labelledby`), uses `novalidate`, and sets `aria-busy` while loading or submitting.
- Every control has a `Field.Label` bound by `for`; the description and message are wired to the control by `Field`.
- The loading region is `role="status"` with an accessible name (`Loading the form`).
- Focus moves to the first field in error, only after the lock is released, since a disabled control cannot take focus.
- Toasts are announced by the app's `Toaster` region; the error toast keeps its Retry reachable by keyboard.
- A section `Alert` sits in reading order before the fields it governs.

## States

- Default: the empty Create Variable form, idle.
- ValidationErrors: Create pressed with gaps; empty Value and Environment take `required`, the malformed Key takes `invalid`, each with its own message, and focus moves to Key.
- Submitting: the request is in flight; Create shows `loading`, the fields and Cancel are disabled.
- ServerError: the request failed and no field owns it; an error toast with Retry, the lock released, every entry kept.
- Conflict: the key is already in use; the danger `Alert` opens above the fields, Key takes `invalid` with its reason and focus, and nothing toasts.
- Saved: the save went through; a success toast names the variable and where it is available, and the form is cleared.
- Loading: the form data is still arriving; `Skeleton` rows hold the layout and Create is disabled.

## Related

- `platform/states/form-error` — a server rejection scoped to one section of a long form: the section `Alert` with its recovery action, and the field's own reason.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the long-running counterpart: the outcome reports back wherever the user is.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the sectioned create page these states apply to.
- `platform/auth` — the signed-out version, where every outcome lands in one card `Alert` and nothing toasts.
- `platform/settings/settings-form` — the same field states on an existing object.
- `Field` — the label, description and state triad every field here uses.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `ValidationErrors` · `Submitting` · `ServerError` · `Conflict` · `Saved` · `Loading`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/form-validation.md](blocks/platform/states/form-validation.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/form-validation", { variant })`.

# NotFound (`platform/states/not-found`)

> The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/not-found/not-found.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/not-found")`
- Components: Button, EmptyState, `Error403`, `Error404`
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-microcopy`

## Asked as

404 page; not found page; page not found; 403 forbidden page; access denied page; 500 error page; server error page; error page; resource not found; página não encontrada; página de erro; acesso negado; erro 404; erro 500

The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the user may not see it (403), or the server failed to build it (500). The user's job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address or the access and not their work, and to get somewhere useful in one click. The block keeps the error code out of the headline (it is in the figure and in a hidden `h1`) and says what happened in plain words.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A route that matches nothing: the catch-all route of the app renders the primary.
- A route the user's role does not include: render Forbidden instead of hiding the page silently or sending them to the home page.
- A page whose server request failed as a whole (the data the page needs did not arrive and nothing on it can render): render ServerError.
- A valid route whose record does not exist (a deleted service, a stale link with an old ID): render ResourceNotFound inside the console shell.

## When not to use

- One region of a page failed to render while the rest works: wrap the region in `ErrorBoundary`; it shows a danger `Alert` with Try again in the region's place.
- A list with no items yet: use `platform/states/first-use`. A list whose filter matched nothing: use the no-match state of `platform/view/table-view`.
- A form the server rejected: use `platform/states/form-error`.
- A build or deploy that failed: use `platform/states/async-submit`; its toast and page `Alert` carry Edit and Redeploy.
- The account itself could not load after sign-in: that is an auth screen; see `platform/auth`.

## Building blocks

- A. Figure — `Error404` (`@aziontech/webkit/svg/error-404`)
- B. Message — `EmptyState` (required)
- C. Actions — `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/not-found.md](blocks/platform/states/not-found.md).

## Do

- Render the block on the address the user asked for; do not redirect to `/404`, so reloading tries the real address again and the browser history stays honest.
- Answer with the matching HTTP status when the server renders the page (404, 403, 500), so crawlers and monitoring see it.
- Keep the shell (navigation, header) around ResourceNotFound and around a 403 inside the console, so the user can move on without the back button.
- Give a 500 an error reference the user can quote to support, and log the same reference on the server.
- On 403, say who can grant access (an account admin) and offer the switch when the user belongs to more than one account.

## Don't

- Don't blame the user (`You typed a wrong URL`) or show a stack trace, a raw status line or an exception message.
- Don't hide a 403 behind a 404 inside the product: a user who followed a link from a teammate needs to know to ask for access. Use 404 for a 403 only where revealing that the page exists would leak information.
- Don't add a search box, a sitemap or a list of popular pages; two actions are enough.
- Don't auto-redirect after a countdown; the user decides where to go.
- Don't put the error code in the visible title; the figure already shows it.

## Copy

- **Title:** what happened, sentence case, no code: `Page not found`, `You don't have access to this page`, `Something went wrong on our side`, `Service 4821 not found`.
- **Description:** why, and what to do: `There is nothing deployed at this address. Check the URL or head back to the start.` On a 500, reassure: `Nothing you saved was lost.`
- **Primary action:** where it goes: `Go to home`, `Back to services`; or what it does: `Try again`.
- **Secondary action:** `Docs`, `Switch account`, `System status`.
- **Reference:** `Error reference: req_7f3c91ab`, in monospace, wrapped in `<bdi>` so it keeps its order in right-to-left pages.

## Accessibility

- Each variant has exactly one `h1` (visually hidden) naming the error code, so the page has a heading and the code is announced even though the figure is decorative.
- Every variant is a body inside the layout's `main`, with no `main` of its own.
- The figure is `aria-hidden` (inside the `EmptyState` icon wrapper); never put the only statement of the error in the art.
- The `EmptyState` is `role="status"`, so a client-side route change to this page is announced.
- Try again shows the `Button` loading state while the page reloads; the button keeps its label.
- Buttons that open a new tab carry an icon; do not rely on colour.

## States

- Default: 404, the 404 numeral art, Page not found, Go to home and Docs.
- Forbidden: 403, the 403 numeral art, You don't have access to this page, Go to home and Switch account.
- ServerError: 500, the warning icon tile, Something went wrong on our side, Try again, System status and the error reference.
- ResourceNotFound: a bordered EmptyState in the console's content column naming the missing service and its ID, with Back to services.

## Related

- `shells/console` — the shell that frames ResourceNotFound and a 403 inside the product.
- `platform/states/first-use` — an empty list, which is not an error.
- `platform/states/form-error` — a server rejection scoped to a form section.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the outcome of a build or deploy, with Edit and Redeploy.
- `platform/auth` — the sign-in screens, including the account that could not load.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Forbidden` · `ServerError` · `ResourceNotFound`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/not-found.md](blocks/platform/states/not-found.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/not-found", { variant })`.

<!-- blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md -->

# PageWires (`platform/states/page-wires`)

> The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (HomeWire), the first-access Home (HomeFirstUseWire), and the whole shell while an expired session signs out (SessionWire), which draw…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/page-wires/page-wires.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/page-wires")`
- Components: Card, Item, Skeleton
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

page skeleton; loading skeleton; skeleton screen; page loading state; wireframe loading; session expired; carregando; esqueleto de carregamento; tela de carregamento

The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

Overview and Onboarding are page bodies for the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`); the Session wires stand in for the whole app, layout included.

## When to use

- The first paint of a page whose data is still loading, when the layout is known.
- Home, before its metrics and recent activity arrive (Overview), or before the first project (Onboarding).
- Over the whole app while an expired session signs out (the Session wires), so the user sees the page dissolve into its frame instead of a blank screen.

## When not to use

- A single control or panel loading inside a ready page: use `Skeleton` or `Spinner` inside that panel only.
- A form whose options are loading: use the Loading state of `platform/states/form-validation`.
- A dashboard's own loading: use the Loading variant of that dashboard block (for example `platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard`).
- A long upload or build: use `platform/states/project-intake` or `platform/states/async-submit`, which report progress.
- After the sign-out completes: `platform/auth` (SessionExpired).

## Building blocks

- A. Bands — `Skeleton` (required)
- B. Frames — `Card` (required)
- C. Lists — `Item` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md](blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md).

## Do

- Draw the exact grid of the page that is coming: same columns, gaps and breakpoints.
- Use the real layout utilities (`layout-column`, `layout-boundary`, `--layout-section-gap`), not fixed sizes.
- Hide the bands from assistive technology and announce the wait once: `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-busy="true"`, with a short screen-reader text on every wire.
- Size the session wire to the measured header and rail in the app, so the frame does not move when it appears.
- Fade the session wire in with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

## Don't

- Don't show a wire for less than a perceptible moment; if the data arrives within about 300 ms, paint the page directly.
- Don't use a generic spinner for a page whose layout is known.
- Don't animate each band independently; a shimmer comes from `Skeleton`.
- Don't mix real content and bands in one card; the card swaps in whole.
- Don't let the wire collapse to a few lines on wide screens; it holds the page's full footprint.

## Copy

- **Bands:** no visible text. The wire has nothing to read.
- **Screen-reader status (session):** states what is happening, as a sentence: `Session expired. Signing you out.`
- **Screen-reader status (page):** names what is loading: `Loading the overview.` on the Overview wire, `Loading Home.` on the Onboarding wire.

## Accessibility

- The bands are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"` on the wire's body).
- The region that stands in for the page is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-busy="true"`; clear `aria-busy` when the content lands.
- The wire takes no focus and traps none; the real page receives focus as it would on a normal load.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` on the entrance and on the shimmer.

## States

- Overview: the Home overview wire: heading, the four-metric strip, the side card, and the five-column row of list panels.
- Onboarding: the first-access Home wire: headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each with its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.
- Session: the whole shell as a wire over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.
- SessionDetail: the same over a detail page: tab bands under the header, a heading and two cards of field rows in the data column.
- SessionForm: the same over a create page: a heading and two cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.
- SessionHome: the same over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.

## Related

- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — the Home page the Overview and Onboarding wires stand in for.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list page the Session wire draws.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the detail page the SessionDetail wire draws.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — the create page the SessionForm wire draws.
- `platform/auth` — where the session wire lands once the sign-out completes.
- `shells/console` — the header and rail the session wires reproduce.

## Variants

`Overview` (primary) · `Onboarding` · `Session` · `SessionDetail` · `SessionForm` · `SessionHome`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md](blocks/platform/states/page-wires.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/page-wires", { variant })`.

# ProjectIntake (`platform/states/project-intake`)

> The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the dashed drop target that fills the page while a folder hovers over it, then the full-screen Initializing overlay that reads like the deploy logs…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/states/project-intake/project-intake.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/states/project-intake")`
- Components: Card, Spinner
- Skills: `webkit-ui-states`, `webkit-motion-polish`

## Asked as

drop zone; drag and drop upload; upload project; folder upload; initializing project; file drop; arrastar e soltar; enviar projeto; upload de arquivos

The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: while a folder hovers over the page, a dashed drop target fills it and says what will happen; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay reads like the deploy logs, one row per received file, until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

DropZone is a page-body overlay inside the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`); Initializing covers the whole screen.

## When to use

- Pages where dropping a project is a shortcut to deploying it: Home, its empty state, a creation hub, and a project detail page.
- Showing upload progress per file, when the files are few enough to list.

## When not to use

- Choosing a single file as a form value: use a file upload field inside the form (`skills/webkit-form`).
- Browsing or managing stored files: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- The build and deploy that follow the upload: use `platform/states/async-submit` and `platform/create/deployment-flow`.
- Importing from a repository: use the From GitHub method in `platform/states/first-use` or `platform/create/source-wizard`.

## Building blocks

- A. Drop target — plain elements (required while dragging)
- B. Drop message — plain elements (required while dragging)
- C. Initializing overlay — plain elements (Initializing)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md](blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md).

## Do

- Show the drop target only while a folder is dragged over the page, and remove it on drop or drag leave.
- Say what dropping does, not how to drop: the user is already dragging.
- Render Initializing over the page the drop came from (Home, its empty state, the creation hub), so the user keeps their place.
- Advance the rows in order and keep finished rows visible; the list is the progress.
- Offer an upload or import action elsewhere on the page; drag and drop is a shortcut, never the only way.

## Don't

- Don't intercept the drop with the overlay; it is `pointer-events-none`.
- Don't use a percentage bar alone for a handful of files; the per-file rows say more.
- Don't show the drop target on pages where a drop does nothing.
- Don't keep the overlay up after the upload ends; hand over to the deploy's own progress.

## Copy

- **Drop heading:** what the drop does, one line: `Drop your project to deploy it`. On a project page: `We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.`
- **Drop lead:** what is accepted, full sentences: `A project folder, or the files inside one. We detect what it is built with.`
- **Overlay heading:** one word for the phase: `Initializing`.
- **Overlay progress:** what is happening and how far, with a period: `Setting up your deployment. 2 of 5 files.`
- **Summary:** count and total size: `5 files, 8.17 KB`.

## Accessibility

- The drop target is `aria-hidden="true"`: it is a pointer affordance. Keyboard and screen reader users need the page's own upload or import action.
- The Initializing overlay is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so progress is announced without stealing focus; announce the count, not every row.
- Status glyphs are decorative; the row text and the progress line carry the state.
- Every fade and the row advance honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## States

- DropZone: a folder hovers over the page; the dashed drop target fills it with the drop message.
- Initializing: the overlay mid-upload, two files uploaded, the third running, two queued, each row with its status glyph, path and size.

## Related

- `platform/states/first-use` — an empty list page that can also render the drop target.
- `platform/create/create-hub` — a creation hub that renders the drop target and Initializing.
- `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — Home and its empty state, which render both surfaces.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — the step-row anatomy the Initializing rows reuse.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — how the deploy that follows reports back.

## Variants

`DropZone` (primary) · `Initializing`. Code: [blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md](blocks/platform/states/project-intake.md), `get_pattern("platform/states/project-intake", { variant })`.

# CardView (`platform/view/card-view`)

> The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/card-view/card-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/card-view")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Cards, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, Input, PageHeader, Pagination, PropertyFilter, Tag, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

card view; cards view; card list; cards list; resource cards; grid of cards; card grid page; gallery of resources; applications as cards; selectable cards; cards with filters; cards with pagination; visualização em cards; lista em cards; cartões de recursos; grade de cards

The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources people tell apart by a handful of fields or a picture rather than by comparing one column across many rows (applications, sites, templates, images).
- Each item has a short, stable set of fields (four to six) that reads well as label and value pairs.
- Users act on several items at once (delete, move, tag) and need the selection to survive paging and filtering.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and visible fields must survive the next visit.

## When not to use

- Records compared and sorted column by column, or more than six fields per item: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use `platform/detail/details-page` or `platform/detail/record-table`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Choosing a starting point to create from (templates, products): use `platform/create/create-hub` or `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `platform/states/first-use`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Bulk action — `Button` (required)
- D. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- E. Card preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- F. Cards — `Cards`, `Tag` (required)
- G. Pagination — `Pagination` (required)
- H. No matching applications — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- I. Empty listing — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/card-view.md](blocks/platform/view/card-view.md).

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call with `selection: { mode: 'multi' }` and bind `cardsProps`, `paginationProps`, `propertyFilterProps` and `preferencesProps` with `v-bind`.
- Keep the controls row, the cards and the pagination in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Name every card with a link to the resource in the `header` slot, and keep its fields to the few that tell one item from another.
- Render the fields from `preferences.columns`, so the order and visibility set in the dialog reach every card.
- Count the selection in the bulk action's label and disable it at zero.
- Put every Delete behind the confirmation dialog, with the count in its title and the names in its body.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens, the sort and the page live in the query string, and give the list a `storageKey` of its own.
- Choose page sizes that fill whole rows of four.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` replaces the cards with the create state, `no-match` fills the `#empty` slot with Clear filters.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`.
- Don't make the whole card a link or a click target when it is also selectable; the name link opens it and the checkbox selects it.
- Don't put row-style action menus on every card for actions the bulk action already covers.
- Don't vary a card's height or field order from one card to the next; every card shows the same fields in the same order, with a dash for a missing value.
- Don't truncate the name in the header to fit a badge; the status lives in the fields.
- Don't hide Delete when nothing is selected; disable it so its place in the row stays put.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every card, or Clear filters when the account has none.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Applications". Description: one sentence with a period.
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Application"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter applications".
- **Bulk action:** the verb, then the count in parentheses, e.g. "Delete", "Delete (3)".
- **Field labels:** one or two words, sentence case, no colon, e.g. "Status", "Domain", "Region", "Requests in 24h", "Owner". Preferences title: "Card preferences".
- **Delete dialog:** title `Delete <n> applications`, consequence `The selected applications will be deleted, along with their domains and settings:` followed by the names, prompt `Type delete to confirm.`, actions `Cancel` and `Delete applications` (singular for one).
- **No match:** "No matching applications", then "No application matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No applications yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create an application to start serving traffic."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- `Cards` is a list named by its `aria-label`; each card is labelled by its header, and its checkbox is named by the same text.
- Select all items is a visible, labelled checkbox, not an icon; its state is mixed when part of the page is selected.
- Field labels and values are a `dl`, so each value is read with its label; status is a `Tag` with text, never color alone.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Delete, Preferences, Select all items, each card's checkbox and link, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, names itself by its title, labels its input by the prompt and returns focus to Delete (n) when it closes.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.

## States

- Default: applications exist; the cards show them with the property filter, multi-select with Delete (n) behind its confirmation dialog, preferences and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching applications with Clear filters.
- Empty: the account has no applications; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a medium empty state with Create Application replaces the cards.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the same collection, rendered as a sortable table.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind Delete (n).
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where a card's name leads.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `useCollection`, `Cards` and `Pagination` — see `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Empty`. Code: [blocks/platform/view/card-view.md](blocks/platform/view/card-view.md), `get_pattern("platform/view/card-view", { variant })`.
