# FileBrowser (`platform/view/file-browser`)

> The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `TableRoot` whose toolbar is the whole page header.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/file-browser/file-browser.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/file-browser")`
- Components: Alert, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, Combobox, ConfirmDialog, Dialog, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, EmptyState, Field, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, IconButton, Input, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, SplitButton, Switch, Table, `TableRoot`, `TableSearch`, Toast, Tooltip, UploadProgress
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

file browser; file manager; storage browser; bucket browser; object storage; folders and files; upload files; navegador de arquivos; gerenciador de arquivos; arquivos do bucket; upload progress; move files; move objects; drag and drop upload; enviar arquivos; mover arquivos

The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A storage resource (an Object Storage bucket, a build output) opens on its files and folders.
- Users move through a folder tree and need to know where they are and how to go back up.
- Files are compared by name, size and last change, and acted on one at a time: open, download, delete.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources of one type: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Rows of one resource that are records, not files (database rows, variables): use `platform/detail/record-table`.
- Events or logs explored over time: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- Tables and queries of a database: use `platform/view/query-editor`.
- Picking an existing resource inside a create form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Surface — `Card`, `TableRoot` (required)
- B. Storage title and search — `TableSearch` (required)
- C. Toolbar actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- D. Columns panel — `PopoverRoot`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverContent`, `Field`, `Switch`, `Button` (optional)
- E. Path and create — `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton` (required)
- F. Cell recipes — `Table.CellTime` (optional)
- G. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption` (required)
- H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- I. Empty folder — `EmptyState`, `SplitButton` (required)
- J. Upload — `SplitButton` (optional)
- K. Transfer card and outcome toast — `Button` (optional)
- L. Selection and Move — `TableRoot`, `DropdownMenuOption` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md](blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md).

## Do

- Keep the storage name, search, path and Add to files inside the table toolbar, on the same surface as the rows.
- Sort folders before files and open a folder on row click.
- Show the path as a `Breadcrumb` and keep the `..` row while inside a folder.
- Use one Add to files `SplitButton` for every way of adding content.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and confirm it with `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Keep refused files in the upload dialog with their reason, and leave them out of the upload count.
- Run every transfer in the one floating `UploadProgress` card and let the person keep working.
- End every transfer with a toast whose action fits the files: Open folder or Retry failed.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't add a `PageHeader` above the card; the toolbar is the header.
- Don't split Upload file and Add folder into two primary buttons.
- Don't give the `..` row a row menu, a size or an author.
- Don't let the table scroll the page sideways; on a phone the grid scrolls sideways inside its card, never the page.
- Don't replace the toolbar with a full-page empty state when a folder is empty; only the table area changes.
- Don't block the page with a modal progress dialog while files upload or move.
- Don't offer View deployments, Edit or Redeploy after a storage transfer; nothing is deployed.
- Don't drop a refused file silently, and don't send a file the dialog marked as refused.

## Copy

- **Storage name:** the resource name as created, e.g. "acme-assets"; never prefixed with the type.
- **Search:** placeholder names the scope, e.g. "Search in folder".
- **Add action:** "Add to files", with options "Upload file" and "Add folder".
- **Row menu:** one verb per option, e.g. "Open", "Download", "Delete"; the trigger is named "Actions for <file>".
- **Delete dialog:** title and confirm `Delete file` or `Delete folder`, consequence `The selected folder will be deleted, along with all its files.`, prompt `Type <name> to confirm.`
- **Column headers:** short fragments, e.g. "Name", "Size", "Last modified".
- **Empty folder:** title states the fact, e.g. "This folder is empty"; description is one sentence, e.g. "Upload files or create a folder to get started."
- **Upload dialog:** title `Upload files`, primary `Upload file` or `Upload 3 files`, refusal `Larger than 300 MB, the limit per file`.
- **Drop overlay:** `Drop files to upload them to <folder>`, description `Up to 300 MB per file.`
- **Move dialog:** title `Move <name>` or `Move 2 files`, field `Destination folder`, placeholder `/ (storage root)`, errors `Use letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and slashes only.`, `A destination cannot go up with "..". Type the full path.`, `The files are already in this folder. Pick another one.`
- **Toasts:** `5 files uploaded to acme-assets.` with Open folder; `1 of 5 files weren't uploaded.` with Retry failed; `2 files moved to logs/.` with Open folder.
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The card sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; the storage name is the visible title of the surface.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; file and folder glyphs carry `aria-hidden="true"`, so the name cell reads as the name alone.
- The `Breadcrumb` crumbs are links the keyboard reaches in order; the last crumb is the current folder.
- Folder rows open on click and the Open option in the row menu gives the same action to keyboard users.
- Focus order follows reading order: search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns, path, Add to files, the rows.
- `Table.CellTime` names the author and reads the absolute time to screen readers.
- The drop overlay is `aria-hidden`: dragging is a pointer path, and Add to files with Browse files is the keyboard path to the same upload.
- `UploadProgress` is a region named File transfers with a polite status that announces each file finishing and the outcome; percentages are not announced. The toast repeats the outcome for people who collapsed the card.
- In the upload dialog each refused file's reason is the `aria-describedby` of its Remove button, and removing a file moves focus to the next one.
- The Move dialog's `Field` wires the label, description and error to the `Combobox`; the error is read when focus returns to it.

## States

- Default: the storage root with folders first, then files, and the full toolbar.
- InsideAFolder: inside a build folder the crumb gains the folder, a `..` row leads back up and files show glyph, size, editor and age.
- Uploading: a transfer is running in the floating card; one file fails once and can be retried; the upload dialog and the page drop overlay add more.
- MoveObject: two files selected inside a build folder with the Move dialog open; moving runs in the card and ends in a toast.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the first-level list a storage resource is opened from.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind Delete on a file or folder.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — the storage resource's own details and settings.
- `platform/detail/record-table` — records of a resource, not files.
- `FileTokenGroup`, `FileDropzone` and `UploadProgress` — the upload pieces; see their component docs.
- `platform/states/async-submit` — the rule for long actions; storage transfers follow it with item actions instead of Edit and Redeploy.
- `TableRoot` — the data-driven table this page wraps; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `InsideAFolder` · `Uploading` · `MoveObject`. Code: [blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md](blocks/platform/view/file-browser.md), `get_pattern("platform/view/file-browser", { variant })`.

# Marketplace (`platform/view/marketplace`)

> The marketplace page: a medium page heading with the outlined Documentation action over `Tabs` for Integrations and Templates.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/marketplace/marketplace.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/marketplace")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, DocProse, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, Field, Input, Item, KeyValuePairs, Link, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, PropertyFilter, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Skeleton, Switch, Table, Tabs, Tag, Toast, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

marketplace; integration catalog; integrations marketplace; install an integration; browse integrations; extensions catalog; plugin catalog; app store page; integration detail; installed integrations; configure integration; marketplace de integrações; catálogo de integrações; instalar integração; loja de extensões

The page where people find something made by Azion or a partner and add it to what they run. Two kinds of item live here: integrations, installed into an existing application, and templates, which start a new project. People browse by need ("block bots", "split traffic"), compare by publisher and context, read what an integration does and what it may touch, then install it on one application and keep working while it installs. One `useCollection` call holds the search and the filters; one drawer holds the detail and the install; the install reports by toast wherever the person is.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A catalog of installable add-ons (integrations, extensions, plugins) with a publisher, a category and an installed state per account.
- Installing means choosing a target (an application) and waiting for an asynchronous run.
- The same page also points people at templates, the other way to start from someone else's work.

## When not to use

- Only templates, with a preview and a README: use `platform/view/template-browser`.
- Deploying a chosen template: use `platform/create/deploy-template`.
- The resources the account already created: use `platform/view/card-view` or `platform/view/table-view`.
- Changing the settings of an installed integration on one application: use `platform/edit/edit-resource` from Configure.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Item kinds — `Tabs` (required)
- C. Featured — `Card` (required)
- D. Search and filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- E. Integration tiles — `Card`, `Button` (required)
- F. No matching integrations — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- G. Popular templates — `Card`, `Button` (required)
- H. Integration drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` (required)
- I. Install outcome — `Alert` (required)
- J. Integration facts — `KeyValuePairs` (required)
- K. Overview — `DocProse` (required)
- L. Install form — `Field`, `Select` (required)
- M. Solution page — `Tabs`, `Card`, `Select`, `Field`, `KeyValuePairs`, `DocProse` (optional)
- N. Configure screen — `Field`, `Select`, `Alert`, `Button` (optional)
- O. Template page — `Field`, `Button`, `KeyValuePairs` (optional)
- Install toast — through `toast`

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/marketplace.md](blocks/platform/view/marketplace.md).

## Do

- Run the catalog on one `useCollection` call with `filtering`, `propertyFiltering` and `url: true`; derive the Status property from where each integration is installed.
- Use `Card kind="integration"` for every integration tile, with the installed state as the `installed` prop and one action in the `action` slot.
- Hide the Featured row while any filter is set.
- Open the detail in a drawer so the catalog, the filter and the scroll stay put.
- Show the permissions before the install form, and the target as a required field.
- Treat install as an async run: `loading` on Install, a progress toast, then the outcome as a toast and an inline `Alert`, with actions that fit an integration (Configure, Open application; Edit, Reinstall).
- Keep the failure toast until the person closes it.

## Don't

- Don't install from the tile in one click; the person must pick the application and see the permissions.
- Don't point the outcome at a list of runs ("View installs", "View deployments"); the toast carries Configure or Edit and Reinstall.
- Don't use "Retry" or "Try again" for a failed install; the action is Reinstall.
- Don't show Install for an application that already runs the integration; filter it out of the `Select`.
- Don't badge every tile with more than one tag beside Installed; the publisher and the category are enough to compare.
- Don't rebuild the template browser inside the Templates tab; link to it.

## Copy

- **Title:** "Marketplace". Description: "Find integrations and templates that run on your applications."
- **Tabs:** "Integrations", "Templates". **Sections:** "Featured", "All integrations", "Popular templates".
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` "Search integrations".
- **Tile action:** "Install" or "Configure"; its `aria-label` adds the name.
- **Drawer:** the name, "by <publisher>", "Overview", "Permissions", "Install" or "Install on another application", the field "Application" with "Select an application".
- **Validation:** "Select the application to install <name> on."
- **Progress toast:** "Installing <name> on <application>…" / "It keeps running if you close this panel."
- **Success:** toast "<name> is installed on <application>." / "It runs from the next request to the application.", actions "Configure" and "Open application"; the inline `Alert` says the same in one line.
- **Failure:** toast "<name> wasn't installed on <application>." with the reason as a full sentence, actions "Edit" and "Reinstall"; the inline `Alert` carries the reason and "Reinstall".
- **No match:** "No matching integrations", "No integration matches this search. Remove a filter to widen the results.", "Clear filters".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the only `h1`, each section heading an `h2`, each tile name an `h3`.
- The tabs follow the tablist pattern: arrow keys move between Integrations and Templates, and each panel is labelled by its tab.
- Each tile's target is a real button named by the integration; the action button sits above it and is named with the integration, so "Install" is never ambiguous in a list.
- The Installed state is text in a `Tag`, never colour alone.
- The drawer traps focus, is named by `DrawerTitle`, closes on Escape and returns focus to what opened it; its form has an accessible name.
- The Application field is required and labelled; its error is tied to the `Select` through the `Field`, and focus stays on Install so the person can correct and resubmit.
- Toasts are announced politely and never take focus; the failure toast stays until closed and its actions are reachable by keyboard.

## States

- Default: the Integrations tab with Featured, All integrations, the filter and the tiles; a tile opens the drawer and Install runs and lands as a success toast and Alert.
- Templates: the Templates tab with popular templates linking to the template browser.
- Detail: the drawer is open on Request Signer with its details, overview, permissions and the install form.
- Installing: Install is running on storefront; the button is `loading`, the field disabled and the progress toast says it keeps running.
- Installed: Request Signer is installed on storefront; the success Alert, the Installed tag, Configure in the footer and the success toast with Configure and Open application.
- InstallFailed: the install on checkout failed; the danger Alert with the reason and Reinstall, and the permanent toast with Edit and Reinstall.
- NoMatch: the search "kubernetes" matches nothing; the Featured row hides and the empty state offers Clear filters.
- Loading: the filter is disabled and six `Skeleton` tiles (logo, name, two lines, badge, action) hold the grid in a band that is `aria-busy`.

- SolutionPage: Waiting Room as a page, storefront on 1.3.0 (Update available) and checkout on 1.4.0.
- Configure: Waiting Room settings on storefront, with the SaveBar after a change.
- TemplatePage: Nuxt Storefront as a page with its deploy form.

# QueryEditor (`platform/view/query-editor`)

> The query editor page (the app passes the Databases breadcrumb to the layout): the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/query-editor/query-editor.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/query-editor")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Brand, Breadcrumb, Button, Card, CodeEditor, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, FileDropzone, FileTokenGroup, GlobalHeader, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PaginationRoot`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Sidebar, Switch, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, Toast, ToggleGroup, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-layout`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

query editor; sql editor; run query; query results; sql query page; query history; sql code editor; código sql; editor de consultas; editor sql; executar consulta; sql database; database tables; database detail; table schema; data grid; sql templates; banco de dados; banco de dados sql; tabelas do banco; create database; criar banco de dados; table rows; linhas da tabela; import csv; import data; csv import; importar csv; importar dados

The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The editor is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the side panel, the rows, the editor and the results each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview). CreateDatabase is a focused create page with its own header and no rail, rendered outside it.

## When to use

- A database resource opens on its tables and an editor that runs SQL against them.
- Users switch between browsing data (rows, columns, constraints) and writing queries without leaving the resource.
- Results need both a table view and the raw JSON, with paging over large result sets.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of databases: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Rows of a resource that are not a SQL table (variables, records): use `platform/detail/record-table`.
- Editing a function or configuration as code: use `platform/edit/code-editor`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Events explored over time: use `platform/view/split-view`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page tabs — `PageTabs`, `Tabs` (required)
- B. Tables panel — `Sidebar`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- C. Empty database — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- D. Table data — `ToggleGroup`, `Input`, `Button`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `TableRoot` (required)
- E. Table definition — `Button`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag` (optional)
- F. Query history — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `DropdownMenu` (required)
- G. Editor — `Button`, `CodeEditor` (required)
- H. Results — `Input`, `ToggleGroup`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `TableRoot`, `Alert`, `EmptyState`, `PaginationRoot` (required)
- I. Templates drawer — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `PanelContent`, `Input` (optional)
- J. Bulk row delete — `Button` (optional)
- K. Create database page — `Input`, `Button` (optional)
- L. Import data from CSV — `Drawer`, `Alert`, `TableRoot`, `Button` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/query-editor.md](blocks/platform/view/query-editor.md).

## Do

- Keep both tabs on the same layout: side panel to list, working pane to act.
- Let the side panel resize and collapse, and keep its width when the user switches tabs.
- Make the editor read-only and disable its toolbar while a query runs, and show Run query loading.
- Show the outcome of a run in the Results band: the rows, a success `Alert` with what ran, or a danger `Alert` with why it failed.
- Offer JSON beside Table for results, so the raw shape is one click away.
- Confirm Delete table with `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation`.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill` (every variant but CreateDatabase), so the panes scroll on their own instead of the page.
- Raise toasts with `toast` only; the app mounts the one toast region (`ToastPlugin`, or one `Toaster` at its root, as `shells/console` does), so this page body never renders a `Toaster`.

## Don't

- Don't open a separate page for a table or a query; they open in the pane.
- Don't run a query on every keystroke; Run query is the only trigger.
- Don't hide the tabs when the database is empty.
- Don't put a second primary action in a pane; Insert on Data and Run query on Editor are the only ones.
- Don't let the results scroll the page sideways; they scroll inside their band.
- Don't size the root with `calc(100dvh - …)`; `data-layout-fill` fits it to the layout's `main`.

## Copy

- **Tabs:** one noun each, e.g. "Tables", "Editor".
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>`, e.g. "Create Table", the same in the panel and the empty state.
- **Editor toolbar:** verb-first, e.g. "Run query", "Prettify", "Templates".
- **Editor placeholder:** one instruction, e.g. "Write your SQL query here".
- **Search:** names the scope, e.g. "Search tables", "Search queries", "Search templates".
- **Empty states:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No tables yet" with "Create your first table to store your data."; "Ready to execute" with "Execute a query to see the results here."
- **Import:** `Import data from CSV` opens `Import data into <table>`; the submit is `Insert <n> rows`; per-line errors read `Line <n>: <column> “<value>” is not <expected> (<type>).` or `<column> is empty and cannot be.`
- **Row menus:** verb and object, e.g. "Delete table", "Run query", "Delete query".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the tabs are a real tab list, so arrow keys move between Tables and Editor.
- Each side `Sidebar` is named (Tables, Query history) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The `CodeEditor` has the `aria-label` "SQL editor"; its markers are listed in its problems list as text, not by colour.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label` that matches its `Tooltip`; the rows table is named `Rows of <table>` and its selection checkboxes come from `TableRoot`, named per row.
- On Create Database, the Name error is the input's `aria-describedby` and focus returns to the input after a failed submit.
- `ToggleGroup`s are named ("Table view", "Result view") and the pagination is named "Results pagination".
- The templates drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape.
- In the import drawer each mapping `Select` is named `Table column for <CSV column>`, the mapping and the per-line errors are named lists, and the ready count is a polite live region, so changing a mapping announces the new count.

## States

- Tables: the Tables tab with the tables listed in the side panel and the selected table's Data view in the pane.
- Schema: the Definition view of customers, with the Columns heading, Add column and a card of column name, type and constraints.
- EmptyDatabase: a database with no tables; the side panel says so and the pane shows the Create Table empty state.
- Query: the Editor tab after a query ran, with the history in the side panel, the statement in the editor and its rows in Results.
- Templates: the Editor tab before anything ran, with Results ready to execute and the SQL quick templates drawer behind the Templates button.
- TableData: the events table, 137 rows paged 25 at a time, with two rows selected and Delete 2 rows in the toolbar.
- ImportCsv: the empty subscribers table with the import drawer open on a seven-row file: `plan_name` still on Skip (Insert asks to map `plan`), `referrer` skipped, three lines with errors (a non-boolean, an empty required email, a date that does not parse).
- CreateDatabase: the create database page with its Name and Active fields; try `acme-store` for the name conflict and a name starting with `offline` for the failed request.
- Failed: the selected table's rows did not load; the Data view shows a danger `Alert` that names the table and offers Retry.

# RulesList (`platform/view/rules-list`)

> An ordered list of rules grouped by phase, the Rules tab of an application or a firewall.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/rules-list/rules-list.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/rules-list")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, AttributeEditor, Button, Card, Combobox, Dialog, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, EmptyState, Field, HelperText, IconButton, Input, Item, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, RadioButton, SaveBar, Select, SettingRow, SettingsSection, Switch, `TableRoot`, Tag, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

rules list; rules engine list; reorder rules; rule order; drag and drop reorder; firewall rules; request and response phases; review changes; enable disable rule; lista de regras; ordem das regras; reordenar regras; regras do firewall; fases de requisição e resposta; lista de reglas; reordenar reglas

An ordered list of rules grouped by phase: the Rules tab of an application (Request and Response phases) or a firewall (Request only). Order is behavior here, so the list is built to change the order safely: drag, keys or Move up and Move down move a rule, every move is announced, and nothing runs in the new order until the user reviews the changes and saves.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A resource runs an ordered program of rules and the user needs to see it, reorder it and turn rules on or off: application rules engine, firewall rules, routing rules.
- Rules split into phases that never interleave (request and response), each with its own order.
- Changes to the order must be reviewed before they apply to live traffic.

## When not to use

- Records whose order does not matter: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Writing or editing one rule's criteria and behaviors: use `platform/edit/rule-builder`, which this list opens from Add Rule and from a rule's name.
- Fewer than two rules that can move: show the list without the Order controls.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Search — `Input`, `Alert` (required)
- C. Phases — `Card`, `Accordion` (required)
- D. Rules table — `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Field`, `Switch` (required)
- E. Order controls — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- F. Save bar and review — `SaveBar`, `Button`, `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogClose`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert` (required)
- G. States — `EmptyState` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/rules-list.md](blocks/platform/view/rules-list.md).

## Do

- Keep phases separate: a rule moves only within its phase, and drag ignores drops on another phase.
- Offer every way to move: drag for a pointer, arrow keys, Home and End on the grip, and Move up and Move down for touch and switch access.
- Say why a control is disabled, in its accessible name and its tooltip.
- Collect changes and apply them only after Review changes and Save; the review lists every rule whose position changes, not only the one the user dragged.
- Let a rule be turned off in place; an inactive rule keeps its position and is skipped at runtime.
- Follow `skills/webkit-tables` for the table, `skills/webkit-form` for the save bar and `skills/webkit-errors` for the failed save.

## Don't

- Don't save on every drop; one wrong drag would reorder live traffic.
- Don't allow reordering while a search hides rows; positions would be ambiguous.
- Don't let anything move above a locked default rule, or turn it off.
- Don't put the review in a toast or a popover; it is a decision with a list to read.
- Don't offer drag as the only way to reorder.

## Copy

- **Phase triggers:** "Request phase", "Response phase", with "5 rules" or "2 of 5" beside.
- **Order control names:** "Reorder Docs rewrite, position 5 of 5" (the table's grip, described by its drag-or-arrow hint), "Move Docs rewrite up", and when disabled "Move Default rule down. The default rule runs first and stays first."
- **Disabled reasons:** "The default rule runs first and stays first.", "Clear the search to change the order rules run in.", "There is no other rule in this phase to move it past."
- **Announcements:** "Docs rewrite moved to position 3 of 5 in the Request phase.", "Changes discarded. The rules are back in their saved order."
- **Save bar:** "3 changes to the rules, not saved yet." with Discard and Review changes.
- **Review lines:** "<Rule> moves from position 5 to 3.", "<Rule> is turned on."
- **Failure:** "The new order wasn't saved. The rules still run in the saved order; save again to apply it."
- **Success toast:** "Rule order saved." with "The application runs its rules in the new order."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Each phase is a disclosure: the trigger is a button inside an `h2` with `aria-expanded`, and the panel is a region named by it.
- Every Order control has a name that includes the rule and the phase; disabled controls include the reason.
- Keyboard: Tab reaches the grip, Move up, Move down, the rule link and its switch, in that order; the grip moves the rule with Up, Down, Home and End and Escape cancels a drag. Focus follows the moved rule.
- Moves and discards are announced once in a polite `role="status"` region that exists from the first render.
- The `Switch` is named "Run <rule>"; its visible Active or Inactive text is hidden from the accessibility tree so the state is read once, from `aria-checked`.
- The review dialog traps focus, returns it to Review changes on close, and is not dismissible while saving; the failure `Alert` is read when it appears.
- Drop targets show a 2 px accent line and the dragged row fades; transitions respect reduced motion.

## States

- Application: Request and Response phases, a locked Default rule first in Request, one inactive rule per phase.
- Firewall: one Request phase, every rule movable.
- ReviewChanges: two moves and one status change, the save bar and the review dialog open.
- SaveFailed: the review dialog open with the failure `Alert` and Save again.
- Searching: "cache" typed, reordering off with its `Alert`, phases reading "n of total".
- Empty: a firewall with no rules, the Request phase showing its `EmptyState`.
- Loading: skeleton rows in each phase.
- EditRule: the list composed with `platform/edit/rule-builder`. A rule's name is a button ("Edit Docs rewrite") that opens the builder `Drawer` as Edit Rule, seeded with the rule and its phase locked; Add Rule in the header or in an empty phase opens it as Add Rule in that phase. Saving an edit updates the row and says so in a toast; a new rule lands last in its phase with a toast that offers Edit. Neither is an order change, so the `SaveBar` still counts only moves and switches. Product pages (an application's or a firewall's Rules tab) compose the two the same way.

## Related

- `platform/edit/rule-builder` — the drawer that adds or edits one rule.
- `platform/view/table-view` — lists whose order does not matter.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the failed-save `Alert` pattern the review dialog follows.
- `platform/view/waf-tuning` — the WAF tuning list a firewall's WAF rule links to.

## Variants

# SplitView (`platform/view/split-view`)

> The events explorer (the app marks its Events navigation entry active): the controls row (Filter popover, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied filter chips, and the explorer.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/split-view/split-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/split-view")`
- Components: Accordion, Alert, Badge, Button, `CalendarRoot`, Chart, Checkbox, Chip, CodeBlock, CopyButton, DateRangePicker, Drawer, `DrawerClose`, `DrawerContent`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, `PanelHeader`, Popover, PropertyFilter, Sidebar, Table, `TableRoot`, Tabs, Tag, Tooltip, `use-collection`
- Skills: `webkit-data-viz`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

real-time events; events visualizer; event explorer; log explorer; logs viewer; request logs; events search; eventos em tempo real; visualizador de eventos; explorador de logs; split view; master detail; list and detail panes; visão dividida; query language; events query; saved searches; saved queries; query history; date range; time range picker; investigation tabs; event document; consulta de eventos; buscas salvas; intervalo de datas

The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`. The explorer is a workspace: its root carries `data-layout-fill`, so the layout's `main` stops scrolling, the root fills it, and the fields panel, the log and the event document each scroll on their own at every width (`h-dvh` only sizes a standalone preview).

## When to use

- Events or logs explored over time, where the volume chart and the rows must agree on one period and one set of filters.
- Users pivot on field values (level, source, status, host) to find a pattern, then read one event's full document.
- The record has more fields than a table row can hold, so the full document opens beside the list instead of in a details page.

## When not to use

- A first-level list of resources the user creates and manages: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- The log of one deployment or build run: use `platform/detail/deployment-logs`.
- Metrics and charts without a row-level log: use `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Querying a database with SQL: use `platform/view/query-editor`.

## Building blocks

- A. Filter popover — `Popover`, `Button`, `Badge`, `CalendarRoot`, `Input` (required)
- B. Search and toolbar — `Input`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (required)
- C. Applied filters — `Chip` (optional)
- D. Fields panel — `Sidebar`, `Input`, `Field`, `Checkbox`, `Popover`, `Accordion`, `Tag` (optional)
- E. Log — `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Table`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)
- F. Event document — `Sidebar`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- G. Narrow document — `Drawer`, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, `DrawerContent`, `PanelHeader`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerClose`, `Tag`, `CodeBlock` (required)
- H. Query bar — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- I. Saved and recent queries — `Popover`, `IconButton`, `Input`, `Button`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- J. Investigation tabs — `IconButton`, `Input`, `Tooltip` (optional)
- K. Document tools — `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Chip` (optional)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/split-view.md](blocks/platform/view/split-view.md).

## Do

- Drive the summary, the chart and the table from one filtered set, so every number agrees.
- Let a click or drag on the chart set the period, and show the period as a filter the user can clear.
- Keep the row selected while its document is open, and switch between pane and drawer by the explorer's width, not the viewport's.
- Count applied fields on the Filter `Badge` and show each one as a `Chip` in field order.
- Pick the empty message that matches why the log is empty.
- In query mode, keep the applied query text as the user typed it, and save and list that text.
- Keep each investigation tab self-contained: its own filters, search and period.
- Let the document act on the log (Filter by, Exclude), so a pivot is one click from the value.
- Mark the page root with `data-layout-fill`, so the panes scroll on their own instead of the page.

## Don't

- Don't navigate away to read one event; the document opens beside the log.
- Don't add a second filter surface (a row of `Select`s, a filter bar in the fields panel) beside the Filter popover.
- Don't hide the controls row or the summary when the log is empty.
- Don't encode level by colour alone; the chart has a card with level names and counts, and the table shows level as text.
- Don't let a wide log scroll the page sideways.
- Don't size the root with `calc(100dvh - …)`; `data-layout-fill` fits it to the layout's `main`.
- Don't offer the query bar and the Filter popover at once; pick the one that fits the users.
- Don't guess the meaning of a query that mixes AND and OR; say so and let the user fix it.
- Don't let investigation tabs grow without a limit, and never close the last one.

## Copy

- **Search:** placeholder names what is searched, e.g. "Search events, hosts, paths or addresses"; `aria-label` "Search events".
- **Summary labels:** short nouns, e.g. "Events", "Errors", "Avg request time".
- **Chart hint:** one instruction, e.g. "Drag across the chart, or hold Shift with the arrow keys and press Enter, to filter the log to a span."
- **Empty log:** title states the fact and the description says what to do, e.g. "No events in this window" with "Widen the period or clear a filter to see more of the log."
- **Fields panel:** controls name the panel, e.g. "Hide the fields panel", "Show the fields panel".
- **Document:** drawer title "Event"; close button "Close the event document".
- **Query bar:** `aria-label` "Query events"; placeholder with one real example; the range "Events time range".
- **Saved queries:** "Name the current query", Save, "Delete <name>"; empty "No saved queries yet. Name the current query to keep it."
- **Tabs:** "New investigation", "Actions for <name>", Rename, Duplicate, "Close investigation"; limit "Up to 5 investigations stay open. Close one to start another."
- **Document tools:** "Search in this event", "Filter by <field> <value>", "Exclude <field> <value>", "Copy the fields shown as JSON"; no match "No field matches “<text>”."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The explorer sits in the layout's one `main` landmark; each `Sidebar` is named (Fields, Event document) with its own collapse, expand and resize labels.
- The chart is `Chart`'s one tab stop with an `aria-label` that carries the summary (busiest bucket) and the instruction; arrow keys move between buckets, Shift extends a span, Enter commits it, and the tooltip follows keyboard focus as it follows the pointer.
- The Errors value carries an `aria-label` with its share of all events.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; the filter `Badge` and decorative glyphs are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Value options in the popovers expose `aria-checked`, so applied values are announced.
- The document drawer traps focus while open and closes on Escape; motion is turned off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Query: the bar is a `combobox` whose invalid state sets `aria-invalid` and points `aria-describedby` at the reason; the mixed AND / OR message and the saved-query confirmations are `role="status"`.
- Sessions: the tabs follow the `Tabs` keyboard map (arrows, Home, End); F2 renames and Delete closes the focused tab, and the same actions sit in a named menu for pointer and screen-reader users; focus returns to the tab after rename or close.
- EventDocument: Filter by and Exclude are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) named with the field and value; the match count of the document search is announced in a `role="status"`.

## States

- Default: live traffic with the summary, the chart and the log filled, and no filters applied.
- Filtered: errors from the Security and Access Control sources; the Filter button counts three fields and each shows as a chip.
- Empty: a workspace with no traffic yet; the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows No events yet.
- Failed: the event request failed; the fields panel stays and the log pane shows a danger `Alert` that says the events did not load, with Retry, which reruns the request like Refresh.
- Query: `level = Error AND host = api.example.com` over the last 24 hours, with two saved and two recent queries.
- Sessions: three investigation tabs, API errors active.
- EventDocument: an error event's document open, with Host is not legacy.example.com applied.

## Related

- `platform/view/table-view` — the same controls row over a resource list.
- `platform/detail/deployment-logs` — logs of one deployment run.
- `platform/dashboard/data-dashboard` — the metrics view for the same traffic.
- `shells/console` — the layout this explorer renders in.
- `TableRoot` — the log table; see `skills/webkit-tables`, `skills/webkit-data-viz` and `skills/webkit-ui-states`.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Filtered` · `Empty` · `Failed` · `Query` · `Sessions` · `EventDocument`. Code: [blocks/platform/view/split-view.md](blocks/platform/view/split-view.md), `get_pattern("platform/view/split-view", { variant })`.

# TableView (`platform/view/table-view`)

> The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large contr…

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/table-view/table-view.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/table-view")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, CollectionPreferences, ConfirmDialog, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption`, EmptyState, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, PropertyFilter, Table, `TableRoot`, Tooltip, `use-collection`, `utils/csv`
- Skills: `webkit-lists`, `webkit-tables`, `webkit-ui-states`

## Asked as

list; list page; resource list; module list; index page; resources index; list with filters; workloads list; listagem; lista de recursos; página de listagem; resource table; data table; table; sortable table; paginated table; table with copy id; listing table; tabela de listagem; tabela; tabela de recursos; tabela paginada; list controls; filter bar; search and filter; table toolbar; filter chips; column visibility; filtros; barra de filtros; busca e filtro; users; users management; users list; team members; members list; invite user; invite teammate; manage users; remove user; usuários; gestão de usuários; lista de usuários; convidar usuário; membros; teams and permissions; teams; permissions; roles and permissions; access control; team list; create team; user groups; times e permissões; permissões; controle de acesso; equipes; credentials; api tokens; personal tokens; api keys; access tokens; token list; revoke token; credenciais; tokens de api; chaves de api; environments; environments list; production stage preview; deployment environments; deployment policies; create environment; ambientes; lista de ambientes; ambientes de deploy; activity history; audit log; activity log; audit trail; account activity; event history; user actions log; histórico de atividades; log de auditoria; registro de atividades; table view; index table; visualização em tabela; property filter; filter tokens; collection preferences; table preferences; saved preferences; filters in the url; shareable filters; use collection; filtro por propriedade; preferências da tabela; filtros na url

The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- The module the sidebar routes to lists resources of one type (applications, workloads, users, tokens, environments, activity history).
- Users compare many records by the same few attributes (status, domain, owner, last change) and need to sort, filter and page through them.
- The filtered list must survive a reload or a shared link, and each person's page size and columns must survive the next visit.
- The list must survive its last row being deleted: the page keeps its heading and controls and the table gives way to an empty state.

## When not to use

- Resources people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column: use `platform/view/card-view`.
- A list nested inside one resource (a tab of a details page): use the table inside `platform/detail/details-page` or `platform/detail/record-table`, with `Add <Module>` instead of `Create`.
- Files and folders of a storage resource: use `platform/view/file-browser`.
- Events or logs explored over time with a chart and a document pane: use `platform/view/split-view`.
- An account that has never created the resource: use `platform/states/first-use`, which teaches the module before any list exists.
- Choosing one existing resource inside a form: use `platform/create/resource-picker`.

## Building blocks

- A. Page heading — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Property filter — `PropertyFilter` (required)
- C. Listing actions — `Tooltip`, `IconButton` (optional)
- D. Table preferences — `CollectionPreferences` (required)
- E. Resource table — `Card`, `TableRoot` (required)
- F. Cell presets — `Table.CellLink`, `Table.CellId`, `Table.CellStatus`, `Table.CellTime` (optional)
- G. Row actions — `Table.CellActions`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuOption` (required)
- H. Delete confirmation — `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Input` (required)
- I. No matching resources — `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)
- J. Empty listing — `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/table-view.md](blocks/platform/view/table-view.md).

## Do

- Run the whole list on one `useCollection` call and bind its props with `v-bind`; let it own the filter, sort, page and preferences.
- Keep the controls row and the table in one band at the group gap; the heading sits one section step above.
- Set `url: true` so the tokens, the sort and the page live in the query string and a filtered list can be shared or reloaded.
- Give the list a `storageKey` of its own and lock the column that names the row.
- Keep `CollectionPreferences` the last control of the row and every control on it medium.
- Branch on `status`: `empty` swaps the table for the empty listing, `no-match` fills the table's `#empty` slot with Clear filters.
- Give every icon-only control a `Tooltip` and an `aria-label` with the same words.
- Put Delete last in the row menu, in its own group, and always behind the confirmation dialog.

## Don't

- Don't add a search `Input`, a filter popover, a chip row or a row of `Select`s beside the `PropertyFilter`; one control narrows the list.
- Don't filter, sort or page rows in a `computed` outside the collection, or pass `:data`, `paginated` and `v-model:globalFilter` by hand beside `tableProps`.
- Don't build a columns popover of `Switch`es; column visibility and order belong to `CollectionPreferences`.
- Don't wrap a bordered table in a padded card, or let the page scroll sideways for a wide table.
- Don't add a second create button to the controls row.
- Don't show the first-use empty state when filters hide every row, or Clear filters when the account has none.
- Don't replace the heading and controls with a full-page empty state when the rows run out; only the table area changes.

## Copy

- **Title:** the module name as the sidebar shows it, e.g. "Resources". Description: one sentence with a period, e.g. "View and manage your resources."
- **Create action:** `Create <Object>` with the entity's capitalization, e.g. "Create Resource"; never "New" or a bare noun. The empty state repeats the same label.
- **Filter:** placeholder and `aria-label` name what is filtered, e.g. "Filter resources".
- **Properties:** the column header's words, e.g. "Name", "Author", "Status", "Domain".
- **Icon buttons:** a verb or noun in sentence case, e.g. "Refresh", "Download CSV", "Row actions". Preferences title: "Table preferences".
- **Column headers:** one or two words without punctuation, e.g. "Name", "ID", "Domains", "Status", "Last Modified".
- **No match:** "No matching resources", then "No resource matches these filters.", and the action "Clear filters".
- **Empty:** title states the fact, e.g. "No resources yet"; description is one sentence with what to do, e.g. "Create a resource to start serving traffic on your domains."
- **Copy buttons:** name what they copy, e.g. "Copy resource ID", "Copy domain name".
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- The layout owns the one `main` landmark; the `PageHeader` title is the page's only `h1`.
- The `PropertyFilter` has an `aria-label` that matches its placeholder; each token's remove button names the token, and the match count is announced after each change.
- Every icon-only button has an `aria-label`; decorative icons carry `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Focus order follows reading order: heading actions, filter, Refresh, Download CSV, Preferences, table, pagination.
- The delete dialog traps focus, is named by its title and labels its input by the prompt.
- The preferences dialog traps focus, is named by its title and returns focus to its trigger when it closes.
- Sorting is announced by the table header; the row menu is reachable by keyboard and closes back to its trigger.
- Links that open a new tab add "(opens in a new tab)" in visually hidden text; the `+N` popover names its count and the copy buttons name what they copy.

## States

- Default: resources exist; the table shows them with the property filter, refresh, export, preferences, sorting and pagination wired, and filtering to nothing shows No matching resources with Clear filters.
- Empty: every resource was deleted on an account that is not new; `useCollection` reports `empty`, the heading and controls stay, and a flush card with Create Resource and Documentation replaces the table.

## Related

- `platform/view/card-view` — the same collection, rendered as selectable cards.
- `platform/create/single-page-create` — where the Create action leads for a short form.
- `platform/create/create-in-drawer` — create without leaving the list when the form is three fields or fewer.
- `platform/detail/details-page` — where a row name leads.
- `platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation` — the dialog behind the row menu's Delete.
- `platform/states/first-use` — the module before its first resource.
- `TableRoot` and `useCollection` — the table this page wraps and the state behind it; see `skills/webkit-tables` and `skills/webkit-lists`.

template browser; template gallery; template catalog; start from a template; browse templates; templates by framework; template preview; template readme; deploy a template; starter templates; galeria de templates; catálogo de templates; navegar templates; começar a partir de um template; pré-visualizar template

The catalog of templates a person starts a project from. ## When to use

## Do

- Show the framework on the tile as text in a `Tag`, not only as the mark.
- Open the preview in a drawer, so the catalog and the filter stay where they were.
- End the preview on Deploy, a link into `platform/create/deploy-template`, and let that flow run the deploy and raise the async-submit toast.
- Keep README headings below the drawer title (`h4` and down).

## Don't

- Don't deploy from the tile or the drawer without the deploy flow; the template needs a scope, a repository name and its settings.
- Don't put a Deploy button on every tile; the preview is where a person confirms the choice.

- Don't colour the tile per framework; the mark carries the brand and the surface stays neutral.
- Don't hide the filter while loading or after a failure; disable it, so the page keeps its shape.
- Don't show the README as raw markdown or in a code block.

- The focus ring is drawn inside the tile on the stretched target, so it is never clipped by the grid.
- The drawer traps focus, is named by `DrawerTitle`, closes on Escape and returns focus to the tile that opened it.
- The `PropertyFilter` is named by its `aria-label` and announces the match count after each change.
- The loading band is `aria-busy`; the failure `Alert` is announced and its Retry is a button.

- Failed: the catalog could not load; a danger `Alert` reads Couldn't load templates with Retry, and a medium empty state offers Import from Git so a project can still start.

# WafTuning (`platform/view/waf-tuning`)

> The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set: the requests it matched, grouped by rule, so the user can allow the legitimate ones.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning/waf-tuning.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("platform/view/waf-tuning")`
- Components: Alert, Button, Card, Dialog, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, EmptyState, Field, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, `TableRoot`, Tag, Textarea, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-tables`, `webkit-lists`, `webkit-form`, `webkit-errors`

## Asked as

waf tuning; web application firewall; allow rules; false positives; attacks table; matched requests; waf allowed rules; threshold; ajuste do waf; falsos positivos; permitir regras; ajuste de waf; falsos positivos waf

The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set. It shows the requests the rule set matched, grouped by the rule that matched them, with enough context (hits, top addresses, countries and paths) for the user to tell an attack from a false positive, and turns the legitimate ones into allowed rules with a recorded reason.

This block is a page body: render it in the default slot of `ConsoleLayout` (`shells/console`), which owns the rail, the header and the `main`.

## When to use

- A security rule set blocks or flags traffic, and users need to review what it caught and allow what is legitimate.
- Each finding is a rule that matched many requests, summarized by its sources and targets.
- Allowing changes what the rule set lets through, so it needs a reason that stays with the change.

## When not to use

- A plain list of records to browse and act on one at a time: use `platform/view/table-view`.
- Charts of attack volume over time: use `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard`.
- Editing the allowed rules once created: an `edit-resource` form on the Allowed Rules tab.

## Building blocks

- A. Header — `PageHeader`, `Button` (required)
- B. Threshold settings — `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` (required)
- C. Matches table — `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `EmptyState` (required)
- D. Allow dialog — `Dialog`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogContent`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogClose`, `DialogDescription`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Textarea`, `Button` (required)
- E. Outcome — `Alert` (required)

What each part takes: [blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md](blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md).

## Do

- Sort by hits so the noisiest rules come first, and keep the sort when settings change.
- Show sources and targets as samples with a count of the rest, not as full lists.
- Say how many allowed rules the action creates before the user confirms it.
- Require a reason, and validate it only after the user tries to allow.
- Keep the selection when settings change, so the user can narrow the list and still act on what they checked.

## Don't

- Don't allow from a single click on a row; allowing changes what the rule set blocks.
- Don't hide the threshold settings in a menu; they decide what the list shows.
- Don't put a free-text reason in a toast or a confirm without a field.
- Don't use real or customer addresses in examples; use documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24).

## Copy

- **Header action:** "Add Allowed Rule", then "Allow 2 selected".
- **Settings labels:** "Time range", "Minimum hits".
- **Empty after threshold:** "No rule reaches the minimum", "No rule matched 100 times or more in the last 24 hours. Lower the minimum hits or widen the time range."
- **First use:** "No matches yet", "This rule set has not matched any request. Matches appear here as traffic arrives."
- **Dialog:** title "Allow 2 rules", submit "Allow rules", reason error "Enter why these requests are legitimate."
- **Outcome:** "6 allowed rules created." and "The allowed rules weren't created. Nothing changed in the rule set; try again."
- Follow `skills/webkit-microcopy`: sentence case, no em dash, no "please", no exclamation marks.

## Accessibility

- Time range and Minimum hits have visible labels; the search and Refresh have accessible names.
- The selection checkboxes and sort buttons come from `TableRoot` and are named per row and column.
- The dialog is a labelled `form`: its title names it, the reason is a required `Field` whose error is tied by `aria-describedby`, and Enter in a text field does not submit by accident because the reason is a `Textarea`.
- The failure `Alert` is read when it appears; focus stays in the dialog and returns to the allow action on close.
- Code-font values (rule ids, addresses, paths) are plain text; nothing depends on color.

## States

- Default: five rules matched in the last 24 hours, minimum 100 hits.
- Allow: two rules checked and the dialog open.
- AllowFailed: the dialog with the failure `Alert` and Try again.
- Empty: no match yet, no settings.
- Loading: settings disabled, skeleton rows.

## Related

- `platform/view/rules-list` — the firewall's rules, where a WAF rule set is applied.
- `platform/view/table-view` — the list recipe this table follows.
- `platform/states/form-error` — the failure pattern in the dialog.
- `platform/dashboard/security-dashboard` — attack volume over time.

## Variants

`Default` (primary) · `Allow` · `AllowFailed` · `Empty` · `Loading`. Code: [blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md](blocks/platform/view/waf-tuning.md), `get_pattern("platform/view/waf-tuning", { variant })`.

# Console (`shells/console`)

> The console shell as one component: `ConsoleLayout`, composed once in the app around RouterView, so a console page is only its body.

- Surface: product
- Source: `blocks/shells/console/console.vue` in `@aziontech/webkit`
- MCP: `get_pattern("shells/console")`
- Components: Alert, Avatar, Badge, Button, ButtonHighlight, Card, Command, ConsoleLayout, ConsoleLayout, Dialog, `DialogClose`, `DialogContent`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogOverlay`, `DialogPortal`, `DialogTitle`, DropdownMenu, EmptyState, IconButton, Input, PageHeader, PageTabs, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `PanelHeader`, Select, StatusIndicator, Table, Tabs, Tag, ThemeSwitcher, Toast, Tooltip
- Skills: `webkit-navigation`, `webkit-layout`

## Asked as

platform shell; console shell; app shell; sidebar layout; navigation rail; dashboard layout; admin layout; app layout with sidebar; estrutura do console; layout com menu lateral; menu lateral; console; console layout; layout do console; notifications panel; notifications drawer; notification center; central de notificações; painel de notificações; switch account; account switcher; organization switcher; change organization; trocar conta; trocar organização; selecionar conta; console layout component; ConsoleLayout; app layout with router view; layout do console com RouterView

The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: the navigation rail (wordmark, grouped navigation with drill-in levels, the account at its foot), one global header (breadcrumbs, search, the app's actions, the avatar) and the ⌘K palette. All of that is one component, `ConsoleLayout`: this block is the app's `App.vue` — compose it once around `RouterView` and every console page is only the body rendered through its default slot. The body here is a stand-in for `platform/view/table-view`.

## When to use

- The root of a console app: every browse page (first-level lists, Home and dashboards, resource details with their tabs, settings) renders inside it.

## When not to use

- Create, edit and deploy flows: use the focused shell headed by `headers/creation-header`, with no rail.
- Signed-out screens: `platform/auth` with `headers/auth-header`.
- Documentation and marketing: `shells/documentation`, `shells/website`.
- A page needing the resizable split panel: compose `AppLayout` directly for that page.

## Building blocks

- A. Shell — `ConsoleLayout` (required)
- B. Actions — `Button` (required)
- C. Agent — `ButtonHighlight` (required)
- D. Hints — `Tooltip` (required)
- E. Icon actions — `IconButton` (required)
- F. Palette groups — `Command` (required)
- G. Account menu — `DropdownMenu` (required)
- H. Theme — `ThemeSwitcher` (required)
- I. System status — `StatusIndicator` (required)
- J. Page title — `PageHeader` (stand-in body)
- K. Search field — `Input` (stand-in body)
- L. Table frame — `Card` (stand-in body)

What each part takes: [blocks/shells/console.md](blocks/shells/console.md).

## Do

- Compose `ConsoleLayout` once in `App.vue` and render every browse page through its default slot; replace this block's stand-in body with `<RouterView />`.
- Keep the navigation in one data file shared by the app; the rail and the palette both read it.
- Give every row an `href` (never `to` or `path`); derive a static `breadcrumbs` trail from the route.
- Let a detail page set its own trail, control crumb included, with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`.
- Frame a list or form body with `layout-boundary` + `layout-column`; open a detail body flush on `PageTabs`.

## Don't

- Don't render `AppLayout`, `Sidebar`, `GlobalHeader`, `SearchTrigger`, a `Command` palette or a `<main>` in a page; the layout owns them.
- Don't put a page's control crumb in `App.vue`, or size a body with `calc(100dvh - …)`.
- Don't render the rail on create, edit or deploy pages.
- Don't add page actions to the global header; they belong to the page's header, controls row or tab row.
- Don't hide the avatar when the rail is collapsed or in the drawer.
- Don't open the notifications region as a popover over the page; it is the layout's tools region beside the content.

## Copy

- **Palette groups:** `Recents`, `Actions`; the layout's placeholder `Search pages and commands` and its empty line come from the locale catalog.
- **Navigation and menu items:** nouns as the module pages are titled (`Personal tokens`, `Activity history`, `Build and deployment`, `Account settings`); Azion product names keep theirs (`Edge DNS`, `Real-Time Metrics`). No ampersand.
- **Status:** a short state, not a sentence: `All systems normal`.
- **Header actions:** `Create`, `Agent`.
- **Module create:** `Create` plus the entity: `Create Application`.

## Accessibility

- One `main` (the layout's), one `banner` (the header), the rail as a labelled navigation (`Main navigation`); the page body starts with its `h1` (`PageHeader`).
- ⌘K / Ctrl K opens the palette, announced through `aria-keyshortcuts` on the search; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- The rail's drawer traps focus while open, closes on `Escape` and when a row is chosen, and returns focus to the menu button.
- Icon-only controls have both an `aria-label` and a tooltip.
- The bell is a toggle (`aria-pressed`) and names the unread count; unread items carry a visually hidden `Unread:` prefix, not colour alone.

## States

- ListPage: a first-level list page in the `ConsoleLayout` default slot: no breadcrumb on a first level, the page opens on its `PageHeader` (title, description, Documentation and the create action) and its controls row (Filter, search, Refresh, Download CSV, Columns) over the table.
- DetailPage: a resource detail page rendered through `ConsoleLayout`. The page body sets its own trail with `ConsoleLayout.Breadcrumbs`: Applications and the application as `items`, then the environment in its slot, a `Select` with `kind="transparent"` and `size="small"` labelled `Switch environment` (a search `Input`, each environment tagged with its deployment policy, a muted line when nothing matches, Add Environment at its foot). The default slot is flush and opens on a full-bleed `PageTabs` (Overview, Deployments, Settings, the outlined Deploy in `#actions`), sticky at the top of the layout's scrolling region so it stays in view while the tab content scrolls under it; no `main` of its own, the layout owns it.
- Notifications: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the bell after Create and Agent in the `actions` slot; it toggles the layout's tools region (`v-model:tools-open`, `tools-label="Notifications"`), a region beside the content and a drawer when narrow. The `tools` slot holds the list: unread items raised, Edit and Redeploy on each deploy, Mark all as read, Clear all, and the EmptyState `You are all caught up` once cleared. The failed deploy also shows as a flash Alert (Edit, Redeploy) in the `notifications` slot above the page. The bell's `aria-label` carries the unread count, `aria-pressed` follows the region, and the `Badge` on it is hidden from assistive technology.
- AccountSwitch: the ListPage through `ConsoleLayout` with the current account in the `header-start` slot, before the breadcrumbs (square `Avatar` with its initials, the name, a chevron), `Switch account (Ctrl+O)` on its tooltip and `aria-keyshortcuts`; while the slot's `compact` is true it shows the avatar and the chevron only (the name stays in its `aria-label`). It and the shortcut open a large `Dialog`, rendered beside the layout, with a search `Input` (name, ID or client ID) over a `Table` of the account tree: organizations, groups and workspaces indented by depth, expand and collapse buttons with `aria-expanded`, each name a button that switches, `Current` on the active one, type as `Table.CellStatus`, ID and client ID as `Table.CellId`. Switching closes the dialog and toasts `Switched to <name>.` with the IDs; the footer shows the current account and Account settings. A search with no match shows Clear search.

## Related

- `headers/resource-header` — this shell's header on its own.
- `headers/creation-header` — the focused shell for create, edit and deploy.
- `platform/view/table-view`, `platform/detail/details-page`, `platform/dashboard/home-dashboard` — the page bodies rendered in the slot.

docs shell; documentation layout; docs page layout; documentation site; docs sidebar; on this page outline; knowledge base layout; layout da documentação; página de documentação; estrutura da documentação; documentation shell; docs layout; documentation article; docs article page; tutorial page; getting started guide; how-to guide; product reference page; reference documentation; docs page with steps and code; documentation home; docs home page; docs landing page; developer portal home; artigo da documentação; página de tutorial; guia de primeiros passos; página de referência do produto; página inicial da documentação; home da documentação; docs home with copy prompt and AI agent logos; your AI agent fluent in Azion card; botão copiar prompt com logos de IA; docs layout component; DocLayout

## When not to use

## Building blocks

- Don't measure the viewport in script to place the footer brand; the `lg:` utilities and `signature="compact"` decide it in CSS.
- Don't reuse the console rail here; docs navigation is pages, not modules.

## Copy

- **Article headings:** verb-led tasks in sentence case: `Create the function`, `Verify the response`.
- **Navigation rows:** page titles exactly as the `h1` reads.
- **Step titles:** imperative, ending with a period when the step is a sentence: `Open Azion Console.`
- **Landing groups:** `Start by interface`, `Start by objective`, `Ready-made templates`, `Follow along`; card link labels are a verb and the object (`Install the CLI`).

## Accessibility

- One main landmark: the layout's. The article is an `<article>` inside it, never a second `<main>`.
- One `h1` per article (the masthead or the hero); `DocHeading` levels follow it in order (2, then 3 under a 2), and outline entries target those ids.
- Landmarks: the header is a banner, the rail and the outline are labelled navigation regions, the footer is contentinfo; `Tab` runs header → rail → article → outline → footer.
- Choosing an outline entry moves focus to its heading and clears the sticky header.

## States

- Default: the chrome around a short guide; rail from `lg` (drawer below), outline with the GitHub and Community groups and the `DocCta` from `xl`, the full footer under the article.
- Article: a tutorial page from the `Doc*` parts, pager in both directions, outline with an indented level 3 entry.
- Reference: a product reference page with a callout, the request-path diagram, a JSON rule and a term list; pager forward only.
- Landing: the documentation home; navigation rail, no outline rail, `DocHero` with `CopyPromptButton`, `DocAgentCard`, entry-point grids, pager forward to the first page.
