<!-- components/stat-tile-group.md -->

# Stat Tile Group

> One card split into cells, one `StatTile` per cell: the KPI strip at the top of an overview (data transferred, requests per second, bandwidth saving, data offload). The group draws the card (surface, border, radius) and the grid; each tile inside it drops its own card and draws its end and bottom edges as the dividers, with its delta aligned to the end of the figure row. The cells sit one per row in a narrow box, two per row from the group's `@md`, and all in one row from its `@3xl`.

- Import: `import StatTileGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile-group'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The usage or KPI row of an overview, where the figures read as one band.
- Two to six related figures for the same period.

## Do

- Put only `StatTile`s in the default slot, in reading order.
- Name the strip with `ariaLabel` when the page has more than one (`Usage`, `Traffic`).
- Give every tile in a strip the same `kind` and the same period.
- Prefer four cells: they fill one row on a desktop and two rows of two on a tablet.
- Next to a taller card in a row (a dashboard's usage band beside a chart), let the row stretch the group: it fills the height and the cells grow with it. Do not pin a height. Inside a wrapper element, give the group `h-full` (or make the wrapper a flex column) so the stretch reaches it.

## Don’t

- Figures that stand alone or carry their own sparkline history at different periods → separate `StatTile`s in a grid.
- Marketing figures on a site band → use `big-numbers`.
- Label/value details of one resource → use `key-value-pairs`.

## Related

- `stat-tile` — the cell; the group changes its chrome through an injected context, so the tiles take no extra prop.
- `card` — a plain surface; do not hand-build a strip by putting tiles in a `Card` grid.
- `key-value-pairs` — static label/value details.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the strip, such as Usage; empty leaves the group unnamed. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The StatTile cells, in reading order. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` only; loading and empty are each tile's own (`loading`, a null `value`).
- The group provides an injected context (`StatTileGroupInjectionKey`); a `StatTile` inside it sets `data-grouped`, drops its border, radius and surface, and draws `border-e` + `border-b` as dividers. The inner grid is pulled out by `-me-px -mb-px` and the root clips it (`overflow-hidden`), so the last column's end edge and the last row's bottom edge fall under the card border and every column count gets correct dividers with no `nth-child` rules.
- Not applicable: `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`/`closed`, `error`.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: a `role="group"` container named by `ariaLabel` when set; each cell stays a `StatTile` `<section>` named by its label, so the reading order is the slot order.
- Keyboard map: none of its own; focusable content inside the tiles (an info `Tooltip` in `aside`) keeps its own.
- Dividers are borders, not content; they carry no meaning.
- Contrast: the divider and card border use `--border-default`, the same as a separate tile.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`-me-px`, `border-e`), so the dividers sit between the cells under `dir="rtl"` too.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key    | English source | Override prop |
| ------ | -------------- | ------------- |
| _none_ | —              | —             |

- No built-in strings: the name comes from `ariaLabel`; the tiles carry their own.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the root is the `@container/stat-tile-group`; one cell per row below its `@md`, two per row from `@md`, every cell in one row (`grid-flow-col auto-cols-fr`) from `@3xl`.
- Height: the root is a flex column and the cell grid is `flex-1`, so when a grid or flex row stretches the group to a taller neighbour, the cell rows share the extra height instead of leaving an empty band under them.
- Touch: no targets of its own.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; the cells stack.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatTile from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile'
  import StatTileGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/stat-tile-group'
</script>

<template>
  <StatTileGroup aria-label="Usage">
    <StatTile
      label="Data transferred"
      :value="842"
      unit="GB"
      :delta="12.4"
    />
    <StatTile
      label="Requests / second"
      :value="1240"
      unit="/s"
      :delta="3.8"
    />
    <StatTile
      label="Bandwidth saving"
      :value="588"
      unit="GB"
      :delta="6.2"
    />
    <StatTile
      label="Data offload"
      :value="70"
      unit="%"
      :delta="-1.5"
      inverse
    />
  </StatTileGroup>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/stat-tile-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/stat-tile-group.md).

<!-- components/tracker.md -->

# Tracker

> A status strip: one block per period — a day, an hour, a deployment — colored by its severity, with a readout of the period's label on hover or keyboard focus. It shows the history of a state at a glance (uptime, health checks, build results), where a `chart` would plot a measure.

- Import: `import Tracker from '@aziontech/webkit/tracker'`
- Category: chart · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Uptime and availability history: ninety days of a service, a region or an origin.
- Pass/fail history: health checks, scheduled jobs, deployments.
- Any discrete sequence where each period has one state and the pattern of failures matters.

## Do

- Write each `label` as period plus state ("Nov 3 · Partial outage"), so the readout stands alone.
- Leave periods with no data without a severity; they render neutral rather than pretending to be healthy.
- Keep the period count fixed for a given view (90 days, 24 hours) so strips stacked in a list line up.
- Put the summary figure (99.98% uptime) beside the strip; the strip shows where, the figure shows how much.

## Don’t

- A measured value over time → use `chart` or `spark-chart`.
- The current state of one thing → use `status-indicator`.
- A ranking across categories → use `bar-list`.

## Related

- `status-indicator` — the current state; a Tracker is that state's history.
- `spark-chart` — a measured trend rather than a sequence of states.
- `chart-card` — the box a Tracker sits in, with the uptime figure in its header.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TrackerItem[]` | `[]` | false | One block per period, oldest first; each item is `{ id?: string; severity?: ChartStatus; label: string }`. No severity renders a neutral no-data block. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders a Skeleton strip in place of the blocks. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the strip. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `active block` (pointer or keyboard; the others dim), `loading` (Skeleton strip), `empty` (one neutral strip announced as No data)
- `data-loading` mirrors `loading`
- `data-severity` on each block: `success` | `warning` | `danger` | `info` | `none`
- `data-active` on the active block; `data-dimmed` on every other block while one is active
- `data-visible` on the readout while a block is active; `data-moving` while it follows from one block to the next

## Accessibility

- The strip is one tab stop: `role="group"` named by `ariaLabel`, with `aria-roledescription="status history"`.
- Keyboard map: Left / Right move the active block, Home / End jump to the ends, Escape clears.
- A polite live region reads the active block's `label`; the visual readout is `aria-hidden`.
- Severity never rests on color alone: the label names the state.
- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface)` on the strip (the offset takes the surface color, so it never shows as a white gap in the dark theme).
- Status colors clear 3:1 against the chart surfaces in both themes.
- Forced colors: the blocks keep their status colour (`forced-color-adjust: none`), because a background-painted block would be forced to `Canvas` and the whole tracker would vanish (`src/test/forced-colors-charts.test.ts`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move the active bar later/earlier, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`); the oldest bar sits at the start edge.
- Pointer: the hovered bar is measured from the start edge (`rect.right - clientX` under `rtl`), and the readout is anchored with a physical `left: 0` plus the mirrored bar center.
- User data: dates in the readout are printed by `Intl` in the active locale.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tracker from '@aziontech/webkit/tracker'

  const DAYS = 90
  const DEGRADED_DAY = 52
  const OUTAGE_DAY = 73

  const days = Array.from({ length: DAYS }, (_, index) => {
    const date = new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10 - (DAYS - 1 - index)))
    const id = date.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
    const day = date.toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
      month: 'short',
      day: 'numeric',
      timeZone: 'UTC'
    })
    if (index === DAYS - 1) return { id, label: `${day} · No data` }
    if (index === OUTAGE_DAY) return { id, severity: 'danger', label: `${day} · Partial outage` }
    if (index === DEGRADED_DAY)
      return { id, severity: 'warning', label: `${day} · Degraded performance` }
    return { id, severity: 'success', label: `${day} · Operational` }
  })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-xl) pt-(--spacing-xl)">
    <Tracker
      aria-label="Edge Application uptime, last 90 days"
      :items="days"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/tracker.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/tracker.md).

<!-- components/code-block.md -->

# Code Block

> Read-only code viewer for docs, API examples, and configuration previews. Supports four Figma-documented layouts that share one monolithic shell: 1. **Language switcher** ([4567:33761](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-33761)) — tabbed snippets with a sliding pill, optional filename bar, syntax highlighting, and copy. 2. **Show filename** ([4567:30198](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-30198)) — single snippet with a raised filename bar (language icon + name), no tabs. 3. **Diff** ([4567:29012](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-29012)) — per-line added/removed markers (`+`/`-`), semantic row backgrounds, and a 2 px leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. 4. **Highlighted line** ([4567:31473](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=4567-31473)) — one active line with info background and leading bar; no tabs or filename bar. Two more regions serve docs: a **label header** — a 40 px bar naming the block (`</>` + "Shell", "JavaScript", from the active tab's label or the language's readable name, or `title`) when `showLabel` is on and there is no tab strip or filename bar — and the **output** kind (`kind="output"`): what a command prints, drawn flat in `--text-muted` on `--bg-canvas` under an "Output" label, with no copy control by default. A command block and its output are always two blocks. The other regions render conditionally from tab data. Tab header appears when `tabs.length > 1`. Filename bar appears when the active tab sets `fileName`. Diff and highlight decorations come from `lineChanges` and `highlightedLine` on the active tab. **Syntax highlighting** is driven by the active tab's `language` and resolves to one of these tokenisers, all of which emit the same seven token types (`keyword`, `string`, `function`, `type`, `punctuation`, `identifier`, `comment`) so every language shares the one `--code-sintax-*` palette:

- Import: `import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Read-only code in docs, API examples or configuration previews that readers copy from.
- The same snippet in several languages, switched by tabs (one `tabs` entry per language).
- Showing a change as a diff (`lineChanges`) or pointing at one line (`highlightedLine`) on the active tab.

## Do

- Put the source on each tab's `code`. There is no top-level `code` prop, and a tab without a `value` or a `code` is dropped.
- Set `language` on every tab. Only JavaScript/TypeScript, shell, HCL, GraphQL and Markdown are tokenised; anything else renders as flat text.
- Use `default-value` for the initial tab, and `v-model` only when something outside the block must follow the selected tab.
- Set `:copyable="false"` on decorative blocks, and `:bordered="false"` when the block sits inside a surface that already frames it.
- Keep `animate-lines` for marketing layouts; leave it off in docs and console screens.
- Do: keep a command block to what the reader runs — the copy control copies exactly that. Put what it prints in a second block with `kind="output"` (or in prose).
- Don't: write expected output into the command, as a `# HTTP/2 200` comment or as unprompted lines after a `$ ` prompt — the reader pastes it into the terminal. The `webkit/no-output-in-command` lint warns on it.
- Do: turn `show-label` on in docs (`DocCodeGroup` does by default) so every block is titled with its language; set `title` only when the language name is not the right title.

## Don’t

- The content is build or deploy output with timestamps and log levels → use `log-view`.
- It is a marketing band that pairs a claim with its code → use `code-split`, or `sticky-scroll-code` for several claims.
- It is a terminal session of CLI commands on a product page → use `cli-terminal`.
- You only need to copy one short value (a token, an ID) without showing a block → use `copy-button`.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the copy control CodeBlock embeds; use it alone for one-line values.
- `log-view` — terminal-style viewer for CI and deploy logs.
- `code-split` — page section built around one code sample.
- `scroll-area` — the scroll container the code region runs in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `CodeBlockTab[]` | `[]` | false | Tab definitions with label, value, code, and optional language, filename, diff, or highlight metadata. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initial active tab when uncontrolled. |
| `showLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows a fixed-width gutter with zero-padded line numbers before each code line. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the copy control (forwarded to CopyButton's aria-label). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy code`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Shows the copy control. Unset, a `code` block shows it and an `output` block does not; turn it off for a decorative block nobody copies from. |
| `kind` | `'code' \| 'output'` | `'code'` | false | What the block holds: `code` the reader runs or reads, or `output` — what a command prints — drawn flat and muted under an "Output" label, without a copy control. |
| `showLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a header naming the block when there is no tab strip or file name: the active tab's label, else the language's readable name (Shell, JavaScript). Docs blocks show it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the label header; empty uses the tab label or the language name, or "Output" for an `output` block. |
| `animateLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Staggered line entrance for website layouts: each line slides from `-8px` with opacity `0 → 1`, `40ms` apart. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border around the block. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the block flush when it sits inside a surface that already frames it. Internal dividers (tab header, filename bar) are unaffected. |
| `modelValue` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Fires after the active tab code is copied to the clipboard. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tab-icon` | { tab: CodeBlockTab } | Leading mark before a tab's label in the tab strip; nothing renders when it is not filled. |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                  | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Active tab `value` via `defineModel`. While unbound (`undefined`) the block is uncontrolled: it starts at `defaultValue`, else the first tab. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible` on tabs and copy control
- `data-state` on tabs: `active` | `inactive`
- `data-state` on code lines: `default` | `added` | `removed` | `highlighted`
- `data-disabled` not used (tabs are not disabled in v2)
- `data-kind` on the root: `code` | `output`; `output` paints the shell `--bg-canvas` and every line flat in `--text-muted`

#### Layout rules (derived from Figma)

| Region                                                                     | Visible when                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab header (`CodeBlockHeader`, 40 px strip: a 32 px tab over a 4 px inset) | `tabs.length > 1`                                                        |
| Filename bar (`FileName`, 40 px)                                           | active tab has `fileName`                                                |
| Label header (40 px, `pi pi-code` / `pi pi-align-left` + label)            | no tab strip, no `fileName`, and `showLabel`, `title` or `kind="output"` |
| Diff gutter (`+`/`-` + 8 px spacer on unchanged lines)                     | active tab `lineChanges.length > 0`                                      |
| Line highlight (info background + 2 px leading bar)                        | active tab `highlightedLine` is set                                      |

When only one tab is provided and it has no `fileName`, the shell is code content + copy only (minimal block).

Code content scrolls inside `@aziontech/webkit/scroll-area` (`orientation="both"`, capped at a `320 px` max height so shorter snippets fit their content and taller ones scroll). Lines never wrap (`whitespace-pre`); on narrow viewports the scroll region grows horizontally so long lines stay on one row.

**The shell is fluid: it takes the width its container gives it and never grows past it.** Long lines are a scroll, never a wider block — so the root is a size container (`@container`, i.e. inline-size containment) and its code width is invisible to the layout above it. Without that, the block's intrinsic width leaks upward: an `auto`-sized grid track or flex row (a one-column `grid` on mobile, a `md:grid-cols-2` panel below its breakpoint) sizes itself to the widest code line and the block overflows the viewport instead of scrolling — a consumer's `min-w-0` on the wrapper cannot fix it, because `min-width` is a floor on the intrinsic contribution, not a cap. The copy control (a `CopyButton`, `kind="outlined"` `size="small"`) is absolutely positioned on the non-scrolling content shell (`__content`) so it stays pinned top-right while lines scroll. **On a single-line block it centres on that row instead** (`data-single-line` on the anchor): the shell is 44 px, the control 28 px, so the `--spacing-sm` top inset would leave it 4 px below the line's own centre. Every line reserves the control's full footprint on its right (`pr-11` = 28 px control + its 12 px inset), so a long line always scrolls clear of it rather than under it. With `copyable` off (`data-copyable` absent on the root) the control is not rendered and lines reserve only `--spacing-sm` on their right.

- Long files: above 300 lines the panel mounts lines in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep an estimated 24 px per line), so a 5,000-line file mounts and switches tabs within its runtime budget. Copy always copies the whole file.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses tabs and copy; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`Home`/`End` move between tabs; `Enter`/`Space` activates tab; copy uses `Enter`/`Space` on the CopyButton (native `<button>`); when focus is in the code scroll region, `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`PageUp`/`PageDown`/`Home`/`End` scroll vertically and `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` scroll horizontally via ScrollArea.
- ARIA: tab list uses `role="tablist"` when visible; tabs use `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`; panel uses `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby`; copy uses CopyButton `ariaLabel` (forwarded to its inner IconButton); diff `+`/`-` markers are `aria-hidden="true"` (change semantics conveyed by row `data-state` and visible background).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for code text on surface, including syntax token colors and diff/highlight row backgrounds in light and dark. Row backgrounds for `added`, `removed` and `highlighted` are the feedback fills at 40% (`bg-(--success)/40`, `bg-(--danger)/40`, `bg-(--info)/40`): at full strength the light fills (`--danger` `#F3A5A5`, `--info` `#99C9FF`) put the line numbers and the `function` and `type` syntax colours under 4.5:1 (3.93:1 for a line number on a removed row); at 40% every syntax colour clears 4.5:1 in light and dark (the lowest, the light `function` orange `#B03C02` on a removed row, is 4.6:1).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on indicator and panel motion.
- When `animateLines` is enabled, line motion is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion` (lines render fully visible immediately).
- Copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move between the file tabs, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`); the tab indicator is anchored with a physical `left: 0` and moved by `offsetLeft`.
- Motion: the panel slide between tabs mirrors (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x` presets).
- User data: code lines render `dir="ltr"`: code always reads left to right. The scroll area keeps the copy button's width free on its side (`pe-10` when `copyable`), so under `dir="rtl"` the button never covers the start of a line.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeBlock from '@aziontech/webkit/code-block'

  const tabs = [
    {
      label: 'Javascript',
      value: 'js',
      language: 'javascript',
      fileName: 'file name.js',
      code: "export default {\n  async fetch(request) {\n    const { prompt } = await request.json()\n\n    const modelResponse = await Azion.AI.run(\n      'Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8',\n      {\n        messages: [\n          { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },\n          { role: 'user', content: prompt }\n        ]\n      }\n    )\n\n    return new Response(JSON.stringify(modelResponse))\n  }\n}"
    },
    {
      label: 'Typescript',
      value: 'ts',
      language: 'typescript',
      fileName: 'file name.ts',
      code: "export default {\n  async fetch(request: Request) {\n    const { prompt } = await request.json()\n\n    const modelResponse = await Azion.AI.run(\n      'Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8',\n      {\n        messages: [\n          { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },\n          { role: 'user', content: prompt }\n        ]\n      }\n    )\n\n    return new Response(JSON.stringify(modelResponse))\n  }\n}"
```

<!-- components/code-editor.md -->

# Code Editor

> An editable code surface with line numbers, diagnostics and a read-only and a diff mode. It is a plain-text editor first: a monospace textarea with a line-number gutter that works on the server, without JavaScript and on any device. When the app passes a `loader` (a function that wires Monaco's workers and returns `import('monaco-editor')`), Monaco is loaded lazily, painted with the design tokens and takes over the same value, markers and options; until it loads, or if it fails, the plain editor stays in place. It differs from `code-block`, which only shows code.

- Import: `import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Editing a function, a script, a SQL query, a JSON or YAML document inside the product.
- Showing the change between two versions of code side by side (diff mode), for example before a deploy or a revert.
- Code that the server validates: the diagnostics come back as `markers` and show on their lines and in a list.
- A read-only view of code that still needs the editor's navigation (find, folding) once Monaco is loaded.

## Do

- Wrap it in a `Field` with a visible label, or give it an `ariaLabel`; the label names the textarea and the Monaco editor.
- Pass `loader` from the app so Monaco is code-split and never part of the WebKit bundle. The loader sets `MonacoEnvironment.getWorker` before it returns `import('monaco-editor')`; without workers Monaco has no language services. With `monaco-editor` 0.56 and later under Vite the worker imports are `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker?worker` and `monaco-editor/languages/features/<json|css|html|typescript>/<name>.worker?worker` (`ts.worker` serves `javascript` too); the old `monaco-editor/esm/vs/...?worker` paths fail the build. Copy `loadMonaco` from the Usage block or the `Monaco` example.
- Set `padLineNumbers` on a full-page code editor (`fill`, a function's Code or Arguments document), as the console does (01, 02…); leave it off on a small editor inside a form.
- Function calls are coloured for you (JavaScript and TypeScript, with `--code-sintax-function`); do not register your own Monarch grammar for that.
- Send server diagnostics as `markers` with 1-based lines; keep each message one sentence.
- Give the editor a fixed `height`, or `fill` inside a flex column that has its own height; never let it grow with the content.
- Use `readonly` for code the user may read and select but not change; use `disabled` only when the whole form is locked.
- In diff mode, `original` is the left side and `v-model` the right side; keep the right side editable only when the change can still be edited.

## Don’t

- Showing a snippet to copy, with tabs and a file name → use `code-block`.
- A one-line value such as a header, a regex or a path → use `input` inside a `field`.
- Free prose or a description → use `textarea`.
- A stream of log lines → use `log-view`.
- A form generated from a JSON schema → use `schema-form` (the arguments tab of a function pairs both).

## Related

- `code-block` — read-only snippets with copy; same syntax colour tokens.
- `textarea` — plain multi-line text; the fallback editor is built in its spirit but keeps code typography and a gutter.
- `field` — wraps the editor with a label, a description and an error; the editor reads id, `aria-describedby`, invalid and disabled from it.
- `toggle-group` — the document switch (Code / Arguments) placed in the `toolbar` slot.
- `log-view` — output of a run next to the editor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `string` | `'plaintext'` | false | Monaco language id (`javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `sql`, `lua`, `yaml`…). The fallback ignores it. |
| `loader` | `() => Promise<CodeEditorMonaco>` | `undefined` | false | Loads Monaco lazily; without it the plain editor is the editor. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The code can be read, selected and copied but not changed. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Locks the editor; it leaves the tab order. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the danger border; also set by a surrounding `Field`. |
| `diff` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows `original` beside the value as a side-by-side diff. |
| `original` | `string` | `''` | false | The left side of the diff. |
| `markers` | `CodeEditorMarker[]` | `[]` | false | Diagnostics shown on their lines and in the problems list. |
| `height` | `string` | `'16rem'` | false | CSS height of the editing area. |
| `fill` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Fills a flex column instead of using `height`. |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the line-number gutter. |
| `padLineNumbers` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Zero-pads line numbers to two digits (01, 02…), as the console's full-page function and arguments editors do. |
| `path` | `string` | `''` | false | Model path for Monaco language services (`index.ts`, `args.json`). |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no `Field` label names it. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | `unknown` | Monaco mounted; the payload is the editor instance (for actions). |
| `load-error` | `unknown` | The loader rejected; the plain editor stays. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolbar` | — | A bar above the editing area: a document switch, the file name, a Format or Run action. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — monolithic. The gutter, the fallback textarea, the Monaco host, the toolbar bar and the problems list are fixed parts.

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                    |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''`    | `update:modelValue` | The code via `defineModel`. Updated on every edit, from the plain editor or from Monaco. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible` (ring on the frame), `invalid`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `loading` (Monaco on the way, the plain editor is live)
- `data-mode`: `plain` | `loading` | `monaco` — which editor is live
- `data-invalid`, `data-readonly`, `data-disabled`, `data-diff`, `data-fill` mirror their props
- Each gutter line with a marker carries `data-severity` (`error` | `warning` | `info`)
- Load failure: the plain editor stays and a muted note says the full editor could not load

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the frame shows `focus-within:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color)` for both editors.
- Keyboard map (plain editor): typing edits; `Tab` inserts two spaces and `Shift+Tab` removes them at the line start; `Escape` releases the trap so the next `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` leaves the editor (WCAG 2.1.2); the problems list buttons move the caret to the marker's line. Monaco runs in tab-focus mode by default, so `Tab` moves focus out unless the user toggles it with `Ctrl+M`.
- ARIA: the textarea is a native multi-line text box named by the `Field` label or `ariaLabel`; `aria-invalid`, `aria-readonly` and `aria-describedby` (the field's description plus the problems summary); the gutter is `aria-hidden`; the problems list is a named list; the problem count is a polite `status`.
- Diagnostics are never colour only: each one is a list item with its line and severity in text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: code and line numbers use the code syntax tokens tuned for both themes.
- Forced colors: the frame keeps a system border and the gutter marker becomes a system glyph colour.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the gutter sits at the start edge.
- Code: the textarea and Monaco host are `dir="ltr"` (code reads left to right in every locale); the toolbar and problems list follow the page direction.
- Keyboard: no direction-dependent keys.
- User data: problem messages sit in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                     | English source                                             | Override prop |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `codeEditor.label`                      | Code editor                                                | `ariaLabel`   |
| `codeEditor.original`                   | Original                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.modified`                   | Modified                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.problems`                   | Problems                                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.problemCount`               | No problems / {count} problem / {count} problems (plural)  | —             |
| `codeEditor.line`                       | Line {line}                                                | —             |
| `codeEditor.error` / `warning` / `info` | Error / Warning / Info                                     | —             |
| `codeEditor.loading`                    | Loading the full editor…                                   | —             |
| `codeEditor.loadFailed`                 | The full editor could not load. You can keep editing here. | —             |
| `codeEditor.tabHint`                    | Press Escape, then Tab, to leave the editor.               | —             |

- Formatting: the problem count goes through the plural rules of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/code-editor` on the root; in diff mode the two panes sit side by side from `@lg` and stack below.
- Narrow: the editing area keeps its height and scrolls in both axes; long lines never wrap in code.
- Touch: problem buttons are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Reflow: the page never scrolls horizontally; the editor scrolls inside its frame.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/code-editor'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const code = ref(`export default async function handler(request) {
  const url = new URL(request.url)
  const name = url.searchParams.get('name')
  return new Response(\`Hello, \${name}\`)
}
`)

  const markers = [
    { line: 3, severity: 'warning', message: 'name can be null; give it a default value.' },
    { line: 4, severity: 'info', message: 'Set a Content-Type header on the response.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field>
    <Field.Label>Function code</Field.Label>
    <CodeEditor
      v-model="code"
      language="javascript"
      :markers="markers"
      height="14rem"
    />
    <Field.Description>Runs on every request that reaches this function.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

<!-- components/log-view.md -->

# Log View

> Composition-based terminal log viewer for CI/deploy output. **LogView** is the root shell and context provider; **LogViewHeader**, **LogViewContent**, and **LogViewFooter** are composed as children so teams can reorder, omit, or replace the toolbar and footer without forking the log renderer.

- Import: `import LogView from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Showing build, deploy or CI output as timestamped lines the reader can search, filter to warnings, and copy.
- A log shell whose toolbar and footer vary by screen — compose `LogViewHeader`, `LogViewContent` and `LogViewFooter` in the order you need, or drop the ones you don't.
- A log that is still loading from the server — set `loading` to show a spinner and `loading-label` in place of the body.

## Do

- Give every line a stable `id` and a `type` (`text`, `folder`, `framework-version`, `success`, `warning`); the type drives the line's rendering and the warnings filter.
- Bind `v-model:search` and `v-model:warnings-only` when the app needs the filter state; otherwise leave them unbound and the header manages them.
- Set `:bordered="false"` when the log sits inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer).
- The copy control hides while `disabled` or `loading`, or when there is nothing to copy; listen to `@copy` for the copied text instead of reading the clipboard.
- Use the header's `left` / `right` / `search` slots and the footer's default slot to add actions, rather than rebuilding the toolbar.

## Don’t

- Static, read-only code or configuration snippets → use `code-block`.
- An animated terminal session on a marketing page → use `cli-terminal`.
- Rows of structured records with columns, sorting or paging → use `table`.

## Related

- `code-block` — highlighted source code with a copy action, not a stream of typed log lines.
- `cli-terminal` — marketing band that plays a scripted terminal session.
- deploy-success` — the post-deploy screen that embeds `log-view` for the build log.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `LogViewLine[]` | `[]` | false | Log entries; filtered in LogViewContent by search and warnings-only. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the outer card border and corner radius around the log shell. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the shell flush inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer). Internal dividers (header/footer edges) are unaffected. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder for the default header search field. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Find in logs`). |
| `copyable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the copy-to-clipboard control (a CopyButton pinned top-right over the log content in LogViewContent). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables toolbar controls in LogViewHeader. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces the LogViewContent log body with a centered spinner and label. |
| `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label shown beneath the spinner while `loading`. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Loading…`). |
| `search` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:search`). |
| `warningsOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:warningsOnly`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Fires after a successful copy; payload is the copied plain text. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Sub-components (LogViewHeader, LogViewContent, LogViewFooter) composed in the desired order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-header`

## Sub-components

LogView ships flat, individually importable sub-components (each from its own `@aziontech/webkit/log-view-*` entry); every sub-component reads the root's shared state through the injected context, so the consumer wires nothing.

- `log-view-header.vue` — Default 48px toolbar: line count, warning filter, and a search field.
- `log-view-content.vue` — Scrollable log body with per-`type` line rendering, search highlighting, `ScrollArea`'s `fade` on the log body (the edges that still have lines beyond them fade out), and the copy-to-clipboard…
- `log-view-footer.vue` — Optional footer region for actions (download, follow live, pagination).

## v-model

| Model                   | Type      | Default | Emits                 | Notes                                                                |
| ----------------------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:search`        | `string`  | `''`    | `update:search`       | Two-way search query; filters LogViewContent and highlights matches. |
| `v-model:warnings-only` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:warningsOnly` | When true, shows only lines whose `type` is `warning`.               |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (per log line), `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` / `data-warnings-only` / `data-loading` / `data-border` on the LogView root
- `loading` state: LogViewContent renders a centered spinner + `loadingLabel` in place of the log body
- Log line `data-type` reflects `line.type`
- Long logs: above 300 visible lines `LogViewContent` mounts lines in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep an estimated 24 px per line), so a 10,000-line log mounts within its runtime budget. Search, warnings-only, the line count and copy work on every line, mounted or not.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus on the interactive controls in the header/footer.
- LogViewContent carries a visually hidden `role="log"` region (`aria-live="polite"`) that holds only the lines appended to `lines` since the last update (filtered by the current search and warnings-only view). The scrolling log body is not a live region, so the lines already present at mount and the chunks that mount on scroll are never announced; replacing `lines` with a different log clears the region.
- The warning filter exposes `aria-pressed`; the copy control (a CopyButton in LogViewContent) uses `aria-label="Copy logs"` at rest, switching to `"Copied logs"` after a successful copy.
- The loading state uses `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`; the spinner is `aria-hidden` (from the Spinner component) and the `loadingLabel` text conveys status.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every motion-bearing class.
- Touch target: the warning control is ≥40×40 px; the copy control uses CopyButton `size="small"` (28×28 px) to match CodeBlock — a justified deviation for the compact overlay.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: timestamps render `dir="ltr"`; each message renders `dir="auto"`, so a log line in another script keeps its own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import LogView from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view'
  import LogViewContent from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view-content'
  import LogViewHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/log-view-header'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const lines = [
    { id: '1', time: '13:47:33', type: 'text', message: 'Deploy started successfully!' },
    { id: '2', time: '13:47:41', type: 'success', message: 'Build finished' },
    {
      id: '3',
      time: '13:47:42',
      type: 'folder',
      message: 'dist/index.js',
      folderType: 'asset',
      size: '12.4 kB',
      gzipSize: '4.1 kB'
    },
    { id: '4', time: '13:47:43', type: 'warning', message: 'Bundle larger than recommended' }
  ]
  const search = ref('')
  const warningsOnly = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-[640px]">
    <LogView
      :lines="lines"
      v-model:search="search"
      v-model:warnings-only="warningsOnly"
      class="h-full"
    >
      <LogViewHeader />
      <LogViewContent />
    </LogView>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/trace.md -->

# Trace

> A span waterfall: one row per span of a run (a function invocation, a request through several services), indented under the span it ran inside and drawn as a bar placed against the run's own clock. The rows form a tree grid that expands and collapses, a search narrows them to the spans whose name or service matches, and selecting a row opens its details (service, start, duration, share of the run, outcome message and attributes) under the waterfall. It reads a flat `spans` list with `parentId` links and never fetches anything.

- Import: `import Trace from '@aziontech/webkit/trace'`
- Category: code · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The test run of a function or the detail of one invocation, to show where the time went.
- A request that crossed several services, each with its own span, where the order and the overlap matter.
- Next to the run's logs (`log-view`), on the same clock.

## Do

- Pass `start` and `duration` in milliseconds from the start of the run; the axis spans the latest end.
- Link children with `parentId`; a span whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a partial trace still renders.
- Set `status: 'error'` and a one-line `message` on the span that failed, and on its parents if the failure bubbled up.
- Bind `v-model:selected` when another view (a request path, a log line) selects the same span.
- Name the waterfall after the run (`aria-label="Trace of inv_7f21"`).

## Don’t

- A list of log lines with levels → use `log-view`.
- Durations to compare across many items with no parent/child relation → use `bar-list` or `chart`.
- Status history of a service over days → use `tracker`.
- A hierarchy without time → use `tree`.

## Related

- `log-view` — the run's log lines, shown under the trace on the same clock.
- `tree` — the same expand and collapse model without the time axis.
- `bar-list` — ranked durations without nesting.
- `key-value-pairs` — the facts of the run above the trace.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spans` | `TraceSpan[]` | `[]` | false | Spans of the trace, each `{ id, parentId?, name, service?, icon?, start, duration, status?, message?, attributes? }` in milliseconds. |
| `selected` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the span whose details show under the waterfall. Supports v-model:selected. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the waterfall. Empty uses the locale catalog. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:selected` | `string` | A row was selected, selected again (empty: deselected), or Close used. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row), `focus-visible` (row), `selected` (row and details band), `collapsed` / `expanded` (parent rows), `searching` (rows narrowed, every match's ancestors shown), `empty` (no spans, or no match with Clear search).
- Bar tones on `data-tone`: `root` (info), `ok` (success), `error` (danger), `running` (warning).
- `data-selected` on the selected row; `aria-expanded` on parent rows.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px inset ring on the focused row.
- Keyboard map: one row is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move between visible rows; `Home`/`End` go to the first and last row; `ArrowRight` expands a collapsed parent, or moves into its first child; `ArrowLeft` collapses an expanded parent, or moves to the parent; `Enter` or `Space` selects the row (again: deselects). Close in the details returns focus to the row.
- ARIA: the waterfall is a named `treegrid` of `row`s with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (parents only) and `aria-selected`; each row is named with its span, service, start, duration and outcome; the details band is a named `region` that describes the grid. The axis, the bars' duration labels and the expand glyph are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Rows are 36 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Colour is never the only signal: a failed span also carries an icon in the row and a Failed tag in the details.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens; duration labels use the `-contrast` tokens of their tone.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; bars sit at `inset-inline-start` with an inline size, so the waterfall runs from the inline start and mirrors; indentation is `padding-inline-start`.
- Icons: the collapsed chevron is mirrored (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); span icons are not.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight` and `ArrowLeft` swap under `dir="rtl"` (expand is the inline-end arrow).
- User data: span names, services and attribute values sit in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                                                  | English source                                   | Override prop |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `trace.label`                                        | Trace                                            | `ariaLabel`   |
| `trace.search`                                       | Search spans                                     | —             |
| `trace.noMatch`                                      | No span matches “{query}”.                       | —             |
| `trace.clearSearch`                                  | Clear search                                     | —             |
| `trace.empty`                                        | No spans in this trace.                          | —             |
| `trace.details`                                      | Details of {name}                                | —             |
| `trace.close`                                        | Close                                            | —             |
| `trace.copyName`                                     | Copy span name                                   | —             |
| `trace.service` / `startedAt` / `duration` / `share` | Service / Started at / Duration / Share of trace | —             |
| `trace.percent`                                      | {value}%                                         | —             |
| `trace.failed` / `running`                           | Failed / Running                                 | —             |
| `trace.attributes`                                   | Attributes                                       | —             |
| `trace.milliseconds` / `seconds`                     | {value} ms / {value} s                           | —             |

- Formatting: durations under one second print whole milliseconds, longer ones seconds with two decimals, both through `Intl.NumberFormat` of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/trace`; the name column grows from 9 rem to 20 rem with the container, the service column and the grid lines appear from `@xl`/`@3xl`.
- Narrow: names truncate, the duration labels stay on the bars, the details facts take two columns.
- Touch: rows are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import { ref } from 'vue'

    { id: 'root', name: 'image-resizer', service: 'Function', start: 0, duration: 412 },

      id: 'parse',
```

<!-- components/accordion.md -->

# Accordion

> A vertically stacked set of disclosure items: each item has a clickable header that expands or collapses its content panel. Use it to condense long content into scannable sections. Unlike `tabs` (mutually-exclusive panels shown in place), an accordion can keep one item open at a time (`type="single"`) or several at once (`type="multiple"`), and its content expands inline below each header.

- Import: `import AccordionRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Long content splits into independent sections the reader scans by heading and opens on demand (settings groups, help topics, a details list).
- The reader may want one section open at a time (`type="single"`) or to compare several side by side (`type="multiple"`).
- Content should expand inline below its heading, pushing the rest of the page down.

## Do

- Give every `Accordion.Item` a unique `value`; the open state is keyed by it, and `default-value` / `v-model` refer to it.
- Bind `v-model` to a string in `type="single"` and to an array in `type="multiple"`; set `collapsible` to `false` only when one item must always stay open.
- Set the trigger's `level` to fit the page outline (default `3`) — each trigger is wrapped in a real heading.
- Accordion.Content` applies no padding; pad the content you put inside it.
- Set `size` and `arrow-position` on the root, not per item — they are provided to every item through context.

## Don’t

- The panels are mutually exclusive views shown in the same place → use `tabs`.
- It is the frequently-asked-questions band of a marketing page → use `faq-section` (or `faq` for the band without the page-section wiring).
- It is hierarchical navigation with expandable rows → use `menu`.

## Related

- `tabs` — switches between panels in place; one panel visible, headers in a row.
- `faq` — the marketing FAQ band that composes `accordion` with a heading column and hairline register.
- `menu` — expanding rows for navigation, not for revealing content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | false | Whether one or multiple items can be open at the same time. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[] \| null` | `null` | false | Initial open item(s) when uncontrolled. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | In single mode, lets the open item collapse so that no item is open. |
| `size` | `'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects header height, padding, and typography. Provided to every item via context. |
| `arrowPosition` | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'right'` | false | Side of the header the chevron sits on. Provided to every item via context. |
| `modelValue` | `AccordionValue \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Accordion.Item` children. Each sub-component's own `default` slot is documented in the Sub-components section. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/accordion-content`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `accordion.vue`) attaches every sub-component to the root so `<Accordion.Item>` / `<Accordion.Trigger>` / `<Accordion.Content>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports above remain the tree-shaking path. The root is a disclosure component with `data-state="open|closed"`, so `Trigger` / `Content` are the correct anatomy names. Shared open-state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing.

- `accordion-item/accordion-item.vue` — One disclosure row.
  - Props: `value: string` (**required** — unique identifier used by the open-state model), `disabled?: boolean` (default `false` — prevents this item from toggling; from the Figma component description).
  - Slot: `default` — the item's `Accordion.Trigger` and `Accordion.Content`.
- `accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue` — The clickable header row (Figma "Header"): renders the title plus the `pi pi-chevron-down` glyph, toggles the item through the injected context, and exposes `aria-expanded`…
  - Props: `level?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` (default `3` — heading level of the wrapping `<h{level}>` for correct document outline).
  - Slot: `default` — header title content.
- `accordion-content/accordion-content.vue` — The collapsible panel.
  - Slot: `default` — panel body content.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json` — dropped repo-wide; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` resolves every path; `.d.ts` is generated at publish time, never committed):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/accordion/
├── accordion.vue                 (root; owns type/modelValue/size/arrowPosition, provides context)
├── index.ts                      (compound: attaches Item / Trigger / Content to the root)
├── injection-key.ts              (shared AccordionContext)
├── accordion-item/
│   └── accordion-item.vue
├── accordion-trigger/
│   └── accordion-trigger.vue
└── accordion-content/
    └── accordion-content.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the folder only):

```jsonc
"./accordion": "./src/components/content/accordion/index.ts",
"./accordion-item": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-item/accordion-item.vue",
"./accordion-trigger": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-trigger/accordion-trigger.vue",
"./accordion-content": "./src/components/content/accordion/accordion-content/accordion-content.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model     | Type                                      | Default     | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model` | `string \| string[] \| null \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:modelValue` | Open item(s) via `defineModel`: a single `value` string in single mode, an array of values in multiple mode, `null` when none is open. While unbound (`undefined`) the accordion is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultValue`. |

`./accordion` and `./accordion-root` export the type `AccordionValue` (`string | string[] | null`), the model's value without its unbound `undefined`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` — on the item, the trigger, and the content
- `data-disabled` mirrors the per-item `disabled` prop
- `data-orientation`: `vertical`
- Reflow: the trigger label region is `min-w-0`, so long trigger content truncates or wraps instead of overflowing a narrow box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus (Figma has no focus variant; we own it): `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each `Accordion.Trigger`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` move between triggers and into open content; `Enter` / `Space` toggle the focused item; `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move focus to the next / previous trigger; `Home` / `End` move focus to the first / last trigger.
- ARIA: each trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` reflecting open state and `aria-controls` referencing its content; the trigger button is wrapped in a heading element (`<h{level}>`, default `h3`); the content panel has `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` referencing its trigger. A `disabled` item sets `disabled` + `aria-disabled` on its trigger.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text (title `--text-default`, body `--text-muted` on the surface) / ≥3:1 for the chevron glyph, including the disabled state (`--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on the chevron rotation and content reveal.
- Touch target: the `large` header is 40px tall and the full-width header row is the hit area (≥40×40). The `medium` header is 32px tall — a justified deviation matching the Figma `medium` size token, mitigated by the full-width clickable row.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Accordion from '@aziontech/webkit/accordion'
</script>

<template>
  <Accordion
    type="single"
    collapsible
    default-value="overview"
    size="medium"
    arrow-position="right"
    class="w-full max-w-[40rem]"
  >
    <Accordion.Item value="overview">
      <Accordion.Trigger>What is Azion?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Azion runs your code at the edge, close to users.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="pricing">
      <Accordion.Trigger>How does pricing work?</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Pay only for what you use, with no upfront cost.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Item value="support">
      <Accordion.Trigger>Enterprise support</Accordion.Trigger>
      <Accordion.Content>Available on Business and Enterprise plans.</Accordion.Content>
    </Accordion.Item>
  </Accordion>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/accordion.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/accordion.md).

# Avatar

> Displays content or metadata in the UI. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/content/avatar/`.

- Import: `import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Identify a person next to their name: comment threads, member lists, "Last modified" cells, quotes.
- The user entry in a header or account menu.

## Do

- Pass initials in `label` (`"JD"`); it keeps the first two characters, so a full name shows its first two letters, not initials.
- Set `alt` to the person's name ("Jane Doe"). With `src` it is the image's `alt`; without an image it names the initials or icon fallback (`role="img"`), so a screen reader hears "Jane Doe", not "JD". Without `alt` the name falls back to the initials, then "Avatar" for an image or "User avatar" for the icon.
- Content precedence is `src`, then `label`, then `icon` (default `pi pi-user`).
- size` maps to 24 / 32 / 48 px with `medium` as the default; `kind` is `circle` (default) or `square`.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `brand`.
- A count or short status → use `badge`.
- A loading placeholder → use `skeleton`.

## Related

- `badge` — overlay on an avatar to show a count.
- `quote` — composes an avatar for the speaker.
- `brand` — the product mark, not a person.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Image URL. When set, renders a photo and takes precedence over label and icon. |
| `alt` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Accessible name: the image's `alt` with `src`, and the name of the initials or icon fallback without it. |
| `label` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Initials shown when no image (normalized to two uppercase characters). |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-user'` | false | Icon class for the fallback when no image or label (PrimeIcons class). |
| `kind` | `AvatarKind` | `'circle'` | false | Visual shape of the avatar container. |
| `size` | `AvatarSize` | `'medium'` | false | Size preset matching Figma sm / md / lg (24 / 32 / 48 px). |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'
</script>

<template>
  <Avatar
    label="AB"
    kind="circle"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/avatar.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/avatar.md).

# Badge

> Badge is a compact, non-interactive indicator that surfaces a numeric count or a very short status label with severity-based color coding. Use it to draw attention to a small piece of state — an unread count, a quantity, a short status word — and it is commonly overlaid on icons, avatars, or buttons. It differs from its sibling `tag`: `tag` is a labelled status/category chip (optional leading icon, optional pill shape, masked surfaces), whereas `badge` is a denser count/short-label indicator with fully filled severity surfaces and no icon affordance.

- Import: `import Badge from '@aziontech/webkit/badge'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Surface a numeric count or a very short status label attached to another element (a bell with unread count, a status dot with a label).
- Convey severity through `kind` (neutral / success / danger / …) with a fully filled surface.

## Do

- Keep the content to a count or a 1–2 word label; longer text belongs in `tag`.
- Drive color from `kind`, never a hardcoded color or a raw palette class.

## Don’t

- The label is user-removable or selectable → use `chip`.
- It is a labelled category/status with an optional leading icon or pill shape → use `tag`.

## Related

- `tag` — labelled status/category chip with optional icon and pill shape; use when the label is descriptive, not a count.
- `chip` — interactive/removable token; use when the user can select or dismiss it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `severity` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'default'` | `'primary'` | false | Color style for the badge surface and label; `default` uses the neutral `var(--bg-surface)` / `var(--text-default)` surface. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is 20px tall, `medium` is 24px, `large` is 30px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content; falls back to `label` when empty. |

## States

Badge is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed verbatim as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop (`primary` | `secondary` | `success` | `warning` | `danger` | `default`).
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium` | `large`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Badge is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Badge is not focusable and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is a presentational `<span>`; consumers that use the badge as a live count should label the host control (e.g. `aria-label="3 unread"`) since the visual label alone is not announced as status.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): every severity pairs a surface token with its matching `-contrast` (or `--text-default` for `default`), which the theme guarantees in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Badge is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Badge is non-interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the label renders `dir="auto"`, so a count or value in another script keeps its own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Badge from '@aziontech/webkit/badge'
</script>

<template>
  <Badge
    label="99"
    severity="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/badge.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/badge.md).

<!-- components/brand.md -->

# Brand

> The Azion brand logo, rendered as an inline SVG lockup. A single `kind` prop selects the lockup: `default` (the AZION wordmark) for standard surfaces, `reduced` (the "A" glyph) for compact headers and tight spaces, and `extended` (the AZION wordmark with the "move to the edge technologies®" tagline) for marketing-oriented layouts. It consolidates the loose `@aziontech/webkit/svg/azion/*` assets — which remain individually importable — behind one component.

- Import: `import Brand from '@aziontech/webkit/brand'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The Azion logo in a header, navigation bar, footer, sign-in screen or product mockup.
- kind="reduced"` where space is tight (collapsed sidebar, mobile header).
- kind="extended"` in marketing layouts that carry the tagline.

## Do

- Choose the lockup with `kind` and the height with `size` (16 / 24 / 32 px); do not pass width or height classes, the width follows the lockup's aspect ratio.
- Do not recolor or rebuild the SVG; use the component so every surface shows the same mark.
- For a home link, wrap Brand in an anchor; its `role="img"` and accessible name "Azion" give the link its name.

## Don’t

- A customer or partner logo → use `logo-wall`.
- A person's or organization's picture → use `avatar`.
- A decorative product graphic → use `illustration`.

## Related

- `site-nav` and `site-footer` — compose Brand for the site chrome.
- `avatar` — the picture or initials of a user, not the product mark.
- `logo-wall` — third-party company marks.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'reduced' \| 'extended'` | `'default'` | false | Brand lockup to render: `default` (AZION wordmark), `reduced` (the "A" glyph for tight spaces), `extended` (wordmark with the "move to the edge technologies®" tagline). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; sets the lockup height (16 / 24 / 32 px) while width scales automatically so each `kind` keeps its own aspect ratio. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop

## Accessibility

- The root carries `role="img"` and a default `aria-label` (`Azion`) so the logo has an accessible name; consumers may override the label via a passed `aria-label`.
- Non-interactive: the logo is not focusable and emits no events; the inner SVG is presentational.
- Contrast ≥3:1 for the brand mark against its background (large graphic).
- `motion-reduce` not applicable — the component is static.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Brand from '@aziontech/webkit/brand'
</script>

<template>
  <Brand kind="default" />
</template>
```
