<!-- components/browser-frame.md -->

# Browser Frame

> A browser window that renders live webkit components inside a viewport of its own, so a page or story can show a real screen at a real device size — desktop, tablet or mobile — and resize it by hand. The default slot is teleported into an internal `iframe`, which gives the content a true width × height viewport: CSS breakpoints fire against the frame's simulated width, viewport units resolve against its simulated height, and content taller than the viewport scrolls inside it like a page. When the simulated width is wider than the space available, the frame scales the whole viewport down to fit instead of clamping it. The chrome's window dots, address and size readout are decoration; its one control is a copy button inside the address bar, and the frame's other controls are the resize handles on its right edge, bottom edge and bottom-right corner.

- Import: `import BrowserFrame from '@aziontech/webkit/browser-frame'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Showing a real screen — a site band, a console page, a template — built from webkit components, at a device size you choose.
- Letting a reader drag a layout from desktop to tablet to mobile to see how it responds, on a documentation page.
- Pinning a composed example to a device size (`v-model:width` + `v-model:height`) so a story or page always shows the tablet or mobile layout.
- Showing that a result lives at a URL — a deployed site, a preview link — by setting `address`.

## Do

- Compose the default slot exactly as the screen would be composed in an app — the frame mirrors the page's stylesheets and theme into its viewport, so no extra wiring or classes are needed.
- Pin the device the example is about with `v-model:width` and `v-model:height` (`375 × 812` mobile, `768 × 1024` tablet, `1280 × 800` desktop); leave `width` unset to fill the container.
- Give the frame an `ariaLabel` that names what is shown (`Pricing page at tablet size`); it becomes the viewport's accessible name.
- Viewport-height units (`h-screen`, `min-h-dvh`) in slot content resolve against the simulated height, so a full-height shell renders as it would on the device.
- Do not add controls to the chrome — the address's copy button and the resize handles are the frame's only controls. Interactive content belongs in the default slot.

## Don’t

- For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- For third-party content loaded from another origin → use `embed`.
- For a mock of the Azion console's own shell on a marketing band → use the console shell mockup the page composes; it draws the console chrome and staggers its parts.
- For content whose layout depends on an overlay (`dialog`, `drawer`, a dropdown panel) or a JS breakpoint composable — those still read the outer page (see States), so the frame cannot show them at the simulated size.
- For a framed page section or grid cell → use `frame-box`.

## Related

- `doc-frame` — the documentation figure frame for stills and clips; no live viewport.
- `embed` — a titled `iframe` for another origin's document; `browser-frame` renders our own components.
- `frame-box` — the page's registration frame (hairlines + corner marks), not a window.
- `copy-button` — the clipboard control the address bar composes; reach for it directly to copy any other value.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `string` | `''` | false | Read-only URL shown in the chrome's address bar; the address bar is not rendered when empty. |
| `minWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxWidth` | `number` | `1920` | false | Largest viewport width the resize handles can reach, in pixels; widths wider than the container are scaled down to fit. |
| `minHeight` | `number` | `320` | false | Smallest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `maxHeight` | `number` | `1440` | false | Largest viewport height the resize handles can reach, in pixels. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the viewport; when empty it falls back to `address`, then to `Preview`. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the address bar's copy button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Copy address`). |
| `widthHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the right-edge width handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview width`). |
| `heightHandleAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the bottom-edge height handle. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize preview height`). |
| `width` | `number \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:width`). |
| `height` | `number` | `800` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:height`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The live content, teleported into the frame's viewport `iframe` once it is ready. Renders client-side only. |

## v-model

| Model            | Type     | Default     | Emits           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | -------- | ----------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model:width`  | `number` | `undefined` | `update:width`  | Simulated viewport width in pixels via `defineModel('width')`. Undefined fills the container; the width and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minWidth`…`maxWidth`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled. |
| `v-model:height` | `number` | `800`       | `update:height` | Simulated viewport height in pixels via `defineModel('height', { default: 800 })`. The height and corner handles write a number, clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`, on every resize step. Works controlled or uncontrolled.         |

## States

The frame is static apart from its resize handles.

- **Viewport.** The root renders an `iframe` (blank document). Once it loads, the frame mirrors the host page's stylesheets (every `style` and stylesheet `link` in `head`, kept in sync as they change so HMR still applies) and the theme attributes of the host's root element (`data-theme`, `class`) into it, then teleports the default slot into its `body`. The content is the same Vue app — props, reactivity, provide/inject and events behave as if it were rendered in place.
- **Breakpoints.** CSS media queries and viewport units in the content resolve against the viewport's width and height. JS breakpoint reads (`matchMedia` in a composable) and overlays that teleport to the document `body` still resolve against the host page — a documented limit, not a bug.
- **Size.** The viewport renders at the effective width (`width` when set, otherwise the container's width) and at `height`. Content taller or wider than the viewport scrolls inside the `iframe`'s own document, exactly as a page scrolls in a browser.
- **Scale.** When the effective width exceeds the container, the viewport is scaled down by `container / effective` on both axes, and the frame's on-page height is `height × scale`. A frame narrower than its container is centered in it.
- **Resizing.** Three handles resize the viewport:
  - the **width handle** on the right edge writes `width`;
  - the **height handle** on the bottom edge writes `height`;
  - the **corner handle** at the bottom-right writes both at once.
    Pointer drags use pointer capture. A width drag moves the right edge under the pointer (the frame is centered, so the width changes by twice the pointer's travel) and is clamped to `minWidth` and the container width; a height drag follows the pointer's travel divided by the current scale and is clamped to `minHeight`…`maxHeight`. The keyboard reaches up to `maxWidth` / `maxHeight`. While any handle is dragged the root sets `data-resizing` and the content ignores the pointer.
- **Size readout.** While any handle is dragged or focused, the chrome shows the viewport size (`768 × 1024`) at its trailing end; it is hidden otherwise.
- **Scaled.** The root sets `data-scaled` while the viewport is scaled below 1.
- **Address.** Rendered only when `address` is non-empty, centered in the chrome as a compact, fully rounded pill up to `--container-xs` wide and exactly as tall as the small copy button (28px), which sits flush at its trailing end, never overlapping the window dots or the readout. The pill is filled with the skeleton placeholder fill (static — no sweep) and edged with a muted hairline. Its text is set in the monospace code label and centered in the space left of the copy button; long addresses truncate in the middle: a leading part ellipsizes and the last 12 characters always stay visible.
- **Copy.** The address bar's trailing end composes the package's `CopyButton` (`kind="transparent"`, `size="small"`) with `value` = the full `address`; its copied feedback is the `CopyButton`'s own.
- **Test ids.** Root fallback `content-browser-frame` (consumer override wins); `${testId}__address`, `${testId}__viewport` (the `iframe`), `${testId}__copy`, `${testId}__width-handle`, `${testId}__height-handle`, `${testId}__corner-handle`.
- **Composable.** The document mirroring and teleport target live in a co-located lifecycle composable, `composables/use-frame-document.ts`, that disconnects every observer on scope dispose.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the width and height handles show `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; focusable content inside the viewport keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map:
  - width handle — `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` change the width by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minWidth`, `End` to `maxWidth`;
  - height handle — `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` change the height by 10px, `Shift` + arrow by 100px, `Home` jumps to `minHeight`, `End` to `maxHeight`;
  - the corner handle is pointer-only and not focusable — both of its axes are already reachable through the two keyboard handles;
  - the copy button is a normal tab stop before the handles and keeps `CopyButton`'s own keyboard behavior (`Enter` / `Space` copy);
  - the viewport's content is reached with `Tab` as part of the page's normal order.
- ARIA:
  - width handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `aria-valuenow` (effective width), `aria-valuemin` (`minWidth`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxWidth`), `aria-valuetext` (`768 pixels wide`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id, from `useId()`), `aria-label` from `widthHandleAriaLabel`;
  - height handle — focusable `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `aria-valuenow` (`height`), `aria-valuemin` (`minHeight`), `aria-valuemax` (`maxHeight`), `aria-valuetext` (`1024 pixels tall`), `aria-controls` (the viewport id), `aria-label` from `heightHandleAriaLabel`;
  - the corner handle, the window dots, the address text and the size readout are `aria-hidden="true"`; the chrome bar itself is not hidden, so the copy button stays reachable, named by `copyAriaLabel`;
  - the `iframe` carries `title` from `ariaLabel` → `address` → `Preview`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-placeholder)` over `var(--bg-surface)` for the address and on `var(--bg-surface)` for the readout; the handle grips at rest `var(--border-strong)` meet 3:1 against `var(--bg-canvas)` as non-text controls.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the handles' color transition; nothing else moves.
- Touch target: the edge handles' hit areas are 24px deep and run the frame's full width or height, and the corner handle is 24×24 — a justified deviation from 40×40: a deeper strip would cover more of the content's edge, and 24px meets WCAG 2.5.8.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: the width handle grows with `ArrowRight` and shrinks with `ArrowLeft` in reading order, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- Pointer: the width drag delta is inverted under `rtl`.
- User data: the address bar renders `dir="ltr"`: a URL always reads left to right.

<!-- components/card.md -->

# Card

> Displays content or metadata in the UI. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/content/card/`.

- Import: `import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Group related console content into one bordered surface with a title header, a body and an optional footer, such as a settings block, a summary or a form section.
- Host a divided list edge to edge: set `:padded="false"` and put an `Item` list in the `content` slot.
- A centered single-card screen (sign-up, onboarding, a success page) that needs header, body and footer regions.
- A catalog tile for an integration, an extension or a plugin: set `kind="integration"` for the logo, the name, the vendor, a short description, badges, the installed state and one action.

## Do

- Put the body in the `content` slot. There is no `default` slot, so children passed without `#content` don't render.
- Use `title` for a plain heading (rendered as an `h2`). Use the `header` slot only when the header needs another layout: it replaces both the title and `header-action`.
- header-action` content stays hidden until the header is hovered or focused, so keep it to secondary actions and never make it the only way to reach a control.
- Set `:padded="false"` only when the content draws its own inset or needs flush dividers.
- The footer renders only when the `footer` slot has content; don't pass an empty template to reserve space.
- kind="integration"` lays the card out from props: `title`, `logo` (or the `logo` slot), `vendor`, `description`, `badges` and `installed`. The title becomes a link when `href` is set, otherwise a button that emits `select`, and it stretches over the whole card so the tile is one target. Put a single action (Install, Configure) in the `action` slot; it sits above the stretched target and stays reachable on its own.
- Keep the description to one or two sentences; the card clamps it to three lines.
- Show at most two badges (category, context, plan). The installed state is a prop, not a badge, so it reads the same everywhere.
- Integration cards sit under a section heading, so their title is an `h3`.

## Don’t

- The surface sits above the page as a modal or a side sheet → use `dialog` or `drawer`.
- It is one tier of a pricing comparison → use `card-pricing`.
- It is a framed cell or band of a marketing page → use `frame-box` or `card-grid`.
- It is a single row of title, description, media and actions → use `item`.
- It is one record of a resource list shown as cards, with selection and fields → use `cards` (with `useCollection`).
- It is a template tile in a gallery with no vendor, badge or install state → keep `kind="default"` with a `content` slot (see `platform/view/template-browser`).

## Related

- `item` — rows inside the card; with `padded` set to false, an `Item` list runs its dividers to the card edges.
- `card-pricing` — pricing tier card with its own price hierarchy and action.
- `card-grid` — responsive grid of cells for marketing pages.
- `panel` — the layered shell behind overlays, not an in-page card.
- `empty-state` — goes in the `content` slot when the card has no data yet.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading rendered in the header when the `header` slot is empty; with `kind="integration"`, the item name. |
| `padded` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Pads the content region. Set `false` for flush, edge-to-edge content such as an `ItemList` with full-width dividers. |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'integration'` | `'default'` | false | integration` lays the card out as a catalog tile from `title`, `logo`, `vendor`, `description`, `badges`, `installed` and the `action` slot. |
| `logo` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: icon class for the logo mark. The `logo` slot takes an image instead. |
| `vendor` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: who publishes the item, shown as "by {vendor}". |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: one or two sentences on what the item does. |
| `badges` | `CardBadge[]` | `[]` | false | Integration kind: small tags such as the category or the context (`{ label, severity? }`, severity defaults to `info`). |
| `installed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Integration kind: shows the Installed tag. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Integration kind: the title links here; without it the title is a button that emits `select`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `event: MouseEvent` | Integration kind without `href`: the title (the whole tile) was activated. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | — | Replaces the default header layout (title + header-action). |
| `header-action` | — | Actions aligned to the end of the default header; visible on header hover. |
| `content` | — | Main card body; with `kind="integration"` it renders under the description. |
| `footer` | — | Footer actions or metadata; omitted when empty. |
| `logo` | — | Integration kind: replaces the logo mark, for an `img` with an empty `alt`. |
| `action` | — | Integration kind: one action at the end of the tile, above the stretched title target. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- Responsive: the content region is the `@container/card`, so `KeyValuePairs`, `Field orientation="responsive"` and any `@sm:`/`@md:` utility inside follow the card, not the window. A card used as a shrink-to-fit flex item must get an explicit width (`flex-1`, `w-full`, a grid track): inline-size containment gives the content no intrinsic width.
- Hover-free devices: the `header-action` slot stays visible where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).
- Integration kind: `hover` shades the surface, `focus-visible` rings the whole tile (the ring sits on the stretched title target), `installed` adds the success Installed tag.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the logo sits at the start, the badges and the action at the end.
- Icons: the logo is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: the vendor and the title render in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key              | English source | Override prop |
| ---------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `card.byVendor`  | by {vendor}    | —             |
| `card.installed` | Installed      | —             |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the content region is `@container/card`; the integration layout does not change with width, the description wraps and clamps to three lines.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the badges wrap under the title row; the action stays at the end of its own row.
- Touch: the whole tile is the target; the action is a regular `Button`.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
</script>

<template>
  <Card
    title="Card Title"
    class="w-full max-w-[512px]"
  >
    <template #content>
      <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Card body content. Place forms, tables, or any markup in the content slot.
      </p>
    </template>
  </Card>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/card.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/card.md).

<!-- components/card-pricing.md -->

# Card Pricing

> One tier of a pricing table: what it is called, what it costs, what that price includes, and the one action that moves the account onto it. The card owns the typographic hierarchy of a price — an overline plan name, the amount as the headline figure, and the billing caveat under it in muted body copy — so a row of tiers reads as a comparison rather than as three differently-typeset cards. `slotPosition` is the axis that decides which of the two compositions the card is. **`bottom`** is the compact tier: the name, a `medium` amount and the caveat stack at the top, the action follows, and the slot sits under it — a card sized by its own content, for a row of tiers a reader scans. **`middle`** is the full tier: the amount becomes the `large` headline figure, the caveat moves up to `body-md`, the slot grows to fill the card, and the action is pinned to the bottom edge so a row of `middle` cards has its buttons on one line whatever each tier's feature list holds. `kind` decides only whether the card draws its own surface (`contained`) or sits on the one behind it (`transparent`); it never changes the composition. The name, the amount and the caveat are **one column**, capped at `--container-xs` (348px) rather than at the card's full width: the caveat is a sentence about the price directly above it, so it wraps on the price's measure. The cap shipped as `--container-3xs` (256px) — two rungs down the ladder, and too narrow for the copy it holds. 256px sets `body-md` at roughly 33 characters, under the 45–75 a prose measure wants, and all three billing caveats on the sample pricing page (66, 69 and 84 characters) ran to three lines there. At 348px the measure is ~46 characters and the same three set in two, while the card's own content box at 1440 is 413px — so the caveat is still held to the price's column instead of the card's. The card carries **one** prose region — the pricing caveat, below the amount. It used to carry a second paragraph above the amount as well, and with `aligned` reserving a band for each, a row of tiers showed two two-line muted blocks around every price doing the same visual job. The Figma component (`3605:2260`) has a single prose region, `Pricing Details`, positioned below the amount, so that is the one the card keeps; a tier's positioning sentence belongs to whatever the consumer puts in the slot. `aligned` makes a ROW of cards read as one comparison. Every region is content-sized by default, which is right for a single card and wrong for three side by side — a tier with a two-line caveat and a tier with none put their feature lists on different lines, and the reader has to re-find the row in every column. It reserves **three** lines for the caveat, in `lh` so the reservation follows the type token rather than a hard-coded height. Three is the design's 64px band expressed in whole lines of the region's own token (`body-md` is a 22px line box, so `3lh` is 66px; `2lh` is 44px and twenty short) — it shipped as `2lh`, and the shortfall stayed invisible until a tier's caveat ran to three lines at the region's then-256px measure, overflowed the band, and pushed that column's feature list 22px below the other two. Opt-in, because reserving empty lines is wrong for a lone card; set it on every card in the row. A caveat past three lines still pushes the row down, like any overflow. The plan title is an **overline** (`.text-overline-md` on an `<h3>`): the token carries the display face, the uppercase transform and the widest tracking step, so the tier reads as a label on the card rather than as a title competing with the price beneath it. It stays an `<h3>` for the document outline — the tier is the section heading — while looking like an overline.

- Import: `import CardPricing from '@aziontech/webkit/card-pricing'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- One tier in a row of plans: plan name, price, billing caveat, one action and the tier's feature list.
- A compact tier sized by its content (`slot-position="bottom"`), or a full tier whose action is pinned to the bottom so a row's buttons line up (`slot-position="middle"`).
- A tier set on the surface behind it (`kind="transparent"`) inside a section that already draws the frame.

## Do

- In a row of tiers, set `aligned` on every card so each caveat reserves the same band and the feature lists start on one line.
- Keep `pricing-details` to the billing caveat. A tier's positioning sentence goes in the default slot with the feature list.
- The card emits no events, and the built-in button has no handler. To act on the click, fill the `actions` slot with your own `Button`.
- Hide the symbol or the period with `:show-prefix="false"` / `:show-suffix="false"` (for example on a custom-quote tier) instead of clearing `prefix` / `suffix`.
- Mark at most one card in a row with `show-tag` and `tag-label`.

## Don’t

- You need the whole plans band of a pricing page, with the billing-period toggle and the framed row → use `pricing-plans`.
- You need a feature-by-feature comparison across plans → use `compare-plans`.
- You only need to show an amount, in a table cell or a summary → use `currency`.
- The card holds general content rather than a price → use `card`.

## Related

- `currency` — typesets the amount inside the card; use it directly for prices outside a tier card.
- `pricing-plans` — the page section that lays out a row of plan cards with the billing toggle.
- `compare-plans` — the matrix that sits under the plan cards.
- `card` — generic bordered card with header, content and footer regions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planTitle` | `string` | `'Pro'` | false | plan Title. |
| `pricingDetails` | `string` | `''` | false | pricing Details. |
| `showPricingDetails` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Pricing Details. |
| `showTag` | `boolean` | `false` | false | show Tag. |
| `tagLabel` | `string` | `'Popular'` | false | tag Label. |
| `aligned` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Reserves the caveat's band so a row of cards aligns row-for-row. Set it on every card in the row. |
| `slotPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'middle'` | `'bottom'` | false | slot Position. |
| `kind` | `'contained' \| 'transparent'` | `'contained'` | false | card Style. |
| `value` | `string` | `'20'` | false | value. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `'/ mon'` | false | suffix. |
| `showPrefix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Prefix. |
| `showSuffix` | `boolean` | `true` | false | show Suffix. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `'Label'` | false | action Label. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Named slot. |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

<!-- components/currency.md -->

# Currency

> Typesets one monetary amount as three separately-styled parts — the currency symbol, the figure, and a trailing period or unit — so money reads the same everywhere in the product instead of being a formatted string each screen spells its own way. The suffix carries the code typeface (`text-label-code-*`), which keeps the unit visually subordinate to the figure and aligns the whole set with the way the system typesets metered values. The size ladder is the house one (`small` / `medium` / `large`) and each step is a different reading distance: `small` is an amount inside a table row or a list cell, `medium` an amount stated as a fact on a card, `large` the headline figure of a pricing card. `large` bottom-aligns the suffix against the figure rather than centring it, because a 56px numeral centred against a 14px unit reads as two unrelated pieces of text.

- Import: `import Currency from '@aziontech/webkit/currency'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Any monetary amount in the product: a price in a table row or list cell (`small`), an amount stated on a card (`medium`), the headline figure of a pricing card (`large`).
- An amount followed by a period or unit (`/ mon`, `/ GB`) that should read as secondary to the figure.

## Do

- Pass `value` already formatted as a string (`'1,250.00'`). The component does no number or locale formatting.
- prefix` defaults to `'$'`; set `prefix=""` to drop the symbol. The suffix renders only when `suffix` is set.
- Pick `size` by reading distance, not by available space: `small` (the default) in tables and lists, `medium` on cards, `large` only for a headline price.
- Don't restyle the parts with classes; each size takes its typography from the `text-amount-*` and `text-label-code-*` tokens.

## Don’t

- You need a full pricing tier with plan name, caveat and action → use `card-pricing`.
- The headline figures are not money (throughput, uptime, points of presence) → use `big-numbers`.

## Related

- `card-pricing` — composes Currency for its price, `medium` or `large` depending on `slotPosition`.
- `big-numbers` — display-scale figures for metrics that aren't money.
- `stats-band` — page section of big figures with their own prefix and unit.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `''` | false | value. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'$'` | false | prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | `''` | false | suffix. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'small'` | false | Size token; affects typography and the gap between the figure and the suffix. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Currency from '@aziontech/webkit/currency'
</script>

<template>
  <Currency
    value="20"
    prefix="$"
    suffix="per month"
    size="small"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/currency.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/currency.md).

<!-- components/feature-list.md -->

# Feature List

> The features a plan, product or upgrade includes, each behind a check mark, in one or two columns. It is the "what you get" list of a plan card, an upgrade card or a change-plan drawer: short labels, an optional one-line description under each, and a check that says "included", never "done". It replaces the hand-written `ul` with a `pi pi-check` per row that the billing pages and the change-plan drawer drew with different icon colours.

- Import: `import FeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-list'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The perks of an upgrade card (Upgrade to Pro: Unlimited Applications, Unlimited Workloads, Custom Domains).
- The features a plan includes in a change-plan or upgrade drawer, each with a short description.
- Any short list of included capabilities where the check is the only marker.

## Do

- Keep each label to a few words in title case or sentence case, one capability per row; put the detail in `description`, not in the label.
- Use `columns: 2` for six or more short labels in a wide card; it falls back to one column in a narrow box on its own.
- Name the list with `ariaLabel` (for example "Pro plan features") when no visible heading right above it says what the features belong to.
- Do not hand-write the list with your own check icons: the check colour and spacing are part of the component.

## Don’t

- Steps or tasks with a done/not-done state (a production checklist, a setup guide) → use `outcome-mark` per row, or the `stepper`.
- A comparison of features across plans → use `compare-plans` or `table`.
- Label and value facts → use `key-value-pairs`.
- Rows that navigate or carry actions → use `item`.
- Marketing pricing cards on the site → use `card-pricing` / `pricing-plans`, which carry their own feature lists.

## Related

- `key-value-pairs` — the plan facts that sit next to the feature list in a billing card.
- `card` — the surface the list sits in; FeatureList brings no surface of its own.
- `outcome-mark` — the mark for a step that finished, which this check is not.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `FeatureListItem[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order; each item is `{ label: string; description?: string }`. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | false | Columns when the list's own box is at least the md container; a narrower box always shows one column. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-columns` on the list mirrors `columns`
- Empty: with no `items` the component renders nothing (no empty list, no placeholder); the card around it decides what to say
- No `loading`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error` or `open` states: the list is static, read-only text

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none; the list has no interactive part.
- Keyboard map: no tab stop.
- ARIA: a native `ul` with `role="list"` (so the list semantics survive `list-style: none` in Safari); each feature is an `li`; the check glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; `ariaLabel` is set as `aria-label` on the `ul` only when non-empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label and the muted description, ≥3:1 for the check glyph, on `var(--bg-surface)` in both themes.
- No motion.
- No touch target: nothing is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the check sits at the inline start and the text after it, so the row mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the check does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key logic.
- User data: each label and description renders `dir="auto"`, so a product name in another script keeps its own direction.

## Internationalization

No built-in strings: every visible text comes from `items`, and the accessible name from `ariaLabel`.

- Formatting: none

## Responsive

- Container queries: the root is `@container/feature-list`; `columns: 2` applies from `@md` of that box (472 px) and the list shows one column below it, so a card in a split view or on a phone stacks the features by itself.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): one column; labels and descriptions wrap, never truncate.
- Touch: nothing is interactive.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long unbroken words break.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FeatureList from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-list'

  const features = [
    { label: 'Unlimited Applications' },
    { label: 'Unlimited Workloads' },
    { label: 'Custom Domains' },
    { label: 'Priority Support' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureList
    :items="features"
    aria-label="Pro plan features"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/feature-list.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/feature-list.md).

<!-- components/help-panel.md -->

# Help Panel

> The content of a help side region: a topic's title, a few sections of short guidance, and the "Learn more" links that leave for the documentation — or, in tutorial mode, an ordered list of tasks with the reader's progress through them. It is the thing that goes **inside** a side region, not the region itself: the consumer places it in a `Drawer` or in the page's side rail, and that host owns opening, closing and the close button. It owns no open state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content` and no `data-state="open|closed"`. Its anatomy is the anatomy of a help page — `Header`, `Section`, `Links`, `Tutorial`, `Task` — composed by hand, so a topic can omit the links, carry one section or five, or be a tutorial with no prose at all.

- Import: `import HelpPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A Console screen needs contextual help beside the work: what this page is for, what a field means, where the docs are.
- A guided, multi-task tutorial runs beside the real UI, and the reader needs to see which task they are on and how many are done.
- The help content is loaded asynchronously and the region must reserve its space while it arrives (`loading`).

## Do

- One topic per panel. When the reader moves to another part of the page, swap the panel's content — do not stack two headers.
- Keep each `Section` to a short paragraph or a short list. If the reader has to scroll a section, the content belongs in the docs and the panel should link to it.
- Title sections with the question the reader is asking (`What is a workload?`), not with a noun (`Overview`).
- Put links to the documentation in `HelpPanel.Links`, at the end, not inline in every section.
- In tutorial mode, exactly one task is `current`. Mark a task `complete` only when the real UI confirms it, never on click.
- Close affordances belong to the host. Do not put a close button in `HelpPanel.Header`; the `Drawer` or side rail already has one.

## Don’t

- A one-line hint attached to a single control → use `doc-tooltip` or the field's `helper-text`.
- The region itself (overlay, slide-in, close button, focus trap) → use `drawer`; put `help-panel` inside it.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates between, with the step's form filling the column beside it → use `stepper`.
- Numbered instructions inside a documentation page, read all at once → use `doc-steps` + `doc-step`.
- A page with nothing configured yet, which needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `drawer` — the host that opens, closes and traps focus around a help panel shown as an overlay.
- `stepper` — the same dot language for steps the reader navigates; tutorial tasks are reported, not navigated.
- `link` — the standalone link each `HelpPanel.Links` row is composed from.
- `button` — the Start / Continue / Restart controls the consumer composes into a tutorial's `actions` slot.
- `skeleton` — what the panel renders in place of its content while `loading`.
- `doc-prose` — long-form documentation prose; a help section is a few short paragraphs, not an article.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the complementary landmark the panel renders. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the help topic loads; sets aria-busy. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The panel's parts — `HelpPanel.Header`, `HelpPanel.Section`, `HelpPanel.Tutorial`, `HelpPanel.Links` — in reading order. Not rendered while `loading`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-section`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-links`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-tutorial`
- `@aziontech/webkit/help-panel-task`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: an `index.ts` (beside `help-panel.vue`) attaches every sub-component
to the root so `<HelpPanel.Header>` … `<HelpPanel.Task>` resolve from one import; the standalone imports
remain the tree-shaking path. The panel has no open/closed state, so there is no `Trigger` / `Content` —
every member is named after a part of a help page. Tutorial progress flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by `HelpPanel.Tutorial`, not by the root): each `HelpPanel.Task` registers
itself and its `status` with the nearest tutorial on mount, reads back its own ordinal, and unregisters
on unmount, so the consumer never counts tasks or numbers them by hand.

- `help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue` — The topic's title and an optional one-line description.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the topic's name, rendered as the panel's heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the title saying what the topic covers; not rendered when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — optional extra content under the description (a `Tag` naming the product state, for example).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-header`.
- `help-panel-section/help-panel-section.vue` — One block of guidance with its own heading.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the question this section answers; the section renders no heading when empty).
  - Slot: `default` — the section's prose: paragraphs, short lists, inline `text-link` anchors.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-section`.
- `help-panel-links/help-panel-links.vue` — The "Learn more" footer: a heading over a column of `Link` items the consumer composes.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `undefined` — the heading over the links; absent uses the locale catalog, `Learn more` in English, and an empty string renders no heading).
  - Slot: `default` — `Link` items, one per destination.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-links`.
- `help-panel-tutorial/help-panel-tutorial.vue` — Tutorial mode: a title, a description, a progress line derived from the registered tasks ("2 of 3 complete"), the ordered task list, and an action row.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — the tutorial's name), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line on what the reader will have done at the end; not rendered when empty), `completed?: boolean` (default `false` — the owner marks the whole tutorial done; renders `data-completed` and a `Tag` reading `Completed` beside the title).
  - Slots: `default` — `HelpPanel.Task` items, in order; `actions` — the Start / Continue / Restart controls (`Button`) the consumer composes; the row is not rendered when the slot is empty.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-tutorial`.
- `help-panel-task/help-panel-task.vue` — One task: a numbered marker, a title, and the task's instructions.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — what the reader does, in their words), `status?: 'upcoming' | 'current' | 'complete'` (default `'upcoming'` — where the reader is in the tutorial; set by the owner from what the real UI confirmed).
  - Slot: `default` — the task's instructions, in `text-body-sm`.
  - `data-testid` fallback: `content-help-panel-task`.

Exported types (from the root folder, so a consumer can type the value it holds): `HelpPanelTaskStatus = 'upcoming' | 'current' | 'complete'`.

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/help-panel/
├── help-panel.vue                         (root; aside landmark, loading state)
├── help-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                               (compound: attaches the five parts to the root)
├── injection-key.ts                       (HelpPanelTutorialContext — provided by Tutorial)
├── composables/
│   └── use-help-panel-tutorial-context.ts (injects; throws outside a HelpPanel.Tutorial)
├── help-panel-header/
│   └── help-panel-header.vue
├── help-panel-section/
│   └── help-panel-section.vue
├── help-panel-links/
│   └── help-panel-links.vue
├── help-panel-tutorial/
│   └── help-panel-tutorial.vue
└── help-panel-task/
    └── help-panel-task.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./help-panel": "./src/components/content/help-panel/index.ts",
"./help-panel-root": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel.vue",
"./help-panel-header": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-header/help-panel-header.vue",
"./help-panel-section": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-section/help-panel-section.vue",
"./help-panel-links": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-links/help-panel-links.vue",
"./help-panel-tutorial": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-tutorial/help-panel-tutorial.vue",
"./help-panel-task": "./src/components/content/help-panel/help-panel-task/help-panel-task.vue"
```

Composed DS components (all present in `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`, imported by relative path
inside the package): `skeleton` (root, `loading`), `divider` (`Links`), `tag` (`Tutorial`, `completed`).
`link` and `button` are composed by the consumer through slots, never imported by the panel.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`; on `HelpPanel.Task`: `upcoming`, `current`, `complete`
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors the `loading` prop
- `data-status` on `HelpPanel.Task` mirrors its `status` prop: `upcoming` | `current` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on `HelpPanel.Tutorial` mirrors its `completed` prop
- No `data-state` — the panel has no open/closed state (the host owns it)
- No `data-disabled` — nothing in the panel is interactive on its own; interactive content (`Link`, `Button`) is composed by the consumer and carries its own states

The root, while `loading`: the default slot is not rendered; in its place the root renders a title
line and three body lines with `Skeleton` (`kind="shape"`; title `width="60%"` `height="1.25rem"`, body
lines `width="100%"`, `width="100%"`, `width="75%"`, each `height="0.875rem"`), and sets
`aria-busy="true"`. The loading lines carry `aria-hidden="true"`; the landmark keeps its accessible
name.

The three task markers, and what each one renders:

| `data-status` | Marker                                                  | Title ink             | Screen-reader word |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------ |
| `upcoming`    | outlined in `--border-default`, muted, shows its number | `var(--text-muted)`   | `Not started`      |
| `current`     | outlined in `--secondary`, shows its number             | `var(--text-default)` | `Current task`     |
| `complete`    | filled `--secondary`, `pi pi-check` glyph               | `var(--text-default)` | `Complete`         |

The tutorial's progress line reads `<complete> of <total> complete`, counting registered tasks whose
`status` is `complete`. It is derived; the consumer never passes the counts.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/help-panel`, so the content in the side panel adapts to the panel width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the panel itself is not focusable; focus rings belong to the composed `Link` / `Button` controls, which already carry `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the composed links and action buttons in reading order. The panel adds no key handling of its own — no roving tabindex, no arrow navigation. `Esc` and focus trap / restore are owned by the host (`Drawer`), not by the panel.
- ARIA: the root is an `<aside>` (complementary landmark) named by `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; `aria-busy="true"` while `loading`. Headings form an outline — `HelpPanel.Header` is `<h2>`, `Section` / `Links` / `Tutorial` titles are `<h3>` — and each `<section>` is `aria-labelledby` its heading via `useId()`. The tutorial's task list is an `<ol>`; the `current` task's `<li>` carries `aria-current="step"`. The task marker glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`, and each task carries an `sr-only` status word (see States). The progress line is `aria-live="polite"` so a task completing in the real UI is announced.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted `upcoming` title and the description ink
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the task marker and title transition
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the panel's own markup (nothing in it is interactive); the composed `Link` / `Button` controls meet it

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HelpPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/help-panel'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <HelpPanel aria-label="Help: Cache settings">
      <HelpPanel.Header
        title="Cache settings"
        description="How long content stays at the edge before it is fetched again."
      />
      <HelpPanel.Section title="What does the cache TTL control?">
        <p>
          The TTL sets how many seconds an object is served from the edge before the origin is asked
          for a fresh copy.
        </p>
      </HelpPanel.Section>
      <HelpPanel.Section title="When should I bypass the cache?">
        <p>Bypass it for responses that change per user, such as carts and account pages.</p>
      </HelpPanel.Section>
      <HelpPanel.Links>
        <Link
          label="Cache settings documentation"

          target="_blank"
        />

          target="_blank"
        />
      </HelpPanel.Links>
    </HelpPanel>
  </div>
```

<!-- components/hotspot.md -->

# Hotspot

> Marks a real control as a step of a tutorial. It wraps the control and, while a tutorial that names its `hotspotId` runs, draws a small marker beside it. The current step's marker pulses and opens the step in a popover: the step's title, `Step n of N` with the task's name, the instructions, and Previous / Next (Finish on the last step). Outside a running tutorial, or outside a `TutorialPanel.Provider`, it renders only the wrapped control, so hotspots can stay on a page for good.

- Import: `import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A tutorial step is about one control on the page, and the reader should see where it is.
- The page runs inside a `TutorialPanel.Provider` and offers guided tutorials from its help region.

## Do

- Wrap exactly the control the step is about; keep the marker beside it, not inside a long row.
- Use `side="start"` when the control sits at the end of a row and the marker would overflow.
- One `hotspotId` per control and per page. The same id on two elements opens two popovers.
- Keep step content short: the popover is a small surface over the real UI.

## Don’t

- A permanent tip on a control → use `hint` or `popover`.
- A new feature announcement with no tutorial behind it → use `popover` or an `alert`.
- Help text for a form field → use the field's `helper-text`.

## Related

- `tutorial-panel` — the provider holds the steps a hotspot shows; the panel lists and runs the tutorials.
- `popover` — the overlay the current step opens in.
- `help-panel` — static help without a guided run.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hotspotId` | `string` | `—` | true | Matches the `hotspotId` of a tutorial step; the marker shows while that step's tutorial runs. |
| `side` | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'end'` | false | Which side of the wrapped control the marker sits on, in reading direction. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The real control the step is about. |

## States

- Visual states: `inactive` (no marker), `active` (static marker: the step belongs to the running tutorial), `current` (marker filled and pulsing, popover open), `dismissed` (current step closed by the reader: marker filled, no pulse, popover closed)
- `data-active` on the root when the marker shows; `data-current` on the root and on the marker for the current step
- `data-side` mirrors `side`
- The popover's `data-state` is `open` | `closed` (owned by `Popover`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the marker.
- Keyboard map: the marker is a `button` in the tab order after the wrapped control (before it with `side="start"`); `Enter` / `Space` opens its step (and makes it current). Inside the popover `Tab` cycles Close, Previous and Next (the `Popover` loop); `Esc` closes the step and returns focus to the marker. Next, Previous and the marker move focus into the new step's popover; Finish moves focus to the panel's completion heading.
- ARIA: the marker is named `Tutorial step: <title>` and carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (from `Popover.Trigger`). The popover is a non-modal `dialog` labelled by the step title and described by `Step n of N`. The pulse ring and dot are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast: the marker's `--primary` against the canvas ≥3:1 (non-text) in both themes.
- Touch target: the visible marker is 24 px; a `before:` pseudo-element extends the hit area by 8 px on each side (40 px).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the root is a flex row that follows `dir`; `side="start"` renders the marker before the control in the DOM, so reading, tab and visual order agree in both directions. The popover placement mirrors through `usePlacement`.
- Icons: none in the marker.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `hotspot.label`    | `Tutorial step: {title}`    | —             |
| `hotspot.stepOf`   | `Step {current} of {total}` | —             |
| `hotspot.previous` | `Previous`                  | —             |
| `hotspot.next`     | `Next`                      | —             |
| `hotspot.finish`   | `Finish`                    | —             |

- Formatting: none (integers interpolated). The close button's name comes from `popover.close`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: fixed-size marker.
- Narrow: the root has `max-w-full` and the popover is `width="small"` (`--container-xs`), clamped by `Popover` to the viewport.
- Touch: 40 px hit area through the pseudo-element.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the popover wraps its text.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Hotspot from '@aziontech/webkit/hotspot'
  import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tutorials = [
    {
      id: 'publish',
      title: 'Publish a change',
      tasks: [
        {
          title: 'Review and deploy',
          steps: [
            {
              title: 'Preview the change',
              content: 'Open the preview to check the change before anyone else sees it.',
              hotspotId: 'preview'
            },
            {
              title: 'Deploy',
              content: 'Select Deploy to send the change to production.',
              hotspotId: 'deploy'
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const active = ref('publish')
  const step = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <TutorialPanel.Provider
    v-model:active="active"
    v-model:step="step"
    :tutorials="tutorials"
  >
    <div class="flex min-h-(--container-3xs) flex-wrap items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="preview">
        <Button
          label="Preview"
          kind="outlined"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
      <Hotspot hotspot-id="deploy">
        <Button
          label="Deploy"
          kind="primary"
          size="medium"
        />
      </Hotspot>
    </div>
  </TutorialPanel.Provider>
</template>
```

<!-- components/illustration.md -->

# Illustration

> Renders an **official product illustration** — one of the scenes drawn in the Assets library in Figma and exported as an SVG that ships with this package. `name` selects a scene from a closed registry; there is no way to assemble artwork out of markup, so a page can only render illustrations design has actually signed off, and a scene can never drift between the screens that use it. The library is drawn once, in dark mode. The scene is drawn into the page as inline SVG and every colour it carries is repainted from the `illustration` theme foundation of `@aziontech/theme` — `--illustration-*` roles that alias the global tokens — so the one export follows light and dark like the rest of the page.

- Import: `import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An empty state, error page, onboarding step, or marketing tile needs a diagrammatic illustration of a product concept (a deploy, a request path, a connected service).
- The same concept appears on more than one screen and must be the same drawing every time.
- The artwork must scale to its container without rasterizing or re-exporting.

## Do

- Leave the illustration decorative (no `ariaLabel`) unless it carries information the surrounding copy does not. A decorative illustration is hidden from assistive tech, which keeps screen readers out of a graphic that adds nothing.
- Size the illustration from the call site with a class. The root is `w-full` at the canvas aspect ratio, so a narrower column simply gets a smaller scene.
- Pick the scene that draws the claim next to it, not the one whose filename matches the page title.
- Find the names in `llms/foundations/illustrations.md` (installed under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/llms/`), the MCP tool `list_assets` (`kind: "illustration"`) or the Assets example. Never guess a name from a file name or a page title: an unknown name renders the placeholder.
- To add a scene, export the frame from the Figma assets library (592×300 for a scene, the tile's own size for a tile or crop), drop the `.svg` into `src/assets/illustrations/`, and register it in `registry.ts`. The test fails while a drawing in the folder is unregistered. Never hand-draw one.
- Leave `<Illustration />` unnamed where a scene is still being drawn: the placeholder frame reserves the space and reads as unfinished on the screen, which is louder than a gap nobody notices.

## Don’t

- A single glyph is enough → use an icon from `@aziontech/icons` (`<i class="ai ai-…">`).
- The artwork is a brand mark (a client logo, a framework mark) → those are brand assets, not illustrations.
- The whole component is "no data here, with a title and an action" → use `empty-state`, which already owns that layout and may embed an `Illustration`.
- The graphic is a live data visualization → that is a chart, not an illustration.
- The scene you need is not in the registry → it has to be drawn in Figma and exported first. Do not approximate it in markup.

## Related

- `empty-state` — the surrounding layout (illustration + title + description + actions); reach for it first and put an `Illustration` inside it.
- `flow` — a real interactive node/edge diagram driven by data; `Illustration` is decorative and static by comparison.
- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder; an illustration is never a loading state.
- svg/azion/*` — drawn brand marks, for artwork that is not part of the illustration library.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | no | Name of an official scene in the illustration asset library. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | no | Accessible name; empty keeps the illustration decorative and hidden from assistive tech. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default` — an illustration is decorative and has no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`, `loading`, or `active` state, and is never interactive.
- Most scenes are drawn on the one 592×300 canvas, so they line up with each other in a grid; a few tiles and crops (`ai-gateway`, `azion-highlight`, `azion-rest-api`, `branches`, `ddos-protection`, `distributed-apis-tile`, `personal-tokens`, `real-time-metrics-error-rate`, `real-time-metrics-status-codes`, `usage-chart`) keep the canvas they were drawn on. The root declares 592×300 as its intrinsic `width`/`height` until the SVG loads, which reserves the box, then the scene's own canvas, and renders at its container's width at that aspect ratio. A call site that wants it smaller caps it with a class.
- A `name` that resolves to no scene — empty, or not in the registry — renders the **placeholder**: a tinted frame reading `PLACE DESIGN ASSET`, marked `data-placeholder`, on the 592×300 canvas. An unregistered `name` also warns in the console, naming where the valid names are listed; neither case throws, and neither collapses the layout. The placeholder is always decorative, `ariaLabel` or not: it draws no scene, so announcing a description of the missing artwork would describe something that is not on the page.
- While a registered scene's SVG is still resolving, the frame already on screen stays — the placeholder never flashes in front of a scene that is about to arrive.
- Theme: each colour of the export palette maps to one `--illustration-*` role (see § Tokens), resolved where the scene renders, so a scene inside a `[data-theme]` subtree follows that subtree. A translucent ground colour is a drop shadow and stays as drawn; colours that read the same in both themes (window controls, framework marks, the dot map) stay as drawn too. Masks, clip paths and filters are never repainted.
- Every instance scopes the SVG's internal ids, so two scenes — or two copies of one — on the same page never resolve each other's gradients, masks or filters.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: _not applicable_ — an illustration is never focusable or interactive, so it declares no focus ring.
- Keyboard map: _none_ — no interactive elements, nothing in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root is an inline `<svg>`. With no `ariaLabel` it carries `aria-hidden="true"` and no role, so assistive tech skips a purely decorative graphic; with an `ariaLabel` it carries `role="img"` and the label as its `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the component declares no text and no colour. An exported scene is decorative shape, not information — no meaning is conveyed by the artwork alone, so the copy beside it must carry the claim.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: _not applicable_ — nothing here is a target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
</script>

<template>
  <Illustration name="modern-frontends" />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/illustration.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/illustration.md).

<!-- components/item.md -->

# Item

> Versatile flex row for title, description, media, and actions. Mirrors the shadcn-vue Item anatomy so consumers can reorder or omit regions. Compose with `ItemGroup` for gapped off-card lists, `ItemList` for divided in-card lists (inside a `Card`), and `ItemSeparator` between rows. Reference: https://www.shadcn-vue.com/docs/components/item (adapted to Webkit tokens and naming).

- Import: `import ItemRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/item-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A row that pairs a title and description with leading media (icon, avatar, image) and trailing actions — settings entries, team members, next steps, notifications.
- A list of such rows: `Item.Group` for gapped rows off a card, `Item.List` for divided rows inside a `card`.
- A whole row that is one link or button — set `as-child` and pass a single `a` / `button` as the item's child.
- A compact option in a chooser list (a workload, a host, an application picked under a search field): `kind="option"` with `as-child` on a `button`. The row is 38 px — `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap, the title at `text-body-md` — and paints `var(--bg-selected)` when the button is `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`.

## Do

- Use `Item.Group` off-card and `Item.List` inside a `card` with `:padded="false"`; both force their child items' `kind` (`inline` in a group, `default` in a list), so do not set `kind` on rows inside them.
- Item.List` draws its own dividers — do not add `Item.Separator` inside it.
- With `as-child`, pass exactly one child element; the row's hover, active and focus ring move onto it, so do not also put buttons inside that row.
- Set `Item.Media` `kind="icon"` for a glyph and `kind="image"` for a picture; the frame sizes and clips the content.
- Use `size="small"` for dense lists; `medium` is the default.
- For the rows of a picker under a search field use `kind="option"` (not `size="small"` plus your own padding): it sets its own density and the selected fill from `aria-pressed` / `aria-selected`, so `size` does not change it. Keep option rows in a plain column, not in `Item.List` or `Item.Group`, which force their own kind.

## Don’t

- Records that share columns and need sorting, selection or paging → use `table`.
- Hierarchical navigation rows in a sidebar → use `menu`.
- A grid of selectable option cards → use `radio-cards`.
- A single surface that frames arbitrary content → use `card`.

## Related

- `card` — the surface an `Item.List` sits in (with `:padded="false"`).
- `table` — columnar data; below `sm`, `listing-table` swaps its table rows for `item` rows.
- `menu` — navigation rows with nesting and drill levels.
- `avatar` — the usual leading media for people rows inside `Item.Media`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'outlined' \| 'muted' \| 'inline' \| 'option'` | `'default'` | false | Item root surface variant. `inline` removes the row's outer padding (transparent surface) for inline placement and divided in-card lists. `option` is a compact chooser row (38 px, title at body-md) that fills when its element is pressed or selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Item root density (padding and gap). |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Merge row layout and interactive-state classes onto the single default-slot child (e.g. anchor). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Every sub-component exposes `default` for its region. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/item-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-separator`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-media`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-actions`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/item-footer`

## Sub-components

- `item.vue` — Root row container (`kind`, `size`).
- `item-group.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) with a gap between rows; for off-card lists.
- `item-list.vue` — Vertical list wrapper (`role="list"`) that draws full-width dividers between rows and no gap; for in-card lists (inside a `Card` with `padded=false`).
- `item-separator.vue` — Horizontal divider between rows in a group.
- `item-media.vue` — Leading media slot (`kind` for icon/image frames).
- `item-content.vue` — Main text column (title + description).
- `item-title.vue` — Primary label line.
- `item-description.vue` — Secondary muted line.
- `item-actions.vue` — Trailing actions cluster.
- `item-header.vue` — Optional top band (e.g.
- `item-footer.vue` — Optional bottom band.

## States

- Visual states on Item shell: `default` only, **except with `asChild`**, where the merged child (the whole-row link/button) gains row-level `hover`, `active`, and `focus-visible`
- Without `asChild`, slotted controls (`Button`, `a`, etc.) own hover, active, and `focus-visible`
- `data-kind` on Item root: `default` | `outlined` | `muted` | `inline` | `option` (an Item inside `ItemGroup` is forced to `inline`; inside `ItemList` to `default`)
- `kind="option"`: `--spacing-xs` block padding, `--spacing-sm` inline padding and gap whatever the `size`, `Item.Title` at `text-body-md`, and `var(--bg-selected)` on the row while it carries `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-selected="true"`
- `data-size` on Item root: `small` | `medium`
- `data-kind` on ItemMedia: `default` | `icon` | `image`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on slotted links and buttons. The Item shell draws no focus ring on its own, except with `asChild`, where the merged focusable child (e.g. an anchor) receives the `focus-visible` ring (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)`) and hover/active feedback.
- Keyboard map: slotted links and buttons supply Tab order; use `asChild` to merge layout onto a single focusable child when the whole row is a link.
- ARIA: `ItemGroup` and `ItemList` use `role="list"` and tell their direct Items, through context, that they are list members; the consumer wires nothing. A member Item renders `role="listitem"` on its root. A member Item with `asChild` renders a `role="listitem"` wrapper (`data-slot="item-listitem"`) around the merged child, so a link row stays a link. An Item outside a list, or nested inside another Item, gets no list role. `ItemSeparator` uses `role="separator"`, and `role="none"` when it sits directly inside a list, where a separator is not an allowed child.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for title and description text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on slotted actions (owned by children).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
</script>

<template>
  <Item>
    <Item.Content>
      <Item.Title>Basic Item</Item.Title>
      <Item.Description>A simple item with title and description.</Item.Description>
    </Item.Content>
    <Item.Actions>
      <Button
        label="Action"
        kind="outlined"
        size="small"
      />
    </Item.Actions>
  </Item>
</template>
```

<!-- components/kbd.md -->

# Kbd

> Kbd renders keyboard input — a single key or a shortcut combination — as a compact, non-interactive keycap. It reads like a real key: a bordered surface with a thicker bottom edge for depth. Modifier keys are passed as boolean props (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl`) and rendered with the correct OS-aware glyph (⌘ on macOS, the catalog's `Ctrl` elsewhere), and named keys (`keyName`) print their localized name, so consumers never hardcode platform symbols or English key names. Use it for shortcut hints in prose, menus, and control suffixes (e.g. the ⌘K hint in `command`).

- Import: `import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show a keyboard shortcut or a single key inline (a ⌘K hint on a search button, an `Esc` hint in a dialog, `/` to focus search).
- Present a modifier combination whose glyph should adapt to the user's OS.

## Do

- Keep the default slot to a single key or glyph (`K`, `7`, `Enter`, `Esc`, `/`); avoid lowercase words or sentences.
- Pass modifiers as boolean props rather than hardcoding `⌘`/`⇧` so the glyph adapts to the OS.
- Name a key with `key-name` (`<Kbd key-name="escape" />`) instead of typing `Esc` or `Enter`: the text comes from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`), so it follows `WebkitProvider` (`Espaço` in pt-BR, `Intro` in es) and a consumer renames it with `messages` (`{ kbd: { ctrl: 'Strg' } }`). The macOS symbols `⌘`, `⌃`, `⌥` and `⇧` are never translated.
- Place surrounding punctuation outside the element, not inside the keycap.

## Don’t

- The token is a status/category label, not a key → use `tag` or `badge`.
- You need an interactive control that fires on click → use `button` / `icon-button`; Kbd is a presentational hint only.

## Related

- `command` — consumes Kbd for its per-item shortcut hints and its ⌘K trigger affordance.
- `badge` — compact non-interactive indicator for counts/status; Kbd is specifically for keyboard keys.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the meta/command modifier glyph (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `ctrl` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Control modifier glyph (⌃ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). |
| `shift` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Shift modifier glyph (⇧). |
| `alt` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prepend the Alt/Option modifier glyph (⌥ on macOS, Alt elsewhere). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a denser keycap for menus, command bars, and table cells. |
| `keyName` | `'ctrl' \| 'alt' \| 'shift' \| 'escape' \| 'enter' \| 'space' \| 'tab' \| 'backspace' \| 'delete'` | `undefined` | false | Named key printed from the locale catalog (`escape` → `Esc`, `enter` → `Enter`); the slot still renders after it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The single key or glyph rendered after any modifier glyphs (`K`, `Enter`, `Esc`). |

## States

Kbd is non-interactive: it has no hover, focus, active, or disabled states and emits no events. Variants are exposed as `data-*` attributes on the root for Tailwind variant styling and for test/Code-Connect hooks:

- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive (no focus, no keyboard, no tab stop).
- Keyboard map: none — Kbd is a presentational hint and exposes no interactive affordance.
- ARIA: the root is the native `<kbd>` element so assistive tech announces it as keyboard input; modifier glyphs render as text so a combination like ⌘K is announced in reading order.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` is theme-guaranteed in both light and dark.
- `motion-reduce:*`: not applicable — Kbd is static (no motion).
- Touch target: not applicable — Kbd is non-interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: modifier symbols (`⌘`, `⌥`, `⇧`) never mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the keycap renders `dir="ltr"`, so a shortcut such as `Ctrl` `K` keeps its order inside right-to-left text; key names come from the locale catalog (`kbd.*`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Kbd from '@aziontech/webkit/kbd'
</script>

<template>
  <Kbd meta>K</Kbd>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/kbd.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/kbd.md).
