<!-- components/key-value-pairs.md -->

# Key Value Pairs

> A grid of labelled facts about one subject: each pair is a key (the term) and its value, which may be plain text or a composed component such as a `Link`, `Tag`, `CopyButton` or `StatusIndicator`. It renders a native description list laid out in 1 to 4 responsive columns, optionally split into titled groups, and owns its loading and empty-value surfaces. It replaces the hand-rolled label/value grids the resource detail templates (`ResourceSummary`, the detail Overview tabs) draw today.

- Import: `import KeyValuePairsRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import KeyValuePairs from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- The facts band of a resource detail or Overview page: ID, status, region, created at, domain.
- A read-only summary of settings before a confirm step (review step, deploy summary).
- Any set of named attributes of a single subject where the reader scans keys to find a value.
- Facts that fall into named clusters (General, Networking, Source) shown side by side as titled columns.
- The rows of a summary card, label on the left and value on the right (a subscription plan: Plan Price, Billing Period, Next Invoice): `kind="split"`.

## Do

- Keep keys short nouns in sentence case ("Created", "Region"), never sentences or trailing colons.
- Order pairs by what the reader looks for first: identity, status, then the rest.
- Pick `kind` by the box: `stacked` (label over value) for a facts band that spans a page; `split` (label at the start, value at the end of one row) for a narrow summary card where each row reads as a line of a receipt. Do not hand-write a `<dl>` with `justify-between` for it.
- Use `columns` for width, not for grouping; use `KeyValuePairs.Group` when the facts form named clusters, one group per column.
- Do not mix bare Items and Groups at the same level; pick one shape per instance.
- Leave the value slot out (or render nothing in it) when a value is absent; the component shows the em dash and its accessible "Not set". Do not type your own "-", "N/A" or "None".
- Put a `CopyButton` after an ID or key, never in place of the visible value.
- Use the `info` slot for a short `Hint` that explains the key; long explanations belong in the page, not in a tooltip.
- Drive `loading` from the data request so the labels stay in place and only the values shimmer.

## Don’t

- Rows of many subjects compared attribute by attribute → use `table`.
- Editable fields → use the form field components (`field` with `input`, `select`, …); this component is read-only.
- A single headline figure with a trend → use `stat-tile`.
- A list of items with no key/value relation → use a plain list or `item`.

## Related

- `table` — many subjects, one row each; KeyValuePairs describes one subject.
- `card` — the surface a KeyValuePairs usually sits in; KeyValuePairs brings no surface of its own.
- `copy-button` — the trailing copy affordance for IDs and keys inside a value.
- `status-indicator`, `tag` — status and category values.
- `link` — a value that navigates (a domain, a linked resource).
- `hint` — the info glyph composed into an Item's `info` slot.
- `skeleton` — rendered in place of each value while the root is `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'stacked' \| 'split'` | `'stacked'` | false | How each pair is laid out: `stacked` puts the label over the value, `split` puts the label at the start and the value at the end of one row. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `1` | false | Columns at full width; fewer columns when a cell would get narrower than `--container-3xs`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Replaces every value with a skeleton while the data loads; labels stay visible. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list when no visible heading names it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | KeyValuePairs.Item` children, or `KeyValuePairs.Group` children — one shape per instance. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs-group`

## Sub-components

The root `key-value-pairs.vue` renders a `<dl>` that is the grid. It provides a context (`injection-key.ts` + `composables/use-key-value-pairs-context.ts`) holding the root test id and the `loading` state, read-only. Every part throws a clear error when used outside `<KeyValuePairs>`.

Markup is valid HTML in both shapes: an Item is a `<div>` wrapping one `<dt>` and one `<dd>` (allowed as a direct child of `<dl>`). A Group is also a `<div>` child of the root `<dl>`: its title is the `<dt>`, and its `<dd>` holds a nested `<dl>` with the group's Items — a term whose description is a list of pairs. A heading element is not used for the group title because `<dt>` does not allow heading content.

- `key-value-pairs.vue` — the root: the `<dl>` grid, the `columns` layout, `aria-label`, `aria-busy`, the context.
- `key-value-pairs-item/key-value-pairs-item.vue` — one pair: `<div>` → `<dt>` (label + `info`) + `<dd>` (value).
  - Props: `label: string` (required — the key, rendered in the `<dt>`).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the value (text or composed components); fallback is the empty-value marker (`<span aria-hidden="true">—</span><span class="sr-only">Not set</span>`), shown when the slot is omitted or renders nothing. `info` — optional affordance after the label text inside the `<dt>`, such as a `Hint`.
  - While the root is `loading`, the `<dd>` renders a `Skeleton` in place of the value; the label stays visible.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}-item`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Item wins.
- `key-value-pairs-group/key-value-pairs-group.vue` — a titled column: `<div>` → `<dt>` (title) + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>` stacking its Items in one column.
  - Props: `title: string` (required — the group's term, shown above its Items).
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the group's `KeyValuePairs.Item` children.
  - Occupies one cell of the root grid, so `columns` sets how many groups sit side by side.
  - `data-testid` fallback `${rootTestId}-group`; a consumer `data-testid` on the Group wins.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`, empty value (per Item)
- `data-kind` on the root and on each Item mirrors `kind`; `split` turns each Item into one row (label start, value end, wrapping under the label only when the value does not fit)
- `data-columns` on the root mirrors `columns` and drives the grid template through `data-[columns=n]:` variants
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `aria-busy="true"` while loading
- Empty value: the Item's `<dd>` shows `—` (`aria-hidden`) plus a visually hidden "Not set"
- Responsive columns follow the list's own box, not the viewport: the grid is `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, max(--container-3xs, share)), 1fr))`, where the share is the box divided by `columns`. It shows `columns` columns when every cell gets at least `--container-3xs` (256 px), fewer otherwise, and one column in a narrow box; a list in a drawer or split view lays out for that box.

- No `disabled`, `invalid`, `readonly`, `error`, `open` states: the component is read-only and fetches nothing. An error loading the facts is the page's surface (e.g. `message`), not this component's.

## Accessibility

- Native description list: root `<dl>`, each Item `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>`; each Group `<div>` → `<dt>` + `<dd>` → nested `<dl>`. Screen readers announce term/definition pairs with no ARIA roles added.
- `ariaLabel` is applied as `aria-label` on the root `<dl>` only when non-empty; when a visible heading precedes the list, the consumer names it with `aria-labelledby` through `$attrs` instead.
- Loading: `aria-busy="true"` on the root; each `Skeleton` is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so assistive tech reads the labels and waits for the values.
- Empty value: `—` is `aria-hidden="true"`; a `sr-only` "Not set" gives the `<dd>` an announced value.
- Keyboard map: the component itself has no tab stop. Focus moves only through interactive values and `info` affordances (`Link`, `CopyButton`, `Hint`) in reading order, each with its own focus ring and key handling.
- Reading order follows source order: row by row across the grid, top to bottom inside a group.
- Contrast: `var(--text-muted)` keys and `var(--text-default)` values at ≥4.5:1 on `var(--bg-surface)` and `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion of its own; the composed `Skeleton` carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`.
- Touch targets belong to the composed interactive values; the component adds none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import KeyValuePairs from '@aziontech/webkit/key-value-pairs'
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <KeyValuePairs aria-label="Workload details">
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Workload ID">
      <span>1752167890</span>
      <CopyButton
        value="1752167890"
        aria-label="Copy workload ID"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Status">
      <StatusIndicator
        severity="success"
        label="Active"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Created">Nov 10, 2026, 14:32</KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Region">US East (Virginia)</KeyValuePairs.Item>
    <KeyValuePairs.Item label="Domain">
      <Link
        label="shop.example.com"
        href="https://shop.example.com"
        size="small"
      />
    </KeyValuePairs.Item>
  </KeyValuePairs>
</template>
```

# Line Figure

> An isometric line-art figure that answers the pointer: one per product (cache TTL, load balancer, DNS lookup, firewall, a 404 page and 20 more), drawn by a small engine into one SVG with the illustration tokens, so it follows the theme. Each figure loads on demand. The pointer, or focus with arrow keys, moves the figure through its answer; `play` walks it through on its own until a person arrives; under reduced motion it holds a still frame. From the design sample's `shared/ui/line-figure` (engine MIT, kept with its `LICENSE`). The figures are marketing assets, listed in the marketing inventory.

- Import: `import LineFigure from '@aziontech/webkit/line-figure'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The art beside a product's copy on a landing or a docs home.
- An empty state or a not-found page (`azion-404`).

## Do

- One figure per view; two figures answering the pointer compete.
- Pass `aria-label` when the page says something more specific than the figure's own description.
- Use `play` only where nothing else moves.
- Take the name from `llms/foundations/line-figures.md` or `list_assets({ kind: "lineFigures" })`; an unknown name draws nothing.
- In a container that sizes to its content (the `EmptyState` `icon` slot, a centred flex column) the figure takes its natural 400×320 size, capped by the space available. Put it in a sized wrapper (`<div class="w-60 max-w-full">`) when the art should be smaller.

## Don’t

- For static, non-interactive art — use `Illustration`.
- For data — use the charts.
- Inside dense application screens.

## Related

- Illustration` — static art from the registry.
- ProductWidget`, `ShellMockup` — product scenes.
- EmptyState` — can carry a figure in its art slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `LineFigureName \| ''` | `''` | false | Registered figure to draw; an unknown or empty name draws nothing. |
| `intensity` | `number` | `0.5` | false | How strongly the figure answers the pointer, from 0 (subtle) to 1 (strong). |
| `play` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Walks the figure through its answer on its own until a pointer or focus arrives; a still frame under reduced motion. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name; falls back to the figure's own English description. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `caption: string` | The figure's current reading each time it changes (the first reading on mount). |

## Assets

- Line figures: every valid name is in line-figures.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "lineFigures" })`). An unknown or empty name draws nothing.

## States

- `data-name` mirrors `name`; `data-play` is present while `play` is on.
- Empty: no role and an empty SVG for an unknown name.

## Accessibility

- `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` or the figure description; the SVG is `aria-hidden`.
- The figure is not a control: it never takes focus on its own, and the page stays operable without it.
- Readings go out through `read`; a page that shows them should put them in a polite live region (see the Play example).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the figure is a picture and is not mirrored (isometric art has no reading direction).
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: the 25 figure descriptions are English asset metadata (like an illustration's name), used only when `ariaLabel` is empty. A localized page passes `aria-label`.

## Responsive

- Fills its width at a 5:4 aspect; strokes stay 1px at every size (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`).
- The SVG is in flow with a natural 400×320 size, so a parent that sizes to its content (a flex column with centred items, the `EmptyState` `icon` slot) gets a 400 px wide figure, never a 0 px one; a narrower container shrinks it, and a sized wrapper sets another size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import LineFigure from '@aziontech/webkit/line-figure'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="max-w-(--container-sm)">
    <LineFigure name="cache-ttl" />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/network-map.md -->

# Network Map

> A decorative, full-bleed layer that paints the dotted world map with Azion's PoPs lit in the brand accent. It is a material — it takes no content and claims no space — but unlike a static illustration it is tuned by the consumer (region, PoP density, landmass opacity, static or animated) to sit behind a band's copy.

- Import: `import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- As the backdrop of a band whose subject is the network (reach, data centers, latency, resilience), composed as a sibling under the band's copy inside a positioned, clipping ancestor.
- When a band is about one part of the network, so only that region's PoPs should light (`region`) while the whole world stays drawn.
- When the same artwork has to read with more or fewer PoPs lit, or with none at all (`density="none"`), from one component instead of separate exports.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative overflow-hidden`); it fills that box and nothing else.
- Never offset or resize the layer with utilities (`left-*`, `w-*`, `inset-*`). It always fills its positioned ancestor, and `position` + `fade` place the map inside that box — so a fade measures from the band's own edges. An offset box moves the fade's edges off the band's and makes the two placements fight.
- To make the map smaller or larger inside its box, set `scale` instead of resizing the layer. The map shrinks toward its `position` corner, so there is no hard edge and the fade keeps measuring from the band's edges.
- Keep `opacity` low (the default `0.4`) when copy sits over the landmass; the PoPs keep full strength so the network still reads.
- For copy on one side of a band, park the map on the other side with `position` and fade it toward the copy (`position="right"` + `fade="left"`); the default stops need no consumer class.
- Tune where a fade holds and ends with `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` only when the default stops do not fit, instead of adding masks.
- Leave `animated` off by default; turn it on for the one band per page whose subject is the network.
- To nudge the map or let it run off the band, set `offsetX` / `offsetY` (for example `:offset-x="0.15"` to bleed right, `:offset-y="-0.1"` to bleed up) instead of offsetting the layer.
- asia` and `oceania` hold no PoPs — the artwork carries no accent field there — so either region lights none and the map reads as landmass alone.

## Don’t

- For a real node/edge diagram driven by data → use `flow`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it.

## Related

- `frame-box` — the ruled box a network band usually sits in; it supplies the positioned, clipping ancestor.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | `'world' \| 'atlantic' \| 'americas' \| 'north-america' \| 'south-america' \| 'europe' \| 'africa' \| 'asia' \| 'oceania'` | `'world'` | false | Which part of the world has its PoPs lit; the map always frames the whole world. |
| `density` | `'none' \| 'low' \| 'medium' \| 'high'` | `'medium'` | false | How many PoPs are lit, from `none` to `high`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pulses the PoPs in three staggered waves; static when false. |
| `opacity` | `number` | `0.4` | false | Opacity of the landmass dots, from 0 to 1; the PoPs stay at full strength. |
| `position` | `'center' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'top-left' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'center'` | false | Where the map parks in the space the box leaves over. |
| `scale` | `number` | `0.85` | false | Size of the map relative to the box; 1 fits it, below 1 shrinks it toward its position, above 1 enlarges it. |
| `offsetX` | `number` | `0` | false | Horizontal shift as a fraction of the map width; negative moves it left, positive right, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `offsetY` | `number` | `0` | false | Vertical shift as a fraction of the map height; negative moves it up, positive down, past the box edge if large enough. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the map out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |
| `traffic` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draws traffic between lit PoPs: faint links and, while `animated`, packets that cross them; the links alone under reduced motion. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-region`, `data-density` and `data-fade` on the root mirror their props; `data-fade` drives the mask that fades the layer out
- `density="none"` draws the landmass alone, with no hole where a PoP would be — every PoP cell is also a landmass cell
- `density` levels are cumulative: `low` (65 PoPs) ⊂ `medium` (186) ⊂ `high` (275); `core` carries a PoP on every main Brazilian capital, so they light at every density
- Each PoP path carries `data-animated` (present only when `animated` is set) and `data-phase` (`0` / `1` / `2`), which select the pulse and its wave delay
- The map always frames the whole world; `region` only chooses which PoPs light — a PoP renders when its cell falls inside the region's bounds, and a phase with no PoP left renders no path
- `scale` sizes the map around the `position` anchor, so it renders at that fraction of its fitted size while the anchored edge stays put; a value of 0 or below falls back to `1`
- `offsetX` / `offsetY` translate the map after `position` and `scale` place it, by that fraction of the map's own width / height; the sign is the direction (negative left / up, positive right / down), so each axis moves independently of the anchor
- The default `scale` of `0.85` leaves room on both axes, so every `position` moves the map in any box shape. At `1` the fitted map fills one axis edge to edge, so `position` acts only on the other axis: `top` / `center` / `bottom` render alike in a wide box, and `left` / `center` / `right` in a tall one
- `top` / `bottom` / `left` / `right` fade the map out toward that edge: full ink from the opposite edge up to `--network-map-fade-start`, zero at `--network-map-fade-end`, both measured from the opposite edge. `top` / `bottom` default to 16% / 55%; `left` / `right` default to 50% / 80%, which clears a copy column on that side of a band
- Custom properties tune the fade in place, set from the consumer's class: `--network-map-fade-start` / `--network-map-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero)

## Accessibility

- Decorative: the root is `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events-none`; the network's claims are carried by the band's copy, never by the artwork
- Keyboard map: none — the layer is not focusable and has no interactive parts
- Visible focus: not applicable (nothing receives focus)
- Contrast: not applicable to the artwork (decorative); the copy above it keeps its own ≥4.5:1 against the band, which the low default `opacity` protects
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` stops the pulse under reduced motion
- Touch target: not applicable (no interactive parts)

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import NetworkMap from '@aziontech/webkit/network-map'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <NetworkMap
      region="world"
      density="medium"
      :opacity="0.4"
      position="center"
      :scale="0.85"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/network-map.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/network-map.md).

<!-- components/overflow-count.md -->

# Overflow Count

> A small `+N` chip that stands for the items a slot cannot show, and opens a popover with the whole list. It replaces the design sample's `DomainOverflowPopover`, the overflow badge of `TagListCell` and `WorkloadCell`, and the Console Kit's `OverflowCountButton`. The popover follows the overflow rule of `webkit-ux-heuristics`: a summary line (`12 domains`, `10 of 34 domains` while paged), a search box once the list holds more than 7 items, a scrolling list, a **Load N more** footer while items remain, a no-match line quoting the query, and a polite status region that announces the summary. Closing it clears the query and the paging.

- Import: `import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A table cell or a detail row shows the first value of a list and the rest hide behind a count: the domains of a workload, the tags of a row, the workloads a rule applies to.
- A card or a header names one item of many and the reader may want the full list without leaving the screen.

## Do

- Show the first item (or as many as fit) beside the chip; the chip counts only the hidden ones, and `items` passes only those.
- Name the items with `noun` (`{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }`) so the summary reads `12 domains`, not `12 items`.
- Give an item an `href` only when it opens something; an item without one renders as plain text.
- Use the `item` slot for a router link or a richer entry; keep every entry to one truncating line.

## Don’t

- The list is the content of the page → render it as a `Table` or an `Item` list.
- The reader picks from the list → use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MultiSelect`.
- A single count without a list behind it → use `Badge`.

## Related

- `table` — `Table.CellTags` and `Table.CellLink` put this chip after the values they fit.
- `tag` — the chip is a small secondary `Tag`.
- `popover` — the list opens in a `Popover`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Array<string \| { label: string; href?: string }>` | `[]` | false | The hidden items. The chip reads `+<length>`; an item with `href` opens in a new tab. |
| `noun` | `string \| { one: string; other: string }` | `undefined` | false | What the items are, for the summary and the trigger's name. Empty uses the catalog (`item` / `items`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` |  | One list entry; replaces the built-in text or link. |

## States

- `data-state` on the trigger: `open` | `closed` (from `Popover`).
- Search shows when `items` holds more than 7 entries; Load more shows while entries beyond the loaded batches (10 per batch) match.
- Empty `items` renders nothing.

## Accessibility

- The trigger is a button named `Show all <count> <noun>` (the visible `+N` alone does not say what it counts); `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from `Popover`.
- Keyboard: `Enter`/`Space` opens, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the chip, `Tab` moves through the search box, the links and Load more.
- A polite `role="status"` region announces the summary after a search or Load more.
- A link that opens a new tab carries a visually hidden `(opens in a new tab)`.
- Contrast: the secondary `Tag` and the muted summary meet 4.5:1 in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the external-link glyph sits at the inline end.
- Icons: `pi-external-link` and `pi-search` are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: each entry is wrapped in `dir="auto"` so a domain keeps its order inside right-to-left text.

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `overflowCount.noun`     | `item` / `items` (plural)   | `noun`        |
| `overflowCount.summary`  | `{count} {noun}`            | —             |
| `overflowCount.paged`    | `{shown} of {count} {noun}` | —             |
| `overflowCount.showAll`  | `Show all {count} {noun}`   | —             |
| `overflowCount.search`   | `Search`                    | —             |
| `overflowCount.noMatch`  | `Nothing matches “{query}”` | —             |
| `overflowCount.loadMore` | `Load {count} more`         | —             |
| `overflowCount.newTab`   | `(opens in a new tab)`      | —             |

- Formatting: counts go through the locale's number format.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the popover is `width="small"` (`--container-xs`).
- Narrow: the popover keeps its width and flips to fit (from `Popover`).
- Touch: the chip sits in a 24 px row; the popover entries are 28 px tall with their own padding.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import OverflowCount from '@aziontech/webkit/overflow-count'

  const domains = ['shop.example.com', 'api.example.com', 'img.example.com', 'docs.example.com']
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) min-w-0 items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
    <a
      :href="`https://${domains[0]}`"
      target="_blank"
      rel="noopener noreferrer"
      class="min-w-0 truncate text-body-sm text-(--text-default) underline-offset-2 hover:underline"
      >{{ domains[0] }}</a
    >
    <OverflowCount
      :items="domains.slice(1).map((label) => ({ label, href: `https://${label}` }))"
      :noun="{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/overline.md -->

# Overline

> Overline is the short uppercase label set above a headline to name the section, panel or group it opens (the "eyebrow"). It renders its default slot in `.text-overline-md` in the brand primary color, optionally behind a preset code-style prefix (`//`, `<>`, `</>`) and followed by a blinking terminal-style cursor. It is purely presentational text with no interaction; the marketing headers (`section-title`, `hero-title`, `call-to-action`, `media-split`, `ticker`) and several page sections render their eyebrow (the `eyebrow` prop, or `label` on `ticker`) through it.

- Import: `import Overline from '@aziontech/webkit/overline'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Name a section, panel or column group with one or two words set above its headline.
- Build a custom marketing header that must match the eyebrow treatment of `section-title` and `hero-title` (the `//` prefix and the blinking cursor).
- Label a band inside a page section (a comparison group, a closing panel) with the same uppercase code-style mark.

## Do

- Keep the label to one or two words: it is set uppercase and, with the default `single-line`, stays on one line whenever it fits its container.
- Turn `single-line` off only when the label can be longer than its container (narrow columns, translated copy); the label then wraps under `text-pretty`, which avoids a lone word on the last line.
- Use a `prefix` from the preset set only (`//`, `<>`, `</>`); the prefix is decorative and hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`), so never put meaning in it.
- Use `show-cursor` for one eyebrow per view at most; the blink stops under reduced motion.
- Keep the semantic heading in the element after the Overline; the Overline itself carries no heading role.

## Don’t

- The header has a headline, description and actions → use `section-title` (or `hero-title` for the hero), which already renders its `eyebrow` through Overline.
- The text is a status, count or category attached to an item → use `tag` or `badge`.
- The text is the heading itself → use a real heading element; Overline renders a `div` and is not a heading.
- The text is a keyboard shortcut → use `kbd`.
- The text is a field label → use `label`.

## Related

- `section-title` — the framed section header; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline with `prefix="//"` and `show-cursor`.
- hero-title` — the hero copy block; renders its `eyebrow` as an Overline closed by the cursor, with `single-line` turned off.
- `tag` — a compact label attached to an item, not a heading companion.
- `badge` — a compact count or status indicator.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `singleLine` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Keeps the prefix unbroken and the label on one line while it fits; a longer label wraps instead of overflowing. |
| `showCursor` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a blinking terminal-style cursor after the label. |
| `prefix` | `'' \| '//' \| '<>' \| '</>'` | `''` | false | Preset prefix rendered before the label; empty renders no prefix. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The label text, rendered uppercase in the brand primary color. |

## States

- Static: no hover, focus, active or disabled states; the root is a non-interactive `div`.
- Prefix: a `span` before the label is rendered only when `prefix` is not empty; it carries `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Cursor: a `span` after the label is rendered only when `showCursor` is set; the root drops its end padding (`pr-0`) while the cursor is shown and keeps `pr-(--spacing-xxs)` otherwise.
- Wrapping: with `singleLine` (default) the prefix carries `whitespace-nowrap` and the label sits on one line because the root is `w-fit`; it wraps (with `text-pretty`) only when the container is narrower than the label. With it off the prefix may wrap too.
- Attributes (including `class`) are forwarded to the root `div` (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- Test ids: root `content-overline` (consumer `data-testid` wins).
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container, and a label that does not fit wraps instead of overflowing at any width, at 200% zoom and with translated copy (no viewport breakpoint involved).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the component renders no focusable element.
- Keyboard map: none; the component is not interactive.
- ARIA: no role; the root is a plain `div` and the label is read as text. The prefix `span` is decorative and carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so only the label is announced; the cursor `span` is empty and contributes no text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text): the label uses `var(--text-primary)` (`primary-700` in light, 4.77:1 or more on every light surface; `primary-500` in dark) and the prefix `var(--text-default)` on the surface the consumer places it on.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the cursor's `animate-blink`.
- Touch target: not applicable (non-interactive).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Overline from '@aziontech/webkit/overline'
</script>

<template>
  <Overline>OVERLINE TEXT</Overline>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/overline.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/overline.md).

# Payment Brand

> The card-brand plate shown beside a payment card: a small bordered plate with the network's mark (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Diners Club, JCB, Discover, Elo, Hipercard, UnionPay) drawn in one colour in theme tokens, so it reads in light, dark and forced colors without a raster image or a brand hex. It replaces the design sample's `CardBrandMark` (a Visa plate on a hard-coded blue fill), the Console Kit's `card-flag-block` (six colored SVG logos) and the inline Visa SVG the account blocks repeated. A brand it does not draw (Maestro, Hiper, or any unknown value) shows a generic card glyph and keeps the brand's name for assistive technology.

- Import: `import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A payment method row, a checkout summary or a billing table names the card on file: the plate sits before `Ending in 4242` or `Visa •••• 4242`.
- A list of saved cards where the brand helps the reader tell them apart.

## Do

- Pass the brand as the payment API returns it; the plate normalizes `American Express`, `american_express`, `Diners Club` and casing.
- When the row text already says the brand (`Visa •••• 4242`), set `decorative` so the name is not read twice; when the text says only `Ending in 4242`, leave the plate named.
- Keep the plate at `medium` in rows and forms, `small` inside dense tables.

## Don’t

- The Azion logo → use `Brand`.
- A partner or integration logo (Git providers, clouds) → use the product's logo asset or an `Avatar`.
- A status or category of the card (expired, default) → use `Tag` beside the plate.

## Related

- `brand` — the same idea for the Azion lockup: an inline mark, sized by token.
- `tag` — put `Default` or `Expired` next to the plate, not inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `string` | `''` | false | The card network as the payment API names it (`visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, `American Express`, `diners`, `jcb`, `discover`, `elo`, `hipercard`, `unionpay`…). Unknown values draw the generic card glyph. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Plate size: `small` 20 × 32 px for dense tables, `medium` 28 × 40 px for rows and forms. |
| `label` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Accessible name. Empty uses the brand's name (`Visa`), or the catalog's `Card` for an unknown brand. |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Hide the plate from assistive technology when the text next to it already names the brand. |

## States

- `data-brand` on the root: `visa` | `mastercard` | `amex` | `diners` | `jcb` | `discover` | `elo` | `hipercard` | `unionpay` | `unknown`.
- `data-size`: `small` | `medium`.
- `data-glyph`: `mark` when the brand has a drawn mark, `generic` otherwise.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `label` or the brand's name; with `decorative` it is `aria-hidden="true"` and has no role.
- The SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the plate takes no focus.
- Contrast: the mark is `--text-default` on `--bg-surface` (above 4.5:1 in both themes); forced colors draw it in `CanvasText` because it uses `currentColor`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the plate is symmetric; no logical spacing inside it.
- Icons: brand marks are not mirrored (they are logos).
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                    | English source | Override prop |
| ---------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `paymentBrand.unknown` | `Card`         | `label`       |

- Brand names (`Visa`, `Mastercard`, `American Express`, `Diners Club`, `JCB`, `Discover`, `Elo`, `Hipercard`, `UnionPay`) are trademarks and are not translated.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: fixed size; `shrink-0` so a row never squeezes it.
- Touch: not interactive.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PaymentBrand from '@aziontech/webkit/payment-brand'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <PaymentBrand brand="visa" />
    <span class="text-label-md text-(--text-default)">Ending in 4242</span>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/product-widget.md -->

# Product Widget

> Draws one of the **official console widgets**: a scaled, inert mock of an Azion Console screen or fragment, built from real webkit components inside a `shell-mockup` frame, that marketing bands use to show the product. `name` selects the widget from a closed registry of 70 drawings, loaded on demand, so a page can only render mocks that already exist and the same screen is the same drawing on every page that shows it. The remaining props pass through to the widget that declares them, and a widget that does not declare one keeps its own value.

- Import: `import ProductWidget from '@aziontech/webkit/product-widget'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A product band (hero, media split, feature tab, widget grid cell) needs to show a console screen or a fragment of one.
- The same console screen appears on more than one page and must be the same drawing on each.
- Several widgets share one slot (tabs), and only the one showing should play: drive `active` from the host.
- A grid cell plays its fragment's beat while the pointer is over it: drive `hover` from the host.

## Do

- Give the host a size (a height or an aspect ratio). A widget fills its host and scales its design width to fit.
- Host a framed widget (a full screen) in a wide panel, and a fragment in a grid cell with its own padding. A bare fragment floats on the cell's surface and a framed one fades its window into it, so set `--mockup-fade-color` on the cell when it is not `--bg-canvas`. The cell clips on both axes (`overflow-clip`, as a media split's media cell does): a fragment's collaborator cursor and shadows float onto the cell's padding, and at a large root font size (200% zoom) its mock text outgrows the drawing; clipping them at the cell's border keeps the page from scrolling sideways. Never frame a fragment with `overflow-x-visible`.
- Leave `kind`, `chrome`, `width`, `tab` and `interval` unset unless the host needs a different value: unset keeps the widget's own.
- Leave a fragment's plating to the registry. Each fragment has its own default: a form or a list that reads as a console screen is framed in a console window titled with its module, and a fragment that draws its own card, terminal or code panel is bare, because a window around it would be a window in a window. Set `kind` only when the host needs the other plating, and `chrome` to drop the window's console bar. `width` and `fade` re-plate only the workload screens listed under Props; a fragment keeps its own design width and fade, and the root warns in development when a prop is set on a widget that does not read it.
- Turn `cursor` off when the widget stands for a screen the reader uses alone. Fragments act their beat with a named collaborator cursor; that is right in a feature grid that plays on hover, and a fake second person in a product band that reads as a screenshot.
- Keep the copy beside the widget saying what it shows. Every widget but `function-code` and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` is hidden from assistive technology.

## Don’t

- The screen you need is not in the registry → compose it with `shell-mockup` and its parts, then add it to the registry. Do not approximate it at the call site.
- A live, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`.
- A static product concept drawing → use `illustration`.
- A screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.

## Related

- `shell-mockup` — the frame every widget is drawn in; reach for it directly to compose a new screen.
- `illustration` — the same closed-registry pattern for static scenes.
- `texture-material` — the texture a full-screen widget grounds itself with through `texture`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `'ai-inference-function' \| 'ai-inference-model' \| 'ai-inference-template' \| 'application-accelerator-cookie' \| 'application-accelerator-method' \| 'application-accelerator-query-string' \| 'application-cache' \| 'application-function' \| 'application-rule' \| 'application-version' \| 'applications-create-method' \| 'applications-device-group' \| 'applications-rule-phases' \| 'bot-manager-metrics' \| 'bot-manager-rule' \| 'bot-manager-traffic' \| 'cli-terminal-deploy' \| 'cli-terminal-start' \| 'data-stream-connector' \| 'data-stream-sampling' \| 'data-stream-source' \| 'ddos-firewall-modules' \| 'ddos-http-events' \| 'ddos-requests-metric' \| 'edge-dns-dnssec' \| 'edge-dns-nameserver' \| 'edge-dns-record' \| 'firewall-function' \| 'firewall-modules' \| 'firewall-rules-order' \| 'function-code' \| 'functions-start' \| 'image-processor-events' \| 'image-processor-module' \| 'image-processor-rule' \| 'kv-store-function' \| 'kv-store-key' \| 'kv-store-security-list' \| 'load-balancer-address' \| 'load-balancer-method' \| 'load-balancer-origins' \| 'network-shield-ip-list' \| 'network-shield-lists' \| 'network-shield-rule' \| 'object-storage-access' \| 'object-storage-browser' \| 'object-storage-buckets' \| 'real-time-events-filter' \| 'real-time-events-log' \| 'real-time-events-volume' \| 'real-time-metrics-dashboard' \| 'real-time-metrics-filter' \| 'real-time-metrics-panel' \| 'sql-database-query' \| 'sql-database-row' \| 'sql-database-table' \| 'waf-allowed-rule' \| 'waf-firewall-rule' \| 'waf-threat' \| 'workload-deploy' \| 'workload-deploy-logs' \| 'workload-deployments' \| 'workload-domain' \| 'workload-domains' \| 'workload-overview' \| 'workload-rollout-rows' \| 'workload-topology-chain' \| 'workload-topology' \| 'workload-topology-flow' \| 'workloads-list'` | `—` | true | Name of the console widget to draw. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether this widget is the one showing; it replays its entrance each time it becomes active. |
| `hover` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the pointer is over the host; a fragment plays its beat while it is. |
| `kind` | `'window' \| 'bare'` | `undefined` | false | How the widget is plated (window or bare): a workload screen re-plates its own frame, a fragment is drawn bare or framed in a console window, and unset keeps the widget's own plating. |
| `chrome` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Draws the console bar on a workload screen or on the window a framed fragment is drawn in; unset keeps the widget's own bar, and a bare fragment ignores it. |
| `width` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Design width of a workload screen from md up; fragments keep their own width, and unset keeps the widget's own. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'y'` | `'none'` | false | Edge a workload screen, workload-overview or application-version fades out along; fragments keep their own fade. |
| `texture` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Texture a full-screen widget is grounded with. |
| `tab` | `'agents' \| 'console' \| 'cli' \| 'overview' \| 'topology' \| 'deploy' \| 'main-settings' \| 'cache-settings' \| 'device-groups' \| 'functions' \| 'rules-engine'` | `undefined` | false | Tab a tabbed widget plays (`workload-overview`, `application-version`, `functions-start`); other widgets ignore it, and unset plays the first tab. |
| `cursor` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the named collaborator cursor a fragment acts its beat with; turn it off for a still console picture. Widgets without a cursor ignore it. |
| `interval` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Milliseconds between revealed log lines in the deploy logs widget; unset keeps its own pace. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` only. A widget is decorative: no `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled` or `loading` state of its own. `hover` and `active` are triggers the host drives, not states the root renders.
- Every widget is drawn in an inert `shell-mockup`, except `function-code`, whose frame is `interactive` so the viewer can switch its file tabs and copy its code. `functions-start` draws `function-code` on its `console` tab, and on its `agents` tab a `toggle-group` above its inert frame that switches the coding agent.
- `cli-terminal-start` and `cli-terminal-deploy` play a recorded Azion CLI session (init to curl, or link and deploy); `workload-topology-flow` draws domains, a workload and its bindings joined by `flow` connectors, with the workload ringed in the primary glow.
- `data-name` mirrors `name` on the root, and `data-kind` mirrors a fragment's plating (`window` or `bare`, the registry default when `kind` is unset); a workload screen leaves `data-kind` off the root. The window around a framed fragment carries `data-testid="<root testid>__frame"` and its body `<root testid>__frame-body`.
- Loading: the widget's code is loaded on demand, and the plating registry with the window part beside it. The root keeps its size while it loads and draws nothing until the widget (and its window) arrives, so a framed fragment is never drawn bare first. A `name` change clears the current widget at once, so the root never shows the earlier widget under the new `data-name`, whether the new load is still in flight or has failed.
- A `name` outside the registry (from untyped code), or a widget chunk that fails to load, warns in development only (`import.meta.env.DEV`) and leaves the root empty; it never throws.
- A plating prop the loaded widget does not read warns in development only, once per load, and changes nothing.
- `cursor` off: no collaborator cursor or name tag is drawn; the fragment's controls still open, highlight and settle on their beat.
- Each widget owns its entrance (a `shell-mockup` replay when `active` turns on) and, for fragments, its beat while `hover` is set or the device cannot hover. Under reduced motion every widget is drawn in its settled state.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none in an inert widget, where nothing takes focus. In `function-code` the code block's file tabs and copy button keep their own focus rings, and the coding-agent switch of `functions-start` keeps the segmented button's.
- Keyboard map: none in an inert widget. In `function-code`, `Tab` reaches the code block's file tabs and copy button, which keep their own keyboard behaviour. In `functions-start` on its `agents` tab, `Tab` reaches the coding-agent switch, which keeps the segmented button's arrow-key behaviour.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div`; the widget inside is a `figure` with `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` (except `function-code`), and so is the window around a framed fragment, so assistive technology skips the picture. The coding-agent switch of `functions-start` sits outside that figure, named `Coding agent`. The band's own copy carries what it shows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): widgets use the console's own text and surface pairs (`var(--text-default)` / `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` / `var(--bg-surface)`).
- Every motion class inside a widget pairs with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target: not applicable in an inert widget; `function-code` keeps the code block's own targets, and `functions-start` the segmented button's.
- Reflow: the workload-topology node header wraps (`flex-wrap`), so a status tag moves under the node name in a narrow frame instead of overflowing it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: every chevron and angle inside the widget fragments mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), the pagination angles included.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: domains, IDs and code samples in the mock data keep their own direction.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings in the root. Widget text is console UI copy drawn as part of the picture (hidden from assistive technology), and the collaborator names on the cursors are mock data.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; every widget scales its design width to fit its host (`shell-mockup`), with a narrower design width below `md`. A framed fragment scales once: the window scales to the host, and the fragment inside measures the window body's layout width (untransformed), not its scaled box.
- Narrow: the host sets the size; the widget scales down with it.
- Touch: a fragment shows its finished beat on a device that cannot hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll; the frame scales instead. A bare fragment's decorative overflow (cursor, mock text grown by a 200% root font) is clipped by its host cell, never by the page; the Library example's cells clip, and `src/test/reflow.test.ts` checks it on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ProductWidget from '@aziontech/webkit/product-widget'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="h-96 w-full">
    <ProductWidget name="workloads-list" />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/product-widget.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/product-widget.md).

<!-- components/qr-code.md -->

# Qr Code

> A QR code drawn as SVG from a string, with no image request and no dependency: WebKit's own encoder (byte mode, UTF-8, versions 1–40, error correction L/M/Q/H) turns the value into modules, and the component draws them as one path. It is for setup flows that hand a URI to a phone, first the `otpauth://` URI of an authenticator app in `auth#MfaSetup`, where it replaces the image the API returned and the framed placeholder of the demo. The code is always dark on a light plate (the plate pins the light theme), because several authenticator scanners do not read an inverted code.

- Import: `import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A phone has to pick up a value the screen shows: an authenticator `otpauth://` URI, a pairing link, a short download URL.
- Next to a typed alternative: the same value (or its secret) as text with a `CopyButton`, for people who cannot scan.

## Do

- Always give the code a typed alternative next to it: the setup key or the link as text.
- Name the code after what it does (`QR code to add jane.doe@example.com to an authenticator app`), not `QR code`.
- Keep the default `M` error correction; raise it only when the code is printed or shown small.

## Don’t

- The value is only for reading or copying on the same device → show it as text with `CopyButton`.
- A brand or partner logo → use `Brand` or the partner's asset.
- A long payload (over a few hundred characters) → link to it; a dense code is hard to scan from a screen.

## Related

- `copy-button` — the typed alternative beside the code.
- `otp-input` — the 6-digit code the app shows after the scan.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | The text the code carries (a URI, a key), encoded as UTF-8 bytes. |
| `label` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Accessible name of the image. Empty uses the catalog's `QR code`; name it after what the scan does. |
| `errorCorrection` | `'L' \| 'M' \| 'Q' \| 'H'` | `'M'` | false | Error-correction level: `L` 7 %, `M` 15 %, `Q` 25 %, `H` 30 % of the code can be lost and still read. Higher levels make denser codes. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Rendered width: `small` 128 px, `medium` 160 px, `large` 224 px, quiet zone included. |

## States

- `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`.
- `data-version` on the root: the QR version the encoder picked (1–40); `data-modules`: the module count per side.
- An empty value draws no code: the plate keeps its size and `data-version` is absent. A value too long for version 40 at the chosen level draws no code either and logs one warning.

## Accessibility

- The root is `role="img"` named by `label` (catalog `QR code` when empty); the SVG inside is `aria-hidden` and not focusable; the code takes no focus.
- The code is never the only way: the page puts the value or its secret beside it as text.
- Contrast: dark modules on a light plate in both themes (the plate sets `data-theme="light"`); `forced-color-adjust: none` keeps the code dark on light in forced colors, so a scanner still reads it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the code is never mirrored (`dir="ltr"` on the SVG); the plate is symmetric.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: the value is not shown as text by the component.

## Internationalization

| Key            | English source | Override prop |
| -------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `qrCode.label` | `QR code`      | `label`       |

- The value is encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so non-Latin text works; most authenticator URIs are ASCII.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none.
- Narrow: fixed size; `shrink-0`; `max-w-full` so it never overflows a 320 px column.
- Touch: not interactive.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CopyButton from '@aziontech/webkit/copy-button'
  import QrCode from '@aziontech/webkit/qr-code'

  const account = 'jane.doe@example.com'
  const secret = 'JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'
  const uri = `otpauth://totp/Azion:${encodeURIComponent(account)}?secret=${secret}&issuer=Azion`
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-md)">
    <QrCode
      :value="uri"
      :label="`QR code to add ${account} to an authenticator app`"
    />
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-xxs)">
      <p class="text-label-sm text-(--text-default)">Can't scan the code?</p>
      <div class="flex items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
        <code
          class="text-label-code text-(--text-default)"
          dir="ltr"
          >{{ secret.match(/.{1,4}/g).join(' ') }}</code
        >
        <CopyButton
          :value="secret"
          aria-label="Copy setup key"
          copied-label="Setup key copied"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/severity-tag.md -->

# Severity Tag

> SeverityTag labels an item with its place on an ordered severity scale: critical, high, medium, low or info. The level reads from a four-bar glyph, where the filled bars count the level, and from the label, so two levels never depend on colour alone to differ. It differs from `tag`, whose `severity` prop is a colour tone (success, warning, danger) with no order between values.

- Import: `import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Show how severe an alert, finding, detection, incident or vulnerability is, in a table cell, a list row or a detail header.
- Rank items on a fixed five-step scale where critical and high must stay visibly distinct.

## Do

- Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `WebkitProvider`) so the text always names the level; override `label` only when the product glossary names the level differently.
- Use one SeverityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
- Do not pair the tag with a toned `tag` for the same level; the glyph and the ramp already carry it.

## Don’t

- The value is an outcome or a status with no order (allowed, blocked, healthy) → use `tag`.
- The value is a count or a one-word indicator on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove the value (a severity filter) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `tag` — a toned status or category label; use it for outcomes and states, not for an ordered level.
- `badge` — a dense count or short-label indicator.
- `chip` — an interactive or removable token, for severity filters.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'critical' \| 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low' \| 'info'` | `'info'` | false | Severity level; sets how many glyph bars fill, their colour and the default label. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Replaces the label text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (static, non-interactive)
- `data-severity` mirrors the `severity` prop: `critical` | `high` | `medium` | `low` | `info`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium`
- Filled bars per level: critical 4, high 3, medium 2, low 1, info 0

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not focusable; the tag is static text and takes no `tabindex`.
- Keyboard map: none; the tag has no interaction.
- ARIA: the glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`; the visible text names the level, so the tag needs no `role` or `aria-label`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the label (`var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`) and ≥3:1 for every filled bar on `var(--bg-canvas)` in both themes.
- No motion, so no `motion-reduce:*` fallback is needed.
- Touch target: not applicable; the tag is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <SeverityTag
    severity="info"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/severity-tag.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/severity-tag.md).

<!-- components/shell-mockup.md -->

# Shell Mockup

> A scaled, inert picture of an Azion Console screen, for marketing bands that show the product. The consumer composes the screen's body from real webkit components at a fixed design width; the frame draws the console shell around it (the slim console bar, the side rail with breadcrumbs and actions, or the previous console's top bar) and scales the whole drawing to fit its host. Each piece of the body is a `ShellMockup.Part` that travels in on its own beat once the mockup scrolls into view, so the screen assembles itself instead of appearing all at once.

- Import: `import ShellMockupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import ShellMockup from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Showing a console screen or fragment on a marketing band: a hero, a media split, a feature tab, a widget grid cell.
- Depicting a product workflow with real webkit controls instead of a screenshot, so the drawing follows the theme and stays sharp at any size.
- Staggering the parts of a mock so they arrive in reading order when the band scrolls into view, and replaying that entrance each time a tab makes the mock active.
- Drawing only a fragment of a screen (a list, a form row) floating on the band's own surface, with `kind="bare"` and `chrome` off.

## Do

- Compose the body at the design width (`width`, `mobileWidth`), not at the host's width; the frame scales the drawing, so sizes inside are design pixels.
- Give the host a height (or an aspect ratio); the frame fills its host and derives its design height from it.
- Number parts in reading order with `order`, starting at `0`; parts on the same beat land together.
- Keep the mockup decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology unless `interactive` is set, so the band's own copy must say what the picture shows.
- Set `active` from the host when several mockups share one slot (tabs), so only the visible one plays and it replays when it returns.
- Tune a fade with the consumer-side custom properties `--mockup-fade-start` / `--mockup-fade-end` (or `--mockup-fade-edge` for `y`) and match its color to the host surface with `--mockup-fade-color`.

## Don’t

- To show a real, working screen at a device size → use `browser-frame`; it renders live content in a true viewport, not a scaled picture.
- For a static screenshot or clip in documentation → use `doc-frame`.
- For an illustration scene → use `illustration`.

## Related

- `browser-frame` — a live, resizable viewport for real screens; `shell-mockup` is an inert, scaled drawing of the console.
- `texture-material` — the texture the frame grounds itself with when `texture` is set.
- `frame-box` — the page's registration frame a mockup band is often placed inside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'window' \| 'bare'` | `'window'` | false | How the mockup is plated: a bordered console window, or bare parts floating on the host's surface. |
| `shell` | `'console' \| 'legacy'` | `'console'` | false | Console generation the shell draws: the current one, or the previous one with its top bar. |
| `width` | `number` | `860` | false | Design width of the frame from `md` up; the frame scales to fit its host. |
| `mobileWidth` | `number` | `390` | false | Design width of the frame below `md`. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'y'` | `'none'` | false | Edge the mockup fades out along; `y` fades top and bottom. |
| `chrome` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the console bar over the body. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Module label on the console bar; with a rail, `›` splits it into breadcrumbs. |
| `rail` | `string` | `''` | false | Active entry of the console's side rail; empty renders no rail. |
| `texture` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'none'` | false | Texture the frame is grounded with, behind the body. |
| `textureFade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'vignette'` | false | How the frame's texture fades out before its edges. |
| `travel` | `'fast-01' \| 'fast-02' \| 'moderate-01' \| 'moderate-02' \| 'slow-01' \| 'slow-02'` | `'slow-01'` | false | Duration token of each part's travel. |
| `beat` | `'fast-01' \| 'fast-02' \| 'moderate-01' \| 'moderate-02' \| 'slow-01' \| 'slow-02'` | `'fast-01'` | false | Duration token of the gap between one part's beat and the next. |
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether this mockup is the one showing; parts replay their entrance each time it becomes active. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lets the viewer operate the controls inside instead of drawing them as an inert picture. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Plays the entrance as the frame comes into view and replays it when `active` turns back on. Off draws every part in place from the start, with no entrance and no replay. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The mockup's body, composed of `ShellMockup.Part` beats. |
| `overlay` | — | A layer over the whole frame, bar and rail included, such as a drawer. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup-part`

## Sub-components

- `shell-mockup-part/shell-mockup-part.vue` — one beat of the mockup's entrance.
  - Props: `order?: number` (default `0` — beat this part arrives on; each beat lands one `beat` after the one before it).
  - Slots: `default` — the part's content.
  - Root: a `div` with `data-entered` while landed, forwarding attributes; `data-testid` fallback `content-shell-mockup-part`.

Layout:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/shell-mockup/
├── shell-mockup.vue
├── shell-mockup.test.ts
├── index.ts                         (Object.assign(ShellMockup, { Part }))
├── injection-key.ts                 (ShellMockupContext + SHELL_MOCKUP_KEY)
├── composables/
│   └── use-shell-mockup-context.ts  (inject + throw outside the provider)
└── shell-mockup-part/
    └── shell-mockup-part.vue
```

Exports: `./shell-mockup` → `index.ts`, `./shell-mockup-root` → `shell-mockup.vue`, `./shell-mockup-part` → `shell-mockup-part/shell-mockup-part.vue`.

## States

- `data-kind` (`window` \| `bare`) on the root and the frame: `window` paints the canvas fill, a hairline rim lit from the top-left and bottom-right corners, and the card shape, and clips the drawing; `bare` paints nothing and lets parts overflow sideways while clipping vertically.
- `data-fade` mirrors `fade` on the root and the fade layer; `none` renders no fade layer.
- `data-interactive` is present while `interactive` is set; otherwise the root is `inert` and `aria-hidden`, ignores the pointer and blocks text selection.
- The bars and the rail are drawings: plain `div`s (no `header`, `aside` or `nav` landmark), each `inert` and `aria-hidden="true"` whatever `interactive` says, so only the slot body is ever operable.
- Shell matrix: `shell="console"` without `rail` draws the slim bar (brand, title, avatar); with `rail` it draws the side rail (from `md` up) and a top bar with breadcrumbs, a search field, Create, Agent and the avatar; `shell="legacy"` draws the previous console's top bar (menu, brand, Create, Copilot, Feedback, help, account) and swaps the legacy typography weights and line heights onto the frame. `chrome` off removes the bars; the rail stays.
- Entrance: parts are at rest offset and transparent until the root is at least 30% on screen and `active`; two animation frames later the root flips to entered and each part lands on its beat. `active` turning off resets it so it replays. `animated` off, or a reduced-motion preference, starts entered with no transition.
- Scale: the frame keeps the design width (`width` from `md` up, `mobileWidth` below) and scales to the host's width, deriving its design height from the host's height; It measures the host's layout box (its untransformed border box), never its on-screen box, so a mockup nested in another scaled mockup (a fragment framed in a window) scales once, at any frame width. It re-measures when the host resizes and when `width` or `mobileWidth` changes.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none by default — the root is `inert`, so nothing inside takes focus. With `interactive`, the composed controls keep their own focus rings.
- Keyboard map: none by default (inert). With `interactive`, `Tab` reaches the composed controls in DOM order and each keeps its own keyboard behavior; the shell's own bar, rail and search are drawings and never take focus.
- ARIA: the root is a `figure` with `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` unless `interactive`; the band hosting it carries the text that describes it. The bars and the rail are non-landmark `div`s that stay `inert` and `aria-hidden="true"` even when `interactive`, so the mockup never exposes a `banner`, `navigation` or `complementary` landmark, nor a focusable drawn control, inside the host page.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the shell's text uses `var(--text-default)` and `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-canvas)` / `var(--bg-surface-raised)`, the same pairs the console uses.
- `motion-reduce:` landing classes and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every part.
- Touch target: not applicable by default (inert). Interactive content keeps the composed components' own targets.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`. The scaled frame is anchored at `start-0` and scales from its start corner (`origin-top-left`, `rtl:origin-top-right`), so it fits its host in both directions.
- Icons: the breadcrumb angle mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the `Kbd` search hint stays left to right.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/tag.md -->

# Tag

> Compact status or category label with severity-based color coding. Supports optional icon, pill shape via `rounded`, and two sizes aligned with the Webkit Figma Tag component set.

- Import: `import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Label or categorize an item with a short descriptive text, optionally with a leading icon or pill shape.
- Show a status/category with severity color via `severity`.
- Mark the one value a list highlights (the Owner role in a users table) with `severity="highlight"`: the brand orange as a tint, orange text on `--primary-mask`, like the success, info and warning tints.

## Do

- Severity comes from `severity`; the optional icon is decorative — keep it `aria-hidden`.
- Pick the severity by meaning: `success` Active, `warning` Pending, `secondary` Inactive or a neutral category (Developer, Viewer), `info` a second role (Admin), `highlight` the one value to single out (Owner), `primary` a solid brand label. Do not use `danger` for a state that is only off (Inactive): it reads as an error.
- Do not restyle a Tag with colour classes to get a tint; every tint is a `severity`.
- Use `rounded` for the pill shape rather than a custom radius.

## Don’t

- It is purely a count or one-glance status label → use `badge`.
- The user can select or remove it (filters, multi-select values) → use `chip`.

## Related

- `badge` — denser count/short-label indicator with no icon affordance.
- `chip` — interactive/removable token.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `severity` | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'success' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'accent' \| 'contrast' \| 'highlight'` | `'primary'` | false | Color style for the tag surface and label; `primary` is solid brand orange, `highlight` the brand orange as a tint, `contrast` uses `var(--bg-contrast)` / `var(--text-contrast)`. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `medium` is 24px tall, `small` is 20px. |
| `rounded` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pill shape when true. |
| `icon` | `string` | `undefined` | false | PrimeIcons class for the leading icon. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Main content. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional `icon` is the consumer's choice and does not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- Isolation: the label renders `dir="auto"`, so a value in another script (a domain, an ID) keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'
</script>

<template>
  <Tag
    label="Label"
    severity="primary"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```
