<!-- components/tutorial-panel.md -->

# Tutorial Panel

> The guide that runs tutorials beside the real product. It lives in the page's tools or help region, lists the tutorials a reader can take, and while one runs it shows the tutorial's tasks and the reader's place in them. The steps themselves happen on the page: each step points at a `Hotspot` placed beside the real control, and the current step opens there in a popover. `TutorialPanel.Provider` wraps the whole page (the content and the tools region), holds the running tutorial and the current step, and is what the panel and every `Hotspot` read. It is the stateful layer over `help-panel`. The panel draws its views from `HelpPanel` parts (`Header`, `Tutorial`, `Task`), so a tutorial looks the same whether a product shows a static checklist with `HelpPanel.Tutorial` or a guided run with `TutorialPanel`. Design call (M2.9, WP app-layout): neither the design sample nor the Console Kit has a guided tutorial, so the model is Cloudscape's tutorial panel, hotspot and annotation context, rebuilt on WebKit parts.

- Import: `import TutorialPanelRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import TutorialPanel from '@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel'`
- Category: content · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A reader learns a product task by doing it on the real screen, step by step, with the instructions pointing at the control they need next.
- A product offers several tutorials in its help region and records which ones the reader finished.
- A first-run or onboarding flow guides the reader through a real create and deploy, not a mock.

## Do

- Wrap the whole page in `TutorialPanel.Provider`, so the panel and every hotspot share one state.
- Keep tutorials as data (`Tutorial[]`): the panel lists them and the hotspots on the page read the same steps. This is the one place a config array is right — the step content is shown away from where it is declared.
- One step, one control. Write the step title as the action (`Name the service`) and the content as one or two sentences.
- Place every `Hotspot` a tutorial names on the page that runs it. A step whose hotspot is missing still shows in the panel, and focus moves to it there.
- Set `completed` on a tutorial from what the product recorded (the `finish` event), not from a click.
- Bind `v-model:active` and `v-model:step` and persist them when a tutorial must survive a navigation.

## Don’t

- Static help beside the page, with no guided run → use `help-panel` (a `HelpPanel.Tutorial` checklist when the owner only reports progress).
- A multi-step create flow whose steps are forms in one surface → use `wizard`.
- Ordered steps the reader navigates inside a page → use `stepper`.
- A single tip pinned to one control → use `popover` or `hint`.
- An empty page that needs one call to action → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `hotspot` — the marker beside a real control; the current step opens from it. Every step names one by `hotspotId`.
- `help-panel` — the parts the panel draws with; use it alone for help without a guided run.
- `popover` — what a hotspot opens; the step's title, content and Previous / Next live in it.
- `drawer` — the host of the tools region on narrow screens; the panel goes inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The panel's heading. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Tutorials`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One line under the heading. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the panel's landmark. Empty uses the title. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders skeleton lines in place of the content while the tutorials load. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion` | { tutorial: Tutorial } | Extra content on the completion screen, such as a feedback link. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/tutorial-panel-provider`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**: `index.ts` attaches the provider to the panel, so
`<TutorialPanel.Provider>` resolves from the same import. The panel has no open state (the tools region
that hosts it owns that), so there is no `Trigger` / `Content`. State flows through `provide`/`inject`
(`injection-key.ts`, provided by the provider): the panel reads it through
`composables/use-tutorial-context.ts`, which throws outside a provider, and `Hotspot` reads it through
the optional variant, which returns null so a hotspot outside a provider renders only its content.

- `tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue` — Holds the tutorials, the running tutorial (`v-model:active`), the current step (`v-model:step`, flat across tasks), whether the reader dismissed the current step…
  - Props: `tutorials?: Tutorial[]` (default `[]`), `active?: string \| null` (default `undefined` — controlled when bound; uncontrolled starts at `null`), `step?: number` (default `undefined` — controlled when bound; uncontrolled starts at `0`; equals the step count once the tutorial is finished).
  - Events: `update:active` (`string \| null`), `update:step` (`number`), `start` (`string` — the tutorial id, on Start and Restart), `exit` (`string` — on Exit or Back to tutorials), `finish` (`string` — on Finish of the last step).
  - Slot: `default` — the page, with the panel and every hotspot inside.

Exported types: `Tutorial` (`id`, `title`, `description?`, `completed?`, `tasks`), `TutorialTask` (`title`, `steps`), `TutorialStep` (`title`, `content`, `hotspotId`).

```
packages/webkit/src/components/content/tutorial-panel/
├── tutorial-panel.vue                    (root; the panel views)
├── tutorial-panel.test.ts
├── index.ts                              (compound: attaches Provider)
├── injection-key.ts                      (types + TutorialContext)
├── composables/
│   └── use-tutorial-context.ts           (strict and optional injectors)
└── tutorial-panel-provider/
    └── tutorial-panel-provider.vue
```

Exports:

```jsonc
"./tutorial-panel": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/index.ts",
"./tutorial-panel-root": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel.vue",
"./tutorial-panel-provider": "./src/components/content/tutorial-panel/tutorial-panel-provider/tutorial-panel-provider.vue"
```

Composed DS components (relative imports): `help-panel` (root, `Header`, `Tutorial`, `Task`), `button`, `tag`.

## States

- Visual states: `list`, `running`, `complete`, `empty` (no tutorials), `loading`
- `data-view` on the root: `list` | `running` | `complete`
- `data-completed` on each list item mirrors the tutorial's `completed`
- In `running`, each task's `HelpPanel.Task` status is derived from the current step: `complete` when every step of the task is behind it, `current` when it holds the current step, `upcoming` otherwise. The current step's row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- `complete` shows a completion section (check icon, `Tutorial complete`, `You finished <title>.`, the `completion` slot, Restart and Back to tutorials) above the task list, every task complete.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the composed `Button`s carry the standard ring; focus targets that are not controls (the list heading, the completion heading, the current step row) take `tabindex="-1"` and `outline-none` because they receive focus only programmatically.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through Start / Restart, Exit, Restart and Back. Focus management: Start moves focus to the current step's popover (through its hotspot) or, when that hotspot is not on the page, to the step's row in the panel; Finish moves focus to the `Tutorial complete` heading; Exit and Back move focus to the list's heading.
- ARIA: the panel is a `HelpPanel` complementary landmark named by `ariaLabel` or the title. Each list item's Start button is described by its tutorial's heading (`aria-describedby`), so repeated buttons are distinct. The task progress line (`HelpPanel.Tutorial`) is `aria-live="polite"`. The current step row carries `aria-current="step"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 on muted ink over `--bg-surface` in both themes.
- Touch target: the composed `Button`s (small) meet 24 px; the panel adds no other control.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; every row is a flex row that follows `dir`.
- Icons: `pi pi-check-circle` (not mirrored), `pi pi-sign-out` on Exit (not mirrored; it names the action, not a direction).
- Keyboard: no arrow keys.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                  | English source                                                | Override prop |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `tutorialPanel.title`                | `Tutorials`                                                   | `title`       |
| `tutorialPanel.description`          | `Learn the product by doing a real task, one step at a time.` | `description` |
| `tutorialPanel.listLabel`            | `Available tutorials`                                         | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.empty`                | `No tutorials yet.`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.start`                | `Start tutorial`                                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.restart`              | `Restart tutorial`                                            | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.exit`                 | `Exit tutorial`                                               | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.back`                 | `Back to tutorials`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completed`            | `Completed`                                                   | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedTitle`       | `Tutorial complete`                                           | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.completedDescription` | `You finished {title}.`                                       | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.taskCount`            | `{count} task` / `{count} tasks`                              | —             |
| `tutorialPanel.stepCount`            | `{count} step` / `{count} steps`                              | —             |

- Formatting: plurals through `Intl.PluralRules` (the catalog's plural messages); tutorial content is the consumer's own text.

## Responsive

- Container queries: inherits `@container/help-panel` from `HelpPanel`; no breakpoint of its own — the list and the task rows stack at every width.
- Narrow: the panel goes inside a `Drawer` (the tools region on phones); its content reflows to the drawer width.
- Touch: targets are the composed small `Button`s (≥ 24 px; the drawer host gives them room).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; titles wrap.

<!-- components/cards.md -->

# Cards

> A collection shown as cards, after Cloudscape's cards: one card per item, named by its `header` slot, with the item's fields in the default slot. It shares Table's item and selection model — `items`, `trackBy`, `selectedKeys` — so `useCollection` binds it through `cardsProps`, and selection (single or multi, with a visible select-all) survives paging. Four cards a row in a wide container, then three, two and one as the container narrows.

- Import: `import Cards from '@aziontech/webkit/cards'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Items people recognise by a few fields or a picture rather than compare column by column (applications, templates, environments).
- The card form of a list page (`platform/view/card-view`), filtered and paged by `useCollection`.

## Do

- Put the item's name, as a link to the item, in the `header` slot: it also names the selection control.
- Keep each card to a handful of label and value pairs; let `collection-preferences` choose which.
- Use `selectionMode="multi"` only when a bulk action exists next to the list.
- Pass items typed with your own interface (`Domain[]`): the slots read `item.name` with that type, so never cast `item` in a slot or widen the items to `Record<string, unknown>[]`.

## Don’t

- Records compared, sorted or scanned across many fields → use `table`.
- A fixed marketing grid of features or links → use `card-grid`.
- A single content box → use `card`.

## Related

- use-collection` — filters, pages and selects; `cardsProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the same collection as rows; same item and selection model.
- `property-filter`, `collection-preferences`, `pagination` — the controls around it.
- `card` — one standalone card.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `[]` | false | The items, one card each. |
| `trackBy` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field that identifies an item; selection keys read it. |
| `selectionMode` | `'none' \| 'single' \| 'multi'` | `'none'` | false | No selection, one card, or several cards with a select-all above them. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards and sets aria-busy while true. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `selectedKeys` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | CardsItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card title; names the card and its selection control. |
| `default` | CardsItemSlotProps<TItem> | Card body: the item's fields. |
| `empty` | — | Shown when there are no items. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:selected-keys`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys (`item[trackBy]`) of the selected cards; keys of items not on the current page are kept.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `selected`, `loading`, `empty`
- `data-state` on each card: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` when selected
- `data-selection` on the root mirrors `selectionMode`; `aria-busy` while loading

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the checkbox, the radio and the links in the header slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the select-all, each card's control and its content; `Space` toggles a control.
- ARIA: the cards are a named `list` of `listitem`s; each selection control is labelled by its card's header (`aria-labelledby`); the select-all has a visible label; the root sets `aria-busy` while loading.
- Selection is never conveyed by color alone: the control is checked.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) and ≥3:1 for the selected border.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the selection control sits at the end of the header row.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: the slots isolate user data (`<bdi>` around domains in the examples).

## Internationalization

| Key                      | English source              | Override prop |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `cards.label`            | Items                       | `ariaLabel`   |
| `cards.selectAll`        | Select all items            | —             |
| `cards.emptyTitle`       | No items yet                | `empty` slot  |
| `cards.emptyDescription` | Items you create show here. | `empty` slot  |

- Formatting: none; the slots format the item's fields.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/cards`; one column below `@xl` (644 px), two from `@xl`, three from `@4xl` (1024 px), four from `@6xl` (1388 px), so a card is never narrower than about 310 px.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): one card a row at full width.
- Touch: the checkbox and radio grow their hit area on `pointer: coarse` (from the inputs); nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Cards from '@aziontech/webkit/cards'
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'

  const applications = [
    {
      id: 'app-1',
      name: 'storefront',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'shop.example.com',
      requests: '1.2M'
    },
    {
      id: 'app-2',
      name: 'checkout',
      status: 'Active',
      domain: 'pay.example.com',
      requests: '310K'
    },
    { id: 'app-3', name: 'blog', status: 'Inactive', domain: 'blog.example.com', requests: '0' },
    { id: 'app-4', name: 'docs', status: 'Active', domain: 'docs.example.com', requests: '88K' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Cards :items="applications">
    <template #header="{ item }">{{ item.name }}</template>
    <template #default="{ item }">
      <dl class="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] gap-x-(--spacing-sm) gap-y-(--spacing-xxs)">
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Status</dt>
        <dd>
          <Tag
            :label="item.status"
            :severity="item.status === 'Active' ? 'success' : 'secondary'"
            size="small"
          />
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Domain</dt>
        <dd class="truncate">
          <bdi>{{ item.domain }}</bdi>
        </dd>
        <dt class="text-(--text-muted)">Requests</dt>
        <dd class="tabular-nums">{{ item.requests }}</dd>
      </dl>
    </template>
  </Cards>
</template>
```

# Collection Preferences

> The preferences panel of a collection, after Cloudscape's collection preferences: a cog button opens a dialog (or a drawer) with the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; a locked column always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density. Changes are a draft until Confirm; Cancel, `Esc` and the close button discard them. It holds no saved state itself: `useCollection` saves the confirmed value in `localStorage` and `preferencesProps` binds the value, the columns and the page sizes in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A table or card collection whose people choose how many items a page shows and which fields they see.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, which saves the result per collection.

## Do

- Lock the column that names the item (`locked: true`): a row without its name is unreadable.
- Show only the sections the collection uses (`sections`): cards have no striped rows.
- Keep the trigger at the end of the controls row, after Refresh and Download.

## Don’t

- A single column-visibility toggle inside a table toolbar → use `table-column-selector`.
- Settings of the resource itself (not of how the list shows it) → use a form page or `dialog`.

## Related

- use-collection` — saves the preferences; `preferencesProps` is the binding.
- `table` — takes `density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`, the visible columns and their order.
- `cards` — takes the page size and the visible fields.
- `property-filter` — sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | `{}` | false | The saved preferences. Supports v-model:preferences; changes apply on Confirm. |
| `columns` | `CollectionPreferencesColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns to show, hide and order. Empty hides the columns section. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Page sizes offered. Empty hides the page size section. |
| `sections` | `CollectionPreferencesSection[]` | `['page-size', 'columns', 'wrap-lines', 'striped', 'density']` | false | Sections the panel shows, in this order. |
| `container` | `'dialog' \| 'drawer'` | `'dialog'` | false | Opens in a centered dialog or a side drawer. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Panel title and trigger label. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:preferences` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | Confirm was activated. |
| `confirm` | `CollectionPreferencesValue` | Same value, for a handler that is not a model. |
| `cancel` | `void` | Cancel was activated; the draft is discarded. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open: () => void } | Replaces the cog button; call `open` to open the panel. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether the panel is open; the trigger, Confirm, Cancel, the close button and `Esc` update it.
- **`v-model:preferences`** — `CollectionPreferencesValue`. Emitted on Confirm with the sections shown.

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`; the trigger reflects `disabled`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- Move up is disabled on the first column, move down on the last; a locked column's switch is disabled and on

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons, switches, radios and the toggle group.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens; `Tab` is trapped in the panel; `Esc` closes; focus returns to the trigger on close; after a move, focus stays on the moved column's button.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; the panel is a dialog named by its title; the page size and the columns are `fieldset`s with a `legend`; each move button is named `Move <column> up|down`; the density group is labelled by its heading.
- Columns reorder with buttons, never by drag only (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the drawer opens from its own side logic.
- Icons: the up and down arrows are vertical and not mirrored; the cog is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation of its own.
- User data: column labels are plain text; none.

## Internationalization

| Key                                          | English source                               | Override prop |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `collectionPreferences.title`                | Preferences                                  | `title`       |
| `collectionPreferences.confirm` / `cancel`   | Confirm / Cancel                             | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSize`             | Page size                                    | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.pageSizeOption`       | {count} item / {count} items (plural)        | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columns`              | Columns                                      | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.columnsDescription`   | Choose which columns show, and their order.  | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.alwaysShown`          | Always shown                                 | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.moveUp` / `moveDown`  | Move {column} up / Move {column} down        | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.wrapLines` (+ `Description`) | Wrap lines / Show the whole text of every cell. | —     |
| `collectionPreferences.striped` (+ `Description`)   | Striped rows / Shade every other row.    | —             |
| `collectionPreferences.density`, `comfortable`, `compact` | Density, Comfortable, Compact       | —             |

- Formatting: page sizes go through the plural rules and number format of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/preferences` on the sections and `@container/preferences-actions` on the footer (`@md`: buttons side by side).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the dialog becomes a bottom sheet (from `dialog`), the footer buttons stack at full width.
- Touch: radios and column rows are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long column labels truncate.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CollectionPreferences from '@aziontech/webkit/collection-preferences'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const columns = [
    { id: 'name', label: 'Name', locked: true },
    { id: 'status', label: 'Status' },
    { id: 'region', label: 'Region' },
    { id: 'requests', label: 'Requests' }
  ]

  const preferences = ref({
    pageSize: 25,
    columns: [
      { id: 'name', visible: true },
      { id: 'status', visible: true },
      { id: 'region', visible: false },
      { id: 'requests', visible: true }
    ],
    wrapLines: false,
    striped: false,
    density: 'comfortable'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <CollectionPreferences
    v-model:preferences="preferences"
    :columns="columns"
    :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/flow.md -->

# Flow

> Flow renders a directed flow diagram: a horizontal sequence of steps (`flow-node`) joined by decorative connectors, with optional parallel branches (`flow-parallel`) and custom connector-attachment points (`flow-anchor`). Use it to visualize pipelines, workflows, and step-by-step processes inside a data view; unlike `table` it expresses ordered/branching relationships rather than tabular records. Steps are written as direct children of `flow`; a `flow-parallel` between two steps fans out from the previous step and fans back into the next, and a `flow-parallel` at the start/end fans only inward/outward (no dangling stubs). A node can be styled (the default box) or `unstyled` so its slot content defines the entire node — a dot, a tall card, a multi-row card — while connectors still attach correctly, optionally at `flow-anchor` points inside the node. Connectors run port-to-port: a styled node renders a small square **connector port** just outside each of its edges, and a `flow-anchor` renders one outside the edge it attaches to, so a line always terminates on a visible attachment point instead of a bare edge (the port is the endpoint treatment — connectors carry no arrowheads). The port sits fully clear of the box rather than overlapping it, so neither the node's surface nor its focus ring crops it. A port is only rendered where a connector actually attaches: the leading child has no incoming connector and the trailing child no outgoing one, so those two edges show no port and the chain opens and closes on a node rather than on a stub. An `unstyled` node renders no ports, because its slot content owns its appearance; put a `flow-anchor` inside it to place ports on the parts a connector should touch. Design source (rewritten to our conventions, never inherited as-is): the kumo "Flow" component group at https://kumo-ui.com/components/flow/. Scope boundary: large diagrams pan via a native `overflow: auto` scroll container on the root — free 2D drag-pan is intentionally out of scope (it would require an external positioning library forbidden by `.claude/rules/dependencies.md`). The connector port is specified by the Figma frame in the frontmatter; the remaining tokens are inferred from intent and recorded in the Theme gaps table.

- Import: `import FlowRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/flow-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Flow from '@aziontech/webkit/flow'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Showing an ordered pipeline or request path as steps joined by connectors — build → deploy → serve, or a request through a load balancer, a function and its bindings.
- A step fans out to several parallel targets and (optionally) back in — wrap those steps in `Flow.Parallel`.
- A node with custom content (a card with several rows) where connectors must touch specific parts — mark them with `Flow.Anchor`.

## Do

- Write steps as direct children of `Flow` in flow order; connectors are drawn between siblings, so wrapping nodes in extra elements breaks the chain.
- Use `unstyled` when the slot content is the whole node, and put a `Flow.Anchor` (`type="end"` incoming, `type="start"` outgoing) on each part a connector should touch — an unstyled node renders no ports of its own.
- Mark a leaf that hangs off the chain with `terminal`; it receives a connector but sends none on.
- Do not clip a node with `overflow-hidden` in a wrapping card — the connector ports sit outside the node's box and would disappear.
- Let a wide flow scroll in its own container; the root is an `overflow: auto` region, and there is no drag-to-pan.

## Don’t

- One of the official architecture drawings, or a node-and-connector picture for a marketing page → use `diagram`.
- Tabular records with no ordering between them → use `table`.
- A numbered set of instructions in documentation → use `doc-steps`.

## Related

- `diagram` — marketing architecture drawings from a closed library or a one-off spec; `flow` is the in-product, hand-composed pipeline.
- `doc-steps` — an ordered walkthrough of text steps joined by a rail, not connected nodes.
- `table` — records without ordered or branching relationships.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `'start' \| 'center'` | `'start'` | false | Vertical alignment of nodes within the diagram. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Diagram content: `flow-node` and `flow-parallel`, in flow order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-node`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-parallel`
- `@aziontech/webkit/flow-anchor`

## Sub-components

- `flow-node/flow-node.vue` — A single step in the flow.
- `flow-anchor/flow-anchor.vue` — Marks a connector-attachment point inside a node and wraps the content that the connector should touch.
- `flow-parallel/flow-parallel.vue` — Container whose direct `flow-node` children are laid out as parallel branches stacked vertically; the `flow` root draws the fan-out/fan-in junction connectors.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on `flow-node`
- `data-styled` is present on `flow-node` unless `unstyled` (gates the default box utilities)
- `data-align` mirrors the `align` prop on `flow` and `flow-parallel`
- `data-flow-anchor` mirrors the `type` prop on `flow-anchor` (`start` / `end` / `both`)
- `data-flow-port` marks a connector port and selects the edge it sits on (`start` = outgoing / right, `end` = incoming / left). Emitted on both edges of a styled `flow-node`, and on the attaching edge(s) of a `flow-anchor`. The port sits entirely **outside** the box, flush against that edge — never inside it, so the node's surface and its `focus-visible` ring cannot crop the port
- Port appearance follows the enclosing node: solid border by default, `border-dashed` under `data-disabled`
- `data-flow-terminal` mirrors the `terminal` prop on `flow-node`. The composable drops that branch's exit, so no connector is drawn leaving it; the root additionally hides any outgoing port inside it (including one rendered by a nested `flow-anchor`)
- `data-flow-leading` / `data-flow-trailing` are stamped by the connector composable on the first / last direct child of the diagram (both, when there is only one). The root hides the ports on those outer edges, because no connector reaches them. They are attributes rather than `:first-child` / `:last-child` rules because the connector `<svg>` is a sibling of the nodes in the same container
- A consuming component that wraps a node in its own card must not clip it (`overflow-hidden`): the ports are positioned outside the anchor's box, so a clipping ancestor renders them invisible
- `data-faded` marks a connector path whose endpoint node is disabled (drives the reduced opacity)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus through focusable nodes in document order; no arrow-key roving (the diagram is a static list). When the diagram is wider than its box, the scroll root itself takes `tabindex="0"` (measured with a resize observer, removed again when it fits) so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys; it shows the focus ring inset.
- ARIA: root `flow` is `role="list"`; each `flow-node` is `role="listitem"` with accessible text content; `flow-parallel` is a `role="listitem"` (one step of the outer list) holding a nested `role="list"` (`data-flow-branches`, testid `<parallel testid>-branches`; it is the flex column that stacks and aligns the branches) of its branch nodes, because a `group` is not an allowed child of a `list` and its nodes would lose their `list` parent; the connector SVG is decorative and carries `aria-hidden="true"`, as does every connector port (`data-flow-port`) — the ports are a visual attachment affordance and carry no meaning for AT. A `flow-anchor` wraps meaningful node content and is therefore not hidden.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` not required — the component is static (no motion).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where a node is interactive.
- Right-to-left: under `dir="rtl"` the flow runs from the inline start (right) to the inline end (left). Connectors leave a node's inline-end edge and enter the next node's inline-start edge, the elbow bus sits between them, and the ports (`data-flow-port`) sit outside the node on the edge they mark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Flow from '@aziontech/webkit/flow'
</script>

<template>
  <Flow align="center">
    <Flow.Node>Source</Flow.Node>
    <Flow.Node>Transform</Flow.Node>
    <Flow.Node>Deliver</Flow.Node>
  </Flow>
</template>
```

<!-- components/pagination.md -->

# Pagination

> Pagination controls for tables and lists, pixel-perfect to Figma, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): a three-region landmark — page-info text, navigation buttons (Previous / page numbers / overflow / Next), and a rows-per-page selector — wired by hand through slots, with the consumer owning the current page, total, and page-size state. **Data-driven mode**: pass `total` (and optionally `page` / `pageSize`) and the Pagination renders its own info text, Previous / windowed page numbers / overflow ellipsis / Next, and the rows-per-page selector, emitting `update:page` / `update:pageSize` so the consumer can bind state via `v-model`. This component owns markup, tokens, and a11y; the data engine is a small internal page-window calculation — **no external pagination library**. Pairs with the `Table` component.

- Import: `import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A list or table outside `table`'s own footer needs page navigation and a rows-per-page selector.
- You know the item count — pass `total` and bind `v-model:page` / `v-model:page-size`; the component renders the info text, the windowed page numbers and the selector.
- The page strip needs custom content (a different info line, extra controls) — compose `Pagination.Info`, `Pagination.Button` and `Pagination.PageSize` through the slots.

## Do

- Prefer data-driven mode (`total` set); in composition mode the root emits nothing and you own every button's `selected` / `disabled` state and every click.
- page` is 1-based. Changing the page size through the selector emits `update:pageSize` and resets the page to `1`.
- Keep `page-size-options` aligned with what your data source accepts; the default is `[10, 25, 50, 100]`.
- Tune `sibling-count` (default `1`) instead of hiding buttons — it controls how many numbers sit on each side of the current page before the overflow ellipsis.
- Set `aria-label` when a page carries more than one pagination, so each navigation landmark has a distinct name.

## Don’t

- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table; it renders this pagination in its footer and wires it for you.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a documentation page → use `doc-pagination`.
- The content loads more as the reader scrolls or clicks "Load more" → use a `button` at the end of the list.

## Related

- `table` — renders a wired pagination in its footer when `paginated` is set.
- `doc-pagination` — previous / next links between documentation pages, not numbered pages of a list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` | `1` | false | Current page, 1-based (data-driven mode). Supports `v-model:page`. |
| `total` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total item count. When set, the Pagination runs in data-driven mode and renders its own controls. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Rows per page (data-driven mode). Supports `v-model:page-size`. |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Page-size options offered in the rows-per-page selector. |
| `siblingCount` | `number` | `1` | false | Page numbers shown on each side of the current page before collapsing into an overflow ellipsis. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Pagination`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:page` | `[page: number]` | Current page changed in data-driven mode (Previous / Next / page number). Supports `v-model:page`. |
| `update:pageSize` | `[pageSize: number]` | Rows-per-page changed via the internal selector. Supports `v-model:page-size`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `info` | — | Left region: page-info text (typically PaginatorInfo). In data-driven mode, overrides the default "Showing X to Y of Z entries" text. |
| `default` | — | Center region: pagination navigation buttons (composition mode only — ignored in data-driven mode, where the buttons are rendered internally). |
| `controls` | — | Right region: rows-per-page selector (PaginatorPageSize). In data-driven mode, overrides the internally-rendered selector. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-info`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-page-size`

## Sub-components

- `pagination-button/pagination-button.vue` — one segment of the numbers strip, 28px tall with a 28px minimum width and no horizontal padding; it carries no radius of its own except the outer corners at the two ends of…
- `pagination-info/pagination-info.vue` — muted page-info text container (default slot), `.text-body-xs` / `var(--text-muted)`.
- `pagination-page-size/pagination-page-size.vue` — rows-per-page selector (native `<select>`), 64×28 (same height as the numbers strip), `var(--shape-elements)` radius, `var(--bg-canvas)` frame over a `var(--bg-surface…

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`
- The page buttons render as one **segmented strip**: a single container carrying the `var(--border-default)` border and the `var(--shape-elements)` radius, with the buttons butted against each other at zero gap. Only the two end buttons round their outer corners.
- `data-kind` on PaginationButton: `previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are mutually exclusive: pressing a button drops the hover layer and shows the `var(--bg-active)` layer alone, so the pressed surface reads one step below hover.
- `data-selected` on PaginationButton mirrors the current-page `selected` prop; `aria-current="page"` set when selected.
- `data-disabled` on PaginationButton mirrors the `disabled` prop; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled` set.
- Data-driven mode: `Previous` is disabled on the first page, `Next` on the last; the current page button is `selected` (`aria-current="page"`); the overflow ellipsis (`more`) is non-interactive: an `aria-hidden` `span`, out of the tab order, that emits nothing.
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/pagination`. The page list stays whole at every width (`siblingCount` already caps it at seven slots, e.g. `1 2 3 4 5 … 60`), so a phone footer reads the same numbered strip as a desktop one, as in the design sample; when the box is too narrow for the info text and the controls on one line, the strip and the page-size control wrap together under the info text, aligned to the end.
- Touch: the buttons and the page-size select are drawn at 28 px on every pointer. On a coarse pointer (`pointer-coarse:`) each button carries an invisible, `aria-hidden` hit area that extends it to 44 px tall (vertical only: the buttons are butted, so the width stays the drawn 28 px), and the select itself grows to 44 px tall inside its 28 px frame, which draws the border, surface and focus ring.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every pagination button.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves across buttons and the rows-per-page selector; `Enter`/`Space` activates a button; disabled buttons and the overflow ellipsis are skipped. In data-driven mode, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` inside the button group go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`useDirection`).
- ARIA: root `<nav>` with `aria-label` (the `ariaLabel` prop); current-page button sets `aria-current="page"`; disabled buttons set the `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled`; icon glyphs and the overflow ellipsis are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: each button is drawn 28×28 (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8) so the strip stays compact in a table footer; on a coarse pointer its hit area grows to 28×44 invisibly and the page-size select's to its full width × 44. The width cannot grow because the buttons are butted with no gap; growing the drawn size instead was rejected because it turned the phone footer into an oversized strip that no longer matched the design sample.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`).
- Keyboard: in data-driven mode `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` go to the next/previous page, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <template #info>
      <Pagination.Info>Showing 1 to 10 of 20 entries</Pagination.Info>
    </template>

    <Pagination.Button
      kind="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="number"
      selected
      >1</Pagination.Button
    >
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">2</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="number">3</Pagination.Button>
    <Pagination.Button kind="more" />
    <Pagination.Button
      kind="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />

    <template #controls>
      <Pagination.PageSize
        :model-value="10"
        :options="[10, 25, 50, 100]"
      />
    </template>
  </Pagination>
</template>
```

<!-- components/pagination-button.md -->

# Pagination Button

> PaginationButton is one segment of the pagination's numbers strip: a 28px-tall native `button` that renders a page number or a Previous / Next chevron, or — for `kind="more"` — an inert, decorative overflow ellipsis (`span`, `aria-hidden`), selected by `kind`. It is the part `pagination` renders in data-driven mode and the one consumers compose by hand in composition mode, where it is reached as `Pagination.Button` (or imported standalone from `@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button`). It owns the segment's surface, current-page (`selected`) and `disabled` treatment, but not the strip's frame, border or the page state, which belong to the `pagination` root and the consumer.

- Import: `import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Compose a custom page strip inside `pagination`'s default slot (composition mode), one button per Previous, page number, overflow and Next.
- Render the current page of a hand-wired pagination with `selected`, and the unavailable Previous / Next ends with `disabled`.

## Do

- Place it only inside `pagination`'s default slot: the strip's border and frame come from the root, and the outer radius is applied through `first:` / `last:`, so only the first and last buttons of the strip round their corners.
- Pass `aria-label` on every `previous` and `next` button: those kinds render an `aria-hidden` icon only and have no accessible name otherwise. `more` is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so it takes no `aria-label`.
- Put the page number in the default slot of `kind="number"` only; the other kinds ignore the slot.
- Set `selected` on exactly one number button (it sets `aria-current="page"`), and `disabled` on Previous at the first page and Next at the last.
- In composition mode you own every click: listen to `click` and update the page yourself; a `disabled` button never emits it.

## Don’t

- You know the item count → pass `total` to `pagination` and bind `v-model:page`; it renders and wires every PaginationButton itself.
- The rows live in a data-driven `table` → set `paginated` on the table instead.
- The control is a previous / next link between documentation pages → use `doc-pagination`.
- It is a standalone action outside a pagination strip → use `button` or `icon-button`; this button has no radius or frame of its own except at the strip's ends.
- It is a "Load more" control at the end of a list → use `button`.

## Related

- `pagination` — the root that frames the strip and, in data-driven mode, renders these buttons; re-exports this component as `Pagination.Button`.
- pagination-info` — the page-info text that sits beside the strip.
- pagination-page-size` — the rows-per-page selector placed in the pagination's `controls` slot.
- `icon-button` — a standalone icon-only action with its own frame and radius.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'previous' \| 'next' \| 'number' \| 'more'` | `'number'` | false | Button role within the pagination. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the current page (filled surface + aria-current). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | Fires on activation. Not emitted while `disabled` (the native `disabled` attribute also blocks it), and never for `kind="more"`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page number. Rendered only when `kind` is `number`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `active`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`.
- Root: a native `button` with `type="button"`, or a `span` with `aria-hidden="true"` when `kind` is `more` (inert: not focusable, no hover / active layer, no `selected` / `disabled` treatment, never emits `click`); attributes (including `aria-label` and `class`) are forwarded to it (`inheritAttrs: false` + `v-bind="$attrs"`).
- `data-kind` mirrors `kind` (`previous` | `next` | `number` | `more`). `previous` renders `pi pi-chevron-left`, `next` renders `pi pi-chevron-right`, `more` renders `pi pi-ellipsis-h`; only `number` renders the default slot. `number` and `more` carry `var(--bg-surface)`; `previous` and `next` have no surface of their own.
- `hover` and `active` are two stacked pseudo-element layers (`before:` hover, `after:` active) and are mutually exclusive: pressing hides the hover layer and shows the active layer alone.
- `data-selected` is present when `selected` is set; it adds `var(--bg-selected)` and a `var(--border-default)` border, and sets `aria-current="page"`.
- `data-disabled` is present when `disabled` is set; the button also gets the native `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"`, mutes the foreground to `var(--text-disabled)`, shows `cursor-not-allowed`, hides both state layers and keeps the kind's own surface.
- Coarse pointer: a `number`, `previous` or `next` button renders an empty `aria-hidden` `span` (`data-slot="touch-target"`) that is shown only under `pointer-coarse:` and extends the hit area vertically to 44 px; the drawn button does not grow.
- Test ids: `<pagination testId>__button` when rendered inside a `pagination` (`data-pagination__button` by default), `data-pagination__button` outside one; a consumer `data-testid` wins.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: native button — `Tab` focuses; `Enter` / `Space` activates; a `disabled` button is skipped by `Tab`; the `more` ellipsis is a `span` and never receives focus.
- ARIA: `aria-current="page"` when `selected`; `disabled` attribute and `aria-disabled="true"` when `disabled`; the chevron icons are `aria-hidden="true"`, so `previous` and `next` take their accessible name from a consumer `aria-label` (data-driven `pagination` sets one on both); the `more` ellipsis root is `aria-hidden="true"` and decorative, so it needs no name.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons): `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)` / `var(--bg-selected)`; disabled uses `var(--text-disabled)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none`, `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:after:transition-none` on the state transitions.
- Touch target: drawn 28×28 on every pointer (above the 24×24 minimum of WCAG 2.5.8); on a coarse pointer an invisible `aria-hidden` child (`data-slot="touch-target"`) extends the hit area to 28×44. The width stays 28 because the buttons are butted into the strip (see `pagination`). The inert `more` span has no hit area.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`).
- Keyboard: arrow keys are handled by `pagination`, swapped under `dir="rtl"`.
- User data: none.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
  import Pagination from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination'
  import PaginationButton from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-button'
</script>

<template>
  <Pagination>
    <PaginationButton
      kind="previous"
      aria-label="Previous page"
      disabled
    />
    <PaginationButton
      kind="number"
      selected
      >1</PaginationButton
    >
    <PaginationButton kind="number">2</PaginationButton>
    <PaginationButton kind="more" />
    <PaginationButton
      kind="next"
      aria-label="Next page"
    />
  </Pagination>
</template>
```

<!-- components/pick-list.md -->

# Pick List

> Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Derived from the PrimeVue PickList behavior but rewritten to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<PickList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, `<PickList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<PickList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.

- Import: `import PickListRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import PickList from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
- Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
- Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.

## Do

- Set `data-key` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves; without it rows are keyed by their index.
- Set `title` on both `PickList.Source` and `PickList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
- Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
- Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.

## Don’t

- Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
- Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
- A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.

## Related

- `multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
- `table` — row selection over tabular data.
- `checkbox` — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | `() => [[], []]` | false | Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]` (v-model). |
| `dataKey` | `string` | `''` | false | Item field used as each row's render key (falls back to the index). Selection is always tracked by index. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens. |
| `moveOnDoubleClick` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `[unknown[], unknown[]]` | v-model update with the new `[sourceItems, targetItems]` pair. |
| `move` | `{ direction: 'to-target' \| 'to-source'; items: unknown[] }` | Fired after items move between lists, with the moved items. |
| `item-double-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' \| 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })` | Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading } | Composition slot; receives `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, and `<PickList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<PickList.Controls>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-source`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-target`
- `@aziontech/webkit/pick-list-controls`

## Sub-components

- `pick-list-source/pick-list-source.vue` — The source listbox (the left/top list).
- `pick-list-target/pick-list-target.vue` — The target listbox (the right/bottom list).
- `pick-list-controls/pick-list-controls.vue` — The context-aware control column between the lists.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (option), `focus-visible` (option / control), `selected` (option), `disabled`, `loading`
- `data-disabled` on the root mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-loading` on a list (`pick-list-source` / `pick-list-target`) mirrors that list's `loading` prop
- A loading list renders a centered spinner instead of its options and sets `aria-busy="true"`; while any list is loading, both the move controls and double-click-to-move are disabled until loading clears
- Each option carries `data-selected` mirroring its selection and `aria-selected`
- Server render and hydration: the options are the direct `v-for` children of the `TransitionGroup` list (an empty list while loading) and the spinner a sibling `v-if`, so the server renders no fragment markers inside the list and the HTML hydrates as is.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each option and on every move control.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the two listboxes and the control column; within a listbox `Space`/`Enter` toggle the focused option's selection; the move controls are activated with `Enter`/`Space`. Double-click on an option is a pointer affordance for moving it to the opposite list; the same move is reachable via select + the move controls (no keyboard-only feature is double-click-only).
- ARIA: each list is `role="listbox"` with `aria-label` from its title text; options are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; the source/target listboxes set `aria-multiselectable="true"`; every move control is an icon-only button with an explicit `aria-label`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` on both listboxes, and a disabled root becomes `role="group"` with `aria-disabled="true"`, so the titles dimmed by the root's `opacity-60` belong to a disabled control (WCAG 1.4.3 inactive-component exemption) instead of reading as low-contrast live text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (borders + icons), including the disabled state.
- A loading list sets `aria-busy="true"`; its `Spinner` is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and carries its own reduced-motion fallback. Control hover transitions pair with `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px for every move control (medium icon-button height).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PickList from '@aziontech/webkit/pick-list'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const model = ref([
    [
      { id: 1, label: 'Edge Functions' },
      { id: 2, label: 'WAF' },
      { id: 3, label: 'Image Processor' }
    ],
    [{ id: 4, label: 'Cache' }]
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <PickList
    v-model="model"
    data-key="id"
  >
    <PickList.Source title="Available">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </PickList.Source>

    <PickList.Controls />

    <PickList.Target title="Selected">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </PickList.Target>
  </PickList>
</template>
```

<!-- components/property-filter.md -->

# Property Filter

> One field that filters a collection by properties and free text, after Cloudscape's property filter. Typing suggests a property, then an operator, then a value, and each choice becomes a removable token (`Status = Active`); text typed without a property becomes a free-text token. Two or more tokens combine with Match all (and) or Match any (or). With `mode="query"` the same field edits one query string instead (`level = Error AND method = GET`), after the Console Kit events query bar: suggestions follow the word at the caret (a field, an operator, a value, then AND or OR), a check explains what is wrong under the field, and Enter submits the text with its flat token list. It edits a `PropertyFilterQuery` and never filters anything itself: `useCollection` (or the server) applies the query, and `propertyFilterProps` binds the query, the properties and the match count in one `v-bind`.

- Import: `import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A list or table that people narrow by several fields at once (status, region, owner) and by text.
- Any collection driven by `useCollection`, client or server mode.
- Filters that must survive a reload or a shared link: the query serializes into the URL through `useCollection`.
- With `mode="query"`: an explorer (events, logs) whose users type queries by hand, keep and reuse them as text, or need a grammar of the product (pass `validate` and `suggest`).

## Do

- Give every property with a closed set of values its `options`, so values are suggested and tokens print labels.
- Set `type: 'number'` or `type: 'date'` on ordered properties to offer `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`.
- Bind `totalCount` so people hear how many items match after each change.
- Name the field after the collection (`aria-label="Filter resources"`).
- In query mode, fields are written by `key` (no spaces); quote values that hold spaces or operator characters (`"edge cache"`). Apply the `query` of `submit` when it is not null; keep the `text` for saved and recent queries.
- A product grammar (`like`, `between`, parentheses) passes `validate` and `suggest`; `submit` then carries `query: null` for text the built-in grammar cannot flatten, and the product parses `text` itself.

## Don’t

- A single text search over a short list → use `input` bound to `filterProps`.
- A few fixed choices always on screen → use `toggle-group` or `chip` filters.
- A structured filter builder with its own panel inside a table toolbar → use `table-filter`.

## Related

- use-collection` — applies the query; `propertyFilterProps` is the binding.
- `table` — the collection it usually filters.
- `cards` — the card form of a collection.
- `collection-preferences` — the panel that sits beside it in the controls row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | `undefined` | false | The tokens and how they combine. Supports v-model:query. |
| `properties` | `FilteringProperty[]` | `[]` | false | Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values. |
| `totalCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `freeText` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field and the tokens. |
| `mode` | `'tokens' \| 'query'` | `'tokens'` | false | tokens` turns each choice into a token; `query` edits one query string. |
| `text` | `string` | `undefined` | false | The query string in query mode. Supports v-model:text. |
| `validate` | `(text: string) => string` | `undefined` | false | Checks the query string in query mode: '' when valid, else the message shown under the field. Replaces the built-in check. |
| `suggest` | `(text: string, caret: number) => PropertyFilterQuerySuggestion[]` | `undefined` | false | Suggestions for the word at the caret in query mode. Replaces the built-in field, operator, value and AND / OR suggestions. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:query` | `PropertyFilterQuery` | A token was added or removed, the operation changed, or all cleared. Tokens mode only. |
| `update:text` | `string` | The query string changed (typing, a suggestion, Escape clearing). Query mode only. |
| `submit` | `PropertyFilterSubmit` | Enter with no active suggestion and a valid query. Query mode only. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `focus-visible`, `open` (suggestions shown), `disabled`, `invalid` (query mode: after Enter or blur on a query that fails the check, then live until it passes or is cleared)
- `data-mode` on the field wrapper mirrors `mode`; query mode sets the typed text in the code type (`text-label-code-sm`)
- `aria-expanded` on the field mirrors the open suggestions; `data-active` marks the active option
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the field's own `focus-within` ring (from `input`); tokens and buttons keep theirs.
- Keyboard map (query mode): typing opens the suggestions for the word at the caret; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option (it replaces the word and moves the caret after it) or submits the query; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`, `Home`/`End` and clicks move the caret and the suggestions follow it; `Backspace` only edits text.
- In query mode an invalid query sets `aria-invalid` on the field and `aria-describedby` to the message, which sits in a polite live region under the field; the token group is not rendered.
- Keyboard map (tokens mode): typing opens the suggestions; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option (wrapping); `Enter` applies the active option or commits the typed text; `Escape` closes the suggestions, then clears the text; `Backspace` in an empty field removes the last token.
- ARIA: the field is a `combobox` (`aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-activedescendant`); the suggestions are a named `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected` on the active one; the tokens sit in a named `group`; each token's remove button is named `Remove <token>`; the match count is a `status` region.
- Option targets are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`, `ps-`/`pe-` from `input`); the suggestions anchor to the start edge of the field.
- Icons: the filter glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are not direction-dependent.
- User data: suggestion labels sit in `<bdi>` so a value in another script does not reorder the line.
- Query mode: the query string keeps `dir="auto"` from `input`, so a Latin query stays left-to-right inside a right-to-left page; the message sits at the start and the match count at the end (`ms-auto`).
- Teleported content: the teleported suggestions listbox binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Internationalization

| Key                                 | English source                 | Override prop |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `propertyFilter.label`              | Filter                         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `propertyFilter.placeholder`        | Filter by property or text     | `placeholder` |
| `propertyFilter.suggestions`        | Suggestions                    | —             |
| `propertyFilter.useText`            | Use: “{text}”                  | —             |
| `propertyFilter.properties`         | Properties                     | —             |
| `propertyFilter.values`             | Values                         | —             |
| `propertyFilter.tokens`             | Applied filters                | —             |
| `propertyFilter.operation`          | Combine filters                | —             |
| `propertyFilter.matchAll` / `matchAny` | Match all / Match any       | —             |
| `propertyFilter.and` / `or`         | and / or                       | —             |
| `propertyFilter.clear`              | Clear filters                  | —             |
| `propertyFilter.matches`            | {count} match / {count} matches (plural) | —   |
| `propertyFilter.equals` … `lessOrEqual` | operator names (Equals, Contains, …) | —   |
| `propertyFilterQuery.label`         | Query                          | `ariaLabel`   |
| `propertyFilterQuery.placeholder`   | Type a query, for example status = Active AND requests > 10 | `placeholder` |
| `propertyFilterQuery.fields`        | Fields                         | —             |
| `propertyFilterQuery.all` / `any`   | Every condition matches / Any condition matches (AND / OR) | — |
| `propertyFilterQuery.unknownField` … `unclosedQuote` | the built-in check messages (`{field}`, `{operator}`, `{word}`, `{connective}`, `{position}`) | `validate` |

- Formatting: the match count goes through the plural rules and number format of the active locale (`Intl.PluralRules`, `Intl.NumberFormat`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/property-filter` on the root; the token row wraps.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the field takes the full width, tokens wrap onto several lines, the count moves to the end of the last line.
- Touch: options are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom; long tokens truncate inside the chip.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import PropertyFilter from '@aziontech/webkit/property-filter'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const properties = [
    {
      key: 'status',
      label: 'Status',
      options: [{ value: 'Active' }, { value: 'Inactive' }, { value: 'Degraded' }]
    },
    {
      key: 'region',
      label: 'Region',
      options: [{ value: 'sa-east' }, { value: 'us-east' }, { value: 'eu-west' }]
    },
    { key: 'name', label: 'Name' },
    { key: 'requests', label: 'Requests', type: 'number' }
  ]

  const query = ref({
    tokens: [{ propertyKey: 'status', operator: '=', value: 'Active' }],
    operation: 'and'
  })
</script>

<template>
  <PropertyFilter
    v-model:query="query"
    :properties="properties"
    :total-count="12"
  />
</template>
```
