<!-- components/table.md -->

# Table

> Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the `Pagination` component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.

- Import: `import TableRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/table-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Table from '@aziontech/webkit/table'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
- A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
- Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.

## Do

- For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
- Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
- Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
- Give `Table.CellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
- Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.
- On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.
- Type the rows, not the slot: pass a typed `data` (`ref<Domain[]>([])`, or a literal array) and destructure `#cell-name="{ row, value }"` — `row` is a `Domain` and `value` is `Domain['name']`. Keep a column's `id` equal to its `accessorKey` (or leave `id` out) so the typed `value` is the field the cell shows. Do not annotate the slot scope by hand or cast `row as Domain`; a wrong field (`row.nmae`) should be a type error.
- Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.

## Don’t

- A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
- A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
- Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
- A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.

## Related

- `pagination` — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
- `listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
- `empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
- `item` — list rows without a column structure.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxHeight` | `string` | `''` | false | Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header). |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected. |
| `data` | `TRow[]` | `[]` | false | Data-driven mode: row records. |
| `columns` | `TableColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack. |
| `rowKey` | `string` | `'id'` | false | Field used as the stable row id (for selection). |
| `enableSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Enable sorting globally; per-column `enableSorting` overrides. |
| `enableRowSelection` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Add a leading selection-checkbox column. |
| `rowSelectable` | `(row: TRow) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | Data-driven mode: decides per row whether it can be selected (`(row) => row.kind === 'file'`). A row it rejects draws no checkbox, ignores row clicks and stays out of Select all. |
| `selectOnRowClick` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `enableRowSelection`); interactive cells still own their own click. |
| `headerKind` | `'default' \| 'compact'` | `'default'` | false | Header density (data-driven): `compact` shrinks the column-header row's height and padding. Forwarded to the `TableHeader`'s `kind`. |
| `paginated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Render a Pagination in the footer. |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` | false | Rows per page when paginated. |
| `sorting` | `SortingState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:sorting (TanStack SortingState). |
| `rowSelection` | `RowSelectionState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:rowSelection (TanStack RowSelectionState). |
| `columnVisibility` | `VisibilityState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:columnVisibility (TanStack VisibilityState). |
| `globalFilter` | `string` | `undefined` | false | v-model:globalFilter text. |
| `pagination` | `PaginationState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:pagination (TanStack PaginationState). |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally. |
| `manualPagination` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side pagination: emit events, do not slice locally. |
| `manualFiltering` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally. |
| `rowCount` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Total row count for manual pagination. |
| `rowsPerPageOptions` | `number[]` | `[10, 25, 50, 100]` | false | Rows-per-page options shown in the footer selector. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `Table.RefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`. |
| `filters` | `AppliedFilter[]` | `undefined` | false | v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch. |
| `filterFields` | `FilterField[]` | `[]` | false | Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder. |
| `state` | `TableStateSnapshot` | `undefined` | false | v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern. |
| `initialState` | `Partial<TableStateSnapshot>` | `undefined` | false | Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model. |
| `exportRows` | `(scope: 'filtered' \| 'all') => TRow[] \| Promise<TRow[]>` | `undefined` | false | Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download. |
| `exportFilename` | `string` | `'export.csv'` | false | Default filename for `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` when no per-call filename is given. |
| `stackable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: opt in to stacked rows. When the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of the horizontally scrolling grid. Off by default: a console list scrolls sideways on a phone. |
| `wrapLines` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating. |
| `striped` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface. |
| `density` | `'comfortable' \| 'compact'` | `'comfortable'` | false | Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding. |
| `virtual` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout. |
| `estimateRowHeight` | `number` | `48` | false | Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured. |
| `reorderable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Data-driven mode: a leading grip column lets people drag rows, or move the focused grip's row with Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home and End, into a new order. Emits `update:data` (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder`; locked while a sort is applied. |
| `rowReorderable` | `(row: TRow) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | With `reorderable`: decides per row whether it can move (`(row) => !row.locked`). A rejected row keeps its place: its grip is disabled, and no row is dropped onto it or moved past it with the keys. |
| `getSubRows` | `(row: TRow) => TRow[] \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Data-driven mode: tree rows. Returns a row's children (`(row) => row.children`); a row with children gets an expand toggle in the principal column, its children render under it indented one step (`--spacing-md`) per level, and the grid element takes `role="treegrid"`. Sorting and filtering keep each child under its parent; selection is per row (selecting a parent does not select its children). `reorderable` is ignored in tree mode. |
| `expanded` | `ExpandedState` | `undefined` | false | v-model:expanded (TanStack ExpandedState: `true` for every row, or `{ [rowId]: true }`). Uncontrolled it starts collapsed. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:sorting` | `value: SortingState` | v-model:sorting. |
| `update:rowSelection` | `value: RowSelectionState` | v-model:rowSelection. |
| `update:columnVisibility` | `value: VisibilityState` | v-model:columnVisibility. |
| `update:globalFilter` | `value: string` | v-model:globalFilter. |
| `update:pagination` | `value: PaginationState` | v-model:pagination. |
| `row-click` | `(event: MouseEvent, row: TRow)` | Fires when a rendered row is clicked (data-driven mode). `event` is the click; `row` is the clicked record. |
| `update:filters` | `value: AppliedFilter[]` | v-model:filters. |
| `update:state` | `value: TableStateSnapshot` | v-model:state; debounced so bursts of changes coalesce. |
| `filter-apply` | `filters: AppliedFilter[]` | The filter builder was committed (Apply) — the explicit re-query signal for `manualFiltering`. |
| `filter-remove` | `filter: AppliedFilter` | One applied filter/chip was removed. |
| `refresh` | `—` | Refresh requested (`Table.RefreshButton` or `reload()`); the app refetches. |
| `export` | `rows: TRow[]` | Export requested with the resolved rows; a consumer may handle it server-side (otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads). |
| `update:data` | `value: TRow[]` | reorderable`: the records in their new order; bind `v-model:data`. |
| `reorder` | `payload: { from: number; to: number; row: TRow }` | reorderable`: a row moved from index `from` to index `to` of `data`. |
| `update:expanded` | `value: ExpandedState` | Tree rows: v-model:expanded, after a toggle by pointer or keyboard. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition mode: the scrollable region (TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody). |
| `footer` | — | Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (e.g. TableFooter + Pagination), so it never scrolls with the body. In data-driven mode it renders automatically when `paginated`. |
| `caption` | — | Data-driven mode: caption content (wrapped in TableCaption), fixed above the scroll viewport. |
| `title` | — | Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport (both modes). |
| `toolbar` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Action band (search, filter trigger, refresh, export, column-selector) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance in data-driven mode, `undefined` in composition mode; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop. |
| `filters` | { table, selectedRows, selectedCount, clearSelection, loading } | Active-filter chips row below the toolbar (both modes); same scope as `toolbar`. |
| `empty` | — | Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `selected`
- The viewport is always a scroll container (`overflow: auto`): horizontal scroll is automatic when columns overflow; vertical scroll engages only when `maxHeight` constrains the content.
- `data-frozen` on TableHeader (`true`), TableHeadCell / TableCell (`start` | `end`), and TableRow (`true`). A frozen head/body cell renders a CSS-only fade (gradient pseudo-element) just outside its inner edge that dissolves the horizontally scrolling content into the row background (`from-transparent` → `var(--table-row-bg)`, the row-published color, so it matches the row on hover/selected) — `frozen=start` fades on the right, `frozen=end` on the left. The fade tints nothing; it only masks the content sliding under the pinned column.
- `data-state` on TableRow: `selected` | `unselected`; `data-selected` mirrors the `selected` prop; `aria-selected` set when selected.
- `data-kind` on TableHeadCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action` | `slot`) and TableCell (`default` | `checkbox` | `action`).
- `data-align` on head/body cells: `start` | `center` | `end`.
- `data-grow` on head/body cells: `1` | `2` | `3` (flex weight).
- `data-sortable` and `data-sort` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) on TableHeadCell; `aria-sort` mirrors `data-sort`.
- `data-direction` (`none` | `ascending` | `descending`) and `data-visible` on TableSortButton.
- `data-clickable` on TableCell mirrors the `clickable` prop.
- Stacked rows (data-driven, opt-in `stackable`): by default the grid scrolls sideways at every width, as the console does on a phone. With `stackable`, the table measures its own box; below `--container-lg` (552 px) it sets `data-stacked` and each body row becomes a bordered card. The checkbox, the principal column and the action column share the first line; every other column takes its own line as a label (the column `label` or `header`, `aria-hidden`) and its value. The header row stays in the DOM visually hidden, so screen readers keep the column headers; frozen offsets and fades are dropped. A hand-composed table never stacks.
- Stacked select-all (data-driven, `enableRowSelection`): in the stacked layout the header checkbox is not rendered; a visible, labelled **Select all rows** checkbox sits above the stacked rows (`__stacked-select-all`) and toggles the page, with the same indeterminate state.
- Per-row selectability (data-driven, `rowSelectable`): a row the function rejects renders an empty selection cell, ignores `selectOnRowClick` and is skipped by Select all; the header checkbox reads `all` when every selectable row is selected.
- Density and wrapping: `data-density="compact"` on the root shrinks body cells (`min-h-9`, `--spacing-xxs` block padding); `data-wrap` lets cell text (and any `.truncate` inside a cell) wrap. `striped` shades odd body rows with `var(--bg-surface-raised)` (selected and hover still win).
- Virtual rows (`virtual`): only the rows in view plus 8 above and below render; the slice starts on an even row so stripes stay put; rows of different heights (`wrapLines` with long text) are measured as they render and the rows in view do not shift while scrolling; the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`. Skeleton and stacked layouts render every row.
- Long lists (more than 200 rows, not `virtual`): the first 50 rows render, a spacer (`__lazy-rows`, `aria-hidden`) stands in for the rest and more rows mount as it nears the viewport, until every row is in the DOM; while rows are still missing the root sets `aria-rowcount` and each row `aria-rowindex`.
- Responsive toolbar: the root is the `@container/table`; the toolbar wraps, and below `@md` of the table the `toolbar` slot moves under the title and starts at the start edge. `Table.Toolbar` wraps its controls.
- Hover-free devices: a sortable header shows its sort affordance where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`).
- Reorderable rows (`reorderable`): a 40 px leading column holds a grip `IconButton` per row (`data-reorder-handle`), frozen at the start edge when other columns are; the row being dragged sets `data-dragging` (dashed accent outline, 60% opacity) and the row under the pointer `data-drop="before" | "after"` (a 2 px accent line on that edge). While a sort is applied every grip is disabled and its description says to clear the sort.
- Tree rows (`getSubRows`): the grid element is `role="treegrid"` and sets `data-tree`. Each body row carries `aria-level` (1-based depth), `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` among its siblings, `aria-expanded` when it has children, and `data-depth`; the principal cell starts with one `aria-hidden` gutter (`data-tree-gutter`) `calc(var(--spacing-md) * depth + var(--size-7))` wide, which holds the 28 px chevron toggle (`__expand-toggle`, `pi-chevron-right` mirrored in RTL, `pi-chevron-down` when open) at its end on rows with children, so the content of every row at one depth starts on one column and each level shifts it by exactly one step. Rows use a roving tab stop (one row has `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`) and draw an inset `var(--ring-color)` outline on `focus-visible`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the sort button and any interactive cell content.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses sortable headers and interactive cell content; `Enter`/`Space` toggles a sortable header; row click is mouse/touch (no keyboard trap).
- ARIA: `role="table"` sits on the grid element inside the scroll viewport (testid `<testid>__table`), not on the root: the root also holds the toolbar, applied filters, the focusable scroll viewport, the stacked select-all, the empty state and the pagination, and any of those inside a `table` is an unallowed child (`aria-required-children`). Every `aria-*` attribute passed to `Table` (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`…) is forwarded to that element, as are `aria-busy` (loading) and `aria-rowcount` (windowed); every other attribute stays on the root. The data-driven pagination is a plain region under the viewport (`<testid>__footer`), not a `rowgroup`, and the `caption` slot renders as the table's first child. `table-caption` is a plain element (no `role`) that names the table through `aria-labelledby` unless the consumer names it with `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. In composition mode the default slot is the table's content, so it holds rowgroups (and a caption) only; anything else goes in `footer` or around the `Table`. `table-header`/`table-body` `role="rowgroup"`; `table-footer` has no role (it hosts pagination or an action, not rows); `table-row` `role="row"`; `table-head-cell` `role="columnheader"` with `aria-sort` when sortable; `table-cell` `role="cell"`; selected rows set `aria-selected`.
- Virtual rows keep their position for assistive technology: `aria-rowcount` on the `role="table"` element (rows + header) and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row.
- Reorderable rows: each grip is a button named `Reorder <row name>, position <n> of <total>` and described by a visually hidden hint (`Drag, or press Arrow Up or Arrow Down to move.`, or the lock reason). Arrow Up / Arrow Down / Home / End move the row and keep focus on its grip; `Esc` cancels a drag. A polite `role="status"` region announces `Moved <name> to position <n> of <total>.` (keyboard) or `Dropped …` (pointer). Dragging is never the only way to reorder (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Tree rows follow the APG treegrid row-focus pattern: `Tab` enters the grid on one row (the last one focused, else the first); `Arrow Down` / `Arrow Up` move between visible rows; `Home` / `End` go to the first / last row; `Arrow Right` (inline end, mirrored in RTL) opens a closed row or moves to the first child of an open one; `Arrow Left` closes an open row or moves to the parent; `Enter` toggles the row; `Space` toggles its selection when `enableRowSelection` allows it. Interactive content inside the row (checkbox, menus) stays reachable with `Tab`. The pointer toggle is `aria-hidden` (the row's `aria-expanded` is the accessible state), and when a row collapses while one of its descendants holds focus, focus moves to that row.
- Stacked layout: the select-all is a visible checkbox with a `<label>`, not a screen-reader-only header cell (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including muted header text.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the sort button and row action controls.
- Filter count: `Table.Filter`'s trigger is named `Filters` with no filter applied and `Filters, <n> applied` (`tableFilter.triggerCount`, plural in pt-BR and es) otherwise; the count badge is `aria-hidden`, so the number is read once.
- Teleported content: the `Table.Filter` and `Table.ColumnSelector` panels, teleported to `body`, bind `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so they keep the provider's direction and language. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

      status: 'Active',
      editor: 'user1@example.com',
      modified: 'Jan 1, 2026, 09:00 AM',
      protocol: 'HTTP & HTTPS',
      domains: 2,
      origins: 1,
      created: 'Dec 1, 2025, 10:00 AM'
    },
    {
      id: '1002',
      name: 'Workload Bravo',
      status: 'Inactive',
      editor: 'user2@example.com',
      modified: 'Jan 2, 2026, 09:00 AM',
      protocol: 'HTTP',
      domains: 1,
      origins: 2,
      created: 'Dec 2, 2025, 10:00 AM'
    },
    {
      id: '1003',
      name: 'Workload Charlie',
      status: 'Degraded',
      editor: 'user3@example.com',
      modified: 'Jan 3, 2026, 09:00 AM',
      protocol: 'gRPC',
      domains: 3,
      origins: 1,
      created: 'Dec 3, 2025, 10:00 AM'
    }
  ]

  const columns = [
    { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
    { accessorKey: 'id', header: 'ID', enableSorting: false },
    { accessorKey: 'status', header: 'Status' },
    { accessorKey: 'editor', header: 'Last Editor', enableSorting: false, grow: 2 },
    { accessorKey: 'modified', header: 'Last Modified', grow: 2 },
    { id: 'actions', header: '', kind: 'action', enableSorting: false }
  ]

  const sorting = ref([])

  const rowActionGroups = [
    [
      { value: 'view', label: 'View details', icon: 'pi pi-eye' },
      { value: 'edit', label: 'Edit', icon: 'pi pi-pencil' },
      { value: 'duplicate', label: 'Duplicate', icon: 'pi pi-copy' }
    ],
    [{ value: 'delete', label: 'Delete', icon: 'pi pi-trash' }]
  ]

  const statusSeverity = (status) =>
    status === 'Active' ? 'success' : status === 'Degraded' ? 'warning' : 'danger'

  const onRowClick = (_row) => {}
  const onRowAction = (_payload) => {}
</script>

<template>
  <TableRoot
    :data="rows"
    :columns="columns"
    row-key="id"
    enable-sorting
    paginated
    :page-size="5"
    bordered
    v-model:sorting="sorting"
    @row-click="onRowClick"
  >
    <template #cell-name="{ row, value }">
      <a
        :href="'/workloads/' + row.id"
        class="cursor-pointer truncate text-(--text-default) no-underline hover:underline active:underline"
        >{{ value }}</a
      >
    </template>
    <template #cell-status="{ value }">
      <Tag :severity="statusSeverity(value)">{{ value }}</Tag>
    </template>
    <template #header-actions>
      <span class="sr-only">Actions</span>
    </template>
    <template #cell-actions="{ row }">
      <DropdownMenuRoot @select="({ value }) => onRowAction({ id: row.id, action: { value } })">
        <DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <IconButton
            icon="pi pi-ellipsis-v"
            aria-label="Row actions"
            kind="transparent"
            size="small"
          />
        </DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <DropdownMenuGroup
          v-for="(group, gi) in rowActionGroups"
          :key="gi"
        >
          <DropdownMenuOption
            v-for="option in group"
            :key="option.value"
            :value="option.value"
            :label="option.label"
          >
            <template #left
              ><i
                :class="option.icon"
                aria-hidden="true"
            /></template>
          </DropdownMenuOption>
        </DropdownMenuGroup>
      </DropdownMenuRoot>
    </template>
  </TableRoot>
</template>

<!-- components/topology-diagram.md -->

# Topology Diagram

> The deployment topology of a resource as a left-to-right diagram: each column is a depth (domains, project, policy, service, cache rules, integration, storage), each node a collapsible card with the resource kind, its status tag, its name and, when opened, a message and labelled fields; dashed connectors join every node of a column to the next. A node without a name is an unbound slot (dashed, Not bound) and a `bindable` node carries the bind control (bind an existing resource, change it, create one, remove it). Taken from the design sample's workload topology (`TopologyNode`, `TopologyNodeCard`, `TopologyBindNode`, `TopologyBindControl`, the empty node). It reuses `Flow`'s connector engine and anchors and draws its own list semantics, with no node-graph dependency.

- Import: `import TopologyDiagram from '@aziontech/webkit/topology-diagram'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The topology tab of a project, service or workload: what serves its traffic, in order, and what is still unbound.
- A review before a deploy where binding or removing a resource is staged on the diagram.

## Do

- Keep a column per depth and put the nodes that serve in parallel in the same column.
- Mark a staged change `dashed` with a warning status and a message that says the deploy applies it.
- Mark the last node of each branch `terminal` so no connector leaves it.
- Give every unbound slot a message that says what happens without it.
- Give a node `href` when its resource has a page: the name becomes a link that ends in the open glyph (`pi pi-external-link`), as every resource name in the console does.
- A node that collects many resources and adds to itself, such as Domains (add a domain), puts its `+` in the `actions` slot: an `IconButton` (`pi pi-plus`, `kind="outlined"`, `size="small"`) named `Add domain` inside a `Tooltip`, picked by `node.key`. `bindable` is for a slot that holds one resource (Firewall, Custom Page): it brings its own `+` with the bind menu. Do not hand-draw a node card to get the `+`.

## Don’t

- A sequence of steps or a pipeline without data cards → use `flow`.
- A nested list of items with no flow between them → use `tree`.
- A marketing architecture picture → use `diagram`.

## Related

- `flow` — the connector engine and anchors this component reuses.
- `tree` — hierarchical data without connectors.
- `dropdown-menu` — the bind control's menu.
- platform/detail/details-page` — the page whose topology tab holds it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `levels` | `TopologyLevel[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of the diagram, from the entry point to the last dependency. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows placeholder cards while the topology loads. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the diagram. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deployment topology`). |
| `expanded` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:expanded`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bind` | `[key: string, value: string]` | An existing option was picked in the bind control. |
| `remove` | `[key: string]` | Remove was activated on a bound, removable node. |
| `create` | `[key: string]` | Create was picked in the bind control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | { node: TopologyNode } | Extra controls in a node's identity row, before the bind control. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the line shown when there are no levels. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:expanded`** — `string[]`, default `[]`. Keys of the open node cards; a header click toggles its key.

## States

- Root: `data-loading` and `aria-busy` while `loading`; empty when `levels` is empty.
- Node card: `data-state` `open` | `closed`; `data-dashed` for a staged or unbound node.
- Connectors: dashed, flowing; faded never (no disabled nodes).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: header buttons `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`; the scroll area when it scrolls.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through header buttons, links, copy, bind and remove controls in reading order; `Enter`/`Space` on a header toggles its card; the bind menu follows `dropdown-menu` (arrows, `Enter`, `Esc`). The scroll area is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) only when it overflows, so arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the root is a `section` named by `ariaLabel`; columns are an `ol` of `li`, each with an optional visually hidden label; each header is a `button` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the collapsed body is `inert`; connectors are `aria-hidden`; icon-only controls are named (`Bind Policy`, `Remove Policy`, `Copy Domains Custom domain`) and carry a `Tooltip`; loading announces once through a `role="status"` line.
- The unbound dash is `aria-hidden`; the status tag says Not bound in words.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-auto`, `text-start`); the columns run from the inline start.
- Connectors: the engine reads `direction` and mirrors the elbows; ports swap sides.
- Icons: the chevron rotates vertically and is not mirrored; kind icons are not mirrored.
- User data: field values carry `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source              | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------- |
| `topologyDiagram.label`     | Deployment topology         | `ariaLabel`   |
| `topologyDiagram.notBound`  | Not bound                   | node `status` |
| `topologyDiagram.bind` / `change` / `remove` / `create` | Bind {kind} / Change {kind} / Remove {kind} / Create {kind} | — |
| `topologyDiagram.existing`  | Existing                    | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.noOptions` | No options yet.             | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.copy`      | Copy {field}                | —             |
| `topologyDiagram.empty`     | Nothing is connected yet.   | `empty` slot  |
| `topologyDiagram.loading`   | Loading the topology        | —             |

- Formatting: none; kinds, names, statuses and fields are data.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; each column keeps `min-w-(--size-56)` and grows to share the width.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the diagram scrolls inline in its own focusable area; the page does not.
- Touch: header buttons are full-width rows; bind, remove and copy are small icon buttons with tooltips that also work on focus.
- Reflow: the diagram is a two-dimensional figure, an accepted exception to 1.4.10 inside its own scroll area.

<!-- components/tree.md -->

# Tree

> A hierarchical list of nodes, each row a name with an optional glyph and one line of detail, where a parent row folds its children open and closed under a chevron. It renders a nested `items` data structure on its own (recursively, through one internal row template) and follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, so it fits file and object browsers: the objects of a bucket, the source files of a deployment, the routes of an application. Unlike `menu` it navigates data, not the app, and unlike `accordion` its nodes are rows of the same kind at any depth, not panels of free content.

- Import: `import Tree from '@aziontech/webkit/tree'`
- Category: data · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Browsing a hierarchy whose depth is not fixed: bucket objects under folders, the source tree of a deployment, functions grouped by application.
- Picking one node out of a hierarchy (`selectable`) to show its detail beside the tree.
- A hierarchy the user expands piece by piece, where showing every level at once would bury the node they are after.

## Do

- Give every node an `id` that is unique across the whole tree, not only among its siblings; `v-model:expanded`, `v-model:selected` and focus are keyed by it.
- Seed `v-model:expanded` with the path to the node the user is most likely after (the open folder, the selected file), not with every parent.
- Keep labels short and put secondary detail (size, count, modified date) in `description` so rows scan as names first.
- Use `selectable` only when the selection drives something on the screen (a detail pane, a preview); for a tree whose rows only lead somewhere, listen to `item-click` instead.
- Put per-row controls in the `actions` slot (an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`), never inside the `item` slot, so they do not take over the row's activation.

## Don’t

- Navigation between views of the app → use `menu` inside `sidebar`.
- Flat records with several attributes each → use `table`.
- A few sections of free content that open and close → use `accordion`.
- A two- or three-level directory of destinations on a marketing page → use `column-navigation`.

## Related

- `table` — the flat, multi-column view of the same records; switch to it when columns matter more than nesting.
- `menu` — the hierarchical list for app navigation, with routes and active state instead of selection.
- `accordion` — disclosure of free content panels rather than rows of one kind.
- `empty-state` — what the tree renders when `items` is empty.
- `skeleton` — the rows the tree renders while `loading`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TreeItem[]` | `[]` | false | Nodes to render; each is `{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; children?: TreeItem[] }`. A node with a non-empty `children` array is a parent. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Enables single selection: activating a node writes its id to `v-model:selected` and marks it `aria-selected`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders Skeleton rows in place of the tree and sets `aria-busy`. |
| `emptyTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the default empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No items`). |
| `emptyDescription` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting line under the empty title. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tree. |
| `expanded` | `string[]` | `() => []` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:expanded`). |
| `selected` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selected`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item-click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, item: TreeItem)` | A node activated: click on its row, or Enter / Space on the focused node. `item` is the consumer's own node object. Fires after `update:selected` when `selectable`. Not fired for a `disabled` node, nor for a click on the chevron or inside the `actions` region. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean } | Replaces the label region of every row (glyph + label + description). The fallback inside the slot renders `item.icon`, `item.label` and `item.description`. `level` is 1 for top-level nodes; `expanded` is false for leaves. The chevron, indentation, row states and the `actions` region stay owned by the tree. |
| `actions` | { item: TreeItem; level: number } | Trailing per-row controls, end-aligned in the row (e.g. an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`). Clicks and keys inside it do not activate the row nor move tree focus. No fallback; when unused, the region is not rendered. |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the default empty state. The fallback inside the slot is `EmptyState` titled by `emptyTitle` with `emptyDescription`. |

## v-model

| Model              | Type       | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ---------- | ------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:expanded` | `string[]` | `[]`    | `update:expanded` | Ids of the expanded parents, via `defineModel<string[]>('expanded', { default: () => [] })`. Uncontrolled when unbound. Ids of leaves or of unknown nodes are ignored. Collapsing a parent removes only its own id: descendants keep theirs, so re-expanding restores the subtree as it was. Always emits a new array.              |
| `v-model:selected` | `string`   | `''`    | `update:selected` | Id of the selected node, via `defineModel<string>('selected', { default: '' })`. Written only while `selectable`; read only while `selectable` (otherwise no node is marked selected). `''` means nothing is selected. Emits only when the id changes. Single selection only; activating the selected node again does not clear it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; row `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `disabled`; parent `expanded` / `collapsed`; `loading` (Skeleton rows); `empty` (`EmptyState`).
- Precedence: `loading` → Skeleton rows, else `items` empty → `empty` slot, else the tree.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`; `data-empty` on the root when `items` is empty and not loading.
- `data-selectable` on the root mirrors `selectable`.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on each parent row and its chevron (drives the rotation); absent on leaves. The tree is not an overlay, so this is disclosure state only.
- `data-selected` on the selected row (only while `selectable`); `data-disabled` on a disabled row.
- Collapsed children are not rendered (`v-if`), so they cost nothing and are out of the accessibility tree.
- A disabled node can still be focused (arrow keys) and, if it is a parent, expanded and collapsed; it cannot be selected and does not emit `item-click`.
- `data-testid`: the root falls back to `data-tree` (a consumer `data-testid` wins); parts derive from the resolved root id — `<testId>-item` on every treeitem, `<testId>-toggle` on every chevron. Each treeitem also carries `data-item-id="<item.id>"` so a test reaches one node without depending on DOM order.
- Loading renders five Skeleton rows (`kind="shape"`, row height, descending widths) at top level.

## Accessibility

- Structure (WAI-ARIA tree pattern): the tree is a `<ul role="tree">` named by `ariaLabel`, inside the root wrapper that carries `data-testid` and `$attrs`. Each node is an `<li role="treeitem">` with `aria-level` (1-based), `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` (among its siblings), and `aria-labelledby` pointing at its label region (ids from `useId()`), so the name excludes the children and the actions. A parent carries `aria-expanded="true|false"` and, when expanded, renders its children in a nested `<ul role="group">` inside its `<li>`. Leaves carry no `aria-expanded`.
- Selection: while `selectable`, every treeitem carries `aria-selected="true|false"`; otherwise none does. `aria-multiselectable` is not set (single selection).
- Disabled: a disabled node carries `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Roving tabindex: exactly one treeitem has `tabindex="0"`, every other `-1`. The tab stop is the selected node when it is visible, else the last focused node when visible, else the first node. When the tab-stop node is hidden by a collapse (from the keyboard or from a `v-model:expanded` change), the tab stop moves to its nearest visible ancestor. Clicking a row moves the tab stop and focus to it.
- Keyboard map (required, on the focused treeitem):
  - `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` — focus the next / previous visible node, without wrapping.
  - `ArrowRight` — on a collapsed parent, expand it (focus stays); on an expanded parent, focus its first child; on a leaf, nothing.
  - `ArrowLeft` — on an expanded parent, collapse it (focus stays); otherwise focus the parent node; on a top-level collapsed parent or leaf, nothing.
  - `Home` / `End` — focus the first / last visible node.
  - `Enter` / `Space` — activate the node: select it when `selectable`, then emit `item-click`; nothing on a disabled node. `Space` does not scroll the page.
  - `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — leave the tree from the tab stop, passing through the focused row's `actions` controls (their natural tab order).
  - Arrow keys, `*` and type-ahead are not handled inside the `actions` region; `*` (expand siblings) and type-ahead are not part of v1.
- Chevron: a `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">` that toggles the parent on click (pointer affordance; keyboard expansion is ArrowRight / ArrowLeft on the treeitem). It never receives focus and is not announced.
- Visible focus: the ring is drawn on the focused node's own row, not around its whole subtree — `focus-visible:outline-none` on the treeitem and `ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on its direct row child (an arbitrary variant scoped to `:focus-visible > row`).
- Loading: the root carries `aria-busy="true"`; the Skeleton rows are `aria-hidden`, and no `role="tree"` is rendered without treeitems.
- Glyphs (`item.icon`), the chevron and the indent guide are decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label and description on the canvas, the hover fill and `var(--bg-selected)` in both themes; disabled text follows the disabled-token exemption.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the chevron and selection transitions; `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` on the hover layer.
- Touch target: rows are 32px tall and full width (the same deviation as `bar-list`), justified by row density in file trees; the whole row is the activation target and the chevron box extends to the row height.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the expand caret mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`) and rotates the other way when open (`rtl:data-[state=open]:-rotate-90`).
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight` expands a node or moves to its first child and `ArrowLeft` collapses it or moves to the parent, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: node labels are text; file names and IDs in another script keep their own direction.

<!-- components/doc-accordion-group.md -->

# Doc Accordion Group

> The FAQ and "expand for detail" block of a documentation page. It reads the `title` of each `DocAccordionItem` child to build the triggers and renders the child body in the panel, so an author writes only titles and prose. It always ships as a card (surface, outer rule, radius) so a run of rows reads as one closed group in an open prose column. Built on `Accordion` at `size="large"`.

- Import: `import DocAccordionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-group'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A list of questions with answers at the end of a guide.
- Optional detail that would interrupt the main path of a page (edge cases, troubleshooting).

## Do

- Write each title as the full question the reader would ask.
- Keep answers short; link out for anything longer than a few paragraphs.
- Open at most one entry by default.

## Don’t

- For steps the reader must follow in order — use `DocSteps`.
- For alternative paths through the same instruction — use `DocTabs`.
- Inside an application screen — use `Accordion` directly.

## Related

- DocAccordionItem` — the entry it reads.
- Accordion` — the design-system surface it renders on.
- Faq` — the marketing FAQ band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `'single' \ \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | false | Whether one or several entries can be open at once. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `DocAccordionItem` children, in order. Each child's `title` and `defaultOpen` are read; its body is rendered inside the panel. |

## States

- Each row mirrors `Accordion` `data-state=open|closed`.
- The last row drops its own bottom rule while closed so it does not double the card edge.
- `data-doc-block` puts the group on the block rung of `DocProse`.

## Accessibility

- Each trigger is a button inside an `h3`, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` from `Accordion`.
- Keyboard: `Tab` between triggers, `Enter`/`Space` toggles (from `Accordion`).
- The focus ring is drawn inside the button (`ring-inset`) so the card clipping does not cut it.
- Contrast: `--text-default` on `--bg-surface` in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only.
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged (the underlying component handles arrow direction).

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is content and arrives through props or slots, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- Fills its column; triggers wrap with `text-wrap-style: pretty` so a wrapped question keeps its chevron at the inline end.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocAccordionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-group'
  import DocAccordionItem from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-item'
</script>

<template>
  <DocAccordionGroup>
    <DocAccordionItem
      title="Why does my first request miss the cache?"
      default-open
    >
      <p>Each location warms up on its own first request. Warm-up is per location, not global.</p>
    </DocAccordionItem>
    <DocAccordionItem title="Can I purge a single path?">
      <p>Yes. Purge by URL for one object, or by wildcard for a folder.</p>
    </DocAccordionItem>
    <DocAccordionItem title="How long does a purge take to reach every location?">
      <p>Usually a few seconds. The purge request returns once every location has confirmed it.</p>
    </DocAccordionItem>
  </DocAccordionGroup>
</template>
```

<!-- components/doc-accordion-item.md -->

# Doc Accordion Item

> One collapsible entry inside a `DocAccordionGroup`. It carries its title and its body only; the group owns the open-state model, the trigger and the panel. Rendered on its own it is a `display: contents` wrapper around its body.

- Import: `import DocAccordionItem from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-item'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- As a direct child of `DocAccordionGroup`.

## Do

- Keep the title a question; keep the body prose.

## Don’t

- Outside a `DocAccordionGroup` — it renders no trigger of its own.

## Related

- DocAccordionGroup` — the group that reads it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The question the trigger shows; `DocAccordionGroup` reads it to build the row. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Opens this entry on first render. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The answer shown when the entry is open. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the group owns open and closed).

## Accessibility

- No role of its own; the group renders the heading, the button and the region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only.
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged (the underlying component handles arrow direction).

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is content and arrives through props or slots, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- Inherits the group.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocAccordionGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-group'
  import DocAccordionItem from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-accordion-item'
</script>

<template>
  <DocAccordionGroup>
    <DocAccordionItem
      title="Can I keep a stale object while the origin is down?"
      default-open
    >
      <p>
        Yes. Turn on stale cache and the last good copy is served until the origin answers again.
      </p>
    </DocAccordionItem>
  </DocAccordionGroup>
</template>
```

# Doc Agent Card

> The "Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" card that opens the first section of a documentation home. Two columns in one framed card: on the left the title, one or two sentences on what the prompt gives the agent, and the inline `CopyPromptButton` with the agent marks; on the right, behind a vertical divider, the question "Prefer the guided route?" over an orange `Agent setup` button, set on an orange halftone panel that fades in from the bottom corner. Below the card's `@3xl` container size the columns stack and the divider turns horizontal. All four strings default to the catalog, so `<DocAgentCard :prompt="…" />` is the whole reference card.

- Import: `import DocAgentCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-agent-card'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The first block under "Start by interface" (or the hero) of a documentation home, to hand the reader's coding agent the platform in one prompt and offer the guided setup next to it.

## Do

- Pass the exact prompt in `prompt`; leave the strings to the catalog unless the product differs.
- Point `action-href` at the agent setup guide.
- Follow it with a three-column `DocCardGroup` (Console, CLI, API) in the same section.
- Do not add an overline or an eyebrow above the title; the card has none.

## Don’t

- To show the prompt text itself → use `DocPrompt`.
- As a generic two-column banner → use `DocCard`, `DocCta` or a marketing `Banner`.
- On an article page → put `CopyPromptButton` in `DocPageHeader`'s meta actions instead.

## Related

- CopyPromptButton` — the left column's action.
- DocHero` — the masthead above it on a docs home.
- DocCardGroup` — the Console / CLI / API cards that follow it; both share `FrameBox`'s corner marks.
- TextureMaterial` — the `dither` halftone behind the guided action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | `—` | true | The prompt `CopyPromptButton` copies. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Card heading (an `h3`); empty uses the catalog's `Your AI agent, fluent in Azion`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences on what the prompt gives the agent; empty uses the catalog's. |
| `agents` | `CopyPromptAgent[]` | `undefined` | false | The agents whose marks the copy button shows; unset keeps the button's default list. |
| `asideTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Question over the guided action; empty uses the catalog's `Prefer the guided route?`. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the guided action; empty uses the catalog's `Agent setup`. |
| `actionHref` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination of the guided action; empty renders it as a button that only emits `action`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copy` | `string` | Re-emitted from `CopyPromptButton` after a successful copy. |
| `action` | `MouseEvent` | The guided action was activated. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` |  | Replaces the copy button in the left column. |

## States

- Wide (container ≥ `@3xl`): two columns, 7 : 3, vertical divider. Narrow: one column, horizontal divider.
- The copy button carries its own `idle` / `copied` / `disabled` states.
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `open`/`closed`.

## Accessibility

- A `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`), with the title as an `h3` (it sits under the section's `h2`).
- The halftone is `aria-hidden` and never sits under text that needs contrast: the question and the button keep ≥ 4.5:1 on the surface.
- The actions keep their own roles, names and focus rings; reading order is left column, then right.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s`, `end-0`); the divider and the halftone move to the mirrored side, and the dither ramp runs toward the bottom-left.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source                   | Override prop |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `docAgentCard.title`      | `Your AI agent, fluent in Azion` | `title`       |
| `docAgentCard.description`| `One prompt teaches any coding agent the platform: …` | `description` |
| `docAgentCard.asideTitle` | `Prefer the guided route?`       | `asideTitle`  |
| `docAgentCard.action`     | `Agent setup`                    | `actionLabel` |

## Responsive

- Container query on the card itself (`@container`): two columns from `@3xl`, stacked below it.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the copy button truncates its label before overflowing.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocAgentCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-agent-card'

  const prompt =
    'Set up the Azion CLI, connect the Azion docs over MCP and link this project to my Azion account.'
</script>

<template>
  <DocAgentCard
    :prompt="prompt"
    action-href="#"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/doc-callout.md -->

# Doc Callout

> The admonition a documentation page interrupts itself with — Note, Info, Tip, Check, Warning, Danger — rendered on the webkit `Alert` surface, so the severity colour, the border, the icon and the radius come from the design system rather than from this layer. Its anatomy is a glyph and a column of prose — a sentence, or a few short paragraphs and a list — nothing else: no title row.

- Import: `import DocCallout from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-callout'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An aside the reader must not miss mid-prose: a caveat, a prerequisite, a warning about data loss.
- A short confirmation that a step worked (`check`), or a shortcut worth knowing (`tip`).

## Do

- Let the glyph and the tint carry the severity; do not restate it in the copy ("Warning: …").
- Keep the body short — a sentence or two, links and inline code. A list is fine when the aside enumerates actions; the callout lays it out itself, because `DocProse` stops at its edge.
- Reach for `tip` when the aside claims nothing about stakes. Borrowing `check` for a friendly shortcut paints a shortcut the same green as a confirmed success.

## Don’t

- For a block that needs its own box — a fenced sample, a table, a card grid. Those belong outside the callout; its body is prose, at most a short list.
- For an application-screen banner or a form error — use `Alert` directly, which is what this composes.
- As a section heading. A callout is an interruption, not structure.

## Related

- Alert` — the webkit surface this renders on; reach for it directly outside documentation prose.
- DocProse` — the contract around it. A callout marks itself `data-doc-chrome`, so prose rules stop at its edge, and `data-doc-block`, so it takes the block rung of the ladder.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'note' \| 'info' \| 'tip' \| 'check' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'note'` | false | Which admonition this is; drives the severity color and the icon. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback copy when the default slot is empty. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The callout copy: prose with links and inline code, or paragraphs and a list, laid out by the callout since `DocProse` stops at its edge. The copy region is a flow container, so server-rendered block markup stays inside the box. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the component is not interactive and holds no state)
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop, so a test or a consumer can target one flavour
- `data-neutral` is present only for `tip`, the one kind that carries no severity
- `data-doc-block` + `data-doc-chrome` are the `DocProse` contract (block rung; prose stops here)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the callout is not focusable; a link inside it inherits the prose focus ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` reaches only a link in the copy.
- ARIA: the role comes from `Alert`; the glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so the copy is the accessible content.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: the copy is `--text-default` in every kind, measured 13.31:1–18.97:1 across the six fills in both themes. The inline-code chip keeps `--text-default` too, measured 10.05:1–14.43:1 — the severity ink on that chip drops to 4.03:1 in dark danger, which is why it is not used.
- `tip` deliberately does **not** speak in `--text-muted` (3.95:1 light, under AA).
- Touch target: not applicable; the component is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocCallout from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-callout'
</script>

<template>
  <DocCallout kind="note">
    The first request to a location is a cache miss. Warm-up is per location, not global.
  </DocCallout>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/doc-callout.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-callout.md).

<!-- components/doc-card.md -->

# Doc Card

> One cell of the grid a documentation page scans across: a leading glyph, an optional eyebrow, the title, the copy, and an optional call-to-action row at the foot. It renders as an anchor when it has an `href` and as a plain block when it does not, so a card is either a destination or a statement — never a dead link.

- Import: `import DocCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A grid of peer destinations: "what you can build", the product tiles a landing section opens with.
- A set of short, scannable entries whose titles carry most of the meaning.

## Do

- Keep the title to a noun phrase and let the copy carry the verb.
- Use `eyebrow` only when the title alone does not say who or when; it is not a category label.
- Set `link-label` when the card should close on an explicit call to action; otherwise the whole tile being the link is enough.

## Don’t

- When each entry needs a sentence to be understood — use `DocItem` rows, one column, so every description is read at the page's own measure instead of squeezed into a cell.
- For a single call to action at the end of a page — that is a button, not a card.
- For an application surface — use `Card`, which is the console's carded surface.

## Related

- DocCardGroup` — the frame and grid this is a cell of; a card outside one has no cell ring.
- DocItem` — the row counterpart. A card claims a whole tile; a row claims one line.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Card heading. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Small muted line above the title — who makes the thing, when the title does not say. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons class for the leading glyph. Ignored when the `icon` slot is filled. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination; when set the whole card becomes the link. |
| `target` | `'_self' \| '_blank'` | `'_self'` | false | Where the link opens. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback copy when the default slot is empty. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Call-to-action text; when set the card closes on a link row. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Card copy. |
| `icon` | — | The leading mark, when a font glyph will not do. Replaces `icon`. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` — the last two only when the card is a link
- The root element switches on data, not on an `as` prop: an anchor when `href` is set, a plain block otherwise
- `data-doc-chrome` is the `DocProse` contract (prose rules stop at the card's edge)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a linked card takes `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the anchor root.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches a linked card; `Enter` follows it. A card with no `href` is not focusable and not announced as interactive.
- ARIA: the accessible name is the card's own title text — the anchor wraps the content, so nothing is duplicated into an `aria-label`. The glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- A card that leaves the documentation (absolute URL, `mailto:`, or explicit `target="_blank"`) carries `rel="noreferrer"` and swaps the chevron for a diagonal arrow, so the destination change is visible and not colour-only.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- Touch target: the whole tile is the hit area, comfortably over 40×40 px.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the chevron mirrors; the external-link arrow does not, but its hover nudge moves toward the end edge (`rtl:group-hover:-translate-x-0.5`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card'
</script>

<template>
  <DocCard
    title="Edge Application"
    icon="pi pi-server"
    href="/docs/edge-application"
    link-label="Read the guide"
  >
    Serve and cache your application at the edge, close to the people using it.
  </DocCard>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-card.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-card.md).

<!-- components/doc-card-group.md -->

# Doc Card Group

> The framed, responsive grid a `DocCard` set sits in. The group is the frame, not each card: `FrameBox` draws the perimeter and the four corner registration marks once around the whole set, the grid keeps 1px gaps, and every cell paints a 1px ring into them — so two neighbours share one hairline, an incomplete last row stays simply empty, and the set reads as one object the reader scans across rather than as loose tiles. `cols` names the widest column count; the grid always steps down toward one column on a phone unless a set of tiny cells opts into two with `mobileColumns`.

- Import: `import DocCardGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card-group'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Around every `DocCard` set — a card outside a group has no frame and no cell ring.
- The fan-out at the top of a landing or section-index page: product tiles, a framework grid, a "what you can build" band.

## Do

- Pick `cols` for the widest screen and let the breakpoints do the rest; do not wrap the group in another grid.
- Leave `mobileColumns` at 1 unless every cell is a mark plus one word — a card with copy needs the whole phone width.
- Let an incomplete last row be empty; do not stretch the last card to fill it.

## Don’t

- When each entry needs a full-measure sentence to be understood — use `DocItem` rows, one column, instead of cells.
- As a general-purpose layout grid for application screens; it is documentation chrome, tied to the `DocProse` ladder.

## Related

- DocCard` — the cell this frames; the group draws the perimeter and the cells paint the internal rules.
- FrameBox` — the layout primitive that draws the frame and the corner registration marks.
- DocProse` — the contract around it; `data-doc-block` puts the group on the block rung of the prose ladder.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cols` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | false | Column count at the large breakpoint. |
| `mobileColumns` | `1 \| 2` | `1` | false | Column count on a phone. Two only pays when the cells are a mark plus a word. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `DocCard` children. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the component is not interactive and holds no state)
- `data-cols` and `data-mobile-cols` mirror `cols` and `mobileColumns`; Tailwind data-variants switch the grid's column count on them at the `sm` and `lg` breakpoints
- `data-doc-block` is the `DocProse` contract (the group takes the block rung of the ladder)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the group is not focusable; a linked `DocCard` inside it carries its own inset focus ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` moves through the linked cards in DOM order, which follows the grid's reading order.
- ARIA: no role is added; the group is pure layout, so assistive tech reads the cards as a plain sequence of links.
- Contrast: the frame and the hairline rules are decorative; every readable surface belongs to the cells, which own their contrast.
- Touch target: not applicable; the component itself is not interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocCard from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card'
  import DocCardGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-card-group'
</script>

<template>
  <DocCardGroup :cols="2">
    <DocCard
      title="Start from a template"
      icon="pi pi-th-large"
      href="#templates"
    >
      Ready-made projects that go live in a few clicks. No local tooling.
    </DocCard>
    <DocCard
      title="Import from GitHub"
      icon="pi pi-github"
      href="#github"
    >
      Connect a repository and let Azion build it on every push.
    </DocCard>
  </DocCardGroup>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/doc-card-group.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/doc-card-group.md).
