<!-- components/doc-update.md -->

# Doc Update

> One entry in a changelog: what shipped, when, and under which version. The release's identity sits in a left column — the date, the version under it, the tags under that — the notes sit on the right, and a rule runs between them for the length of the entry and bridges the block gap to the next one, so a set of entries reads as one continuous timeline rather than a stack of boxes. The label is an `h2` and a link to its own id, because every entry is a URL somebody sends — the id is the label slugified, unless an explicit `anchor` overrides it. Given a `title`, the entry becomes a release: the label turns into a plain date beside a node on the rule, and the title takes the `h2`, the anchor and the tags, sized above every heading the notes carry.

- Import: `import DocUpdate from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-update'`
- Category: documentation · Surface: docs · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A changelog or release-notes page: one `DocUpdate` per release, newest first, inside `DocProse`.
- Any dated series a reader scans by its left edge — announcements, incident retrospectives, versioned API changes.

## Do

- Put the date (or release name) in `label` and the version in `description` — the left edge is what a reader scans, so the label carries the identity.
- Give each release its own entry with a `title` when one date ships several things — one title per entry, the date repeated, rather than several product headings inside one entry.
- Keep headings inside an entry one level below the heading: the label (or the `title`, when set) is the entry's `h2`.
- Set `anchor` only when two entries share a label; otherwise let the id derive from the label so shared links match what readers see.

## Don’t

- For a single dated aside inside a guide — that is a `DocCallout`, not a timeline entry.
- As a styled row inside another section. The label is an `h2`, so every entry claims a slot in the page outline; nesting one under a deeper heading breaks the outline.
- To generate a feed. Mintlify's `rss` prop is deliberately absent — this layer renders pages and generates nothing, so the prop would be inert.

## Related

- DocProse` — the contract around it: `data-doc-block` takes the block rung of the spacing ladder, and `data-doc-chrome` keeps prose rules off the label column.
- Tag` — renders the entry's tags row (`severity="secondary"`): small and rounded in the label column, medium with the default shape under a `title`.
- use-heading-nav` — the composable the label anchor calls. A page that owns its scroll container provides a scroller-aware handler with `provideHeadingNav`; rendered outside a provider, the injected default is a no-op — never a throw — and the browser's native hash navigation takes over.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | The entry's name — a date, a release name. Also its anchor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The release's heading, shown above the notes. The label becomes the date beside it. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Secondary line under the label; usually the version. |
| `tags` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Short labels categorising the entry: a product, an area, a kind of change. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Anchor override; wins over the slug derived from the label. Set it when two entries share a label. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The release notes: prose, lists, code, or any documentation component. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, plus `hover` / `focus-visible` on the label anchor — the label underlines and the chain glyph fades in
- Anchor derivation: an explicit `anchor` prop wins; otherwise the id is the `label` slugified (inline markup stripped, lowercased, kebab-cased), or the `label` and `title` slugified together when a `title` is set, so entries sharing a date stay distinct. The `h2` takes the same id with a `-label` suffix, and the section's `aria-labelledby` points at it
- Heading navigation degrades gracefully: the anchor calls the handler a page provided via `provideHeadingNav`; outside a provider the injected default is a no-op — activation never throws, and native hash navigation handles the jump
- `data-doc-block` + `data-doc-update` mark the entry for `DocProse` block rhythm and let an entry that follows another bridge the rule through the block gap; `data-doc-chrome` keeps prose rules off the label column
- Below `md` the columns stack and the rule drops; from `md` up the label column sticks (`md:sticky`) while the notes scroll past
- Titled (`title` set, `data-titled` on the root and notes column): the label renders as a date, not a heading, centred on the title's first line; a decorative node sits on the rule at the same line (`md` up), centred on the rule in both directions (`-translate-x-1/2`, `rtl:translate-x-1/2`); the title is the `h2` and self-link, the tags move under it, and consecutive titled entries are padded apart below the notes

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `h2` inside a `section` whose `aria-labelledby` points at it, so every entry is a named region and joins the page outline and the "On this page" rail. With a `title`, the title is that `h2` and the date is plain text, so the region is named by what shipped.
- The titled node on the rule is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the heading anchor (the label, or the title when set); `Enter` follows it — through the page's provided heading-nav handler, or native hash navigation without one. Nothing else in the entry's chrome is interactive.
- Visible focus: the anchor takes `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2` in the ring token.
- The chain glyph is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and revealed on `focus-visible` as well as hover, so the self-link affordance is not pointer-only.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- Touch target: the label anchor is a text link on its own line in the label column, with nothing else competing for the hit area.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DocProse from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-prose'
  import DocUpdate from '@aziontech/webkit/doc-update'
</script>

<template>
  <DocProse>
    <DocUpdate
      label="August 19, 2026"
      description="v2.4.0"
      :tags="['Console', 'Edge Functions']"
    >
      <p>
        Rules Engine conditions now match on request headers, so a rule can branch on anything the
        client sends without a function in the path.
      </p>
    </DocUpdate>
  </DocProse>
</template>
```

<!-- components/alert.md -->

# Alert

> Inline feedback banner that communicates status, alerts, or progress. Presents a severity-colored surface with a leading icon and a single line of message copy that may carry inline links, plus an optional secondary action button.

- Import: `import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A status, warning or error that belongs to a page, section or form and should stay visible in context.
- A notice with an inline link, or with one follow-up action (`actionLabel` or the `action` slot).

## Do

- Pick `severity` by meaning. `danger` and `warning` render with `role="alert"`.
- Use `label` for plain copy and the default slot when the copy needs inline links.
- Use either the built-in action (`actionLabel` with `@action`) or the `action` slot, not both. The slot replaces the button.
- Once `closable` or `life` dismisses the message, it stays hidden until it is remounted. Listen to `close` to keep your own state in sync.
- Use `size="small"` inside dense surfaces such as cards and drawers.

## Don’t

- A transient confirmation of an action → use `toast`.
- Validation feedback under one form field → use `helper-text`.
- An admonition inside documentation prose → use `doc-callout`.
- A promotional band between page sections → use `banner`.

## Related

- `toast` — overlay stack raised imperatively, auto-dismissing and not anchored to content.
- `helper-text` — field-level guidance and errors below an input.
- `doc-callout` — docs admonition rendered on the `Alert` surface.
- `empty-state` — a full zero-data block, not a status banner.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'info'` | false | Visual severity variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token. Drives the banner height, inline padding, copy scale, and the trailing control sizes. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback message copy when the default slot is empty. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons class override for the leading icon. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label for the built-in secondary action button; hidden when empty. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, shows a close control that dismisses the message. |
| `life` | `number` | `0` | false | Duration in milliseconds before auto-dismiss; `0` disables auto-dismiss. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `MouseEvent` | Emitted when the built-in action button is clicked. |
| `close` | `void` | Emitted when the message is dismissed manually or after `life` expires. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | — | Custom action control; replaces the built-in Button when provided. |
| `default` | — | Alert copy. Inline content — plain text plus anchors, which the message region styles with the `.text-link` token — or flow content such as paragraphs and a list. The copy region is a flow container (a `div`, not a `p`), so block markup arriving from a server render stays inside it instead of being closed out beside the copy. Falls back to `label` when empty. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: default (per severity)
- Responsive: the root is the `@container/alert`. Below `@sm` of its box the action (built-in or the `action` slot, wrapped in `[data-slot=alert-action]`) moves to its own line under the message while the close button stays on the message line.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses inline links in the message copy, then the action and close controls when present; `Enter` follows a link, `Enter`/`Space` activates the controls; `Escape` dismisses when `closable` is true.
- ARIA: root uses `role="alert"` for danger/warning severities and `role="status"` for info/success.
- Inline links are underlined, not colour-only, so they stay distinguishable against every severity surface (WCAG 1.4.1); the `.text-link` token supplies the focus outline.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Alert from '@aziontech/webkit/alert'
</script>

<template>
  <Alert
    severity="info"
    label="Your workload finished deploying in 42 seconds."
    action-label="Label"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/alert.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/alert.md).

<!-- components/empty-state.md -->

# Empty State

> Centered placeholder shown when a resource list or section has no content yet. Stacks an optional standardized adornment, a title, an optional description, and a consumer-composed actions area (buttons + documentation link) to guide the user toward a first action. The adornment is a standardized, size-scaled featured-icon tile driven by the `icon` prop; the consumer may instead supply custom content via the `icon` slot, or omit both for no adornment. Unlike `Alert`, which is an inline severity banner, `EmptyState` is a full-region zero-data state and renders either inside a bordered surface card or on a plain transparent background.

- Import: `import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A list, table or section that has no items yet, with a first action that fills it.
- A search or filter that returned nothing, with an action to clear it.

## Do

- title` is required. Say what is missing ("No domains yet"), not that something went wrong.
- Keep the `actions` slot to one primary action, plus an optional documentation link.
- Leave the actions at their own width, centred, on every screen size (the design sample's look). Do not add `w-full` to a button in the slot to make it span a phone screen.
- Use the `icon` prop for the standard featured-icon tile. Use the `icon` slot only for custom art, and omit both when the context already explains the state.
- Use `bordered` when the block sits directly on the page. Leave it off inside a card or panel that already has a border, and use `size="small"` there.

## Don’t

- The data is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- An inline warning or error about content that is present → use `message`.
- The empty body of a data-driven `table` → use the `table` `empty` slot, which already renders this block by default.

## Related

- `skeleton` — the loading placeholder shown before the empty state is known.
- message` — inline severity banner, not a zero-data block.
- `table` — renders an empty-state block in its `empty` slot.
- `button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Primary heading announcing the empty resource. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting body copy below the title. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | PrimeIcons/Azion icon class for the standardized adornment (e.g. `pi pi-inbox`). When set, renders a size-scaled featured-icon tile; when empty and the `icon` slot is unused, no adornment renders. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token (subset — only `small` and `medium`; no `large`). Scales the whole block on one harmonic ramp — the adornment size, the title and description typography, the surrounding padding, and the gaps between adornment, text, and actions all step up together. |
| `bordered` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, wraps the content in a dashed-bordered surface card; otherwise renders on a transparent background. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | — | Custom adornment centered above the title, rendered inside an `aria-hidden` container. Overrides the `icon` prop's featured-icon tile. When neither this slot nor the `icon` prop is provided, no adornment renders. |
| `actions` | — | Action area below the description; consumer composes buttons and the documentation link. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-bordered` mirrors the `bordered` prop
- Responsive: the actions keep their own width and stay centred at every box width, as the design sample draws them (a phone included); the action column is capped at `max-w-full`, so a long label wraps inside the box instead of overflowing it.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses the consumer-supplied controls in the `actions` slot in DOM order; the region itself is non-interactive.
- ARIA: root uses `role="status"` so assistive tech announces the empty-data message; the `icon` slot container is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import EmptyState from '@aziontech/webkit/empty-state'
  import MiniButton from '@aziontech/webkit/mini-button'
</script>

<template>
  <EmptyState
    title="No resource yet"
    description="Get started by creating your first resource."
    icon="pi pi-inbox"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <div class="flex gap-(--spacing-3)">
        <Button
          kind="secondary"
          label="Secondary Item"
        />
        <Button
          kind="outlined"
          label="Create Item"
        />
      </div>
      <MiniButton
        label="Docs"
        icon="pi pi-arrow-right"
        size="medium"
        href="#"
      />
    </template>
  </EmptyState>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/empty-state.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/empty-state.md).

<!-- components/error-boundary.md -->

# Error Boundary

> Guards one region of a page. When a component inside the region throws while it renders, sets up or runs a lifecycle hook, the boundary catches the error, reports it through its `error` event, and puts a recoverable message in the region's place: a danger `Alert` that says the section failed and offers **Try again**, which mounts the region again. The rest of the page keeps working. A `fallback` slot replaces the built-in message when the region needs a different shape (a card-sized `EmptyState`, for example).

- Import: `import ErrorBoundary from '@aziontech/webkit/error-boundary'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A dashboard card, a side panel, a tab body or any region whose failure should not take the whole page down.
- A region that renders data you do not control (a third-party widget, a chart fed by a remote response, a plugin).
- Around each route's content inside the app shell, so a failing page leaves the navigation usable (pass the route path as `resetKey`).
- When the app reports render errors to a monitoring service: the `error` event carries the error and where it was thrown.

## Do

- Wrap regions, not the whole app. One boundary per card, panel or route body keeps the blast radius small.
- Report every error: listen to `error` and send it to your monitoring service. The boundary stops the error from reaching the app error handler unless `propagate` is set.
- Make Retry mean something. Listen to `retry` and reset the state that broke the region (refetch, clear the bad value) before it mounts again; a retry that renders the same bad data fails again.
- Pass `resetKey` when the region shows different content for different keys (route path, record id), so moving on from a failed record clears the fallback.
- Keep the fallback the size of the region. In a card, use a small `EmptyState`; in a page body, the built-in `Alert` is right.

## Don’t

- A request that failed (a fetch, a mutation): that is data state, not a render error. Show it in the region with an `alert` and a Retry, as `platform/states/form-error` and `skills/webkit-ui-states` describe.
- A whole page that cannot be shown (missing route, no access, server failure) → use the `platform/states/not-found` block.
- A field that failed validation → use `field` with its error message.
- Errors thrown in click or submit handlers you can catch yourself: catch them where you call the action and show the outcome with `toast` or `alert`.

## Related

- `alert` — the built-in fallback; also what a failed request shows inside a region that rendered fine.
- `empty-state` — a common custom fallback for a card-sized region.
- `skeleton` — what the region shows while it loads; the boundary only covers the failed case.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of an action; never use it for a region that failed to render.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`This section failed to load`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the heading of the built-in fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `retryLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the built-in Retry action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Try again`). |
| `resetKey` | `string \| number` | `undefined` | false | When this value changes while the fallback shows, the region is mounted again (pass the route path or the record id). |
| `propagate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the error keeps travelling to the parent boundaries and the app error handler after this boundary handles it. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error` | `ErrorBoundaryErrorEvent` | Fires once per failure with `{ error, info }`: what was thrown and Vue's description of where. Report it from here. |
| `retry` | `void` | Fires when the region is mounted again (Retry, the slot's `retry`, or a `resetKey` change). Reset the broken state here. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The region the boundary guards. Mounted again, from scratch, on every retry. |
| `fallback` | { error: unknown, retry: () => void } | Replaces the built-in `Alert` while the region is failed. Call `retry` to mount it again. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (the region renders), `error` (the fallback renders in its place)
- `data-error` on the root is present while the fallback shows
- A second error captured while the fallback already shows (a failing custom fallback) is not handled again: it travels to the parent, so a broken fallback can never loop.
- What the boundary catches is what Vue's `onErrorCaptured` catches from descendant components: errors in render, setup, watchers, lifecycle hooks and component event handlers. Errors thrown directly in the slot's own markup belong to the component that owns the markup, and errors in native DOM listeners or promises outside Vue are not caught.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the root is focusable only by script (`tabindex="-1"`, `outline-none`) and never in the tab order; the Retry button carries the `Button` focus ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the Retry action in the fallback; `Enter` / `Space` runs it. No key handling of its own.
- Focus: when the region fails while focus was inside it (or had fallen to the document body), focus moves to the fallback `Alert`, which is announced. After a retry from inside the boundary, focus moves to the boundary's root so it is not lost to the body.
- ARIA: the built-in fallback is an `Alert` with `role="alert"` (danger), so the failure is announced once when it appears. A custom fallback is responsible for its own announcement (`EmptyState` is `role="status"`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): inherited from the `alert` danger tokens.
- No motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the Retry action is a `Button`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: the boundary adds no layout; the `Alert` uses logical utilities and puts the action at the inline end.
- Icons: the danger glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key navigation.
- User data: the error message is never rendered by the built-in fallback; none.

## Internationalization

| Key                         | English source                                                                              | Override prop |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `errorBoundary.title`       | This section failed to load                                                                 | `title`       |
| `errorBoundary.description` | Something went wrong while showing this part of the page. The rest of the page still works. | `description` |
| `errorBoundary.retry`       | Try again                                                                                   | `retryLabel`  |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; the `Alert` is `@container/alert` and moves its action under the copy in a narrow region.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): the action wraps under the text (from `alert`).
- Touch: the Retry button is 40 px; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BarList from '@aziontech/webkit/bar-list'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
  import ErrorBoundary from '@aziontech/webkit/error-boundary'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const items = [
    { id: 'web-app-prod', name: 'web-app-prod', value: 11420000 },
    { id: 'payments-api', name: 'payments-api', value: 6240000 },
    { id: 'storefront-checkout', name: 'storefront-checkout', value: 4910000 }
  ]

  const broken = ref(false)
  const reported = ref('')

  const format = (value) =>
    new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { notation: 'compact', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(value)

  const failingFormat = () => {
    throw new Error('The response held a value the list could not read.')
  }

  const report = ({ error }) => {
    reported.value = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
  }

  const recover = () => {
    broken.value = false
    reported.value = ''
  }
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-[512px] flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Card title="Top services">
      <template #content>
        <ErrorBoundary
          @error="report"
          @retry="recover"
        >
          <BarList
            :items="items"
            :format-value="broken ? failingFormat : format"
            aria-label="Top services by requests"
          />
        </ErrorBoundary>
      </template>
    </Card>
    <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-xs)">
      <Button
        label="Simulate a failure"
        kind="outlined"
        size="medium"
        :disabled="broken"
        @click="broken = true"
      />
      <p
        v-if="reported"
        class="m-0 text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)"
      >
        Reported: {{ reported }}
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/error-boundary.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/error-boundary.md).

<!-- components/outcome-mark.md -->

# Outcome Mark

> A small round mark that states how something ended: a check for success, a cross for danger, an exclamation for warning and a dash for neutral (not set, not run). It replaces the design sample's `StateMark` and `SuccessMark`. With `animated` the disc scales in and the glyph draws itself when the mark appears and every time its severity changes, so an outcome screen or a finished row can mark the moment a run lands; under reduced motion it shows at once.

- Import: `import OutcomeMark from '@aziontech/webkit/outcome-mark'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- At the head of an outcome screen (deploy succeeded or failed), at the large size, animated.
- In a checklist or a list of steps, at the small size, to say a step is done or not set.
- Beside a label that reports a finished run, when the run's state turns from running to an outcome.

## Do

- Pair the mark with words that say the same thing; the mark is not the only cue.
- Animate only the mark that just changed; a list of animated marks on load is noise.
- Give a specific `ariaLabel` (`Deployed`, `Done`) when the catalog name is too generic.

## Don’t

- A state that is still running → use `spinner` or `status-indicator` with `loading`.
- A labelled status pill in a table cell → use `tag` or `status-indicator`.
- A message with text and actions → use `alert` or `toast`.

## Related

- `status-indicator` — a coloured dot with a label, for live states.
- `tag` — a labelled pill for a state.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of an async action wherever the user is.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'success' \| 'danger' \| 'warning' \| 'neutral'` | `'success'` | false | The outcome the mark shows: a check, a cross, an exclamation or a dash. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token: 16, 20 or 48 px. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Scales the disc in and draws the glyph when it appears or its severity changes; static under reduced motion. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name. Empty uses the locale catalog name of the severity. |

## States

- `data-severity`: `success` | `danger` | `warning` | `neutral`; `data-size`: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-state`: `pending` (disc scaled down and transparent, glyph undrawn) | `settled`; a static mark is always `settled`
- `data-animated` mirrors the `animated` prop

## Accessibility

- Not focusable; no keyboard map.
- ARIA: the root `svg` is `role="img"` named by `ariaLabel` or the catalog name of the severity.
- The shape of the glyph tells the outcomes apart without colour (WCAG 1.4.1); glyph against disc meets 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) in both themes.
- Motion is decorative and skipped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: no layout of its own.
- Icons: the check, cross, exclamation and dash are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: none.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                    | English source  | Override prop |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------- |
| `outcomeMark.success` | Succeeded       | `ariaLabel`   |
| `outcomeMark.danger`  | Failed          | `ariaLabel`   |
| `outcomeMark.warning` | Needs attention | `ariaLabel`   |
| `outcomeMark.neutral` | Not set         | `ariaLabel`   |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none: fixed size per `size`.
- Narrow: unchanged.
- Touch: not interactive.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import OutcomeMark from '@aziontech/webkit/outcome-mark'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-(--spacing-lg)">
    <OutcomeMark severity="success" />
    <OutcomeMark severity="danger" />
    <OutcomeMark severity="warning" />
    <OutcomeMark severity="neutral" />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/outcome-mark.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/outcome-mark.md).

<!-- components/progress.md -->

# Progress

> Communicates the progress of an ongoing task as a horizontal bar. Use it for a determinate value within a range (`value` / `max`) or, when progress can't be measured, as an indeterminate loading indicator. Unlike `skeleton` (placeholder geometry) or `status-indicator` (discrete state), it expresses a continuous quantity.

- Import: `import Progress from '@aziontech/webkit/progress'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A task with measurable progress: an upload, a build, a multi-step import.
- A bar-shaped busy indicator at the top of a region when progress can't be measured (`indeterminate`).

## Do

- Pass `value` on the scale of `max`, for example `:value="3" :max="5"` for steps. Don't convert it to a percentage yourself.
- Switch to `indeterminate` when progress is unknown. `value` is then ignored and `aria-valuenow` is dropped.
- There is no label prop. Give the bar an accessible name with an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute, and show the percentage in text next to it if users need the number.
- The default is the thin `small` bar with `flat` corners. Use `shape="rounded"` and a larger `size` only when the bar stands alone.

## Don’t

- A placeholder for content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- A busy state inside a button or another compact control → use `spinner` (or the control's own `loading` prop).
- A discrete state with no quantity, such as Active or Failed → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `skeleton` — reserves the layout of loading content instead of showing task progress.
- `spinner` — compact, always-indeterminate busy glyph.
- `status-indicator` — labelled dot for a settled or transitional state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | `0` | false | Current progress, relative to `max`. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | false | Upper bound; percentage = `value / max * 100`. |
| `shape` | `'rounded' \| 'flat'` | `'flat'` | false | Track and fill corner-radius variant. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'small'` | false | Bar height token. |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Loading state; animates a sliding segment and ignores `value`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `indeterminate`
- `data-shape` mirrors the `shape` prop: `rounded` | `flat`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-indeterminate` is present while `indeterminate` is `true`

## Accessibility

- Non-interactive: the bar is not focusable and takes no keyboard input.
- Name: the bar takes `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` from the consumer; with neither it is named by the locale catalog (`progress.label`, "Progress"), so a bare bar never fails `aria-progressbar-name`.
- ARIA: root uses `role="progressbar"`. Determinate sets `aria-valuemin="0"`, `aria-valuemax="<max>"`, `aria-valuenow="<value>"`; indeterminate omits `aria-valuenow` and sets `aria-busy="true"`.
- Contrast ≥3:1 between the fill (`var(--primary)`) and the track (`var(--bg-placeholder)`). The track is an alpha overlay, not an opaque surface, so it keeps that contrast on any background the bar is placed over (canvas, surface, raised, overlay).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the determinate width morph and `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the indeterminate animation (it falls back to a static fill under reduced motion).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Progress from '@aziontech/webkit/progress'
</script>

<template>
  <Progress :value="60" />
</template>
```

<!-- components/skeleton.md -->

# Skeleton

> A loading placeholder that reserves the space of content while it loads, gently pulsing to signal activity. Use it in place of text lines, media, or avatars during fetches; unlike `status-indicator` (which communicates a settled state) the skeleton is a transient, decorative stand-in. Two geometries cover the common cases: a rounded rectangular block (`shape`) and a `circle` (for avatars / icons).

- Import: `import Skeleton from '@aziontech/webkit/skeleton'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Content is loading and its final layout is known: text lines, cards, media blocks.
- Avatar and icon placeholders, with `kind="circle"`.

## Do

- Size each skeleton like the content it stands in for (`width`, `height`) so nothing shifts when the data arrives.
- For `kind="circle"`, set `width` and `height` to the same value.
- The skeleton is `aria-hidden`. Mark the container you own with `aria-busy="true"` while it loads.
- Keep `animated` on (the default). The shimmer already turns off under reduced motion; use `:animated="false"` only for static captures.

## Don’t

- The duration is unknown and no layout is reserved → use `progress` with `indeterminate`, or `spinner`.
- Rows in a data-driven `table` → use the `table` `loading` prop, which renders aligned skeleton rows.
- Loading finished with no data → use `empty-state`.
- A settled state such as Active or Failed → use `status-indicator`.

## Related

- `progress` — measured or indeterminate progress of a task, not a placeholder.
- `spinner` — compact busy glyph for buttons and inline status.
- `empty-state` — what replaces the skeleton when the request returns nothing.
- `table` — its `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for you.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'shape' \| 'circle'` | `'shape'` | false | Geometry: a rounded rectangular block (`shape`) or a circle. |
| `width` | `string` | `'100%'` | false | CSS width (any length). |
| `height` | `string` | `'1rem'` | false | CSS height (any length); for a circle, set equal to `width`. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shimmer while loading; suppressed under reduced motion. |

## States

- Visual states: `default` (a single decorative placeholder; no hover/focus/active — it is not interactive)
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop (`shape` | `circle`)
- `data-animated` is present when `animated` is true (drives the shimmer)

## Accessibility

- The skeleton is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"` so assistive tech skips it. The loading status is conveyed by the surrounding region (e.g. `aria-busy="true"` on the container the consumer owns), not by the placeholder itself.
- Not focusable, not interactive: no keyboard map, no focus ring.
- The shimmer is gated behind `motion-safe:` and `motion-reduce:animate-none` suppresses it for users who prefer reduced motion (static flat fill).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Skeleton from '@aziontech/webkit/skeleton'
</script>

<template>
  <Skeleton
    kind="shape"
    width="240px"
    height="100px"
    animated
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/skeleton.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/skeleton.md).

# Status Indicator

> Communicates status, alerts, or progress to the user. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/feedback/status-indicator/`.

- Import: `import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The state of a resource in a table cell, a list row or a detail header: Active, Failed, Paused.
- A transitional state such as Deploying or Propagating, with `loading`.

## Do

- Always pass `label`. The default is the literal `'Status'`, and the color alone does not carry the meaning.
- Map `severity` to meaning and keep it consistent across the app: `success`, `info`, `warning` and `danger` follow their tokens, `neutral` is muted, and `alt` uses the primary color.
- With `loading`, pass the bare verb (`"Deploying"`). The component appends the ellipsis character (`…`, not three periods) and swaps the dot for a spinner. A label that already ends in `…` or `...` (copy pasted from a design: `"Building..."`) is trimmed first, so it renders `Building…`, never `Building......`.
- It is a non-interactive `role="status"` element with no click or keyboard behavior. Don't attach handlers to it.

## Don’t

- A count or a very short label attached to another element → use `badge`.
- A category or status chip with an optional icon → use `tag`.
- A page or section notice with copy and actions → use `message`.
- Measurable progress → use `progress`.

## Related

- `badge` — filled count indicator, usually overlaid on an icon or avatar.
- `tag` — labelled chip for categories and statuses.
- `spinner` — replaces the dot while `loading` is true.
- `progress` — continuous progress instead of a discrete state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `severity` | `'success' \| 'info' \| 'neutral' \| 'warning' \| 'alt' \| 'danger'` | `'success'` | false | Severity token driving the status dot color. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Transitional state: a spinner replaces the dot and the label gains a trailing ellipsis (`…`), so pass the bare verb; a trailing `…` or `...` already in the label is not doubled. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label text. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Status`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Forced colors: the dot opts out of forced colour adjustment and paints `CanvasText`, so it stays visible when backgrounds are forced to `Canvas`; the severity is still carried by the label text, never by the dot's colour alone. Tests: `src/test/forced-colors.test.ts`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <StatusIndicator
    severity="success"
    label="Status"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/status-indicator.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/status-indicator.md).

<!-- components/toast.md -->

# Toast

> A transient, non-blocking notification system: mount the `<Toaster>` region **once** near the application root, then raise notifications imperatively from anywhere via the exported `toast()` function (`toast('Saved')`) and its type shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.info`, `toast.warning`, `toast.loading`, `toast.promise`, `toast.dismiss`). Each notification is a self-dismissing card that stacks in a corner, animates in and out, and is announced to assistive technology — without stealing focus. Unlike the sibling `Alert`, which is an **inline** banner the consumer places in the document flow and controls with `v-model`-style props, Toast is a **transient overlay** stack driven by an imperative call and a shared reactive store, so the call site needs no local visibility state and no markup of its own. The card surface, typography, and severity icons follow the Figma design (see `figma` in the frontmatter). The interaction model follows the established mount-once toast pattern (a single anchored region + imperative trigger + auto-dismiss stack that groups collapsed and expands on hover), built on our tokens, our semantic animation utilities, and our composition/compound-API conventions per [`.claude/rules/migration.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/migration.md); nothing is inherited from any external library. Each severity tints only its leading **icon** via the matching `-contrast` token (`var(--success-contrast)` / `var(--warning-contrast)` / `var(--danger-contrast)` / `var(--info-contrast)`) over the shared `var(--bg-surface-raised)` surface.

- Import: `import ToastRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/toast-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Toast from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## Setup

One-time app-level wiring before the first toast() call — service (recommended): import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast' and chain .use(ToastPlugin) onto createApp() in the app entry; the plugin mounts the toast region automatically. Alternative: mount a Toaster component once near the app root. `webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

## When to use

- Confirming the result of an action that finished out of view or in the background: saved, deployed, copied.
- Following an async operation from start to finish with `toast.promise`, or `toast.loading` plus a dismiss by id.
- A short notice that is not tied to one place on the page and can disappear on its own.

## Do

- Mount `Toaster` once at the app root (in `App.vue`, before the layout or `RouterView`), or install `ToastPlugin`. Never render a `Toaster` in a page, a view or a page-body block: only the first `Toaster` to mount is active and it gives the role up when it unmounts, so a page's copy is either inert or, when it mounted first, silences every toast in the app once the user leaves that page. A page only imports `toast`. A full page routed outside the console layout is still a route of the same app, not a root. `patterns:check` fails a block outside `blocks/shells/` that renders one.
- Use the typed shortcuts (`toast.success`, `toast.error`, …). The type sets the icon; every type is announced once and politely by the Toaster's single live region (an error interrupting what the user is doing is worse than hearing it a moment later, and switching the region between polite and assertive made screen readers drop or repeat the stack).
- Keep the message text to one line and move detail to `description`. Offer at most two actions: one `action`, or `actions` with two entries when a failure has two ways forward (**Edit** and **Redeploy**).
- duration: 0` keeps a toast until it is dismissed. Keep the returned id and call `toast.dismiss(id)`, or pass the same `id` to update the toast in place.
- Don't make a toast the only path to an important action. It auto-dismisses and never takes focus.

## Don’t

- The message must stay visible next to the content it concerns → use `message`.
- The user must decide something before continuing → use `dialog`.
- Validation feedback for a single field → use `helper-text`.

## Related

- message` — inline severity banner placed in the page flow; it stays until it is closed.
- `dialog` — blocking modal for decisions and confirmations.
- `spinner` — rendered by the `loading` toast type.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `'top-left' \| 'top-center' \| 'top-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'bottom-center' \| 'bottom-right'` | `'bottom-right'` | false | Corner (or edge-center) the stack is anchored to. |
| `duration` | `number` | `4000` | false | Default auto-dismiss time in ms each toast inherits; a per-toast `duration` overrides it, and `0` keeps the toast until dismissed. |
| `max` | `number` | `3` | false | Maximum simultaneously visible toasts per corner before the rest queue behind. |
| `expand` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lay the stack out fully expanded with a gap; when `false` the resting stack overlaps into a peek. |
| `closable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Show an always-visible close control on every toast; a per-toast `closable` option overrides it. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { toast, dismiss } | Optional override for a single toast's body. `toast` is the store entry (`{ id, type, message, description?, action?, actions?, duration }`); `dismiss` dismisses that entry. When omitted, the `Toaster` composes `ToastItem` + `Title`/`Description`/`Action`/`Close` from the entry, rendering one `Action` per entry of `actions` (the first two) or the single `action`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-action`
- `@aziontech/webkit/toast-close`

## Sub-components

- `toaster.vue` — the mount-once region, at the component root.
- `toast-item/toast-item.vue` — a single notification card (outer flex row, `items-center` so the content and its `trailing` action/close share one centered line; the leading icon and the content column sit in an inner…
- `toast-title/toast-title.vue` — the primary line of a toast (`text-body-xs` `var(--text-default)`).
- `toast-description/toast-description.vue` — the supporting line below the title (`text-body-xs` `var(--text-muted)`).
- `toast-action/toast-action.vue` — the inline action control, rendered as the webkit `Button` (`kind="transparent"`, `size="small"`).
- `toast-close/toast-close.vue` — the dismiss control, rendered as the webkit `IconButton` (`pi pi-times`, `kind="transparent"`, `size="small"`, `aria-label="Close notification"`).

The imperative API is backed by a small reactive store composable, declared here (undeclared composables are forbidden):

- `use-toast-store.ts` — a singleton reactive store (one module-level reactive list of toast entries) exposing `add(entry)`, `update(id, patch)`, `dismiss(id?)`, and the reactive `toasts` list.

## States

- `data-type` on `ToastItem` (and mirrored on the `Toaster`'s items): `default` | `success` | `info` | `warning` | `error` | `loading`. Drives the leading icon and its severity color (the `-contrast` icon token).
- `data-position` on the `Toaster` container: one of the six `position` values; drives the fixed anchoring (`top`/`bottom` × `left`/`center`/`right`) and the enter/leave translate direction.
- `data-expanded` on the `Toaster` container mirrors the `expand` prop (`true` when expanded).
- The dismiss control (`ToastClose`) renders, and is **always visible**, only when `closable` is set — the per-toast `closable` option, or the Toaster's `closable` default (the per-toast option overrides). When unset, no close control is shown.
- `aria-live="polite"` on the region for every type; items inside a Toaster carry no role of their own, so each toast is announced once by the region and never twice by a nested live region. A `ToastItem` rendered outside a Toaster keeps `role="status"` (or `role="alert"` for `error`/`warning`). Focus is never stolen (the region is not focused on mount). Tests: `toast.test.ts` › live region (spec).
- Visual states on interactive controls (`ToastAction`, `ToastClose`): `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (inherited from `Button` / `IconButton`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-1` on the action and close controls (inherited from `Button` / `IconButton`).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the action then the close control of each visible toast; `Enter`/`Space` activates them. The region itself is not a focus trap and is not focused on mount, so toasts never steal focus from the current task.
- ARIA: the region carries `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-relevant="additions text"` and `aria-atomic="false"`; items inside it have no role (a standalone `ToastItem` is `role="status"`, or `role="alert"` for `error`/`warning`); the close control has an `aria-label`; the severity icon is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted description text and severity icons.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the enter/leave fades and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the move transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the action and close controls (from `Button` / `IconButton` `size="small"`).
- Teleported content: each teleported toaster region binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import { toast, Toaster } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast'

  const show = () =>
    toast('Event has been created', {
      description: 'Sunday, December 03, 2023 at 9:00 AM',
      action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} }
    })
</script>

<template>
  <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
  <Button
    label="Show toast"
    @click="show"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/toast.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/toast.md).

# Upload Progress

> A card that follows a file transfer to its end while the person keeps working: uploading files into a bucket, moving objects between folders or deleting them. Its header says what is happening and how far it got (`Uploading 2 of 5 files`) over one overall bar; below it each file has its own bar, its state and a Cancel or Retry button. When every file has finished the header turns into the outcome (`5 files uploaded`, or `4 files uploaded, 1 failed` with Retry failed) and the card can be closed. It floats at the inline-end bottom corner by default, so it survives route changes in the console shell. Taken from the Console Kit's object storage progress card, extended with the per-file list the design sample's bucket browser needs.

- Import: `import UploadProgress from '@aziontech/webkit/upload-progress'`
- Category: feedback · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A bucket upload that keeps running after the upload dialog closes.
- A move or delete of many objects that takes more than a second or two.
- Any batch of file transfers where the person should be able to cancel one file, or retry the ones that failed.

## Do

- Keep the card until the person closes it when anything failed; close it yourself a few seconds after a clean finish if you like.
- Send `error` as the reason (`Connection lost`, `Larger than 300 MB`), not a status code.
- Update `progress` no more than a few times a second; the bars animate between values.
- Report the outcome with a toast only when the card is not in view (for example, after the person collapsed it and left the page).

## Don’t

- The files picked in a form before it is submitted → use `file-token-group`.
- A single action with no per-file parts (a deploy, a build) → use the async-submit toast (`toast` with Edit and Redeploy).
- Progress of a page load or a determinate step inside a form → use `progress`.

## Related

- `file-token-group` — the files picked for upload, before the transfer starts.
- `progress` — the bar used for the overall and per-file progress.
- `toast` — reports the outcome of a single async action.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `UploadProgressItem[]` | `[]` | false | The files in the transfer, in order, with their state and progress. |
| `operation` | `'upload' \| 'move' \| 'delete'` | `'upload'` | false | What the transfer does; picks the header wording and the glyph. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Overrides the header text. Empty builds it from the operation and the counts. |
| `floating` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Fixes the card to the inline-end bottom corner of the viewport; false renders it in the flow. |
| `cancelable` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows Cancel on running and waiting files and Cancel all in the header. |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:collapsed`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cancel` | `id?: string` | Cancel on one file (its `id`) or Cancel all (no `id`). The parent stops the transfer. |
| `retry` | `id?: string` | Retry on one failed file (its `id`) or Retry failed (no `id`). |
| `close` | `—` | Close was pressed; offered only once every file has finished. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | Buttons for the finished transfer beside Close (for example `Open folder`). Shown when done. |

## v-model

| Model               | Type      | Default | Emits              | Notes                                                     |
| ------------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:collapsed` | Hides the file list and keeps the header and overall bar. |

## States

- Root `data-state`: `running` (some file queued or running) | `done` (all finished, none failed) | `failed` (all finished, at least one error).
- Root `data-floating` when floating; `data-collapsed` when the list is hidden.
- Row `data-status`: `queued` | `running` | `done` | `error` | `canceled`.

## Accessibility

- The card is a `section` named by the catalog (`File transfers`), a region landmark that screen-reader users can jump to.
- The header text is mirrored in a visually hidden `role="status"` region (polite), so each file finishing and the final outcome are announced; percentages are not announced.
- The overall bar is a `progressbar` named by the header text; each row bar is named `<file> progress`.
- Keyboard map: Tab reaches the collapse toggle (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` the list), Cancel all or Retry failed and Close, then each row's Cancel or Retry. After Close the card unmounts in the parent; the parent returns focus to the control that started the transfer.
- State is never colour alone: rows carry a status word (`Waiting`, `Done`, `Canceled`) or the error text, and an `OutcomeMark` in the header when finished.
- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1 on `--bg-surface-raised` in both themes.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the floating card anchors at `end-*`, so it sits at the bottom left under rtl.
- Icons: the chevron of the collapse toggle points up or down and is not mirrored; status glyphs are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: Tab order follows the reading order.
- User data: file names render in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                           | English source                                 | Override prop |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `uploadProgress.label`        | File transfers                                 | —             |
| `uploadProgress.uploading`    | `Uploading {done} of {count} file(s)` (plural) | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.moving`       | `Moving {done} of {count} file(s)` (plural)    | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.deleting`     | `Deleting {done} of {count} file(s)` (plural)  | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.uploaded`     | `{count} file(s) uploaded` (plural)            | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.moved`        | `{count} file(s) moved` (plural)               | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.deleted`      | `{count} file(s) deleted` (plural)             | `title`       |
| `uploadProgress.failed`       | `{count} failed` (plural)                      | —             |
| `uploadProgress.queued`       | Waiting                                        | —             |
| `uploadProgress.done`         | Done                                           | —             |
| `uploadProgress.canceled`     | Canceled                                       | —             |
| `uploadProgress.cancelAll`    | Cancel all                                     | —             |
| `uploadProgress.cancelItem`   | Cancel {name}                                  | —             |
| `uploadProgress.retryItem`    | Retry {name}                                   | —             |
| `uploadProgress.retryFailed`  | Retry failed                                   | —             |
| `uploadProgress.close`        | Close                                          | —             |
| `uploadProgress.expand`       | Show files                                     | —             |
| `uploadProgress.collapse`     | Hide files                                     | —             |
| `uploadProgress.itemProgress` | {name} progress                                | —             |

- Formatting: sizes with `formatFileSize`, percentages with `formatNumber` (`style: 'percent'`), plural rules with `Intl.PluralRules`, all from `useLocale`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none. Floating, the card is `--container-xs` wide and capped to the viewport minus the gutters; below 640 px it spans the viewport width minus the gutters.
- Narrow: names truncate with an ellipsis and keep the full name in `title`; the list scrolls inside a capped height.
- Touch: buttons are `IconButton` and `Button` small (32 px).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import UploadProgress from '@aziontech/webkit/upload-progress'
  import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from 'vue'

  const initial = () => [
    { id: 'logo', name: 'logo.svg', size: 4210, status: 'done' },
    { id: 'app', name: 'app.js', size: 248_320, status: 'running', progress: 64 },
    { id: 'styles', name: 'styles.css', size: 52_100, status: 'running' },
    { id: 'hero', name: 'hero.webp', size: 1_482_000, status: 'queued' }
  ]

  const items = ref(initial())
  let timer = 0

  const tick = () => {
    let started = false
    items.value = items.value.map((item) => {
      if (item.status === 'running') {
        const progress = Math.min(100, (item.progress ?? 0) + 18)
        return progress >= 100 ? { ...item, status: 'done', progress } : { ...item, progress }
      }
      if (item.status === 'queued' && !started) {
        started = true
        return { ...item, status: 'running', progress: 0 }
      }
      return item
    })
    if (items.value.every((item) => item.status !== 'running' && item.status !== 'queued')) {
      clearInterval(timer)
    }
  }

  const start = () => {
    clearInterval(timer)
    items.value = initial()
    timer = setInterval(tick, 600)
  }

  const cancel = (id) => {
    items.value = items.value.map((item) =>
      (id === undefined || item.id === id) &&
      (item.status === 'running' || item.status === 'queued')
        ? { ...item, status: 'canceled' }
        : item
    )
  }

  onBeforeUnmount(() => clearInterval(timer))
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-xs) flex-col items-start gap-(--spacing-sm)">
    <Button
      label="Start upload"
      kind="secondary"
      size="medium"
      icon="pi pi-upload"
      @click="start"
    />
    <UploadProgress
      :items="items"
      :floating="false"
      @cancel="cancel"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/upload-progress.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/upload-progress.md).

<!-- components/attribute-editor.md -->

# Attribute Editor

> An editable list of rows with the same fields, after Cloudscape's attribute editor: key and value pairs (environment variables, headers, metadata) or any set of columns given by a `definition`. It owns the row anatomy every hand-built editor repeats: a label per cell, one control per cell, a per-cell error under the field, Add and Remove, an item limit, the empty text, focus after add and remove, and a polite announcement of each change. A grouped mode lays rows out as AND groups joined by OR, the shape of rule criteria. It edits an array and validates nothing itself: the consumer passes `errors`.

- Import: `import AttributeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/attribute-editor'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Users add, edit and remove a variable number of pairs or tuples: environment variables, request headers, query arguments, labels, metadata.
- Rule criteria: conditions inside a group must all match (and), groups are alternatives (or).
- A bulk form where each row has the same two to four fields and a row-level error can occur.

## Do

- Keep two to four columns; more columns belong in a drawer per row.
- Pass `errors` only after the first Save (rule of the form-error block), then keep them live while the user fixes the rows.
- Use `minItems: 1` when the form needs at least one row, so the last row keeps its fields and loses its Remove.
- Set `limit` when the backend has one; the component says how many rows are left and disables Add at the limit.
- Replace a cell's control through `cell-<key>` (a `Select` for an operator, a `Switch` for secret) instead of drawing rows by hand; use `row` only when the row needs a layout of its own.
- Type the rows with your own interface (`ref<Header[]>`): `value` in `cell-<key>` and `item` in every slot then carry the field types, so a `Select` or `Switch` binds `value` without `as string` / `as boolean`.
- Name the editor (`ariaLabel`) after what the rows are: "Environment variables", "Request headers".

## Don’t

- Key and value tags with limits, reserved prefixes and removal of saved tags → use `tag-editor`, which is built on this component.
- A fixed set of named settings on one resource → use `field` controls in a form.
- Many records the user browses, filters and acts on → use `table` with row actions.
- An ordered list of actions with drag and drop and per-type arguments → compose it by hand as in the `platform/edit/rule-builder` block.

## Related

- `tag-editor` — key and value tags with limits and validation, on top of AttributeEditor.
- `field` — every cell is a `Field` with its label, control and error.
- `input` — the default control of a cell; any control can replace it through `cell-<key>`.
- `button`, `icon-button` — Add and Remove.
- `separator` — the "or" between groups in grouped mode.
- platform/edit/rule-builder` (block) — its criteria are this component in grouped mode (AND rows inside a group, OR between groups), with a `Combobox` variable cell.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `[]` | false | Rows in list mode. Supports v-model:items. |
| `groups` | `TItem[][]` | `undefined` | false | Rows in grouped mode: every inner array is an AND group, groups are joined by OR. Supports v-model:groups. |
| `definition` | `AttributeEditorColumn[]` | `[]` | false | Columns of every row: key of the item field, label, placeholder, required. |
| `errors` | `AttributeEditorErrors` | `[]` | false | Error per cell, aligned with the rows (nested per group in grouped mode). Empty shows none. |
| `addButtonLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the Add button. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `removeButtonLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the Remove button, followed by the row number. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `addGroupLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the Add group button in grouped mode. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `empty` | `string` | `''` | false | Text shown when there are no rows. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `limit` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Most rows allowed (per group in grouped mode); Add is disabled at the limit and the rows left are announced. |
| `groupLimit` | `number` | `undefined` | false | Most groups allowed in grouped mode. |
| `minItems` | `number` | `0` | false | Fewest rows kept; rows at the minimum lose their Remove button. |
| `newItem` | `() => TItem` | `undefined` | false | Builds a new row. Unset creates an item with an empty string per column key. |
| `itemRemovable` | `(item: TItem) => boolean` | `undefined` | false | Hides Remove on the rows it returns false for. Unset makes every row removable. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size of the default controls and the Remove button, on the 28 / 32 / 40 rhythm. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every control, Add and Remove. |
| `addDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables Add only, for example until the last row is filled in. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of rows. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:items` | `TItem[]` | A row was added, removed or edited in list mode. |
| `update:groups` | `TItem[][]` | A row or group was added, removed or edited in grouped mode. |
| `add` | `{ index: number; groupIndex?: number }` | After a row is added; `groupIndex` only in grouped mode. |
| `remove` | `{ index: number; item: TItem; groupIndex?: number }` | After a row is removed. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | { item, index, groupIndex, errors, update, remove, removable, removeLabel } | Replaces the whole row; the column header is not drawn. |
| `row-actions` | { item, index, groupIndex, remove, removable, removeLabel } | Replaces the Remove button at the end of a default row (for example Remove / Undo that marks a row instead of deleting it). |
| `empty` | — | Replaces the empty text. |
| `actions` | — | Extra buttons after Add (for example Upload or Paste .env). |
| `info` | — | Extra help text under the buttons, after the limit text. |
| `limit` | { count, limit, left } | Replaces the limit text in list mode (for example "You can add 3 more tags."). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `empty`, `at limit` (Add disabled), `invalid` (per cell), `disabled`
- `data-size` mirrors `size`; `data-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; `data-mode` is `list` or `grouped`
- Each row carries `data-row` with its index (and `data-group` in grouped mode)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every control and button keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map: Tab moves through the cells of a row, its Remove, then the next row; Add moves focus to the first control of the new row; Remove moves focus to the same position in the next row, else the previous row, else Add.
- ARIA: the rows are a `list` named by `ariaLabel`; each cell is a `Field` whose label is programmatically tied to its control (visually hidden on wide containers, where one header row shows the labels and is `aria-hidden`); an error is a `FieldError` referenced by `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid`; each Remove is named "Remove item n" (or `removeButtonLabel` n); groups are `group`s named "Group n"; a polite `status` region announces "Item n added" and "Item n removed".
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens, including the disabled state.
- Touch target: Remove follows `size` (40 px at `large`); the stacked layout keeps it at the row's end.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the Remove column sits at the inline end.
- Icons: the trash and plus glyphs are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling of its own.
- User data: values stay in their controls, which set no direction of their own.

## Internationalization

| Key                            | English source                               | Override prop       |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `attributeEditor.add`          | Add new item                                 | `addButtonLabel`    |
| `attributeEditor.remove`       | Remove item                                  | `removeButtonLabel` |
| `attributeEditor.rowAction`    | {label} {index}                              | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.addGroup`     | Add OR group                                 | `addGroupLabel`     |
| `attributeEditor.empty`        | No items yet.                                | `empty`             |
| `attributeEditor.remaining`    | You can add {count} more item(s) (plural)    | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.limitReached` | You have reached the limit of {limit} items. | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.added`        | Item {index} added.                          | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.removed`      | Item {index} removed.                        | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.group`        | Group {index}                                | —                   |
| `attributeEditor.and` / `or`   | and / or                                     | —                   |

- Formatting: the rows left go through the plural rules of the active locale.

## Responsive

- Container queries: `@container/attribute-editor` on the root; at `@md` (472 px) the cells sit in one grid row under a shared header, below it every cell stacks with its own visible label and rows are divided by a line.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): stacked cells, Remove at the end of the row.
- Touch: buttons follow `size`; nothing depends on hover (the Remove tooltip repeats its accessible name).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import AttributeEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/attribute-editor'
  import { computed, ref } from 'vue'

  const definition = [
    { key: 'key', label: 'Key', placeholder: 'MY_VARIABLE', required: true },
    { key: 'value', label: 'Value', placeholder: 'my-value' }
  ]

  const items = ref([
    { key: 'API_BASE_URL', value: 'https://api.example.com' },
    { key: 'max uploads', value: '25' }
  ])

  const errors = computed(() =>
    items.value.map((item) => {
      if (!item.key.trim()) return { key: 'Key is required.' }
      if (!/^[A-Z0-9_]+$/.test(item.key))
        return { key: 'Use only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.' }
      return undefined
    })
  )
</script>

<template>
  <AttributeEditor
    v-model:items="items"
    :definition="definition"
    :errors="errors"
    :limit="10"
    :min-items="1"
    add-button-label="Add variable"
    remove-button-label="Remove variable"
    aria-label="Environment variables"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/attribute-editor.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/attribute-editor.md).
