# Calendar

> Date-range picker. A trigger button opens a popover that holds a month grid, Start/End date + time fields (suppressible with `show-fields`), an optional timezone selector, and an Apply action; it also offers a "Select Period" mode whose hint chips and typed text are read in the active locale (`45m`, `12 hours` / `12 horas`, `last month` / `mês passado`, `yesterday` / `ontem`, `1/1 - 1/2`). When consumer-provided `presets` are supplied, the trigger splits into two side-by-side segments — a preset dropdown (left, `🕐 <label> ⌄`) that applies a preset range in one click, and the calendar (right, `📅 <range>`) that opens the grid for fine-tuning. Selection is staged in a draft inside the popover and committed to `v-model` only on Apply (or immediately when `show-apply` is false); a preset commits immediately. In period mode, once a span is applied the trigger shows the same two-segment shape — the relative token (e.g. `45m`) beside the concrete window it resolves to (e.g. `14:44 – 23:59`) — since a period selects a time interval rather than whole days. Date math uses the native `Date` API only — no date library; timezone is a selectable IANA label used for display formatting via `Intl` (the picker does not re-interpret `Date` objects across zones).

- Import: `import CalendarRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/calendar-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Calendar from '@aziontech/webkit/calendar'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Picking a date range for analytics, logs, or billing windows, optionally with times and a timezone.
- Offering one-click ranges ("Last 7 days") next to the grid through `presets`.
- Relative time windows typed as text (`45m`, `last month`) with `period`.
- A single date with `mode="single"`.

## Do

- modelValue` is committed only on Apply; read the final value from `update:modelValue` or `apply`, and set `:show-apply="false"` when every edit should commit at once.
- Bind a `{ start, end }` object in range mode and a `Date` or `null` with `mode="single"`.
- Bound the selectable days with `min` and `max` instead of validating after commit.
- Pair `show-timezone` with `v-model:timezone`; the timezone changes display formatting only, not the `Date` values.
- Prefer the `presets` prop; use the `presets` slot with `Calendar.Preset` only when preset content needs custom markup.

## Don’t

- Only a fixed list of named windows, with no custom range → use `select`.
- A duration or count (retention days, TTL) rather than a date → use `number-input`.

## Related

- `select` — a fixed list of named periods without a grid.
- `input` — the trigger and the Start/End fields share its heights, hover, and disabled treatment, so they align side by side.
- `number-input` — numeric durations instead of dates.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `Date \| null \| CalendarRange` | `null` | false | Committed selection for v-model. A `Date` (or null) in single mode; a `{ start, end }` range in range mode. Only updated on Apply (or immediately when `showApply` is false). |
| `mode` | `'single' \| 'range'` | `'range'` | false | Selection mode. Single picks one date; range picks a start and end date. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects the trigger, day-cell hit-area, and typography. |
| `min` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Earliest selectable date; earlier days render disabled. |
| `max` | `Date \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Latest selectable date; later days render disabled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger, grid, and all controls, applying disabled tokens. |
| `open` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state of the popover. Use with v-model:open; omit for uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text shown when there is no selection. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Select a date range`). |
| `presets` | `CalendarPresetItem[]` | `[]` | false | Consumer-provided shortcuts; each is `{ label, value }` where value is a `Date` or range. When present, the trigger becomes a two-part control whose left segment opens a dropdown of these presets. |
| `showFields` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the Start/End date fields in the panel. Set false when the shortcuts and the grid are the whole interaction and typing a boundary by hand is not offered. |
| `showTime` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows Start/End time fields alongside the date fields. |
| `showTimezone` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the timezone selector below the fields. |
| `timezone` | `string` | `''` | false | Selected IANA timezone for display formatting (v-model:timezone). Empty resolves to the local zone. |
| `timezones` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Timezone options for the selector; empty falls back to a curated list derived from `Intl`. |
| `horizontal` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Lays the fields/apply column beside the calendar instead of below it. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a clear control on the trigger that empties the committed selection. |
| `showApply` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Stages edits in a draft and requires Apply to commit; when false, every edit commits immediately. |
| `period` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Enables the "Select period" relative-time mode: a relative-preset list plus a text input that parses spans like `45m` or `last month`. |
| `split` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the trigger as a split control with a separate chevron affordance. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `Date \| null \| CalendarRange` | v-model. The committed `Date` (single) or `{ start, end }` (range); empty value on clear. |
| `update:open` | `boolean` | v-model:open. Emitted when the popover opens or closes. |
| `update:timezone` | `string` | v-model:timezone. Emitted when the timezone selection changes. |
| `month-change` | `CalendarMonth` | Emitted when the first visible month changes via navigation or keyboard paging. Payload is `{ year, month }` (month is 0-indexed). |
| `apply` | `Date \| null \| CalendarRange` | Emitted when the draft selection is committed via Apply. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | { open, value, displayValue } | Replaces the default trigger button; scope exposes the open state, raw value, and formatted label. |
| `presets` | — | Custom preset dropdown content (e.g. `<Calendar.Preset>`); overrides the `presets` prop rendering. |
| `footer` | — | Custom footer/action-bar content (e.g. `<Calendar.Clear>`) alongside Apply. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/calendar-preset`
- `@aziontech/webkit/calendar-clear`

## Sub-components

- `calendar-preset/calendar-preset.vue` — context-aware shortcut button; applies its `value` (a `Date` in single mode or a `{ start, end }` range) to the popover's draft selection through injected context and reflects a…
- `calendar-clear/calendar-clear.vue` — context-aware button that clears the draft selection through injected context; disabled when there is no selection.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `selected`, `in-range`, `disabled`, `today`, `outside` (adjacent-month), popover `open` / `closed`
- **Field contract parity.** Every field-shaped surface — the trigger, the Start/End date+time fields, and the timezone selector — follows the shared `inputs` field contract used by `input`, `number-input`, `select-trigger` and `textarea`, so a Calendar reads identically to a text field placed beside it: heights are `small=28px` / `medium=32px` / `large=40px`, the value renders at `.text-label-sm`, and `disabled` applies `var(--bg-disabled)` + `var(--text-disabled)` + `cursor-not-allowed` rather than an opacity wash.
- **Hover is identical to `input`.** The whole trigger is one field with one border, so hover raises **only** that border to `var(--border-strong)` — no background wash on any segment. It is suppressed while the control is focused (the focus ring is the active affordance) and while `disabled`, via the same selector `input` uses: `[&:not(:focus-within):not([data-disabled])]:hover:border-(--border-strong)` (the timezone `<select>` is focusable itself, so it uses the `:not(:focus):not(:disabled)` form). Because the border lives on the trigger shell, hovering any segment — preset, calendar, clear, or split — raises the single shared border, exactly as hovering a text field's icon slot does. `hover:bg-(--bg-hover)` survives only on the preset **dropdown menu rows**, which are menu items inside the popover, not field surfaces, and have no `input` counterpart.
- `data-state` on the root and trigger mirrors the popover open state (`open` | `closed`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop on the root, trigger, and each day cell (`small` | `medium` | `large`)
- `data-selected` mirrors a fully-selected day cell (single value, or a range endpoint) and an active preset
- `data-band` on each day cell drives the connected range highlight: `none` | `single` | `start` | `middle` | `end`
- `data-today` marks the current date; `data-outside` marks an adjacent-month day cell
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on the root, unselectable day cells, and the clear control when there is no selection
- When `presets` are supplied, the trigger is a two-part control: a left preset button (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, clock glyph, `data-testid` `…__presets-trigger`) opening the preset dropdown, and a right calendar button (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, calendar glyph) opening the popover; the two dropdowns are mutually exclusive, and each preset menu item sets `data-selected` when it is the active preset
- In period mode, a committed selection renders the trigger as two side-by-side segments: the relative token (e.g. `45m`, with a clock glyph) beside the resolved concrete window (e.g. `14:44 – 23:59`, with a calendar glyph), separated by a divider
- Reflow: the root is capped at the width of its container (`max-w-full`), so the trigger, presets included, never overflows a 320 px box.
- Server render and hydration: the time zone select lists only the chosen zone until mount (its city name, or the catalog's `Local` with no zone chosen), because the zone list, the local zone and the offsets depend on the runtime's clock and tz data. On mount it lists every zone with its offset, so the server HTML and the first client render match.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and `focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-surface-raised)` inside the popover. The Start/End date+time fields reuse `input`, whose ring offset resolves `var(--input-ring-offset, var(--bg-canvas))`; the fields container declares `--input-ring-offset: var(--bg-surface-raised)` once and it inherits to every field, so the ring gap matches the raised popover the fields sit on.
- Field labels: each visible Start / End / Date label is a `<label for>` bound to its date field through `useId()`; the time field beside it carries its own `aria-label` (`Start time` / `End time` / `Time`), so every field has a programmatic accessible name.
- Keyboard map: the trigger toggles the popover with `Enter`/`Space` and exposes `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`; `Escape` and click-outside close it and return focus to the trigger; focus is trapped in the open popover. In the grid, `Tab` enters at the focused day, `Arrow` keys move focus (paging the visible window when crossing its first/last month), `Enter`/`Space` selects, `PageUp`/`PageDown` change month. Apply, Clear, presets, fields, and the timezone control are all reachable by `Tab`.
- ARIA: each month grid uses `role="grid"` with `role="row"` and `role="gridcell"` descendants; selected cells set `aria-selected="true"`; the current date sets `aria-current="date"`; navigation buttons carry `aria-label`; the popover is labelled by the trigger; decorative icons are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the popover and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px (or justified deviation): day cells use a 32×32 px (`small`), 36×36 px (`medium`), or 40×40 px (`large`) hit area; `small`/`medium` are a justified deviation for dense month-grid layouts, `large` meets the 40 px target.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the previous/next month chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the clock and calendar trigger icons do not.
- Motion: the month strip slide mirrors (`rtl:` swaps `translate-x-full` and `-translate-x-full`), so under `dir="rtl"` the next month enters from the left, the side its chevron points to.
- Keyboard: in the day grid `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move one day later/earlier, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`): `ArrowLeft` moves to the next day. `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`, `PageUp`/`PageDown` and `Home`/`End` are unchanged.
- User data: dates and times are printed by `Intl` in the active locale; the typed field value uses the `Input` `dir="auto"`.
- Teleported content: the teleported date popover and presets menu bind `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Internationalization

- Every built-in string comes from the `calendar` group of the locale catalog (`useLocale`): trigger placeholder, Period / Select period, Start / End / Date / Time labels, Apply, preset labels, hint headings, timezone label, and the words that separate a typed range (`calendar.rangeSeparators`: `to|through`, `a|até`, `a|hasta`).
- Printed text uses `Intl` in the active locale: the trigger label, the field values and their placeholders (`Jun 1, 2026` in `en`, `1 de jun. de 2026` in `pt-BR`), the time fields, weekday and month names.
- Period hint chips are printed by `Intl` (`Intl.NumberFormat` units and `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`): `12 hours` / `12 horas`, `yesterday` / `ontem`, `last month` / `mês passado`, and the fixed hints (`Jan 1` / `1 de jan.`, `1/1 - 1/2` / `01/01 - 02/01`). A chip applies exactly the text it shows.
- Typing is parsed in the active locale with English always accepted as well: unit words and their abbreviations, `today`/`yesterday`/`last week`/`last month`/`last year`/`this month` and their translations, month names (long and short, accents optional), numeric dates in the locale's day/month order (`1/2/2026` is 2 January in `en`, 1 February in `pt-BR`), ISO `2026-01-05`, and ranges split by `-`, `–` or a separator word. Times accept `14:30`, `14h30` and `2:30 pm`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CalendarRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/calendar-root'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const range = ref(null)
</script>

<template>
  <CalendarRoot
    v-model="range"
    mode="range"
    clearable
    show-time
    show-timezone
  />
</template>
```

# Checkbox

> Binary selection control. Supports a single boolean (`binary: true`) and array-based multi-select (adds or removes its `value` in the `modelValue` array) (used by `MultiSelect` and `DataTable` to drive bulk selection). The new `indeterminate` prop renders a third visual state (horizontal bar) and sets the native `indeterminate` property, which exposes the mixed state — used by parents that own a partial-selection summary (e.g. "select all" rows where some children are selected). Aligned with Figma frame `2027:7311`.

- Import: `import Checkbox from '@aziontech/webkit/checkbox'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A bare boolean control whose label lives outside it: a table row-selection cell, an option row in a list, a settings matrix.
- Picking several values from a short set: give each box its own `value` and bind them all to one array `v-model`.
- A "select all" control over a partial selection: set `indeterminate` while only some children are checked.

## Do

- Set `binary` for a plain true/false value; without it the checkbox adds or removes its `value` in an array `modelValue`.
- Give every checkbox an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at `inputId`, or pass `aria-label` (attributes land on the inner input).
- indeterminate` only changes the visual and sets the native `indeterminate` property (exposed as mixed); the parent computes it and decides what a click does.
- Use `readonly` for a value that cannot change in this context and `disabled` for an option that is unavailable.

## Don’t

- A form field that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
- Each option needs a bordered card with a label and description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
- An on/off setting that applies as soon as it flips → use `switch`.
- Only one option of the set may be chosen → use `radio-button`.

## Related

- `field` — `orientation="horizontal"` puts the checkbox beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping that Field turns it into a bordered choice card.
- `switch` — on/off toggle for settings that take effect immediately.
- `multi-select` — renders this checkbox in every option row; use it when the option list is long.
- `table` — uses this checkbox for row selection and the select-all header.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `TModel` | `undefined` | false | Two-way bound value. Boolean in `binary` mode, scalar when paired with `value`, array when multi-selecting. |
| `value` | `unknown` | `undefined` | false | Identifier for this checkbox in non-binary mode. Compared against `modelValue` (or included in the array). |
| `binary` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the checkbox toggles `modelValue` as a boolean (no `value` pairing). |
| `indeterminate` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Renders the indeterminate visual (horizontal bar). Does not affect `modelValue`; the parent owns the tri-state logic. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; value is visible but cannot change via interaction. |
| `inputId` | `string` | `''` | false | Forwarded to the inner `<input id>` for label association. |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | false | HTML name for form submission. |
| `tabindex` | `number` | `0` | false | Forwarded to the inner `<input tabindex>`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TModel` | Fires on activation. Payload is the next boolean (binary mode) or the next array (every other mode). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `checked`, `indeterminate`, `disabled`, `readonly`
- `data-state` on the root: `unchecked` | `checked` | `indeterminate`
- `data-checked` mirrors `isChecked` (legacy; kept for backwards compatibility with existing `data-[checked]:` styling)
- `data-indeterminate` mirrors the `indeterminate` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop
- Touch: the native input that receives the click extends past the 18 px box to 24 × 24 px, and to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer; the drawn box does not change.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Space` toggles. (The native `<input type="checkbox">` carries the semantics.)
- ARIA: native `<input type="checkbox">` is the source of truth. No `aria-checked` is set on it: the checked state comes from `checked`, and the mixed state from the `indeterminate` DOM property, which browsers expose as mixed (an `aria-checked` on a native checkbox conflicts with its real state, axe `aria-conditional-attr`). The wrapping `<span>` is decorative.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition-bearing class.
- Touch target — the `1.125rem` size is below 40×40 px; consumers should wrap it in a horizontal `Field` (the label extends the target) or expand the parent click area when the control sits on its own.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Checkbox from '@aziontech/webkit/checkbox'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const checked = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Checkbox
    v-model="checked"
    binary
    input-id="webkit-checkbox"
    aria-label="Toggle option"
  />
</template>
```

# Chip

> A Chip is a compact, pill-shaped token that labels a discrete value the user has applied — most often a filter on a data view. Unlike `tag` (a read-only status/category badge with severity color coding), a Chip carries no severity and exposes an optional trailing remove control: when `removable` is set, it renders a real `<button>` that emits `remove`, so the consumer can drop the value from a collection. This is the token consumed by the data table's `#filters` slot (`<Chip :label="f.label" removable @remove="dropFilter(f)" />`): each active filter becomes one removable Chip, and dismissing it removes that filter. Reach for a Chip when a value is user-applied and dismissible; reach for `tag` when it is a static status or category indicator. `kind` covers the three jobs a chip does in a filter surface, so a consumer never restyles the component to get one of them: - **`filled`** — a value that IS applied. The grey `--bg-selected` fill on the shared border, plus `--shadow-sm`: the loudest of the three, because it is state. This is the applied-filter chip of the console's filter bar. - **`outlined`** — a value the user COULD apply. The `--bg-surface` fill and the shared border, no shadow: it recedes to an offer without becoming disabled, so a filter vocabulary can stay on screen instead of hiding inside a menu. - **`dashed`** — the control that CREATES a chip ("Add filter"). A dashed outline is the standing convention for "add another one of these", which is what separates the thing that makes filters from the things that are filters. **Selected is a mode, not a kind.** `selectable` turns the chip into a toggle: activating it flips the `selected` model (`v-model:selected`), and the state stays after the click until the chip is activated again. It is independent of `kind` — `filled` marks an applied filter and never means "selected", so a selectable chip of any kind paints its selected state the same way (`--bg-selected` fill, `--border-selected` outline) and announces it as `aria-pressed`. Because `filled` already wears the `--bg-selected` fill, a `filled` toggle shows its on state by the outline alone; a row of toggles is `outlined`. Reach for `selectable` when a set of chips is a row of toggles (quick filters, facets); keep `clickable` when activation opens or does something without holding a state. **Presence is the consumer's, not the chip's.** `remove` fires the moment the control is activated; the chip does not animate itself away or unmount itself. A chip that hid itself on remove could only ever serve the one case where removing it also destroys it — a filter bar where a removed value stays on screen as an `outlined` offer was impossible, because the instance stayed invisible forever. Exit motion, if wanted, belongs to whatever owns the list (a `TransitionGroup` around the group).

- Import: `import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chip'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Represent a selectable or removable token — active filters, multi-select values, entered keywords.
- Represent a value that is _available_ but not applied (`kind="outlined"`), so the set of things a view can be narrowed by stays visible.
- Represent the "add another" affordance for such a set (`kind="dashed"`).
- Represent a row of toggles that each hold an on/off state (`selectable` + `v-model:selected`).
- The element is interactive (clickable / dismissible).

## Do

- When removable, expose an accessible remove control with a clear label.
- Group related chips in a `chip-group` rather than ad-hoc layout.
- Do: draw an applied filter as `kind="filled"` (the default) — the grey fill is what says "this narrows the view"; draw the values it could still take as `outlined`, and "Add filter" as `dashed`.
- Do: make a row of toggles `outlined` + `selectable`, so off reads as surface and on as the selected fill and outline.
- Don't: restyle a chip's fill with a class (`bg-(--bg-muted)`, `bg-(--bg-surface)`) to get the applied or the available look; pick the `kind`.
- Don't: use `filled` for a value that is merely offered; the fill would claim it is applied.

## Don’t

- It is a static count or one-glance status → use `badge`.
- It is a static descriptive label/category with no interaction → use `tag`.

## Related

- `badge` — static count/short-value indicator.
- `tag` — static labelled status/category chip.
- `tooltip` — composed by the remove control to name what it removes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Fallback text when the default slot is empty. |
| `kind` | `'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'dashed'` | `'filled'` | false | Visual variant. Filled (grey fill) is an applied value, outlined an available one, dashed the control that adds one. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; `small` is a fixed 24px, `medium` a fixed 32px. |
| `removable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, renders a trailing remove button that emits `remove`. |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the chip body becomes interactive (`role="button"`, focusable) and emits `click` on activation (click / Enter / Space). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the chip becomes a toggle: activating it flips the `selected` model and emits `click`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Suppresses activation, toggling and removal. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:selected`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove` | `(event: MouseEvent, label: string)` | Fires when `removable` is true and the remove button is activated (click / Enter / Space), **immediately** — the chip does not hide or unmount itself first, so the consumer decides whether the chip disappears, stays, or becomes an `outlined` offer. `label` is the chip's `label` prop, identifying which chip was removed. |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, label: string)` | Fires only when `clickable` or `selectable` is true, `disabled` is false, and the chip body is activated — by pointer, or `Enter` / `Space` while the root is focused. `label` identifies which chip was clicked. When `selectable`, the `selected` model is already flipped when `click` fires. The trailing remove button stops propagation, so activating it emits `remove` only, never `click`. `update:selected` comes from `v-model:selected` (see above). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Chip content; falls back to `label` when empty. |

## v-model

| Model              | Type      | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:selected` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:selected` | Whether a selectable chip is toggled on. Flipped on every activation while `selectable` and not `disabled`; ignored otherwise. Uncontrolled when unbound. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop (`filled` | `outlined` | `dashed`)
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop (`small` | `medium`)
- `data-removable` is present when the `removable` prop is true
- `data-clickable` is present when the chip is interactive (`clickable` or `selectable`) and not `disabled`
- `data-selected` is present when `selectable` is true and the `selected` model is true
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true
- When `selectable`, the chip is interactive exactly like `clickable`, and additionally carries `aria-pressed="true|false"` mirroring `selected`. Selected paints the `--bg-selected` fill and the `--border-selected` outline on top of whichever `kind` the chip has; `kind` keeps its own meaning (elevation, dash), so a `filled` chip is an applied value whether or not it is selected. Hover and active keep their `--border-strong` affordance over the selected outline.
- When `disabled`, the root is not focusable, activation, toggling and removal are suppressed, the text drops to `--text-disabled` with `cursor-not-allowed`, and the remove button is a disabled `<button>`. An interactive chip keeps `role="button"` and adds `aria-disabled="true"`.
- When `clickable`, the root is an interactive `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`: it shows `cursor-pointer`, a `::before` ghost-layer darkening overlay (`--bg-hover`) on `hover` and `active`, a `--border-strong` border on `active` (the pressed state, per Figma), and a visible focus ring on `focus-visible`. When not clickable, the root stays a non-interactive container.
- The remove button (when `removable`) is always independently focusable and shows its own focus ring on `focus-visible`. It carries a **`tooltip`** naming what it removes, shown on hover and on keyboard focus — in a row of chips four identical `×` controls sit side by side, and the field name is what tells them apart.
- All three kinds share the `--border-default` border at rest, so a row of chips reads as one family. `filled` fills with `--bg-selected` (grey: `#E5E5E5` on the light theme's white surface, `#1A1A1A` on the dark theme's `#0A0A0A`) and adds `--shadow-sm`; `outlined` and `dashed` fill with `--bg-surface` and carry no shadow, so an applied value is louder than an available one in both themes. `dashed` is `outlined` with a dashed border. When `clickable`, hover raises the border to `--border-strong` — the same rest→hover pair `input` and `select-trigger` use. That pair is what makes the outline read as interactive at all: `--border-default` is 8% black, the _same value_ as `--border-muted` in the light theme, so a static border of either token is indistinguishable.
- **Why `--bg-selected` and not `--bg-surface-raised`.** `filled` once specified `--bg-surface-raised`, which resolves to the _same value_ as `--bg-surface` in the light theme (the contrast existed only in dark), and the utility carried a stray space inside the paren shorthand, so it compiled to no CSS at all; for a while every chip then shared `--bg-surface` and `--shadow-sm` alone carried the state, which read as a white pill on white cards. The design sample's filter bar draws the applied chip on `--bg-selected`, which differs from `--bg-surface` in both themes; that is the fill.
- The remove control's glyph sits at `--text-muted` at rest and rises to `--text-default` on hover: at rest it is punctuation after a label, and on hover it is the thing being aimed at. It stays above the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum in both themes (3.95:1 light, 5.02:1 dark).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: both the clickable root (when `clickable`) and the remove button use `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`.
- Keyboard map: when `clickable` or `selectable` (and not `disabled`), the root is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) and `Enter` / `Space` **dispatch a real DOM click** on the root (`preventDefault`ed first, so `Space` does not scroll), which in turn emits `click` (and, when `selectable`, toggles `selected`). Dispatching rather than emitting directly is what lets a chip serve as an overlay trigger — `Popover.Trigger` and friends open on the DOM click that bubbles out of their child, so a chip that only emitted a Vue event would work with the mouse and do nothing from the keyboard. When `removable`, `Tab` reaches the remove button and `Enter` / `Space` activate it and emit `remove`. Keystrokes that originate on the remove button do not bubble to the root activation (the handler ignores events whose `target` is not the root itself). When a chip is both interactive and `removable`, the button role, `tabindex`, `aria-pressed` and the `Enter` / `Space` handler move from the root to an inner body element (`data-chip-body`, testid `<testid>__body`) that holds the label, and the remove button sits beside it, not inside it: a `role="button"` with a `<button>` inside is `nested-interactive`, and screen readers flatten the inner control away. The root keeps the click handler and draws the focus ring when the body is focused (`has-[[data-chip-body]:focus-visible]`). Tab order is body, then remove button.
- ARIA: when neither `clickable` nor `selectable`, the root is a non-interactive `<span>` container; when either is set, it is `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`. A `selectable` chip is a toggle button: `aria-pressed="true|false"` mirrors the `selected` model and flips on every activation, so the state is announced, not only painted. When `disabled`, an interactive root drops `tabindex` and carries `aria-disabled="true"`; the remove control is a native disabled `<button>`. The remove control is a real `<button type="button">`; the `pi pi-times` glyph is `aria-hidden="true"`. Its `aria-label` and its tooltip text are **the same derived string** — `Remove <label>` when `label` is set, `Remove` otherwise — so what is shown and what is announced cannot drift.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the remove icon.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition the chip declares (kind/border colour, remove-button colour). The chip declares no dismiss animation at all, so there is nothing to suppress there.
- Touch target: the remove control is **24×24 px at `medium`** — the WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) minimum — and 16×16 px at `small`, a justified deviation for the compact 24px token where the surrounding chip remains the visible affordance. The earlier build drew the control at 14×14 px at every size, which met neither.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Chip from '@aziontech/webkit/chip'
</script>

<template>
  <Chip
    label="Label"
    kind="filled"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/chip.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/chip.md).

# Combobox

> A text field with a list of suggestions under it: typing filters the options, picking one fills the field, and a value that is not in the list is accepted as typed. It holds one string value, after the design sample's `ComboboxInput` and the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern. It differs from `Select`, whose value must be one of its options and whose trigger is a button, and from `Command`, which runs commands from a palette instead of filling a form field.

- Import: `import Combobox from '@aziontech/webkit/combobox'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A form field whose usual values are known but a new one is valid: an environment variable name, a header, a path, a region tag, a branch.
- A long option list the user would rather type than scroll, with the list as a reminder.
- Options that come from the server as the user types (`search` event, `loading`, `filter: false`).
- Suggestions grouped by origin (Recent, Suggested, System) in one field.

## Do

- Put the Combobox in a `Field` so it gets a visible label; use `ariaLabel` only where no label can be shown.
- Keep `allowCustom` on only when a new value is genuinely valid; with it off, the field restores the last valid value when the typed text matches nothing.
- Give options a `description` for what tells them apart (a scope, a count), not a second copy of the label.
- For server data set `filter` to `false`, listen to `search` (debounce on your side), and drive `loading` from the request.
- Validate the committed value (`update:modelValue`) in the form, not each keystroke; `search` is for suggestions only.
- Use `group` when options come from distinct sources; keep group titles one or two words.

## Don’t

- The value must be one of a short fixed list → use `select` (or `radio-group` for 2–5 visible choices).
- Several values at once → use `multi-select`.
- Searching and running commands or jumping to a page → use `command`.
- Filtering a collection by properties → use `property-filter`.
- Key/value pairs or tags → use `attribute-editor` or `tag-editor` (their key cells may hold a Combobox).

## Related

- `select` — closed list, button trigger, no free entry.
- `input` — the field Combobox is built on; use it alone when there are no suggestions.
- `field` — label, description and error around the Combobox; it reads id, invalid, disabled and required from it.
- `command` — palette of actions, not a form value.
- `property-filter` — token-based filtering with the same listbox look.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ComboboxOption[]` | `[]` | false | Suggestions: `{ value, label?, description?, group?, disabled? }`. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the field. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no `Field` label names the field. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token, as `Input`: 28 / 32 / 40 px. |
| `allowCustom` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Accepts a typed value that matches no option, offered as `Use "…"`. |
| `filter` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Filters `options` by the typed text. Turn off when the server filters on `search`. |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a clear button while the field has a value. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner and the loading row while options are fetched. |
| `emptyText` | `string` | `''` | false | Text of the list when nothing matches. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the field. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the value without the list or editing. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field required (`aria-required`). |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field invalid (`aria-invalid`, danger border). |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `string` | The typed text, on each keystroke while the list is open (server filters). |
| `create` | `string` | A value that matches no option was committed (`allowCustom`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `option` | { option: ComboboxOption, active: boolean, selected: boolean } | Replaces the content of one option row. |

## Sub-components

_none_ — one `.vue` file. The list is rendered by the component itself (teleported to `body`, positioned with `usePlacement`); options are data, rendered through the optional `option` slot.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v-model` | `string` | `''` | `update:modelValue` | The committed value via `defineModel`. Changes on pick, Enter, Tab, blur and clear, not on each keystroke. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `loading`, empty list
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid` on the root mirror the resolved props (prop or `Field`)
- Option rows: `data-active` (the keyboard/pointer highlight), `data-selected` (equals the committed value), `data-disabled`
- The field shows the selected option's `label` when the value equals an option's `value`, otherwise the value itself

## Accessibility

- ARIA 1.2 combobox: the `<input>` has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` (the listbox id) and `aria-activedescendant` (the highlighted option); the list is `role="listbox"`, rows are `role="option"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-disabled`; grouped rows sit in `role="group"` named by their title (`aria-labelledby`).
- Keyboard map: focus or `ArrowDown` opens the list; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the highlight (wrapping, skipping disabled rows); `Home`/`End` move it to the first/last option while the list is open (otherwise the caret moves); `Enter` commits the highlighted option, or the typed text when nothing is highlighted (`allowCustom`); `Escape` closes the list, and a second `Escape` restores the last committed text; `Tab` commits the highlighted option or the typed text and moves on; `Alt+ArrowUp` closes.
- Focus stays in the input the whole time; pointer clicks on rows do not move focus (`mousedown.prevent`).
- A polite status region announces the number of options after each change of the typed text ("3 options"), "No matches" and "Loading options"; it is visually hidden.
- The clear button is a real button with an accessible name ("Clear"), reachable by Tab only while there is a value, and returns focus to the input.
- `Field` integration through `Input`: label `for`/`id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, disabled.
- Contrast: option text and muted descriptions ≥4.5:1 on `--bg-surface-raised` in both themes; the active row is marked by its fill and `aria-activedescendant`, never colour alone for selection (a check icon marks the selected row).
- Touch targets: rows are 32 px tall, 44 px on `pointer: coarse`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-`/`pe-`, `text-start`, `ms-auto`); the list anchors at `bottom-start` and mirrors.
- Icons: the search glyph and the check mark are not mirrored.
- Keyboard: arrows are vertical, no change under rtl; `Home`/`End` keep their meaning.
- User data: option labels and the field value render with `dir="auto"` / `<bdi>`, so Latin identifiers inside rtl text keep their order.

## Internationalization

| Key                    | English source                                | Override prop |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `combobox.empty`       | `No matches`                                  | `emptyText`   |
| `combobox.loading`     | `Loading options`                             | —             |
| `combobox.useValue`    | `Use "{value}"`                               | —             |
| `combobox.clear`       | `Clear`                                       | —             |
| `combobox.suggestions` | `Suggestions`                                 | —             |
| `combobox.count`       | `{count} option` / `{count} options` (plural) | —             |

- Formatting: plural rules through the locale catalog (`Intl.PluralRules`); matching is case- and accent-insensitive with `String.prototype.normalize('NFD')` and `toLocaleLowerCase(locale)`.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the field fills its container and the list is at least as wide as the field (`matchTriggerWidth` floor, may grow to the longest row within the viewport).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): the list flips above the field when there is no room below, and rows truncate with an ellipsis.
- Touch: rows grow to 44 px on `pointer: coarse`; no hover-only affordance (the highlight follows the pointer and the keyboard).
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Combobox from '@aziontech/webkit/combobox'
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const name = ref('API_URL')

  const options = [
    { value: 'API_URL', description: 'Suggested' },
    { value: 'API_TOKEN', description: 'Suggested' },
    { value: 'NODE_ENV', description: 'System' },
    { value: 'LOG_LEVEL' },
    { value: 'CACHE_TTL' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Field.Label>Variable name</Field.Label>
    <Combobox
      v-model="name"
      :options="options"
      placeholder="Search or type a name"
      clearable
    />
    <Field.Description>Pick a known variable or type a new one.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/combobox.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/combobox.md).

# Date Range Picker

> A time range for queries over time: logs, events, traces and metrics. After the Console Kit date-time range (quick ranges, absolute range with times, previous and next) and Cloudscape's date range picker. The value is either **relative** (`{ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute' }`, read as "the last 15 minutes" and re-resolved against the clock on every query, so a live view keeps moving) or **absolute** (`{ type: 'absolute', start, end }`, two ISO 8601 instants). The trigger prints `Last 15 minutes` or the absolute range in the selected time zone with its UTC offset. The panel switches between Relative range (the quick ranges and a custom duration) and Absolute range (the `Calendar` month grid, start and end date and time fields, and the time zone selector) and commits only on Apply; Cancel and Escape drop the draft. Absolute boundaries are typed as wall-clock time in the selected zone and stored as instants, so the same value reads correctly in every zone. With `showStep`, Previous and Next move the range by its own length. Date math uses `Intl` and the native `Date` only.

- Import: `import DateRangePicker from '@aziontech/webkit/date-range-picker'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Filtering events, logs, traces or metrics by time, where "the last N minutes" must stay relative.
- Any range that needs times of day and a time zone, not only dates.
- Investigations that page through time window by window (`show-step`).

## Do

- Keep relative values relative: resolve them to instants when the query runs (`now - amount × unit` to `now`), never when the user picks them.
- Fix the reference clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages so labels and step limits are deterministic: `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` covers every picker below it; the `now` prop overrides it for one picker.
- Bind `v-model:time-zone` to the user's saved preference, and show times elsewhere on the page in the same zone.
- Set `max` (usually now) and `min` (the retention limit) instead of validating after Apply.
- Name the picker after what it filters (`aria-label="Events time range"`).

## Don’t

- Picking whole days for a report or a billing period, with day presets → use `calendar`.
- A single date or a date and time → use `calendar` with `mode="single"`.
- A fixed list of named intervals and nothing custom → use `select` or `toggle-group`.

## Related

- `calendar` — the month grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector come from it, so both pickers look and behave the same.
- `property-filter` — the query bar it sits next to in an events toolbar.
- `chart` — the histogram whose brush usually writes an absolute range back into this picker.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relativeOptions` | `RelativeOption[]` | `5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d` | false | Quick ranges listed on the Relative tab. |
| `timeZones` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Zones offered by the selector. Empty falls back to the zones `Intl` supports. |
| `showTimeZone` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Shows the time zone selector in the panel. |
| `showStep` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows Previous and Next buttons that move the range back or forward by its own length. |
| `rangeSelectorMode` | `'default' \| 'relative-only' \| 'absolute-only'` | `'default'` | false | Which kinds of range the panel offers. |
| `min` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Earliest instant an absolute range may start at. |
| `max` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Latest instant an absolute range may end at. |
| `now` | `Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference clock for relative ranges and stepping. Unset uses the nearest `WebkitProvider`'s `now`, then the real clock. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Trigger text with no range. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the trigger. Empty uses the locale catalog. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and the step buttons. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token of the trigger and the panel controls. |
| `modelValue` | `DateRangeValue \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |
| `timeZone` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:timeZone`). |

## v-model

| Model              | Type                     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model`          | `DateRangeValue \| null` | `null`  | `update:modelValue` | The committed range: relative (last N units, re-resolved against now) or absolute (ISO instants). Set on Apply with a valid draft, or by Previous / Next (always an absolute range). |
| `v-model:timeZone` | `string`                 | `''`    | `update:timeZone`   | IANA time zone the absolute range is typed and shown in; empty uses the local zone. Set on Apply after the zone changed in the panel.                                                |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `open`, `disabled`; the panel shows an inline error after an Apply that the draft cannot satisfy.
- `data-state="open|closed"` on the root and the panel; `data-size`; `data-disabled`; `data-empty` on the trigger with no value; `data-selected` on the chosen quick range.
- The Next button is disabled while the range is relative (it already ends now) or when the step would pass `max` (or now); Previous is disabled when the step would pass `min`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: a 2 px `--ring-color` ring inset on each trigger segment; the quick ranges ring their row when the radio inside has focus.
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the panel and the focus trap moves into it; `Tab` cycles inside the panel; the range type is a `ToggleGroup` (arrow keys); the quick ranges are native radios (`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` move and select); the grid keeps the `calendar` keyboard map; `Escape` closes without committing and returns focus to the trigger.
- ARIA: the trigger has `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and a name that starts with the picker's label and contains the visible range; the panel is a named `dialog`; the quick ranges are a `fieldset` with a `legend`; the custom duration and unit have visible labels; the error is `role="alert"` and described from the duration field; Previous and Next are named buttons.
- Targets: options are 32 px high (44 px on `pointer: coarse`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s`, `border-e`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `end-`, `text-start`); the panel anchors to the start edge of the trigger.
- Icons: the Previous and Next chevrons mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`); the clock and calendar glyphs do not.
- Keyboard: the grid's arrow keys follow the reading direction (from `calendar`).
- User data: the range text sits in `<bdi>`.
- Teleported content: the panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`).

## Internationalization

| Key                                       | English source                                | Override prop          |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `dateRangePicker.label`                   | Time range                                    | `ariaLabel`            |
| `dateRangePicker.placeholder`             | Select a time range                           | `placeholder`          |
| `dateRangePicker.dialog`                  | Choose a time range                           | —                      |
| `dateRangePicker.rangeType`               | Range type                                    | —                      |
| `dateRangePicker.relative` / `absolute`   | Relative range / Absolute range               | —                      |
| `dateRangePicker.quickRanges`             | Quick ranges                                  | —                      |
| `dateRangePicker.custom`                  | Custom range                                  | —                      |
| `dateRangePicker.amount` / `unit`         | Duration / Unit                               | —                      |

- Formatting: the absolute range goes through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the active locale; the relative labels through the plural rules of the active locale; the grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector use the `calendar` keys.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the trigger is inline and truncates its text inside the available width (`max-w-full`).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): the panel is at most `min(90vw, 24rem)` wide and scrolls inside itself when taller than the viewport.
- Touch: options are 44 px high on `pointer: coarse`; nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

```vue
    v-model="range"
    aria-label="Events time range"
  />
</template>
```

# Field

> One composable form field that wraps **any** control — `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput`, `PasswordInput`, `PhoneInput`, `InputGroup`, `Checkbox`, `RadioButton`, `Switch`, `Slider` — with its label, description and error. The root `Field` owns the field state (`invalid`, `disabled`, `required`) and the ids, and shares them through `provide`/`inject`: the control picks up its `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required` from the Field, `Field.Label` points its `for` at the control and shows the Required marker, and `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` register themselves so the control is described by them. Grouping parts (`Field.Set`, `Field.Legend`, `Field.Group`, `Field.Content`, `Field.Title`, `Field.Separator`) build fieldsets, choice cards and settings rows. It replaces the v5 `field-*` family (`field-text`, `field-select`, `field-checkbox-block`, …), one wrapper per control, with a single anatomy.

- Import: `import FieldRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/field-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Any labelled form control: a text input, a select, a textarea, a password, a phone number, a slider.
- A checkbox, radio or switch with its label beside it (`orientation="horizontal"`).
- A selectable choice card: `Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field` (replaces the v5 `*-block` variants).
- A group of related controls under one caption (`Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`), or a form section (`Field.Group`).

## Do

- Put the state on the `Field`, not on the control: `<Field invalid>` sets `aria-invalid` on the control and the invalid tone on `Field.Description`.
- Let the Field own the ids. Pass an explicit `id` on the control and `for` on `Field.Label` only when another part of the page needs the id (focusing the first invalid field, an error summary link).
- Render `Field.Description` for guidance and `Field.Error` for a validation message; both are announced through `aria-describedby`. `Field.Error` has `role="alert"`, so render it only when there is an error.
- Choice cards: `<Field.Label><Field orientation="horizontal">control + Field.Content</Field></Field.Label>`. Never nest a choice card inside another `Field`; group cards with `Field.Set`.
- Use `orientation="responsive"` for settings rows that stack in a narrow container and sit side by side in a wide one; it follows the nearest container (a `Field.Group`, a Card, a dialog or drawer body).

## Don’t

- A control with no visible label inside a toolbar or a table cell → render the control alone with an `aria-label`.
- A group of mutually exclusive cards with icons → use `radio-cards`.
- A static key/value read-out → use `key-value-pairs`.

## Related

- `label` — the standalone label; `Field.Label` adds the `for` wiring and the Required marker from the Field.
- `helper-text` — the tone-aware helper line that `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` render.
- `input-group` — wraps an input with addons; put it inside a `Field` and use `InputGroup.Input` as the control.
- `phone-input`, `password-requirements` — the controls that replaced `field-phone-number` and the requirements row of `field-password`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'responsive'` | `'vertical'` | false | Layout axis: label above the control, beside it, or beside it once the enclosing container (a FieldGroup, Card, drawer or dialog body) is wide enough. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field invalid: the control sets aria-invalid and FieldDescription switches to the invalid tone. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the wrapped control and dims the field. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows the Required marker on FieldLabel and sets required on the wrapped control. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Field.Label`, the control, `Field.Description`, `Field.Error` (or `Field.Content` beside the control in a horizontal field). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/field-label`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-error`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-set`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-legend`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/field-separator`

## Sub-components

The root `Field` provides `fieldContextKey` (`injection-key.ts`): a generated `controlId`, the reactive `invalid` / `disabled` / `required` flags, `describedBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` parts), `labelledBy` (the ids of the mounted `Field.Title` parts) and `register`. Controls read it through the shared `useFieldControl` composable (`src/composables/use-field-control`); an explicit prop or attribute on the control always wins over the Field. Composite controls (`Select`, `MultiSelect`, `PhoneInput`) consume the context on their root and provide `null` below it, so their inner search inputs never take the field id. Every part works outside a `Field` too (it then reads no state). Member names mirror the anatomy; there is no `Trigger`/`Content` pair because the field has no open/closed state.

- `field-label/field-label.vue` — `<label>` whose `for` defaults to the Field's `controlId`; appends the Required marker (`*` + "(Required)") when the Field is `required`, and a `Hint` glyph when `hint` is set.
  - Props: `hint` (`string`, default `''`) — short explanation revealed by a `Hint` glyph.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — label text, or a horizontal `Field` for a choice card.
- `field-description/field-description.vue` — guidance line rendered through `HelperText`; registers its id with the Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-error/field-error.vue` — validation message rendered through `HelperText kind="invalid"` with `role="alert"`; registers its id with the Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-group/field-group.vue` — vertical stack of fields; it is a `@container/field-group`, one of the containers `orientation="responsive"` can follow.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-set/field-set.vue` — native `<fieldset>` without browser chrome, for a group of related fields or choices.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-legend/field-legend.vue` — native `<legend>` captioning a `Field.Set`.
  - Props: `kind` (`'legend' \| 'label'`, default `'legend'`) — `legend` titles a section, `label` matches a `Field.Label` for a group of choices.
  - Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-content/field-content.vue` — column that holds the label/title and descriptions beside a control in a horizontal Field.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-title/field-title.vue` — title inside a choice card; registers its id with the Field so the card's `Checkbox`, `RadioButton` or `Switch` is named by it through `aria-labelledby` (the wrapping `Field.Label` make…
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default`.
- `field-separator/field-separator.vue` — horizontal rule between fields, with optional centred text.
  - Props: _none_. Events: _none_. Slots: `default` — optional text.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `required`
- `data-orientation`: `vertical` | `horizontal` | `responsive`
- `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required` mirror the props on the root
- `data-slot` identifies every part (`field`, `field-label`, `field-description`, `field-error`, `field-group`, `field-set`, `field-legend`, `field-content`, `field-title`, `field-separator`)
- Responsive: `orientation="responsive"` queries the nearest container (`@md:`), not only `Field.Group`: inside a Card, a drawer or dialog body (`@container/panel`), a settings section or a `Field.Group` it stacks the label above the control in a narrow box and puts them side by side from `@md`. With no container ancestor it stays vertical.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the control keeps its own ring; a choice card shows `has-[:focus-visible]:ring-2 ring-(--ring-color) ring-offset-1 ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` around the whole card.
- Keyboard map: the Field adds no keys; `Tab` reaches the control, and clicking `Field.Label` focuses or toggles it.
- ARIA: root `role="group"`; `Field.Label` `for` → control `id`; control `aria-describedby` → every mounted `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` id; control `aria-invalid` when the Field is `invalid`; `required` / `aria-required` when it is `required`; `Field.Error` `role="alert"`; `Field.Set` is a native `fieldset` named by its `legend`; the Required marker's `*` is `aria-hidden` and the word "(Required)" is read.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for label, description and error text in every tone, including disabled.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the choice card transition.
- Touch target: the whole choice card is the target; a horizontal Field's label extends the control's target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Field from '@aziontech/webkit/field'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const email = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Field class="max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Input
      v-model="email"
      type="email"
      autocomplete="email"
      placeholder="you@example.com"
    />
    <Field.Description>We'll never share your email.</Field.Description>
  </Field>
</template>
```

<!-- components/file-dropzone.md -->

# File Dropzone

> A FileDropzone is the target a user drags files from the operating system onto. It owns the drag lifecycle (only drags carrying `Files` count), the `accept` / `multiple` filtering, and the idle/active look, and it hands the result back as two activation events: `drop` with the accepted files, `reject` with the files it filtered out. It holds no value and renders no file list. The list, upload progress and validation messages belong to the consumer (typically a `Field` around this component, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` carry the messages). `kind` covers the two places a drop target lives: - **`inline`**: a dashed region that is always visible (icon, title, description, plus a default slot for the "Browse files" action the consumer composes). It switches to the active look while files are dragged over it. This is the Cloudscape FileDropzone / Cloudflare Pages "Upload assets" shape. - **`overlay`**: invisible at rest. When files are dragged into the window it fades in over its nearest positioned ancestor (`absolute inset-0`), and it fades out on window drag-leave, drop or `Escape`. This is the Vercel "drag and drop a folder to deploy" shape, and it replaces the sample app's page-level `ProjectDropZone` and the drop target in the `Templates/Platform/States/ProjectIntake` story. The drop target itself is pointer-only. It is never a keyboard control. The keyboard (and screen-reader) path to the same outcome is a real button the consumer puts in the default slot (`inline`), or elsewhere on the page (`overlay`).

- Import: `import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A form or settings surface accepts one or more files and should also accept them by drag (`kind="inline"` with a Browse button in the slot).
- A whole page or card should accept a project, folder contents or assets dropped anywhere on it, with no permanent drop region taking up space (`kind="overlay"` inside a `relative` container).
- The consumer needs the accepted and rejected files separated by an `accept` filter before it uploads anything.

## Do

- Always give the user a non-drag path. In `inline`, put a `Button` in the default slot that opens a native `<input type="file">`. In `overlay`, keep an upload button somewhere on the page. The drop target is pointer-only by design.
- Pass the same `accept` string to the dropzone and to the native input behind your Browse button, so both paths filter the same way.
- Handle `reject`. Tell the user which files were skipped and why (e.g. a `toast` naming the files and the accepted types). A silent rejection reads as a broken drop.
- Announce the outcome of a drop yourself (a toast, or a live region on your file list). The dropzone does not announce drag states (see Accessibility).
- Render one `overlay` dropzone per positioned container, and make the container `relative`. Without a positioned ancestor the overlay covers the nearest positioned element up the tree, which may be the whole page.
- Place the `overlay` dropzone as the last child of its container, so it paints above the container's other positioned content (see Theme gaps).
- When the consumer's own flow is busy (an upload in progress), set `disabled` and disable the Browse button too.
- Put the accepted types and limits in `description` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"). The title is the instruction, the description is the constraint.

## Don’t

- Picking files by keyboard or click only, with no drag affordance → a `button` that opens a native file input is enough.
- Showing the chosen files, their progress or their errors → render them yourself with `progress`, `message` or `helper-text`. The dropzone renders none of these.
- Dragging items inside the page (reordering rows, moving cards) → this component only reacts to OS drags that carry `Files`. In-page drag and drop is out of scope.
- A static "nothing here yet" panel with no drop behavior → use `empty-state`.

## Related

- `button`: the "Browse files" action composed into the default slot. It is the keyboard path to the same outcome as a drop.
- `empty-state`: a no-data panel. Compose a FileDropzone inside or beside it when the empty state's call to action is "upload".
- `progress`: the consumer renders per-file progress after `drop`. The dropzone does not track uploads.
- `toast`: confirms the result of a drop or reports rejected files to everyone, including users who never see the drag.
- `card`: a positioned container (`class="relative"`) that hosts an `overlay` dropzone.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'inline' \| 'overlay'` | `'inline'` | false | Placement. Inline is an always-visible dashed region; overlay stays hidden until files are dragged over the window, then covers its nearest positioned ancestor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Instruction shown under the icon. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Drop files to upload`). |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Secondary line under the title, typically the accepted types and limits. Not rendered when empty. |
| `accept` | `string` | `''` | false | Comma-separated file filter using the native input accept syntax (extensions, MIME types, type wildcards). Files that do not match are rejected. Empty accepts every file. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When false, only the first accepted file of a drop is accepted and the rest are rejected. |
| `directories` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Accepts dropped folders: walks every dropped folder and emits the files inside, each with its `webkitRelativePath` (`assets/img/logo.svg`). The events fire after the walk. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Ignores drags and drops: no active state, no events. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Paints the inline region with the danger border so a wrapping field can show a validation error. Drops still work. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-cloud-upload'` | false | PrimeIcons class for the glyph above the title. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drop` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires when files are dropped on the target (the inline root, or the visible overlay) and at least one passes `accept` / `multiple`. `files` holds only the accepted files, in `dataTransfer.files` order, and is never empty. Not emitted when `disabled`. Declaring `drop` means a consumer `@drop` listener binds to this event, never to the native DOM `drop` on the root. |
| `reject` | `(event: DragEvent, files: File[])` | Activation event. Fires on the same drop when one or more files were filtered out, because they do not match `accept` or exceed `multiple="false"`. `files` holds only the rejected files and is never empty. When a drop has both kinds of file, `drop` fires first, then `reject`, with the same `event`. Not emitted when `disabled`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Actions or extra content under the description, typically a "Browse files" `Button`. Rendered only in `kind="inline"`. The overlay is `aria-hidden` decoration, so interactive content there would be unreachable and is not rendered. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `idle`, `active` (files dragged over the target), `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `idle` | `active`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop (`inline` | `overlay`)
- `data-disabled` is present when the `disabled` prop is true. A disabled dropzone is always `data-state="idle"`.
- `data-invalid` is present when the `invalid` prop is true.
- **Inline / invalid**: the dashed border turns `--danger-border` while idle; the active state still wins while files are dragged over it. Overlay ignores `invalid`.
- **Inline / idle**: dashed `--border-strong` border on a `--bg-surface` fill. Icon, title, description and slot are centered.
- **Inline / active**: the border turns `--border-selected` and the fill `--bg-selected`. Layout does not move (same border width in both states).
- **Inline / disabled**: `--border-default` dashed border, `--bg-disabled` fill, icon, title and description in `--text-disabled`, `cursor-not-allowed`. The slot still renders, and the consumer disables its own Browse button.
- **Overlay / idle**: not displayed (`v-show`). The root stays in the DOM so `data-testid` and `$attrs` are always present.
- **Overlay / active**: `absolute inset-0` over the nearest positioned ancestor. 2px dashed `--border-selected` border on a `--bg-canvas` fill, `--shape-card` radius. The content column sits in a `sticky top-0` wrapper capped at the viewport height (`h-dvh max-h-full`), so the prompt stays centered in the viewport even when the ancestor is taller than the screen (the page-level case). It receives pointer events while active so the drop lands on it, and `data-[state=idle]:pointer-events-none` keeps the fade-out from swallowing clicks.
- No `loading`, `empty` or `error` state: the dropzone does not upload, validate or list anything. `invalid` only paints the border; the message and the file list belong to the consumer (compose it inside a `Field`).

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the dropzone root is **not focusable** and has no focus ring. Focus belongs to the controls in the default slot, which carry their own `focus-visible` ring (e.g. `Button`).
- Keyboard map: none on the dropzone. Drag and drop from the OS is a pointer gesture with no keyboard equivalent on the target. The keyboard path is the consumer's Browse button, which opens a native file input and reaches the same outcome. `Escape` during a drag hides the overlay (window `keydown` fallback; browsers also cancel the drag natively).
- No `@click` on the root: clicking the region does nothing, so there is no click-without-key handler. The Browse button is the click target.
- ARIA, inline: the root is a `<div role="group">` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title and `aria-describedby` pointing at the description (only when `description` is non-empty), both ids from `useId()`. A screen reader therefore reads the slotted Browse button in context ("Drop files to upload, group, PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB each, Browse files, button"). The title is a `<p>`, not a heading: the page owns its heading outline. When `disabled`, the group carries `aria-disabled="true"`, so the dimmed title and description are announced as part of a disabled control and fall under the WCAG 1.4.3 exemption for inactive components.
- ARIA, overlay: the root is `aria-hidden="true"`. It is a pointer-only duplicate of an affordance that must exist elsewhere on the page, and it renders no interactive content.
- No `aria-live` in the component. Announcing every drag that crosses the window is noise, and the outcome that matters (files accepted or skipped) is the consumer's to announce from `drop` / `reject` (a `toast`, or a live region on its file list). `aria-dropeffect` / `aria-grabbed` are deprecated in WAI-ARIA 1.1 and are not used.
- The icon is decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `data-disabled` has no ARIA mirror because the root is not a control. The slotted button carries its own `disabled` / `aria-disabled`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and description in both themes, including `--text-muted` on `--bg-selected` (inline active) and on `--bg-canvas` (overlay). The `webkit-ui-verifier` must confirm the active state in both themes, since the unit suite has no CSS. The dashed border (`--border-strong` idle, `--border-selected` active) must meet 3:1 non-text contrast against the surrounding surface.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both overlay fades, `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the inline colour transition.
- Touch target: not applicable. The region is not a control (touch devices cannot drag OS files into a page), and the slotted Button carries its own ≥40×40 px target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import FileDropzone from '@aziontech/webkit/file-dropzone'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const input = ref(null)
  const browse = () => input.value?.click()
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-md)">
    <FileDropzone description="Or browse for files on your computer.">
      <Button
        label="Browse files"
        kind="secondary"
        size="medium"
        @click="browse"
      />
    </FileDropzone>
    <input
      ref="input"
      type="file"
      multiple
      class="hidden"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```
