<!-- components/radio-button.md -->

# Radio Button

> Atomic exclusive-choice control only — the circular radio input from Figma (no label, description, or helper). Wrap it in a horizontal `Field`, or a `Field.Label` choice card, for labeled layouts.

- Import: `import RadioButton from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-button'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- One choice from a small set of mutually exclusive options whose labels are laid out separately (a table row, a custom option row).
- A custom radio layout that the horizontal `Field` and the `Field.Label` choice card do not cover.

## Do

- Bind every radio in a group to the same `v-model` and give them the same `name`; each one emits its own `value` when selected.
- value` and `modelValue` are strings; map numeric or object ids to strings before binding.
- Give each radio an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at `inputId`, or pass `aria-label`.
- Wrap the group in a `fieldset` with a `legend` so the question itself is announced.

## Don’t

- A radio option in a form that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
- Options that need visual weight, such as plans or tiers → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`), or `radio-cards` for a horizontal grid of cards.
- More than one option may be selected → use `checkbox`.
- The options are many or loaded from data → use `select`.

## Related

- `field` — a horizontal `Field` puts the radio beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option with a selected border and background. Group the options in `Field.Set` + `Field.Legend`.
- `radio-cards` — horizontal grid of selectable cards with its own model.
- `checkbox` — the multi-pick counterpart.
- `select` — single choice from a dropdown when the options do not fit inline.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Selected value for v-model. |
| `value` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Option value for this radio instance. |
| `name` | `string` | `undefined` | false | HTML name shared across a mutually exclusive group. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `inputId` | `string` | `undefined` | false | id for the native input; links label to control. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `string` | v-model. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-checked` mirrors selected state
- Touch: the native input that receives the click extends past the 20 px circle to 24 × 24 px, and to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer; the drawn circle does not change.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses native input; `Space` selects within group.
- ARIA: native `type="radio"` input with `aria-checked`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import RadioButton from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-button'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const selected = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioButton
    v-model="selected"
    name="webkit-radio"
    value="a"
    input-id="webkit-radio-a"
    aria-label="Option A"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/radio-button.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/radio-button.md).

<!-- components/radio-cards.md -->

# Radio Cards

> Horizontal grid of selectable cards for mutually exclusive choices (plans, roles, feature tiers). Each option shows label, optional icon and description, with optional trailing content via the `tag` slot. Migrated from the legacy `radio-cards` core component into the webkit inputs layer.

- Import: `import RadioCards from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-cards'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- One choice among a few options where each option needs a label plus an optional icon or one-line description: usage intent, role, plan tier.
- Options laid out side by side as cards that wrap onto new rows, bound to one `v-model` value for the whole group.
- A card needs small trailing content under its text, such as a price or a "Recommended" tag, through the `tag` slot.

## Do

- Give every item a unique `value`; it is both the `v-model` payload and the render key.
- Name the group by passing `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label` on the component: it renders a `role="radiogroup"` with no visible label of its own. Set an item's `ariaLabel` when its `label` alone is ambiguous.
- disabled` applies to the whole group; there is no per-item disabled state, so leave unavailable options out of `items`.
- Use the `tag` slot for trailing content. The `default` slot replaces the whole card body (icon, label, description and `tag`), so use it only when the card needs a different layout.
- Arrow keys move and select in one step, as in any radio group, so `update:modelValue` fires while a keyboard user browses. Don't trigger navigation or requests on every change.

## Don’t

- You place each card-style radio by hand, or the choice must submit through a native form `name` → use `field` choice cards (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field` with a `radio-button`).
- The options don't need card weight and read fine as inline rows → use horizontal `field`s with a `radio-button`.
- There are more options than fit in a row or two, or the choice sits in a compact form → use `select` inside a `field`.
- More than one option can be picked → use `field` choice cards with a `checkbox`.

## Related

- `field` — a `Field.Label` choice card is a single card-style radio (or checkbox) with title and description; compose several by hand with a shared `name`, or use a horizontal `Field` for an inline labelled row.
- `select` — dropdown for long option lists.
- onboarding-form` — uses this component for its usage-intent question.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `string \| number` | `undefined` | false | Currently selected item value (v-model). |
| `items` | `TItem[]` | `undefined` | true | Options rendered as selectable cards; each entry must include `value` and `label`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables all options and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TItem['value']` | v-model when the user selects an option. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | { item: TItem; selected: boolean } | Overrides the entire card body for an option. |
| `tag` | { item: TItem; selected: boolean } | Trailing content below label/description (e.g. plan badge). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `selected`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root and each option
- `data-selected` mirrors whether `modelValue === item.value`
- Reflow: each option is capped at the width of the group (`max-w-full`) so long descriptions and tags wrap inside a narrow box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on each option.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` / arrow keys move focus between options; `Enter` / `Space` selects the focused option.
- ARIA: root `role="radiogroup"`; each option `role="radio"` with `aria-checked` and `aria-label` from `item.ariaLabel` or `item.label`. The `aria-label` replaces the option's text, so an item with a `description` also points `aria-describedby` at the rendered description, which would otherwise never be announced.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px via card padding.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none mirror.
- Keyboard: in a horizontal row `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move to the next/previous card, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`); `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` are unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import RadioCards from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-cards'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const items = [
    {
      value: 'option1',
      icon: 'pi pi-check',
      label: 'Option One',
      description: 'First option description'
    },
    {
      value: 'option2',
      icon: 'pi pi-times',
      label: 'Option Two',
      description: 'Second option description'
    },
    {
      value: 'option3',
      icon: 'pi pi-star',
      label: 'Option Three',
      description: 'Third option description'
    }
  ]
  const selected = ref('option1')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioCards
    v-model="selected"
    :items="items"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/radio-cards.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/radio-cards.md).

<!-- components/schema-form.md -->

# Schema Form

> A form rendered from a JSON schema: each property of an object schema becomes a `Field` with its label, description, Required marker and control, and a nested object becomes a fieldset with its own legend. It edits one value object through `v-model`, seeds the schema's defaults, validates the supported draft-07 keywords with built-in messages (on leaving a field, or only after `validate()`), and shows server messages passed by field path. It is for forms whose fields are data (a function's arguments, an integration's settings), not for forms a designer lays out by hand.

- Import: `import SchemaForm from '@aziontech/webkit/schema-form'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A function, template or integration declares its own arguments as a JSON schema and the console must ask for them.
- The same settings form must follow a schema the server sends (fields added or removed without a release).
- A form of typed values (text, choices, numbers, switches, lists) with constraints that already live in a schema.

## Do

- Give every property a `title` and a one-sentence `description`; the key is only the fallback label.
- Put limits in the schema (`minimum`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `enum`) so the form checks them; say the rule in the `description` when it is a `pattern`, since the built-in message cannot name it.
- Keep the default `validate-on="blur"` for short forms; use `submit` when the form sits in a drawer or dialog with one Save.
- Call `validate()` on submit and stop when it returns `valid: false`; it shows every message and focuses the first invalid field.
- Pass server rejections in `errors` keyed by path (`origin.host`): the field turns invalid with that message until the user edits it (the form-error rule). Put a section-level failure in an `Alert` above the form, not in `errors`.
- Use a `field:<path>` slot for a control the schema cannot express (`RadioCards`, a resource picker); the slot keeps the label, description and messages.
- Do not rely on unsupported keywords (`$ref`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `if`/`then`, `const`, `format`, `uniqueItems`, `multipleOf`, `additionalProperties`): they are ignored, so validate them on the server.

## Don’t

- A form with a fixed, designed layout (settings sections, create pages) → compose `field`, `input`, `select` and `switch` by hand (`platform/edit/edit-resource`, `platform/create/single-page-create`).
- Rows of key/value pairs the user adds and removes → use `attribute-editor`.
- Editing the schema itself, or raw JSON → use `code-editor`.
- A single choice or value → use the control directly inside a `field`.

## Related

- `field` — the wrapper every generated field uses; SchemaForm adds no field chrome of its own.
- `input`, `select`, `switch`, `textarea` — the controls it renders per type.
- `attribute-editor` — user-defined key/value rows, where SchemaForm renders a fixed set of keys.
- `code-editor` — the JSON view of the same value, when the user prefers to type it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `SchemaFormSchema` | `—` | true | JSON schema of an object (draft-07 subset); each property becomes a Field. |
| `errors` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | false | Server or external messages by field path; a field shows its message until it is edited. |
| `ui` | `Record<string, SchemaFormUi>` | `{}` | false | Presentation overrides by field path: widget, placeholder, hidden, and key order (`''` is the root). |
| `validateOn` | `'blur' \| 'submit'` | `'blur'` | false | When fields first show their validation message: on leaving the field, or only after `validate()`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every field. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows every value without letting it change. |
| `modelValue` | `SchemaFormValue` | `—` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                      | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}`    | `update:modelValue` | The edited object. Each change emits a new object; an emptied field removes its key, and an emptied nested object is removed. Defaults are seeded on mount and on a schema change. |

## States

- Visual states per field come from `Field`: `default`, `invalid` (message under the control), `disabled`, read-only.
- `data-disabled` and `data-readonly` on the root mirror the props; each field carries `data-path` and `data-widget`.
- Validation timing: a field shows its own message after the user leaves it (`validate-on="blur"`), after `validate()` in both modes, and from then on updates as the user types. Opening a `Select` does not count as leaving its field.
- Server messages (`errors`) show at once, win over the field's own message and leave once that field is edited; a new `errors` object shows them again.
- Draft text: a number, list or JSON field keeps what the user typed while it does not parse; the value then holds no key for it, and the field reports "Enter a number." or "Enter valid JSON."

## Accessibility

- Every control is wrapped in a `Field` (`role="group"`): `Field.Label` targets the control by id, the description and the message join `aria-describedby`, `required` and `invalid` set `aria-required` and `aria-invalid`.
- A nested object is a real `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, so its fields are announced with the group name.
- Messages are text under the control, never colour alone; the message replaces the description while it shows, as the design sample does.
- `validate()` moves focus to the first invalid control, in reading order, so keyboard and screen-reader users land on the problem.
- Keyboard map: no keys of its own; Tab moves through the controls in schema order (or `ui` order); each control keeps its own keys.
- A `field:<path>` slot control must name itself (the scope gives `invalid`, `required`, `disabled`); WebKit inputs read the Field context and need nothing.
- Visible focus, contrast and touch targets come from the composed controls.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: no layout of its own beyond a column of `Field`s; the composed controls use logical utilities.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: no arrow keys of its own.
- User data: list and JSON text keep the browser's own direction per line; values are not wrapped in `<bdi>`.

## Internationalization

| Key                            | English source                                | Override prop          |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `schemaForm.required`          | This field is required.                       | —                      |
| `schemaForm.minLength`         | Use at least {min} characters.                | —                      |
| `schemaForm.maxLength`         | Use at most {max} characters.                 | —                      |
| `schemaForm.pattern`           | This value doesn't match the expected format. | —                      |
| `schemaForm.minimum`           | Enter {min} or more.                          | —                      |
| `schemaForm.maximum`           | Enter {max} or less.                          | —                      |
| `schemaForm.number`            | Enter a number.                               | —                      |
| `schemaForm.integer`           | Enter a whole number.                         | —                      |
| `schemaForm.enum`              | Choose one of the options.                    | —                      |
| `schemaForm.minItems`          | Add at least {min} values.                    | —                      |
| `schemaForm.maxItems`          | Add at most {max} values.                     | —                      |
| `schemaForm.listItem`          | Line {line}: {message}                        | —                      |
| `schemaForm.json`              | Enter valid JSON.                             | —                      |
| `schemaForm.selectPlaceholder` | Select an option                              | `ui[path].placeholder` |
| `schemaForm.numberPlaceholder` | A number                                      | `ui[path].placeholder` |
| `schemaForm.numberFrom`        | From {min}                                    | `ui[path].placeholder` |
| `schemaForm.listPlaceholder`   | One value per line                            | `ui[path].placeholder` |
| `schemaForm.jsonPlaceholder`   | A JSON value                                  | `ui[path].placeholder` |

- Formatting: `{min}` and `{max}` go through the locale's number format (`useTranslate`). Labels and descriptions come from the schema, so a translated form needs a translated schema.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; the root is a `@container/schema-form` so slot content can react to the form's width.
- Narrow: fields are full width at any size; there is no side-by-side layout.
- Touch: targets come from the composed controls.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; long values wrap in the textarea.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SchemaForm from '@aziontech/webkit/schema-form'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const schema = {
    type: 'object',
    required: ['greeting', 'region'],
    properties: {
      greeting: {
        type: 'string',
        title: 'Greeting',
        description: 'The text the function returns on every request.',
        default: 'Hello from the edge',
        maxLength: 80
      },
      region: {
        type: 'string',
        title: 'Region',
        description: 'Where the function reads its data from.',
        enum: ['sa-east', 'us-east', 'eu-west']
      },
      timeout: {
        type: 'integer',
        title: 'Timeout (ms)',
        description: 'How long the function waits for its origin.',
        minimum: 100,
        maximum: 30000,
        default: 3000
      },
      debug: {
        type: 'boolean',
        title: 'Debug headers',
        description: 'Adds timing headers to every response.',
        default: false
      },
      allowedPaths: {
        type: 'array',
        title: 'Allowed paths',
        description: 'Requests to other paths return 404.',
        items: { type: 'string', pattern: '^/' }
      }
    }
  }

  const args = ref({ greeting: 'Hello from the edge', timeout: 3000, debug: false })
</script>

<template>
  <div class="flex w-full max-w-(--container-sm) flex-col gap-(--spacing-lg)">
    <SchemaForm
      v-model="args"
      :schema="schema"
    />
    <pre
      class="m-0 overflow-auto rounded-(--shape-elements) bg-(--bg-surface) p-(--spacing-sm) font-code text-body-xs text-(--text-muted)"
      >{{ JSON.stringify(args, null, 2) }}</pre>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/select.md -->

# Select

> Select control for choosing one (`multiple={false}`) or many (`multiple={true}`) options from a list. The trigger field mirrors `Input`'s visual API (size, hover/focus/filled/disabled/invalid/required states) so a Select sits next to a TextInput without visual drift. The dropdown panel is teleported to `body` and anchored to the trigger by the shared `usePlacement` composable — no `@floating-ui` runtime. Each option carries a radio indicator in single mode or a checkbox indicator in multi mode, optionally a leading slot/icon and a trailing tag. Search and "Create new" footer are exposed as slots on `<SelectContent>`. Aligned with Figma frames `3714:10801` (trigger states) and `3899:29361` (options panel).

- Import: `import SelectRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/select-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- One value from a list too long to show inline (regions, runtimes, plans).
- Options grouped under headings, with icons or trailing tags.
- A list that needs a search box or a "Create new" action inside the panel.

## Do

- Render `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Content` inside the root; the parts read the root's context and throw outside it.
- Give each `Select.Option` a stable `value`; pass `displayValue` to control how the trigger renders the selection.
- Type an options list as `SelectOptionItem<string>[]` and render it with `v-for` into `Select.Option` (`:value`, `:icon`, `:disabled`, the `label` as the slot); bind a typed model so `displayValue` and `update:modelValue` take that type with no cast.
- With `multiple`, `modelValue` becomes an array; for a field that is always multi-pick prefer `multi-select`.
- Use `readonly` to show a fixed selection and `disabled` when the field is unavailable; neither opens the panel.
- A switcher inside a line of text, such as the environment that ends a resource's breadcrumb (`Workloads › workload_01 › Production ⌄`), is `kind="transparent"` with `size="small"` and an `aria-label` on `Select.Trigger`: no border or fill until hover, sized to its value. Never put a bordered field in the header, and never restyle the trigger with `!` overrides.
- Keep `kind="transparent"` out of forms: it draws no border, so it cannot show the `invalid` or `required` border; a form field is the default `outlined` inside a `Field`.

## Don’t

- A select with a visible label and helper/error text in a form → put it inside a `field`; the trigger picks up the field's id, description and state.
- The field is always multi-pick → use `multi-select`.
- Two to five options that fit on screen → use horizontal `field`s with a `radio-button`, or `radio-cards` for cards.
- The list triggers actions or navigation instead of holding a value → use `dropdown`.

## Related

- `field` — label, this select, and description/error, with the wiring done.
- `multi-select` — multi-only variant with checkbox rows and an array model.
- dropdown` — action menu that reports the chosen option as an event and holds no form value.
- `input-group` — joins a select to an input, such as currency plus amount.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `TValue` | `undefined` | false | Two-way bound selection. Scalar in single mode; array in multi mode. Its type flows to `displayValue` and `update:modelValue`. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, switches the component to multi-select; options render checkbox indicators and `modelValue` is an array. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | false | Controlled open state for the dropdown. Use with `v-model:open`. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `undefined` | false | Trigger placeholder shown when no option is selected. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; affects trigger height (small=28px, medium=32px, large=40px) matching `Input`. |
| `kind` | `'outlined' \| 'transparent'` | `'outlined'` | false | Trigger look: `outlined` is the bordered field; `transparent` has no border or fill until hover, sized to its value, for a switcher inside a line of text such as the environment at the end of a breadcrumb. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the trigger and prevents opening; applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only; the current selection is visible but the dropdown cannot open. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required; applies the required (warning) border and sets `aria-required` on the trigger, matching `Input`. The label's Required tag is owned by the wrapping form-field, not by this component. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the invalid border + ring tokens and sets `aria-invalid` on the trigger. |
| `displayValue` | `(value: TValue) => string` | `undefined` | false | Custom formatter used by the trigger to render the selected label(s); receives the current `modelValue`, typed as the bound model. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TValue` | Fires when an option is selected (single) or toggled (multi). |
| `update:open` | `boolean` | Fires when the dropdown opens or closes. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Composition slot; receives `<SelectTrigger>` and `<SelectContent>` (and the option tree inside it). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/select-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/select-option`

## Sub-components

- `select-trigger/select-trigger.vue` — Bordered trigger field with optional left icon slot, selected-value label, and chevron-down.
- `select-content/select-content.vue` — Popover panel teleported to `body` and anchored with `usePlacement`; exposes `#search` and `#footer` slots and scrolls its option list when content exceeds `max-h-[320px]`.
- `select-group/select-group.vue` — Section wrapper for a labelled group of options; renders a `text-label-sm` heading in `--text-muted` when `label` is set.
- `select-option/select-option.vue` — Selectable option row with a mode-aware indicator (radio in single mode, checkbox in multi mode), an optional `icon` (PrimeIcons), an optional leading `#left` slot, the option label…

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `filled`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `required`, `opened`
- `data-state` on the root and trigger: `open` | `closed`
- `data-size` on the trigger mirrors the `size` prop
- `data-kind` on the root, the trigger and the panel mirrors `kind` (`outlined` | `transparent`)
- `kind="transparent"`: the trigger and root size to the value (`w-auto`, capped at the container), no border, no fill, `--spacing-xs` inline padding, `.text-label-md` like a breadcrumb crumb, `--bg-mask` on hover and while open; the panel stops matching the trigger's width and takes at least `--container-3xs`
- `data-disabled`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-filled` mirror the matching props (or the selection state for `data-filled`)
- `data-mode` on the root: `single` | `multiple`
- `data-selected` on `<SelectOption>` when the option's value is part of the current selection
- Long lists: above 300 options the list mounts in chunks of 100 as they scroll near view (unmounted chunks keep their height, 32 px per option), so opening a 1,000-option list stays within its runtime budget. The first arrow, `Home` or `End` key in the list mounts every option before moving focus, so keyboard navigation always reaches every option.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and on every option row.
- Keyboard map (trigger): `Tab` focuses; `Space`/`Enter`/`ArrowDown` opens the panel; `Escape` closes it.
- Keyboard map (open panel): opening focuses the search field when there is one, else the selected option, else the first enabled option; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` move the active option and wrap; `Home`/`End` jump to first/last; `Enter`/`Space` select, close and return focus to the trigger; `Escape` closes and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes and moves focus to the control after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes and returns focus to the trigger. Tests: `select.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: trigger uses `role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded` bound to open state, `aria-controls` pointing to the content element. Content uses `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable` mirroring `multiple`. Each option uses `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring its selection. Decorative icons (`pi pi-chevron-down`, `pi-heart`, etc.) are `aria-hidden="true"`.
- `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` on the trigger mirror the matching props.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons + borders), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every transition/animation-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on `size="large"`; smaller sizes are documented as dense-layout-only (consistent with `Input`).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="listbox"` content binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
  const options = [
    { value: 'opt-1', label: 'Option 1' },
    { value: 'opt-2', label: 'Option 2' },
    { value: 'opt-3', label: 'Option 3' },
    { value: 'opt-4', label: 'Option 4' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Select
    aria-label="Option"
    v-model="value"
    size="large"
    placeholder="Select an option"
  >
    <Select.Trigger />
    <Select.Content>
      <Select.Option
        v-for="o in options"
        :key="o.value"
        :value="o.value"
        >{{ o.label }}</Select.Option
      >
    </Select.Content>
  </Select>
</template>
```

<!-- components/slider.md -->

# Slider

> Bare range control `Slider`: one thumb on a horizontal track that picks a single number between `min` and `max` in `step` increments, with the portion from `min` to the value filled. It is built on a native `<input type="range">`, so the keyboard model, the `slider` role and the value announcements come from the platform; the component only styles the track, fill and thumb with tokens and adds optional tick marks and labelled reference values under the track. It renders no label, value readout or helper text — a field composes it with `Label` and `HelperText`, the same way `switch` and `number-input` are composed.

- Import: `import Slider from '@aziontech/webkit/slider'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Picking an approximate value inside a known, bounded range where the position matters more than the exact digit (a spend or usage limit, a percentage threshold, a sampling rate).
- A plan or capacity selector whose stops are evenly spaced and few enough to read as tick marks.
- A bounded value the user adjusts by feel and then commits (listen to `change` to persist on release instead of on every drag frame).

## Do

- Always give the slider an accessible name: `aria-label`, or a `Label` whose `for` matches the slider's `id`.
- Keep the value inside `[min, max]` and on a `step` multiple; the component clamps the displayed fill but never rewrites the bound value on its own.
- Turn on `ticks` only when every step is meaningful and the range has at most 21 positions; above that the ticks are not rendered.
- Use `referenceValues` for a few landmarks (`[0, 50, 100]`), not for every step — labels need horizontal room.
- Set `unit` when the number alone is ambiguous; it is appended verbatim to the reference labels and to the announced value, so include a leading space for word units (`' GB'`) and none for symbols (`'%'`).
- Listen to `change` for expensive side effects (saving a limit to the API); `v-model` updates on every movement.
- Use `readonly` to show a value the current user may not change but should still be able to focus and hear; use `disabled` when the control does not apply at all.

## Don’t

- The user must type an exact number, or the range is unbounded → use `number-input`.
- The choice is between a handful of named options (1h / 24h / 7d) → use `toggle-group`.
- An on/off setting → use `switch`.
- Showing progress or a read-only quantity the user cannot change → use `progress`.
- Selecting a range with two thumbs (from–to) — not supported by this component.

## Related

- `number-input` — exact numeric entry; pair it next to a slider when the user needs both coarse dragging and an exact value.
- `label` — names the slider; point its `for` at the slider's `id` (the `id` attribute lands on the native input).
- `helper-text` — description or error message under the slider in a field layout.
- `toggle-group` — a few discrete, named choices instead of a continuous range.
- `progress` — displays a fraction; it is not interactive.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | false | Lowest selectable value; the left end of the track. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | false | Highest selectable value; the right end of the track. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | false | Increment between selectable values, used by dragging and the arrow keys. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction, removes the control from the tab order and applies the disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Keeps the control focusable but prevents the value from changing. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies the danger tokens and sets aria-invalid. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name when no visible label is associated with the slider. |
| `ticks` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a tick mark at every step when the range has at most 21 positions. |
| `referenceValues` | `number[]` | `[]` | false | Values marked and labelled under the track; entries outside min and max are ignored. |
| `unit` | `string` | `''` | false | Text appended verbatim to the reference labels and to the announced value. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `change` | `number` | Commit signal: emitted from the native `change` event — on pointer release after a drag, and after each keyboard step — with the committed value. Lets the consumer persist once per interaction instead of once per drag frame (`update:modelValue` fires continuously). A value event, so no DOM event in the payload (see `.claude/rules/event-payloads.md`). Not emitted while `disabled` or `readonly`. |

## v-model

| Model     | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `v-model` | `number` | `0`     | `update:modelValue` | Current value via `defineModel<number>({ default: 0 })`. Emitted on every native `input` event (drag frame or key press) as `valueAsNumber`. Never emitted while `disabled` or `readonly`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (dragging), `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; the native input is also `disabled`, so it leaves the tab order and ignores pointer and keys.
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop. A native range input ignores the HTML `readonly` attribute, so the component owns the behaviour: the input stays focusable, `aria-readonly="true"` is set, the navigation keys (arrows, `PageUp`/`PageDown`, `Home`/`End`) are prevented, pointer dragging is prevented, and any native `input` that still slips through writes the current model back to the element without emitting. Visual: fill and thumb border switch to the muted token and the cursor is `default`.
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop: the fill and the thumb border switch to the danger tokens; `aria-invalid="true"` is set on the input.
- Fill: the root sets the custom property `--slider-fill` (the clamped value as a percentage of `max - min`; `0%` when `max <= min`) through an inline `style` binding, the same way `tracker` and `chart` set their custom properties. The WebKit/Blink track paints the fill with a bracketed gradient (`[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:bg-[linear-gradient(to_right,var(--accent)_var(--slider-fill),var(--bg-surface)_var(--slider-fill))]`); Firefox paints it natively with `[&::-moz-range-progress]:bg-(--accent)`. Expression values and custom-property declarations stay in brackets per `.claude/rules/styling.md`.
- Track and thumb are styled only through arbitrary pseudo-element variants on the native input (`appearance-none`, `[&::-webkit-slider-runnable-track]:…`, `[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:appearance-none …`, `[&::-moz-range-track]:…`, `[&::-moz-range-thumb]:…`) — no extra track/thumb elements, no `<style>` block.
- Geometry: the native input is 40 px tall (`h-10`, the hit area) and full width; the track is 4 px tall and centred; the thumb is 16×16 px.
- Ticks (`ticks`) and reference marks (`referenceValues`) render in an `aria-hidden` row under the track. Each mark is positioned at the thumb-centre position for its value — `thumb/2 + (100% - thumb) × fraction` — so marks line up with the thumb at both ends; the fraction is passed per mark through an inline custom property. Every reference value also draws a tick. Reference labels read `{value}{unit}`; the first label is start-aligned, the last end-aligned, the rest centred on their mark.
- Attribute routing (as in `number-input`): consumer `class` merges onto the root wrapper; every other attribute (`id`, `name`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, …) is forwarded to the native input so a `Label for` and a `HelperText` association reach the focusable element. `data-testid` is read from attrs and applied to the root.
- `data-testid`: root fallback `input-slider`; native input `${testId}__input`; each reference label `${testId}__reference`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the ring is drawn on the thumb, not the 40 px input box — `focus-visible:outline-none` on the input plus `focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-2 focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:[&::-webkit-slider-thumb]:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` and the same set for `[&::-moz-range-thumb]`.
- Keyboard map (native): `Tab` focuses; `ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp` +`step`; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowDown` −`step`; `PageUp`/`PageDown` move by a larger browser-defined increment; `Home` → `min`; `End` → `max`. Under `dir="rtl"` the track runs right to left, so `ArrowLeft` adds `step` and `ArrowRight` subtracts it (handled by the component through `useDirection`, so every browser agrees). When `readonly`, `Tab` still focuses and every value key is inert. When `disabled`, the control is skipped by `Tab`.
- ARIA: the native `<input type="range">` provides `role="slider"` and the implicit `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` / `aria-valuenow` from `min` / `max` / the value. `aria-label` comes from `ariaLabel` (omitted when empty, so an associated `Label` wins). `aria-valuetext="{value}{unit}"` is set only when `unit` is non-empty. `aria-readonly="true"` when `readonly`; `aria-invalid="true"` when `invalid`. The ticks and reference-label row is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast: thumb border and fill against the track ≥3:1 (non-text UI), reference labels ≥4.5:1, including the disabled state per the disabled tokens.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transitioned pseudo-element class.
- Touch target: the native input is 40 px tall and full width, so the whole track row is the hit area (≥40×40); the 16 px thumb is a visual, not the target.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: the track runs right to left under `dir="rtl"`; `ArrowLeft` adds `step` and `ArrowRight` subtracts it (`useDirection`); tick marks and labels are placed with `start-[…]`.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Slider from '@aziontech/webkit/slider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref(40)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="w-full max-w-(--container-xs)">
    <Slider
      v-model="value"
      :min="0"
      :max="100"
      :step="1"
      aria-label="Alert threshold"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/slider.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/slider.md).

<!-- components/switch.md -->

# Switch

> Control-only pill toggle `Switch` (36×20 px). Two visual types: `default` (plain handle) and `privacy` (handle carries a `pi-lock` / `pi-lock-open` icon mirroring the toggled state). No label or description — wrap it in a horizontal `Field` or a `Field.Label` choice card for labeled layouts, or place it bare where the label already exists outside the control (an ItemGroup row names the field with `Item.Title`). Because the bare form has no wrapper to defer to, the control owns its own `disabled` state.

- Import: `import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it flips (enable a feature, turn a rule on).
- A row that already names the setting outside the control, such as an `item` row whose title is the label.
- A visibility or access toggle: `kind="privacy"` shows a closed lock when off and an open lock when on.

## Do

- The switch renders no text: give it an accessible name with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label.
- Set `disabled` on the switch itself; it renders a native disabled button, so it leaves the tab order and ignores clicks and keys.
- focused` moves real focus and forces the ring; use it only to mirror an external focus state, never as decoration.
- Keep `kind="default"` unless the setting is about visibility or access.

## Don’t

- The toggle needs its own label, description, or helper text in a form → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
- The toggle should sit in a bordered card with a description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
- A text value that only applies while a feature is on → compose a `Field` with an `InputGroup` (`InputGroup.Input` + an `InputGroup.Addon` holding the switch).
- The choice is submitted with a form instead of applied immediately → use `checkbox`.

## Related

- `field` — a horizontal `Field` gives the switch its label and description; a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option.
- `input-group` — a text input with a trailing switch addon that enables it, inside a `Field`.
- `checkbox` — boolean selection submitted with a form.
- `item` — list row whose title names a bare switch.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Toggled-on state. Bind with `v-model="value"`. Mirrors the Figma checked/on variant. |
| `kind` | `'default' \| 'privacy'` | `'default'` | false | Visual variant. `privacy` renders a lock icon inside the handle (closed when off, open when on). |
| `focused` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Forces the focused visual state regardless of keyboard focus. Mirrors the Figma `focused` variant. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies the disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `boolean` | Emitted when the user toggles the switch. Paired with `v-model`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `checked`, `disabled`
- `data-checked` mirrors the `modelValue` prop (toggled-on state)
- `data-focused` mirrors the `focused` prop and applies the same ring tokens as `:focus-visible`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop (`default` | `privacy`)
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop; the root is also natively `<button disabled>`, so it leaves the tab order and neither click nor `Space`/`Enter` emits `update:modelValue`. The disabled treatment is the `--bg-disabled` track + `--text-disabled` handle + `cursor-not-allowed` — token surfaces, never an opacity wash. It wins over the checked tokens, so a disabled switch reads locked in both the off and on positions.
- Hover applies an inset `var(--bg-hover)` overlay on both off and on tracks; disabled suppresses that overlay (`data-[disabled]:hover:shadow-none`) while keeping the element hit-testable so `cursor-not-allowed` is what the pointer shows
- Touch: an invisible `::after` extends the hit area of the 36 × 20 px track to 24 px tall, and to 44 × 44 px on a coarse pointer.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`. The same ring is applied when `focused` is `true` (`data-[focused]` mirror).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Space` / `Enter` toggles. When `disabled`, the native `<button disabled>` root is skipped by `Tab` and both keys are inert.
- ARIA: `role="switch"` on the root; `aria-checked` mirrors `data-checked`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `data-disabled`. The lock icon in `kind="privacy"` is decorative — `aria-hidden="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: the control itself is 36×20 — the consumer is responsible for placing it inside a ≥40×40 hit area (typically a horizontal `Field`, whose label extends the target). The component still exposes a clickable root.
- Forced colors: the track border is `CanvasText` (`Highlight` when checked) and the handle opts out of forced colour adjustment (`forced-color-adjust: none`) to paint `CanvasText`, `Highlight` when checked and `GrayText` when disabled; without it the handle's background is forced to `Canvas` and disappears into the track. Tests: `src/test/forced-colors.test.ts`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const modelValue = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Switch
    v-model="modelValue"
    aria-label="Toggle setting"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/switch.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/switch.md).

# Tag Editor

> Key and value tags of one resource, after Cloudscape's tag editor, built on `AttributeEditor`. It adds what tags need on top of the rows: key and value suggestions while typing, a tag limit (50 by default) that ignores tags marked for removal, the built-in key checks (required when the row has a value, unique, length, allowed characters, no reserved `azion:` prefix), and a removal that only marks a saved tag, with Undo, until the form is saved.

- Import: `import TagEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/tag-editor'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The Tags section of a create or settings form of any resource.
- Labels used for cost allocation, ownership or search, where keys repeat across resources and suggestions help keep them consistent.

## Do

- Mark saved tags with `existing: true`: their key is read-only, and Remove marks them `markedForRemoval` (Undo puts them back) so the save request knows what to delete.
- Call the exposed `validate()` on Save; it also flags empty keys, which are not flagged while typing.
- Feed `keySuggestions` with the keys already used in the account so tags stay consistent.
- Pass server errors per row through `errors`; they replace the built-in message of that cell.
- Keep the default `limit` unless the backend has another one.

## Don’t

- Environment variables, headers or any pairs without tag rules → use `attribute-editor`.
- Showing tags read-only → use `tag` (or `key-value-pairs`).
- Picking from a fixed list of labels → use `multi-select`.

## Related

- `attribute-editor` — the rows, Add, Remove, limit text, focus and announcements underneath.
- `input` — key and value controls; suggestions come from a native `datalist`.
- `tag` — how the saved tags read outside the editor.
- platform/states/form-error` — the rule for server errors passed through `errors`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tags` | `TagEditorTag[]` | `[]` | false | Tags being edited. Saved tags carry `existing`; Remove marks them `markedForRemoval` until Undo. Supports v-model:tags. |
| `keySuggestions` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Keys offered while typing a key, for example the keys already used in the account. |
| `valueSuggestions` | `Record<string, string[]>` | `{}` | false | Values offered per key while typing a value. |
| `limit` | `number` | `50` | false | Most tags allowed; tags marked for removal do not count. |
| `keyMaxLength` | `number` | `128` | false | Longest key allowed, in characters. |
| `valueMaxLength` | `number` | `256` | false | Longest value allowed, in characters. |
| `reservedPrefix` | `string` | `'azion:'` | false | Prefix reserved for the platform; keys may not start with it. Empty allows every prefix. |
| `errors` | `TagEditorErrors` | `[]` | false | Server errors per row, aligned with `tags`; shown in place of the built-in checks. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables every control. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of tags. Empty uses the locale catalog. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:tags` | `TagEditorTag[]` | A tag was added, edited, removed, marked for removal or restored. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `empty`, `at limit` (Add disabled), `invalid` (per cell), `marked for removal` (controls disabled, a muted note, Undo), `disabled`
- Saved tags (`existing`) render the key read-only.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every control keeps its own ring.
- Keyboard map: as `attribute-editor`; suggestions open with the browser's native `datalist` keys (ArrowDown, Enter, Escape).
- ARIA: rows, labels, errors and announcements come from `attribute-editor`; Undo is named "Undo removal of tag n"; a marked tag keeps a visible note ("This tag will be removed when you save.").
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 from the semantic text tokens.
- Touch target: Remove and Undo are 32 px buttons (`medium`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: inherited from `attribute-editor` (logical utilities only).
- Icons: the trash glyph is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: no arrow-key handling of its own.
- User data: keys and values keep the direction of their own text.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source                                         | Override prop                    |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `tagEditor.label`            | Tags                                                   | `ariaLabel`                      |
| `tagEditor.key` / `value`    | Key / Value                                            | —                                |
| `tagEditor.keyPlaceholder`   | Enter key                                              | —                                |
| `tagEditor.valuePlaceholder` | Enter value                                            | —                                |
| `tagEditor.add`              | Add new tag                                            | —                                |
| `tagEditor.remove`           | Remove tag                                             | —                                |
| `tagEditor.undo`             | Undo                                                   | —                                |
| `tagEditor.undoLabel`        | Undo removal of tag {index}                            | —                                |
| `tagEditor.markedForRemoval` | This tag will be removed when you save.                | —                                |
| `tagEditor.empty`            | No tags associated with the resource.                  | —                                |
| `tagEditor.remaining`        | You can add {count} more tag(s) (plural)               | —                                |
| `tagEditor.limitReached`     | You have reached the limit of {limit} tags.            | —                                |
| `tagEditor.keyRequired`      | Enter a key.                                           | —                                |
| `tagEditor.keyDuplicate`     | This key is already used by another tag.               | —                                |
| `tagEditor.keyReserved`      | Keys cannot start with "{prefix}".                     | `reservedPrefix`                 |
| `tagEditor.keyInvalid`       | Use letters, numbers, spaces and + - = . _ : / @ only. | —                                |
| `tagEditor.tooLong`          | Use {max} characters or fewer.                         | `keyMaxLength`, `valueMaxLength` |

- Formatting: the tags left go through the plural rules of the active locale. Allowed key characters include letters of every script (`\p{L}`).

## Responsive

- Container queries: inherited from `attribute-editor` (cells side by side from `@md`, stacked below).
- Narrow (≤ 640 px or a narrow container): stacked key and value with their own labels.
- Touch: nothing depends on hover.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px and 200 % zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import TagEditor from '@aziontech/webkit/tag-editor'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const tags = ref([
    { key: 'team', value: 'payments', existing: true },
    { key: 'cost-center', value: 'cc-1042', existing: true },
    { key: 'environment', value: 'staging' }
  ])

  const keySuggestions = ['team', 'cost-center', 'environment', 'owner', 'project']
  const valueSuggestions = { environment: ['production', 'staging', 'preview'] }
</script>

<template>
  <TagEditor
    v-model:tags="tags"
    :key-suggestions="keySuggestions"
    :value-suggestions="valueSuggestions"
    aria-label="Resource tags"
  />
</template>
```

# Textarea

> Collects multi-line free-form text from the user. Sibling of `input` in the `inputs` category; renders a fixed-size (`large`) multi-line field with a minimum height of 80px. The resize axis is controlled by the `resizable` prop (defaults to `vertical`). Native textarea attributes (`rows`, `maxlength`, `name`, etc.) flow through via attribute fallthrough.

- Import: `import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Capture multiple lines of free-form text (descriptions, comments, messages).

## Do

- Give it a sensible default size; avoid auto-growing beyond the viewport.
- Wrap it in a `Field` for the label, description and error.
- Set `monospace` on a value that is code: a pasted zone file, a certificate, a JSON or YAML snippet, a list of IPs. Pair it with `:spellcheck="false"`. Prose (a description, a message) stays in the sans face.
- A value people edit as code with highlighting and line numbers belongs in `CodeEditor`; `monospace` is for a plain paste box.
- Do not restyle a read-only textarea (dashed border, transparent fill): it is the same filled field, made non-editable; the reason belongs in the field's description.

## Don’t

- The value is a single line → use `input`.
- The value is strictly numeric → use `number-input`.

## Related

- `input` — single-line sibling with the same field API.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | false | Bound value (v-model). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder shown when the field is empty. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field read-only: the value is visible, focusable and copyable but not editable. Keeps the filled field (surface and solid border) with no hover border and a default cursor (`data-readonly`), the same look as `Input`; distinct from the disabled field. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Applies invalid styling and sets `aria-invalid`. Combined with `required`, switches to warning border tone. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the field as required and sets `aria-required`. |
| `resizable` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both' \| 'none'` | `'vertical'` | false | Which axes the user can drag to resize the field. `none` locks the size; `vertical` keeps the default behavior. |
| `monospace` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Sets the value and placeholder in the monospace code face (`.text-body-code-sm`, which wraps) for pasted zone files, certificates, JSON and lists of IPs (`data-monospace`). Same prop as on `Input`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `string` | v-model update. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `filled`, `disabled`, `required` (warning border), `invalid` (danger border), `readonly`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-invalid` mirrors the `invalid` prop
- `data-required` mirrors the `required` prop
- `data-readonly` mirrors the `readonly` prop: a read-only textarea keeps the editable field's fill (`var(--bg-surface)`) and solid `var(--border-default)` border, as `Input` does and the design sample draws it; it only drops the hover border and takes a default cursor. The value keeps `var(--text-default)` and the textarea stays focusable. Why the value cannot change is said by the field's description, not by a different chrome.
- `data-monospace` mirrors the `monospace` prop: the value and the placeholder render in `.text-body-code-sm` instead of `.text-body-xs`.
- `data-filled` mirrors whether `modelValue` is non-empty
- `data-resize` on the native `<textarea>` mirrors the `resizable` prop and drives the `resize-*` Tailwind variant

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on `:focus`, a `ring-2` shadow in `var(--ring-color)` plus a `ring-offset-2` in `var(--bg-canvas)` render around the field; the color transition respects `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; typing inserts text; `Enter` inserts a newline; `Shift+Tab` moves focus to the previous element.
- Direction: the `<textarea>` renders `dir="auto"` so a value typed in another script keeps its own direction inside right-to-left UI; a `dir` attribute overrides it.
- ARIA: root is a native `<textarea>`; `aria-invalid` mirrors `invalid`; `aria-required` mirrors `required`; `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled` when applicable.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (border + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated state transitions.
- Touch target: field min-height ≥80px ensures adequate hit area.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: the `<textarea>` renders `dir="auto"`; a `dir` attribute overrides it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const value = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <Textarea
    v-model="value"
    placeholder="Write your message"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/textarea.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/textarea.md).

<!-- components/theme-switcher.md -->

# Theme Switcher

> A compact pill-shaped segmented control that lets the user pick the app color-theme mode — `system`, `dark`, or `light` — via three icon-only segments. It reflects and emits the selected mode through `v-model` and applies no global side effect itself (the app decides what each mode means). Unlike `switch` (a boolean toggle) or `tabs` (view navigation), it is a fixed three-way single-select over the theme modes.

- Import: `import ThemeSwitcher from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'`
- Category: inputs · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The app-wide color mode picker in a header, footer, account menu or settings page.

## Do

- Bind with `v-model` and apply the mode in the app (for example a `data-theme` attribute, resolving `system` from `prefers-color-scheme`); the component has no side effects.
- Persist the chosen mode on the app side so it survives a reload.
- Localize `ariaLabel`; the segment names (System, Dark, Light) are fixed in the component.

## Don’t

- A general on/off preference → use `switch`.
- Picking one of other mutually exclusive options → use `toggle-group`.
- Moving between views or panels → use `tabs`.

## Related

- `toggle-group` — the generic mutually exclusive option group, with labels and sizes.
- `switch` — boolean toggle for a single setting.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the whole control and applies disabled tokens. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the icon-only segmented group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Theme`). |
| `modelValue` | `ThemeSwitcherValue` | `'system'` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model     | Type                            | Default    | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model` | `'system' \| 'dark' \| 'light'` | `'system'` | `update:modelValue` | Selected theme mode via `defineModel`. Emits when the user selects a different mode; the component applies no side effect itself. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on the root
- Selected segment carries `aria-checked="true"` and `data-state="active"`; unselected segments `aria-checked="false"` and `data-state="inactive"`
- A single `aria-hidden` indicator element renders the selection highlight (`var(--bg-selected)`) and slides to the active segment (position measured from the active segment's box); segments themselves stay transparent

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the focused segment.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves focus into the group (roving tabindex lands on the selected segment); `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` (and `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`) move selection between segments; `Space`/`Enter` selects the focused segment.
- ARIA: root is `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel`; each segment is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked` and its own `aria-label` (`System` / `Dark` / `Light`); the glyph is `aria-hidden`. `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled`.
- Each segment is wrapped in `@aziontech/webkit/tooltip` (`placement="bottom"`) surfacing its mode label (`System` / `Dark` / `Light`) on hover and keyboard focus; the tooltip owns its own `aria-describedby` wiring.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target: segments follow the compact Figma sizing (28px pill height, 28×20px segments) and are below the 40×40 px target; justified deviation for a dense global control, consistent with the design.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the sun, moon and monitor glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move to the next/previous theme, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- Indicator: the selection pill is anchored with a physical `left: 0` and moved by the measured offset, so it lands on the selected option in both directions.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ThemeSwitcher from '@aziontech/webkit/theme-switcher'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const theme = ref('system')
</script>

<template>
  <ThemeSwitcher v-model="theme" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/theme-switcher.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/theme-switcher.md).

<!-- components/app-layout.md -->

# App Layout

> The frame every signed-in product page renders inside. It places named regions — navigation, header, notifications, breadcrumbs, content, tools (the help panel) and the split panel — and owns how they open, close, resize and remember their state. It responds to its **own** width, not the viewport's: below `compactBelow` pixels the navigation and the tools turn into drawers and the split panel moves to the bottom. The regions are slots, so the shell (the `shells/console` block) keeps its own `Sidebar`, `GlobalHeader` and page content and only hands the frame to `AppLayout`.

- Import: `import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A product shell needs a navigation rail, a global header and a scrolling content area that turn into a drawer-based layout on phones.
- A page offers contextual help beside the work (`HelpPanel` in the tools region) that the reader opens and closes.
- A list or table needs a resizable detail panel under it or beside it (the split panel), showing the selected item without leaving the page.
- Page-level flash messages (`Alert`) must sit above the content and stay visible while the content scrolls.

## Do

- One `AppLayout` per page, at the root. Do not nest them.
- Keep the navigation in the `navigation` slot and read its `drawer` scope flag to drop rail-only controls (resize, collapse) when it renders inside the drawer; call `closeNavigation` from the scope when an item is chosen in the drawer.
- Put the control that opens the navigation drawer in the header, and show it only when the header scope's `compact` is true.
- Put a help button in the header that calls `toggleTools`; the tools region carries its own close button.
- Use the split panel for the selected item of a collection. Close it when the selection clears.
- Pass `storageKey` when the reader's choices (split panel size and position, navigation and tools open) should survive a reload.
- Flash notifications belong in the `notifications` slot, one `Alert` per message, dismissible. Use toasts for results of actions that finish in the background.
- A page body that fills the screen (an empty state, a centred form) is `<main class="flex min-h-full flex-col">` in the default slot. Its height is what is left under the breadcrumbs, so it never scrolls by the breadcrumb row; do not subtract the breadcrumbs yourself.

## Don’t

- A single resizable split inside a page, with no shell around it → use `resizable`.
- A navigation rail on its own (resize, collapse, footer) → use `sidebar`; put it in the `navigation` slot.
- A one-off overlay for a task (a create form, a detail preview) → use `drawer`.
- Marketing and documentation pages → use the `shells/website` and `shells/documentation` blocks.

## Related

- `sidebar` — the navigation rail that goes in the `navigation` slot; it owns its own width, resize and collapse.
- `global-header` — the bar that goes in the `header` slot.
- `help-panel` — the content of the tools region.
- `drawer` — what the navigation and tools regions become below `compactBelow`.
- `resizable` — a split between panes inside a page, without the shell.
- `alert` — the flash messages composed into the `notifications` slot.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigationOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Whether the navigation region shows beside the content. Use with `v-model:navigation-open`. Not used while compact. |
| `navigationLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the navigation drawer. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Navigation`). |
| `toolsOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the tools region (help) is open; while compact it drives the tools drawer. Use with `v-model:tools-open`. |
| `toolsLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the tools region, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Help`). |
| `toolsWidth` | `number` | `320` | false | Width of the tools region in pixels while not compact. |
| `splitPanelOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Whether the split panel is open. Use with `v-model:split-panel-open`. |
| `splitPanelPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'side'` | `'bottom'` | false | Where the split panel sits: under the content or beside it. Use with `v-model:split-panel-position`. Bottom while compact. |
| `splitPanelSize` | `number` | `320` | false | Height (bottom) or width (side) of the split panel in pixels. Use with `v-model:split-panel-size`. |
| `splitPanelTitle` | `string` | `''` | false | Title of the split panel, shown in its header. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Details`). |
| `storageKey` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the split panel size and position and the navigation and tools open state are kept in `localStorage` under it. |
| `compactBelow` | `number` | `768` | false | Width of the layout itself, in pixels, under which navigation and tools become drawers and the split panel moves down. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:navigationOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:navigation-open. |
| `update:toolsOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:tools-open. |
| `update:splitPanelOpen` | `boolean` | v-model:split-panel-open. |
| `update:splitPanelPosition` | `'bottom' \| 'side'` | v-model:split-panel-position. |
| `update:splitPanelSize` | `number` | v-model:split-panel-size; on every step. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page content (the consumer's `<main>`). Fills the content region under the breadcrumbs, so a full-height body (`min-h-full`) takes the rest of the height without overflowing; taller content scrolls. |
| `navigation` | { drawer: boolean, closeNavigation: () => void } | The navigation rail. Rendered once: beside the content, or inside the navigation drawer when compact. `closeNavigation` closes the drawer, e.g. after an item is chosen. |
| `header` | { compact: boolean, openNavigation: () => void, toggleNavigation: () => void, toggleTools: () => void } | The global header, above content, tools and split panel. |
| `notifications` | — | Flash messages (`Alert`) above the breadcrumbs and the content; stays in place while content scrolls. |
| `breadcrumbs` | — | Breadcrumbs above the content, inside the scroll area; the page body fills the height left under them. |
| `tools` | — | The tools region's body, usually a `HelpPanel`. |
| `split-panel` | — | The split panel's body. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `compact`; per region `open` / `closed`; the split separator `focus-visible` and `resizing`.
- `data-compact` on the root while the layout is narrower than `compactBelow`.
- `data-navigation`, `data-tools`, `data-split-panel` on the root: `open` | `closed`.
- `data-split-panel-position` on the root: `bottom` | `side` (always `bottom` while compact).
- `data-resizing` on the split separator while it is dragged.
- First render (server and client) is the wide layout; the compact layout applies after mount, once the layout has measured itself.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the separator shows `var(--accent)` on `focus-visible`; the region buttons are `IconButton` with their own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region controls in DOM order (navigation, header, content, split panel, tools). On the split separator: `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` grow and shrink a bottom panel; `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` grow and shrink a side panel (mirrored under RTL); `Shift` makes the step 64 px instead of 16 px; `Home` / `End` go to the minimum / maximum. `Escape` closes a compact drawer (from `Drawer`) and returns focus to the control that opened it. The split panel and tools bodies are focusable scroll regions (`tabindex="0"`, `role="group"` named by their heading), so a keyboard reader can scroll them when they hold no control.
- ARIA: the tools region and the split panel are `<section aria-labelledby>` their header title (`<h2>`); the separator is `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` in pixels, `aria-controls` the split panel and an accessible name from the catalog. The compact drawers are named by `navigationLabel` and `toolsLabel`. The layout adds no landmark of its own around the content; the consumer's `<main>` and `Sidebar` `<nav>` are the landmarks.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the region titles; ≥3:1 for the separator against the surfaces.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the separator transition.
- Touch target: the separator's hit area is 16 px across (a `before:` pseudo-element) over a 4 px line; region buttons are 32 px `IconButton` (40 px on `pointer: coarse` from `IconButton`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`border-s`, `border-e`, `ms-auto`); the navigation sits at the inline start and the tools and side split panel at the inline end.
- Icons: the position toggle icons (`pi pi-window-maximize` family) are not mirrored; close is not mirrored.
- Keyboard: on a side split panel, the arrow that points away from the panel grows it — `ArrowLeft` in LTR, `ArrowRight` in RTL.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source          | Override prop     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------- |
| `appLayout.navigation`       | Navigation              | `navigationLabel` |
| `appLayout.tools`            | Help                    | `toolsLabel`      |
| `appLayout.closeTools`       | Close help              | —                 |
| `appLayout.splitPanel`       | Details                 | `splitPanelTitle` |
| `appLayout.closeSplitPanel`  | Close panel             | —                 |
| `appLayout.resizeSplitPanel` | Resize panel            | —                 |
| `appLayout.showAtSide`       | Show beside the content | —                 |
| `appLayout.showAtBottom`     | Show under the content  | —                 |

- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: the root is `@container/app-layout`; a `ResizeObserver` on the root switches to compact when its own width is under `compactBelow` (768 px by default), so the layout also goes compact inside a narrow host, not only on a narrow viewport.
- Narrow (compact): navigation renders in a `Drawer` from the inline end (the design sample's phone menu), the tools in a `Drawer`, the split panel is forced to the bottom and its position toggle hides; the split panel's maximum is 70 % of the layout height.
- Touch: region buttons are `IconButton`; the separator has a 16 px hit area and pointer drag works with touch (pointer events).
- Reflow: the content scrolls on its own; no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>

  import AppLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/app-layout'
  import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'
```
