<!-- components/setting-row.md -->

# Setting Row

> One setting inside a flush `Card`: an `Item` whose content carries the title and description, with the control placed by what it needs. A typed or picked field sits in a right cell capped at the 3xs container so every field on the card ends at the same edge (`field`); a switch or a button sits hard right at its natural width (`compact`); a textarea, list, radio group or editor drops under the copy at the full measure (`stacked`). A child setting indents one or two levels under a rule (`level`). The copy top-aligns with the control, and the row keeps its two columns at every width (the description clamps to two lines); `stackable` opts a row into moving a `field` control under the copy in a narrow box.

- Import: `import SettingRow from '@aziontech/webkit/setting-row'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every row of a settings card: account settings, build settings, create pages, resource settings.
- A field with a validation message under it (put the `HelperText` in the default slot after the control).

## Do

- The title is the label: give the control the same text as `aria-label`.
- Pick `kind` by the control: `field` for Input and Select, `compact` for Switch and Button, `stacked` for Textarea, radio groups and editors.
- Show a validation message only after Save was pressed.
- Use `level` only for a setting that applies when the row above it is on, and render it with `v-if` on that state.
- Keep the default two columns on a phone: the title and the clamped description sit on the start side, the control on the end side, both aligned to the top. This is the console layout at every width.
- Set `stackable` only when the field needs the full measure to be usable in a narrow box (a long URL or a code value in a side drawer); never to fix a centred or cramped look.
- Let a tall control (an input group of three nameservers, a textarea) sit beside the copy: the title stays at the top of the row.
- Do not wrap the row or its copy in your own flex box to change the alignment or to stack it; use `kind` and `stackable`.
- Do not set `stackable` on a `compact` row: a switch or a button always stays at the end side.

## Don’t

- A stand-alone form field with a visible label above it → use `field-text` and the other `field-*` components.
- A read-only list of label and value pairs → use `key-value-pairs`.
- A navigable list row → use `item` directly.

## Related

- `settings-section` — the band the card of rows sits in.
- `item` — the row primitive it renders; place rows in an `Item.List` inside the card.
- `helper-text` — the required or invalid message under the control.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The setting name; the control takes the same text as its aria-label. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence under the title that says what the setting does. |
| `kind` | `'field' \| 'compact' \| 'stacked'` | `'field'` | false | Where the control sits relative to the copy. |
| `level` | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | `0` | false | Indent depth under a rule, for a setting that only applies when its parent is on. |
| `stackable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Below the md container of the row, move a field control under the copy at full width. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The control, plus the HelperText message under it when there is one. |
| `title` | — | Rich title content (a Tag, a Hint); replaces the `title` prop. |
| `description` | — | Rich description content (links, inline code); replaces the `description` prop. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-row-kind` mirrors `kind` and `data-level` mirrors `level` on the root; `data-stackable` is set when `stackable` is on
- Alignment: the copy and the control align to the top of the row, so a title stays level with the first line of a tall control.
- Responsive: the row is the `@container/setting-row`. By default the row keeps its two columns at every width: the copy shrinks (the description clamps to two lines with an ellipsis) and a `field` control keeps the end cell, capped at the 3xs container. With `stackable`, below `@md` of the row a `field` control moves under the copy at full width.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the control in the default slot.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the control; the row is not interactive.
- ARIA: the row is an `Item` (a `listitem` inside `Item.List`); the control carries `aria-label` equal to the title, and a message is linked with `aria-describedby`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title and the muted description.

## Examples

### SettingsCard

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
  import Input from '@aziontech/webkit/input'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
  import SettingRow from '@aziontech/webkit/setting-row'
  import Textarea from '@aziontech/webkit/textarea'
  import { reactive } from 'vue'

  const form = reactive({ companyName: '', taxId: '', billingEmails: '' })
</script>

<template>
  <Card :padded="false">
    <template #content>
      <Item.List>
        <SettingRow
          title="Company Name"
          description="The legal entity that owns this account."
        >
          <Input
            v-model="form.companyName"
            size="large"
            class="w-full"
            aria-label="Company Name"
          />
        </SettingRow>
        <SettingRow
          title="Tax ID"
          description="The tax identification number of the entity that owns this account."
        >
          <Input
            v-model="form.taxId"
            size="large"
            class="w-full"
            aria-label="Tax ID"
          />
        </SettingRow>
        <SettingRow
          title="Billing emails"
          description="Billing is forwarded to every address listed here. Separate each one with a semicolon ( ; )."
          kind="stacked"
        >
          <Textarea
            v-model="form.billingEmails"
            class="w-full"
            :rows="3"
            aria-label="Billing emails"
          />
        </SettingRow>
      </Item.List>
    </template>
  </Card>
</template>
```

<!-- components/settings-section.md -->

# Settings Section

> A band of a settings page: an h2 with a `Hint` glyph that carries the one-sentence guidance, over the band body (usually a flush `Card` of `SettingRow` rows). Bands stack at the section gap with no rule between them. An anchored band shows a copy-link button in the gutter when the heading is hovered or focused; a collapsible band turns the heading into a disclosure that unfolds the body along the grid track.

- Import: `import SettingsSection from '@aziontech/webkit/settings-section'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every settings page and create page: a resource's Settings tab, Account Settings, a create form, a create drawer.
- An Advanced band that starts closed (`collapsible`).

## Do

- One sentence of guidance in `hint`; the title names the band in one or two words.
- Set `anchor` on bands people link to.
- Use `collapsible` only for an Advanced band whose defaults are right for most people; it starts closed.
- Stack the bands inside one form column (`layout-column-form`); the first band takes no top margin.

## Don’t

- A band whose heading carries a description line and actions → use `section-header`.
- The page title → use `page-header`.
- A disclosure list of several independent panels → use `accordion`.

## Related

- `setting-row` — the rows inside the band's card.
- `card` — the flush (`:padded="false"`) surface the rows sit on.
- `hint` — the guidance glyph beside the title.
- `section-header` — the band heading with a description and actions.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The band title, rendered as an h2. |
| `hint` | `string` | `''` | false | One-sentence guidance shown in a Hint glyph beside the title. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | Id of the h2 that a hash link targets; when set, a copy-link button appears in the gutter on hover or focus. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Turns the title into a disclosure that folds the band body. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Glyph shown before the title of a collapsible band (e.g. `pi pi-cog`). |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The band body, usually a flush Card of SettingRow rows. |
| `title` | — | Rich title content; replaces the `title` prop text in the h2. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether a collapsible band is unfolded; it updates when the disclosure toggles. Ignored unless `collapsible`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` / `focus-within` (reveals the copy-link button)
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed` when `collapsible`
- `data-open` on the body mirrors whether it is unfolded
- Responsive: the body is the `@container/settings-section`, so rows and fields inside lay out for the section, not the window.
- Hover-free devices: the copy-link button is shown inline after the title where the pointer cannot hover (`@media (hover: none)`), instead of floating outside the start edge on hover.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the copy-link and the disclosure button (plus `ring-offset` on the disclosure).
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the copy-link, the disclosure and then the body; `Enter`/`Space` toggles the disclosure.
- ARIA: the disclosure is a `button` inside the h2 with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the body (`useId`); a folded body is `inert` and `aria-hidden`. The copy-link button is named "Copy link to the {title} section"; after a successful copy its glyph turns into a check and its name into "Link copied" for two seconds, then both return.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for the title.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Card from '@aziontech/webkit/card'
  import Item from '@aziontech/webkit/item'
  import Select from '@aziontech/webkit/select'
  import SettingRow from '@aziontech/webkit/setting-row'
  import SettingsSection from '@aziontech/webkit/settings-section'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const fonts = [
    { label: 'Rubik (Default)', value: 'rubik' },
    { label: 'Inter', value: 'inter' },
    { label: 'IBM Plex Sans', value: 'ibm-plex-sans' },
    { label: 'Geist', value: 'geist' }
  ]

  const appearances = [
    { label: 'System', value: 'system' },
    { label: 'Light', value: 'light' },
    { label: 'Dark', value: 'dark' }
  ]

  const font = ref('rubik')
  const theme = ref('system')

  const labelFor = (options) => (value) =>
    options.find((option) => option.value === value)?.label ?? ''
</script>

<template>
  <div class="layout-column-form flex min-w-0 flex-col">
    <SettingsSection
      title="Appearance"
      hint="Preferences for this browser, applied the moment you change them and not part of Save."
      anchor="appearance"
    >
      <Card :padded="false">
        <template #content>
          <Item.List>
            <SettingRow
              title="Font family"
              description="The primary sans typeface across the interface."
            >
              <Select
                v-model="font"
                size="large"
                :display-value="labelFor(fonts)"
              >
                <Select.Trigger
                  class="w-full"
                  aria-label="Font family"
                />
                <Select.Content>
                  <Select.Option
                    v-for="option in fonts"
                    :key="option.value"
                    :value="option.value"
                  >
                    {{ option.label }}
                  </Select.Option>
                </Select.Content>
              </Select>
            </SettingRow>
            <SettingRow
              title="System appearance"
              description="Follow the operating system, or force a light or dark theme."
            >
              <Select
                v-model="theme"
                size="large"
                :display-value="labelFor(appearances)"
              >
                <Select.Trigger
                  class="w-full"
                  aria-label="System appearance"
                />
                <Select.Content>
                  <Select.Option
                    v-for="option in appearances"
                    :key="option.value"
                    :value="option.value"
                  >
                    {{ option.label }}
                  </Select.Option>
                </Select.Content>
              </Select>
            </SettingRow>
          </Item.List>
        </template>
      </Card>
    </SettingsSection>
  </div>
</template>
```

<!-- components/sidebar.md -->

# Sidebar

> Helps users move between views or sections. Composable application sidebar with optional header and footer regions; navigation content scrolls inside a built-in `ScrollArea`. It also owns **the rail gesture** — sizing the sidebar by dragging its trailing edge, and collapsing it out of the layout entirely. That belongs here rather than in each shell: the interaction is not a small one (a pointer drag that crosses the collapse boundary continuously, a keyboard equivalent, token-derived bounds, a phase-aware transition, and an affordance that brings a collapsed rail back), and every app that has a sidebar wants the same one. Two shells re-implementing it is how the two drift apart. Both halves are **opt-in and independent**: `resizable` adds the drag, `collapsible` adds the collapse trigger and the edge affordance. With neither set the component renders exactly as it always has, with the host owning the width — every existing consumer is unaffected.

- Import: `import Sidebar from '@aziontech/webkit/sidebar'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- The persistent navigation column of an app shell, with an optional header (brand, workspace switcher) and footer (profile, settings) around a scrolling `Menu`.
- The user should be able to resize the rail by dragging its trailing edge (`resizable`) or take it out of the layout and bring it back (`collapsible`).
- The rail's size or collapsed state must survive navigation or reloads — bind `v-model:width` and `v-model:collapsed` and persist them in the app.

## Do

- Put a `Menu` with `role="presentation"` in the default slot; the sidebar already renders the `nav` landmark and its `aria-label` (default `'Sidebar'`) names the region.
- Use `Menu.Group` for new navigation — `SidebarGroup` still works but is superseded.
- Without `resizable` or `collapsible`, size the rail with a width class on the root; with either set, the sidebar owns the width and clamps it between `min-width-token` and `max-width-token`.
- When the sidebar is revealed after mount (for example leaving a mobile layout where it was hidden), call the exposed `measure()` so the rail does not keep a zero width.
- Keep the profile block in the `footer` slot; with `collapsible`, the collapse trigger renders in the same footer row.

## Don’t

- Adjacent work areas the reader resizes (editor beside a preview, a terminal under it) → use `resizable`.
- Horizontal top-level navigation with dropdown panels → use `navigation-menu`.
- A temporary panel that slides over the page → use `drawer`.

## Related

- `menu` — the navigation rows, groups and drill levels that go in the sidebar's default slot.
- `resizable` — draggable splits between content regions; the sidebar's rail gesture is for navigation only.
- `global-header` — the top bar that usually sits above the sidebar in an app shell.
- platform-shell` — the console layout template that composes the header, the sidebar and the page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Sidebar`). |
| `resizable` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds the drag handle on the trailing edge; dragging past the minimum collapses the rail. |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Adds the collapse trigger at the bottom of the rail and the edge affordance that brings a collapsed rail back. |
| `minWidthToken` | `string` | `'--container-3xs'` | false | Theme container token the sized width is clamped up to, read off the document at runtime. |
| `maxWidthToken` | `string` | `'--container-sm'` | false | Theme container token the sized width is clamped down to, read off the document at runtime. |
| `collapseAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the collapse trigger. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Collapse sidebar`). |
| `expandAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the control and the grab bar that bring a collapsed rail back. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Expand sidebar`). |
| `resizeAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the drag handle separator. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Resize sidebar`). |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:collapsed`). |
| `width` | `number \| null` | `null` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:width`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:collapsed` | `boolean` | v-model:collapsed` — the rail entered or left the layout, by the trigger, the drag crossing the snap boundary, the keyboard nudge, or a double-click on the handle. |
| `update:width` | `number` | v-model:width` — the sized width in px, already clamped to the token bounds. Emitted continuously during a drag. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |
| `header` | — | Named slot. |
| `footer` | — | Named slot. The collapse trigger renders after this content in the same row, under one full-width separator, so a profile block and the trigger read as one footer. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/sidebar-footer`

## Sub-components

- `sidebar-footer.vue` — Public sub-component `sidebar-footer`.
- `sidebar-group.vue` — Public sub-component `sidebar-group`.
  optional title, **superseded by `Menu.Group`**: the docs, the stories and every example here
  compose `Menu`, which does everything this does and also nests, collapses and drills. It keeps
  working untouched for existing consumers and is **not** deprecated (no `@deprecated` tag, because
  `webkit/no-deprecated-component` is `error` in the recommended config and would turn a consumer's
  lint green→red on a minor). Reach for `Menu` in anything new.
- `sidebar-header.vue` — Public sub-component `sidebar-header`.

`Sidebar` does not import `Menu` and `Menu` does not import `Sidebar`; the only thing that passes
between them is the ring-offset surface below.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-collapsed` on the root while the rail is out of the layout
- `data-resizing` on the root and on the handle while a pointer drag is in flight
- `data-preview` on the collapsed edge zone while it is showing the rail's preview sliver
- `data-collapsed` / `data-resizing` / `data-preview` are **reported state, not the motion
  driver**: the collapse/expand animation itself runs off the hidden checkbox's `:checked` (see
  Motion & Animations), so these attributes exist for consumer styling hooks and for tests, not
  because the component's own CSS depends on them for that transition.
- `data-hydrated` on the root once Vue has mounted — internal only (switches the native
  `resize: horizontal` pre-hydration fallback back off in favor of the JS-driven handle); not a
  documented consumer styling hook.
- `data-settled` on the root and on the panel two frames after mount — internal only (gates the
  rail's motion off until then, so a state restored at mount lands in place; see Motion &
  Animations); not a documented consumer styling hook.
- Region testids derived from the root: `__panel` (the fixed-width inner panel),
  `__collapse-input` (the hidden checkbox that carries `collapsed` for CSS — not an interactive
  control; see Accessibility), `__header`, `__nav`, `__scroll`, `__footer`, `__collapse` (the
  trigger), `__handle` (the drag separator), `__expand` / `__expand-button` (the collapsed
  affordance)
- A collapsed rail carries `inert` + `aria-hidden`, so it holds no tab stops while it is out

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
  The **scroll viewport is not a tab stop** (`tabindex="-1"` on the built-in `ScrollArea`): a scroll
  region needs one only when nothing inside it is focusable, and this one holds a `Menu` of rows —
  so `Tab` reaches the first row directly instead of the box around it.
  The region also keeps `var(--spacing-xxs)` of padding — and the same as `scroll-padding` — inside
  the clip, because the first row's focus ring (`ring-2` over `ring-offset-2`) reaches 4 px past the
  row and a viewport flush against it would cut the ring off.
  The **drag handle is a focusable `role="separator"`**, so the gesture has a keyboard equivalent:
  `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` nudge the width, `ArrowLeft` past the snap boundary collapses, and
  `ArrowRight` from the collapsed splitter brings the rail back. Pointer-wise that same collapsed
  splitter is click-to-restore as well as drag-to-size, so the edge is never a drag-only control.
  Right-to-left: the rail sits on the inline start, so in an `rtl` subtree the keys and the drag
  mirror (`ArrowLeft` and a leftward drag widen it, `ArrowRight` narrows it), the expand affordance
  slides in from the right, and its tooltip opens on the left.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component. Each
  separator is named (`resizeAriaLabel` / `expandAriaLabel`) because a bare separator announces
  nothing about what it sizes; the collapse trigger is named by `collapseAriaLabel`.
- A focusable `role="separator"` is a **window splitter**, so both separators report their position:
  `aria-valuenow` (the sized width in px, `0` while collapsed), `aria-valuemin="0"` and
  `aria-valuemax` (the resolved `maxWidthToken`). `aria-valuemin` is `0` rather than the minimum
  width token because collapsed is a real position of this splitter — the rail never rests between
  1 px and the minimum, and reporting the token bound would put the collapsed position outside the
  range the control announces. Without these, `axe` reports `aria-required-attr` and a screen reader
  announces a separator carrying no information at all.
- A **collapsed rail carries `inert` and `aria-hidden`** — the content is still mounted so its width
  can animate, and it must not be reachable while it is out of the layout. That is why the control
  that brings it back is a sibling of the rail rather than inside it.
- The **hidden checkbox that mirrors `collapsed`** (`__collapse-input`) carries `aria-hidden="true"`
  and `tabindex="-1"`: it is a CSS state carrier, not a second control, so it is never reachable by
  keyboard or announced by a screen reader. The trigger's accessible name and role are unaffected —
  the consumer-facing control is still the `IconButton`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states; the width /
  transform / opacity transition is dropped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive. The drag handle is a **justified
  deviation**: it is a `var(--spacing-xs)`-wide edge strip, which is the target a pointer resize
  wants, and it is not the only route — the trigger, the keyboard nudge, and double-click all reach
  the same state, so no capability depends on hitting it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Avatar from '@aziontech/webkit/avatar'
  import CommandEmpty from '@aziontech/webkit/command-empty'
  import CommandGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/command-group'
  import CommandInput from '@aziontech/webkit/command-input'
  import CommandItem from '@aziontech/webkit/command-item'
  import CommandList from '@aziontech/webkit/command-list'
```

<!-- components/site-layout.md -->

# Site Layout

> The marketing site's chrome, composed once in the app: `SiteNav` on top, the page's sections in the layout's `<main>`, `SiteFooter` at the foot, and the `Command` search palette wired to the bar's search button and to ⌘K / Ctrl K. The navigation and the footer are data (the `SiteNav` and `SiteFooter` props), the canvas is painted with the theme tokens so a dark site never shows an unpainted page below the fold, and the palette lists every destination of the navigation by default. Site pages are only their sections, rendered through the default slot; they never repeat the bar or the footer.

- Import: `import SiteLayout from '@aziontech/webkit/site-layout'`
- Category: layout · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Every public marketing page (home, product, solution, company, legal): put one `SiteLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page's sections as its default slot.
- A site that needs the Azion navigation, footer and search palette without hand-composing `GlobalHeader`, `NavigationMenu`, `Footer`, `SearchTrigger` and `Command`.

## Do

- Compose the layout once, in the app's root; each route renders only its sections. Never add `SiteNav`, `SiteFooter`, `GlobalHeader` or `Footer` to a page.
- The site is dark: set `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` (in `index.html`), so the layout, the teleported menus and the palette all resolve the dark tokens.
- Bind the real navigation and footer data once (`navigation`, `footer`); give every navigation item an `href` so it also appears in the search palette.
- Add extra palette groups (articles, docs results) in the `search` slot; listen to `search-select` for them.
- The page renders no `<main>` of its own: the layout owns the landmark.

## Don’t

- The signed-in console → `ConsoleLayout`. Documentation → `DocLayout`.
- A one-off landing page with no site navigation (a campaign form) → render the sections on their own.

## Related

- SiteNav` — the bar and its mega-menus; `navigation` is bound onto it.
- SiteFooter` — the footer; `footer` is bound onto it (`kind="site"` closes a framed page).
- SectionContainer`, `SectionGap` — the frame the page's sections stack in, inside the slot.
- Command` — the search palette the bar's search button opens.
- shells/website` — the block that shows this layout with the azion.com navigation and footer.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigation` | `SiteLayoutNavigation` | `—` | true | The bar, bound onto `SiteNav`: `{ menus, home?, links?, contact?, primaryAction?, secondaryAction?, secondaryActionOnPhones? }`. |
| `footer` | `SiteLayoutFooter` | `undefined` | false | The footer, bound onto `SiteFooter`: `{ kind?, home?, columns?, socials?, statusLabel?, languages? }`; `kind` defaults to `site`. No footer when absent. |
| `searchPlaceholder` | `string` | `''` | false | Placeholder of the palette's input. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Search the site`). |
| `searchOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:searchOpen`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, page: SiteLayoutPage)` | Fired when a navigation destination is chosen in the palette (`{ label, href }`); the layout then follows it (with the app's router for an in-site path). Event first. |
| `search-select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fired when a palette item from the `search` slot is chosen. Event first. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The page's sections, rendered inside the layout's `<main>`. |
| `search` | { query: string } | Extra `Command.Group`s listed before the navigation destinations. |

## v-model

| Model                 | Type      | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                               |
| --------------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:search-open` | `boolean` | `false` | `update:searchOpen` | Whether the search palette is open; the bar's search button and ⌘K / Ctrl K set it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the palette `open` / `closed`; the bar's sheet and mega-menus own their states (`SiteNav`).
- Not applicable: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid` (the sections own their states).

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: the bar is the `SiteNav` banner named "Azion"; the sections are inside the layout's single `<main>`; the footer is the `SiteFooter` `contentinfo`. A page must not render a second `<main>`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` runs bar → page → footer; `⌘K` / `Ctrl K` opens the palette (owned by `Command`); in the palette `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown` move, `Enter` chooses, `Escape` closes and returns focus. The bar's menus and sheet own their keyboard models.
- Visible focus and contrast: owned by the composed components; the canvas tokens keep text ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; `SiteNav` and `SiteFooter` mirror their own rows.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: arrow handling is `Command`'s and `SiteNav`'s, both direction-aware.
- User data: destination labels render inside `Command.Item` with `dir="auto"`.

## Internationalization

| Key                            | English source                 | Override prop       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| `siteLayout.searchPlaceholder` | `Search the site`              | `searchPlaceholder` |
| `siteLayout.searchEmpty`       | `No page matches your search.` | —                   |
| `siteLayout.pages`             | `Pages`                        | —                   |

- Formatting: none. Navigation and footer text is consumer data.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; `SiteNav` switches to its sheet below `xl` and `SiteFooter` reflows its rows.
- Narrow: the main column is full width; the sections own their measure (`SectionContainer`).
- Touch: owned by the composed components.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px; the page scrolls the document (no inner scroll area), so a full-page capture shows the whole page.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/band-stack.md -->

# Band Stack

> A run of framed bands that follow one another down the page, each one drawn as two registration frames — its left half and its right half — sharing a hairline with the next. With `sticky` on, each band pins under the site header a step lower than the band before it, so the run piles up as the reader scrolls and every band already read stays visible as a ledge above the one being read. The component owns the band rules, the shared hairlines and the pin offsets, and by default every band is split into two frames: a `media-split` composed into the stack frames its copy cell and its media cell as two `frame-box`es, left and right, each with its four marks. The bands themselves are whatever the consumer composes into the default slot — each direct child becomes one band. It carries no copy, heading or media of its own.

- Import: `import BandStack from '@aziontech/webkit/band-stack'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For a run of peer bands — three to six `media-split`s, one per solution or capability — that should read as one sequence.
- With `sticky`, when the run is the page's centrepiece and the reader should feel each band land on the last.
- Without `sticky`, to frame a run of bands with one shared hairline between neighbours, with no pinning.

## Do

- Keep the run to three to six bands. With `sticky` every band read stays pinned as a ledge, and a long run fills the viewport with ledges.
- Give every band the same height class (`media-split` `size="large"`, same `align`), so the ledges line up as the pile grows.
- Pass `flush` when the element directly above the stack already draws a rule (a `section-gap`, another frame), so the first band does not draw a second one.
- Give each band an opaque fill (`media-split` paints its own cells). A pinned band covers the one before it, and a transparent band shows the one underneath through it.
- Compose `media-split`s as the bands. The two frames are the band's own cells, so a child that is not a `media-split` carries no marks unless it frames itself — wrap it in a `frame-box` with `borders="none"`.
- Render the bands with `v-for` directly in the default slot; each direct child is one band, so a wrapper element around them collapses the run into a single band.

## Don’t

- For a run where the scroll position should decide which claim is open beside one media pane → use `sticky-stack`.
- For peer claims a reader jumps between at will → use `media-tabs`.
- For a single band → frame it with `frame-box` directly, or set `framed` on the `media-split`.
- For a grid of cards → use `card-grid`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the band this stack holds, typically at `size="large"`. Inside the stack it frames its own two cells, so leave its `framed` off.
- `sticky-stack` — the scroll-driven sibling: one pinned frame whose open claim follows the scroll, instead of bands that pile up.
- `frame-box` — the frame each band is drawn in.
- `section-gap` — the spacer usually above the stack; pass `flush` so the first band does not draw a second rule under it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Pin each band under the site header from `lg` up, a step lower than the band before it, so the run piles up as the page scrolls. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Drop the first band's top rule, for a stack sitting directly under an element that already draws one. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The bands. Each direct child — including every child a `v-for` renders — is wrapped in its own frame and becomes one band; comment nodes are skipped. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-sticky` mirrors the `sticky` prop and is what pins the bands: from `lg` up each band is `position: sticky`, its `top` the site header's height plus one `var(--spacing-md)` step per band before it. Below `lg` the bands stack in normal flow with no pinning, because a pinned pile of full-width bands leaves a phone no room to read
- `data-flush` mirrors the `flush` prop; the first band's frame then draws no top rule
- Each band is a `frame-box` with its top and bottom rules and no marks of its own. The stack provides a context that tells a `media-split` band to frame its two cells, left and right, each with all four registration marks, so every band reads as two frames and both sides of its seam are ticked. Every band after the first pulls up one pixel so neighbouring rules overlap into a single hairline, while each band still owns its top rule — the rule a pinned band shows when it covers the one before it
- The pin offset is owned by the component, not the page: the stack pins below the site header's `3.5rem` bar, and a page sets nothing to get it
- Later bands paint over earlier ones in DOM order, so the pile grows downward with no `z-index` of its own

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable to the stack; controls inside each band keep their own `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` moves through each band's controls in DOM order, band by band.
- ARIA: the stack is a plain `div` with no role; each band keeps its own semantics (`media-split` is a `section` named by its heading).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): not applicable — the stack draws only rules; each band owns its text contrast.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the stack declares no motion. Pinning is scroll position, not animation.
- Touch target — not applicable; the stack composes no control of its own.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BandStack from '@aziontech/webkit/band-stack'
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
  import MediaSplit from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split'
</script>

<template>
  <BandStack>
    <MediaSplit
      title="Build and Run Applications"
      description="Deploy applications and static sites straight from Git."
      size="large"
      align="center"
      :heading-level="3"
    >
      <template #media>
        <Illustration name="ai-applications" />
      </template>
    </MediaSplit>
    <MediaSplit
      title="Secure Applications and Networks"
      description="Stop DDoS attacks, bots and exploits before they reach your origin."
      size="large"

```

<!-- components/banner.md -->

# Banner

> A split promotional band: the announcement and its actions in the wide leading column, a short supporting note on a raised surface in the narrow trailing one. It is the page's one loud interruption between sections — wider and more assertive than `call-to-action`, which is a single-column closing ask.

- Import: `import Banner from '@aziontech/webkit/banner'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To announce a launch, programme or offer part-way down a marketing page.
- Whenever an announcement needs both a primary action and a short piece of supporting context beside it.
- Once per page. A second banner turns the first into furniture.

## Do

- The band draws no frame of its own: the rule and the corner marks belong to the `section-module` or `frame-box` that the page assembles it into, so a band placed in a framed column never lands a second hairline on the column's own.
- Put the announcement in `title` and keep the trailing column to one supporting sentence — it is context, not a second pitch.
- Lead with one primary action in the `actions` slot; the band's whole job is that one target.
- Use `eyebrow` to name the programme the banner belongs to, so the band reads in context when a reader lands mid-page.
- Keep the trailing note short enough not to set the band's height; it sits beside the announcement, not under it.

## Don’t

- For the closing ask at the end of a page or section → use `call-to-action`, a single-column panel.
- For the page's leading statement → use `hero`, whose `Hero.Title` owns the `h1`.
- For a dismissible or status-bearing notice inside the product → use `message`.
- For a feature tile in a grid → use `topic` in a `card-grid`.

## Related

- `call-to-action` — the single-column closing ask; this is the wider mid-page announcement.
- `hero` — the page's leading band; its `Hero.Title` owns the page's statement and `h1`.
- message` — the in-product notice, which can be dismissed and carries severity.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The announcement, rendered as the band's `h2` in the leading column. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting note set on the raised trailing column; overridden by the `aside` slot. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short uppercase overline naming the programme, above the announcement. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | — | The controls the band exists to offer, under the announcement. |
| `aside` | — | Trailing column content; replaces the `description` prop when provided. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The band holds no state of its own; controls composed into `actions` keep theirs
- Below `md` the two columns stack, announcement first, so reading order matches visual order

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable to the band itself; controls composed into `actions` keep their own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` reaches only the controls placed in the `actions` slot, in DOM order.
- ARIA: the announcement is a real `h2` rendered by the composed `section-title`, and the band is a `<section>` named by its `title`, so it is reachable as a named landmark; no `role` is added.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the announcement is `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)`; the trailing note uses `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface-raised)`, which clears AA on the dark canvas and is a known theme-level shortfall on the light one (see `big-numbers`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the band is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the `actions` row stretches its children to full width below `md`, so slotted buttons keep their own target size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Banner from '@aziontech/webkit/banner'
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
</script>

<template>
  <Banner
    eyebrow="Edge Runtime"
    title="WebAssembly now runs in every edge location."
    description="Ship the same binary everywhere — no regions to pick and no cold starts to budget for."
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button label="Read the announcement" />
    </template>
  </Banner>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/banner.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/banner.md).

<!-- components/banner-art.md -->

# Banner Art

> The decorative backdrop a site, hub or docs band stands on, for a `Hero` `background` slot or any band with `relative overflow-hidden`: `globe` hangs half a globe past the page's inline-end rule over the dot lattice, `map` insets the world map beside the copy, `network` lays the map full bleed with its PoPs lit, the sample's `MapMesh` traffic crossing between them (`NetworkMap` `traffic`: links and packets, the links alone as the still frame under reduced motion) and a scrim over the copy column. From the design sample's `shared/ui/banners` (GlobeBanner, MapBanner, NetworkBanner), drawn with WebKit's own `SpinningGlobe` and `NetworkMap` so there is one map and one globe in the system. The inventory's "`Banner` `art` variants" became this sibling component under `marketing/banner`: `Banner` is an announcement band with its own surfaces, and a backdrop layer is a different thing.

- Import: `import BannerArt from '@aziontech/webkit/banner-art'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Behind the opening band of a landing, the hub or the docs home.

## Do

- One backdrop per page.
- Keep the copy at the inline start: every art is washed toward it.

## Don’t

- As content: it is `aria-hidden` and says nothing.
- Behind dense text or a form.
- For a plain texture — use `TextureMaterial`.

## Related

- Hero` — the `background` slot it fills.
- NetworkMap`, `SpinningGlobe` — what it draws.
- TextureMaterial` — the dot lattice.
- Banner` — the announcement band (unrelated surface).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `art` | `'globe' \ \| 'map' \ \| 'network'` | `'map'` | false | Which backdrop to draw. |
| `animated` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Spins the globe or pulses the PoPs; a still frame when false or under reduced motion. |

## States

- `data-art` mirrors `art`.

## Accessibility

- `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events-none`: never announced, never in the way of a click.
- The washes keep the copy column at canvas contrast.

## Right-to-left

- The globe hangs off the inline-end rule and the washes run from the inline start in both directions (`rtl:` variants).
- Keyboard: not focusable.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none.

## Responsive

- The globe is sized off the band height (a size container on the backdrop) and capped by `150vw` and `--container-5xl`.
- The map takes the full width below medium and the inline-end three fifths from medium.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BannerArt from '@aziontech/webkit/banner-art'
  import Hero from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-root'
  import HeroTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-title'
</script>

<template>
  <Hero
    kind="band"
    size="large"
    max-width="site"
  >
    <template #background>
      <BannerArt art="map" />
    </template>
    <HeroTitle
      eyebrow="Network"
      eyebrow-prefix="//"
      title="Close to every user, by default"
      description="Requests land on the nearest location and stay there."
    />
  </Hero>
</template>
```

<!-- components/bento-grid.md -->

# Bento Grid

> A mosaic of unequal cells on one set of shared rules: each cell claims a number of columns and rows, and the rules between them are drawn once so the whole block reads as a single framed surface. It is the layout a marketing page uses when several claims deserve different amounts of room — the alternative to a row of identical tiles.

- Import: `import BentoGridRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/bento-grid-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import BentoGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/bento-grid'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: composition

## When to use

- When a set of claims is genuinely unequal and one or two deserve more room than the rest.
- As the framed body of a product or platform section, under a `section-title`.
- For a logo wall, a client-story band, or any set where a few members carry a headline and the rest carry only a mark.
- Whenever the cells hold composed content — copy, media, a control — rather than one repeated shape.

## Do

- Size the mosaic so the cells fill the rectangle: count the tracks (`columns` × rows) and check the spans add up, or the grid ends on a gap of bare canvas.
- Keep cells in reading order — the grid auto-places in DOM order, so that order is what a screen reader and a keyboard follow, and it is what puts a cell in the track you meant.
- Compose real elements inside a cell rather than passing a config array; the cell is a slot, and that is the point of it.
- Let the grid draw the rules. Do not add borders inside a cell, or the shared edges double.
- Give a cell `kind="none"` + `padded="false"` when its own content paints the cell — a media layer, a brand fill, or a link that must be the whole tile.
- Inside a framed page column, set `flush` so the column's rules stay one hairline each.

## Don’t

- When every claim carries the same weight → use `card-grid`.
- For a row of measured figures → use `big-numbers`, which already draws this grid for numbers.
- For a single copy-and-media pairing → use `media-split`.
- For a list of questions → use `faq`.

## Related

- `card-grid` — the equal-cell grid with no spans, in the gap or divider register.
- `big-numbers` — the same collapsed-rule grid, specialised for figures.
- `media-split` — the two-column band when there is one claim, not several.
- `frame-box` — the frame each cell is drawn with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the grid, when the surrounding section does not already name it. |
| `columns` | `BentoGridColumns` | `2` | false | How many columns the mosaic lays out from the medium breakpoint up. |
| `mobileColumns` | `BentoGridMobileColumns` | `1` | false | How many columns the mosaic holds below the medium breakpoint, where every cell claims one of them. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The surrounding frame already draws the grid's outer rules: the grid drops its own top and left ones and lays its right and bottom ones onto the frame's, so a framed column keeps one hairline per edge. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The grid's cells, composed as `BentoGrid.Cell` elements in reading order. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/bento-grid-cell`

## Sub-components

- `bento-grid-cell/bento-grid-cell.vue` — one cell of the mosaic; owns its own frame, and takes the tracks it claims (`span`, `rows`), the fill it carries (`kind`) and whether it pads its content (`padded`).

Cell props: `span` (`'1' | '2' | '3' | '4' | 'full'`, default `'1'`) — columns claimed from the medium breakpoint up; `rows` (`'1' | '2'`, default `'1'`) — rows claimed from the medium breakpoint up; `kind` (`'surface' | 'canvas' | 'none'`, default `'surface'`) — the cell's fill, where `none` leaves the surface to the composed content; `padded` (`boolean`, default `true`) — off for a cell whose content reaches its edges.

The compound `index.ts` annotates the `Object.assign` result with an explicit `typeof BentoGrid & { Cell: typeof BentoGridCell }` type. Without it, declaration emit expands the root's private `Props` interface and `vue-tsc` fails with TS4082 ("default export of the module has or is using private name"). Do not simplify it back to a bare `Object.assign`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-columns` and `data-mobile-columns` on the grid mirror the track counts it lays out at each breakpoint
- `data-flush` on the grid mirrors `flush`, and is what withholds its own outer rules
- `data-span` and `data-rows` on each cell mirror its props and drive the tracks it claims from `md` up
- `data-kind` and `data-padded` on the cell's content box mirror its fill and its padding
- Below `md` every cell claims one of the mobile columns — only `span="full"` still takes the whole row — and no cell claims a second row
- Empty: a grid with no cells renders no rules, so an unfilled grid leaves no empty frame on the page

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the grid and its cells are containers and are not focusable; controls composed inside a cell keep their own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` follows DOM order through whatever the cells contain. The grid is not a composite widget, so it declares no arrow-key model.
- ARIA: the grid is a plain container named by `ariaLabel` when set; cells add no role, so headings composed inside them keep the document outline the page intends.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the cells provide `var(--bg-surface)` or `var(--bg-canvas)`; a `kind="none"` cell hands both the fill and its contrast to the composed content.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the grid is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable; the grid holds no interactive target of its own.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BentoGridCell from '@aziontech/webkit/bento-grid-cell'
  import BentoGridRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/bento-grid-root'
</script>

<template>
  <BentoGridRoot aria-label="Platform capabilities">
    <BentoGridCell>
      <h3 class="m-0 text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Deploy in seconds</h3>
      <p class="m-0 mt-(--spacing-sm) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Push to a repository and the application is live at every location, with no pipeline to
        assemble first.
      </p>
    </BentoGridCell>
    <BentoGridCell>
      <h3 class="m-0 text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Scale without capacity planning</h3>
      <p class="m-0 mt-(--spacing-sm) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Traffic is absorbed where it arrives, so there is no region to size and nothing to provision
        ahead of a launch.
      </p>
    </BentoGridCell>
    <BentoGridCell>
      <h3 class="m-0 text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Observe every request</h3>
      <p class="m-0 mt-(--spacing-sm) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Real-time events and metrics land in the same console that runs the application, without a
        second tool to wire up.
      </p>
    </BentoGridCell>
    <BentoGridCell>
      <h3 class="m-0 text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Pay for what you use</h3>
      <p class="m-0 mt-(--spacing-sm) text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Billing follows requests and compute time, so an idle application costs nothing to keep
        running.
      </p>
    </BentoGridCell>
  </BentoGridRoot>
</template>
```

<!-- components/big-numbers.md -->

# Big Numbers

> A band of headline figures — throughput, uptime, points of presence — set in the display face at big-number scale, each in its own cell of a hairline `card-grid` with a short caption underneath. It is the proof band of a marketing page: the one place a page states its numbers, between a `section-title` and the section body.

- Import: `import BigNumbers from '@aziontech/webkit/big-numbers'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To state a handful of measured facts (2–6) as the proof band of a marketing or landing page.
- Whenever the figure itself is the message and the caption only names what was measured.
- Under a `section-title`, as the opening evidence of a section.

## Do

- The band draws no frame of its own: the rule and the corner marks belong to the `section-module` or `frame-box` that the page assembles it into, so a band placed in a framed column never lands a second hairline on the column's own.
- Keep the band to 2–6 figures: it reads as a row, and past six the cells stop being scannable.
- Put the unit in `suffix` and the qualifier in `prefix`, so the figure itself stays the largest, highest-contrast thing in the cell.
- Keep `label` to a few words — it is set at overline scale and is a caption, not a sentence.
- Round the figures. A band is a claim, not a readout; `99.99%` belongs here, `99.9873%` does not.
- Leave `size` at `medium` unless the band is the page's hero statement (`large`) or sits inside a denser section (`small`).

## Don’t

- For a single monetary amount → use `currency`, which owns the amount ladder and its symbol placement.
- For a plan's headline price inside a pricing card → use `card-pricing`.
- For tabular or comparable figures a reader will scan row by row → use `table`.
- For a label-and-value pair at body scale inside a card or list → use `item`.

## Related

- `section-title` — the framed section header this band usually sits under.
- `card-grid` — the hairline grid the cells sit in; its `gap-px` seams are the rules between them.
- `currency` — a monetary amount at three reading distances, with symbol handling.
- `card-pricing` — a plan card, where the headline figure is a price.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BigNumberItem[]` | `[]` | false | The figures rendered as cells, in order; each item is `{ value, label, prefix?, suffix? }` where `value` is the figure, `label` its caption, and `prefix` / `suffix` the qualifier and unit set beside it. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Size token; picks the big-number scale the figures are set at. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and drives the figure's type scale
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders no cells and draws no frame — a marketing proof band with nothing to prove is absent from the page, not an `empty-state`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the band is static copy and holds no interactive control.
- Keyboard map: none of its own; the band contains no focusable element and is skipped by `Tab`.
- ARIA: each cell is a `<figure>` whose `<figcaption>` carries the caption, so the figure and what it measures are one unit for a screen reader; `prefix` and `suffix` are plain spans inside the figure's text, so the announced value is the whole expression.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the figure is `var(--text-default)` (17.65:1 light, 20.12:1 dark) and the accent prefix `var(--text-primary)` (`primary-700` in light, `primary-500` in dark) is large text (5.5:1 or more light, 6.71:1 dark). The caption is `var(--text-muted)` at overline scale — 5.32:1 on the dark canvas, but **3.78:1 on the light canvas, under AA for normal text**. This is a system-wide property of `--text-muted`, not of this component; it is carried as a theme-level follow-up and is not worked around here with an off-token colour.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the component is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, no interactive target.
- Reflow: the figure row wraps (`flex-wrap`), so the prefix and the suffix move under the value when a cell is narrow, and the value itself breaks (`wrap-anywhere`) rather than overflow at 200% zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BigNumbers from '@aziontech/webkit/big-numbers'
</script>

<template>
  <BigNumbers
    :items="[
      { value: '120', suffix: '+', label: 'Points of presence' },
      { value: '99.99', suffix: '%', label: 'Availability' },
      { prefix: '<', value: '15', suffix: 'ms', label: 'Median latency' },
      { value: '4.5', suffix: 'Tbps', label: 'Network capacity' }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/call-to-action.md -->

# Call To Action

> The closing ask of a marketing page: a headline, a supporting sentence and the actions that follow from them, set apart from the surrounding copy by its own surface. It is a panel, not a section header — `section-title` opens a section, `call-to-action` closes one. Four registers. `panel` sets the copy and its controls on one surface, as a row from `md` up. `split` divides the band in two at a 7fr/3fr ratio: a raised lead cell carrying the headline and the primary action, and an aside carrying the supporting line and the secondary one — each cell pushing its control to the band's floor, so the two actions share a baseline at any height. `split` is the register a product page closes on, where the ask has a primary and a secondary path and the headline turns on a second, muted line. `lead` is that lead cell standing alone: the same raised surface, the same two-tone headline, with the supporting line moved under it and every control in one row on the band's floor. It is the register for a close that has no second, quieter path to describe — the band states the ask once and offers its actions together, rather than dividing them across two cells of unequal weight. `primary` is the loud close: one centred ask standing alone as a billboard, on the page canvas lit from above by the brand. The texture composed into the band — a pixelated layer whose two waves travel across it in the primary colour — is lit by its waves alone and carries the band's colour, so the ground stays the canvas and the copy keeps its ordinary ink. The texture is composed in through the `background` slot and the strip along the floor through `bottom`, so the band owns the light and the page owns what is drawn on it.

- Import: `import CallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/call-to-action'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- At the end of a marketing page or section, to carry the reader into signup, docs or sales.
- Whenever a page needs one visually separated block whose whole job is the action.
- Between two sections, as a mid-page ask that should not read as a new section header.
- In `split`, when the ask has two paths of unequal weight — a primary one to start and a secondary one to talk to someone.
- In `primary`, when the page ends on a single ask and the close should be the most lit band on the page, with benefits or proof running along its floor.
- In `lead`, when the band's actions are peers and belong in one row, so an aside cell would have nothing of its own to carry.

## Do

- framed` decides who draws the rule. On, the band draws its own registration frame — vertical rules handed back to the column, a tick at its floor. Off, the rule and the corner marks belong to the `section-module` or `frame-box` the page assembles it into, so a band placed in an already-framed column never lands a second hairline on the column's own.
- Keep `title` to one line and one ask. A panel that poses two questions gets neither answered.
- Put the controls in the `actions` slot; the panel lays them out as a row beside the copy from `md` up and stacks them full-width below it.
- Lead with the primary action and keep secondary ones `outlined` or `text`, so the panel has one obvious target.
- Use `eyebrow` only when the panel needs naming out of context; the headline usually carries the ask on its own.
- In `split`, `title` states the claim and `title-muted` states its consequence — one sentence in two tones, not two headlines. The band renders them as two spans of a single `h2`, so a screen reader reads one heading.
- In `split`, put the primary control in `actions` and the secondary one in `aside`; each cell floors its own control, which is what gives the two a shared baseline. `actions` stretches its child full-width below `md`; `aside` stretches its child at every width, so a control drawn to size to its own content goes in a wrapper there.
- In `lead`, every control goes in `actions` — they lay out as one row from `md` up and stack full-width below it. The copy column is capped at `--container-2xl` so the headline keeps a readable measure however wide the band runs.
- lead` sets the copy-to-actions gap at `--spacing-xl`, not the `--spacing-xxl` the other two use. In `split` that larger number is the *floor* of a stretched cell — what pushes the control onto the band's bottom edge — and in `panel` the controls sit beside the copy from `md` up. In `lead` nothing stretches and nothing sits beside, so `--spacing-xxl` stops reading as a floor and starts reading as a hole.
- In `primary`, the band is centred and carries `title` and `description` only; `eyebrow` and `titleMuted` are not drawn, so the headline stands alone over the texture.
- In `primary`, compose one `texture-material` into `background` — `pixelate` at `small` with `fade="bottom"` — and a `ticker` into `bottom`. The band moves the pixelate's resting pools out of frame and runs its two waves at triple gain and double pace, so the travelling bands carry the light instead of a still glow; keep the headline clear of the densest cells by leaving the band's own padding alone.
- In `primary`, give the ticker enough claims that the loop never repeats inside one screen, and let the pass derive itself: an item pass runs three times slower per claim than a mark pass, because a claim is read.
- Leave `framed` on when the band stands in a section column of its own, and off when the page already wraps it in a `frame-box` — two frames draw two hairlines on the same edge.

## Don’t

- To open a section with a headline and optional actions → use `section-title`, which draws a header rule rather than a panel.
- For the page's leading statement and primary CTAs → use `hero`, whose `Hero.Title` owns the `h1`.
- For a dismissible or time-bound announcement → use `message`.
- For a close that sits quietly in the column → use `split` or `panel`; `primary` fills a whole brand-coloured band and should appear once per page.
- For a plan's call to action inside pricing → use `card-pricing`, which owns its own action row.

## Related

- `section-title` — opens a section with a header rule; this closes one with a panel.
- `hero` — the page's leading band; its `Hero.Title` owns the statement and the `h1`.
- `frame-box` — the registration frame the band draws when `framed` is on, and the one the page supplies around it when off.
- `button` — the controls composed into the `actions` and `aside-actions` slots.
- `overline` — the `//`-prefixed eyebrow the band renders above the headline.
- `texture-material` — the pixelated, waving texture composed into `background` in `primary`.
- `ticker` — the strip of benefits composed into `bottom` in `primary`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`. |
| `titleMuted` | `string` | `''` | false | Second line of the headline, set in muted ink; rendered as a second span of the same `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence — under the headline in `panel` and `lead`, in the aside cell in `split`; overridden by the default slot. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short uppercase overline rendered above the headline. |
| `kind` | `CallToActionKind` | `'panel'` | false | Layout of the band: `panel` sets the copy and its controls on one surface, `split` divides it into a raised lead cell and an aside that each floor their own control, `lead` is that lead cell standing alone with every control in it, `primary` is a centred ask on the canvas lit by a pixelated, waving primary texture, with a floor. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Draw the band's own registration frame. Turn it off when the page already wraps the band in a frame. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Description body; replaces the `description` prop when provided. |
| `actions` | — | The controls the band exists to offer; in `split`, the lead cell's primary control. |
| `aside` | — | The aside cell's control in `split`; ignored in `panel`, `lead` and `primary`, where every control belongs in `actions`. |
| `background` | — | Decoration drawn behind the copy in `primary`, such as a `texture-material`; ignored in the other registers. |
| `bottom` | — | The strip that floors the band in `primary`, such as a `ticker`, under a hairline; ignored in the other registers. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Register: `data-kind="panel" | "split" | "lead" | "primary"` on the root
- The band holds no state of its own; controls composed into `actions` / `aside` keep theirs

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable to the panel itself; controls composed into `actions` keep their own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` reaches only the controls placed in the `actions` slot, in DOM order.
- ARIA: the headline is a real `h2` — rendered by the composed `section-title` in `panel`, and by the band itself in `split` and `lead`, where `title` and `title-muted` are two spans of that one heading so it is announced as a single string. The band is a `<section>` named by its `title`, reachable as a landmark with a name; no `role` is added.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): in `primary` the copy is ordinary ink on `var(--bg-canvas)`, so the pair is the same as `panel`'s. The headline is `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface)`; the description uses `var(--text-muted)`, which clears AA on the dark canvas and is a known theme-level shortfall on the light one (see `big-numbers`).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the panel is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — both action slots stretch their children to full width below the breakpoint, so slotted buttons keep their own target size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import CallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/call-to-action'
</script>

<template>
  <CallToAction
    title="Run your first application at the edge today."
    description="Deploy once and it runs in every location on the network — no servers to size, no credit card to start."
  >
    <template #actions>
      <Button label="Start for free" />
      <Button
        kind="outlined"
        label="Talk to a specialist"
      />
    </template>
  </CallToAction>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/call-to-action.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/call-to-action.md).

<!-- components/card-grid.md -->

# Card Grid

> The responsive cell grid of the page language, in three registers: spaced cards separated by real gutters, a hairline box grid whose internal rules are the gaps themselves, and a framed grid whose cells are real `frame-box` elements. The `frame` register is the one that composes: each `CardGrid.Cell` draws its own rules and corner marks and carries its own fill, so the grid needs no background trick and nests flush inside a column that already owns the outer edges.

- Import: `import CardGridRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import CardGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: composition

## When to use

- For a row or block of equal cells that should fan out from one column on a phone to several on a wide screen.
- With `kind` set to `frame` whenever the cells are real content — a `topic`, a claim, a figure — and should carry the page's frame language, corner marks included.
- For the hairline cell grid a `section-module` body holds, with `kind` set to `divider`.
- For a row of self-contained cards with gutters between them, with the default `gap`.

## Do

- **Do** hand the grid however many cells the content has. The default `balanced` layout takes the fewest rows `columns` allows and the narrowest track count that keeps them, so a count that splits evenly fills every row; a short last row keeps the track width and starts at the start edge, its trailing tracks left empty, as azion.com lays out its grids (compliance badges, the use-case grid). Under `columns: 3` that is 1 → one full-width cell, 2 → halves, 3 → thirds, 4 → 2 × 2, 5 → 3 + 2, 6 → 3 + 3, 7 → 3 + 3 + 1; under `columns: 4`, 4 → four across, 5 → 3 + 2, 6 → 3 + 3, 7 → 4 + 3; under `columns: 5`, 5 → five across. Below `lg` the same rule runs against two columns (`sm`) and against `mobileColumns` (phone), so 4 cells are 2 × 2 on a tablet and four across from `lg`.
- **Don't** pick `columns` from the item count or pad the list with placeholder cells. `columns` is the most a row may hold, not how many it must; the track count already drops to the even split (2 → halves, 4 → 2 × 2), and a short last row is never stretched across the empty tracks — a stretched last cell reads as a different, wider card.
- **Don't** reach for `layout="fixed"` to fix a count: keep it for tiles whose width must not change from row to row — square logo tiles, a cell that spans rows (`use-cases`) or columns (`subject-library`'s closing cell), a floor that keeps its track count whatever it holds (`network-section` benefits), a wall that overrides the track count. Anything else that wants unequal cells belongs in `bento-grid`.
- Prefer `frame` over `divider` for new work. The hairline register depends on every child filling its own background; the framed register draws real rules, so a cell that forgets its fill still reads correctly, and the corner marks come with it.
- Give every child of a `divider` grid its own background fill, or the gap trick has nothing to show through and the whole band goes the colour of the rule.
- Leave the perimeter to the container: the `divider` register draws no outer border, and a `frame` grid set to `flush` withholds its own top and left rules so a surrounding `frame-box` keeps one hairline per edge.
- Let the grid draw the rules. Do not add borders inside a `frame` cell, or the shared edges double.
- Give a cell `kind="none"` and `:padded="false"` when its own content paints the cell — a media layer, a brand fill, or a link that must be the whole tile.
- Reach for `mobileColumns` of `2` only for short, glyph-led cells; a cell carrying a description reads better one-up on a phone.

## Don’t

- For a mosaic whose cells claim different numbers of columns and rows → use `bento-grid`, which is this grid with spans.
- For a single framed box → use `frame-box`.
- For one card with a header, content and footer → use `card`.
- For the band that wraps the grid → use `section-module`.
- For tabular data a reader scans row by row → use `table`.
- Built to be personalized (style seam): any class is accepted on the tag.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the same framed grid with unequal cells; reach for it when one claim deserves more room than the rest.
- `topic` — the glyph, headline and sentence a `frame` cell usually holds.
- `section-module` — the band whose body holds this grid.
- `section-container` — the column whose vertical rules the `divider` and flush `frame` grids deliberately do not repeat.
- `frame-box` — the frame each `frame` cell is drawn with, and the framed box a `gap` cell may be built from.
- `card` — a padded card surface, the usual child of a `gap` grid.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `CardGridKind` | `'gap'` | false | Register of the grid: gutters between self-contained cards, hairline rules drawn by the gaps, or framed cells that draw their own rules and marks. |
| `columns` | `CardGridColumns` | `3` | false | How many columns the grid fans out to at the large breakpoint. |
| `mobileColumns` | `CardGridMobileColumns` | `1` | false | How many columns the grid holds below the small breakpoint. |
| `dividerColor` | `CardGridDividerColor` | `'default'` | false | Weight of the hairline rules in the `divider` register. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | `false` | false | In the `frame` register, the surrounding frame already draws the grid's outer rules: the grid drops its own top and left ones and lays its right and bottom ones onto the frame's, so a framed column keeps one hairline per edge. |
| `layout` | `CardGridLayout` | `'balanced'` | false | How the cells fill the rows: `balanced` picks the narrowest track count that keeps the fewest rows `columns` allows, so a count that splits evenly fills every row (2 → halves, 4 → 2 × 2), and a short last row keeps the track width with its trailing tracks left empty, as azion.com does (5 → 3 + 2, 7 → 3 + 3 + 1); `fixed` keeps a strict `columns`-wide grid whatever the count. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The cells, in reading order. In the `frame` register they are `CardGrid.Cell` elements; in the `divider` register each cell fills its own background. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/card-grid-cell`

## Sub-components

- `card-grid-cell/card-grid-cell.vue` — one cell of the `frame` register; wraps `frame-box` so the cell owns its own rules and corner marks, and takes the fill it carries (`kind`) and whether it pads its content (`padde…

Cell props: `kind` (`'surface' | 'canvas' | 'none'`, default `'surface'`) — the cell's fill, where `none` leaves the surface to the composed content; `padded` (`boolean`, default `true`) — off for a cell whose content reaches its edges.

The cell's `frame-box` is set `flush` on its top and left edges, so it draws only its right and bottom rules; the grid root draws the matching top and left ones. That is what gives the block one hairline per edge instead of two at every junction.

The compound `index.ts` annotates the `Object.assign` result with an explicit `typeof CardGrid & { Cell: typeof CardGridCell }` type. Without it, declaration emit expands the root's private `Props` interface and `vue-tsc` fails with TS4082 ("default export of the module has or is using private name"). Do not simplify it back to a bare `Object.assign`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` carries the register
- `data-columns` carries the large-breakpoint column count
- `data-mobile-columns` carries the small-breakpoint column count
- `data-divider-color` carries the hairline weight
- `data-flush` mirrors `flush`, and is what withholds the `frame` grid's own outer rules
- `data-layout` mirrors `layout`; `data-count` carries how many cells render (comments and empty text are not cells)
- The root is a CSS grid of equal tracks; it sets `--card-grid-cols-base`, `--card-grid-cols-sm` and `--card-grid-cols-lg` to the track count each breakpoint resolves to (`balanced`: the narrowest count for the fewest rows; `fixed`: `mobileColumns`, two, `columns`); every direct child is set to `height: auto` and stretches to its row; the counts come from the render, so the server HTML and the hydrated page lay out the same
- `data-fill-trailing` marks a `balanced` `divider` grid: its `::after` fills the trailing empty tracks of a short last row with `--bg-canvas` (spanning `--card-grid-rest`, hidden when the row is full), so the rule colour the gaps show through never shows as a block
- `data-filled` mirrors whether any cell renders, so an empty `frame` grid draws no stray rules
- `data-kind` and `data-padded` on each cell's content box mirror its fill and its padding
- Empty: a `frame` grid with no cells renders no rules, so an unfilled grid leaves no empty frame on the page

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the grid and its cells are containers; controls composed into a cell keep their own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none — the grid is not focusable; `Tab` order follows the cells in DOM order, which is reading order at every breakpoint.
- ARIA: the root adds no role, so a list composed into it keeps its own semantics and the cells reach the accessibility tree unchanged; a cell adds no role either, so headings composed inside it keep the document outline the page intends.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons) — the rules are non-informational decoration; a `frame` cell provides `var(--bg-surface)` or `var(--bg-canvas)`, and a `kind="none"` cell hands both the fill and its contrast to the composed content.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the component is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, no interactive control of its own.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CardGridRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/card-grid-root'
</script>

<template>
  <CardGridRoot :columns="3">
    <div class="bg-(--bg-canvas) p-(--spacing-xl) text-body-md text-(--text-muted)">One</div>
    <div class="bg-(--bg-canvas) p-(--spacing-xl) text-body-md text-(--text-muted)">Two</div>
    <div class="bg-(--bg-canvas) p-(--spacing-xl) text-body-md text-(--text-muted)">Three</div>
  </CardGridRoot>
</template>
```
