<!-- components/section-title.md -->

# Section Title

> The framed header row that opens a page section: an optional overline, the section's `h2`, an optional description and an optional row of actions, held inside a registration frame whose bottom rule is what divides the header from the section body. `kind` picks the layout — `centered` for a symmetric opener, `left` for a reading-order one, and `horizontal` for a wide row that sets the headline against its description.

- Import: `import SectionTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/section-title'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Opening a marketing or landing page section that needs a framed header.
- Whenever the header itself should carry the rule that separates it from the content below, with no extra margin.
- For a wide band whose headline and supporting sentence should sit side by side rather than stacked — `kind="horizontal"`.

## Do

- Leave `framed` on when the header is a brick of its own in a page column; turn it off when a band composes the header inside a frame it already draws, so the rule and the padding are not drawn twice.
- Keep one `section-title` per section, and let it own the section's `h2` so the page keeps one document outline. `size` changes the headline's step on the type scale, never its heading level — a page with a `large` and a `small` header still reads as two `h2`s.
- Leave `size` at `medium` for an ordinary section opener. Reach for `large` only where the headline is the band's whole statement, and for `small` where the header opens a subsection inside a band that already has one.
- Write the eyebrow as one or two words: it is set uppercase and prefixed with `//`, so a sentence in it reads as noise.
- Reach for `horizontal` when the description is long enough to earn its own column — on a narrow viewport it stacks back under the headline.
- In `horizontal`, set `--section-title-headline-span` to `2` from the consumer's class to run the headline across the middle column too, when it would otherwise wrap to three lines; the description keeps the third column, and the default `1` leaves that column as air. `--section-title-headline-max` caps the headline's width inside its span (`none` by default), so a headline that would fit on one line across two columns still breaks into two.
- In `horizontal`, set `descriptionWidth="wide"` when the description runs to a paragraph and would stack six or more lines in the third column alone; it then spans the middle and third columns, capped at `--container-xl` and aligned to the right edge so it ends where the narrow description ends. It takes the column a `--section-title-headline-span` of `2` would claim, so use one or the other. Outside `horizontal` the prop has no effect.
- Put the section's CTAs in the `actions` slot rather than in the body; the slot already stacks them fluid below `sm` and aligns them with the chosen `kind` above it.
- The vertical rhythm around the header belongs to the `section-gap` frames on either side, not to this component.

## Don’t

- For the page's leading band and its `h1` → use `hero` instead.
- For the top bar of an application shell → use `global-header` instead.
- For a plain framed container with arbitrary content → use `frame-box` instead.

## Related

- `hero` — the opening band; its `Hero.Title` renders the page's `h1` at hero scale.
- `frame-box` — the frame this component composes.
- `section-gap` — the empty frame that sets the air before and after a section header; this component holds no vertical air of its own beyond its padding.
- `overline` — the eyebrow treatment rendered above the headline.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | Headline of the section, rendered as the section's `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline; overridden by the default slot. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short uppercase overline rendered above the headline. |
| `kind` | `'centered' \| 'left' \| 'horizontal'` | `'centered'` | false | Layout of the header: `centered` stacks and centers the copy, `left` stacks it at the start edge, `horizontal` sets the headline and its description in two columns. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Step of the headline on the heading scale: `small` for a subsection inside a band, `medium` for an ordinary section opener, `large` for a band whose headline is the statement. |
| `framed` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draw the header's own frame and padding. Turn it off when the header is composed inside a band that already owns both. |
| `padding` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Vertical padding of the framed header: `medium` for a section opener, `small` for a header that sits tight over its band. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `'narrow' \| 'wide'` | `'narrow'` | false | Width of the description in the horizontal layout: `narrow` keeps it to the third column, `wide` runs it across the middle column too. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Description body; replaces the `description` prop when provided. |
| `actions` | — | Call-to-action row under the copy, aligned with the chosen `kind`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop: `centered` | `left` | `horizontal`
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop: `small` | `medium` | `large`
- `data-framed` present when the header draws its own frame and padding
- `data-padding` mirrors the `padding` prop: `small` | `medium`
- `data-description-width` mirrors the `descriptionWidth` prop: `narrow` | `wide`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable to the header itself; controls composed into the `actions` slot keep their own `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: none of its own — `Tab` reaches only the controls placed in the `actions` slot, in DOM order.
- ARIA: the headline is a real `h2` (the page's `h1` belongs to `Hero.Title`), so no `role` or `aria-label` is added; the frame's rules and corner marks stay `aria-hidden="true"`. In `horizontal` the headline precedes its description in DOM order, so the reading order matches the visual one.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline on `var(--text-default)`, description on `var(--text-muted)`, both over the page canvas.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — not applicable, the component is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the `actions` row stretches its children to full width below `sm`, so slotted buttons keep their own target size.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SectionTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/section-title'
</script>

<template>
  <SectionTitle
    eyebrow="Platform"
    title="Everything runs at the edge"
    description="One platform for applications, security and observability."
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/section-title.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/section-title.md).

<!-- components/site-page.md -->

# Site Page

> The page renderer of the marketing site: it takes a page as data — the page JSON `{ hero, sections }` whose entries are `{ _id, props, scenes?, gap?, submission? }` — and renders each entry with the page section published at `@aziontech/webkit/<_id>`, binding `props` onto it. Openings (`hero`) run full bleed; the column (`sections`) sits in one `SectionContainer max-width="site"` with a hatched `SectionGap` before each band and one more after the last, the hatched break a page closes on before the footer (in the design sample that break is drawn by the closing call to action of every page), as the design sample's `SitePage` lays a page out. A scene named in `scenes` is resolved by name through the scene registry and drawn in the section's slot of that name (`hero-band` `top` / `bottom`, `console-panel` `scene`). Every section and scene is loaded on demand, so a page pulls in only the sections it lists. An `_id` or scene name the renderer does not know is skipped with a development warning naming it, never silently. It reverses the earlier rule in `.claude/docs/SECTIONS.md` ("the package ships no registry and no dispatcher"): the owner decided to ship the renderer (ROADMAP M2.10 row 44), and that doc is updated with it. **Section registry.** `src/components/marketing/site-page/site-page-sections.ts`, beside the component, maps every folder in `src/components/sections/` except `site-nav` and `site-footer` (the frame, which `shells/website` owns) to a `() => import('../../sections/<name>/<name>.vue')` thunk, keyed by the folder name, which is the `_id`. The component test fails when a section folder has no entry. **Scene registry.** `src/assets/scene-registry.ts` exports `sceneAssets` (scene name to a `() => import(...)` thunk), the `SceneName` union of its keys and `resolveScene(name)`, which returns one cached async component per name or `null` for a name it does not hold. It is seeded with `BrandGlobeScene` and `SpinningGlobe` (the two scenes `media-split-band` drew from a private map) and with `Diagram`, `ProductWidget` and `Illustration`, the components a scene slot already takes. `media-split-band` moves from its private `SCENES` constant onto it in the same change, so the system has one scene map, and a scene ported later (`ConsoleApplicationScene`, `ConsoleTraceScene`, `FunctionsHeroCanvas`) becomes drawable on every page by one entry there. **Root.** A plain `div` with no role, carrying `v-bind="$attrs"` and the `data-testid` fallback `marketing-site-page`.

- Import: `import SitePage from '@aziontech/webkit/site-page'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Rendering a marketing page stored as data (a CMS entry, a JSON file, the site's page modules) on WebKit sections.
- A campaign landing built from existing sections with no page-specific code.

## Do

- Write `_id` as the section's public subpath (`use-cases` for `@aziontech/webkit/use-cases`); the `props` object is exactly what the section's own `site-*.json` example carries.
- Put openings (`hero-band`, `hero-form`, `hero-with-opening`, `hero-copy-on-top-art`, `article-body`, `pricing-plans`) in `hero` and every band after them in `sections`.
- Keep scenes as names (`{ component: 'BrandGlobeScene' }`), never as code, so the page stays plain JSON.
- Use `gap` only to change the default break: `none` for a band that follows its neighbour with no break, `small` for two bands that belong together.
- Keep transport details of a form (`endpoint`, `hiddenFields`) in `submission`, next to `props`; the renderer passes the entry back on `submit` and the site sends.
- Watch the development console after changing a page: an unknown `_id` or scene is named there.
- Keep one opening per page: every opening renders the page `h1`, so two openings put two `h1` on the page.
- Render the page on the server when layout shift matters: a section still loading on the client reserves no space.

## Don’t

- A page that composes marketing primitives by hand (`Hero`, `MediaSplit`, `CardGrid`) — write the SFC with `SectionContainer` / `SectionGap` instead.
- A console screen or a docs page — use `shells/console` or `shells/documentation`.
- One section on its own — import that section (`@aziontech/webkit/<name>`) and bind its props.

## Related

- `section-container` — the column the renderer lays `sections` in.
- `section-gap` — the hatched break it draws before each band.
- The page sections (`hero-band`, `use-cases`, `faq-section`, …) — what each `_id` names.
- shells/website` — the nav and footer frame a page renders inside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hero` | `SitePageSection[]` | `() => []` | false | Opening sections, rendered full bleed above the column in order; each is `{ _id, props?, scenes?, gap?, submission? }`. |
| `sections` | `SitePageSection[]` | `() => []` | false | Column sections, rendered in order inside the site column with a hatched gap before each and after the last; each is `{ _id, props?, scenes?, gap?, submission? }`. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, payload: SitePageSubmit)` | A section's form passed its own validation (`hero-form`, `closing-call-to-action-newsletter`); the site sends it and feeds `loading` / `submitted` / `error` back through that entry's `props`. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.
- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- No state of its own; each section owns its states (`loading`, `submitted`, `error` on a form band come from its `props`).
- An unknown `_id` or scene name renders nothing in its place and warns once per name in development.
- A section or scene still loading renders nothing in its place until its chunk arrives.
- A section or scene whose chunk fails to load (network failure, deploy skew) or takes longer than 10 s renders nothing in its place, the rest of the page keeps rendering, and a development warning names the `_id` or scene; it does not retry (`defineAsyncComponent` with `timeout` and `onError`).

## Accessibility

- The renderer adds no landmark, heading or focusable element of its own; each section owns its landmark (`<section>` named by its title) and its keyboard model.
- Openings render before the column, so the page `h1` (in the opening) comes first in reading order.
- The breaks are decorative (`SectionGap` is `aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard map: none of its own; focus moves through the sections in page order.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: block flow only; the column and the sections use logical utilities.
- Icons: none of its own.
- Keyboard: none of its own.
- User data: none of its own; sections isolate their own user data.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string comes from the page data.
- Development warnings are English and never rendered.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none of its own; the column follows `SectionContainer` and each section its own breakpoints.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): the column runs edge to edge as `SectionContainer` does; sections stack themselves.
- Touch: no targets of its own.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px from the renderer; the sections hold the same contract.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/sticky-stack.md -->

# Sticky Stack

> A band that pins to the viewport and is read by scrolling through it: a stack of claims on one side, one piece of media on the other, and the scroll position — not a pointer — deciding which claim is open. Each claim expands in turn while the ones already read collapse and stack above it, so the column keeps one height and the reader always sees where they are in the run. The media beside it is replaced, not dimmed: the outgoing scene leaves and the incoming one mounts, so a scene that animates plays its entrance every time it is reached.

- Import: `import StickyStack from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-stack'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For a sequence of claims a reader should take in one at a time, each with a medium worth looking at — five ways a platform is used, each with the file you would actually write.
- When the media is the payload and the copy is the caption: a code sample, a console shot, an official scene.
- As the one band on a page that rewards scrolling slowly, placed where a reader has already committed to the page.

## Do

- Keep the run to three to six claims. The band holds the page for `dwell` of a screen per claim, and a reader who cannot see the end of it reads it as a page that will not let go.
- Write each claim to stand alone. A reader can land mid-band from a deep link or a focus jump, so no claim may depend on the one above it.
- Keep a title to one line. The collapsed rows set the column's height, and a title that wraps changes it for every claim at once.
- Keep a description to two or three lines. Only the open claim shows one, and a long one pushes the stack past the pinned frame.
- Give every claim a medium. The frame holds one at a time and mounts it fresh, so a claim with nothing to show reads as a band that broke rather than one that is quiet.
- Use media of the same shape. The frame does not resize between claims, and a scene that changes the frame's height un-pins the band mid-read.
- Set `--sticky-stack-top` to the height of any sticky header above the band, or the first claim opens underneath it. Set it on a wrapper around the band rather than on the band's own tag: custom properties inherit, and the band is not a style seam.
- Leave `showProgress` on. It is the only thing telling a reader how much of the pin is left.
- Raise `dwell` for claims that carry code a reader must actually read; lower it for scenes that are grasped at a glance.

## Don’t

- For peer claims a reader should be able to jump between at will → use `media-tabs`, which selects on hover, click and a timer without taking the scroll.
- For one claim beside one picture → use `media-split`.
- For questions and answers, or any run longer than about six items → use `faq`. A pinned band holds the page for its whole run, and a long run holds it too long.
- On a page that is already a single short screen: there is no scroll to spend.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the pointer-driven sibling. Same two-column anatomy; the selection moves on hover, click and a timer, and the band does not pin.
- `media-split` — one claim, one medium, no selection and no pin.
- `code-block` — the medium this band most often holds, one sample per claim.
- `illustration` — the official scene a claim's `media` slot otherwise holds.
- `section-title` — the heading above the band; this component carries no title of its own.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `StickyStackItem[]` | `[]` | false | The claims, in reading order; each item is a title, the sentence that opens with it, and the image shown while it is open. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Height the open claim is held to, and so the height of the whole stack beside the media. |
| `dwell` | `number` | `0.7` | false | Screen-heights of scrolling each claim holds while the band is pinned; the band's total scroll is one screen plus this much per claim. |
| `showProgress` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Fills a hairline along the open claim's bottom edge as its share of the scroll is spent. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index-change` | `number` | The open claim changed; the payload is the index now open. Fires on the scroll that moved it and on a reader selecting a claim. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | { item: StickyStackItem, index: number, active: boolean } | The claim's medium; replaces the image built from the item's own source. Mounted fresh on every change, so an entrance animation inside it replays. |
| `actions` | { item: StickyStackItem, index: number, active: boolean } | The claim's own controls, pinned to the bottom edge of the open claim. From `lg` up they show only while the claim is open and are out of the tab order while it is collapsed; below `lg` every claim is open and carries its own. Nothing renders when the slot is empty. |
| `backdrop` | — | Fills the media frame behind every claim's medium, from `lg` up. Mounted once and never swapped, so a texture or an animated surface placed here holds still while the media change over it. Nothing renders when the slot is empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible` on each claim's title control
- `data-active` marks the open claim; it holds the plain text tone and shows its description
- `data-complete` marks every claim already read; they collapse to their title and rest at a muted tone, further dimmed so the read part of the run is legible at a glance, stacked above the open one
- `data-size` carries the size token, which is what sets the open claim's height and so the stack's height
- `data-progress` is present on the root while `showProgress` is on
- The media frame shows exactly one medium: the outgoing one leaves as the incoming one mounts
- The backdrop is not part of the medium: it stays mounted across every change, under the medium that is leaving and the one arriving
- A claim's description is held to `var(--container-sm)` so the measure stays short however wide the column is
- Below `lg` the band does not pin: every claim is open, each with its own medium under it, and nothing moves
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on every claim's title control
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each claim's title control in reading order; focusing or activating one scrolls the band to that claim's share of the scroll, so a keyboard reader moves the band exactly as a pointer reader does. There is no key that scrolls the page other than the reader's own — the band never takes the scroll it is given.
- ARIA: the claim list is an `<ol>` (the run is ordered); the open claim's control carries `aria-current="true"`; the progress hairline is `aria-hidden="true"`; the scroll anchors are `aria-hidden="true"`
- Every claim's description stays in the accessibility tree while collapsed (clipped, never `display: none`), so the whole run is readable without scrolling through it
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the muted tone a read claim rests at
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` / `motion-reduce:animate-none` on every animated state; the pin itself is not motion and stays
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: each claim's control spans its whole row

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Illustration from '@aziontech/webkit/illustration'
  import StickyStack from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-stack'

  const scenes = ['ai-applications', 'live-debugging', 'deploy-secure-mcp-server']

  const items = [
    {
      title: 'Automated deployment via Git or CLI',
      description:
        'Push to a branch or run one command; the platform builds the project and puts the result in every location, with the build before it a rollback away.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Infrastructure as code with Terraform',
      description:
        'Declare workloads, rules and domains in the provider and apply them the same way as the rest of your estate, with the same review and the same plan.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Metrics and events via GraphQL API',
      description:
        'Query the same numbers the console charts, from one endpoint, so a dashboard you already run can carry the platform alongside everything else.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <StickyStack :items="items">
    <template #media="{ index }">
      <Illustration :name="scenes[index]" />
    </template>
  </StickyStack>
</template>
```

# Texture Material

> The one decorative surface every band in the system is painted on: a full-bleed, non-interactive layer that tiles a texture behind whatever sits above it. It is a material, not a container — it takes no content and claims no space, so a band composes it into its own backdrop slot and keeps ownership of its layout.

- Import: `import TextureMaterial from '@aziontech/webkit/texture-material'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- In a band's `background` slot (`hero`), where the opening band needs the site's own lattice under its copy.
- Behind a panel, dropzone or slide that would read as empty at a flat fill.
- Anywhere a surface should look like a technical drawing ground without shipping an image.

## Do

- Give the layer a positioned ancestor (`relative`) that also clips it; it fills that box and nothing else.
- Keep the texture behind copy, never over it. `dots` is the quiet default; `lines` is quieter still and reads as ruled paper; `dither` and `pixelate` are loud enough to need their ink dropped or their dense end steered away from the words.
- Do not stack two layers at different pitches — that reads as a moiré, not as a texture.
- Quiet a texture with `--texture-ink` rather than with `opacity`, so the ground keeps showing through at full strength.
- Leave it out when the band already sits inside a `frame-box`; rules plus texture is usually one layer too many.

## Don’t

- To draw the rules between real content cells → use `frame-box`, whose rules are structural.
- For the ruled divider between sections → use `section-gap`, which composes this layer's `lines` kind and owns that treatment.
- For a meaningful image or diagram → use `illustration`.
- As a wrapper around content. The layer is absolutely positioned and paints only itself; content is a sibling above it, inside the positioned ancestor.

## Related

- `hero` — the band whose `background` slot this is composed into.
- `frame-box` — structural rules and corner marks, not decoration.
- `section-gap` — the hatched rhythm band between sections.
- `hero` — the marketing band that paints this texture behind its own copy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'dots' \| 'grid' \| 'lines' \| 'dither' \| 'pixelate' \| 'none'` | `'dots'` | false | Which texture to paint; `none` renders the layer with no texture at all. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'medium'` | false | Pitch of the tiling — how far apart the cells sit. |
| `fade` | `'none' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'right' \| 'edges' \| 'vignette'` | `'none'` | false | Fades the layer out along an axis so it meets content without a hard edge. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind`, `data-size` and `data-fade` mirror their props and drive which texture paints, at what pitch, and how it fades out
- `kind="none"` paints nothing, so a band can switch its texture off without unmounting the layer
- `fade="none"` leaves the layer unmasked; every other value masks it so the ink reaches zero before the layer's own edge; `top` and `bottom` are a single fade — full ink at the leading edge, zero at `--texture-fade-end`; `left` and `right` fade out toward the named edge in the same way, full ink at the opposite edge, which is how a band keeps its texture behind the media and clears it under the copy. Setting `--texture-fade-lead: transparent` adds a second ramp in from zero at the leading edge, so the layer also clears whatever overlaps that edge; `hero` sets it on its backdrop because its opening band sits under the site header, and no other band needs it
- Custom properties tune a texture in place, set from the consumer's class: `--texture-ink` (every kind), `--texture-fade-start` / `--texture-fade-end` (where the fade holds full ink and where it reaches zero), `--texture-fade-lead` (the ink at the leading edge of `top` / `bottom`; `black` by default, `transparent` for the double fade), `--texture-from` / `--texture-to` / `--texture-direction` (the `dither` ramp's density span and axis), `--texture-pool-x` (where both `pixelate` light pools sit on the x axis), `--texture-pool-a` / `--texture-pool-b` (each pool's own `x y` position, so the two can sit on opposite edges; either falls back to `--texture-pool-x`), `--texture-wave-gain` (multiplies the ink of both `pixelate` waves, 1 by default, capped at full ink, so a band can make the motion read over the pools), `--texture-wave-pace` (a whole number of wave periods each loop travels, 1 by default; 2 doubles the speed without changing the animation's duration token)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: not applicable — the layer is decorative and holds no interactive control.
- Keyboard map: none; the layer is `pointer-events-none` and is never in the tab order.
- ARIA: the root carries `aria-hidden="true"`, so no texture is announced and the layer adds no role.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the ink is mixed down from `var(--text-default)` to a surface step, deliberately below text contrast — content above the layer keeps its own colours and its own contrast against the page canvas.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on both pixelate waves; every other kind is static.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, no interactive target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import TextureMaterial from '@aziontech/webkit/texture-material'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative h-80 w-full overflow-hidden bg-(--bg-canvas)">
    <TextureMaterial
      kind="dots"
      size="medium"
      fade="none"
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/texture-material.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/texture-material.md).

# Ticker

> An endlessly looping row of brand marks — the trust strip that names the companies running on the platform, and the stack strip that names the frameworks and clouds a workload already uses. The marks come from the package's own registry and are drawn in one ink, so a strip reads as a list rather than as a dozen competing palettes. The same strip can instead print short claims, each with an optional leading icon, for the benefits line that floors a closing band.

- Import: `import Ticker from '@aziontech/webkit/ticker'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Under a hero, to name the companies a product already serves ("Trusted by mission-critical workloads").
- To state compatibility as a list of framework, cloud and tooling marks ("Your Stack, Your Way").
- Whenever the set of marks is longer than the row that holds it and no single mark has to be read.
- To run a handful of short benefits ("Deploy to 330+ cities instantly") along the floor of a closing band, where each claim restates what the band above already argues.

## Do

- Name marks from the registry rather than passing artwork: the registry is what keeps one company's mark identical on every surface, and a name with no entry still renders as its own wordmark so a strip is never incomplete.
- Let `duration` derive itself. The component holds speed constant rather than duration (two seconds per mark, six per item, since a claim is read and a mark is not), so an eleven-mark strip and a thirty-mark strip advance at the same rate; pass a number only to slow one deliberately.
- Keep `label` to the claim the row makes, not to a heading — the strip sits under a hero, and a second heading competes with the one above it.
- Use `size="small"` only where the strip is the quietest thing on the page, such as the floor of a sign-in column; `medium` is the marketing band and carries its own responsive ladder.
- Keep each `items` label to a short clause with no punctuation to end it, and give every item the same kind of icon; the row repeats, so a claim is read as one of a run, never on its own.
- Never put a call to action, a price or anything else a reader needs inside a strip. It scrolls away, and under `prefers-reduced-motion` it becomes a wrapped grid instead.

## Don’t

- When every mark must be seen → use `logo-wall`, which wraps into a grid and never moves.
- When the reader chooses how far to go through browsable content → use `carousel`, which is user-driven and never advances on its own.
- For a mark a reader must act on, such as a partner directory → the strip is decorative motion, so put linked marks in a `logo-wall`.
- For one mark in its own right (a header lockup, a client story card) → use `brand`.

## Related

- `logo-wall` — the static, wrapping grid of consumer-supplied marks; reach for the strip only when the wall would be too long.
- `carousel` — the user-driven snap scroller; this one moves on its own and holds no essential content.
- `brand` — the Azion lockup, for the product's own mark rather than a third party's.
- `overline` — renders the `label` above the row.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'plain' \| 'band'` | `'plain'` | false | Whether the strip paints its own ground; `band` fills it with the page canvas so a textured hero cannot show through the marks, and the floor still reads continuous with the band above it. |
| `marks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the marks rendered in the row, in order; an unregistered name renders as its own typographic wordmark so the row stays complete. |
| `items` | `TickerItem[]` | `[]` | false | Short claims printed in the row instead of marks, each with its label and an optional leading icon class; when set, `marks` is not rendered. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the row, stating the claim the marks make. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'medium'` | false | Mark scale; `medium` is the marketing band and climbs 32/40/48 px by device class, `small` is a flat 24 px for a column. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds for one full pass; left at `0` it is derived from the number of marks, or of items, so every strip moves at one speed. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the row of marks, announced instead of an unnamed list. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: every mark rests at 70% opacity and lifts to full on `hover`; an item is real text and rests at full ink
- `data-size` mirrors the `size` prop and is what drives the mark height, the cell width and the row gap
- `data-content` is `items` when `items` is set and `marks` otherwise; in `items` mode the cells size to their text, the row gap widens to `--spacing-xxl` (never under twice `--spacing-xl`, so a phone keeps room between claims), and the label steps down to `text-body-sm` under `size="small"`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop; `band` paints the page canvas and the strip's own vertical rhythm so nothing behind it shows through while the fill still matches the band it floors, `plain` leaves it transparent over whatever it sits on
- `data-duplicate` marks every `aria-hidden` copy after the first — the copies the loop translates into place, and the ones hidden outright under reduced motion
- Short rows: the row repeats until half the track is at least as wide as the strip, so a strip with few marks never shows an empty run; the pass lengthens with each repeat so the speed stays the same
- Empty: when `marks` and `items` are both empty the row renders nothing, so a page with no marks to name shows no empty band
- Reduced motion: the track stops and wraps into a centred static grid, with the duplicate rows removed, so every mark stays reachable

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: none of its own — no mark is a focusable target, so the strip adds no tab stop and needs no ring. The loop still pauses on `:focus-within`, so anything a consumer places over it stays still while it is reached.
- Keyboard map: no arrow-key model and no tab stop — this is a list, not a composite widget.
- ARIA: the row is a `<ul>` of `<li>` named by `ariaLabel` when set; every copy after the first carries `aria-hidden="true"` so a screen reader hears each mark once, and each mark is titled with its own name. In `items` mode the labels are the row's text and each icon is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): marks are drawn in `var(--text-default)` at 70%, which WCAG 1.4.11 exempts as a logotype; the typographic fallback is real text and clears the minimum in both themes at that strength. Item labels are real text drawn at full `var(--text-default)`, so their contrast is the ground's to meet, and a strip placed on anything but the canvas or a surface must keep the labels at body size or larger.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the track and `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the mark hover. WCAG 2.2.2 applies — the loop is longer than five seconds, so it pauses on hover and on focus-within, and stops outright under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: marks are not interactive targets; the whole strip is one decorative band.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: the marquee runs toward the start edge in both directions: under `dir="rtl"` the track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Ticker from '@aziontech/webkit/ticker'
</script>

<template>
  <Ticker
    label="Trusted by mission-critical workloads"
    aria-label="Companies running on Azion"
    :marks="[
      'global-fashion-group',
      'herospark',
      'itau',
      'nzn',
      'netshoes',
      'caixa',
      'agibank',
      'prime-video',
      'america-movil',
      'gpa',
      'fourbank'
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/ticker.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/ticker.md).

<!-- components/topic.md -->

# Topic

> One claim stated in three parts: a glyph, a short headline it shares a line with, and a sentence under them that explains it. It is the repeated unit of a marketing claim grid — the content of a cell, not the cell itself, so it carries no surface, no padding and no rules of its own and reads the same dropped into a `card-grid` cell, a `bento-grid` cell, or a column the page lays out by hand. Given an `href` the whole claim becomes the link, and its headline closes on a trailing arrow, so a band of claims needs no separate row of "learn more" controls.

- Import: `import Topic from '@aziontech/webkit/topic'`
- Category: marketing · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For each cell of a "what you get" band: a row of equal claims under a section's headline.
- Inside `CardGrid.Cell` or `BentoGrid.Cell`, where the grid owns the frame and the fill and the topic owns only the copy.
- Whenever a claim is glyph-led and one sentence long, repeated three to six times across a band.

## Do

- Let the cell own the surface. A topic paints no background and adds no padding, so put it inside `CardGrid.Cell` / `BentoGrid.Cell` (or a padded cell the page owns) rather than giving the topic a fill.
- Keep `headingLevel` in step with the page outline: `2` when the band has no headline of its own and these are the first sub-headings under the `h1`, `3` when a `section-title` has already opened the section. The level is the outline; the size is fixed at `heading-xs`.
- Keep the description to one sentence. The glyph carries the recognition, the headline carries the claim, and a second sentence turns a scannable grid into a wall of prose.
- Drop `icon` for a band whose claims are not glyph-led rather than reaching for a decorative glyph that says nothing.
- Give the claim an `href` rather than composing a button under it. A grid of six claims that each close on their own "Learn more" reads as six calls to action instead of six claims, and the button is a second target for the destination the claim already points at.
- A linked claim stretches its link over the nearest positioned ancestor, so the whole cell is the hover and click target, not just the copy. `CardGrid.Cell` and `BentoGrid.Cell` are positioned; a cell the page builds by hand needs `relative`, or every claim in the grid covers the band.

## Don’t

- For a tile with its own border and surface → keep the topic and put it in a `CardGrid.Cell`, which draws the frame and the fill.
- For a claim that carries an eyebrow, a media region or a button → use `media-split`.
- For the headline that opens the whole section → use `section-title`.
- For a measured figure with a unit → use `big-numbers`.
- For a console list row with media and actions → use `item`.

## Related

- `card-grid` — the equal-cell grid a topic is usually repeated in; its `frame` register gives each topic a real `frame-box` cell.
- `bento-grid` — the unequal-cell mosaic, when one claim deserves more room than the rest.
- `section-title` — the headline that opens the band a row of topics sits in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The claim, rendered as the topic's heading. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence explaining the claim; overridden by the default slot. |
| `icon` | `string` | `''` | false | Icon class for the glyph that leads the headline. |
| `href` | `string` | `''` | false | When set, the whole claim renders as an anchor link to this URL and its headline closes on a trailing arrow. |
| `headingLevel` | `TopicHeadingLevel` | `2` | false | Level of the heading element. Keep `2` when the band has no headline of its own; drop it to `3` when a `section-title` has already opened the section, so the document outline stays in order. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Description body; replaces the `description` prop when provided. |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, and `hover` / `focus-visible` when `href` is set
- `data-icon` mirrors whether a glyph is rendered, so a band can style the glyph-less case
- `data-described` mirrors whether a description is rendered, from either the prop or the slot
- `data-linked` present when the claim carries an `href`
- The root element switches between `<a>` and `<div>` on the `href` data prop, never on an `as` string — so the whole claim is the target, not a control composed under it
- A linked root lays an `::after` over its positioned cell, so hovering anywhere in the cell hovers the claim
- The heading element follows `headingLevel`; its size does not change with it

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the linked root draws an inset `focus-visible` ring in `var(--ring-color)` on its `::after`, so the ring outlines the whole cell it covers. Without an `href` the topic holds no interactive control of its own.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the linked claim and `Enter` follows it — the anchor's own behaviour, no handler of our own. Unlinked, the topic is static content and `Tab` passes through whatever the description slot contains.
- ARIA: both glyphs are decorative and carry `aria-hidden="true"` — the leading icon and the trailing arrow — so the link's accessible name is the headline and the sentence, the copy a reader sees. `headingLevel` is what keeps the document outline in order (axe `heading-order`); the heading stays a heading inside the anchor.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): `var(--text-default)` for the heading, `var(--text-muted)` for the description, `var(--primary)` for the glyph and `var(--text-primary)` for the hovered headline — all against the fill the surrounding cell provides.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on both transitions a linked claim carries.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the whole claim is the target, so it is the cell's own height; a topic is never smaller than its heading plus its sentence.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the external-link arrow does not mirror; its hover nudge moves toward the end edge (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Topic from '@aziontech/webkit/topic'
</script>

<template>
  <div class="relative">
    <Topic
      icon="ai ai-edge-nodes"
      title="Consistent global speed"
      description="Serve content and run web apps across hundreds of locations with median latency under 30 ms. No infra to manage."
    />
  </div>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/topic.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/topic.md).

# Breadcrumb

> Shows the page hierarchy so users can navigate back to parent views. Composes `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, and `BreadcrumbSeparator` (chevron). Accepts an `items` array for the common case or slot composition for custom layouts. Reference: PrimeNG Breadcrumb (adapted to Webkit tokens).

- Import: `import BreadcrumbRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A page sits two or more levels deep and the reader needs a way back to its parents (resource detail under a list, a settings sub-page).
- The trail is known as data — pass `items` and let the component render the segments, separators and the collapse below `md`.
- The trail needs a custom layout the `items` array cannot express — compose `Breadcrumb.List`, `Breadcrumb.Item` and `Breadcrumb.Separator` in the default slot.

## Do

- Prefer `items`; only `items` mode collapses the middle segments into an overflow menu below `md`. The default slot renders only when `items` is empty, and a hand-composed trail never collapses.
- Let the last entry be the current page — it is treated as current unless its `current` is set to `false`; give every ancestor an `href`.
- Handle routing in `@navigate`, which receives `(event, href)` for ancestor segments; call `event.preventDefault()` when a client-side router takes over.
- **Vue Router:** a segment has no `to`; put the route's path in `href` (for a named route, `router.resolve(to).href`) and write `@navigate="(event, href) => { event.preventDefault(); router.push(href) }"`. The segment stays a real link, so open-in-new-tab keeps working; leave a modified click (Ctrl, ⌘, Shift, middle button) to the browser.
- In slot mode, wrap each `Breadcrumb.Item` in an `li`: `Breadcrumb.List` is an `ol` and the item renders an `a` / `span`, while `Breadcrumb.Separator` is already an `li`.

## Don’t

- It is the app's primary navigation → use `navigation-menu` or `sidebar` with `menu`.
- It moves between sibling views of the same page → use `tabs`.
- It is the previous / next pair at the end of a docs page → use `doc-pagination`.

## Related

- `breadcrumb-item` — the single segment this component renders; use it alone only inside a hand-composed trail.
- `navigation-menu` — top-level navigation with dropdown panels, not a location trail.
- `link` — a standalone link; a breadcrumb segment is a link with the trail's muted / current styling.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `BreadcrumbItemData[]` | `() => []` | false | Ordered path segments; the last entry is treated as the current page when `current` is omitted on that entry. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `navigate` | `(event: MouseEvent, href: string)` | Fires when an ancestor segment is activated. `event` is the activation event; `href` is the segment's destination. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Custom composition (`BreadcrumbList` + items + separators). Used when `items` is empty. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item`

## Sub-components

- `breadcrumb.vue` — Root `<nav>` with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`.
- `breadcrumb-list.vue` — Ordered list wrapper (`<ol>`) for segments.
- `breadcrumb-item.vue` — Re-exported segment control (same API as `@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item`).
- `breadcrumb-separator.vue` — Decorative chevron between segments (`aria-hidden`).

## States

- Visual states: inherited from `BreadcrumbItem` (default, hover, focus-visible, disabled)
- Last segment in `items` is current when its `current` is not explicitly `false`

#### Responsive contract

- The trail is always a **single row**. A segment wider than the space available shrinks and ellipsizes its label; a trail that still does not fit scrolls horizontally. It never wraps to a second line and never extends past its container.
- **`items` mode** additionally collapses below `md` (768px): first segment, an overflow menu holding the middle segments, then the current segment. The breakpoint is owned by the component's own `use-breadcrumb-collapse` composable.
- **Slot (hand-composed) mode** keeps every segment it was given, since the root cannot know which of the consumer's children are middle segments, so on a narrow screen it degrades through the single-row rules above rather than through a collapse.
- Server render and hydration: the collapse reads the viewport only after mount (`use-breadcrumb-collapse` gates the media query on `useMounted`), so the server HTML and the first client render are the full trail and match; below `md` the collapse applies in the same tick as mount, before paint.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: on each interactive `BreadcrumbItem` segment.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between ancestor links; current page is not in tab order when rendered as `span`.
- ARIA: root `nav` with `aria-label="Breadcrumb"`; list uses `<ol>` / `<li>`; separators are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for labels and chevron.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on segment color transitions.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the separator chevron and any directional item `icon` mirror (`rtl:-scale-x-100`), so the trail reads from the start edge.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: item labels are text; page names in another script keep their own direction.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Breadcrumb from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-root'

  const items = [
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Page Name', href: '#' },
    { label: 'Current Page', current: true }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <Breadcrumb
    :items="items"
    class="max-w-[42.5rem]"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/breadcrumb.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/breadcrumb.md).

<!-- components/breadcrumb-item.md -->

# Breadcrumb Item

> Single segment in a breadcrumb trail. Ancestor segments use muted label text and optional leading icon; the current page uses default text. Hover and focus-visible states match the Webkit navigation pattern (ghost overlay + focus ring).

- Import: `import BreadcrumbItem from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Composing a breadcrumb trail by hand inside `Breadcrumb.List`, one segment per ancestor plus the current page.
- A single ancestor or current-page segment that must match the breadcrumb's muted / current styling and focus ring.

## Do

- Set `current` on the last segment only; it renders a `span` with `aria-current="page"`, drops out of the tab order and ignores `href`.
- Always pass a real `href` on ancestors — it defaults to `'#'`, and the segment renders an `a`.
- Use `show-icon` together with `icon` (a PrimeIcons class, default `pi pi-box`); `icon` alone renders nothing.
- disabled` suppresses the `click` emit and removes the segment from the tab order; prefer omitting an unreachable ancestor over disabling it.

## Don’t

- The whole trail is known as data → use `breadcrumb` with `items`, which renders the segments for you.
- It is a standalone text link in content or a page footer → use `link`.
- It is a navigation row in an app menu → use `menu`.

## Related

- `breadcrumb` — the trail root; renders `breadcrumb-item` for each entry of `items` and re-exports it as `Breadcrumb.Item`.
- `link` — a general-purpose link without the segment's ghost hover and current-page treatment.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `'Page Name'` | false | Visible segment label. |
| `href` | `string` | `'#'` | false | Destination when the segment is a link (ignored when `current` is true). |
| `current` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Marks the current page (last segment); renders as span with `aria-current="page"`. |
| `showIcon` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, renders a leading PrimeIcons icon before the label. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-box'` | false | PrimeIcons class for the leading icon when `showIcon` is true. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `(event: MouseEvent, item: { label: string; href: string })` | Fires when the segment's link is activated (the `current` segment renders a non-interactive `span`). `item` carries the segment's `label` and `href`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-current` mirrors the `current` prop
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses link segments; `Enter` activates.
- ARIA: current segment uses `aria-current="page"`; disabled segments use `aria-disabled="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on color transitions.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on interactive segments (padding + min height).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import BreadcrumbItem from '@aziontech/webkit/breadcrumb-item'
</script>

<template>
  <BreadcrumbItem
    label="Page Name"
    href="#"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/breadcrumb-item.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/breadcrumb-item.md).

<!-- components/dropdown-menu.md -->

# Dropdown Menu

> Overlay menu that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders a list of selectable options grouped into named sections. The root `DropdownMenu` owns open/closed state, positioning, focus return, and keyboard navigation; `DropdownMenu.Trigger` wires `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` onto whatever element the consumer passes through its slot; `DropdownMenu.Group` groups options under an optional label; `DropdownMenu.Option` is the selectable row with left/right/command affordances. Replaces and removes the legacy monolithic input `dropdown` and the previous `dropdown-menu` composition — there is one `DropdownMenu` in the project, in `navigation/`.

- Import: `import DropdownMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import DropdownMenu from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A menu of actions opened from a button: row actions, an account menu, an overflow ("more") menu.
- Options grouped under section labels, optionally with keyboard-shortcut hints.

## Do

- Give every `DropdownMenu.Option` a unique `value` and handle the root `select` event as `(event, value)`. The panel closes and focus returns to the trigger on its own.
- selected` is a display flag. The dropdown never sets it, so derive it from your own state.
- Use the `command` prop or the `right` slot on an option, not both. A `command` shortcut is live only while the panel is open.
- Add a `label` to each `DropdownMenu.Group` when there is more than one group. Put search in the root `top` slot and footer actions in `bottom`; those regions stay outside the scrolling list.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- Choosing a value that a form submits → use `select` (inside a `field` for a label).
- A primary action joined to a menu of alternatives → use `split-button`.
- A searchable palette of commands → use `command`.
- Free-form or interactive content such as forms or filters → use `popover`.
- Vertical application navigation → use `menu`.

## Related

- `split-button` — composes `DropdownMenu` for its chevron menu.
- `select` — form control with a field trigger and a bound value.
- `popover` — same trigger and anchoring model, with free-form content instead of option rows.
- `command` — modal ⌘K palette with search and filtering.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `'auto' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-end' \| 'top-start' \| 'top-end'` | `'bottom-start'` | false | Where the panel opens relative to the trigger. `'auto'` picks the best-fitting corner at open time based on viewport space. |
| `offset` | `number` | `4` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: DropdownMenuOptionValue)` | Fires when an enabled option is activated (click, `Enter`/`Space`, or a `command` shortcut). `event` is the activation event; `value` is the activated option's identifier. The panel closes automatically and focus returns to the trigger when activated from inside the open panel. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<DropdownMenu.Trigger>` followed by one or more `<DropdownMenu.Group>`. |
| `top` | — | Sticky region rendered above the scrollable group list (e.g. search input). |
| `bottom` | — | Sticky region rendered below the scrollable group list (e.g. footer action). |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-option`

## Sub-components

- `dropdown-menu-trigger/dropdown-menu-trigger.vue` — as-child trigger.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the consumer's trigger element. The trigger forwards aria + click; the consumer must not bind those props itself.
- `dropdown-menu-group/dropdown-menu-group.vue` — labeled section.
  - Props: `label: string` default `''` — section label rendered above the options. Omit for an unlabeled group.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<DropdownMenu.Option>`; `top` — inline region rendered between the group label and the options (e.g. a per-section search or description); `bottom` — inline region rendered after the options (e.g. a "see all" link).
- `dropdown-menu-option/dropdown-menu-option.vue` — selectable row.
  - Props:
    - `value: string | number` (required) — identifier emitted on the root `select` event when this option is activated.
    - `label: string` default `''` — plain-text label; falls back to the default slot when omitted.
    - `command: string` default `''` — keyboard-shortcut hint rendered on the right side (e.g. `'⌘P'`, `'⇧⌘P'`, `'Ctrl+,'`). While the panel is open the root listens for `window` `keydown`, matches the shortcut against every mounted option, and emits `select` for the matching option (preventing the browser default). Shortcuts are active only while the panel is open, since options are only mounted then. Mutually exclusive with the `right` slot.
    - `disabled: boolean` default `false` — disables interaction and applies disabled tokens.
    - `selected: boolean` default `false` — marks the option as currently selected (background + checkmark).
  - Events: _none_ (root emits `select`).
  - Slots: `default` (override of the `label` prop, for rich label content), `left` (left icon / avatar), `right` (right icon / badge; mutually exclusive with `command`).

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, option activation, `Esc`, outside click). While unbound the menu is uncontrolled and starts closed. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`, `selected`
- `data-state` values (root + trigger): `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root, trigger, and option
- `data-selected` on option mirrors the `selected` prop
- `data-placement` on the root mirrors the `placement` prop (`'auto'` stays as `'auto'`)
- `data-placement` on the panel mirrors the resolved placement (`'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end'`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on trigger and option.
- Keyboard map:
  - On the trigger: `Enter` / `Space` opens the panel and focuses the first enabled option; `Down` opens and focuses the first option; `Up` opens and focuses the last option.
  - Inside the panel: `Down` / `Up` move between enabled options (wrap-around); `Home` / `End` jump to first/last enabled option; `Enter` / `Space` activate the focused option; `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger; `Tab` closes the panel and lets focus proceed to the next focusable element after the trigger; `Shift+Tab` closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Typing in a search field inside the top slot keeps `Home` / `End` for the caret. Tests: `dropdown-menu.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: the slotted control (or the wrapper, when the slot has none) exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, with a single tab stop; the panel's `aria-labelledby` follows the control's `id`; the `role="menu"` element wraps only the groups and options, and the optional top and bottom slots (search fields, footers with buttons) sit beside it inside the floating panel, because a `menu` may own only menu items, groups and separators (`aria-required-children`); each group uses `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` pointing at its label id (when `label` is set); each option uses `role="menuitem"`, `aria-disabled` mirrors `disabled`; selected option uses `aria-current="true"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state (validated via `--text-disabled` token).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on `transition-colors` for hover/selected states.
- Teleported panel: the `role="menu"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it lays out and is announced in the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger; option rows are 32 px tall and are activated by full-row click + keyboard, satisfying the 24×24 px target floor for in-menu items per WCAG 2.5.8.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import DropdownMenuGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-group'
  import DropdownMenuOption from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-option'
  import DropdownMenuRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-root'
  import DropdownMenuTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/dropdown-menu-trigger'
  import IconButton from '@aziontech/webkit/icon-button'
</script>

<template>
  <DropdownMenuRoot>
    <DropdownMenuTrigger>
      <IconButton
        kind="outlined"
        icon="pi pi-plus"
        aria-label="Open menu"
      />
    </DropdownMenuTrigger>
    <DropdownMenuGroup>
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="profile"
        label="Profile"
      />
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="settings"
        label="Settings"
      />
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="billing"
        label="Billing"
      />
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="invite"
        label="Invite members"
      />
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="logs"
        label="Audit log"
      />
      <DropdownMenuOption
        value="signout"
        label="Sign out"
      />
    </DropdownMenuGroup>
  </DropdownMenuRoot>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/dropdown-menu.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/dropdown-menu.md).

<!-- components/link.md -->

# Link

> Helps users move between views or sections. Migrated from the existing implementation at `packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/link/`. Design source: [Webkit — Link](https://www.figma.com/design/t97pXRs7xME3SJDs5iZ5RF/Webkit?node-id=3548-578) (`Size` × `State` variants; hover handled in CSS).

- Import: `import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A standalone navigation link: a domain, a repository, a docs page, "View all".
- An in-console navigation action ("Add custom domain") with `showIcon` set to false.

## Do

- Always set `href` and a `label` that names the destination; the defaults (`'#'`, `'Learn more'`) are placeholders.
- Keep the default `pi pi-external-link` icon for off-site targets with `target="_blank"` (`rel="noopener noreferrer"` is added for you); turn `showIcon` off for in-app destinations.
- Match `size` to the controls around it; heights follow `button` (40 / 32 / 28 px).
- disabled` drops it from the tab order and suppresses `click`; hide a link that can never be followed instead.

## Don’t

- A link inside a sentence → use a plain anchor with the text-link class.
- An action that changes something instead of navigating → use `button`.
- A compact marketing CTA with a brand-colored icon inside a card → use `mini-button`.

## Related

- `mini-button` — same anatomy in default text color with a brand-colored icon; `large` and `medium` only.
- `button` — set `href` when a link must look like a button.
- `breadcrumb` — a trail of links for hierarchical location.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | false | Visible label rendered inside the link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Learn more`). |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `'large'` | false | Size token; affects height and typography (large 40px, medium 32px, small 28px), matching Button. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens. |
| `showIcon` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, renders the trailing icon. |
| `icon` | `string` | `'pi pi-external-link'` | false | PrimeIcons class for the trailing icon. |
| `href` | `string` | `'#'` | false | Destination URL for the anchor. |
| `target` | `'_blank' \| '_self'` | `'_self'` | false | Link target when navigating. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `click` | `MouseEvent` | — |

## Assets

- Icons: every valid name is in icons.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "icons" })`). An unknown class renders nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `hover` and `focus-visible` underline the label (`underline-offset-4`); there is no surface behind the link
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter` activates.
- ARIA: `aria-disabled` and `tabindex="-1"` when disabled.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: a directional glyph passed to `icon` (chevrons, angles, arrows, carets, `sign-in`/`sign-out`, `reply`, `undo`: the list in `utils/directional-icons.ts`) gets `rtl:-scale-x-100`; external-link arrows, media and brand glyphs do not mirror.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: a URL printed as the link text is the consumer's; wrap it in `dir="ltr"` when it sits inside right-to-left prose.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Link from '@aziontech/webkit/link'
</script>

<template>
  <Link
    label="Learn more"
    size="large"
    href="#"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/link.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/link.md).
