<!-- components/wizard.md -->

# Wizard

> A multi-step create flow in one surface. It puts the step rail on the start side, the current step's header and fields in the content column, and a fixed footer with Cancel, Previous and Next. On the last step, Next becomes the submit action. It owns the order, which steps can be reached and where focus goes. The consumer owns the fields, the validation and the request. It differs from its siblings by owning the **whole flow**. `stepper` is only the rail and leaves layout, actions and gating to the caller. `tabs` switches between peer views that have no order and no completion.

- Import: `import WizardRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Wizard from '@aziontech/webkit/wizard'`
- Category: navigation · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Creating a resource takes several ordered decisions, and showing them all at once would overwhelm the
- The reader has to finish a step before moving on. Validation runs on Next and can stop the move.
- The flow needs a review step before the final submit, and earlier steps must stay reachable to fix

## Do

- Keep step state in the consumer (refs or a form store). Only the active step renders its content, so a
- Validate in the `next` handler and call `event.preventDefault()` synchronously to block the move. For
- Show why Next was blocked inside the step (an inline `message` or the field's `invalid` +
- Give every step a title that names the decision (`Settings`, `Review`) and keep it short. The same
- Make the last step a review of the answers when the resource is costly to change after creation, and
- Bind `loading` to the submit request. It disables Cancel, Previous and the rail, so the handler needs no
- Mark a step `optional` only when Next works with every field in it empty.
- Always pass `ariaLabel` naming the task (`Create edge application`). Without it, the root is an
- The wizard sets no page width. Place it inside the page's create container

## Don’t

- A short form that fits one screen. A wizard adds clicks without adding clarity → use a plain form
- A confirmation or a single decision → use `dialog`.
- Peer views with no order and no completion → use `tabs`.
- A custom multi-step layout where the caller needs its own actions or a different arrangement → compose
- Numbered instructions inside documentation → use `doc-steps` + `doc-step`.

## Related

- `stepper` — the rail this component composes. Reach for it alone when the footer and gating must be
- `tabs` — unordered peer views with no completion state.
- `dialog` — a single, short decision on an overlay.
- `drawer` — a single-step create or edit form beside the page.
- message` — the inline error to show inside a step when Next is blocked.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the primary action on the last step, where Next becomes the submit action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Create`). |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Submit in progress: the primary action shows its loading state, and Cancel, Previous and every rail step are disabled. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name for the wizard region. Name the task, for example Create edge application. |
| `activeStep` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:activeStep`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next` | `(event: MouseEvent, step: number)` | Fired when Next is activated on any step but the last, **before** the wizard advances. `step` is the zero-based index of the step being left, which is the one to validate. Cancelable: if a handler calls `event.preventDefault()` synchronously, the wizard stays on `step`. Otherwise it writes `step + 1` to `activeStep`. Not fired by Previous or by rail jumps, which only go back. |
| `submit` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Fired when the primary action is activated on the last step. The wizard changes no state. The consumer starts the request and binds `loading`. Not fired while `loading`. |
| `cancel` | `(event: MouseEvent)` | Fired when Cancel is activated. The wizard changes no state, and the consumer decides where to go. Not fired while `loading`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The `Wizard.Step` children, in the order they are numbered and navigated. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/wizard-step`

## Sub-components

The root ships a **compound API**. An `index.ts` beside `wizard.vue` attaches the sub-component to the
root, so `<Wizard.Step>` resolves from one import. The standalone imports remain the tree-shaking path.
The wizard has no open/closed state, so it has no `Trigger` / `Content`. The anatomy name is `Step`,
because that is what the part is.

Shared state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`injection-key.ts` +
`composables/use-wizard-context.ts`), so the consumer wires nothing. The root provides a context with
the ordered step registry, the active index, the total, `loading`, and the functions `register`,
`attach` and `unregister`. `useWizardContext()` throws a clear error when a `Wizard.Step` is rendered
outside a `<Wizard>`. Steps are ordered by document position (the same `compareDocumentPosition`
approach `stepper` uses), not by mount order, so a step inserted later still numbers correctly.

The root composes, and does not re-implement:

- `Stepper` + `Stepper.Step` (`@aziontech/webkit/stepper`) for the rail.
  `Stepper.Step` per registered `Wizard.Step` and passes:
  - `value` = `String(index)`.
  - `title` = the step's `title`.
  - `state` = `'complete'` for every step before the active one, otherwise `'upcoming'`. The rail
    derives `current` itself.
  - `disabled` = `true` for every step after the active one, and for every step while `loading`.

  An `optional` step shows the word `Optional` in the `Stepper.Step` default slot. The rail's `v-model`
  is the active index as a string, and a rail activation writes `Number(value)` back to `activeStep`.

- `Button` (`@aziontech/webkit/button`) for the three footer actions, all at the house default size
  (`large`, 40px):
  - Cancel is `kind="transparent"`, at the start of the footer.
  - Previous is `kind="secondary"`, at the end. It is not rendered (`v-if`, not hidden) on step 1.
  - Next is `kind="primary"`, at the end. On the last step its label becomes `submitLabel`, it emits
    `submit` instead of `next`, and it carries `loading`.

- `wizard-step/wizard-step.vue` — one step: its header and its content.
  root on mount and reads back its zero-based index, the total, and whether it is the active step. It
  always renders its own root (a `<div role="group">` labelled by its heading), so document-order
  registration works. When inactive, that root is `hidden` and its content is not mounted (`v-if`).
  When active, it renders:
  - The header: the counter `Step {n} of {N}` as an overline paragraph with an id from `useId()`.
  - The title as an `<h2 tabindex="-1">` with `aria-describedby` pointing at the counter, followed by
    `Optional` when `optional` is set.
  - The `description` paragraph, only when non-empty.
  - Below the header, the default slot inside a `<Transition>` that fades it in.
  - When it becomes active after the initial render, it moves focus to its heading.
  - Props: `title?: string` (default `''` — what this step decides, in the reader's words; shown in the
    rail and as the step heading), `description?: string` (default `''` — one line under the heading
    saying what the step is for; omitted when empty), `optional?: boolean` (default `false` — marks the
    step as skippable: shows `Optional` beside the title in the rail and in the header).
  - Slot: `default` — the step's content (fields, review summary).
  - `data-testid` fallback: `navigation-wizard-step` (consumer `data-testid` wins).

Resulting layout (no per-component `package.json`; the root `packages/webkit/package.json#exports`
resolves every path, and `.d.ts` is generated at publish time):

```
packages/webkit/src/components/navigation/wizard/
├── wizard.vue                   (root; owns the model, provides the registry, renders rail + footer)
├── wizard.test.ts
├── index.ts                     (compound: attaches Step to the root)
├── injection-key.ts             (shared WizardContext)
├── composables/
│   └── use-wizard-context.ts    (injects; throws outside a Wizard)
└── wizard-step/
    └── wizard-step.vue
```

Exports to add to `packages/webkit/package.json#exports` (flat public names; category lives in the
folder only):

```jsonc
"./wizard": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/index.ts",
"./wizard-root": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/wizard.vue",
"./wizard-step": "./src/components/navigation/wizard/wizard-step/wizard-step.vue"
```

## v-model

| Model                | Type     | Default | Emits               | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:activeStep` | `number` | `0`     | `update:activeStep` | Zero-based index of the step on screen, two-way through `defineModel('activeStep', { default: 0 })`. Written by Next (after an un-prevented `next`), by Previous (index − 1) and by a rail jump to an earlier step. Rendering clamps an out-of-range value to `0 … N − 1` without emitting. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `loading`. Interactive states (`hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`,
  `disabled`) belong to the composed `Button` and `Stepper.Step`, not to the wizard's own elements.
- `data-loading` on the root mirrors `loading`.
- `data-active-step` on the root mirrors the clamped `activeStep`.
- `data-active` on `Wizard.Step` is present only on the step on screen.
- `data-optional` on `Wizard.Step` mirrors `optional`.
- Rail step statuses come from `Stepper.Step`. Every step before the active one is `complete`, the
  active one is `current` (derived by the rail), and every step after it is `upcoming` + `disabled`.
- No `data-state`: the wizard has no open/closed state.

State matrix:

| State        | Trigger                               | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| first step   | `activeStep === 0`                    | Previous is not rendered. The footer shows Cancel at the start and Next at the end.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| middle step  | `0 < activeStep < N − 1`              | Cancel, Previous and Next.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| last step    | `activeStep === N − 1`                | The primary action reads `submitLabel` and emits `submit`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| single step  | `N === 1`                             | Previous is not rendered, and the primary action is the submit action from the start.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| loading      | `loading`                             | The primary `Button` gets `loading` (spinner + `aria-busy`, click suppressed). Cancel and Previous are `disabled`, and every `Stepper.Step` is `disabled`.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| next blocked | `next` handler calls `preventDefault` | The wizard stays on the step. The consumer renders the reason inside the step's slot.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| narrow box   | wizard box under `@2xl`               | The rail is not displayed (`@max-2xl/wizard:hidden`). The root shows its own `Step n of N` progress line (`wizard.stepOf`, `aria-live="polite"`, `data-testid="<testid>__progress"`) at the top of the content column in place of the step header's overline, which hides at that width; the step title follows it and the footer stays below. |

Layout from `@2xl` of the wizard's own box (`@container/wizard`, so a wizard in a drawer or split view follows that box): a row with the rail column (`@2xl/wizard:w-(--container-3xs) @2xl/wizard:shrink-0`) on the start
side and the content column (`min-w-0 flex-1`) beside it. The content column stacks the active step,
then the footer. The footer is a row with Cancel at the start and Previous + Next grouped at the end,
separated from the content by a top border.

- Server render and hydration: steps register from their own setup, after the root has rendered, so until mount the root does not use the step count. The step shown, `data-active-step` and Previous follow the requested `activeStep` (clamped at 0), and the primary action reads Next; on mount the index is clamped to the registered steps and the last step reads the submit label. The server HTML and the first client render therefore match.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every focusable control is a composed `Button` or `Stepper.Step` and carries their
  ring: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2
focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`. The step heading is a programmatic focus target
  (`tabindex="-1"`), not a control, so it is out of the Tab order and draws no ring.
- Keyboard map:
  - `Tab` order: the enabled rail steps (those before the active one), then the step content, then the
    footer (Cancel, Previous, Next/submit).
  - `Enter` / `Space` on an earlier rail step jumps back to it.
  - `Enter` / `Space` on a footer button activates it.
  - Disabled rail steps and actions are skipped by `Tab`.
  - On every step change after the initial render, focus moves to the new step's heading, so the screen
    reader announces the title and the counter. The initial render does not steal focus.
  - No `Escape` binding: the wizard is not an overlay.
- ARIA:
  - The root is a `<section>` with `aria-label` from `ariaLabel` (omitted when empty).
  - The rail is the `Stepper` `<nav aria-label="Steps">`, with `aria-current="step"` on the active step.
  - Each `Wizard.Step` is a `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading. The heading
    has `aria-describedby` pointing at the `Step n of N` counter (ids from `useId()`).
  - Inactive steps are `hidden`, so they are out of the accessibility tree.
  - While `loading`, the primary `Button` sets `aria-busy`, and the other actions are natively
    `disabled`.
  - The narrow-box progress line is a polite live region (`aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`):
    when the rail is hidden, a step change is also announced as `Step n of N` after the heading. At
    `@2xl` and wider the line is `display: none`, so the live region is silent and the rail carries
    the progress. The initial render announces nothing (the region only reads changes).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including the disabled actions while `loading`
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the step-content transition; the composed parts carry their own
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the footer buttons are `large` (40px), and the rail steps are full-width rows
  at least 40px tall (owned by `Stepper.Step`)

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: none.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: step titles are the consumer's text; the "Step n of N" line comes from the locale catalog.

<!-- components/command.md -->

# Command

> Command Menu is a ⌘K command palette: a modal overlay with a search input and a filtered, keyboard-navigable list of actions. It wraps the `Dialog` primitive for its panel, backdrop, focus trap, scroll-lock, and Escape handling, and adds the palette chrome on top — a search `Input`, a scrollable `List` of `Item`s organized into optional `Group`s, an `Empty` state, and `Separator`s. The root owns open/closed state (controlled or uncontrolled), a global open shortcut (⌘K / Ctrl+K), the substring filter, and roving active-item navigation. It differs from `dropdown` (a small trigger-anchored menu) and `select` (a form value picker): Command Menu is a full-screen search-first launcher for actions, not a positioned menu or an input control.

- Import: `import CommandRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/command-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Command from '@aziontech/webkit/command'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Provide a global ⌘K launcher for navigating to pages or running actions across an app.
- Let users filter a large, grouped list of commands by typing, then activate with the keyboard.

## Do

- Write items as Title Case verb phrases describing an action ("Deploy Project"), not navigation labels.
- Keep the palette controlled via `v-model:open` so the app can open it from a button and from the global ⌘K shortcut.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.
- Group related actions with `<Command.Group heading="…">` and separate distinct sections with `<Command.Separator>`.

## Don’t

- A small menu anchored to a trigger button → use `dropdown`.
- Picking a value for a form field → use `select` / `multi-select`.
- A confirmation or content modal without search/list semantics → use `dialog` directly.

## Related

- `dialog` — the overlay primitive Command Menu wraps for panel, backdrop, focus trap, and Escape.
- `kbd` — renders each item's keyboard-shortcut hint and the ⌘K affordance.
- dropdown` — trigger-anchored menu; reach for it when the list is short and positioned by a trigger.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, backdrop click and Escape close the palette. |
| `shortcut` | `string` | `'meta+k'` | false | Global `'+'`-delimited keyboard shortcut that toggles the palette open (e.g. `'meta+k'`); matched against Ctrl on non-macOS platforms. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, value: string \| number)` | Fires when an enabled item is activated (click or `Enter`). `event` is the activation event; `value` is the item's identifier. The palette closes automatically and focus returns to the element that was focused before opening. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The palette content: a `<Command.Input>` followed by a `<Command.List>`. Rendered inside the teleported dialog panel. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/command-input`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-list`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-group`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-item`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-empty`
- `@aziontech/webkit/command-separator`

## Sub-components

The root ships a compound API via `index.ts` (`Object.assign` attaches every sub-component; vue-tsc emits `index.d.ts`). Root binding is PascalCase `Command`. Folder layout, one folder per part:

```
packages/webkit/src/components/overlay/command/
├── command.vue          (root — wraps Dialog, provides context)
├── index.ts                  (compound Object.assign)
├── injection-key.ts          (CommandContext + useCommandMenuContext())
├── command.test.ts
├── command-input/command-input.vue
├── command-list/command-list.vue
├── command-group/command-group.vue
├── command-item/command-item.vue
├── command-empty/command-empty.vue
└── command-separator/command-separator.vue
```

- `command-input/command-input.vue` — the search field.
  - Props: `placeholder: string` default `''` — input placeholder text; empty uses the locale catalog (`Search everything` in English). `ariaLabel: string` default `''` — accessible name for the search field; when empty it falls back to `placeholder`, so the field keeps its name after the placeholder disappears on the first keystroke.
  - Events: _none_ (the query lives in the injected context).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `command-list/command-list.vue` — the scrollable results region.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<Command.Group>` / `<Command.Item>` / `<Command.Separator>`, plus an optional `<Command.Empty>`.
- `command-group/command-group.vue` — labeled section.
  - Props: `heading: string` default `''` — section label; omit for an unlabeled group.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — one or more `<Command.Item>`.
- `command-item/command-item.vue` — a selectable command row.
  - Props:
    - `value: string | number` (required) — identifier emitted on the root `select` event when the item is activated; also part of the searchable text.
    - `disabled: boolean` default `false` — disables interaction and applies disabled tokens; the item is skipped by roving navigation and never activates.
    - `shortcut: string` default `''` — a `'+'`-delimited shortcut hint (e.g. `'meta+d'`, `'meta+shift+p'`, `'esc'`) rendered on the right via `Kbd`. Modifier tokens (`meta`/`ctrl`/`shift`/`alt`) map to `Kbd` modifier props; the final token is the key. A named final token (`esc`/`escape`, `enter`/`return`, `space`, `tab`, `backspace`, `delete`/`del`) is printed from the locale catalog through `Kbd` `key-name` (`Esc`, `Enter`, `Espaço`…); any other key is upper-cased. Display only — it does not register a global keybinding.
  - Events: _none_ (root emits `select`).
  - Slots: `default` — the item label (rich content allowed); `prefix` — leading icon/avatar; `suffix` — trailing content (mutually exclusive with `shortcut`).
  - **The icon box belongs to the item that has an icon.** An item renders the leading box only when it actually supplies a `prefix`; an icon-less item puts no empty element in the DOM and pays no indent, so a list that mixes iconed and icon-less rows lets each label start at the row inset it earns rather than every label inheriting the widest row's indent. The box is a fixed `size-4` — the same glyph size a `Menu` row uses — so an oversized icon cannot widen the row and pull its own label out of line with the iconed rows around it.
- `command-empty/command-empty.vue` — the no-results state, shown only when the filter produces zero visible items.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the empty-state message (falls back to "No results found." when empty).
- `command-separator/command-separator.vue` — a thin divider between sections.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: _none_.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, the `shortcut`, item activation, `Esc`, backdrop click). While unbound the palette is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active` (roving highlight), `disabled`, `empty`
- `data-state` values (root): `open` | `closed` (inherited from the wrapped `Dialog`)
- `data-active` on an item mirrors the roving active item (keyboard/hover highlight)
- `data-disabled` on an item mirrors its `disabled` prop
- `empty`: when the filter yields no visible items, the `Empty` part renders in place of the list rows

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the input; items use the roving `data-active` highlight (the input keeps DOM focus).
- Keyboard map:
  - Global: the `shortcut` combo (⌘K / Ctrl+K) toggles the palette open from anywhere.
  - Inside the palette: `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` move the active item (skipping disabled, wrap-around); `Home` / `End` jump to first/last enabled item; `Enter` activates the active item; `Esc` closes (via `Dialog`); `Tab` is trapped within the panel (via `Dialog`).
- ARIA: the panel is `role="dialog"` (from `Dialog`) with an accessible name via a visually-hidden title; the input is `role="combobox"` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the list, and carries its own accessible name via `aria-label` (`ariaLabel`, falling back to `placeholder`) so the name survives the first keystroke; the list is `role="listbox"` (no role while nothing matches); each group is `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` referencing its heading id; each item is `role="option"` with `aria-selected` mirroring the active state and `aria-disabled` mirroring `disabled`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled state (validated via `--text-disabled`).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the inherited `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on item `transition-colors`.
- Focus management: opening moves focus to the input; closing returns focus to the element focused before the palette opened. Focus trap and scroll-lock are inherited from `Dialog`.
- Touch target: item rows are full-width click targets ≥32 px tall, satisfying the in-overlay 24×24 px floor (WCAG 2.5.8).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CommandGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/command-group'
  import CommandInput from '@aziontech/webkit/command-input'
  import CommandItem from '@aziontech/webkit/command-item'
  import CommandList from '@aziontech/webkit/command-list'
  import CommandRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/command-root'
  import CommandSeparator from '@aziontech/webkit/command-separator'
  import SearchTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/search-trigger'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <SearchTrigger @open="open = true" />

  <CommandRoot
    v-model:open="open"
    shortcut="meta+k"
  >
    <CommandInput placeholder="Search commands…" />
    <CommandList>
      <CommandGroup heading="Suggestions">
        <CommandItem value="deploy">Deploy Project</CommandItem>
        <CommandItem value="new-app">Create Application</CommandItem>
        <CommandItem value="settings">Go to Settings</CommandItem>
      </CommandGroup>
      <CommandSeparator />
      <CommandGroup heading="Commands">
        <CommandItem
          value="search"
          shortcut="meta+k"
          >Search everything</CommandItem
        >
        <CommandItem
          value="new-app-cmd"
          shortcut="meta+n"
          >New Application</CommandItem
        >
        <CommandItem
          value="toggle-theme"
          shortcut="meta+shift+l"
          >Toggle Theme</CommandItem
        >
      </CommandGroup>
    </CommandList>
  </CommandRoot>
</template>
```

<!-- components/confirm-dialog.md -->

# Confirm Dialog

> A small confirmation dialog: a title with a close button, one sentence of description, and a Cancel plus a confirm button whose `kind` says how destructive the outcome is (`danger` for a removal or a discard, `primary` for a commit). The unsaved-changes guard uses the same shell; the `actions` slot replaces the two buttons when the guard can also save. Built from `Dialog`, `Panel` parts and `Button`.

- Import: `import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Before a removal (Remove domain, Delete resource) or a re-run (Clear again).
- When someone leaves a form with unsaved changes.
- A deletion that needs typed confirmation: put the field in the default slot and set `disabled` until it matches.

## Do

- The confirm label repeats the verb of the title (Remove Domain, Discard changes), never OK or Yes.
- kind="danger"` only when the outcome removes or discards something; a commit is `primary`.
- Close the dialog from `@confirm` once the action has run; keep it open with `loading` while it runs.
- Below `md` the buttons stack full width with the confirm button on top, the same order as `save-bar`.

## Don’t

- A form of several fields → use `dialog` with your own body.
- A non-blocking notice → use `toast` or `alert`.
- A settings save that needs no decision → use `save-bar`.

## Related

- `dialog` — the overlay it composes; use it directly for anything that is not a yes-or-no decision.
- `button` — the trigger and the actions.
- `save-bar` — the unsaved-changes bar this dialog guards.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `—` | true | The question or the outcome, as the dialog title. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One sentence that says what happens on confirm. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the confirm button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Confirm`). |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the cancel button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Cancel`). |
| `kind` | `'danger' \| 'primary'` | `'danger'` | false | Kind of the confirm button. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'medium'` | `'small'` | false | Width of the dialog. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Shows a spinner on the confirm button while the action runs; Cancel, the close button, `Esc` and the overlay stop closing the dialog until it clears. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables the confirm button, for a confirmation that needs input first. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `confirm` | `void` | The confirm button was activated; not emitted while `disabled` or `loading`. |
| `cancel` | `void` | The cancel button was activated; the dialog closes. Not emitted while `loading`. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | — | The control that opens the dialog. |
| `default` | — | Body content under the description: a field, an alert. |
| `actions` | { close: () => void } | Replaces the Cancel and confirm buttons; receives a close function. |

## v-model

- **`v-model:open`** — `boolean`, default `false`. Whether the dialog is open; the trigger, the close button, `Esc` and Cancel update it. While `loading`, only the consumer closes it (set `open` to `false` from `@confirm` once the action settles).

## States

- Visual states: `closed`, `open`
- `data-state` on the root: `open` | `closed` (from `dialog`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the buttons and `dialog`.
- Keyboard map: `Esc` closes; `Tab` is trapped in the dialog and focus returns to the trigger on close (from `dialog`).
- ARIA: the dialog is named by its title and described by its description (`DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1, owned by the composed parts.

## Examples

### Confirm

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <ConfirmDialog
    v-model:open="open"
    title="Remove domain"
    description="shop.example.com stops answering for this resource once you save. Traffic already pointed at it gets no response."
    confirm-label="Remove Domain"
    @confirm="open = false"
  >
    <template #trigger>
      <Button
        label="Remove domain"
        kind="outlined"
        size="medium"
      />
    </template>
  </ConfirmDialog>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/confirm-dialog.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/confirm-dialog.md).

<!-- components/dialog.md -->

# Dialog

> Modal surface above the page, built on the shared Panel shell. The consumer composes a trigger, an overlay backdrop and the panel regions (header, body, footer); the body is the only region that scrolls. Below `md` it renders as a full-width bottom sheet.

- Import: `import Dialog from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A focused, blocking modal task or confirmation that should sit centered over the page and trap focus.
- The interaction must be completed or dismissed before returning to the page.

## Do

- Trap focus, restore it on close, and close on Escape and overlay click.
- One clear primary action; keep the body scannable.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- The content is a side panel, long form, or navigation that should slide from an edge → use `drawer`.
- It is small contextual content anchored to a trigger (a menu, info bubble, picker) → use a popover / `dropdown`.

## Related

- `drawer` — edge-anchored panel for secondary tasks / long content.
- dropdown` — trigger-anchored menu for actions/options.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, overlay click and Escape close the dialog. |
| `size` | `DialogSize` | `'medium'` | false | Panel max-width preset passed to the inner Panel. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-overlay`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-portal`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/dialog-trigger`

## Sub-components

- `dialog-close.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-close`.
- `dialog-content.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-content`.
- `dialog-description.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-description`.
- `dialog-overlay.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-overlay`.
- `dialog-portal.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-portal`.
- `dialog-title.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-title`.
- `dialog-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `dialog-trigger`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (trigger, `Dialog.Close`, `Esc`, overlay click). While unbound the dialog is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)

#### Mobile sheet, height and scroll

- Below `md` the dialog is a bottom sheet, capped at 80% of the **visible** viewport (`dvh`, not `vh`: on mobile browsers `vh` is the largest viewport with the toolbars retracted, so a `vh` sheet can extend under the URL bar with its footer off-screen).
- Exactly one element caps the sheet (the panel) and exactly one element scrolls (`panel-content`), so the title and footer actions stay reachable while the body scrolls. The motion wrapper only positions and animates; it declares no cap and no scroll of its own.
- The page behind the overlay is scroll-locked while the dialog is open, and the lock is released on close.
- Phones: below `md` the panel is a bottom sheet (full width, 80 dvh); below `sm` it becomes a full-height, full-width sheet (`h-dvh`, no radius, no border). The `PanelFooter` stays pinned under the scrolling content, its direct children stretch to equal widths and it keeps `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` clear.
- Server render and hydration: the phone layout reads the viewport only after mount (`use-overlay-mobile` gates the media query on `useMounted`), so a dialog rendered open on the server hydrates with the desktop layout and switches to the bottom sheet in the same tick as mount, before paint.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the dialog and moves focus to its first focusable control. Focus is trapped: `Tab` on the last control wraps to the first and `Shift+Tab` on the first wraps to the last. `Escape` closes it (unless the consumer blocks dismissal) and focus returns to the trigger; when the dialog was opened without a `Dialog.Trigger` (controlled `v-model:open`), focus returns to whatever element held it when the dialog opened. Tests: `dialog.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Teleported content: the portal wraps its content (overlay and panel) in a `display: contents` element that binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Dialog from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog'
  import DialogClose from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-close'
  import DialogContent from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-content'
  import DialogDescription from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-description'
  import DialogOverlay from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-overlay'
  import DialogPortal from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-portal'
  import DialogTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-title'
  import DialogTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/dialog-trigger'
  import PanelContent from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-content'
  import PanelFooter from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-footer'
  import PanelHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-header'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    dismissible
    size="medium"
  >
    <DialogTrigger>
      <Button
        label="Open dialog"
        kind="primary"
      />
    </DialogTrigger>
    <DialogPortal>
      <DialogOverlay />
      <DialogContent>
        <PanelHeader class="w-full">
          <DialogTitle>Dialog Title</DialogTitle>
          <DialogClose />
        </PanelHeader>
        <PanelContent>
          <DialogDescription>
            Modal content. Uses the shared Panel header, body, and footer regions.
          </DialogDescription>
        </PanelContent>
        <PanelFooter>
          <div class="flex w-full flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm) md:flex-row md:justify-end">
            <Button
              label="Cancel"
              kind="outlined"
              @click="open = false"
            />
            <Button
              label="Save"
              kind="primary"
            />
          </div>
        </PanelFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </DialogPortal>
  </Dialog>
</template>
```

# Drawer

> Layered surface above the page (modal, drawer, menu). Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/overlay/drawer/`.

- Import: `import Drawer from '@aziontech/webkit/drawer'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- A panel that slides in from a screen edge for secondary tasks, filters, long forms, or navigation, while keeping page context.
- The content is too large or persistent for a centered modal.

## Do

- Pick the edge (side) intentionally and keep it consistent across the app.
- Trap focus while open and provide an obvious close affordance.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- It is a short, focused confirmation/task best centered and fully blocking → use `dialog`.
- It is a small overlay anchored to a trigger → use a popover / `dropdown`.

## Related

- `dialog` — centered, blocking modal for focused tasks/confirmations.
- `sidebar` — persistent (non-overlay) side navigation.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | When true, overlay click and Escape close the drawer. |
| `side` | `DrawerSide` | `'right'` | false | Edge the drawer panel slides from. |
| `size` | `DrawerSize` | `'medium'` | false | Panel max-width preset (`small` 384px, `medium` 672px, `large` 1024px). Height is always 100% viewport. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-overlay`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-portal`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/drawer-trigger`

## Sub-components

- `drawer-close.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-close`.
- `drawer-content.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-content`.
- `drawer-description.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-description`.
- `drawer-overlay.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-overlay`.
- `drawer-portal.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-portal`.
- `drawer-title.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-title`.
- `drawer-trigger.vue` — Public sub-component `drawer-trigger`.

## v-model

| Model          | Type      | Default     | Emits         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Controlled open state through `defineModel('open')`, the single declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`, as on `dialog` and `popover`. Fires once per transition. While unbound the drawer is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)
- Phones: below `md` the drawer is a bottom sheet (full width, 80 dvh); below `sm` it becomes a full-height, full-width sheet (`top-0`, `h-dvh`, no radius, no border). The `PanelFooter` stays pinned under the scrolling content with full-width actions.
- Server render and hydration: the phone layout reads the viewport only after mount (`use-overlay-mobile` gates the media query on `useMounted`), so a drawer rendered open on the server hydrates with the desktop panel and switches to the phone sheet in the same tick as mount, before paint.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Enter`/`Space` on the trigger opens the drawer and moves focus to its first focusable control. Focus is trapped: `Tab` on the last control wraps to the first and `Shift+Tab` on the first wraps to the last. `Escape` closes it and focus returns to the trigger, or, when opened without a `Drawer.Trigger`, to the element that held focus when it opened. Tests: `drawer.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Teleported content: the portal wraps its content (overlay and panel) in a `display: contents` element that binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

# Panel

> Layered surface above the page (modal, drawer, menu). Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/overlay/panel/`.

- Import: `import Panel from '@aziontech/webkit/panel'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Laying out the regions inside `DialogContent` or `DrawerContent`: `PanelHeader` for the title and close control, `PanelContent` for the body that scrolls, `PanelFooter` for the actions.
- A static preview of an overlay surface outside a live overlay, for example a frozen dialog on a docs or marketing page.

## Do

- Inside a dialog or drawer, use only `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent` and `PanelFooter`. The overlay already renders the `Panel` root, so a second `Panel` inside it nests two shells.
- Put long content in `PanelContent`. It is the only region that scrolls; the header and footer stay in place.
- size` caps the max width (`small`, `medium`, `large` map to the `--container-sm` / `--container-xl` / `--container-2xl` tokens). `sizeAtMd` applies that cap from `md` up only and is meant for the dialog's mobile bottom sheet.
- Panel` has no open state, no dismissal and no focus management. Don't use it alone as a modal.

## Don’t

- The surface has to open over the page and trap focus → use `dialog`.
- The surface slides in from a screen edge → use `drawer`.
- Rich content anchored to a trigger that leaves the page interactive → use `popover`.
- A card in the page layout, with header, content and footer slots → use `card`.

## Related

- `dialog` — renders a `Panel` inside `DialogContent`; compose the `Panel*` regions directly in it.
- `drawer` — renders a `Panel` inside `DrawerContent`; there `PanelContent` scrolls through a `ScrollArea`.
- `card` — in-page card with header, content and footer slots. `Panel` is the elevated overlay shell, with a large shadow and max-width presets.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `PanelSize` | `'medium'` | false | Max width of the panel shell. |
| `sizeAtMd` | `boolean` | `false` | false | When true, the `size` max-width applies from `md` up only (dialog mobile bottom sheet). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | — |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-footer`
- `@aziontech/webkit/panel-header`

## Sub-components

- `panel-content.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-content`.
- `panel-footer.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-footer`.
- `panel-header.vue` — Public sub-component `panel-header`.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed` (where applicable)
- Responsive: `PanelContent` is the `@container/panel`, so the content of a dialog or a drawer lays out for the panel width. Below `sm` the `PanelFooter` wraps, stretches its direct children to equal widths (`max-sm:*:flex-1`) and pads the bottom by `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.
- Scroll region: when `PanelContent` (outside a drawer's `ScrollArea`) overflows and holds nothing focusable, it takes `tabindex="0"` with an inset focus ring, so a keyboard user can scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1, axe `scrollable-region-focusable`); it is measured on resize and on content changes.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Panel from '@aziontech/webkit/panel'
  import PanelContent from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-content'
  import PanelFooter from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-footer'
  import PanelHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/panel-header'
</script>

<template>
  <Panel size="medium">
    <PanelHeader>
      <h2 class="text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">Cache settings</h2>
    </PanelHeader>
    <PanelContent>
      <p class="text-body-sm text-(--text-muted)">
        Objects are cached at the edge for the TTL set on each rule.
      </p>
    </PanelContent>
    <PanelFooter>
      <Button
        label="Cancel"
        kind="outlined"
      />
      <Button
        label="Save"
        kind="primary"
      />
    </PanelFooter>
  </Panel>
</template>
```

<!-- components/popover.md -->

# Popover

> Anchored, **non-modal** overlay that opens from a consumer-supplied trigger and renders rich, interactive content — a header (title + optional description + close), a free-form body, and a footer for actions — in a floating panel anchored to the trigger. Use for inline forms, filter builders, and contextual detail or confirmation that needs interactive children. Unlike `overlay/tooltip` (plain text, non-interactive) and `overlay/dialog` (modal, centered, focus-trapped), the popover leaves the page interactive, anchors to its trigger, and closes on `Esc` or outside-click. It differs from `navigation/dropdown`, which renders a menu of selectable options rather than free-form content.

- Import: `import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'`
- Compound import (dot notation, not tree-shakeable): `import Popover from '@aziontech/webkit/popover'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: composition

## When to use

- Interactive content anchored to a trigger while the page stays usable: an inline form, a filter builder, a quick edit of one field.
- Contextual detail or a light confirmation that needs buttons or links inside it.

## Do

- Place `Popover.Trigger` first and `Popover.Content` after it. The trigger wires `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and the click toggle onto your element, so don't bind them yourself.
- Let `Popover.Trigger` show the pointer: its wrapper sets `cursor-pointer` (`cursor-not-allowed` when disabled), so a `Tag`, `Avatar` or icon slotted in reads as clickable. Don't put `cursor-pointer` on the slotted WebKit component — `webkit/no-style-override` blocks it.
- Include a `Popover.Title`. The panel takes its accessible name from it through `aria-labelledby`.
- Set `width` for forms and filter builders so the panel doesn't resize as content changes. Without it, the panel sizes fluidly between the `--container-3xs` and `--container-xs` tokens.
- Use `placement="auto"` for triggers that can sit near a viewport edge.
- Use a side placement (`right-start`, `left-start`, …) for a trigger in a narrow column or a sidebar, where the panel should open beside the trigger instead of covering the content below it. Type a placement held in a variable with the exported `PopoverPlacement` (or `PopoverPlacementInput` when it can be `'auto'`), never a cast.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open` (or `:open` + `@update:open`, whose handler receives a `boolean`).
- Set `dismissible` to `false` only when an outside click would discard input. Then give the user a way out: `Popover.Close` or a footer action.

## Don’t

- A short, non-interactive hint on hover or focus → use `tooltip`.
- A list of actions or options to pick from → use `dropdown`.
- Choosing a form value from a list → use `select`.
- A blocking task that must be completed or cancelled first → use `dialog`.
- A long form or a secondary workflow → use `drawer`.

## Related

- `tooltip` — plain text only and non-interactive; opens on hover and focus, not on click.
- dropdown` — same trigger and anchoring model, but renders option rows and emits `select`.
- `dialog` — modal and centered, traps focus and locks scroll; the popover does neither.
- `drawer` — edge-anchored modal panel for longer content.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `PopoverPlacementInput` | `'bottom-start'` | false | Where the panel opens relative to the trigger: a side (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`), optionally aligned to its `start` or `end`, or `'auto'`, which picks the best-fitting of the four vertical corners at open time based on available viewport space. A placement that does not fit flips to the opposite side, keeping its alignment. |
| `offset` | `number` | `4` | false | Pixel gap between the trigger and the panel. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Prevents the trigger from opening the panel and applies disabled tokens. |
| `width` | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'` | `undefined` | false | Panel width preset mapped to container tokens: `'small'` (`var(--container-xs)`), `'medium'` (`var(--container-sm)`), `'large'` (`var(--container-md)`). When omitted, the panel sizes fluidly between `var(--container-3xs)` and `var(--container-xs)`. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Light-dismiss: when `true`, the panel closes on outside-click and `Esc`. Set `false` to keep it open until the trigger or `PopoverClose` closes it. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | Place `<Popover.Trigger>` followed by `<Popover.Content>`. |

## Sub-component imports

- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-content`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-header`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-title`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-description`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-close`
- `@aziontech/webkit/popover-footer`

## Sub-components

The root `Popover` owns open/closed state, anchoring/placement (exposing the computed `panelStyle`), outside-click + `Esc` dismissal, focus containment and return. Shared state flows through `provide`/`inject` (`isOpen`, `triggerId`, `contentId`, `titleId`, `descriptionId`, `setOpen`, resolved `placement`, `width`, `panelStyle`, and the `panelRef` that `Popover.Content` assigns), so every sub-component is context-aware and the consumer wires nothing. **`Popover.Content` renders the single teleported, animated floating panel with its content inline** (the Select / Tooltip pattern — one `<Teleport>` + `<Transition>`, so the scale animation carries the whole panel on enter/leave); the panel element carries `role="dialog"`, the surface/border/radius/shadow tokens, the open/close `animate-popup-scale-*`, `--popup-origin` (via `panelStyle`), and `data-state` / `data-placement`, and assigns itself to the root's `panelRef` so the root's placement/focus logic operates on it. Member names mirror this component's anatomy; `Trigger` / `Content` are valid here because the popover has a real `data-state="open|closed"`.

- `popover-trigger/popover-trigger.vue` — as-child trigger.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (the root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: `default` with scope `{ isOpen: boolean }` — the consumer's trigger element. The trigger forwards aria + click; the consumer must not bind those itself.
- `popover-content/popover-content.vue` — renders the floating panel via a single `<Teleport to="body">` + `<Transition>`, with its default slot (`Popover.Header`, the free-form body, `Popover.Footer`) arranged inline a…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — the popover anatomy (`Popover.Header`, body content, `Popover.Footer`).
- `popover-header/popover-header.vue` — full-width header region with a bottom divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding, laid out as a row with the title/description block on the left and the…
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — `Popover.Title`, optional `Popover.Description`, and `Popover.Close`.
- `popover-title/popover-title.vue` — title text (`.text-body-sm`, `var(--text-default)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text title.
- `popover-description/popover-description.vue` — supporting description text (`.text-body-xs`, `var(--text-muted)`).
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — plain-text description.
- `popover-close/popover-close.vue` — close control.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_ (root handles `update:open`).
  - Slots: _none_.
- `popover-footer/popover-footer.vue` — full-width footer region with a top divider and `py var(--spacing-sm)` / `px var(--spacing-md)` padding.
  - Props: _none_.
  - Events: _none_.
  - Slots: `default` — action buttons (e.g. Cancel / Apply).

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v-model:open` | `boolean \| undefined` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void`. Fires on every open/closed transition: trigger toggle, `Popover.Close`, `Esc`, and outside-click. While unbound (`undefined`) the popover is uncontrolled and starts closed. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values (root, trigger, floating panel): `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop on root and trigger
- Cursor: the trigger wrapper shows `pointer`, and `not-allowed` with `data-disabled`
- `data-placement` on the root mirrors the `placement` prop (`'auto'` stays as `'auto'`)
- `data-placement` on the floating panel mirrors the resolved placement (any `PopoverPlacement`; `'auto'` resolves to one of `'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end'`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger and the close button.
- Keyboard map:
  - On the trigger: `Enter` / `Space` toggles the panel. When it opens, focus **stays on the trigger** — it is not moved into the panel.
  - `Esc` closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger, from anywhere (trigger or panel). `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` are **contained** within the trigger and the panel's focusable children: Tab from the trigger moves into the panel, Tab past the last panel child wraps back to the trigger, and Shift+Tab reverses. Tabbing **never** closes the panel — only `Esc` or an outside-click dismiss it.
  - Outside-click closes the panel; focus is not forced back to the trigger on outside-click.
  - Tests: `popover.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
  - A text `<input>` or `<textarea>` as the trigger control keeps its textbox role and gets none of `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`, which ARIA does not allow on a textbox (`aria-allowed-attr`); a field that opens suggestions should be a `Combobox`.
- ARIA: the slotted control (or the wrapper, when the slot has none) exposes `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, with a single tab stop and in the server HTML; the floating panel (rendered by the root) uses `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="false"`, `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `Popover.Title` id and `aria-describedby` pointing at the `Popover.Description` id (when present); `Popover.Close` is an `IconButton` with `aria-label="Close"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (icons), including the disabled trigger state (validated via `--text-muted` / `--text-disabled` tokens).
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on `animate-popup-scale-*`; `motion-reduce:transition-none` on `transition-colors` for hover/focus states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (consumer's element — flagged in docs); the close `IconButton` follows `IconButton`'s own target sizing.
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="dialog"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.
- `PopoverHeader` keeps its `header` tag with `role="none"`, so an open popover does not expose a `banner` landmark (pinned by `src/test/screen-reader.test.ts`).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import PopoverClose from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-close'
  import PopoverContent from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-content'
  import PopoverHeader from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-header'
  import PopoverRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-root'
  import PopoverTitle from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-title'
  import PopoverTrigger from '@aziontech/webkit/popover-trigger'
</script>

<template>
  <PopoverRoot>
    <PopoverTrigger>
      <Button
        kind="secondary"
        label="Open popover"
      />
    </PopoverTrigger>

    <PopoverContent>
      <PopoverHeader>
        <PopoverTitle>Popover title</PopoverTitle>
        <PopoverClose />
      </PopoverHeader>

      <div class="p-(--spacing-md) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)">
        This content is rendered inside the popover panel.
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  </PopoverRoot>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/popover.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/popover.md).

<!-- components/tooltip.md -->

# Tooltip

> Surfaces a short hint anchored to a trigger element when the user hovers, focuses, or long-presses it. Use for icon-only buttons, abbreviations, or any control whose meaning is not obvious from its label alone. **Not** for rich content or interactive children — use `overlay/popover` instead.

- Import: `import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'`
- Category: overlay · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Naming an icon-only control on hover and focus.
- Revealing the full text of a truncated label, or expanding an abbreviation.
- One short, plain-text hint that the user can do without.

## Do

- Wrap a focusable element. The tooltip opens on the wrapper's `focusin`, and the wrapper itself is not focusable.
- Keep `text` to a few words. It renders as plain text, with no markup.
- The tooltip describes its trigger (`aria-describedby`) but does not name it. Icon-only triggers still need their own accessible name.
- Use `disabled` to suppress the tooltip. An empty `text` also blocks opening, but it reads as a bug.
- Keep the default `delay` (200 ms) unless a dense toolbar needs a longer one.
- Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

## Don’t

- The content has links, buttons or more than one line of structure → use `popover`.
- An info glyph beside a field label or column header → use `hint`.
- A glossed term inside documentation prose → use `doc-tooltip`.
- Guidance or errors the user needs to complete a field → use `helper-text`.

## Related

- `popover` — click-opened, interactive, with a header, body and footer.
- `hint` — the focusable info glyph that renders a `Tooltip` for you.
- `doc-tooltip` — inline glossed term for docs pages.
- `icon-button` — the most common trigger; it still needs its own `ariaLabel`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | `—` | true | Plain text shown inside the tooltip. |
| `placement` | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left' \| 'auto'` | `'top'` | false | Anchor side relative to the trigger; `auto` picks the side with room. |
| `delay` | `number` | `200` | false | Hover-open delay in milliseconds. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Disables tooltip activation. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `open` | `boolean` | `undefined as never` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:open`). |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | `void` | Emitted right after the open transition starts. |
| `hide` | `void` | Emitted right after the close transition starts. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The trigger element. Tooltip anchors to its bounding box. |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `undefined` | `update:open` | Open state via `defineModel('open')`, the only declaration of `open`, so `@update:open` is typed `(value: boolean) => void` and fires once per open/closed transition (hover, focus, `Esc`). While unbound the tooltip is uncontrolled and starts at `defaultOpen`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `disabled`
- `data-state` values: `open` | `closed`
- `data-disabled` mirrors the `disabled` prop
- `data-placement`: `top` | `right` | `bottom` | `left`
- `data-anchored` on the panel once its opening position has landed — the flag that lets a re-anchor animate while the entrance stays the open animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` on the trigger wrapper.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` onto the trigger opens the tooltip at once (no hover delay); `Escape` closes it and focus stays on the trigger; `Tab` away closes it; the tooltip never takes or traps focus. Tests: `tooltip.test.ts` › keyboard map (spec).
- ARIA: `role="tooltip"` on the panel; the slotted control references the panel via `aria-describedby` (merged into a WebKit `Button` / `IconButton` or native control at render, otherwise forwarded onto the first focusable element in the slot after mount; on the wrapper only when the slot has none). The wrapper itself has no `role` and no tab stop. `aria-hidden="true"` when `data-state="closed"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 — text against surface verified in both light and dark modes.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the panel; reduced-motion users get instant show/hide.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px on the trigger (the consumer's responsibility — flag in docs).
- Teleported content: the teleported `role="tooltip"` panel binds `dir` and `lang` from the nearest `WebkitProvider` (`usePortalLocale`), so it keeps the provider's direction and language although it renders under `body`. With no provider nothing is set and the document's own `dir` and `lang` apply.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'
</script>

<template>
  <Tooltip
    text="This is a Tooltip"
    placement="top"
  >
    <Button
      label="Hover me"
      kind="outlined"
      size="medium"
    />
  </Tooltip>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/tooltip.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/tooltip.md).

<!-- components/architecture-tabs.md -->

# Architecture Tabs

> The architecture band of a product page: a horizontal section title with one large button, over a row of up to five tabs whose active tab draws its named diagram the full width of the frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'architecture-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `frame-box`, `media-tabs` and `diagram`. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.

- Import: `import ArchitectureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/architecture-tabs'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To plot several architectures of one product, or one request across the platform, one diagram at a time.

## Do

- Keep to five tabs with `position` `top` or `bottom`, three with `left` or `right`; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
- Give every tab a `diagram` from the diagram library and a stable `value`.

## Don’t

- For features shown by an illustration each → use `feature-tabs`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the timed tab row this section renders through.
- `diagram` — the named architecture diagram each tab draws.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence beside the headline. |
| `position` | `ArchitectureTabsPosition` | `'top'` | false | Side of the diagram the tabs sit on: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`; left and right hold up to three tabs. |
| `tabs` | `ArchitectureTabsTab[]` | `[]` | false | The architectures, in order; each is `{ value, title, description, diagram }` where `diagram` is the name of the diagram drawn while the tab is active. |
| `primaryAction` | `ArchitectureTabsAction` | `undefined` | false | Large button in the section title; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## Assets

- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the active tab, its progress and the timer are owned by `media-tabs`
- Empty: when `tabs` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `media-tabs` (the tabs) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the button and the tab row; the tab row's keys are owned by `media-tabs`.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each diagram carries the description its spec ships.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-tabs` and `diagram`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the timer never runs under reduced motion (owned by `media-tabs`).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the large button and the tab rows.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ArchitectureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/architecture-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      value: 'request-path',
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'A call crosses Firewall, the application and the function before it reaches a model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway'
    },
    {
      value: 'failover',
      title: 'Provider failover',
      description: 'When a provider degrades, the gateway moves to the next model on the alias.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-provider-failover'
    },
    {
      value: 'costs',
      title: 'Cost routing',
      description: 'Premium tokens go only where they pay off; everyone else gets a lighter model.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-model-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'latency',
      title: 'Latency routing',
      description: 'Real-time tasks run on AI Inference, close to the user, in under 30 ms.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-latency-routing'
    },
    {
      value: 'cache',
      title: 'Response cache',
      description:
        'A repeated prompt is answered from cache, with no model call and no tokens spent.',
      diagram: 'ai-gateway-response-cache'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Docs',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ArchitectureTabs
    eyebrow="Routing"
    title="Every AI request through one control point"
    description="Every client calls one endpoint. Firewall stops abuse, then a function checks the key, routes the call, and logs it."
    position="bottom"
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```
