<!-- components/article-body.md -->

# Article Body

> The reading page of an article. A brand banner sits over a three-column grid: the share, community and copy-page rail on the left; the breadcrumb, headline, byline and prose down the middle at a reading measure; and the "On this page" outline on the right. Both rails stick under the header and fold away below `lg`, leaving the column alone. The section opens the page itself, so it carries its own `section-container` instead of sitting in the page column. The prose arrives as markdown: blank-line separated blocks render as `##` / `###` headings (each with an id slugged from its text, feeding the outline), `-` lists and paragraphs. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-body', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-container`, `section-module`, `frame-box`, `breadcrumb`, `hero-title`, `divider`, `doc-prose`, `tooltip`, `icon-button`, `split-button` and `doc-on-this-page`; copying to the clipboard is local behaviour.

- Import: `import ArticleBody from '@aziontech/webkit/article-body'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open every blog post and every success story page.

## Do

- Write the body as plain blocks — headings, paragraphs and `-` lists separated by blank lines; inline markdown is rendered as text.
- Mark the last breadcrumb entry `current`.

## Don’t

- For a list of articles → use `article-index-blog`.
- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `doc-prose` — the reading-measure typography the body renders in.
- `doc-on-this-page` — the outline rail fed by the body's headings.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `article` | `ArticleBodyArticle` | `—` | true | The piece being read: its `title` (the page h1), `description`, `date`, `readTime` and canonical `href`. |
| `trail` | `ArticleBodyCrumb[]` | `[]` | false | The breadcrumb over the headline, each a `label` and an `href`, the last one marked `current`. |
| `body` | `string` | `''` | false | The article as markdown; its `##` and `###` headings feed the outline. |
| `banner` | `string` | `''` | false | URL of the image over the masthead; the banner frame is omitted when empty. |
| `share` | `ArticleBodyShare` | `undefined` | false | Labels of the share group: its `title`, `copyLink`, `shareX` and `shareLinkedIn`; the group is omitted when absent. |
| `community` | `ArticleBodyCommunity` | `undefined` | false | The community group: a `title` and `links`, each a `label`, an `href` and an `icon`; omitted when absent. |
| `copyPage` | `ArticleBodyCopyPage` | `undefined` | false | The copy-page split button: its `label` and a `menu` of entries, each a `value`, a `label` and an `icon`; omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on every link and button
- The outline lists the body's headings, the first one active; it is omitted when the body has none
- The left rail renders only the groups that are set, and is omitted when none is
- Copying: the copy-link button and the `link` menu entry copy `article.href`; the split button's main action copies the body; a failed clipboard write is ignored

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every link and button shows a `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the breadcrumb, the rails and the prose links; the split button owns its menu keyboard map.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div` so the page keeps its own landmarks; the headline is the page `h1` (from `hero-title`); the prose is an `article`; the two rails are `aside` landmarks, the left one named by the share title, the right one by the outline's own navigation; the share and community groups are named `section`s; icon-only share buttons are named by their labels and carry a tooltip; the banner is decorative (`aria-hidden`, `alt=""`); heading ids are slugged from their text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by `icon-button` and `split-button`.

## Examples

<!-- components/article-cards.md -->

# Article Cards

> A titled row of three linked article cards on one hairline frame grid with no gutter, stacking to one column on mobile. Each card is a single link: a 16:9 media cell holding the article's cover — or, when it has none, the client's mark in one flat ink that follows the theme — then the headline, the deck and a `meta` overline pinned to the foot. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-cards', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `card-grid`. `kind` places the heading only: `left` at the start (an article's closing row), `centered` centred over the cards under an overline (a landing-page band); the cards keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import ArticleCards from '@aziontech/webkit/article-cards'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a blog post with its related articles, or a success story with its related stories.
- To show three stories as a landing-page band under a centred heading.

## Do

- Give a card either `image` or `mark`; the mark is drawn only when there is no cover.
- Keep the band to three cards so the frame row stays full.

## Don’t

- For the full, filterable list of articles → use `article-index-blog` or `article-index-resource-hub`.
- For one featured article selected from a wall → use `article-highlight`.

## Related

- `card-grid` — the frame grid the cards sit on.
- `article-highlight` — the blog's opening band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `ArticleCardsKind` | `'left'` | false | Placement of the heading: `left` sets it at the start, `centered` centres it over the cards. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the heading. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `items` | `ArticleCardsItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in order; each is `{ key, href, title, description, meta, image?, mark? }`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the card grid. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (the card lifts to the raised surface and its media scales up), `focus-visible` (inset ring)
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and places the heading
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each card is one link with an inset `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves card to card; `Enter` follows the link.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the grid is a `group` named by `ariaLabel` when set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each card's headline an `h3`; a cover is decorative (`alt=""`), a client mark is named by the client.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted` on the canvas.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the whole card is the target.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
</script>

    title="Related Articles"
    aria-label="Related Articles"
    :items="[
      {
        key: 'how-to-reduce-ai-agent-latency',
```

<!-- components/article-highlight.md -->

# Article Highlight

> The band that opens a blog under its hero. One article is shown large — its cover beside its overline, headline, deck, read time and a button into it — over a wall of the highlight articles that acts as its selector. The wall is a tablist and the large article its panel; selecting a title on the wall swaps the panel, and every article is drawn invisibly under the panel so the band keeps the height of its tallest article and never jumps. With four or more articles the wall runs four across. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-highlight', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid` and `button`; the selection is local state.

- Import: `import ArticleHighlight from '@aziontech/webkit/article-highlight'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a blog or a resource page with its newest or most important articles.

## Do

- Feature three to five articles; the wall sets one column per article from `lg`, so five sit in one row of five as on azion.com's blog.
- Give a `highlightImage` cropped for the panel when the cover does not read at that size.
- Bind `v-model` (the selected index) to open on an article other than the first; the band never advances on its own, so it holds whatever the reader or the page picked.

## Don’t

- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.
- For the full list of articles → use `article-index-blog`.

## Related

- `article-cards` — the closing row of related articles.
- `card-grid` — the frame grid the wall of titles sits on.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `items` | `ArticleHighlightItem[]` | `[]` | false | The highlight articles in wall order, the one at the bound index (the first by default) selected on load; each is `{ key, href, image, highlightImage?, meta, title, description, readTime }`. |
| `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the button into the selected article; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the wall of titles. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v-model` | `number` | `0` | `update:modelValue` | Index of the selected article; left unbound the band starts on the first one. A click or an arrow key writes the new index back; an index past the ends is clamped to the wall. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a wall title lights, the panel cover scales up), `focus-visible` (inset ring), `selected` (`data-active` on the selected wall title)
- `data-columns` on the wall: one column per article from `lg`, three at least and five at most
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing
- The band has no timer: the selected article changes only on a click, an arrow key or a bound `modelValue`
- Reflow: the hidden layout sizer is `min-w-0`, so the panel never grows past a 320 px box.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the panel headline link and every wall title show an inset `focus-visible` ring.
- Keyboard map: on the wall, `ArrowRight` / `ArrowDown` select the next title, `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowUp` the previous one (wrapping), `Home` the first and `End` the last; selection follows focus and only the selected title is in the tab order (roving `tabindex`).
- ARIA: the wall is a `tablist` named by `ariaLabel`, each title a `tab` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; the panel is a `tabpanel` labelled by the selected tab; the panel headline is an `h2` whose link covers the article; the invisible sizer is `aria-hidden` and `inert`; covers are decorative (`alt=""`). Ids come from `useId`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted` on the canvas.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every wall title is a full-cell button.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the external-link arrow does not mirror.
- Keyboard: `ArrowRight`/`ArrowLeft` move between the highlighted articles, swapped under `dir="rtl"` (`logicalArrowKey`).
- User data: article titles in another script keep their own direction.

## Examples

```vue
    :items="[
      {
        key: 'ship-portfolio-two-commands-azion-cli',
```

# Article Index Blog

> Every article of the blog as one ruled list, with the controls to narrow it on one row: a category picker and a search field. Each article is a row — its cover on the left, and on the right its overline, headline, a two-line deck and its writers with the byline pinned to the foot; the row is one link named by its headline, and from `lg` up a read cue rises into its end on hover or keyboard focus. The category and the search combine; a load-more button closes the list. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-index-blog', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `toggle-group`, `input`, `avatar` and `button`; the selected category and the search term are local state.

- Import: `import ArticleIndexBlog from '@aziontech/webkit/article-index-blog'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For the blog's full list of posts, filtered by category and searched by text.

## Do

- List the articles newest first; file every article under at least one of `categories`.
- Keep the category list short enough to scroll on one row: the picker keeps every label at its full width and the row scrolls sideways on a phone instead of squeezing the labels.

## Don’t

- For a resource hub filtered by facet dropdowns, with centred rows and no byline → use `article-index-resource-hub`.
- For a closing row of related articles → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `article-index-resource-hub` — the sibling listing with facet dropdowns.
- `article-highlight` — the band that opens the blog above this list.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `items` | `ArticleIndexBlogItem[]` | `[]` | false | The articles, newest first; each is `{ key, href, image, meta, title, description, authors?, byline?, categories? }`. |
| `categories` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Segments of the category picker after the show-all segment; the picker is omitted when empty. |
| `allLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the first segment, which shows every category. |
| `categoryLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the category picker. |
| `search` | `ArticleIndexBlogSearch` | `undefined` | false | The search field's `placeholder` and accessible `label`; the field is omitted when absent. |
| `rowLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Read cue revealed at the end of a row under hover or focus. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the load-more button under the list; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of articles. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a row lights and its read cue rises in), `focus-visible` (inset ring on the row, the read cue rises in)
- Filtered: the selected category keeps the articles whose `categories` hold it, the show-all segment keeps every one; the search matches the title and the description; both combine
- Empty: when no article matches, the list and the load-more button are not rendered
- `data-kind="byline"` on the list: the copy is spread so the byline sits at the foot

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the headline link draws an inset ring over the whole row; the picker, field and button own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the category picker, the search field, each row and the load-more button; the picker owns its arrow-key map.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` (unnamed, no header); the toolbar is a `search` landmark; the picker is a radio group named by `categoryLabel`, the field named by `search.label`; the list is named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `article` whose headline (`h3`) link covers it; the cover is decorative (`alt=""`) and the read cue `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every row is a full-row link.

## Examples

```vue
    :categories="['Developers', 'Security', 'Company news', 'Serverless']"
    :search="{ placeholder: 'Search articles', label: 'Search articles' }"
    :items="[
      {
        key: 'ship-portfolio-two-commands-azion-cli',
```

<!-- components/article-index-resource-hub.md -->

# Article Index Resource Hub

> Every resource of a hub as one ruled list, with a headline and one searchable dropdown per facet (content type, category, industry) on one row that wraps when it runs out of room. Each resource is a row — its cover on the left, and on the right its overline, headline and a two-line deck centred in the row; the row is one link named by its headline, and from `lg` up a read cue rises into its end on hover or keyboard focus. The facets combine; a load-more button closes the list. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'article-index-resource-hub', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `select`, `input` and `button`; the facet selections and each dropdown's option search are local state.

- Import: `import ArticleIndexResourceHub from '@aziontech/webkit/article-index-resource-hub'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For a resource hub that mixes content types (e-books, posts, comparisons, stories), filtered by facet.

## Do

- Give every item a `facets` entry per facet `key` it can be filtered by; an item without one never matches a selection on that facet.
- Keep each facet's `options` to values some item carries.

## Don’t

- For the blog's list filtered by a category picker and a search field, with bylines → use `article-index-blog`.
- For the success-story library with a card grid → use `story-library`.

## Related

- `article-index-blog` — the sibling listing with a category picker and a search field.
- `story-library` — the card-grid library with search and facets.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline beside the dropdowns, rendered as the band's `h2`. |
| `items` | `ArticleIndexResourceHubItem[]` | `[]` | false | The resources, in order; each is `{ key, href, image, meta, title, description, facets? }`. |
| `facets` | `ArticleIndexResourceHubFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet dropdowns, in order; each is `{ key, label, allLabel, options }`. |
| `rowLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Read cue revealed at the end of a row under hover or focus. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the load-more button under the list; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of resources. |

## States

- Each row's deck shows in full in `text-body-lg`, never clamped, as on azion.com's Resource Hub
- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a row lights and its read cue rises in), `focus-visible` (inset ring on the row, the read cue rises in)
- Filtered: each facet keeps the resources whose `facets[key]` holds the selected value; its `allLabel` option keeps every one; the facets combine
- Empty: when no resource matches, the list and the load-more button are not rendered
- `data-kind="centered"` on the list: the copy is centred in the row

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the headline link draws an inset ring over the whole row; the dropdowns and button own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through each dropdown, each row and the load-more button; the dropdowns own their keyboard map.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the toolbar is a `search` landmark; each dropdown trigger is named by its facet `label`; the list is named by `ariaLabel`; each row is an `article` whose headline (`h3`) link covers it; the cover is decorative (`alt=""`) and the read cue `aria-hidden`; an option search with no match announces itself as a `status`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every row is a full-row link.
- Reflow: from `sm` the facet dropdowns sit on one row that wraps (`flex-wrap`), so two or more `w-56` dropdowns never overflow a narrow box or a 200% zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

</script>

<template>
  <ArticleIndexResourceHub
    anchor="resources"
    title="Explore all resources"
    row-label="Read article"
    more-label="Load more"
    aria-label="Resources"
    :facets="[
      {
        key: 'contentType',
        label: 'Content type',
        allLabel: 'All content types',
        options: ['E-books', 'Blog', 'Comparisons']
      },
      {
        key: 'industry',
        label: 'Industry',
        allLabel: 'All industries',
        options: ['Financial', 'Retail', 'Tech']
      }
    ]"
    :items="[
      {
        key: 'security-applications-apis-ai-agents',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/lp/security-applications-apis-ai-agents/',
        image: 'https://www.azion.com/assets/content/blog/uploads/Rich%20contentsdark.png',
        meta: 'E-books • OCT 15, 2026',
        title: 'Security for applications, APIs, and AI agents',
        description:
          'Learn how to bring security policies into deployment, automate protection, and monitor traffic.',
        facets: { contentType: ['E-books'] }
      },
      {
        key: 'azion-mcp-servers-generally-available',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/blog/azion-mcp-servers-generally-available/',
        image: 'https://www.azion.com/assets/content/blog/uploads/mcp-ga/Azion-MCP.svg',
        meta: 'Blog • OCT 14, 2026',
        title: 'Azion MCP servers: Connect Your Coding Agent to Azion',
        description: 'Azion MCP servers connect coding agents to the Azion documentation and API.',
        facets: { contentType: ['Blog'] }
      },
      {
        key: 'cloudflare-to-azion-alternative-guide',
```

<!-- components/capability-grid.md -->

# Capability Grid

> A framed grid of product capabilities under an optional section title: each cell is a `Topic` (glyph, heading, sentence) with optional bullet points, three or four to a row. From the design sample's site `CapabilityGrid`.

- Import: `import CapabilityGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/capability-grid'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- A product page listing what the product does, three or six at a time.
- A bare grid (no title) under a band that already has its heading.

## Do

- Three or six items at three columns, four or eight at four, so rows stay full.
- Keep points to three short lines.
- Set `titleKind: 'left'` for a band whose header sits at the start edge (the Partners page's "Why you should be a partner"); the grid keeps its title, so each capability stays an `h3`. Never wrap a bare grid in `SectionModule` to move the title: the capability headings rise to `h2` and the outline breaks.

## Don’t

- For capabilities with art — use `FeatureTiles` or `BentoGrid`.
- For links to other pages — use `UseCaseLinks` or `ResourceGrid`.

## Related

- Topic`, `CardGrid`, `FrameBox`, `SectionTitle` — the parts.
- FeatureTiles` — tiles with illustrations.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the grid, rendered as the band `h2`; without it the grid is bare and each capability heading is an `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences under the title. |
| `items` | `CapabilityGridItem[]` | `[]` | false | The capabilities, in order; each is `{ title, description, icon?, points? }`. The band renders nothing when empty. |
| `columns` | `CapabilityGridColumns` | `3` | false | Capabilities per row from the large breakpoint up. |
| `actions` | `CapabilityGridAction[]` | `[]` | false | Buttons under the section title; each is `{ label, href, trailing?, target?, kind? }`; without `kind` the first is secondary and the rest outlined. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `titleKind` | `SectionTitleKind` | `'centered'` | false | Layout of the section title: `centered` stacks and centers it, `left` stacks it at the start edge, `horizontal` sets the headline and its description in two columns. |

## States

- Renders nothing without items.
- Heading level drops to `h3` under a title and rises to `h2` without one.
- `titleKind` is passed to the section title as its `kind`; it has no effect on a bare grid.

## Accessibility

- A `section` named by its title; headings nest under it.
- Points are a real list.
- Glyphs are decorative (from `Topic`).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- One column on phones, two on medium, `columns` from large (from `CardGrid`).
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CapabilityGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/capability-grid'

  const items = [
    {
      icon: 'pi pi-bolt',
      title: 'Functions',
      description: 'Run JavaScript and WebAssembly close to every user.'
    },
    {
      icon: 'pi pi-database',
      title: 'Object Storage',
      description: 'Keep files where they are read, with no egress to plan for.'
    },
    {
      icon: 'pi pi-shield',
      title: 'Firewall',
      description: 'Stop bots and attacks before they reach your origin.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <CapabilityGrid
    eyebrow="Platform"
    title="Everything an application needs, in one place"
    description="Compute, storage and security that deploy together."
    :items="items"
    :actions="[{ label: 'Explore the platform', href: '/platform', trailing: true }]"
  />
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/capability-grid.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/capability-grid.md).

<!-- components/card-carousel.md -->

# Card Carousel

> The titled card-carousel band of a product or solution page: a section title on the start of the row with the previous/next controls at its end, over a horizontally scrolling track of standalone cards. Each card is an optional overline (the category), a heading, a sentence and, when it links somewhere, a mono link label closed by an arrow ("See example", "See solution"). The band answers "see how to use", "industries", "orchestration with control" on azion.com product pages, where the cases outnumber the row. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'card-carousel', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below. It composes `carousel` (`kind="cards"`, its `header` slot, `size="medium"` items and its step controls), `section-title` and `overline`, and owns only the card's inner layout.

- Import: `import CardCarousel from '@aziontech/webkit/card-carousel'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Four or more cases, industries or examples of equal weight that do not all need to be seen: the reader steps through them.
- When each case is a short card (overline, heading, one or two sentences) that may link to its own page or example.

## Do

- Give the band a `title`; its arrows sit on the title row, and the title names the row for assistive technology.
- Keep each card to a heading and one or two sentences, so the row height stays even.
- Use `eyebrow` on every card or on none; a row where some cards carry an overline reads as ragged.
- Give every card a `linkLabel` when every card has an `href`, and none when none does. The label is a visual cue; the card heading is the link.
- Pass as many cards as the content has; the track scrolls, so the count never has to fill the row.

## Don’t

- When every case must be visible, or there are three or six of equal weight → use `use-case-links` (linked grid) or `use-cases` (grid with one action).
- For a quote or testimonial row → use `quote-carousel` or `client-quotes`.
- For numbered principles pinned while the page scrolls → use `sticky-carousel`.
- For articles with images → use `article-cards`.

## Related

- `carousel` — the primitive this band composes; reach for it directly only for a non-card row.
- `use-case-links` — the same content as a static, fully visible grid.
- `sticky-carousel` — numbered dark cards pinned on scroll.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the band title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` at the start of the row the step controls end; the band renders no title when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `CardCarouselItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in order; each is `{ eyebrow?, title, description, href?, linkLabel? }`, and a card with `href` links to it. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the card row; defaults to the title. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; each linked card has `hover` (the arrow nudges toward the end edge, the label brightens) and `focus-visible` (an inset ring on the whole card).
- Empty: with no `items` the band renders nothing — no title, no controls.
- Untitled: with no `title` the controls sit alone at the start of the row (the carousel's own layout) and the row is named by `ariaLabel` only.
- Unlinked card: without `href` the card is a plain card with no hover state and no link label.
- The step controls carry `disabled` at each end of the track, from the carousel; a row that fits shows both disabled.
- `loading`, `error`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `invalid`, `open`: the band cannot be in these states; it renders static content from props.

## Accessibility

- Pattern: the WAI-ARIA APG carousel (`aria-roledescription="carousel"`, named region) from `carousel`; the band root is a plain container so the row is the one named region, named by `ariaLabel` or the title.
- Outline: the title is the section title's `h2`; each card heading is an `h3`.
- Links: on a linked card the `h3` holds the anchor, so the link's name is the card title; a stretched `::after` makes the whole card its hit area. The link label and its arrow are `aria-hidden` decoration.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the previous control, the next control, the track (arrow keys scroll it natively) and each card link in order; `Enter` / `Space` on a control steps one card; `Enter` on a card link follows it. A card that scrolls into focus is brought into view by the browser.
- Visible focus: card links draw `focus-visible:after:ring-2 focus-visible:after:ring-inset focus-visible:after:ring-(--ring-color)` around the whole card; the controls and track carry the carousel's ring.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1: copy is `var(--text-muted)` on `var(--bg-surface)`; the link label is `var(--text-muted)` at rest; the arrow is `var(--text-primary)` (≥3:1 as a graphic).
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition; the track never auto-advances (WCAG 2.2.2 does not apply).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the controls are 40×40; a card link spans its whole card.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; the title row keeps the title at the start edge and the controls at the end edge.
- Icons: the link arrow (`pi pi-arrow-right`) mirrors under `rtl:-scale-x-100` and its hover nudge runs toward the end edge (`rtl:group-hover/card:-translate-x-0.5`); the carousel's chevrons mirror in `carousel`.
- Keyboard: the next control steps toward the end edge in both directions (`carousel`).
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props in the page's language. The control names and the `carousel` role description come from `carousel`'s own locale group (en, pt-BR, es).
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; the cards have a fixed width (`size="medium"`, `var(--container-sm)`) and the track scrolls.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): each card is 85% of the viewport wide, so one card fills a phone and the next peeks; the title wraps inside its cell while the controls stay on its row.
- Touch: the track swipes natively; the hover nudge is decoration only, and every card stays a full-card link on touch.
- Reflow: the page never scrolls sideways at 320 px; only the track does, which is the component's purpose (WCAG 1.4.10 exception for a carousel).

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>

  const items = [
    {
      eyebrow: 'E-commerce',
      title: 'E-commerce product image optimization',
      description:
        'Optimize product images for faster page loads and better conversion rates. Automatically deliver responsive images at the right size and format for each device.',
      href: '/docs/products/build/applications/image-processor',
      linkLabel: 'See example'
    },
    {
      eyebrow: 'Media',

        'Deliver optimized images for news articles and media content that load instantly on any device. Automatic format conversion ensures the best experience.',

    {
```

<!-- components/cli-terminal.md -->

# Cli Terminal

> The Azion CLI band of a product page: a horizontal section title with one outlined button, over a terminal session on the pixelate texture that runs off the frame's bottom rule, its lines entering one after another. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'cli-terminal', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `frame-box`, `texture-material` and `code-block`.

- Import: `import CliTerminal from '@aziontech/webkit/cli-terminal'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a product argument on how little it takes to ship from the terminal, like Functions and Workloads.

## Do

- Keep the session to a few commands and their output; comment the output lines so the copied text still runs.
- Name the copy button with `copyAriaLabel` so a screen reader says what it copies.

## Don’t

- For a config file or handler beside the claim → use `code-split`.
- For several capabilities, each with its own file → use `sticky-scroll-code`.

## Related

- `code-block` — the terminal session the band shows.
- `code-split` — the sibling band with the sample beside the copy.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence beside the headline. |
| `session` | `string` | `''` | false | The terminal session shown under the header, commands and their output verbatim, highlighted as bash; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the session's copy button; empty keeps the code block's own. |
| `primaryAction` | `CliTerminalAction` | `undefined` | false | Outlined button in the section title; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the copy button and the button own their hover and focus states
- Empty: when `session` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `code-block` (copy button) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the button and the copy button; `Enter` follows the button.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; the copy button is named by `copyAriaLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `code-block` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the session's line entrance is owned by `code-block` and draws at once under reduced motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the large button.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CliTerminal from '@aziontech/webkit/cli-terminal'

  const session =
    'azion link --preset javascript --name auth-handler --auto\n# Project successfully configured\n\nazion deploy --auto\n# Upload completed successfully!\n# Your Application was deployed successfully\n# Domain: https://k7q2fmx4ze.map.azionedge.net\n\ncurl https://k7q2fmx4ze.map.azionedge.net/\n# Hello World'

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Install the CLI',
    href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/azion-cli/overview/',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <CliTerminal
    eyebrow="Azion CLI"
    title="Deploy your first function in two commands"
    description="Link a project, deploy it, and curl the domain the CLI hands back. Builds run on your machine with --local, or on Azion."
    :session="session"
    copy-aria-label="Copy the deploy session"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

# Client Mosaic

> The client mosaic: a framed bento grid of customer cells where a story cell carries a photograph, the client's mark, one line of its result and a "read the case study" link, and a mark cell carries only the client's linked logo on a chosen fill. The layout is derived from the data: the first story spans two columns and two rows, every other story one column and two rows, every mark one cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-mosaic', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `bento-grid` and `mini-button`.

- Import: `import ClientMosaic from '@aziontech/webkit/client-mosaic'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the home page, to show the best customer stories and a wall of marks in one band.

## Do

- Two stories and six marks fill the four-column grid exactly.
- Pick `fill` and `logoTreatment` together: a `knockout` mark reads on `white` or `primary`, a `monochrome` one on `canvas` or `surface`.

## Don’t

- For three equal story columns → use `client-mosaic-columns`.
- For a plain wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-quote`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the cells are laid in.
- `client-mosaic-columns` — the three-column sibling with brand-coloured faces.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the grid. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the link under every story. |
| `stories` | `ClientMosaicStory[]` | `[]` | false | The story cells, in order; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, photo, text, href, fill?, logoTreatment? }`. The first spans two columns and two rows, the rest one column and two rows. |
| `logos` | `ClientMosaicLogo[]` | `[]` | false | The mark cells, in order; each is `{ logo, logoAlt, href, fill?, logoTreatment? }` where `fill` is `'canvas'`, `'surface'`, `'white'` or `'primary'` and `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'`, `'knockout'` or `'as-is'`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each cell
- `data-fill` on every cell face drives its fill; `data-treatment` on every mark drives its ink; `data-lead` on the first story sets its larger text
- Empty: when both `stories` and `logos` are empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every mark cell is a link with `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`; the story link is a `mini-button` with its own ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between mark links and story links; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by `ariaLabel`; the photo of a story is decorative (`alt=""`, `aria-hidden`); every mark carries `logoAlt`; the story text is a paragraph and its link is named by `linkLabel`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): story text `var(--text-default)` over the canvas gradient; marks are inked to their fill through `logoTreatment`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the fill transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark cell is a full grid cell.

## Examples

<!-- components/client-mosaic-columns.md -->

# Client Mosaic Columns

> Three featured success stories side by side: each column is a client's mark on a face painted in the client's own brand colour, over a one-line story that links to the case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-mosaic-columns', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box` and `logo-wall`.

- Import: `import ClientMosaicColumns from '@aziontech/webkit/client-mosaic-columns'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- When three stories deserve equal weight and their brands should colour the band.

## Do

- Exactly three cells; the grid is three columns from the large breakpoint.
- Leave `brand` out for a client the client registry knows (`clientBrand(name)` from `@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`): the face reads its colours, and its ink, by `name`. Add a missing client to the registry rather than writing its hex colours into the page.
- Pass `brand` only for a one-off client the registry does not carry: `base` and `glow` may be any CSS colour, and `ink` is `'dark'` when the face is light enough that the link text must be dark. A cell with neither paints a black face.

## Don’t

- For a mixed mosaic of stories and marks → use `client-mosaic`.

## Related

- `client-mosaic` — the bento sibling.
- `logo-wall` — the single-mark wall each column's face is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of stories. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label the mark face reveals on hover and the link's accessible name. |
| `cells` | `ClientMosaicColumnsCell[]` | `[]` | false | The stories, in order; each is `{ name, logo, href, story, brand?, logoTreatment? }` where `brand` is `{ base, glow, ink? }` (CSS colours painting the face, `ink` `'dark'` or `'light'`) and defaults to the client registry's colours for `name` and `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'`, `'knockout'` or `'as-is'`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` on each column (the face reveals the link line, the story fill rises)
- The face colours are bound as the `--wall-face` and `--wall-ink` custom properties from `brand`, or from the client registry by `name` when `brand` is left out; `data-treatment` on every mark drives its ink
- Empty: when `cells` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link is `logo-wall`'s, with its ring; the story panel is a duplicate link hidden from the tab order and from assistive technology.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the three mark links; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>`; the grid is a list named by `ariaLabel` whose items are the columns; each mark carries the client `name` as `alt`; the story panel is `aria-hidden` with `tabindex="-1"` so the case is reachable once.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the link line ink follows `brand.ink`; the story text is `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-canvas)`.
- `motion-reduce:before:transition-none` on the hover fill.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark face spans its column.

<!-- components/client-quotes.md -->

# Client Quotes

> The client-stories band: a framed `quote-tabs` carousel of customer quotes, each signed by its author and marked by the client's logo, with one call to action under it. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'client-quotes', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `quote-tabs` and `button`.

- Import: `import ClientQuotes from '@aziontech/webkit/client-quotes'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To let several customers speak in turn, one at a time, near the end of a page's argument.

## Do

- Three to six items; the tabs need room for each client's mark.
- Give each item either a registry `mark` or a `logo` URL with `clientName`, not both.
- On azion.com the client wall is in each brand's colours, not one ink: give each client its logo file from the package, `import gpa from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/gpa-extended-color.svg'`, then `logo: gpa`. On the dark site use `-extended-color.svg` where the colour logo reads on black (GPA, Zoop, HeroSpark, Magalu) and `-extended-reversed.svg` where the colour logo has dark lettering (Axur, Contabilizei, Dafiti, Global Fashion Group as `gfg`); on a light page use `-extended-color.svg`. A registry `mark` (one ink, follows the theme) is for a client that ships no logo file. `catalog.json` lists every file under `imports` with `"kind": "asset"`.
- Every item needs its quotation (`text`): a card is a tab that features it, and an item without one is skipped. Do not invent a quotation to fill the wall; list the clients you have quotes for, or use `logo-wall-quote` for one quotation beside a logo wall.
- The band advances on a timer like azion.com's. Set `:autoplay="false"` when the page must hold one quote (a still capture, a page with other moving content), and bind `v-model` (the selected index) to open on a quote other than the first; never wrap or re-time the band yourself.

## Don’t

- For one quote beside a logo wall → use `logo-wall-quote`.
- For a scrolling strip of analyst recognitions → use `recognition-marquee`.

## Related

- `quote-tabs` — the tabbed quote carousel this band frames.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the quote carousel. |
| `items` | `ClientQuotesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The quotes, in order; each is `{ text, name?, jobTitle?, mark?, logo?, clientName?, photo? }` where `mark` is a registry mark name and `logo` a mark URL named by `clientName`. |
| `primaryAction` | `ClientQuotesAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the quotes; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Advances to the next quote on a timer, as `quote-tabs` does; pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion. |
| `autoplayInterval` | `number` | `5000` | false | Milliseconds each quote is held before the band advances. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | `0` | false | Two-way value (`v-model`). |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## v-model

| Model | Type | Default | Emits | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v-model` | `number` | `0` | `update:modelValue` | Index of the selected quote, passed through to `quote-tabs`; left unbound the band starts on the first quote. A click, an arrow key or the timer writes the new index back. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when no item carries `text` the band renders nothing; an item without `text` is skipped, and the `v-model` index counts the quotes that remain
- The active quote, its progress and the tab keyboard model belong to `quote-tabs`; `autoplay`, `autoplayInterval` and `v-model` are passed straight through to it

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed components.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each link or button; `Enter` follows it.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every affordance is a large `button` or spans its cell.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the carousel is `quote-tabs`' own labelled region (`ariaLabel`), so no second landmark is added.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the tab transition belongs to `quote-tabs`; this band adds no motion.

<!-- components/closing-call-to-action.md -->

# Closing Call To Action

> The last ask at the end of a landing page, followed by a hatched closing frame with no rules of its own, because the site footer under it opens with one. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `call-to-action`, `button`, `frame-box` and `texture-material`. `kind` picks the layout only: `split` sets the headline and the primary action in a raised lead cell beside an aside cell carrying the description and the secondary action, over a tall closing frame; `panel` sets the copy and its actions on one surface, over a short closing frame; `primary` is the loud close, one centred ask on the canvas under a pixelated texture whose waves keep travelling, over a tall closing frame. All three take the same copy and the same two actions.

- Import: `import ClosingCallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a solution or product page on its one or two asks (`split`), or a page such as Careers on one action (`panel`), or a page that ends on its one loud ask (`primary`).

## Do

- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `FrameBox` + `TextureMaterial` (the `shells/website` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.
- Set `anchor: 'contact'` so the page's contact links scroll to the close.
- In `split`, keep `title` and `titleMuted` to one short line each; `panel` and `primary` do not draw `titleMuted`, and `primary` does not draw `eyebrow`.

## Don’t

- For a newsletter sign-up close → use `closing-call-to-action-newsletter`.
- For an ask in the middle of a page → compose `call-to-action` directly.

## Related

- `call-to-action` — the framed band this section renders.
- `closing-call-to-action-newsletter` — the closing band whose ask is a subscribe form.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `ClosingCallToActionKind` | `'split'` | false | Layout of the band: `split` is a raised lead cell beside an aside cell over a tall closing frame, `panel` one surface over a short closing frame, `primary` a centred ask under a pixelated texture over a tall closing frame. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline; not drawn in `primary`. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the call to action as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `titleMuted` | `string` | `''` | false | Second line of the headline in muted ink; drawn in `split` only. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence: in the aside cell in `split`, under the headline in `panel`. |
| `primaryAction` | `ClosingCallToActionAction` | `undefined` | false | The white button of the band, under the headline in `split`; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ClosingCallToActionAction` | `undefined` | false | The outlined button of the band, in the aside cell in `split` and beside the primary one in `panel` and `primary`; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and drives the call-to-action layout and the closing frame height
- `primary`: the call to action takes its `primary` register with a pixelated `texture-material` in its `background` slot; its waves stop under reduced motion (owned by `texture-material`)
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root
- Each action renders only when given

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed buttons.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the primary then the secondary action; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the `call-to-action` renders the band's `<section>` named by its title; the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark. The closing frame is decorative.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `call-to-action` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the texture and the buttons carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the actions are large buttons.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ClosingCallToAction from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action'

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Start for free',
    href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup?tck=build_cta'
  }

  const secondaryAction = {
    label: 'Talk to a specialist',
    href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/contact/',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ClosingCallToAction
    kind="split"
    anchor="contact"
    eyebrow="Build"
    title="Build once."
    title-muted="Run everywhere."
    description="Get a faster path to launch, lower latency, and less infrastructure overhead."
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
    :secondary-action="secondaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/closing-call-to-action.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/closing-call-to-action.md).

<!-- components/closing-call-to-action-agents.md -->

# Closing Call To Action Agents

> The close for a reader who may be a person or an agent: one centred ask in the loud `primary` register of the call to action, under a pixelated, waving texture, with a small segmented switch under the title that picks the way in. Each audience carries an optional copyable line and its actions; under them, a line types its words one after another behind a blinking cursor, then a closing sentence, both the same for every audience so the band keeps its height when the switch changes. The hatched closing frame follows. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action-agents', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `call-to-action`, `toggle-group`, `input-group`, `copy-button`, `button`, `frame-box` and `texture-material`. The switch and the typed word are local state.

- Import: `import ClosingCallToActionAgents from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action-agents'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a developer page whose reader may be a person or the person's agent.

## Do

- Keep two audiences; the first one opens.
- Keep each copyable line short enough to fit the field; the copy button copies exactly what it shows.
- Keep `typedWords` to a few short words; screen readers and reduced motion get the whole list at once.
- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `FrameBox` + `TextureMaterial` (the `shells/website` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.

## Don’t

- For a close on one or two link actions → use `closing-call-to-action` (`primary` for the same loud register without the switch).
- For a newsletter sign-up → use `closing-call-to-action-newsletter`.

## Related

- `closing-call-to-action` — the same close without the audience switch.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the call to action as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `typedLead` | `string` | `''` | false | Fixed opening of the typed line, before the typed word. |
| `typedWords` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Words typed, held, erased and typed again in order after `typedLead`; the typed line renders only when there are words. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Closing sentence under the typed line, the same for every audience. |
| `audiences` | `ClosingCallToActionAgentsAudience[]` | `[]` | false | The ways in, in switch order; each is `{ value, label, copy?, actions? }` and the first one opens. The switch renders only with two or more. |
| `audiencesAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the audience switch. |
| `lineAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the read-only field that shows an audience's copyable line. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Audience switch: picking an audience swaps the copyable line and the actions; the swapped row sits in a polite live region and fades in
- Typed word: after mount the words are typed (90 ms a character), held (1.8 s), erased (45 ms a character) and the next one typed (after 270 ms), in a loop; the timer is cleared on scope dispose
- Reduced motion: the typed word shows every word at once, joined by commas, and the cursor is hidden
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; an audience without `copy` shows no field; without `typedWords` the typed line is omitted

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `toggle-group`, `copy-button` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the switch, the copy button and each action; the arrow keys move the switch (owned by `toggle-group`).
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div`; the call to action owns the band's named region. The switch is a `radiogroup` named by `audiencesAriaLabel`; the swapped row is `aria-live="polite"`; the read-only field is named by `lineAriaLabel` and the copy button by the audience's `copy.label`. The typed line reads its whole sentence from a visually hidden copy while the animated letters are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): the typed line uses `var(--text-muted)` and `var(--text-default)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — see the Motion table; under reduced motion nothing types or blinks.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the switch, the copy button and the actions are large.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ClosingCallToActionAgents from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action-agents'

  const typedWords = ['Console', 'CLI', 'MCP server']

  const audiences = [
    {
      value: 'humans',
      label: 'For humans',
      actions: [
        {
          label: 'Start for free',
          href: '/signup',
          kind: 'secondary',
          trailing: true
        },
        {
          label: 'Talk to a specialist',
          href: '/site/contact',
          kind: 'outlined',
          trailing: true
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      value: 'agents',
      label: 'For agents',
      copy: {
        label: 'Copy prompt',
        text: 'Connect Azion MCP: https://mcp.azion.com'
      },
      actions: [
        {
          label: 'Read the agent docs',
          href: '/site/docs/agent-setup',
          kind: 'outlined',
          trailing: true
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ClosingCallToActionAgents
    anchor="contact"
    title="Built by you, or your agents."
    typed-lead="Drive one platform from the"
    :typed-words="typedWords"
    description="A person and an agent ship the same way."
    audiences-aria-label="Audience"
    line-aria-label="Prompt"
    :audiences="audiences"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/closing-call-to-action-newsletter.md -->

# Closing Call To Action Newsletter

> The closing band whose ask is a newsletter sign-up: the overline and a large headline on the lead side, a subscribe form labelled by the ask on the other, over a strip lit by the pixelated primary wave, then the hatched closing frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action-newsletter', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `overline`, `field`, `input`, `button` and `texture-material`. The block never sends: it validates the address locally (an empty field and a malformed address each show their message under the field) and on a valid submit emits `submit` with the event and `{ email }`; the site posts the address and reports the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `error`, which the band renders with the messages from `form`.

- Import: `import ClosingCallToActionNewsletter from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action-newsletter'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close the Blog or the Resource Hub on a newsletter subscription.

## Do

- Set `loading` while the address is sent, then `submitted` or `error` with the outcome.
- Keep `description` to one sentence; it is set as the large headline.
- Write `form.invalidMessage` with an example address so the fix is obvious.
- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `FrameBox` + `TextureMaterial` (the `shells/website` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.

## Don’t

- For a close on one or two link actions → use `closing-call-to-action`.
- For a lead form with several fields → use `hero-form`.

## Related

- `closing-call-to-action` — the closing band whose ask is a link action.
- `alert` — renders the success and failure messages.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `ClosingCallToActionNewsletterForm` | `—` | true | Copy of the subscribe form: `{ placeholder, submitLabel, successMessage, errorMessage, requiredMessage, invalidMessage }`. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline on the lead side, closed by the blinking cursor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | The ask, rendered as the label of the email field; it also names the band. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | The pitch, rendered as the band's large `h2` on the lead side. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site is sending the address: the field is disabled, the button shows its loading state and a submit is ignored. |
| `submitted` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site sent the address: the form gives way to `form.successMessage`. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site could not send the address: `form.errorMessage` shows under the form. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, values: Record<string, string>)` | Fired on a valid submit, not while `loading`; `values` is `{ email }` with the trimmed address. The block never sends it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `invalid`, `loading`, `submitted`, `error`
- `invalid`: an empty field takes the amber `required` state with `form.requiredMessage`, a malformed address the red `invalid` state with `form.invalidMessage`, under the field (never both at once); focus returns to the field; typing clears it; nothing is emitted
- `loading` (prop): the field is disabled, the button shows its loading state and a submit emits nothing
- `submitted` (prop): the form is replaced by a success `Alert` with `form.successMessage`, which takes focus when focus was in the form
- `error` (prop): a danger `Alert` with `form.errorMessage` shows under the form, which stays editable

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `input` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the field then the button; `Enter` in the field or on the button submits.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the ask is a `<label for>` bound to the field with `useId`; the field is an `<input type="email">` with `autocomplete="email"` and `spellcheck="false"`; the validation message is the field's helper text, an empty submit sets `aria-required` and a malformed address `aria-invalid`. The success message is a `status` region and the failure message an `alert`. The texture strip is `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline and ask `var(--text-default)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the texture and the button carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the field and the button are large.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ClosingCallToActionNewsletter from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action-newsletter'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const form = {
    placeholder: 'Your email',
    submitLabel: 'Subscribe',
    successMessage: 'Thanks for subscribing to the Azion newsletter',
    errorMessage: 'We could not subscribe you. Try again.',
    requiredMessage: 'Enter your email address.',
    invalidMessage: 'Enter an email address like name@example.com.'
  }

  const subscribedEmail = ref('')

  const onSubmit = (event, values) => {
    subscribedEmail.value = values.email
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ClosingCallToActionNewsletter
    anchor="contact"
    eyebrow="Stay up to date"
    title="Subscribe to our newsletter"
    description="Product updates, event highlights, and industry insights, delivered to your inbox."
    :form="form"
    :submitted="subscribedEmail !== ''"
    @submit="onSubmit"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/closing-call-to-action-templates.md -->

# Closing Call To Action Templates

> The close for a page whose last ask is "start from a template": a framed split whose start cell carries the ask — headline, sentence and two actions, start-aligned — over the pixelated, waving texture of the `primary` close, and whose end cell is a scrolling two-column grid of deployable template cards, each with its mark, name, one line and a deploy button, its top and bottom fading out; then the tall hatched closing frame. Below `lg` the cells stack, the ask first. It merges the `primary` close of `closing-call-to-action` with the scrolling template wall of `template-gallery`. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'closing-call-to-action-templates', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `scroll-area`, `card-grid`, `card-grid-cell`, `frame-box` and `texture-material`.

- Import: `import ClosingCallToActionTemplates from '@aziontech/webkit/closing-call-to-action-templates'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a framework, solution or developer page on a ready-to-deploy start rather than on a sign-up alone.

## Do

- Give the grid six to eight templates so it overflows its height and reads as scrollable; an even count keeps its two columns full.
- Keep each template line to one short sentence so the cards keep one height.
- Give every card an `href` and set `deployLabel`, or no card shows its deploy button.
- Place it last on the page, right above `site-footer`, after a hatched `section-gap`. It draws the hatched closing frame itself, so nothing follows it inside the page column: no trailing `SectionGap` and no closing `FrameBox` + `TextureMaterial` (the `shells/website` close is for a page that ends on any other band). `webkit/no-gap-after-closing-section` flags the doubled close.

## Don’t

- For a close on one or two link actions → use `closing-call-to-action` (`primary` for the same loud register without the templates).
- For a mid-page band that browses many templates beside its copy → use `template-gallery`.
- For a close whose reader may be an agent → use `closing-call-to-action-agents`.

## Related

- `closing-call-to-action` — the `primary` close, centred, without the template grid.
- `template-gallery` — a scrolling wall of templates beside its copy, as a mid-page band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` and naming its region; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `ClosingCallToActionTemplatesAction` | `undefined` | false | The white button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ClosingCallToActionTemplatesAction` | `undefined` | false | The outlined button beside the primary one; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `templates` | `ClosingCallToActionTemplatesTemplate[]` | `[]` | false | The template cards of the scrolling grid beside the copy, in order; each is `{ title, description?, icon?, invertInDark?, href? }`. Templates without a title are skipped and the grid is omitted when none is left. |
| `deployLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the deploy button on each card; a card renders its button only when both this and its `href` are set. |
| `templatesAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling grid of templates. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Hovering a card shows the pointer cursor and lights its deploy button
- Layout: from `lg` up the ask and the grid sit side by side; below it they stack, the ask first, and the grid drops to one column below `sm`
- Overflow: the grid holds a fixed height (32rem, 38rem from `lg`) and scrolls vertically, its top and bottom fading out
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; without titled templates the grid is omitted and the ask stands alone in the band; a card without `href` (or without `deployLabel`) shows no deploy button

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`s.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the band's two actions, then the scrolling grid and each card's deploy link in reading order; the arrow keys scroll the focused grid; `Enter` follows a link.
- ARIA: the root is a plain `div`; the split is a `section` region named by `title`, whose headline is the `h2`. The scrolling grid is `scroll-area`'s region named by `templatesAriaLabel`; the texture and the template marks are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): card titles `var(--text-default)`, card lines `var(--text-muted)`; marks flagged `invertInDark` invert under the dark theme.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the waving texture, the button hover and the scrolling belong to `texture-material`, `button` and `scroll-area`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the band's actions are large `button`s, the deploy buttons medium.

## Examples

<!-- components/code-split.md -->

# Code Split

> The claim-beside-its-code band of a product page: a framed media split whose copy states the claim, with one or two large buttons under it, and whose media is a code sample on the pixelate texture, cut off by the frame's bottom rule. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'code-split', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `code-block` and `button`. One tab draws a filename bar; several draw a tab strip, and a tab that carries an `icon` shows that mark beside its label.

- Import: `import CodeSplit from '@aziontech/webkit/code-split'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- When the argument of a product page is a config file or a handler a developer can read, like Functions, Application Accelerator or AI Gateway.

## Do

- Keep the sample short enough to read in the cell; the frame cuts off whatever runs past it.
- Give every tab a `code`; a tab without one is skipped.
- Use `primaryAction` alone for one destination, and add `secondaryAction` only for a second, distinct one.
- Set an action's `kind` to `transparent` for a quiet text link such as "Learn more" (the product pages' Cache, Application Accelerator and Image Processor bands); leave it unset for the filled `secondary` first button and the `outlined` second one.

## Don’t

- For a terminal session under a headline → use `cli-terminal`.
- For a run of capabilities, each with its own sample, pinned while the page scrolls → use `sticky-scroll-code`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the copy-beside-media band this section renders through.
- `code-block` — the tabbed code sample in the media cell.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `codeTabs` | `CodeSplitTab[]` | `[]` | false | The files of the code sample, in order; each is `{ label, value, code, language?, fileName?, fileIcon?, icon? }` where `icon` is a mark drawn beside the tab label. A tab without `code` is skipped. |
| `copyAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the sample's copy button; empty keeps the code block's own. |
| `primaryAction` | `CodeSplitAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, kind? }` where `kind` defaults to `secondary`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `CodeSplitAction` | `undefined` | false | Second button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, icon?, target?, kind? }` where `kind` defaults to `outlined`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the tab strip, copy button and buttons own their hover and focus states
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when no tab carries `code` the media cell is left out
- One tab draws a filename bar, several draw a tab strip; a tab mark renders only when some tab carries an `icon`
- An action's `kind` (`secondary`, `outlined` or `transparent`) picks its button; without it the first action is `secondary` and the second `outlined`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `code-block` (tabs, copy button) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the tabs, the copy button and the buttons; arrow keys move between tabs (owned by `code-block`); `Enter` follows a button.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the named landmark is `media-split`'s own section (labelled by `title`), so no second landmark is added; tab marks are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `media-split`, `code-block` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the sample's line entrance is owned by `code-block`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the large buttons.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import CodeSplit from '@aziontech/webkit/code-split'

  const codeTabs = [
    {
      label: 'cache-settings.json',
      value: 'cache-settings',
      language: 'json',
      code: '{\n  "cache_settings": {\n    "name": "api-cache",\n    "browser_cache_settings": {\n      "ttl": 60\n    },\n    "cdn_cache_settings": {\n      "ttl": 30\n    },\n    "cache_key": {\n      "query_string": "whitelist",\n      "query_string_fields": ["user_id", "category"],\n      "cookie": "whitelist",\n      "cookie_names": ["session_id", "region"]\n    },\n    "methods": ["GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"],\n    "stale_cache": true\n  }\n}',
      fileName: 'cache-settings.json',
      fileIcon: 'ai ai-json'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Learn more',
    href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/build/applications/application-accelerator/',
    trailing: true,
    kind: 'transparent'
  }
</script>

<template>
  <CodeSplit
    title="From basic caching to advanced acceleration"
    description="Application Accelerator extends Cache with protocol optimizations and advanced cache rules for dynamic content."
    :code-tabs="codeTabs"
    copy-aria-label="Copy the cache settings sample"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```
