<!-- components/compare-plans.md -->

# Compare Plans

> The feature-by-feature matrix under the plan cards on Pricing: one column per plan with its name and action button pinned in the header while the page scrolls, one band per product with an overline, a title and a lead, and one row per feature saying what each plan includes — a tick, a dash, or the allowance as text. The recommended plan carries an accent bar, and below the large breakpoint the table folds to one plan picked from a select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'compare-plans', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `select`, `button`, `overline`, `hint`, `tag` and `link`.

- Import: `import ComparePlans from '@aziontech/webkit/compare-plans'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On Pricing, under the plan cards, to show what every plan includes product by product.

## Do

- Give every plan a stable `id`; the narrow-screen picker selects by it.
- Mark one plan `highlighted`; it gets the accent bar, the secondary button and opens the picker.
- Give every row's `values` one entry per plan, in plan order.

## Don’t

- To compare support tiers → use `compare-support-tiers`.
- To compare Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.

## Related

- `pricing-plans` — the plan cards this matrix sits under.
- `compare-support-tiers` — the same matrix for the Support page.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader caption naming the table. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the feature column, shown from the large breakpoint up. |
| `pickerAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the plan picker shown below the large breakpoint. |
| `includedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader text of a ticked cell. |
| `excludedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader text of a dashed cell. |
| `plans` | `ComparePlansPlan[]` | `[]` | false | The plan columns, in order; each is `{ id, name, description?, highlighted?, action }` with `action` as `{ label, href }`; a plan without a name is dropped. |
| `sections` | `ComparePlansSection[]` | `[]` | false | The product bands, in order; each is `{ eyebrow, title, description, rows, link? }` (`link` closes the band, `{ label, href }`) and a row is `{ label, values, group?, hint?, tag? }` with one value per plan: `true` or `✓` ticks, `—` dashes, other text shows as written, empty is blank. |
| `primaryAction` | `ComparePlansAction` | `undefined` | false | Closing link under the table, opened in a new tab; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The highlighted plan carries the accent bar and the secondary button; the others carry an outlined button
- Below the large breakpoint only the picked plan's column shows (`data-folded` on the others); the picker opens on the highlighted plan, or the first
- Below the large breakpoint the plan button's label wraps (auto height, at least 40 px) instead of widening the table, so the folded matrix fits a 320 px screen whatever the font metrics.
- A group row (`group: true`) reads in the default text colour and draws a top rule unless it opens its band
- Empty: when no plan has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `select`, `button`, `hint` and `link`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the picker (below `lg`), each plan button, each hint and the closing link; the picker's keyboard map is `select`'s.
- ARIA: the table carries a `caption`, `scope="col"` plan heads, a `scope="colgroup"` head per band and a `scope="row"` head per feature, so each value is announced with its row and plan. The tick and dash glyphs are `aria-hidden` and carry `includedLabel` / `excludedLabel` as `sr-only` text; the accent bar is decorative; the plan names stay readable to screen readers below `lg`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the composed controls carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the plan buttons and the picker are `large`.
- Reflow: below `lg` (one plan column beside the row labels) the header cells, the section headings and the row labels use `var(--spacing-sm)` side padding instead of `var(--spacing-lg)`, so the two columns fit a 640px box at 200% zoom; from `lg` the padding is unchanged.

## Examples

### Band links

```vue
<script setup>
  import ComparePlans from '@aziontech/webkit/compare-plans'

  const plans = [
    {
      id: 'hobby',
      name: 'Hobby',
      description: 'For side projects.',
      action: { label: 'Start for free', href: '/signup' }
    },
    {
      id: 'pro',
      name: 'Pro',
      description: 'For teams in production.',
      highlighted: true,
      action: { label: 'Start trial', href: '/signup?plan=pro' }
    }
  ]

  const sections = [
    {
      eyebrow: 'Compute',
      title: 'Functions',
      description: 'Run code close to users.',
      rows: [
        { label: 'Requests per month', values: ['1M', '10M'] },
        { label: 'Custom domains', values: [true, true] },
        { label: 'Usage alerts', values: ['—', true] }
      ],
      link: { label: 'See compute rates', href: '/pricing/compute' }
    },
    {
      eyebrow: 'Storage',
      title: 'Object Storage',
      rows: [
        { label: 'Storage included', values: ['5 GB', '100 GB'] },
        { label: 'Versioning', values: ['—', true] }
      ],
      link: { label: 'See storage rates', href: '/pricing/storage' }
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ComparePlans
    caption="Hobby and Pro compared feature by feature"
    column-label="Features"
    picker-aria-label="Plan being compared"
    included-label="Included"
    excluded-label="Not included"
    :plans="plans"
    :sections="sections"
  />
</template>
```

# Compare Support Tiers

> The tier-by-tier comparison on the Support page: one column per support tier with its name, who it is for and its action button pinned in the header while the page scrolls, one band per service family with an overline and a title, and one row per service saying what each tier includes — a tick, a dash, or the allowance as text. Each band closes on its own link to the matching pricing documentation, the recommended tier carries an accent bar, and below the large breakpoint the table folds to one tier picked from a select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'compare-support-tiers', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `select`, `button`, `overline` and `link`.

- Import: `import CompareSupportTiers from '@aziontech/webkit/compare-support-tiers'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the Support page, to show what each support tier includes service by service.

## Do

- Give every tier a stable `id`; the narrow-screen picker selects by it.
- Mark one tier `highlighted`; it gets the accent bar, the secondary button and opens the picker.
- Give every row's `values` one entry per tier, in tier order.

## Don’t

- To compare platform plans → use `compare-plans`.
- To compare Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.

## Related

- `compare-plans` — the same matrix for platform plans, with hints and tags on rows and one closing link.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader caption naming the table. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the service column, shown from the large breakpoint up. |
| `pickerAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tier picker shown below the large breakpoint. |
| `includedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader text of a ticked cell. |
| `excludedLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader text of a dashed cell. |
| `tiers` | `CompareSupportTiersTier[]` | `[]` | false | The tier columns, in order; each is `{ id, name, description, highlighted?, action }` with `action` as `{ label, href }`; a tier without a name is dropped. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The highlighted tier carries the accent bar and the secondary button; the others carry an outlined button
- The header row is sticky under `--layout-header-height` (the SiteNav bar's token), so the tier names and buttons stay in view under the site header; the service column's label sits at the start of its corner cell, as on azion.com's Support page
- Below `md` the band titles are set one step larger (`text-heading-xl`) and the header cells take `--spacing-md` top and bottom (their sides stay `--spacing-sm`, see Reflow below), so a band title breaks over two lines and the picker row has the site's height
- Below the large breakpoint only the picked tier's column shows (`data-folded` on the others); the picker opens on the highlighted tier, or the first
- A group row (`group: true`) reads in the default text colour and draws a top rule unless it opens its band
- Empty: when no tier has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `select`, `button` and `link`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the picker (below `lg`), each tier button and each band's closing link; the picker's keyboard map is `select`'s.
- ARIA: the table carries a `caption`, `scope="col"` tier heads, a `scope="colgroup"` head per band and a `scope="row"` head per service, so each value is announced with its row and tier. The tick and dash glyphs are `aria-hidden` and carry `includedLabel` / `excludedLabel` as `sr-only` text; the accent bar is decorative; the tier names stay readable to screen readers below `lg`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the composed controls carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the tier buttons and the picker are `large`.
- Reflow: below `lg` (one tier column beside the row labels) the header cells, the section headings and the row labels use `var(--spacing-sm)` side padding instead of `var(--spacing-lg)`, so the two columns fit a 640px box at 200% zoom; from `lg` the padding is unchanged.

<!-- components/comparison-table.md -->

# Comparison Table

> The capability-by-capability comparison of Azion with one competitor on a migration landing page: a left section title over a framed table whose header row (the capability column, the Azion brand and the competitor logo) stays pinned while the page scrolls. Each category opens with a heading row; each cell is a support glyph — full, partial or none — named by a tooltip and by screen-reader text, and a capability with a definition carries an info button that opens it in a popover. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'comparison-table', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `brand`, `popover`, `icon-button` and `tooltip`.

- Import: `import ComparisonTable from '@aziontech/webkit/comparison-table'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On a "Azion vs X" page, to lay one competitor against Azion across a few categories of capabilities.

## Do

- Give every row a `definition`; the info popover is where a reader learns what the capability means.
- Ship both `competitor.logo` (dark theme) and `competitor.logoLight` (light theme); with one file it shows in both, with none the name shows as text.
- Keep `caption` equal to the title; it is the table's accessible name.

## Don’t

- To compare Azion's own plans → use `compare-plans`.
- To compare support tiers → use `compare-support-tiers`.

## Related

- `compare-plans` — the plan-by-plan matrix of Pricing.
- `tooltip` — names each support glyph on hover and focus.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2` and naming the band; no header renders when empty. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | false | Screen-reader caption naming the table. |
| `columnLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Heading of the capability column. |
| `fullLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of a full-support cell. |
| `partialLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of a partial-support cell. |
| `noneLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Tooltip and screen-reader text of an unsupported cell. |
| `competitor` | `ComparisonTableCompetitor` | `—` | true | The platform compared with Azion; `{ name, logo?, logoLight? }` where `logo` is the dark-theme file and `logoLight` the light-theme one. |
| `groups` | `ComparisonTableGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The categories, in order; each is `{ title, rows }` and a row is `{ capability, definition?, azion?, competitor? }` with each level `full`, `partial` or `none` (missing reads as `none`). |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- A support cell is one of `full`, `partial` or `none`, mirrored on the glyph's `data-support`
- Without a competitor logo the header shows the competitor name as text
- Empty: when `groups` is empty the band renders nothing but its root — no header, no table

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `icon-button` and `tooltip` triggers.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each definition's info button; `Enter` / `Space` opens its popover and `Esc` closes it (owned by `popover`).
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the table carries a `caption`, `scope="col"` heads, a `scope="colgroup"` head per category and a `scope="row"` head per capability, so each value is announced with its row and column. The glyphs are `aria-hidden` and every cell carries its level as `sr-only` text; each logo has the platform name as `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text and glyph colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the popover and tooltip carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the info button is a small `icon-button`, a secondary affordance next to the capability name.

<!-- components/compliance-badges.md -->

# Compliance Badges

> The compliance band: a framed media split whose copy states the certifications and whose media is a frame grid of badges, each a picture over a check-marked pill, closed by a "see more" cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'compliance-badges', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `media-split` and `card-grid`.

- Import: `import ComplianceBadges from '@aziontech/webkit/compliance-badges'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On security, enterprise or pricing pages, to list the certifications and link to the compliance page.

## Do

- Four or five certifications plus the link cell fill two rows of three.
- Give every badge an `alt` naming the certification; the pill repeats it for sighted readers.

## Don’t

- For client logos → use `logo-wall-quote` or `client-mosaic`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the copy-beside-media band this section renders through.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the badge list. |
| `certifications` | `ComplianceBadgesCertification[]` | `[]` | false | The badges, in order; each is `{ label, badge, alt }` where `badge` is the picture URL and `label` the pill text. |
| `primaryAction` | `ComplianceBadgesAction` | `undefined` | false | The closing "see more" cell; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on the see-more cell
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when `certifications` is empty the media holds only the see-more cell, if any

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the see-more cell carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the see-more link; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the named landmark is `media-split`'s own section (labelled by `title`), so no second landmark is added; the badge grid is a list (`role="list"` named by `ariaLabel`) of list items; each badge image carries its `alt`; the check bubble and chevron are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): pill `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-surface-raised)`; see-more `var(--text-muted)` rising to `var(--text-default)` on hover.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on both transitions above.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the see-more cell is a full grid cell.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the "more" chevron mirrors (`rtl:-scale-x-100`) and its hover nudge moves toward the end edge.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import pciDssSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/pci-dss-symbol-color.svg'
  import socSymbolColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/soc-symbol-color.svg'
  import ComplianceBadges from '@aziontech/webkit/compliance-badges'
</script>

<template>
  <ComplianceBadges
    eyebrow="Compliance"

      {
        label: 'SOC 2 & 3',

        alt: 'AICPA SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 badge'

      {
        label: 'LGPD',
        badge: lgpdSymbolColor,

      }

  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/console-panel.md -->

# Console Panel

> A full-width framed panel that presents a product scene (a console mock or a diagram) under a section title, on a texture, with optional tabs that each play one beat of the scene. The scene is a slot: the page passes a `ShellMockup`, `ProductWidget` or diagram and reads the selected tab from the slot scope. In `console` kind the scene keeps a 1.9:1 aspect and can be cropped and faded at the bottom. From the design sample's site `ConsolePanel`.

- Import: `import ConsolePanel from '@aziontech/webkit/console-panel'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Showing the product itself on a landing page.
- A tour of three or four views of one screen.

## Do

- Two to four tabs, each a different view, labelled with one word.
- Crop the scene only to remove empty space at its bottom (0.1–0.3).

## Don’t

- For a screenshot with copy beside it — use `MediaSplitBand`.
- For code — use `CodeSplit` or `CliTerminal`.

## Related

- ShellMockup`, `ProductWidget` — scenes it frames.
- ToggleGroup` — the tab control.
- TextureMaterial`, `FrameBox`, `SectionTitle`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'console' \ \| 'diagram'` | `'console'` | false | What the panel frames: `console` crops and fades a console mock at a fixed aspect, `diagram` lets a scene keep its own height. |
| `titleKind` | `SectionTitleKind` | `'centered'` | false | Layout of the headline block. |
| `titlePadding` | `SectionTitlePadding` | `'medium'` | false | Vertical padding of the headline block. |
| `size` | `SectionTitleSize` | `'medium'` | false | Step of the headline on the heading scale. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One or two sentences under the headline. |
| `texture` | `TextureMaterialKind` | `'pixelate'` | false | Texture the panel is grounded with. |
| `textureFade` | `TextureMaterialFade` | `'top'` | false | Axis the texture fades out along. |
| `tabs` | `ConsolePanelTab[]` | `[]` | false | Tabs over the frame, each `{ value, title }`; each plays its own beat of the scene. |
| `tabsAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the tab control; empty uses the built-in "Console views". |
| `crop` | `number` | `0` | false | Share of the scene height clipped off its bottom, from 0 to 0.5, from the medium breakpoint up. |
| `actions` | `ConsolePanelAction[]` | `[]` | false | Buttons under the headline; each is `{ label, href, trailing?, target?, kind? }`; without `kind` the first is secondary and the rest outlined. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scene` | { tab: string \ | undefined }` \| The scene the band presents; `tab` is the selected tab value (undefined without tabs). |

## States

- `data-kind` mirrors `kind`.
- The first tab is selected on render.
- `--mockup-fade-start` / `--mockup-fade-end` are set for a `ShellMockup` scene when cropped.

## Accessibility

- A `section` named by its title.
- Tabs are a `ToggleGroup` (radio group) named by `tabsAriaLabel` or "Console views"; arrow keys move between them.
- The scene supplies its own accessible content (a mock is usually `aria-hidden` with a description in the copy).

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

| Key                  | English source  | Override prop   |
| -------------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `consolePanel.views` | `Console views` | `tabsAriaLabel` |

- Every other string is marketing copy passed through props.

## Responsive

- Below medium the console scene is square and uncropped; from medium it is 1.9:1 with the crop applied.
- No horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ConsolePanel from '@aziontech/webkit/console-panel'
  import ShellMockupRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/shell-mockup-root'
  import Tag from '@aziontech/webkit/tag'

  const tabs = [
    { value: 'applications', title: 'Applications' },
    { value: 'metrics', title: 'Metrics' },
    { value: 'logs', title: 'Logs' }
  ]

  const views = {
    applications: { heading: 'Applications', rows: ['storefront', 'checkout-api', 'image-proxy'] },
    metrics: { heading: 'Metrics', rows: ['Requests 1.2M', 'Cache hit 94%', 'Errors 0.02%'] },
    logs: { heading: 'Logs', rows: ['GET /cart 200', 'POST /pay 201', 'GET /img/hero.webp 304'] }
  }
</script>

<template>
  <ConsolePanel
    eyebrow="Console"
    title="One console for every workload"
    description="Deploy, observe and secure from the same place."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :crop="0.2"
  >
    <template #scene="{ tab }">
      <ShellMockupRoot
        :title="views[tab ?? 'applications'].heading"
        rail="workloads"
        fade="bottom"
      >
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-sm) p-(--spacing-lg)">
          <span class="text-heading-sm text-(--text-default)">{{
            views[tab ?? 'applications'].heading
          }}</span>
          <div
            v-for="row in views[tab ?? 'applications'].rows"
            :key="row"
            class="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-(--border-default) py-(--spacing-xs) text-body-sm text-(--text-default)"
          >
            {{ row }}
            <Tag
              label="Live"
              severity="success"
              size="small"
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      </ShellMockupRoot>
    </template>
  </ConsolePanel>
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/console-panel.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/console-panel.md).

<!-- components/contact-hub.md -->

# Contact Hub

> The band under the Contact title band: the team lanes side by side (Sales and Support), each with its scope in one sentence and the action that reaches that team, over a row of self-serve channels. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'contact-hub', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `topic` and `button`. A lane can carry a second link to the system status page, so a reader can check for an incident before opening a ticket.

- Import: `import ContactHub from '@aziontech/webkit/contact-hub'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the Contact page, to route a reader to the team or channel that answers them.

## Do

- Give it as many lanes and channels as the page has: both rows balance themselves (`card-grid` `layout: 'balanced'`), so two channels split the row in halves, three in thirds, four into 2 × 2 and five into 3 + 2, with no empty cell.
- Don't pad `channels` to three or drop one to make the row fit.
- Keep each lane's description to one sentence that states what that team handles.
- Set `target: '_blank'` on a channel or status link that leaves the site.

## Don’t

- For a closing ask at the end of a page → use `closing-call-to-action`.
- For a grid of product use cases → use `use-cases`.

## Related

- `topic` — each self-serve channel is a linked topic.
- `use-cases` — the sibling band of icon-led topics.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lanes` | `ContactHubLane[]` | `[]` | false | The team lanes side by side, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, action?, statusLink? }` where `action` is the lane's button and `statusLink` the system status link beside it. |
| `channels` | `ContactHubChannel[]` | `[]` | false | The self-serve channels under the lanes, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, href, target? }`, rendered as a linked topic. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: the lanes frame renders only when `lanes` is set and the channels frame only when `channels` is set; with neither the band renders nothing but its root
- A lane's action and status link render only when given
- Lanes fill rows of up to two and channels rows of up to three, each balanced so every row is full

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the status link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; buttons and topics own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each lane action, the status link and each channel; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is an unnamed `<section>`; each lane heading and each channel is an `h2`, so the outline reads one entry per route. Glyphs and the status dot are `aria-hidden`. A link with `target: '_blank'` carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lane heading `var(--text-muted)`, description `var(--text-default)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the status link's colour transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the status link is at least `h-10` (`min-h-10`), buttons are large, channels are whole-cell links.
- Reflow: the status link has `min-h-10` and wraps its label inside `max-w-full`, so it never overflows a narrow column or a 200% zoom.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ContactHub from '@aziontech/webkit/contact-hub'
</script>

<template>
```

<!-- components/customer-spotlight.md -->

# Customer Spotlight

> A row of client cards, each painted in the client's own colours with its reversed logo; the hovered or focused card opens to reveal its story line and a "Read story" cue, and the whole card links to the success story. Below the large breakpoint the cards stack and stay open. From the design sample's site `CustomerSpotlight`.

- Import: `import CustomerSpotlight from '@aziontech/webkit/customer-spotlight'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Three or four flagship customer stories on a landing page.

## Do

- Three or four cards.
- Use the client's reversed (white) logo; the face paints the client's brand colours.
- Leave `brand` out for a client the client registry knows (`clientBrand(name)` from `@aziontech/webkit/assets/client-registry`): the card reads its colours by `name`. Add a missing client to the registry rather than writing its hex colours into the page. Pass `brand` only for a one-off client the registry does not carry; a card with neither paints a black face.
- One sentence per story line.

## Don’t

- For many clients — use `ClientMosaic` or `LogoWallQuote`.
- For a quotation — use `ClientQuotes` or `LogoWallQuote` `kind="quote"`.

## Related

- ClientMosaic`, `ClientQuotes`, `LogoWallQuote`.
- FrameBox`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cards` | `CustomerSpotlightCard[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in reading order; each is `{ name, logo, logoWidth?, href, description, brand? }`; `brand` (`{ base, glow }`) defaults to the client registry's colours for `name`. A card opens while hovered or focused. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list; empty uses the built-in "Customer stories". |
| `storyLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label revealed under the description while the card is open; empty uses the built-in "Read story". |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |

## States

- Renders nothing without cards.
- Each item carries `data-state=open|closed`; one is open at a time on large screens.

## Accessibility

- A list of links; each link name is "<story label>, <client>: <story line>", so the logo image is decorative (`alt=""`).
- Focus opens the card the same way hover does; the focus ring is drawn inside the card.
- Contrast of the story line: `--text-default` on `--bg-canvas`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the first card is flush at the inline start.
- Icons: `pi-arrow-up-right` is mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

| Key                       | English source     | Override prop |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------- |
| `customerSpotlight.list`  | `Customer stories` | `ariaLabel`   |
| `customerSpotlight.story` | `Read story`       | `storyLabel`  |

- Client names, logos and story lines are content passed through `cards`.

## Responsive

- Below large: cards stack, open, with the logo above the story line.
- From large: one row, open on hover or focus.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import agibankExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/agibank-extended-reversed.svg'
  import americanasExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/americanas-extended-reversed.svg'
  import arezzoExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/arezzo-extended-reversed.svg'
  import CustomerSpotlight from '@aziontech/webkit/customer-spotlight'

  const cards = [
    {
      name: 'Agibank',
      logo: agibankExtendedReversed,
      href: '/customers/agibank',
      description: 'Agibank moved its digital bank to a platform that scales with every campaign.'
    },
    {
      name: 'Americanas',
      logo: americanasExtendedReversed,
      href: '/customers/americanas',
      description: 'Americanas serves Black Friday traffic with no capacity planning.'
    },
    {
      name: 'Arezzo',
      logo: arezzoExtendedReversed,
      href: '/customers/arezzo',
      description: 'Arezzo cut image weight by half across its storefronts.'
    }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <CustomerSpotlight :cards="cards" />
</template>
```

<!-- components/faq-section.md -->

# Faq Section

> The frequently asked questions band near the end of a landing page: the heading in the left column and the questions on the right, each answer closed until the reader opens it, one at a time. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'faq-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module` and `faq`. An answer is a markdown string, so it can run to several paragraphs (split by a blank line) and `- ` bullet lists, and a sentence can carry a link, bold or italic text, all without a slot or `v-html`.

- Import: `import FaqSection from '@aziontech/webkit/faq-section'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To answer the handful of questions a reader still has before the closing call to action.

## Do

- Use one FAQ section per page and give it `anchor: 'faq'` so a page can link straight to it.
- Keep an answer short; links use `[label](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/href)`, bold `**text**` and italic `*text*`.
- Separate paragraphs with a blank line; start each bullet with `- ` and keep the list in its own block.
- Absolute `https://` links open in a new tab; site-relative links stay in the tab.

## Don’t

- For answers that need content beyond paragraphs, bullet lists and inline links (tables, images, code) → compose `faq` with its `answer` slot.
- For a single highlighted question with an action → use `call-to-action`.

## Related

- `faq` — the framed accordion band this section renders.
- `closing-call-to-action` — the band that usually follows it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the FAQ as its `h2` in the left column. |
| `items` | `FaqSectionItem[]` | `[]` | false | The questions in display order; each is `{ question, answer }` where `answer` is markdown carrying paragraphs, bullet lists, links, bold and italic text. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `open` (one answer at a time, owned by the composed accordion)
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing but its root
- An answer renders `[label](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/href)` as a link, `**text**` as bold and `*text*` as italic; any other text is shown as written
- An answer with a blank line or `- ` lines renders as stacked paragraphs and an ARIA list (`role="list"` / `listitem`, inside the accordion's paragraph); a single-paragraph answer renders as inline text, as before

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed accordion triggers and the answer links.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the questions and the links of an open answer; `Enter` / `Space` toggles a question.
- ARIA: the `faq` renders the band's `<section>` labelled by its `h2`; the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark. A link that opens a new tab carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `faq`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the accordion carries its own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by the accordion triggers.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FaqSection from '@aziontech/webkit/faq-section'
</script>

<template>
  <FaqSection
    anchor="faq"
    title="Frequently asked questions"
    :items="[
      {
        question: 'What types of storefronts can I build and deploy on Azion?',
        answer:
          'You can build and deploy storefronts, marketplaces, campaign pages, and supporting retail apps. Any web app or website runs on Azion. The platform also covers much of the backend, for static and dynamic workloads on a distributed architecture.'
      },
      {
        question: 'Which frameworks are compatible?',
        answer:
          'Azion is compatible with modern frameworks such as Next.js, React, Vue, Astro, Angular, Nuxt, Svelte, and others, so you can reuse your current stack without a full rewrite. See the full [frameworks compatibility list](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/en/documentation/products/devtools/azion-edge-runtime/frameworks-compatibility/).'
      },
      {
        question: 'How do preview deployments work?',
        answer:
          'You can validate storefront changes in preview environments before release, share results across teams, and promote approved versions to production with a controlled workflow.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/feature-scroll.md -->

# Feature Scroll

> The walkthrough band of a product page: a large section title over one screen per feature. From the large breakpoint up the features scroll through a sticky stack — the copy advances while the illustration stays pinned in a framed, textured stage with one small action under each step; below it the same features are a three-column grid of media tiles. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-scroll', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `media-tile`, `illustration`, `sticky-stack`, `texture-material` and `button`.

- Import: `import FeatureScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-scroll'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To walk through four to six capabilities of one product, each with a picture of its own.

## Do

- Four to six items; the stack needs enough steps to earn the scroll.
- Give every item an `illustration`; it is the pinned picture on large screens and the tile media on small ones.
- Keep `action` to a short label such as "Docs" — it sits under the step copy at the small size.

## Don’t

- For three reasons with no scroll story → use `feature-tiles`.
- For code-led steps → use `sticky-scroll-code`.

## Related

- `sticky-stack` — the scroll engine the large layout runs on.
- `media-tile` — the cell the small layout renders each feature with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the large section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `FeatureScrollItem[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order; each is `{ title, description, illustration, action? }` where `illustration` is a registry name and `action` is `{ label, href, trailing? }` rendered as a small secondary button under the step. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Below the large breakpoint the features render as a three-column grid of media tiles; from it up they render as a sticky stack whose active step is `sticky-stack`'s own
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frames

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each step's action; `Enter` follows it; the stack's own progression is scroll-driven and never traps focus.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the step headings are `sticky-stack`'s and `media-tile`'s; the texture layer and the pinned illustration are decorative.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the step transition belongs to `sticky-stack`, which carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the per-step action is a small `button` on the large layout only, where pointer precision is available.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FeatureScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-scroll'
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureScroll
    eyebrow="Workloads"
    title="Everything a workload does, one screen at a time"
    description="Scroll through the console a workload is run from: the list, the topology, the domains, the deploy and the rollout. Each screen is the one you get, not a picture of it."
    :items="[
      {
        title: 'Every workload on one list',
        description:
          'See each workload with its domain, status and last deployment, so what is live is never a question.',
        illustration: 'traffic-and-cost-bar-chart',
        action: {
          label: 'Docs',
          href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/workloads/',
          trailing: true
        }
      },
      {
        title: 'Read the deployment topology',
        description:
          'The domains, the application and the firewall a workload serves, drawn as one chain.',
        illustration: 'global-network',
        action: {
          label: 'Docs',
          href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/workloads/',
          trailing: true
        }
      },
      {
        title: 'Domains and TLS, handled',
        description:
          'Add a domain, get its certificate issued and renewed, and set the TLS floor without leaving the page.',
        illustration: 'dns-protection',
        action: {
          label: 'Docs',
          href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/workloads/',
          trailing: true
        }
      },
      {
        title: 'Ship a version in seconds',
        description:
          'Build, upload, propagate and warm the cache, every step streamed as it happens until the version is live everywhere.',
```

<!-- components/feature-tabs.md -->

# Feature Tabs

> The feature walkthrough band of a product page: a left-aligned section title over up to three tabs on one side and the active tab's illustration on the other, closed by a small link under the frame. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tabs', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `media-tabs`, `illustration` and `mini-button`. The tabs advance on a timer that pauses under the pointer or keyboard focus and never runs under reduced motion; that state is owned by `media-tabs`.

- Import: `import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To walk through the two or three features behind one claim, one picture at a time, like Functions' Observability.

## Do

- Keep to three tabs; tabs past the limit are not rendered.
- Give every tab an `illustrationLabel` saying what its picture shows.

## Don’t

- For architectures drawn as diagrams across the full width → use `architecture-tabs`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough of more features → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tabs` — the timed tabs this section renders through.
- `illustration` — the scene each tab shows.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the left section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `tabs` | `FeatureTabsTab[]` | `[]` | false | The features, in order, at most three; each is `{ title, description, illustration, illustrationLabel? }` where `illustration` is a registry name and `illustrationLabel` its accessible name. |
| `primaryAction` | `FeatureTabsAction` | `undefined` | false | Small link under the frame; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the active tab, its progress and the timer are owned by `media-tabs`
- Empty: when `tabs` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the link renders only when `primaryAction` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `media-tabs` (the tabs) and `mini-button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the tabs and the link; the tabs' keys are owned by `media-tabs`.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each illustration is named by its tab's `illustrationLabel`, or decorative when empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-tabs` and `mini-button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the timer never runs under reduced motion (owned by `media-tabs`).
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the tab rows; the link is supplementary to them.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import FeatureTabs from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tabs'

  const tabs = [
    {
      title: 'Trace',
      description:
        'The run as a waterfall: each step placed against the invocation it belongs to, nested where it nested.',
      illustration: 'live-debugging',
      illustrationLabel: 'A trace waterfall of one invocation'
    },
    {
      title: 'Logs',
      description:
        'Structured output on the same clock as the trace, filtered by level, searchable in place.',
      illustration: 'traffic-and-cost-bar-chart',
      illustrationLabel: 'Structured logs filtered by level'
    },
    {
      title: 'Request path',
      description:
        'The workload, application, function and connector it travelled, each captioned with the time spent there.',
      illustration: 'distributed-apis',
      illustrationLabel: 'The path a request took through the platform'
    }
  ]

  const primaryAction = {
    label: 'Open an invocation',
    href: '/product-preview',
    trailing: true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTabs
    eyebrow="Observability"
    title="Inspect every run end-to-end"
    description="Every invocation of a function is traced on the platform itself — spans, logs and the path the request took. Nothing to configure, no storage to attach. Pick a document to open it."
    :tabs="tabs"
    :primary-action="primaryAction"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/feature-tiles.md -->

# Feature Tiles

> The reasons band of a marketing page: an optional centered section title over a frame grid of media tiles, each an image or an illustration above a short heading and a sentence. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-tiles', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `media-tile` and `illustration`. `kind` picks the layout only: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` is three columns with marks on the bottom rule; the tiles keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import FeatureTiles from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tiles'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To state three or four reasons to buy, each with a picture, under a product or pricing argument.

## Do

- Match the tile count to the kind: four tiles for `artwork`, three for `illustrated`.
- Give a tile either `image` (a URL) or `illustration` (a registry name), not both; `scale` only matters with `illustration`.
- Leave `title` empty to drop the header when the band sits under a hero that already states it; set `anchor` when a link above scrolls to the band.

## Don’t

- For linked use cases → use `use-case-links`.
- For a scroll-driven walkthrough with one screen per feature → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `media-tile` — the picture-over-copy cell each tile is rendered with.
- `feature-widgets` — the sibling band whose cells carry an action each.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `FeatureTilesKind` | `'artwork'` | false | Layout of the grid: `artwork` is four columns with marks on every corner, `illustrated` three columns with marks on the bottom rule. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `tiles` | `FeatureTilesTile[]` | `[]` | false | The tiles rendered as frame cells, in order; each is `{ title, description, image?, illustration?, scale? }` where `image` is a picture URL, `illustration` a registry name drawn fluid, and `scale` its media scale. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and drives the column count and the frame marks
- Empty: when `tiles` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each tile's heading is `media-tile`'s; illustrations are decorative and named by the tile's heading.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title` and `media-tile`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import branches from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/branches.svg'
  import personalTokens from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/personal-tokens.svg'
  import FeatureTiles from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-tiles'
</script>

<template>
  <FeatureTiles
    kind="artwork"
    eyebrow="Why Azion"
    title="From commit to live traffic, on one platform"
    description="Build, ship, and run an application on the same platform that serves it — one place to deploy from, one place to watch it from."
    :tiles="[
      {
        image: branches,
        title: 'Build at AI speed.',
        description:
          'Go from commit to a live URL in minutes. Test on a preview, promote when you are ready, and roll back without a rebuild.'
      },
      {
        image: personalTokens,
        title: 'Secure by default.',
        description:
          'Every workload runs in its own isolated environment, with WAF, rate limits, and leading compliance practices. No configuration required.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/feature-tiles.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/feature-tiles.md).

<!-- components/feature-widgets.md -->

# Feature Widgets

> The "three ways to start" band of a product page: a centered section title with up to two calls to action, over a bento grid where every cell is an illustration above a bold-led sentence and one affordance — a link button or a copy button that puts a prompt on the clipboard. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'feature-widgets', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `button`, `frame-box`, `bento-grid`, `illustration` and `button-highlight`.

- Import: `import FeatureWidgets from '@aziontech/webkit/feature-widgets'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To offer the same outcome through two or three entry points (agent, console, terminal), each with its own next step.

## Do

- Give each item exactly one of `action` (a link) or `copy` (text to put on the clipboard).
- Keep `copy.text` self-contained; it is what the reader pastes into their agent.
- Set `anchor` when a hero button scrolls to this band.

## Don’t

- For reasons without an action per cell → use `feature-tiles`.
- For a long argument per feature → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the cells are laid in.
- `button-highlight` — the copy affordance a cell renders when it carries `copy`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`, and the accessible name of the band. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `FeatureWidgetsAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `FeatureWidgetsAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `columns` | `FeatureWidgetsColumns` | `3` | false | Column count of the grid from the medium breakpoint up: `2`, `3` or `4`. |
| `items` | `FeatureWidgetsItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cells, in order; each is `{ title, description, illustration, action?, copy? }` where `action` is `{ label, href }` rendered as an outlined link button and `copy` is `{ label, text }` rendered as a copy button that puts `text` on the clipboard. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the two actions ride with it
- A cell's copy button writes `copy.text` to the clipboard on activation; the feedback is `button-highlight`'s own

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button` and `button-highlight`, which carry the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the header actions and each cell's button; `Enter` / `Space` activates.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the grid is an unnamed `bento-grid` inside that landmark, so the name is not duplicated; the cell lead is a `strong` inside the sentence, not a heading, so the outline stays the band's `h2`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lead `var(--text-default)`, copy `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the buttons' motion carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the cell buttons are medium `button` / `button-highlight`.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: '/signup' }"
    :secondary-action="{ label: 'Docs', href: '/site/docs', trailing: true }"
    :columns="3"
    :items="[
      {
        title: 'Ask your coding agent',
        description:
          'Connect the Azion MCP servers to Claude Code, Cursor or ChatGPT, and the agent creates, instances and routes the function, with a dry run before every write.',
```

<!-- components/hero-band.md -->

# Hero Band

> The opening band of a marketing page: the page `h1` with its overline, accent phrase, sentence and up to two actions, full width above the page column, with an optional client strip on the floor. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-band', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `button` and `illustration`. `kind` picks the layout only: `centered` fills a screen over a dot field with the copy centered, `title-band` is a padded band with the copy centered, `pixel-floor` sets the copy at the start over an animated pixel floor, and `copy-beside-art` sets an illustration beside the copy; every layout takes the same copy, actions and client strip.

- Import: `import HeroBand from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-band'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a home, solution, product, listing or contact page with its headline and main actions.

## Do

- Use `title-band` with `size="large"` for a product page and `size="medium"` for a page whose bands start right under the headline.
- Give `illustration` and `illustrationAriaLabel` only to the `copy-beside-art` layout; the other layouts ignore them.
- Leave `titleLength` at `short` for a headline of up to about seven words: like azion.com, the `centered`, `title-band` and `centered-band` layouts set it on a narrower measure than the sentence under it, so "Certifications and Compliance" breaks over two lines. Use `long` only for a headline that would run to three lines.
- Leave `headerOffset` at its default under `SiteNav`: it takes the bar's `--layout-header-height` out of a band that fills a screen, so the band fills exactly the first screen with it. Set it empty only on a page with no header above the band; never a literal length.

## Don’t

- For a hero followed by a grid of arguments → use `hero-with-opening`.
- For a hero with a topology scene under the copy → use `hero-copy-on-top-art`.
- For a band inside the page column → use `section-module` or a sibling section.

## Related

- `hero` — the band primitive every layout is rendered with.
- hero-title` — the headline block rendered inside it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `HeroBandKind` | `'title-band'` | false | Layout of the band: `centered` fills a screen over a dot field, `title-band` is a padded band, `centered-band` is a large site-wide band with the copy centered, `compact-band` is a short site-wide band with the copy at the start, `pixel-floor` sets the copy over an animated pixel floor, `copy-beside-art` sets an illustration beside the copy. |
| `size` | `HeroBandSize` | `'medium'` | false | Vertical rhythm of the band; `large` is the opening a product page leads with. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `highlight` | `string` | `''` | false | Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent; reads as one sentence with `title`. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `HeroBandAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `HeroBandAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `carouselLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the client strip. |
| `carouselMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the client marks on the band floor, in order; the strip renders only when it has marks. |
| `illustration` | `string` | `''` | false | Registry name of the illustration set beside the copy in the `copy-beside-art` layout. |
| `illustrationAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible description of the illustration. |
| `headerOffset` | `string` | `'var(--layout-header-height)'` | false | Height of the site header above the band, taken out of a band that fills a screen; defaults to the `SiteNav` bar's token, any CSS length, empty for a page with no header above it. |
| `titleLength` | `HeroBandTitleLength` | `'short'` | false | Length of the headline: `short` sets it on the site's narrow headline measure in the centered layouts, so a four-to-seven-word headline breaks over two balanced lines while the sentence under it keeps the full column; `long` lets the headline take the whole column. |
| `plain` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Drops the dot texture of the `centered` layout. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `top` | — | A scene in the window above the copy (`ShellMockup`, `ProductWidget`, a diagram). The design sample's hero scenes render here. |
| `bottom` | — | A scene in the window under the copy; it enters after the copy (`animate-content-enter`, off under reduced motion) and fades at the inline edges on narrow containers. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and drives the hero's height, width, backdrop and the copy alignment
- `data-title-measure="narrow"` on the root when the headline is set on the narrow measure (`titleLength: 'short'` in the `centered`, `title-band` and `centered-band` layouts); the headline then caps at `--container-lg` while the description keeps the column
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root
- The client strip renders only when `carouselMarks` has marks; each action renders only with a label and a link; the illustration renders only in the `copy-beside-art` layout with `illustration` set

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions; the client strip is not focusable.
- ARIA: the hero `<section>` is named by the full headline (`aria-label`); the headline is the page `h1`; the illustration is named by `illustrationAriaLabel`, decorative when empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `hero-title` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the pixel floor and the client strip stop under reduced motion in `texture-material` and `ticker`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the large buttons meet it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

</script>

<template>
  <HeroBand
    kind="title-band"
    size="large"
    eyebrow="Cache"
    title="Deliver content fast, worldwide"
    description="Serve cached content close to users. Cut origin load and keep applications fast during traffic spikes."
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup/' }"
    :secondary-action="{
      label: 'Docs',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      trailing: true
    }"
  />
</template>
```

# Hero Copy On Top Art

> The opening band of a product page whose copy sits centered on top of a topology scene: the page `h1` with its overline, sentence and up to two actions over columns of status cards wired left to right. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-copy-on-top-art', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `button`, `flow` and `tag`. It is a separate section from `hero-band` because the scene is a data model of its own: levels of cards, each with a status and an optional focus.

- Import: `import HeroCopyOnTopArt from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-copy-on-top-art'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a product page whose object is best shown as a small topology (domains feeding a workload that binds an application and a firewall).

## Do

- Keep three levels of one or two cards so the scene fits the column on a tablet.
- Mark exactly one card `lit`, the focus of the scene.

## Don’t

- For an opening band with no scene → use `hero-band`.
- For an opening band followed by a grid of arguments → use `hero-with-opening`.

## Related

- `hero-band` — the sibling opening band with the same copy and actions and no scene.
- `flow` — the diagram primitive the scene is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `highlight` | `string` | `''` | false | Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent; reads as one sentence with `title`. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `HeroCopyOnTopArtAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `HeroCopyOnTopArtAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `levels` | `HeroCopyOnTopArtLevel[]` | `[]` | false | The columns of the topology, left to right; each is `{ nodes }`, the cards top to bottom, each `{ eyebrow, icon, title, label, severity, lit? }`. A card without `title` is skipped, and the scene renders only when a level has a card. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- A card with `lit` carries `data-lit` and is drawn as the focus of the scene, with the brand border and glow
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; when no level has a card the scene is omitted
- Each action renders only with a label and a link

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button`; the cards are not interactive.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions.
- ARIA: the hero `<section>` is named by the full headline (`aria-label`); the headline is the page `h1`; card icons are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `hero-title`, `button` and `tag`; card text uses `--text-default` and `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:animate-none` on every motion-bearing class.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the large buttons meet it.

<!-- components/hero-form.md -->

# Hero Form

> The opening band of a lead-capture page, where the form is the reason for the page: the hero copy and a list of highlights on one side, the form on the other, above the fold, with the client strip on the floor. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-form', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `topic`, `field`, `input`, `select`, `phone-input`, `textarea`, `button` and `alert`. The fields are data: each entry of `fields` picks its control by `kind`, so the Contact page and the Under attack page are the same block with different `fields`. The block never sends: it validates the fields locally (required fields and the email format, with the messages from `messages`) and on a valid submit emits `submit` with the event and the values keyed by field `name`; the site posts them and reports the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `error`.

- Import: `import HeroForm from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-form'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a page whose purpose is a lead form, such as Contact sales or Under attack.

## Do

- Give every field a unique `name`; it is the key of the submitted value.
- Mark half-width fields in pairs so each row stays full.
- Set `visuallyHiddenLabel` on a field the page labels by its placeholder alone (azion.com's phone field): the label stays the control's accessible name for assistive tech but is not drawn, so give that field a `placeholder` that says what to type.
- Keep the headline to a short phrase; the band sets it on a narrower measure than the description (`--container-md`), so "Grow as an Azion Partner" breaks over two lines as on the site. There is no width prop to tune.
- Set `loading` while the values are sent, then `submitted` or `error` with the outcome.

## Don’t

- For a newsletter sign-up with one email field → use `closing-call-to-action-newsletter`.
- For an opening band with calls to action and no form → use `hero-band` or `hero-with-opening`.

## Related

- `closing-call-to-action-newsletter` — the other form section; same `submit` and state contract.
- `alert` — renders the success and failure messages.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `messages` | `HeroFormMessages` | `—` | true | Copy of the form outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, success, error }`. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `highlight` | `string` | `''` | false | Opening words of the headline, painted in the brand accent. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `HeroFormItem[]` | `[]` | false | The highlights under the description, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The list renders only when there are items. |
| `formAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the field group, read as its legend. |
| `fields` | `HeroFormField[]` | `[]` | false | The form fields in order; each is `{ name, kind, label, placeholder?, required?, half?, options?, country?, visuallyHiddenLabel? }`; `visuallyHiddenLabel` keeps the label as the accessible name but does not draw it. |
| `submitLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the submit button. |
| `carouselLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the client strip. |
| `carouselMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the client marks, in order; the strip renders only when there are marks. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site is sending the values: the button shows its loading state and a submit is ignored. |
| `submitted` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site sent the values: the form gives way to `messages.success`. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | false | The site could not send the values: `messages.error` shows under the form. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | `(event: SubmitEvent, values: Record<string, string>)` | Fired on a valid submit, not while `loading`; `values` holds every field by `name`, trimmed, with a phone number prefixed by its dial code. The block never sends it. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `invalid`, `loading`, `submitted`, `error`
- `invalid`: on submit, an empty required field shows `messages.missing` and a malformed email `messages.invalidEmail` under the field; focus moves to the first field in error; editing the field clears it; nothing is emitted
- `loading` (prop): the button shows its loading state, every field is disabled (the scope locks off the one flag) and a submit emits nothing; `data-loading` on the root
- `submitted` (prop): the form is replaced by a success `Alert` with `messages.success`, which takes focus when focus was in the form; `data-submitted` on the root
- `error` (prop): a danger `Alert` with `messages.error` shows under the button; the form stays editable; `data-error` on the root
- A field with `visuallyHiddenLabel` renders its `Label` visually hidden (`sr-only`), so the control keeps its accessible name and the page shows only the placeholder
- The headline caps at `--container-md` while the description and highlights keep the `lg` column
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; when `items` is empty the list is omitted; when `carouselMarks` is empty the strip is omitted

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the field controls and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` walks the fields in order then the button; `Enter` in a text field or on the button submits.
- ARIA: the band is the `hero` `<section>` named by the title (`aria-label`); the root is a plain `div`. The fields sit in a `fieldset` whose visually hidden `legend` is `formAriaLabel`; each control is labelled through its own `Label` with an id from `useId`; each label is a `Label` rendered by the band, carrying the persistent Required tag of a `required` field from first render. An `email` field is an `<input type="email">` with `autocomplete="email"` and `spellcheck="false"`. Validation runs on submit only: a required field left empty takes the field's amber `required` state (warning border, `kind=required` helper, `aria-required`), a malformed email the red `invalid` state (`aria-invalid`), never both at once; the message is the field's helper text, and editing the field clears it. The success message is a `status` region and the failure message an `alert`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the composed components carry their own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the text fields and the button are large.

```vue
  }
```

<!-- components/hero-with-opening.md -->

# Hero With Opening

> The opening band of a product page followed straight by its arguments: a large centered title band with the page `h1`, overline, sentence and up to two actions, then a frame grid of three-column argument cells in the page column, closed by a hatched gap. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-with-opening', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `button`, `section-container`, `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `topic` and `section-gap`. The grid starts at the hero floor with no gap, so the arguments read as the second half of the hero.

- Import: `import HeroWithOpening from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-with-opening'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To open a product page that argues on three or six claims right under its headline.

## Do

- Use three or six items so every row of the grid is full.
- Keep each item to a short title and one sentence.
- A title longer than 45 characters widens the headline column so it breaks into two lines instead of three.

## Don’t

- For an opening band with no arguments → use `hero-band`.
- For a reasons band further down the page → use `feature-tiles` or `use-cases`.

## Related

- `hero-band` — the opening band without the argument grid.
- `topic` — the icon, heading and sentence each argument is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. A title longer than 45 characters widens the headline column. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Sentence under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `HeroWithOpeningAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `secondaryAction` | `HeroWithOpeningAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link. |
| `items` | `HeroWithOpeningItem[]` | `[]` | false | The arguments in reading order, three to a row; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The grid renders only when there are items. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The headline column is `xl` wide for a title of up to 45 characters and `4xl` wide for a longer one
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; when `items` is empty the grid and its closing gap are omitted
- Each action renders only with a label and a link

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions.
- ARIA: the hero `<section>` is named by the headline (`aria-label`); the headline is the page `h1` and each argument's heading is an `h2` from `topic`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `hero-title`, `button` and `topic`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the large buttons meet it.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import HeroWithOpening from '@aziontech/webkit/hero-with-opening'
</script>

<template>
  <HeroWithOpening
    eyebrow="Firewall"
    title="Programmable firewall for distributed applications"
    description="Protect users, applications, and networks with rules you program, from layer 3 to layer 7."
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: 'https://console.azion.com/signup/' }"
    :secondary-action="{
      label: 'Docs',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
      trailing: true
    }"
    :items="[
      {
        icon: 'pi pi-shield',
        title: 'Programmable rule engine',
        description:
          'Define custom rules and behaviors across OSI layers L3-L7 to control traffic before it reaches your applications.'
      },
      {
        icon: 'pi pi-code',
        title: 'Extensible with Functions',
        description:
          'Run custom JavaScript security code and marketplace integrations on Azion’s distributed infrastructure.'
      },
      {
        icon: 'pi pi-sync',
        title: 'Real-time synchronization',
        description:
          'Rules sync automatically across every data center. SIEM integration keeps threat intelligence flowing.'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```
