# Investor Marks

> The investors band: a centered section title over a two-column bento grid where each cell is an investor's mark, linked to its site, that lifts on hover to reveal a "visit website" line. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'investor-marks', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `bento-grid`.

- Import: `import InvestorMarks from '@aziontech/webkit/investor-marks'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the company page, to name the investors with their marks.

## Do

- Give each item a `logoLight` when its mark needs a different file on the light theme; otherwise one `logo` serves both.
- Keep `linkLabel` short; it is revealed under the mark on hover and read before the investor name.

## Don’t

- For client marks → use `client-mosaic` or `logo-wall-quote`.

## Related

- `bento-grid` — the grid the marks are laid in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the centered section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Line revealed under a mark on hover, and the start of each link's accessible name. |
| `items` | `InvestorMarksItem[]` | `[]` | false | The investors, in order; each is `{ name, logo, logoLight?, href }` where `logo` is the mark on the dark theme and `logoLight` the one on the light theme. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each cell (fill rises, mark lifts, the link line appears)
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each cell link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset` and shows the same reveal as hover.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between investor links; `Enter` follows one (opens in a new tab).
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); each link's accessible name is "`linkLabel`, `name` (opens in a new tab)"; the revealed line is `aria-hidden` since the name already carries it; the two theme marks share the investor's name as `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): link line `var(--text-default)` on `var(--bg-hover)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on every transition above.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each link is a full 12rem-tall cell.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
        logoLight: monasheesExtendedMono,

      },
      {
        name: 'Qualcomm Ventures',
        logo: qualcommExtendedReversed,
        logoLight: qualcommExtendedMono,
        href: 'https://www.qualcommventures.com'
      }
```

<!-- components/listing-browser.md -->

# Listing Browser

> The full, browsable listing of a page such as the Careers jobs list: a headline over a toolbar (a search field, one select per facet and one for the order) and every row under its group, as a table from the small breakpoint up and as a list of items below it, with an empty state when nothing matches. Search, facets and order are local state over the rows the page carries; a facet is seeded from `?<key>=` in the URL when the value is one the page offers. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-browser', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `input`, `select`, `table`, `item`, `empty-state` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import ListingBrowser from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-browser'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- For a listing a reader narrows by text and by a few facets, such as open positions grouped by department.
- When every row links to its own page and the listing fits in the page JSON.

## Do

- Name the first column after what the row is (`Role`); it is the row's link, and the second column describes the row on phones.
- Give every row the facet values it carries under the facet's `key`, so the selects narrow it.
- Keep `groups` in the order the reader scans; rows of a group not listed there are not shown.
- Make the first entry of `sorts` the order the page is authored in, with an empty `by`.

## Don’t

- For a short, unfiltered preview of the same rows → use `listing-table`.
- For a data table with sorting, selection and pagination inside the product → use `table`.
- For a grid of linked topic cards → use `subject-library`.

## Related

- `table` — the composed rows and cells the listing renders from the small breakpoint up.
- `item` — the list rows the listing renders below the small breakpoint.
- `empty-state` — the state shown when the search and facets match nothing.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page `id` of the band, the target of a `#hash` link. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the listing, rendered by the section title as its `h2` and naming the band. |
| `columns` | `ListingBrowserColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The columns, left to right; each is `{ key, label, grow?, align? }`. The first names the row and links it, the second describes it on phones. |
| `rows` | `ListingBrowserRow[]` | `[]` | false | Every row, in source order; each is `{ href, group, values, facets }` where `values` and `facets` are keyed by column and facet. |
| `groups` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | The groups the rows are listed under, in order; a group with no matching row is not shown. |
| `facets` | `ListingBrowserFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet selects; each is `{ key, label, allLabel, options }` where `key` matches a row facet and seeds it from `?key=` in the URL, and every option is `{ value, label }`. |
| `sorts` | `ListingBrowserSort[]` | `[]` | false | The orders, the first the default; each is `{ value, label, by? }` where `by` is the column it sorts on and an empty `by` keeps the source order. |
| `sortAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the order select. |
| `search` | `ListingBrowserSearch` | `undefined` | false | The search field; `{ placeholder, shortPlaceholder, label }` where `shortPlaceholder` is used below the large breakpoint and `label` names the field. Omitted when absent. |
| `empty` | `ListingBrowserEmpty` | `undefined` | false | The state shown when nothing matches; `{ title, description, clearLabel }` where `clearLabel` is the button that clears the search and every facet. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `filtered`, `empty`
- Filtered: the search matches a row when any of its values contains the query, ignoring case; every facet set to a value keeps only the rows carrying it; the order select sorts on its column or keeps the source order
- Empty: when the search and facets match no row, `empty-state` replaces the table and the list, and its button clears the search and every facet; without `empty`, nothing is shown in their place
- Seeded: on mount a facet takes the value of `?<key>=` in the URL when it is one of its options
- Absent: when `rows` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the toolbar
- The table renders from the small breakpoint up, the list below it; the toolbar stacks below the large breakpoint, where the search field shows `shortPlaceholder`
- Server render and hydration: the large-breakpoint check runs only after mount, so the server HTML and the first client render both use `shortPlaceholder` and match; the full placeholder applies on mount.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `input`, `select` and `button`; each row link draws `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color)` on the row it stretches over.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the search field, the selects and the row links in reading order; a select opens on `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowDown`, moves with the arrows and closes on `Escape` (all `select`'s own); `Enter` follows a row link.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the toolbar is a `role="search"` region; the search field is named by `search.label`, each facet select by its `label` and the order select by `sortAriaLabel`; each group is an `h3`; the table is `table`'s `role="table"`, and the phone list is `item`'s `role="list"` of `role="listitem"` rows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): row links and group headings `var(--text-default)`, headers and meta `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the field, select and button transitions belong to the composed components, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the search field, selects and empty-state button are large; each row link stretches over its whole row.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ListingBrowser from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-browser'
</script>

<template>
  <ListingBrowser
    title="Open positions"
    :columns="[
      { key: 'role', label: 'Role', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'team', label: 'Team and location', grow: 2 },
      { key: 'type', label: 'Work type', align: 'end' }
    ]"
    :rows="[
      {
        href: '/careers/software-engineer-go',
        group: 'Engineering',
        values: {
          role: 'Software Engineer (Go)',
          team: 'Engineering · San Francisco',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        },
        facets: { area: ['Engineering'], location: ['San Francisco'] }
      },
      {
        href: '/careers/grc-analyst',
        group: 'Security',
        values: {
          role: 'GRC Analyst (Governance, Risk & Compliance)',
          team: 'Compliance and Corporate IT · San Francisco / New York',
          type: 'Hybrid · Full-time'
        },
        facets: { area: ['Security'], location: ['San Francisco', 'New York'] }
      }
    ]"
    :groups="['Engineering', 'Security']"
    :facets="[
      {
        key: 'area',
        label: 'Department',
        allLabel: 'All departments',
        options: [
          { value: 'Engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
          { value: 'Security', label: 'Security' }
        ]
      },
      {
        key: 'location',
        label: 'Location',
        allLabel: 'All locations',
        options: [
          { value: 'New York', label: 'New York, United States' },
          { value: 'San Francisco', label: 'San Francisco, United States' }
        ]
      }
    ]"
    :sorts="[
      { value: 'newest', label: 'Newest posted', by: '' },
      { value: 'title', label: 'Title (A–Z)', by: 'role' }
    ]"
    sort-aria-label="Sort positions"
    :search="{
      placeholder: 'Search by title, team, or location',
      shortPlaceholder: 'Search positions',
      label: 'Search positions'
    }"
    :empty="{
      title: 'Nothing here yet',
      description: 'No open positions match your search.',
      clearLabel: 'View all open positions'
    }"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/listing-table.md -->

# Listing Table

> A titled preview of a longer listing: a few linked rows in columns, and one outlined button into the full list. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-table', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `table` and, below `sm`, `item`. Each row is one link named by its first column; the whole row is clickable with the pointer and the first column's link is the keyboard and screen-reader path. Below `sm` the same rows become a list of items, the first column as the title and the second as the description, with the button going full width.

- Import: `import ListingTable from '@aziontech/webkit/listing-table'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To preview the latest entries of a listing (open roles, releases, events) with a way into the full list.

## Do

- Keep three columns at most; the first names the row and the second describes it on phones.
- Give the wide columns `grow: 2` and align a short trailing column to `end`.
- Keep the preview to a handful of rows and point `primaryAction` at the full listing.

## Don’t

- For a filterable or paginated listing → use `listing-browser`.
- For a comparison of plans or features → use the pricing matrix.

## Related

- `table` — the composition table the wide layout renders.
- `listing-browser` — the full listing this band links into.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the left-aligned section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `columns` | `ListingTableColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The columns left to right; each is `{ key, label, grow?, align? }` where `key` picks the row value, `grow` is the flex weight (1, 2 or 3) and `align` is `start` or `end`. The first column names the row and the second describes it on phones. |
| `rows` | `ListingTableRow[]` | `[]` | false | The linked rows, in order; each is `{ href, values }` where `values` maps a column key to its text. |
| `primaryAction` | `ListingTableAction` | `undefined` | false | Outlined button into the full listing, in the table footer; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (row fill)
- Empty: when `rows` or `columns` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; the footer button only when `primaryAction` is set
- Below `sm` the table is hidden and the rows render as an item list

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the row links and the composed `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each row's link and then the button; `Enter` follows it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the table keeps its native column headers; the phone list is the same rows as list items.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): row titles `var(--text-default)`, values `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the button carries its own fallback.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each phone row is a whole-item link; the button is large.

## Examples

<!-- components/logo-wall-quote.md -->

# Logo Wall Quote

> The customers band: a section title over a framed logo wall of linked client marks with one signed quote in its aside, closed by a call to action. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'logo-wall-quote', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `logo-wall`, `quote` and `button`.

- Import: `import LogoWallQuote from '@aziontech/webkit/logo-wall-quote'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To prove adoption with marks and let one customer speak, early on a home or solution page.

## Do

- Eight or nine logos fill the rectangle wall beside the aside.
- Set `logoTreatment` per mark: `monochrome` for a mark drawn in one ink that must follow the theme, `invert-light` for a reversed mark that must flip on the light theme, `as-is` for a colour mark; give a `logoLight` file instead when the light theme needs a different drawing.

## Don’t

- For several quotes in turn → use `client-quotes`.
- For marks with photos and stories in a mosaic → use `client-mosaic`.

## Related

- `logo-wall` — the wall the marks are laid in, with the quote in its aside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `LogoWallQuoteKind` | `'wall'` | false | Layout of the band: `wall` sets the client marks with the quote in their aside, `quote` sets the quote alone as a full-width band (the design sample's QuoteBand) and needs no logos. |
| `quoteKind` | `LogoWallQuoteQuoteKind` | `'signed'` | false | Register of the quote in the `quote` layout: the featured `highlight` or the band-sized `signed` sentence. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the logo wall. |
| `logos` | `LogoWallQuoteLogo[]` | `[]` | false | The client marks, in order; each is `{ name, logo, logoLight?, logoTreatment?, href? }` where `logoTreatment` is `'as-is'`, `'monochrome'` or `'invert-light'`. |
| `quote` | `LogoWallQuoteQuote` | `undefined` | false | The signed quote in the wall's aside; `{ text, name, jobTitle, logo, logoAlt }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `primaryAction` | `LogoWallQuoteAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the quote; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `logos` is empty the band renders nothing
- Each mark carries `data-treatment` so the theme-following inks are driven by data attributes

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `logo-wall` (each mark link) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between mark links and the action; `Enter` follows.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the wall is `logo-wall`'s own list named by `ariaLabel`; every mark image carries the client `name` as `alt`; the quote is a `blockquote` signed by its author.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components; marks follow the theme through their treatment.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each mark link spans its wall cell.

## Examples

### Default


<!-- components/media-split-band.md -->

# Media Split Band

> One claim beside its picture, on its own frame: the copy cell with its overline, headline and sentence on one side, and the media on a raised, pixel-textured surface on the other. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-band', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, a framed `media-split`, `button`, `illustration`, `product-widget`, `diagram` and the webkit scene assets. The media is a scene, a product console widget, a request-flow diagram, an image (cover or framed) or an illustration; with one action the whole band links to it, with two the band stays unlinked.

- Import: `import MediaSplitBand from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-band'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To make one point beside one picture and move on (a values statement, a single product claim).

## Do

- Give the band exactly one media: `scene`, `widget` (a `ProductWidget` name), `diagram` (a `Diagram` name), `image` or `illustration`; when several are set the first of that order wins.
- On a product page prefer `widget` or `diagram`: they show the product itself. Do not drop to `media-split` and its `media` slot to place one.
- Set `image.framed` for a picture that is an object rather than a scene (a badge, a logo, a screenshot): it sits whole on a rounded, bordered plate inset in the cell instead of covering it.
- Use `size="large"` for a band that carries only its headline and description.
- Give an `image` its `width` and `height` so the page reserves its box before it loads.

## Don’t

- For several claims stacked one after the other → use `media-split-stack`.
- For a claim beside a code sample → use `code-split`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the band primitive the section is rendered with.
- `media-split-stack` — the stacked sibling for a run of claims.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Short overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph under the headline. |
| `size` | `MediaSplitBandSize` | `'medium'` | false | Type scale of the copy; `large` sets the headline at heading-xl and centres the copy beside the media. |
| `scene` | `MediaSplitBandScene` | `undefined` | false | Scene drawn in the media cell, `{ component }` naming a webkit scene asset; wins over every other media. |
| `widget` | `ProductWidgetName` | `undefined` | false | Name of the product console widget drawn in the media cell when no scene is set. |
| `diagram` | `DiagramName` | `undefined` | false | Name of the request-flow diagram drawn in the media cell when neither a scene nor a widget is set. |
| `image` | `MediaSplitBandImage` | `undefined` | false | Picture drawn in the media cell when no scene, widget or diagram is set; `{ src, alt?, width?, height?, framed? }`, where `framed` sets it whole on a rounded plate instead of covering the cell. |
| `illustration` | `string` | `''` | false | Registry name of the illustration drawn in the media cell when no other media is set. |
| `illustrationAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the illustration; empty keeps it decorative. |
| `primaryAction` | `MediaSplitBandAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. When it is the only action, the whole band links to it. |
| `secondaryAction` | `MediaSplitBandAction` | `undefined` | false | Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. With two actions the band stays unlinked. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `size` is forwarded to the media split and drives its type scale and copy alignment
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing but its root; with no media set the media cell is omitted
- With exactly one action the band is a link to that action's `href`; with none or two it is not a link
- Media precedence: `scene`, `widget`, `diagram`, `image`, `illustration`. A widget, a diagram and a framed image are inset from the cell's edges (`media-split`'s `mediaPadded`); a scene, a plain image (which covers the cell) and an illustration run flush
- A widget plays its beat while the pointer is over the band, and shows its finished state on touch and under reduced motion (owned by `product-widget`); it draws no collaborator cursor (`cursor` off), so the band reads as the product screen
- Scenes, widget and diagram load on demand (`defineAsyncComponent`)

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button` and `media-split`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the actions, and through the media link when the band links.
- ARIA: the media split's `<section>` is the band's named region (`aria-label` from `title`), so the root is a plain `div`; the headline is its `h2`; an image is named by `alt`, an illustration by `illustrationAriaLabel`, and both are decorative when empty; a diagram is a `figure` named by the description its library entry carries; a widget is an inert, `aria-hidden` picture of the console, so the copy carries its meaning.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `media-split` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the scenes stop under reduced motion on their own.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the medium buttons meet it.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (owned by `media-split`).
- Icons: a trailing chevron on an action mirrors (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props in the page's language. Widget and diagram text is product UI copy owned by `product-widget` and `diagram`.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; `media-split` stacks the media under the copy below `lg`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): one column; a widget, a diagram and a framed image scale down with the cell.
- Touch: a widget shows its finished state instead of the hover beat.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import MediaSplitBand from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-band'
</script>

<template>
  <MediaSplitBand
    eyebrow="Our values"
    title="Four values shape every role at Azion"
    description="Quality, Drive, Accountability, and Innovation. They guide how we work every day: we set high standards and measure what we deliver, take on hard problems with persistence, own our commitments and mistakes, and use AI and new technology to solve problems in new ways. Together, they help us earn and keep the trust of our customers."
    size="large"
    :scene="{ component: 'BrandGlobeScene' }"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/media-split-band.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/media-split-band.md).

<!-- components/media-split-stack.md -->

# Media Split Stack

> A run of large media-split bands that pile up under the site header as the page scrolls, each a centered claim with an outlined "learn more" button beside its picture, the whole band linking through. An optional large centered section title opens the run. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-stack', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `band-stack`, `media-split`, `illustration`, `product-widget`, `diagram` and `button`. A band's picture is one of four things: a `ProductWidget` console mock (`widget`), a `Diagram` request-flow figure (`diagram`), a registry `illustration`, or an `image` URL, plain or `imageFramed` on its own plate. `kind` picks the layout only: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band; the bands keep the same shape in both.

- Import: `import MediaSplitStack from '@aziontech/webkit/media-split-stack'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To list the solution areas or the claims of a page, one large band each, with a link through to its own page.

## Do

- Give a band one picture: `widget` (a `ProductWidget` name — the product's console screen), `diagram` (a `Diagram` name — its request flow), `illustration` (a registry name, with `illustrationLabel`) or `image` (a URL, with `imageAlt` when it says something). When several are set the first in that order wins; a band with none renders without its media cell.
- Prefer `widget` or `diagram` on a product page: they show the product itself, where an illustration only evokes it. Do not drop to `media-split` and its `media` slot to place one.
- Set `imageFramed` for a picture that is an object rather than a scene — a badge, a logo, a screenshot: it sits whole on a rounded, bordered plate inset in the cell. A plain `image` is scaled to fit the cell and never overflows it.
- Give every band an `action`; it is both the button and the link the whole band follows.

## Don’t

- For a single claim beside its media → use `media-split` directly.
- For small reasons in a grid → use `feature-tiles`.

## Related

- `band-stack` — the sticky run the bands pile up in.
- `media-split` — the band each entry renders through.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `MediaSplitStackKind` | `'media-end'` | false | Layout of the run: `media-end` sets every picture at the closing end, `alternating` starts it at the opening end and swaps sides band by band. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the run, rendered by the large centered section title as its `h2`; the run renders no header when empty. |
| `bands` | `MediaSplitStackBand[]` | `[]` | false | The bands, in order; each is `{ title, description, widget?, diagram?, image?, imageAlt?, imageFramed?, illustration?, illustrationLabel?, action? }` where `widget` is a `ProductWidget` name, `diagram` a `Diagram` name, `image` a picture URL, `illustration` a registry name, and `action` `{ label, href }` the outlined button and the link the whole band follows. |

## Assets

- Illustrations: every valid name is in illustrations.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "illustrations" })`). An unknown name renders a "PLACE DESIGN ASSET" placeholder and warns in the console.
- Diagrams: every valid name is in diagrams.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "diagrams" })`). An unknown name draws nothing.

## States

- Visual states: `default`; hovering a linked band reveals its link affordance (owned by `media-split`)
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop
- Empty: when `bands` is empty the run renders nothing — not the header, not the stack
- The header renders only when `title` is set; a band renders its button and its link only when it has an `action`, and its media cell only when it has a picture
- Media precedence per band: `widget`, then `diagram`, then `illustration`, then `image`. A widget or a diagram is inset from the cell's edges (`media-split`'s `mediaPadded`), and so is a framed image; an illustration and a plain image run flush
- A widget plays its beat while the pointer is over its band (`hover`), and shows its finished state on touch and under reduced motion (owned by `product-widget`); it draws no collaborator cursor (`cursor` off), so the band reads as the product screen
- Widget and diagram load on demand (`defineAsyncComponent`): a run that uses neither never downloads them

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `button` and `media-split`'s media link.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each band's media link and button; `Enter` follows them.
- ARIA: the run is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; each band is `media-split`'s own section named by the band's title, with its headline as an `h2`; illustrations are named by `illustrationLabel` and images by `imageAlt`, or decorative when empty; a diagram is a `figure` named by the description its library entry carries; a widget is an inert, `aria-hidden` picture of the console, so the band's copy carries its meaning.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `media-split` and `button`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the run adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px: the medium buttons and the band links.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only; `alternating` swaps the media side with the reading direction (owned by `media-split`).
- Icons: the button's trailing chevron mirrors (owned by `button`).
- Keyboard: unchanged.
- User data: none.

## Internationalization

- No built-in strings: every visible string arrives through props in the page's language. Widget and diagram text is product UI copy owned by `product-widget` and `diagram`.
- Formatting: none.

## Responsive

- Container queries: none; `media-split` stacks the media under the copy below `lg`.
- Narrow (≤ 640 px): one column per band; a widget, a diagram and a framed image scale down with the cell.
- Touch: a widget shows its finished state instead of the hover beat; the whole band stays one link.
- Reflow: no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/network-section.md -->

# Network Section

> The infrastructure band of a marketing page: a tall framed panel with the world network map drawn behind a small left-aligned title, a lead line and a row of claim chips, closed by a floor of either client outcomes (a quote with its highlights and, when given, the client's mark) or benefits (a bold lead-in sentence running into its explanation, as on azion.com). It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'network-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `network-map`, `section-title`, `card-grid`, `quote` and `topic`. `kind` picks the floor only: `outcomes` renders the quotes on one column per entry — two at least, four at most; `benefits` renders the topics on a fixed four-column floor from `lg` (two from `sm`, one on a phone) whose trailing cells stay empty, as the site's three-benefit floor does. The band above is the same.

- Import: `import NetworkSection from '@aziontech/webkit/network-section'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To state the network's reach with figures and back it with either client results or product benefits.

## Do

- Four short `claims`; they are chips, not sentences.
- Two to four `outcomes`: the floor sets one column per entry, so it closes the grid; a fifth entry wraps to a second row.
- Three or four `benefits`, each a `title` written as a short sentence ending in a full stop ("Low latency everywhere.") and a `description` that continues it: the title is set bold and runs into the description, like azion.com. Leave `icon` out to match the site; an `icon` turns the benefit into an icon-led topic with its own `h3`.
- Leave `logo` out of an outcome when the site shows the figure alone; the cell then renders no mark row.
- Use `logoTreatment: 'monochrome'` for a dark mark that must invert in the dark theme; leave `as-is` for a colour mark.

## Don’t

- For figures alone → use `stats-band`.
- For a logo wall with one quote → use `logo-wall-quote`.

## Related

- `network-map` — the animated map behind the copy.
- `quote` / `topic` — the two cell types the floor renders.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `NetworkSectionKind` | `'outcomes'` | false | Which floor closes the band: `outcomes` renders the client quotes, `benefits` the run-in benefit topics on a four-column floor. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the small section title as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `lead` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline-set line above the claims. |
| `claims` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Short figures rendered as chips under the lead, in order. |
| `outcomes` | `NetworkSectionOutcome[]` | `[]` | false | Client results for the `outcomes` floor, in order, one column each up to four; each is `{ logo?, logoAlt?, logoTreatment?, text, highlights? }` where `logo` is the mark URL (the cell renders no mark without it), `logoAlt` names the client, `logoTreatment` is `'monochrome'` or `'as-is'`, and `highlights` are the phrases of `text` set in the accent. |
| `benefits` | `NetworkSectionBenefit[]` | `[]` | false | Topics for the `benefits` floor, in order, on four columns from the large breakpoint; each is `{ title, description, icon? }` where `title` is set bold and runs into `description`, and an `icon` turns the topic into an icon-led one with its own heading. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop and selects the floor
- Empty: when `title` is empty the band renders nothing; when the selected floor's array is empty the band renders without a floor
- An outcome without `logo` renders its quote with no mark row
- The `benefits` floor is `card-grid`'s `fixed` layout with `columns: 4`, so three benefits leave the fourth cell empty from `lg`; a benefit without `icon` is one paragraph whose bold title runs into its description, a benefit with `icon` is a `topic` with an `h3`
- The map renders twice: a faded top-right world from the medium breakpoint up, a centered masked world below it; both are `network-map`'s own animation

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the headline is the section title's `h2`; the claims are a real list; the maps are decorative and hidden from assistive technology by `network-map`; each outcome's mark carries the client name as `alt`; benefit topics are `h3`s.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): lead `var(--text-muted)`, claims `var(--text-default)` on a tinted canvas; the map sits at low opacity behind the copy and never under the text column on large screens.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the map animation belongs to `network-map`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue

  import madeiramadeiraExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/madeiramadeira-extended-reversed.svg'
  import rennerExtendedColor from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/renner-extended-color.svg'
</script>

<template>
  <NetworkSection
    kind="outcomes"
    eyebrow="Region: Earth."
    title="One distributed infrastructure without the complexity of managing, securing and scaling it"

    :claims="[
      '100+ data centers',
```

<!-- components/photo-marquee.md -->

# Photo Marquee

> The office band of the careers page: a horizontal section title over a framed strip of photographs of varied aspect ratios that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover or focus. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'photo-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title` and `frame-box`.

- Import: `import PhotoMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/photo-marquee'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To show a place or a team in pictures without a grid.

## Do

- Give every photo its `width` and `height` so the strip reserves each slot before the picture loads.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (ten seconds per photo).

## Don’t

- For quotes → use `recognition-marquee`.

## Related

- `recognition-marquee` — the sibling strip of quotes with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the horizontal section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `PhotoMarqueeDescriptionWidth` | `'narrow'` | false | Width the description is capped at: `narrow` or `wide`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at ten seconds per photo. |
| `photos` | `PhotoMarqueePhoto[]` | `[]` | false | The photographs, in order; each is `{ src, alt, width, height }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus
- Empty: when `photos` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden`, its photos carry an empty `alt`, and it is hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop; under reduced motion arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; every photo carries its `alt` once — the duplicate copy is `aria-hidden` with empty `alt`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed, so photos flow in reading order; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

<!-- components/platform-directory.md -->

# Platform Directory

> A directory of Azion's products under a section title: one column per product group (Build, Store, Secure, Observe), each row an icon, a product name and one line about it, linking to that product. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'platform-directory', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `column-navigation` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import PlatformDirectory from '@aziontech/webkit/platform-directory'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On Home, right under the hero, to show every product the platform offers at a glance.
- On a solution, product or pricing page that repeats the full product map.

## Do

- Keep to four groups or fewer; the directory fans out to one column per group at the large breakpoint, up to four, so one, two or three groups never leave an empty cell.
- Give each item an `href`; an item without a title or a link is skipped, and a group left with no items is skipped too.
- Set `ariaLabel` so the directory's navigation landmark is told apart from the site navigation.

## Don’t

- For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `use-cases`.
- For a site-wide navigation menu → use `navigation-menu`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `column-navigation` directly.

## Related

- `column-navigation` — the named navigation landmark whose columns and rows this band fills.
- `section-title` — the headline over the directory.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline over the directory, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the directory's navigation landmark. |
| `groups` | `PlatformDirectoryGroup[]` | `[]` | false | The columns, in order; each is `{ title, items }` where every item is `{ icon, title, description, href }`. Items without a title or an `href` are skipped, and so are groups left empty. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- One column per group from the large breakpoint, up to four (`column-navigation`'s `columns` is 2, 3 or 4), one column below the small one; the column layout is `column-navigation`'s own
- No empty cell: a single group spans the whole row (`data-span="full"`), and with three groups the third spans both columns between the small and the large breakpoints (`data-span="pair"`), so the rule colour never shows through a missing column
- Empty: when no group carries a linked item the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `column-navigation` item links.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the product links in reading order; `Enter` follows one. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the directory is `column-navigation`'s `nav`, named by `ariaLabel`, and each column's overline heading names its list of rows.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the row hover belongs to `column-navigation`, which carries its own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each row is a full-width link taller than 40 px.

## Examples

### Default

# Pricing Plans

> The plan cards at the top of Pricing: a billing-period toggle over a framed row of pricing cards, each with its plan name, its price for the picked period, what it includes and one button. The recommended plan sits on a raised surface and carries a tag. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'pricing-plans', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `toggle-group`, `card-grid`, `card-pricing` and `button`; the picked period is local state.

- Import: `import PricingPlans from '@aziontech/webkit/pricing-plans'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- At the top of Pricing, to lay the plans side by side with a price per billing period.

## Do

- Give every plan one price per period, matched by `period`; a price without a `period` applies to every period.
- Highlight one plan; it is raised and is the only card that shows its tag.
- Keep `features` to five or so short labels led by an icon.

## Don’t

- To compare plans feature by feature → use `compare-plans`.

## Related

- `card-pricing` — the card each plan renders with.
- `compare-plans` — the matrix that sits under these cards.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `periods` | `PricingPlansPeriod[]` | `[]` | false | The billing periods of the toggle, in order; each is `{ label, value }`. The toggle shows with two or more and opens on the first. |
| `periodsAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the billing-period toggle. |
| `plans` | `PricingPlansPlan[]` | `[]` | false | The plan cards, in order; each is `{ name, highlighted?, tagLabel?, prices, featuresTitle?, features?, action? }` where a price is `{ period?, value, prefix?, suffix?, details? }`, a feature is `{ icon, label }` and `action` is `{ label, href }`; a plan without a name is dropped, and an action without a label or href is dropped. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- The picked period selects each plan's price; a plan with no price for it falls back to its period-less price
- The highlighted plan sits on `var(--bg-surface)`, shows its tag and carries the secondary button; the others sit on `var(--bg-canvas)` with an outlined button
- Empty: when no plan has a name the band renders nothing but its root

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `toggle-group` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the toggle and each card's button; the toggle's arrow-key map is `toggle-group`'s.
- ARIA: the toggle is named by `periodsAriaLabel`; each plan is a `card-pricing` article with its name as `h3`; the features are a list and their glyphs are `aria-hidden`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text colours are the tokens above.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the toggle indicator belongs to `toggle-group`, which carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the toggle and the buttons are `large`.

<!-- components/process-scroll.md -->

# Process Scroll

> The stages of a process as a row of numbered dark cards on a pixel texture, under a section title. On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways with snap; from the large breakpoint up the cards share the width, or, with `pinned`, keep a 26rem card width while the band pins under the site header and the page scroll slides the row sideways until its last card is in view (azion.com's careers hiring process). From the design sample's site `ProcessScroll`.

- Import: `import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- How something works in three to five ordered stages (build, deploy, observe).

## Do

- Name each stage with a verb.
- Keep descriptions to two lines.
- Set `pinned` when the stages run wider than the page column (five tall cards, as the careers hiring process): the band stays on screen while the page scroll walks the row. Do not nest a pinned band in a container that clips overflow; sticky positioning needs the page scroll.

## Don’t

- For more than five stages or stages with art — use `FeatureScroll`.
- For five to eight short points with no section-title layout — use `StickyCarousel`; for ordered stages that pin while the page scrolls, set `pinned` here.

## Related

- StickyCarousel` — the same cards, always pinned, under a plain section title.
- TextureMaterial`, `FrameBox`, `SectionTitle`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the title. |
| `titleKind` | `SectionTitleKind` | `'horizontal'` | false | Alignment of the section title over the card row. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `descriptionWidth` | `SectionTitleDescriptionWidth` | `'narrow'` | false | Column span of the paragraph: `wide` runs it across the middle column too. |
| `steps` | `ProcessScrollStep[]` | `[]` | false | The stages, in order; each is `{ title, description }` and gets its own numbered card. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrollable card row; defaults to the title. |
| `pinned` | `boolean` | `false` | false | From the large breakpoint, pins the band under the site header while the page scrolls and slides the card row sideways until its last card is in view; below it, or under reduced motion, the row scrolls sideways on its own. |
| `headerOffset` | `string` | `'var(--layout-header-height)'` | false | Height of the sticky site header a pinned band sticks under; defaults to the SiteNav bar's token, any CSS length. |

## States

- Renders nothing without a title or steps.
- Cards are `data-theme="dark"` in both themes (the sample's design).
- `data-pinned` on the root mirrors `pinned`. From `lg` with motion allowed, the band is `sticky` under `headerOffset` and one screen tall, the root (the runway) grows by the row's overflow, and the row's `translate` follows the page scroll (mirrored in right-to-left); below `lg` or under `prefers-reduced-motion` the band does not pin and the row scrolls inside itself. The runway is measured on mount and on scroll/resize, so the server HTML is the unpinned band.

## Accessibility

- The band root is a plain container; the scroll row is the one focusable `region`, named by `ariaLabel` or the title, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys and the page has one landmark per band.
- Stages are an ordered list; the big number is `aria-hidden` because the list already orders them.
- Each stage heading is an `h3`.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ps-*`, `border-e`, `ms-*`).
- Icons: none mirrored.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- Below large: cards are `min(22rem, 80vw)` wide and snap; the row scrolls inside itself, never the page.
- From large: cards share the width; with `pinned`, cards keep a 26rem width and the pinned band slides them sideways.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'

  const steps = [
    { title: 'Push', description: 'Every push to the main branch builds a new version.' },
    { title: 'Build', description: 'The build runs in an isolated worker with your settings.' },
    {
      title: 'Deploy',
      description: 'The version goes live everywhere at once, with no regions to pick.'
    },
    { title: 'Observe', description: 'Metrics and logs for the new version arrive in seconds.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ProcessScroll
    eyebrow="How it works"
    title="From commit to production"
    description="Four stages, all automatic once the repository is connected."
    :steps="steps"
  />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/process-scroll.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/process-scroll.md).

# Recognition Marquee

> The analyst-recognition band: a section title over a framed strip of signed quotes — one per report, marked by the firm's logo — that scrolls continuously and pauses on hover or focus. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'recognition-marquee', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box` and `quote`.

- Import: `import RecognitionMarquee from '@aziontech/webkit/recognition-marquee'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To list analyst reports and awards on a page that needs third-party proof.

## Do

- Five to eight items; the loop needs enough width to read as continuous.
- Leave `duration` at `0` to let the strip pace itself (twelve seconds per item).

## Don’t

- For office photos → use `photo-marquee`.
- For customer quotes → use `client-quotes`.

## Related

- `quote` — the signed card each recognition renders with.
- `photo-marquee` — the sibling strip of pictures with the same loop.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling region. |
| `duration` | `number` | `0` | false | Seconds one loop of the strip takes; `0` paces it at twelve seconds per item. |
| `items` | `RecognitionMarqueeItem[]` | `[]` | false | The recognitions, in order; each is `{ text, reportName, date?, firmName, logo, logoLight? }` where `logo` is the firm's mark on the dark theme and `logoLight` the one on the light theme. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, paused while the strip is hovered or holds focus
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing
- The list is rendered twice for a seamless loop; the duplicate is `aria-hidden` and hidden under reduced motion, where the region scrolls by hand instead

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the scrolling region is focusable and carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-inset`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the region, which pauses the loop; under reduced motion arrow keys scroll it.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`); the strip is a `region` named by `ariaLabel`; the second copy of the list is `aria-hidden`; each firm mark carries `firmName` as `alt`; each recognition is a `blockquote` signed by its report and date.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `quote` on `var(--bg-surface)`.
- `motion-reduce:animate-none` on the strip; the duplicate list is hidden so nothing moves and nothing repeats.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable beyond the focusable region.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Motion: under `dir="rtl"` the marquee track starts offset (`rtl:translate-x-1/2`) and the animation runs reversed; `motion-reduce` stops it in both.
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

<!-- components/resource-grid.md -->

# Resource Grid

> A band that points readers to further reading on solution pages: an overline, a headline and a short lead with an optional button sit beside a two-column frame grid of linked resource cards, each a title and one sentence. A card whose link leaves the site opens in a new tab; past four cards the grid scrolls inside a fading scroll area so the band keeps its height. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'resource-grid', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `card-grid`, `topic`, `scroll-area` and `button`.

- Import: `import ResourceGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/resource-grid'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To close a solution page with documentation, articles and stories that go deeper into it.

## Do

- Keep four cards for a full grid; more than four scroll.
- Give a card a full `http` link only when it leaves the site, so only those open in a new tab.

## Don’t

- For related articles with covers → use `article-cards`.
- For linked use cases with media → use `use-case-links`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the copy-beside-media band that owns the heading and the named region.
- `topic` — the linked title-and-sentence cell each card is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, which also names its region and the scroll area. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Lead sentence beside the grid. |
| `items` | `ResourceGridItem[]` | `[]` | false | The resource cards, in order; each is `{ title, description?, href }`, and a card with no title is skipped. |
| `primaryAction` | `ResourceGridAction` | `undefined` | false | Button under the copy; dropped when its label or link is missing. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` and `focus-visible` on each card (owned by `topic`)
- `data-scrollable` is set when more than four cards render, and the grid scrolls inside a fading scroll area
- Empty: when no item has a title the band renders nothing
- The button renders only when `primaryAction` has a label and a link

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `topic` and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves card to card, then to the button; `Enter` follows the link. The scroll area is keyboard-scrollable.
- ARIA: `media-split` renders the named region and the headline (`h2`); the root is a plain `div` so the band has one landmark; each card's title is an `h3`; the scroll area is named by the title; external cards carry `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `media-split` and `topic`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every card is a full-cell link.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import ResourceGrid from '@aziontech/webkit/resource-grid'
</script>

<template>
  <ResourceGrid
    eyebrow="Go Deeper"
    title="Guides and Resources"
    description="Documentation, articles, and customer stories on building secure, compliant financial applications on a distributed architecture."
    :items="[
      {
        title: 'New to Azion? Start here',
        description: 'A guide to your first steps with Azion.',
        href: '/docs'
      },
      {
        title: 'Learning Center',
        description: 'Practical knowledge to speed up, secure, and scale applications.',
        href: '/learning'
      },
      {
        title: 'How Technology Can Help You Comply with Regulations for Fintech',
        description:
          'Distributed infrastructure brings security, compliance, and monitoring together for reliable, scalable operations.',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/blog/how-technology-can-help-comply-with-regulations-for-fintech/'
      },
      {
        title: 'How Justa is evolving its technology to meet modern digital demands',
        description:
          'See how Justa uses the Azion Web Platform to improve security and performance in PIX and QR Code transactions.',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/blog/how-justa-has-been-evolving-its-technology-to-meet-modern-digital-demands/'
      }
    ]"
    :primary-action="{
      label: 'See all guides',
      href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/products/guides/',
      trailing: true,
      target: '_blank'
    }"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/section-command.md -->

# Section Command

> A one-line command or agent prompt with a copy button, set in a large `InputGroup` under hero or section copy ("npm create azion", "Ask your agent to …"). With `shell` a `$` prompt leads the line. From the design sample's site `SectionCommand`.

- Import: `import SectionCommand from '@aziontech/webkit/section-command'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- The one command that starts a product, beside or instead of a call to action.
- A prompt to paste into an AI agent (`shell` off).

## Do

- One line that works when pasted as is.
- Place it in a hero or section-title actions slot.

## Don’t

- For several lines or output — use `CodeBlock` or `CliTerminal`.
- For an editable field — use `InputText`.

## Related

- CopyButton`, `InputGroup` — the parts.
- CliTerminal` — a full terminal session.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `—` | true | Text on the line, copied as written. |
| `shell` | `boolean` | `true` | false | Draws the shell prompt before the text; turn off for a prompt meant for an agent. |

## States

- Read-only input; the copy button shows its copied state (from `CopyButton`).

## Accessibility

- The read-only input is named "Command" or "Prompt"; the copy button is named "Copy command" or "Copy prompt".
- The `$` is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Keyboard: `Tab` reaches the field (text can be selected) and the copy button.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities.
- The command is `dir="ltr"` so a shell line keeps its order inside right-to-left pages.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

| Key                          | English source | Override prop |
| ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| `sectionCommand.command`     | `Command`      | —             |
| `sectionCommand.prompt`      | `Prompt`       | —             |
| `sectionCommand.copyCommand` | `Copy command` | —             |
| `sectionCommand.copyPrompt`  | `Copy prompt`  | —             |

- The command itself is content.

## Responsive

- Fills its column up to `--container-xs`; fixed at that width from large.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SectionCommand from '@aziontech/webkit/section-command'
</script>

<template>
  <SectionCommand value="npm create azion@latest" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/section-command.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/section-command.md).

<!-- components/site-footer.md -->

# Site Footer

> The footer under every marketing page: the link columns, then the social row beside the status indicator and the language select. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-footer', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `footer`, `brand`, `icon-button`, `status-indicator` and `select`. From `md` the Azion mark leads the social row and the status indicator sits beside the language select on the bottom bar; below `md`, as on azion.com, there is no mark and no signature band, and the status indicator stacks over the language select, both at the start. The layout is CSS only, so the server HTML and the hydrated page are the same tree. The language select keeps its own value unless the page binds `v-model:language`; its options are the labels the reader sees.

- Import: `import SiteFooter from '@aziontech/webkit/site-footer'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- As the last block of every marketing page.

## Do

- **Do** render it as the last child of the page shell, as is: it draws its own top rule, its frame and its closing bottom rule.
- **Don't** wrap it in a bordered or padded `div` (`border-t`, `py-*`): the rules double and the frame drifts off the page column.
- Use `kind: 'site'` under a framed marketing page, so the footer draws the page frame and closes on its bottom rule; the page above must not draw a bottom rule of its own.
- Keep four link columns so the grid fills at `md`.
- Set `external: true` on a link that leaves azion.com (Community, Status): it opens in a new tab, draws the external-link glyph after the label and tells assistive tech it opens a new tab. Never add the glyph or `target` yourself.
- Give every social link a `label` that names the network, since the button shows only the glyph.

## Don’t

- Inside the product console or the docs → compose `footer` directly.
- For a closing ask above the footer → use `closing-call-to-action`.

## Related

- `footer` — the composition footer this section fills.
- `closing-call-to-action` — the band that sits right above it.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `SiteFooterKind` | `'site'` | false | Where the footer sits: `site` closes a framed marketing page and draws its frame, `content` runs the bands full bleed. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the footer landmark. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Footer`). |
| `home` | `string` | `''` | false | Destination of the Azion mark; the mark is not rendered when empty. |
| `homeAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the Azion mark link. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Azion home`). |
| `columns` | `SiteFooterColumn[]` | `[]` | false | The link columns, in order; each is `{ title, links }` where every link is `{ label, href, external? }`; an `external` link opens in a new tab and closes on the external-link glyph. |
| `socials` | `SiteFooterSocial[]` | `[]` | false | The profile icon buttons, in order; each is `{ icon, label, href }` where `label` names the button for assistive tech. They open in a new tab. |
| `statusLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Line of the system status indicator; the indicator is not rendered when empty. |
| `languages` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Options of the language select, as the reader sees them; the first one is selected until `v-model:language` holds another. The select is not rendered when empty. |
| `languageAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the language select, also its placeholder. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Language`). |
| `language` | `string` | `''` | false | Two-way value (`v-model:language`). |

## v-model

| Model              | Type     | Default | Emits             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | -------- | ------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `v-model:language` | `string` | `''`    | `update:language` | The chosen option of the language select, one of `languages`. Empty shows the first option; choosing one emits it, so the page can switch its locale. Unbound, the select keeps its value locally. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- `data-kind` mirrors the `kind` prop on the footer
- The footer never renders a signature band, so it ends on its social row on every width; the Azion mark leads the social row from `md` and is not shown below it
- Below `md` the status indicator stacks over the language select at the start of the bottom bar; from `md` they sit side by side at its end
- The status indicator, the language select and the Azion mark each render only when their prop is set
- An `external` link sets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, draws the `pi pi-external-link` glyph after its label (hidden from assistive tech) and appends the catalog's “(opens in a new tab)” as screen-reader text
- Server render and hydration: the mark is always in the DOM and CSS shows it from `md`, so the server HTML, the first client render and every later render are the same tree — nothing moves on mount.

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link carries `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`; links, icon buttons and the select own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the column links, the mark, the social buttons and the language select; the select opens with `Enter` / `Space` and moves with the arrows, owned by `select`.
- ARIA: the `footer` is the `contentinfo` landmark named by `ariaLabel`; each column is titled; the mark link is named by `homeAriaLabel`, each social button by its `label`, the select by `languageAriaLabel`; an external link's name ends with “(opens in a new tab)” from the locale catalog.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the mark link's opacity transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — owned by `icon-button` and `select`.

## Examples

<!-- components/site-nav.md -->

# Site Nav

> The marketing site's own navigation: a sticky bar with the Azion mark, the mega-menu triggers and plain links, and the contact, login and sign-up actions, plus the sheet that carries the same tree below `xl`. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'site-nav', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `global-header`, `brand`, `navigation-menu`, `icon-button`, `search-trigger`, `button`, `drawer`, `panel-header`, `panel-footer`, `scroll-area` and `menu`. Each mega-menu lists its panel as columns of groups, and the sheet's drill-down tree is projected from the same menus, so an entry added to a panel is in both. The open state of the sheet, its drill path and the bar's inline inset are local state. Search is the folded `search-trigger` last in the bar: the section owns no palette, it emits `search` (on a click and on ⌘K / Ctrl K) and the page opens its own `command`, as every header does under `rules/webkit-header-search.md`.

- Import: `import SiteNav from '@aziontech/webkit/site-nav'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- At the top of every marketing page, once.

## Do

- Keep a panel to one, two or four columns; only the four-column panel is stretched to the page column.
- Stack a short group under another in the same column (Platform under Observe) instead of adding a fifth column.
- Give every entry an `href`; an entry without one links to `#`.
- Listen to `search` and open the page's `Command` from it (`@search="searchOpen = true"` beside `<Command v-model:open="searchOpen">`); the trigger already carries ⌘K / Ctrl K.
- Leave `secondaryActionOnPhones` off: on a phone the bar keeps the menu button, the mark, the call to action and search, as azion.com does, and Login stays in the sheet footer.
- The bar is `--layout-header-height` tall: `HeroBand` already takes it out of a screen-filling band; a bare `Hero kind="screen"` takes `offset="var(--layout-header-height)"`, never a literal length.
- Don't wrap the bar, add a second search button beside it, or bind ⌘K yourself.

## Don’t

- For the Console's application header → use `global-header` directly.
- For an in-page list of links → use `navigation-menu` or `menu` directly.

## Related

- `global-header` — the bar primitive the navigation is rendered in.
- `navigation-menu` — the mega-menu the bar opens from `xl` up.
- `menu` — the drill-down tree the sheet carries below `xl`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `home` | `string` | `'/'` | false | Where the Azion mark links. |
| `menus` | `SiteNavMenu[]` | `—` | true | The mega-menus, in bar order; each is `{ value, label, columns }` where `columns` is an array of columns, each holding groups of `{ label, href?, items }` and each item `{ label, description?, href?, icon? }`. |
| `links` | `SiteNavLink[]` | `[]` | false | Bar entries that open no panel, after the menus; each is `{ label, href }`. |
| `contact` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | Contact link set in the bar from `xl` up and last in the sheet's tree; `{ label, href }`. |
| `primaryAction` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | The sign-up button, filled, in the bar and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`. |
| `secondaryAction` | `SiteNavLink` | `undefined` | false | The login button beside it, in the bar from `sm` up and in the sheet footer; `{ label, href }`. |
| `secondaryActionOnPhones` | `boolean` | `false` | false | Keeps the login button in the bar below `sm` too; off, it steps out on phones, as on azion.com, and stays in the sheet footer. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent)` |  |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the sheet is `open` or closed (local state, owned by `drawer`)
- Closing the sheet resets its drill path; following a leaf of the tree closes the sheet
- The bar reads its own inline inset on mount and on resize, so the four-column panel's collision padding lands it on the page column's leading edge
- Each panel's column count is mirrored on `data-columns` and drives its track count; only a four-column panel is stretched to the page column
- An absent `contact`, `primaryAction` or `secondaryAction` is omitted from the bar and the sheet
- The secondary action steps out of the bar below `sm` unless `secondaryActionOnPhones`; the sheet footer always carries it

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: the mark link draws the ring token; triggers, items and buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the bar; ⌘K / Ctrl K fires `search` (a mounted `Command` claims the shortcut first); the mega-menu and the sheet own their keyboard models (arrows, `Enter`, `Esc` closes and restores focus to the trigger).
- ARIA: the bar is the `global-header` landmark named "Azion", so the root is a plain `div`; the mark link is named "Azion home"; the menu button "Open navigation" is an icon button with a name; the search trigger is named "Search" and announces `aria-keyshortcuts` (`Meta+K Control+K`); the sheet is titled "Menu".
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by the composed components.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on the mark link; the sheet and the panels own their reduced-motion fallbacks.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the medium buttons and icon buttons meet it.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup>
import Command from '@aziontech/webkit/command'
import SiteNav from '@aziontech/webkit/site-nav'
import { ref } from 'vue'

const searchOpen = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <SiteNav
    home="/"
    :menus="[
      {
        value: 'developer',
        label: 'Developer',
        columns: [[{ label: 'Docs', items: [{ label: 'Azion Docs', description: 'Documentation and technical references', href: '/docs' }] }]]
      }
    ]"
    :links="[{ label: 'Pricing', href: '/pricing' }]"
    :contact="{ label: 'Contact', href: '/contact' }"
    :primary-action="{ label: 'Start for free', href: '/signup' }"
    :secondary-action="{ label: 'Login', href: '/login' }"
    @search="searchOpen = true"
  />
  <Command v-model:open="searchOpen"></Command>
</template>
```

<!-- components/stats-band.md -->

# Stats Band

> The proof-by-numbers band of a marketing page: a framed row of big figures, each with its caption and optional prefix or unit. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'stats-band', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box` and `big-numbers`, which owns the figures' scale and layout.

- Import: `import StatsBand from '@aziontech/webkit/stats-band'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To state reach, scale or results in three to five figures right after a hero or a claim.

## Do

- Keep `value` short and the unit in `suffix`, so the figure reads at a glance.
- Three to five items; more than that and the figures stop reading as a band.

## Don’t

- For figures that need a quote or a logo beside them → use `network-section` or `logo-wall-quote`.
- For a single figure inside another band → use `big-numbers` directly.

## Related

- `big-numbers` — the figure row this band frames.
- `network-section` — the band that pairs claims with client outcomes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `StatsBandItem[]` | `[]` | false | The figures rendered as cells, in order; each item is `{ value, label, prefix?, suffix? }` where `value` is the figure, `label` its caption, and `prefix` / `suffix` the qualifier and unit set beside it. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — a proof band with nothing to prove is absent from the page

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: nothing in the band is interactive.
- Keyboard map: none.
- ARIA: the band is a plain `div`; the figures' semantics (each figure paired with its caption) belong to `big-numbers`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `big-numbers`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable, nothing is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StatsBand from '@aziontech/webkit/stats-band'
</script>

<template>
  <StatsBand
    :items="[
      { value: '100', suffix: 'ms', label: 'Median response, worldwide' },
      { value: '24', suffix: '/7', label: 'Support on every plan' },
      { value: '99.99', suffix: '%', label: 'Availability, contractual' }
    ]"
  />
</template>
```
