<!-- components/sticky-carousel.md -->

# Sticky Carousel

> A row of numbered dark cards that pins under the site header while the page scrolls and slides the row sideways until its last card is in view, then lets the page continue. Below the large breakpoint, or under reduced motion, it is a plain snap-scrolling row. From the design sample's site `StickyCarousel`.

- Import: `import StickyCarousel from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-carousel'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Five to eight short points that read best one after another (principles, reasons).

## Do

- Keep each card to a heading and two lines.
- Do not nest it inside a container that clips overflow; sticky positioning needs the page scroll.

## Don’t

- For three to five ordered stages that fit the width — use `ProcessScroll`.
- For content the reader must compare side by side.

## Related

- ProcessScroll` — the same cards without pinning.
- StickyStack`, `FeatureScroll` — other scroll-driven bands.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it. |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph beside the headline. |
| `items` | `StickyCarouselItem[]` | `[]` | false | The cards, in order; each is `{ title, description }` and is numbered by its position. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the card row; defaults to the title. |
| `headerOffset` | `string` | `'3.5rem'` | false | Height of the sticky site header the band pins under, from the large breakpoint up; any CSS length. |

## States

- Renders nothing without a title or items.
- Pinned (large, motion allowed): the runway grows by the row overflow and the row translates with the scroll.
- Not pinned: a snap-scrolling row.

## Accessibility

- The band root is a plain container; the row is the one focusable `region`, named by `ariaLabel` or the title.
- Cards are an ordered list; the number is `aria-hidden`.
- Keyboard: when pinned, focus moving into a card scrolls the page, and the row follows the page scroll.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities; the pinned row slides toward the inline start in both directions.
- Keyboard: unchanged.

## Internationalization

- Built-in strings: none. Every visible string is marketing copy and arrives through props, so the page supplies it in its own language.

## Responsive

- Pins only from the large breakpoint up.
- Below large: cards `min(22rem, 80vw)` with snap.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StickyCarousel from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-carousel'

  const items = [
    { title: 'One platform', description: 'Code, data and security deploy together.' },
    { title: 'No regions', description: 'Everything runs everywhere by default.' },
    { title: 'No cold starts', description: 'Isolates start in under a millisecond.' },
    { title: 'Open standards', description: 'Web APIs, so code moves in and out freely.' },
    { title: 'Predictable bills', description: 'Pay for requests, not for idle servers.' },
    { title: 'Support that answers', description: 'Engineers on call, not ticket queues.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <StickyCarousel
    eyebrow="Why teams move"
    title="Six reasons teams run on one platform"
    description="Scroll the page: the row pins under the header and slides until the last card is in view."
    :items="items"
  />
</template>
```

<!-- components/sticky-scroll-code.md -->

# Sticky Scroll Code

> The developer-capabilities band of a product page: a large section title over a sticky stack whose claims scroll past a pinned media frame, the open claim showing its one-file code sample on the pixelate texture and its own button under its description. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'sticky-scroll-code', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `sticky-stack`, `texture-material`, `code-block` and `button`. Which claim is open is scroll-driven state owned by `sticky-stack`.

- Import: `import StickyScrollCode from '@aziontech/webkit/sticky-scroll-code'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To walk a developer through several capabilities, each proven by a short file, while the page scrolls.

## Do

- Keep each sample short enough to read in the pinned frame.
- Give every item a `code`; the item's `action` is optional and shows only while the item is open.

## Don’t

- For one claim beside one sample → use `code-split`.
- For a walkthrough shown by illustrations → use `feature-scroll`.

## Related

- `sticky-stack` — the pinned, scroll-driven run of claims this section renders through.
- `code-block` — the one-file sample each claim shows.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the large section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `StickyScrollCodeItem[]` | `[]` | false | The capabilities, in reading order; each is `{ title, description, code, action? }` where `code` is the one-file sample `{ fileName, code, language?, fileIcon?, copyAriaLabel? }` and `action` is `{ label, href, trailing? }` rendered as a small secondary button under the open item. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`; the open item, its progress and the pinned frame are scroll-driven state owned by `sticky-stack`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; an item's button renders only when it has an `action`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by `code-block` (copy button) and `button`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches each open item's copy button and button.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2`; each sample's copy button is named by its `copyAriaLabel`, or the code block's own name when empty.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): owned by `section-title`, `sticky-stack` and `code-block`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the band adds no motion; the sample's line entrance is owned by `code-block`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — not applicable to the small item button, which is supplementary to the item's copy.

## Examples

### Default


<!-- components/story-library.md -->

# Story Library

> Every success story of a company as one filterable library. A left-aligned title sits over a toolbar — a search field and one searchable select per facet (industry, solution, product) on one row — then a grid of story cards and a load-more button. Each card is one link named by its company: the client mark in a single ink, the story's category as an overline, its description and a read cue whose arrow nudges on hover. The grid runs one column on phones, two from `sm` and three from `lg`. Search and facets combine; when nothing matches, an empty state offers to clear every filter. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'story-library', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `input`, `select`, `button` and `empty-state`; the search, the facet selections and each select's own option search are local state.

- Import: `import StoryLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/story-library'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- To list every success story with search and facet filters.

## Do

- Derive each facet's `options` from the values the items carry, so every option matches at least one story.
- Give every item a `facets` entry per facet `key`; an item without one never matches a selection on that facet.
- Pass `client.logo` as any image URL or imported asset (`import gpaExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/gpa-extended-reversed.svg'`); the card fits a mark of any intrinsic size, so do not pre-scale or crop it.

## Don’t

- For a closing row of three related stories → use `article-cards`.
- For a filterable list of articles → use `article-index-blog` or `article-index-resource-hub`.

## Related

- `article-index-resource-hub` — the sibling listing of articles with facet dropdowns.
- `empty-state` — the no-match state.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered left-aligned as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `items` | `StoryLibraryItem[]` | `[]` | false | The stories, in order; each is `{ key, href, client, category, description, facets? }`. |
| `facets` | `StoryLibraryFacet[]` | `[]` | false | The facet selects, in order; each is `{ key, label, allLabel, options }`. |
| `search` | `StoryLibrarySearch` | `undefined` | false | The search field's `placeholder` and accessible `label`; the field is omitted when absent. |
| `empty` | `StoryLibraryEmpty` | `undefined` | false | The no-match state's `title` and the `action` label of its clear-filters button. |
| `linkLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Read cue at the foot of each card, also the lead of its accessible name. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the load-more button under the grid; the button is omitted when empty. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the list of stories. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover` (a card lifts to the raised surface, the read cue brightens and its arrow nudges), `focus-visible` (inset ring)
- Filtered: the search matches the client name and the description; each facet keeps the stories whose `facets[key]` holds the selected value; all filters combine
- Empty: when no story matches, the grid and the load-more button give way to `empty-state`, whose action clears the search and every facet; it renders only when `empty` is set
- `data-last-row-sm` / `data-last-row-lg` mark the cards on the grid's last row so it drops its bottom rule
- Client mark: drawn at the mark row's height, at most `9rem` wide, keeping its aspect ratio; when the card is narrower than that (two columns at 200% zoom) the mark shrinks to the card's width (`min-w-0`) and stays start-aligned, so a mark of any size or aspect ratio never pushes the card past its column

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: every card shows an inset `focus-visible` ring; the field, selects and buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the search field, each select, the cards and the load-more button; the selects own their keyboard map.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the toolbar is a `search` landmark; the field is named by `search.label` and each select trigger by its facet `label`; the list is named by `ariaLabel`; each card link is named `linkLabel: client name`, its mark decorative (`alt=""`) and its read cue `aria-hidden`; an option search with no match announces itself as a `status`.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): text uses `--text-default` / `--text-muted`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none` on every transition.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — every card is a full-cell link.

## Right-to-left

- Layout: logical utilities only (`ms-`/`me-`, `ps-`/`pe-`, `start-`/`end-`, `text-start`), so the layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`.
- Icons: the external-link arrow does not mirror; its hover nudge moves toward the end edge (`rtl:` flips the `translate-x`).
- Keyboard: no horizontal arrow-key logic.
- User data: none.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import StoryLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/story-library'
  import axurExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/axur-extended-reversed.svg'
  import exameExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/exame-extended-reversed.svg'
  import gpaExtendedReversed from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/gpa-extended-reversed.svg'
</script>

<template>
  <StoryLibrary
    anchor="cases"
    title="Companies building with Azion"
    aria-label="Success stories"
    link-label="Read story"
    more-label="Load more"
    :items="[
      {
        key: 'case-gpa',
        href: '/site/success-cases/gpa',
        client: { name: 'GPA', logo: gpaExtendedReversed },
        category: 'Retail',
        description:
          'Grupo Pão de Açúcar (GPA) solved a targeted DNS attack, secured 100+ critical applications in 15 days, and reduced costs by 30%.',
        facets: { industry: ['Retail'], solution: ['Secure'] }
      },
      {
        key: 'case-axur',

          'See how moving AI inference off managed infrastructure unlocked the fastest automatic takedown in the market.',
        facets: { industry: ['Tech'], solution: ['Build', 'Secure'] }
      },
      {
        key: 'case-exame',
        href: '/site/success-cases/exame',
        client: { name: 'Exame', logo: exameExtendedReversed },
        category: 'Media',
        description:
          'Faster content delivery and resilient infrastructure enabled Exame to handle large traffic spikes during major news events.',
        facets: { industry: ['Media'], solution: ['Build', 'Deploy'] }
      }
    ]"
    :facets="[
      {
        key: 'industry',
        label: 'Industry',
        allLabel: 'All industries',
        options: [
          { value: 'Media', label: 'Media' },
          { value: 'Retail', label: 'Retail' },
          { value: 'Tech', label: 'Tech' }
        ]
      },
      {
        key: 'solution',
        label: 'Solution',
        allLabel: 'All solutions',
        options: [
          { value: 'Build', label: 'Build' },
          { value: 'Deploy', label: 'Deploy' },
          { value: 'Secure', label: 'Secure' }
        ]
      }
    ]"
    :search="{ placeholder: 'Search by company or story', label: 'Search success stories' }"
    :empty="{ title: 'No stories match these filters.', action: 'View all success stories' }"
  />

```

<!-- components/subject-library.md -->

# Subject Library

> A library of learning subjects in a divider grid: each subject is one framed card with its name, what it covers and a list of its article links, and an optional closing call to action spans the grid's last two cells so the grid ends without an empty cell. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'subject-library', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `call-to-action` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import SubjectLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/subject-library'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On the Learning Center index, to list every subject with the articles that teach it.
- Whenever a page needs a grid of topic cards that each carry a short list of links, closed by one call to action.

## Do

- Give every subject a unique `slug`; it is the card's `id`, so a `#slug` link lands on it.
- Keep the subject count at a multiple of three plus one when `closing` is set, so the closing cell fills the last row exactly.
- Keep each subject's articles to a handful; the card grows with its list.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For a filterable list of rows → use `listing-browser`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `frame-box` and `call-to-action` directly.

## Related

- `call-to-action` — the `lead` band drawn in the closing cell.
- `card-grid` — the divider grid the subject cards sit in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor` | `string` | `''` | false | In-page `id` of the band, the target of a `#hash` link. |
| `subjects` | `SubjectLibrarySubject[]` | `[]` | false | The subject cards, in order; each is `{ slug, title, description, articles }` where every article is `{ label, href }`. Subjects without a title or a linked article are skipped. |
| `closing` | `SubjectLibraryClosing` | `undefined` | false | Call to action across the grid's last two cells; `{ eyebrow, title, titleMuted, description, primaryAction, secondaryAction }` where each action is `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Three columns from the large breakpoint, one below the small one, on `card-grid`'s `fixed` layout (equal tracks whatever the count), so the closing cell really spans two columns from the small breakpoint up and takes two thirds of the last row on desktop, as on azion.com's learning page
- Empty: when no subject carries a title and a linked article the band renders nothing — not the grid, not the closing cell

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: each article link draws `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-(--ring-color)`; the closing buttons own theirs.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves through the article links in reading order, then the closing actions; `Enter` follows one. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` carrying `anchor` as its `id`; each subject is an `h3` over a `role="list"` of links; the closing cell is `call-to-action`'s own section, named by its title.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): titles `var(--text-default)`, descriptions and links `var(--text-muted)`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the article link colour transition carries `motion-reduce:transition-none`.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the closing actions are large `button`s; article links are inline text links inside a list.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import SubjectLibrary from '@aziontech/webkit/subject-library'
</script>

<template>
  <SubjectLibrary
    anchor="subjects"
    :subjects="[
      {
        slug: 'bots',
        title: 'Bots',
        description:
          'Bots are automated software programs that perform repetitive tasks on websites and applications.',
        articles: [
          {
            label: 'What is a Bot?',
            href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/learning/bots/what-is-a-bot/'
          },
          {
            label: 'What is Bot Management?',
            href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/learning/bots/what-is-bot-management/'
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        slug: 'cdn',
        title: 'CDN',
        description: 'Reduce latency by caching static content on servers close to the user.',
        articles: [
          { label: 'What is a CDN?', href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/learning/cdn/what-is-a-cdn/' },
          {
            label: 'What is Caching?',
            href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/learning/cdn/what-is-caching/'
          }
        ]
      }
    ]"
    :closing="{
      eyebrow: 'Next step',
      title: 'Put what you learned to work.',
      titleMuted: 'On Azion.',
      description:
        'Deploy your first application in minutes, or talk to an expert about your architecture.',
      primaryAction: { label: 'Start for free', href: '/signup' },
      secondaryAction: { label: 'Talk to a specialist', href: '/contact', trailing: true }
    }"
  />
</template>
```

# Template Gallery

> The templates band of a solution page: a framed media split whose copy side invites the reader to start from a template and whose media side is a scrolling two-column wall of deployable template cards, closed by a ticker of the frameworks and clouds it works with. Each card is a mark, a title, one line and a deploy action. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'template-gallery', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `media-split`, `scroll-area`, `card-grid`, `button`, `frame-box` and `ticker` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import TemplateGallery from '@aziontech/webkit/template-gallery'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On a solution page (Retail, Web Apps, AI Workloads, Security, Performance, Streaming) to show the templates a reader can deploy right away.
- Whenever a band pairs one pitch with a long, browsable list of deployable starters.

## Do

- Keep the wall to an even number of templates so the two columns end level.
- Turn on `invertInDark` only for a mark whose artwork ships in dark ink, so it stays legible on the dark theme.
- Set `templatesAriaLabel` so the scrolling wall is announced by name.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For a ticker of marks alone → compose `ticker` directly.
- For a handful of icon-led use cases → use `use-cases`.

## Related

- `media-split` — the framed copy-and-media split the band is built on; it owns the band's named region.
- `ticker` — the row of framework and cloud marks that closes the band.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the media split as its `h2` and naming its region. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Paragraph under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `TemplateGalleryAction` | `undefined` | false | First button under the copy, drawn as the large secondary button; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `secondaryAction` | `TemplateGalleryAction` | `undefined` | false | Second button under the copy, drawn as the large outlined button; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Omitted when absent. |
| `templates` | `TemplateGalleryTemplate[]` | `[]` | false | The template cards of the scrolling wall, in order; each is `{ title, description?, icon?, invertInDark?, href? }`. Templates without a title are skipped. |
| `deployLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Label of the deploy button on each card; a card renders its button only when both this and its `href` are set. |
| `templatesAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Accessible name of the scrolling wall of templates. |
| `tickerLabel` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the row of marks. |
| `tickerMarks` | `string[]` | `[]` | false | Registry names of the frameworks and clouds in the row of marks, in order; the ticker is omitted when empty. |

## Assets

- Brand marks: every valid name is in brand-marks.md (MCP `list_assets({ kind: "brandMarks" })`). An unknown name is not drawn as a mark: `Ticker` prints it as a typographic wordmark, the quote components show no mark.

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Hovering a card lights its deploy button
- Empty: when no template carries a title the band renders nothing — not the split, not the ticker

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`s and the `scroll-area`.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the copy's actions, the scrolling wall and each card's deploy link in reading order; `Enter` follows a link. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band's root is a plain `div`, because `media-split` already renders the band's region named by its title; the wall is `scroll-area`'s region named by `templatesAriaLabel`; the template marks are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): card titles `var(--text-default)`, card lines `var(--text-muted)`; marks flagged `invertInDark` invert under the dark theme.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the button hover and the ticker scroll belong to `button` and `ticker`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the deploy buttons are medium `button`s, the copy's actions are large.

## Examples

<!-- components/use-case-links.md -->

# Use Case Links

> The use-case directory band of a solution page: a left-aligned section title over a divider grid of linked topics, one per use case, each an icon, a heading and a sentence that link to the page that explains it — or, when the items carry no `href`, a plain grid of the same topics with nothing to follow. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-case-links', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `card-grid` and `topic` rather than owning anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import UseCaseLinks from '@aziontech/webkit/use-case-links'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- When every use case has its own page and the band's job is to route the reader there.
- For three or six use cases of equal weight, in a three-column grid.
- For a link-less use-case grid under a left-aligned title (the KV Store page's "Use cases"): leave out every `href`.

## Do

- Keep the count a multiple of three so the divider grid closes cleanly.
- Link every item or none: an item without `href` renders as a plain topic (no link, no arrow), and a band that mixes both reads as broken.
- Keep `description` to one sentence; the row height follows the longest cell.

## Don’t

- When the use cases carry no link and the band leads with one call to action → use `use-cases`.
- For features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.

## Related

- `use-cases` — the sibling band with a title cell and one action instead of a link per case.
- `topic` — the linked icon-heading-sentence cell each use case is rendered with.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the section title. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered by the left-aligned section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | Supporting sentence under the headline. |
| `items` | `UseCaseLinksItem[]` | `[]` | false | The use cases rendered as linked topics in a three-column divider grid, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description, href? }`; an item without `href` renders as a plain, unlinked topic. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the header, not the frame
- The header renders only when `title` is set; `eyebrow` and `description` ride with it
- The items sit on `card-grid`'s balanced divider grid, three across from `lg`: a count that splits evenly fills every row (4 → 2 × 2), and a short last row keeps the column width with its trailing cell left empty, as on azion.com (5 → 3 + 2)
- An item with an `href` is a link (the whole cell, with the topic's link cue); an item without one is a plain topic, so a band with no `href` at all has no links

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `topic`, whose link carries the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` moves between the use-case links; `Enter` follows one.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` named by its title (`aria-label`) when one is set; the headline is the section title's `h2` and each use case is a `topic` with an `h3`, so the outline reads band → use cases.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): typography and colours belong to `section-title` and `topic`.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — `topic`'s hover carries its own fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — each topic link spans its whole cell.

# Use Cases

> The "what teams use it for" band of a product page: a three-column frame whose first cell carries the band's overline, headline, lead and one call to action, followed by one cell per use case. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'use-cases', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — so its whole API is the props below, and it composes `card-grid`, `frame-box`, `overline`, `topic` and `button` rather than owning any anatomy of its own.

- Import: `import UseCases from '@aziontech/webkit/use-cases'`
- Category: sections · Surface: marketing · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- On a product or solution page, right after the opening band, to name the concrete jobs the product is bought for.
- Whenever a page needs three to six short, icon-led use cases with one link out to the documentation.

## Do

- Keep `items` to four or so; the first cell spans two rows at `lg`, so four cases fill the grid exactly.
- Write `title` as the heading the page's outline needs; it is the band's `h2`.
- Give `primaryAction` an `href` to the documentation and set `trailing` so the chevron reads as "go".
- Leave `eyebrow` as the product name; it is the overline the reader scans first.

## Don’t

- For a grid of features with artwork → use `feature-tiles`.
- For use cases that each link to their own page → use `use-case-links`.
- Inside another band's cell → compose `topic` directly.

## Related

- `topic` — the icon, title and description cell each use case is rendered with.
- `card-grid` — the frame grid this band lays its cells in.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | `string` | `''` | false | Overline above the headline in the title cell, closed by the blinking cursor. |
| `title` | `string` | `''` | false | Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2` in the title cell. |
| `description` | `string` | `''` | false | One-line lead under the headline. |
| `primaryAction` | `UseCasesAction` | `undefined` | false | Button pinned to the foot of the title cell; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent. |
| `items` | `UseCasesItem[]` | `[]` | false | The use cases rendered as frame cells, in order; each item is `{ icon, title, description }`. |

## States

- Visual states: `default`
- Empty: when `items` is empty the band renders nothing — not the title cell, not the frame — because a use-case band with no use cases is absent from the page, not an `empty-state`
- The title cell spans two rows from `lg`, so four items fill a three-column grid exactly

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: owned by the composed `button`, whose anchor carries the `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)` ring.
- Keyboard map: `Tab` reaches the action link; `Enter` follows it. Nothing else in the band is interactive.
- ARIA: the band is a `<section>` labelled by its `h2` (`aria-labelledby`); each use case is a `topic` with an `h3`, so the outline reads band → use cases. The overline is decorative text.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons): headline `var(--text-default)`, lead `var(--text-muted)`; icon colours are `topic`'s.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` — the overline cursor and the button's hover belong to `overline` and `button`, which carry their own reduced-motion fallback; this band adds no motion.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px — the action is a large `button`.

<!-- components/spinner.md -->

# Spinner

> Shared visual utility used by other components. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/utils/spinner/`.

- Import: `import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'`
- Category: utils · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- An inline busy mark inside a row, log line or custom control that has no loading state of its own.
- A small in-progress indicator next to text in a toast or status row.

## Do

- It has no props: size it with a `size-*` class (`size-3`, `size-4`) and color it through the inherited text color (it strokes `currentColor`).
- class` on its tag is its sizing API, not a restyle: the spec is a `style_seam`, so `webkit/no-style-override` accepts `<Spinner class="size-4" />`. Keep the class to a `size-*` and, when it must differ from the surrounding text, a text color token.
- It is `aria-hidden`; announce the busy state on the surrounding element (`aria-busy`, a live region or visible text).
- The spin stops under reduced motion, so pair it with text when the wait matters.

## Don’t

- A button waiting on its action → set `loading` on `button`, `icon-button` or `button-highlight`.
- Content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
- Progress you can measure → use `progress`.
- A status with a color and a label → use `status-indicator`.
- Built to be personalized (style seam): any class is accepted on the tag.

## Related

- `skeleton` — reserves the shape of content while it loads.
- `progress` — determinate progress.
- `button` — renders a Spinner itself when `loading` is set.

## States

- Visual states: `default`, `hover`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`

## Accessibility

- Visible focus: `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-(--ring-color) focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-(--bg-canvas)`
- Keyboard map: `Tab` focuses; `Enter`/`Space` activates; `Escape` closes overlays where applicable.
- ARIA: root uses appropriate roles (`button`, `dialog`, `status`, etc.) per sub-component.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 (text) / ≥3:1 (large + icons), including disabled state.
- `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` on animated states.
- Touch target ≥40×40 px where the control is interactive.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Spinner from '@aziontech/webkit/spinner'
</script>

<template>
  <Spinner class="size-4 text-(--text-default)" />
</template>
```

1 more example(s) in [components/spinner.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/spinner.md).

<!-- components/webkit-provider.md -->

# Webkit Provider

> Sets the language and text direction of every WebKit component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/webkit/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. With no provider mounted every component falls back to English. It also carries the reference time of relative times (`now`), so a page that must render the same text on the server and the client, or an example, fixes it once instead of on every cell. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.

- Import: `import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'`
- Category: utils · Surface: product · Structure: monolithic

## When to use

- Once at the root of every app, with the locale the user chose (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`) and the catalogs of the languages the app offers.
- Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
- To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.

## Do

- Mount one `WebkitProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose; do not nest one per page.
- Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
- Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
- Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.
- Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left.
- Leave `now` unset in an app: relative times then read the real clock and `Table.CellTime` re-renders every minute. Set it to a fixed moment where the text must not depend on when it renders: an example or a test (`const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10, 12)`, sample dates counted back from it), or a server render whose markup the browser hydrates. Never compute that moment from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup: the server and the browser read different clocks.

## Don’t

- Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings WebKit ships.
- Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
- Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.

## Related

- use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match WebKit's formatting.
- `pagination` — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
- `confirm-dialog` — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | false | BCP 47 locale of everything below the provider; picks the catalog from `catalogs` (English is built in) and the `Intl` formats. |
| `catalogs` | `Record<string, Messages>` | `undefined` | false | Extra catalogs keyed by locale tag, imported from `@aziontech/webkit/locales/<tag>` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`); a locale with no catalog falls back to English. |
| `messages` | `PartialMessages` | `undefined` | false | Partial catalog deep-merged over the built-in one, keyed by component group (`{ pagination: { next: 'Seguinte' } }`). |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| 'auto'` | `'auto'` | false | Text direction of the subtree; `auto` derives it from the locale (`ar`, `he`, `fa`, `ur` are right-to-left). |
| `now` | `string \| number \| Date` | `undefined` | false | Reference time for every relative time below the provider (`Table.CellTime`, `useLocale().formatRelativeTime`, the day groups of `ConversationHistory`, the relative ranges of `DateRangePicker` when their own `now` is unset); unset reads the real clock, ticking each minute. |

## Slots

| Slot | Scope | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | — | The app, or the part of it that shares this locale. |

## States

- No visual states; the root carries `lang` (the locale) and `dir` (`ltr` | `rtl`).
- `now` set: every relative time below reads it instead of the real clock; changing it re-renders them. An empty or unparseable value reads the real clock.

## Accessibility

- `lang` on the root lets screen readers pick the right voice and pronunciation (WCAG 3.1.1 / 3.1.2).
- `dir` on the root mirrors reading order for right-to-left languages.
- Overlays that teleport to `body` (Dialog, Drawer, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu, Select, MultiSelect, Toaster, Calendar, PropertyFilter, NavigationMenu.Portal, the doc overlays) read the provider through `usePortalLocale()` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-locale`) and set the same `dir` and `lang` on their teleported root, so they do not fall back to the document's direction and language. A consumer's own `<Teleport>` does the same with `v-bind="usePortalLocale().value"` on its root.
- Every assistive label WebKit ships (close buttons, pagination, sort state, empty states) is read in the provider's language.
- No focusable element of its own; it adds no role and no landmark.

## Examples

### Default

```vue
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import ConfirmDialog from '@aziontech/webkit/confirm-dialog'
  import { ptBR } from '@aziontech/webkit/locales/pt-BR'
  import PaginationRoot from '@aziontech/webkit/pagination-root'
  import WebkitProvider from '@aziontech/webkit/webkit-provider'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const page = ref(1)
  const open = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <WebkitProvider
    locale="pt-BR"
    :catalogs="{ 'pt-BR': ptBR }"
  >
    <div class="flex flex-col gap-(--spacing-md)">
      <PaginationRoot
        v-model:page="page"
        :total="120"
      />
      <ConfirmDialog
        v-model:open="open"
        title="Remover domínio"
        description="shop.example.com deixa de responder por este recurso."
        @confirm="open = false"
      >
        <template #trigger>
          <Button
            label="Remover domínio"
            kind="outlined"
            size="medium"
          />
        </template>
      </ConfirmDialog>
    </div>
  </WebkitProvider>
</template>
```

2 more example(s) in [components/webkit-provider.md](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/components/webkit-provider.md).
